3. $\bar{W}$ measures $\bar{F}$'s laboratory in a superposition basis and announces the result
4. $W$ measures $F$'s laboratory in a superposition basis

When $\bar W$ announces $\overline{ok}$, the nested certainty rule leads $W$ to predict $fail$, while the joint Born law permits $(\overline{ok},ok)$.

**PU Diagnosis.** The FR argument fails at assumption (C): reasoning about others' observations across perspectives without tracking perspective shifts. To formalize this, we introduce the following constraint:

<a id="definition-m62-retained-cross-perspective-import-rule"></a>**Definition M.6.2 (Retained Cross-Perspective Import Rule).** Let $\phi_s$ be a proposition asserting an actualized record relative to $s\in\Sigma$. Within the retained perspectival inference calculus, importing that record as a proposition at a distinct perspective $s'$ requires one of the following certificates:

(a) **Record-sharing certificate:** an Evolve interaction or other registered channel maps the record at $s$ to a correlated record at $s'$ with the stated error tolerance;

(b) **Perspective-invariance certificate:** the imported conclusion is proved to be independent of the actualization index. Functions of a shared density operator, such as registered expectation values or transition probabilities, are examples when their operators and basis conventions are also shared.

This is a typing rule of the perspectival semantics. It does not claim that every logically valid statement is state-only, nor that these certificates are derived from the ordered-pair notation $S_{(s)}=(\rho,s)$; the vector notation is only the pure-state shorthand of Definition 24.

<a id="lemma-m62a-cross-perspective-import-normal-form-in-the-retained-calculus"></a>**Lemma M.6.2a (Cross-Perspective Import Normal Form in the Retained Calculus).** In a derivation system whose cross-perspective import rules are exactly the two clauses of Definition M.6.2, every well-typed derivation that imports an actualized record from $s$ to $s'\ne s$ contains either a record-sharing certificate or a perspective-invariance certificate for that import.

*Proof.* Proceed by induction on the length of a well-typed derivation. A derivation of length one can import an actualized record across perspectives only by one of the two introduction rules in Definition M.6.2, so the required certificate is present. Assume the claim for derivations of length at most $n$ and consider a derivation of length $n+1$. If its final inference is local to one perspective, every cross-perspective import occurs in a premise derivation and has the required certificate by the induction hypothesis. If its final inference imports the record from $s$ to $s'$, the generating-rule hypothesis says that the final rule is either clause (a) or clause (b) of Definition M.6.2, which supplies the corresponding certificate. These cases exhaust the retained derivation rules. ∎

<a id="theorem-m62b-certificate-scoped-cross-perspective-actualization-import"></a>**Theorem M.6.2b (Certificate-Scoped Cross-Perspective Actualization Import).** Suppose that the proposition
$$
\phi_{s_W^{(\mathrm{post})}}
=
\text{“}W\text{ has actualized the record that }F\text{ observed }f\text{”}
$$
is proposed for import as a definite proposition at a distinct perspective $s_{\bar W}^{(\mathrm{pre})}\ne s_W^{(\mathrm{post})}$. Assume that the proposed import has neither (a) a record-sharing certificate supplied by an Evolve interaction or another registered channel nor (b) a perspective-invariance certificate in the sense of Definition M.6.2. Then the import is not well typed in the retained perspectival inference calculus.

*Proof.* The proposition $\phi_{s_W^{(\mathrm{post})}}$ asserts an actualized record and is indexed to $s_W^{(\mathrm{post})}$. Definition M.6.2 declares that an import of such a record to a distinct perspective is admitted only by a record-sharing certificate or a perspective-invariance certificate. The two hypotheses exclude those two generating rules. Hence no rule of the retained calculus types the proposed import at $s_{\bar W}^{(\mathrm{pre})}$. This proves the stated obstruction; Theorem M.6.2c applies it to both certainty routes of the complete four-laboratory protocol. ∎

<a id="theorem-m62c-complete-typed-certainty-graph-of-the-four-laboratory-fr-protocol"></a>**Theorem M.6.2c (Complete Typed Certainty Graph of the Four-Laboratory FR Protocol).** Use the standard unitary laboratory state after the two friends have registered their records,
$$
|\Psi\rangle
=
\frac1{\sqrt3}
\bigl(
|\bar h\rangle|d\rangle
+|\bar t\rangle|d\rangle
+|\bar t\rangle|u\rangle
\bigr),
\tag{M.6.2c.1}
$$
and the superobserver bases
$$
|\overline{ok}\rangle=\frac{|\bar h\rangle-|\bar t\rangle}{\sqrt2},
\quad
|\overline{fail}\rangle=\frac{|\bar h\rangle+|\bar t\rangle}{\sqrt2},
$$
$$
|ok\rangle=\frac{|d\rangle-|u\rangle}{\sqrt2},
\quad
|fail\rangle=\frac{|d\rangle+|u\rangle}{\sqrt2}.
\tag{M.6.2c.2}
$$
Among the eight elementary record propositions
$$
\bar F{:}\bar h,\ \bar F{:}\bar t,\ F{:}d,\ F{:}u,
\ \bar W{:}\overline{ok},\ \bar W{:}\overline{fail},\ W{:}ok,\ W{:}fail,
$$
the complete nontrivial probability-one implication graph obtained by conditioning (M.6.2c.1) in the registered measurement bases is
$$
\bar h\to d,
\quad d\to\overline{fail},
\quad\overline{ok}\to u,
\quad u\to\bar t,
\quad\bar t\to fail,
\quad ok\to\bar h.
\tag{M.6.2c.3}
$$
Moreover,
$$
\Pr(\bar W{:}\overline{ok},W{:}ok)
=
|\langle\overline{ok},ok|\Psi\rangle|^2
=
\frac1{12}.
\tag{M.6.2c.4}
$$
There are exactly two directed certainty routes from this positive-probability event to a complementary record: 
$$
\overline{ok}\to u\to\bar t\to fail
\quad\text{and}\quad
ok\to\bar h\to d\to\overline{fail}.
\tag{M.6.2c.5}
$$
Every edge in both routes changes the record owner. For the typed obstruction, additionally assume that each such edge connects distinct registered perspective indices for its source and target propositions. Under this premise, each route contains three cross-perspective imports governed by Definition M.6.2. If no record-sharing or perspective-invariance certificate is supplied for those imports, neither route is well typed and the contradiction cannot be derived through them in the retained calculus. A change of owner label alone does not establish inequality of the perspective indices. Conversely, a well-typed contradiction for this protocol that uses only exact probability-one record implications and avoids both routes would falsify the graph exhaustion.

*Proof.* Direct projection gives
$$
\langle\overline{ok}|\Psi\rangle=-\frac{|u\rangle}{\sqrt6},
\qquad
\langle ok|\Psi\rangle=\frac{|\bar h\rangle}{\sqrt6},
\tag{M.6.2c.6}
$$
which gives the third and sixth edges in (M.6.2c.3). The absent $|\bar h\rangle|u\rangle$ amplitude gives $u\to\bar t$ and $\bar h\to d$. Conditional on $\bar t$, the second laboratory is $(|d\rangle+|u\rangle)/\sqrt2=|fail\rangle$, while conditional on $d$ the first laboratory is $(|\bar h\rangle+|\bar t\rangle)/\sqrt2=|\overline{fail}\rangle$. These give the remaining two edges. Conditioning on each complementary source $\overline{fail}$ or $fail$ leaves nonzero support on both record alternatives, and the preceding six cases exhaust the eight possible sources; hence (M.6.2c.3) is the complete nontrivial certainty graph. Expanding (M.6.2c.1) in (M.6.2c.2) gives amplitude $1/(2\sqrt3)$ for $(\overline{ok},ok)$, proving (M.6.2c.4). Inspection of the six-edge graph gives exactly the two paths (M.6.2c.5). Their owner labels alternate at every edge, so Lemma M.6.2a applies to every traversal. ∎

<a id="remark-m62"></a>**Remark M.6.2.** The PU resolution does not reject any of (Q), (S), (C) outright. Rather, it refines (C): reasoning about others' observations is valid, but only when the perspective context is properly specified. Cross-perspective reasoning requires either explicit interaction (which correlates perspectives) or careful restriction to statements that are perspective-invariant.

### M.6.4a Composable Tolerance Budgets for Certificate-Scoped Imports

<a id="definition-m62d-registered-tolerance-maps"></a>**Definition M.6.2d (Registered Tolerance Maps).** A tolerance map is a monotone function $f:[0,\infty]\to[0,\infty]$ with $f(u)\ge u$. A certified unary inference carrying $f$ turns a premise uncertainty bound $u$ into the conclusion bound $f(u)$ in the same registered units. Exact local inferences and perspective-invariance certificates carry identity; record-sharing certificates carry their registered channel bounds. The constant $\top(u)=\infty$ records an unbounded tolerance. In derivation order,
$$
f\triangleright g=g\circ f,\qquad
\langle A_1,c_1\rangle\triangleright\langle A_2,c_2\rangle
=\langle A_1A_2,c_1A_2+c_2\rangle,
\tag{M.6.2d.1}
$$
where $\langle A,c\rangle(u)=Au+c$, $A\ge1$, $c\ge0$.

<a id="lemma-m62e-composition-on-unary-derivations"></a>**Lemma M.6.2e (Composition on Unary Derivations).** The ordered composition $w_\pi$ of the maps along a well-typed unary path $\pi$ bounds its conclusion uncertainty. Composition is associative, has identity, and an inserted inference cannot decrease the bound. Every cross-perspective link carries the certificate required by Lemma M.6.2a. Multi-premise inferences require a monotone bound on their full tuple of premise uncertainties, or a registered scalar reduction including every side premise.

*Proof.* Induction on path length applies each link certificate to the preceding bound. Associativity and identity are those of function composition. For a prefix $p$, inserted inflationary map $c$, and monotone suffix $q$, $q(c(p(u)))\ge q(p(u))$. The import normal form supplies each cross-perspective certificate. ∎

<a id="definition-m62f-closed-tolerance"></a>**Definition M.6.2f (Closed Tolerance).** On a finite directed graph of records with finitely many registered unary rule instances, put
$$
D_{xy}(u)=\inf_{\pi:x\to y}w_\pi(u),
$$
with value $\infty$ when no path exists.

<a id="proposition-m62g-pointwise-attainment-and-triangle-law"></a>**Proposition M.6.2g (Pointwise Attainment and Triangle Law).** Every finite value is attained at each fixed $u$ by a path without repeated records. Moreover $D_{xx}(u)=u$ and
$$
D_{xz}(u)\le D_{yz}(D_{xy}(u)).
$$
For translations, $d(x,y)=D_{xy}(0)$ is a directed extended distance. If every valid link carries identity, $D_{xy}=\mathrm{id}$ exactly when $y$ is derivable from $x$; otherwise it is $\top$.

*Proof.* Delete cycles using Lemma M.6.2e's prefix-cycle-suffix inequality. A finite graph has finitely many simple paths, so their pointwise minimum is attained. The empty path and inflationarity give identity. Concatenate a path minimizing at $u$ with one minimizing at the resulting intermediate bound to obtain the triangle law. Translations compose by addition. Identity-labelled paths have identity weight, proving the final claim. ∎

A minimizing path can depend on $u$: the paths with weights $u+10$ and $2u$ exchange optimality at $u=10$. A well-typed path containing $\top$ remains derivable and carries an unbounded budget.

<a id="corollary-m62h-certified-acceptance-horizon"></a>**Corollary M.6.2h (Certified Acceptance Horizon).** For an affine path of $N$ links,
$$
w_\pi(u_0)=u_0\prod_kA_k+\sum_kc_k\prod_{j>k}A_j.
$$
If $A_k\le e^{\lambda\tau_k}$, $c_k\le\delta$, $\lambda\ge0$, $\tau_k\ge0$, and $T=\sum_k\tau_k$, then
$$
w_\pi(u_0)\le e^{\lambda T}(u_0+N\delta).
$$
Put $v=u_0+N\delta$. For finite $u_0,\delta,T$ and a finite budget $B\ge0$, the condition $e^{\lambda T}v\le B$ suffices for acceptance. If $\lambda>0$, $v>0$ and $B>0$, it is equivalent to
$$
T\le\lambda^{-1}\ln\frac{B}{v}.
\tag{M.6.2h.1}
$$
Since $T\ge0$, this branch has an admissible duration only if $B\ge v$. If $B=0<v$, no nonnegative duration meets the sufficient criterion. If $v=0$, the upper bound is zero for every finite $T$, including at $B=0$. If $\lambda=0$, the criterion is $v\le B$. An infinite budget imposes no restriction on these finite upper bounds.

A necessary bound uses the different lower-amplification premise $\prod_kA_k\ge e^{\lambda T}$ with $u_0,\lambda>0$. Acceptance under a finite budget first implies $B\ge u_0>0$, and then
$$
T\le\lambda^{-1}\ln(B/u_0).
$$

*Proof.* Repeated affine composition gives the exact path formula. Nonnegativity of the durations and coefficients bounds every product in it by $e^{\lambda T}$, yielding the upper estimate. For positive $v,B,\lambda$, division and the increasing logarithm give (M.6.2h.1); the listed zero cases follow directly without logarithms. For the necessary bound, discard the nonnegative additive terms to obtain $B\ge w_\pi(u_0)\ge u_0e^{\lambda T}\ge u_0$, and then take the logarithm of positive quantities. ∎

<a id="remark-m62i-orbit-averaging-handoff-test"></a>**Remark M.6.2i (Orbit-Averaging Handoff Test).** A classical comparison can register a finite three-body trajectory, a fine integrator, an orbit-averaged surrogate, a fast-phase uncertainty at handoff, and certified tolerance maps for every transition. Compare uninterrupted fine integration, immediate averaging, and delayed averaging at the same terminal observables and cost. Report the composed bound, measured error, and actual budget decisions. This tests whether the lost phase and subsequent amplification explain an order effect. Application to an Evolve channel uses that channel's own tolerance certificate.

**Perspective Occupancy and Record Import.** Thesis P.2.3.1 describes the realized registration at a perspective as its occupancy. In the Wigner–friend setting, the friend's record event occurs at the friend's perspective; Wigner's later access is a separate readout with the interaction certificate of Definition M.6.2. The occupancy interpretation and the composable import budgets answer complementary questions: what is registered at each perspective, and what another perspective can infer with a specified tolerance. The import calculus derives its conclusions from the stated record-sharing certificates.

### M.6.5 Distinction from Relational Quantum Mechanics

The PU resolution bears surface similarity to Rovelli's Relational Quantum Mechanics (RQM) (Rovelli 1996), which also holds that quantum states are relative to observers. However, fundamental differences exist:

| Aspect | Relational QM | PU Framework |
|--------|---------------|--------------|
| **Ontological status** | Relative quantum information; reconstruction programme | Declared branch structure; physical perspectives require the registered perspective-space, instrument, and realization certificates |
| **Grounding** | Equivalent physical systems, quantum completeness, and information postulates | Conditional on SPAP together with the retained Hilbert/Born, update, and perspective records; a registered physical reset is a separate branch with $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{reset}}=H_q(P\mid R)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{diss}}\ge H_q(P\mid R)$ |
| **Why relational?** | Observer-dependent measurement descriptions | SPAP motivates perspective indexing on the declared response branch; Corollary 26 identifies the quantum perspective space on the ordered rank-one context branch |
| **Mathematical structure** | Quantum questions and Hilbert spaces; no PU perspective manifold | Perspective Space $\Sigma \cong U(d_0)/U(1)^{d_0}$ with Riemannian structure (Definition 25, Theorem 25) |
| **Dynamics** | Hamiltonian evolution and measurement interactions; no PU drift-diffusion kernel | Explicit drift-diffusion realization of $G_{\text{persp}}$ on $\Sigma$ (Equations M.5a–b) |
| **Consistency criterion** | Quantitative correlations under stated measurement dynamics | Bakry-Émery control yields $W_2$-contractive convergence for the constructed class (Equation M.5c) |
| **Origin of probability** | Reconstruction uses an additional superposition postulate | On the accepted carrier branch, Principle 11b fixes the invariant response ledger, Principle 8.0b and $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{car}}$ fix the complex carrier, Theorem 8.2 and Lemma 8.2a give quotienting and retained additivity, and Definition 8.2b plus Theorem 8.3 give the unique trace representation on the accepted full-domain or finite informationally complete positive-reconstruction route; Principle 8.0c separately supplies irreducible registered single outcomes |
| **Temporal structure** | Time-indexed questions and unitary evolution | Directed order is required by Theorem 4; a thermodynamic arrow follows only on the independently certified Appendix O branch |

<a id="remark-m63-rqm-comparison"></a>**Remark M.6.3: RQM Comparison.** Rovelli's relational formulation and PU use distinct additional premises. Corollary 1 excludes a uniformly exact predictor on its diagonal-closed model class; Definition 24 and the declared quantum branch supply PU's perspective-indexed representation and this appendix's dynamics.

### M.6.6 Toward Completing the Relativistic Program

The conditional same-basis record-consistency construction admits a structural comparison with Einstein's operational treatment of simultaneity.

**The Relativistic Insight.** Einstein's key move was recognizing that "simultaneity" had no absolute meaning—it was operationally defined relative to reference frames. What appeared to be an objective, frame-independent fact (whether two events are simultaneous) was revealed to be frame-dependent once the operational content was examined carefully. This was not a retreat from objectivity but its proper relativization.

**The Quantum Extension.** The PU framework applies the same logic to measurement outcomes:

| Special Relativity | PU Framework |
|--------------------|--------------|
| Simultaneity of distant events | Definiteness of measurement outcomes |
| "What measurements determine distant simultaneity?" | "What interactions determine outcome actuality?" |
| Finite signal-speed bound | Nonzero spacing, a registered positive edge-update duration, edge-by-edge serialization, and bounded weights; frontier attainment and Lorentzian promotion require separate records |
| Simultaneity relative to reference frame | Actuality relative to perspective |
| Events have frame-dependent time ordering | Outcomes have perspective-dependent actuality |
| Lorentz group connects frames | $G_{\text{persp}}$ kernel connects perspectives |
| One Minkowski spacetime | One MPU network |
| Spacetime interval $ds^2$ invariant | Born trace weight $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho E)$ unchanged for a common state and effect, or under their simultaneous unitary transport; varying the measurement alone need not preserve it |
| Light postulate + relativity principle | POP + PCE + SPAP |

**Structural Correspondence M.6.4 (Relativistic Parallel).** The logical structure of perspectival quantum mechanics stands to the measurement problem as special relativity stands to pre-relativistic simultaneity. In both cases:

(i) An apparently absolute quantity (simultaneity / outcome definiteness) is revealed to be relative to a reference context (frame / perspective).

(ii) Each relativization is branch-relative. Frame-relative simultaneity uses an accepted Lorentzian characteristic-cone branch; perspective-relative actuality uses the retained SPAP, Hilbert/Born, update, and perspective records. A registered reset, a full-state refresh channel, and a Lorentzian cone are independent additional gates.

(iii) On the nominated Hypothesis 1 branch, one registered MPU network supplies the common substrate, an ontological identification made by Hypothesis 1.

(iv) Lorentz transformations govern frame changes on the Lorentzian branch. A perspective kernel yields record consistency only on the certified strong-readout branch of Lemma M.6.1.

*Justification.* The comparison uses the following branch-relative correspondences:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Reference frame}
&\longleftrightarrow \text{Perspective }s\in\Sigma,\\
\text{Lorentz transformation}
&\longleftrightarrow \text{Perspective transition kernel }G_{\mathrm{persp}},\\
\text{Spacetime interval }ds^2
&\longleftrightarrow \text{Born trace weight of a common or covariantly transported test},\\
\text{Lorentzian characteristic cone on the accepted Appendix O branch}
&\longleftrightarrow \text{perspective-update consistency on the retained quantum branch}.
\end{aligned}
$$
For a density operator $\rho$, an effect $0\le E\le I$ and a unitary $U$,
$$
\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[(U\rho U^\dagger)(UEU^\dagger)\right]
=\operatorname{Tr}(U\rho E U^\dagger)
=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho E).
$$
For a pure state and rank-one effect this trace is $|\langle k|\psi\rangle|^2$. No invariance under changing the effect alone follows.

Frame-relative simultaneity uses the accepted Lorentzian characteristic-cone branch, whose spacing, clock, serialization, frontier-attainment and Lorentzian-promotion data are independent of SPAP. Perspective-relative actuality uses SPAP together with the retained Hilbert/Born, update and perspective records; a registered thermodynamic reset is a separate gate. Thus neither relativization is derived here from a common SPAP/reset premise. ∎

<a id="remark-m65-scope-of-the-correspondence"></a>**Remark M.6.5: Scope of the Correspondence.** The correspondence is structural and conceptual rather than mathematical in detail. Lorentz transformations form a continuous Lie group acting on Minkowski spacetime; the perspective dynamics governed by $G_{\text{persp}}$ are stochastic transitions on a distinct manifold $\Sigma$. The parallel illuminates the *type* of conceptual move—relativizing an apparently absolute concept—rather than claiming isomorphism of the mathematical structures.

**Definition M.6.5a (Covariant Perspectival-Actualization Certificate).** A covariant actualization certificate fixes a Hilbert representation carrier $\mathcal H$, a dense common core $\mathcal D\subseteq\mathcal H$, and a representation $\rho_{\mathrm{Spin}}(\Lambda)$ by bounded invertible operators on $\mathcal H$ leaving $\mathcal D$ invariant. It fixes a lift $\widehat G_{\mathrm{persp}}:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D$ and a bounded surjective linear PPI quotient map $\mathfrak q_{\mathrm{PPI}}:\mathcal H\to\mathcal R_{\mathrm{PPI}}$ whose kernel is $\rho_{\mathrm{Spin}}$-invariant, so
$$
\bar\rho_{\mathrm{Spin}}(\Lambda)\mathfrak q_{\mathrm{PPI}}(\psi)
:=\mathfrak q_{\mathrm{PPI}}(\rho_{\mathrm{Spin}}(\Lambda)\psi)
$$
defines the induced response-space representation. Separately, the certificate fixes an ordered Banach perspective-law carrier $\mathcal X_\Sigma$ with a closed generating cone and a continuous normalization functional, a dense domain $\mathcal D_\Sigma\subseteq\mathcal X_\Sigma$, and a closed generator $G_{\mathrm{persp}}^\Sigma:\mathcal D_\Sigma\to\mathcal X_\Sigma$ of a strongly continuous positive normalization-preserving semigroup. It fixes a bridge $J:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D_\Sigma$, a finite protocol set $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{cov}}$, bounded real-linear readouts $s_P:\mathcal X_\Sigma\to\mathbb R$ and $\ell_P:\mathcal R_{\mathrm{PPI}}\to\mathbb R$, and tolerances $\epsilon_{\mathrm{br}}(P)\ge0$ satisfying, for $P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{cov}}$ and $\psi\in\mathcal D$,
$$
\left|s_P(G_{\mathrm{persp}}^\Sigma J\psi)
-\ell_P\!\left(\mathfrak q_{\mathrm{PPI}}(\widehat G_{\mathrm{persp}}\psi)\right)\right|
\le\epsilon_{\mathrm{br}}(P)\|\psi\|.
\tag{M.6.5a.0}
$$
The covariance entry is
$$
\left\|
\mathfrak q_{\mathrm{PPI}}
\left(
\widehat G_{\mathrm{persp}}\rho_{\mathrm{Spin}}(\Lambda)
-\rho_{\mathrm{Spin}}(\Lambda)\widehat G_{\mathrm{persp}}
\right)\psi
\right\|
\le\epsilon_{\mathrm{cov}}(\Lambda)\|\psi\|
\tag{M.6.5a.1}
$$
for $\psi\in\mathcal D$, with $\epsilon_{\mathrm{cov}}(\Lambda)\ge0$. Without the invariant core, typed lift, and bridge, a commutator between the Markov generator and the spin representation is undefined and no covariance claim is made. A Lorentz-scalar metered rate additionally requires the stationary/metering record of Definition E.2a.8 and Corollary E.2a.9 to fix an invariant proper-time parameter $\tau$ on the same representation branch, to register $I_{\mathrm{acq}}$ as a scalar, and to define $\dot I=dI_{\mathrm{acq}}/d\tau$; without that clock entry, $\dot I/C_{\max}$ is only the rate in the selected meter clock. Order-independence of conditioned process functionals is a separate certificate entry.

**Theorem M.6.5b (Certificate-Relative Covariant Generator Responses).** On an accepted certificate, every registered readout obeys
$$
\begin{aligned}
&\left|s_P(G_{\mathrm{persp}}^\Sigma J\rho_{\mathrm{Spin}}(\Lambda)\psi)
-\ell_P\!\left(\mathfrak q_{\mathrm{PPI}}
(\rho_{\mathrm{Spin}}(\Lambda)\widehat G_{\mathrm{persp}}\psi)\right)\right|\\
&\qquad\le
\epsilon_{\mathrm{br}}(P)\|\rho_{\mathrm{Spin}}(\Lambda)\psi\|
+\|\ell_P\|\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{cov}}(\Lambda)\|\psi\|.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.5b.1}
$$
If that invariant-clock metering record is also accepted, $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Evolve}}=\dot I/C_{\max}$ is a Lorentz scalar on that record. Spacelike order-independence holds only for process functionals covered by its independent entry.

*Proof.* Apply (M.6.5a.0) to $\rho_{\mathrm{Spin}}(\Lambda)\psi$, then add and subtract $\ell_P(\mathfrak q_{\mathrm{PPI}}(\widehat G_{\mathrm{persp}}\rho_{\mathrm{Spin}}(\Lambda)\psi))$. The triangle inequality, boundedness of $\ell_P$, and (M.6.5a.1) give (M.6.5b.1). The invariant-clock metering record defines $I_{\mathrm{acq}}$ and $C_{\max}>0$ as scalars and $\dot I=dI_{\mathrm{acq}}/d\tau$ with scalar proper time $\tau$; hence their quotient is a Lorentz scalar. The order-independence conclusion is restricted by definition to its separately listed process functionals. ∎

<a id="theorem-m65c-complexified-flag-covariance-and-celestial-lorentz-covariance-force-the-identity-kernel"></a>**Theorem M.6.5c (Complexified Flag Covariance and Celestial Lorentz Covariance Force the Identity Kernel).** Let $d\ge2$ and identify $\Sigma=U(d)/U(1)^d$ with the complete flags $V_1\subset\cdots\subset V_{d-1}$ of $\mathbb C^d$ through $V_k=\operatorname{span}\{|1\rangle_s,\ldots,|k\rangle_s\}$. Gram--Schmidt orthonormalization makes this identification a $U(d)$-equivariant homeomorphism, and $SL(d,\mathbb C)$ acts on flags by $g\cdot(V_k)_k=(gV_k)_k$.

1. Every Markov kernel $K$ on $\Sigma$ with $K(gs,gA)=K(s,A)$ for all $g\in SL(d,\mathbb C)$, $s\in\Sigma$ and Borel $A$ is the identity kernel $K(s,\cdot)=\delta_s$.
2. For $d=2$, $\Sigma\cong\mathbb{CP}^1$ and $SL(2,\mathbb C)\cong Spin^+(1,3)$ acts by Möbius maps. Under $[\psi]\mapsto\mathbb R_{>0}\psi\psi^\dagger$ this is the Lorentz action $X\mapsto\Lambda X\Lambda^\dagger$ on the celestial sphere of future null directions of the Hermitian-matrix Minkowski space with quadratic form $\det X$. Every $Spin^+(1,3)$-covariant Markov perspective kernel on $\Sigma$ is the identity, and every Markov transition semigroup on $\Sigma$ with $Spin^+(1,3)$-covariant kernels is $P_t=\mathrm{id}$, with zero generator.
3. For $c,t>0$ the heat semigroup $e^{ct\Delta_\Sigma}$ selected in Theorem M.3.3n is $U(d)$-covariant and not $SL(d,\mathbb C)$-covariant. On a certificate of Definition M.6.5a whose perspective-law semigroup on $\Sigma\cong\mathbb{CP}^1$ is induced by Markov kernels required to be Möbius-covariant, $G_{\mathrm{persp}}^\Sigma=0$; every certificate on that carrier with $G_{\mathrm{persp}}^\Sigma\ne0$ therefore has perspective kernels that are not Möbius-covariant.

*Proof.* The standard flag $o$, with $V_k=\operatorname{span}\{e_1,\ldots,e_k\}$, is fixed by the upper-triangular subgroup $B\subset SL(d,\mathbb C)$, and $SU(d)\subset SL(d,\mathbb C)$ acts transitively on $\Sigma$. Covariance therefore gives $K(go,\cdot)=g_*\nu$ with $\nu:=K(o,\cdot)$ invariant under $B$, and it suffices to prove $\nu=\delta_o$.

Let $a\in B$ be the positive multiple of $\operatorname{diag}(2^{2^{d-1}},2^{2^{d-2}},\ldots,2^{1})$ with determinant one. For a $k$-dimensional subspace $V$ with Plücker coordinates $(p_I)_{|I|=k}$, the power $a^n$ multiplies $p_I$ by $\lambda_I^n$ up to a common positive factor, where $\log_2\lambda_I=\sum_{i\in I}2^{d-i}$. These exponents are pairwise distinct by uniqueness of binary expansions, so the Plücker point of $a^nV$ converges to the coordinate point of $I_*$, the index set maximizing $\lambda_I$ over $p_I\ne0$. The Plücker map is a closed embedding, so $a^nV\to\operatorname{span}\{e_i:i\in I_*\}$. Applying this to every $V_k$ and using closedness of inclusion shows that, for every flag $x$, $a^nx$ converges to a coordinate flag $n_wo$. Since $\nu$ is $a$-invariant on the compact metric space $\Sigma$, Poincaré recurrence gives $\liminf_nd_\Sigma(a^nx,x)=0$ for $\nu$-almost every $x$, and for such $x$ the limit of $a^nx$ equals $x$. Hence $\nu=\sum_{w\in S_d}m_w\delta_{n_wo}$.

Let $w\ne e$. It has an inversion: positions $k<l$ with $j:=w(k)>i:=w(l)$. Put $V=\operatorname{span}\{e_{w(1)},\ldots,e_{w(k)}\}$, so $e_j\in V$ and $e_i\notin V$, and put $u=I+E_{ij}\in B$. Then $uV$ is spanned by $e_i+e_j$ and coordinate vectors different from $e_i$ and $e_j$, so every vector of $uV$ has equal $e_i$ and $e_j$ coefficients. A coordinate subspace containing $e_i+e_j$ contains $e_i$, so $un_wo$ is not a coordinate flag. Invariance under $u$ gives $m_w=\nu(\{n_wo\})=\nu(\{un_wo\})=0$. Therefore $\nu=\delta_o$ and $K(go,\cdot)=\delta_{go}$, proving item 1.

For item 2, a complete flag of $\mathbb C^2$ is the line $V_1=[\psi]$, on which $SL(2,\mathbb C)$ acts by $[\psi]\mapsto[\Lambda\psi]$. The Hermitian matrices $X$ with $\det X=0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}X>0$ are exactly the matrices $\psi\psi^\dagger$ with $\psi\ne0$, and $\Lambda(\psi\psi^\dagger)\Lambda^\dagger=(\Lambda\psi)(\Lambda\psi)^\dagger$. The map $X\mapsto\Lambda X\Lambda^\dagger$ preserves $\det X$ and the future cone and is the covering homomorphism $SL(2,\mathbb C)\to SO^+(1,3)$ of Theorem G.10.5. Item 1 with $d=2$ gives the kernel statement, and each $P_t$ of a covariant transition semigroup is a covariant kernel.

For item 3, the positive-time heat kernel has a continuous strictly positive density with respect to $\mu$, so it differs from the identity kernel; item 1 excludes $SL(d,\mathbb C)$-covariance, while Theorem M.3.3n gives $U(d)$-covariance. Under the stated Möbius-covariant requirement, item 2 gives $P_t=\mathrm{id}$ and hence $G_{\mathrm{persp}}^\Sigma=0$. ∎

<a id="theorem-m65d-frozen-highest-weight-flags-and-nontrivial-covariant-jumps"></a>**Theorem M.6.5d (Frozen Highest-Weight Flags and Nontrivial Covariant Jumps).** Let $n\ge2$, $d=n+1$, $V=\operatorname{Sym}^n(\mathbb C^2)$, and let $\rho_n(g)$ be the restriction of $g^{\otimes n}$ to $V$, for $g\in SL(2,\mathbb C)$. Equip $V$ with its symmetric-tensor Hilbert structure and normalized Dicke basis $e_0,\ldots,e_n$. Retain the full complete-flag carrier $\Sigma$ of $V$ and the action $F\mapsto\rho_n(g)F$. Put
$$
o_k=\operatorname{span}(e_0,\ldots,e_{k-1}),\qquad
\mathcal C=\rho_n(SL(2,\mathbb C))o.
$$
Then $\mathcal C\cong\mathbb{CP}^1$ is a proper closed orbit, and the following hold.

1. Every $SL(2,\mathbb C)$-covariant Borel Markov kernel on $\Sigma$ satisfies $K(F,\cdot)=\delta_F$ for $F\in\mathcal C$. Every covariant Markov semigroup fixes this orbit pointwise.
2. The invariant nondegenerate bilinear form and flag duality
   $$
   B(e_k,e_l)=(-1)^k\delta_{k+l,n},\qquad
   (D_BF)_k=(F_{d-k})^{\perp_B}
   $$
   define a smooth equivariant involution $D_B\ne\mathrm{id}$, which fixes $\mathcal C$ pointwise.
3. For $\lambda>0$, the bounded generator $Lf=\lambda(f\circ D_B-f)$ on $C(\Sigma)$ gives the nonzero covariant Feller semigroup
   $$
   P_tf=\frac{1+e^{-2\lambda t}}2f
        +\frac{1-e^{-2\lambda t}}2f\circ D_B.
   $$
   Its dual is a positive mass-preserving, uniformly strongly continuous semigroup on all finite signed Borel measures with the total-variation norm.

*Proof.* For a line $\ell\subset\mathbb C^2$, the spaces $F_k=\ell^{n-k+1}\operatorname{Sym}^{k-1}(\mathbb C^2)$ form a flag. The first ray $\ell^n$ determines $\ell$, and every line is a group translate of the first defining basis ray. This continuous injection of $\mathbb{CP}^1$ identifies its image with $\mathcal C$. Compactness makes the image closed, and its complex dimension one is smaller than $\dim_{\mathbb C}\Sigma=n(n+1)/2$. The diagonal weights of $\rho_n$ sum to zero and the unipotents have determinant one; these elements generate $SL(2,\mathbb C)$, so $\rho_n$ takes values in $SL(d,\mathbb C)$.

The upper triangular subgroup fixes $o$. For a covariant kernel, $\nu=K(o,\cdot)$ is invariant under that subgroup. For $t>0$, the matrix $a_t=\operatorname{diag}(e^{t/2},e^{-t/2})$ acts on $e_k$ with the distinct positive weights $e^{(n-2k)t/2}$. For any subspace $W$, the Plücker coordinates of $\rho_n(a_t)^mW$, after division by the largest exponential with nonzero coefficient, converge to an eigenvector in the corresponding exterior power. Equal exterior weights are allowed. The limit remains decomposable, and its subspace is invariant under $\rho_n(a_t)$. An invariant subspace of a diagonal matrix with distinct eigenvalues is coordinate: its polynomial spectral projectors preserve that subspace. Thus every subspace limit is coordinate. Incidence is closed, so every flag converges to a coordinate flag.

Poincaré recurrence for $\nu$ now makes it supported on the finite set of coordinate flags. The upper unipotent generator obeys
$$
Ee_k=\sqrt{k(n-k+1)}e_{k-1},\qquad Ee_0=0.
$$
Every nonzero $E$-invariant subspace is an initial coordinate segment. Indeed, choose a vector whose maximal nonzero coordinate index $m$ is as large as possible in the subspace. Its successive $E$-images are triangularly independent and span $e_0,\ldots,e_m$, while maximality of $m$ contains the whole subspace in that span. Hence $o$ is the unique full flag fixed by the upper unipotent subgroup. Every other coordinate flag has an infinite unipotent orbit, because a nonconstant orbit of the connected group $\mathbb C$ cannot be finite. A positive atom at such a flag would, by invariance, give equally positive atoms at infinitely many points. All those masses vanish, proving $\nu=\delta_o$. Covariance proves item 1.

The alternating form with matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ on $\mathbb C^2$ is preserved by every determinant-one matrix. Restricting its $n$-fold tensor power to the symmetric subspace gives exactly $B$. Its matrix is invertible and satisfies $B^{\mathsf T}=(-1)^nB$. Orthogonal-complement reversal therefore preserves flag incidence, is involutive, and commutes with $\rho_n(g)$. Grassmannian duality is smooth. Directly, $(o_{d-k})^{\perp_B}=o_k$, so equivariance makes $D_B$ fix $\mathcal C$.

For $d\ge3$, choose a line $\ell$ and a hyperplane $H\supset\ell$ different from $\ell^{\perp_B}$. Such a choice exists because the hyperplanes containing $\ell$ form a positive-dimensional projective space. Complete $\ell\subset H$ to a full flag $F$. Then $(D_BF)_1=H^{\perp_B}\ne\ell$, proving nontriviality. For $d=2$, the alternating-form duality is the identity, consistently with Theorem M.6.5c.

Finally $U_Df=f\circ D_B$ is a positive isometric involution preserving the constant one. Exponentiating $\lambda(U_D-I)$ gives the displayed formula, whose coefficients are nonnegative and sum to one. Equivariance of $D_B$ gives covariance. The dual pushforward formula preserves mass and positivity on all signed measures; its generator has norm at most $2\lambda$. A continuous function separating $F$ from $D_BF$ proves that the generator is nonzero. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m65e-covariant-quantum-cone-channels-and-generators"></a>**Theorem M.6.5e (Covariant Quantum-Cone Channels and Generators).** Let $\rho:SL(2,\mathbb C)\to GL(W)$ be a smooth finite-dimensional complex-linear representation. Require its $SU(2)$ restriction to be unitary and $d\rho(A)$ to be Hermitian for every traceless Hermitian $A\in M_2(\mathbb C)$. This inner-product compatibility holds for a holomorphic representation with unitary compact restriction and for the standard left/right tensor representations. Define
$$
\mathcal C_g(X)=\rho(g)X\rho(g)^*,\qquad
\mathcal A=\rho(SL(2,\mathbb C))'.
$$
The maps $\mathcal C_g$ act on the unnormalized positive matrix cone. A channel $\Phi$ is completely positive and trace preserving and satisfies $\Phi\mathcal C_g=\mathcal C_g\Phi$ for every $g$ exactly when it has Kraus operators in $\mathcal A$. Every Kraus family of such a channel lies in $\mathcal A$.

The complete norm-continuous covariant CPTP semigroup generators are
$$
\mathcal L(X)=-i[\Omega,X]
+\sum_\alpha\left(V_\alpha XV_\alpha^*
-\tfrac12\{V_\alpha^*V_\alpha,X\}\right),
\qquad
\Omega=\Omega^*\in\mathcal A,\quad V_\alpha\in\mathcal A.
$$
Here $\Omega$ has inverse-time units and $V_\alpha$ has inverse-square-root-time units. All domains are the full finite-dimensional matrix carrier. On an irreducible $\rho$, every such generator is zero.

On the three labeled physical spin-half carrier $\mathcal H_0=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes3}$ of Theorem 7.6o, the all-left extension $\rho(g)=g^{\otimes3}$ has
$$
\mathcal H_0\cong V_{3/2}\oplus(V_{1/2}\otimes\mathbb C^2_{\mathrm{mult}}),
\qquad
\mathcal A\cong\mathbb C I_4\oplus(I_2\otimes M_2(\mathbb C)).
$$
Thus every generator in this class has
$$
\Omega=\omega_+I_4\oplus(I_2\otimes\Omega_-),\qquad
V_\alpha=v_{\alpha,+}I_4\oplus(I_2\otimes v_{\alpha,-}),
$$
with $\omega_+\in\mathbb R$, $\Omega_-^*=\Omega_-$ and arbitrary complex $v_{\alpha,+}$ and $2\times2$ matrices $v_{\alpha,-}$. The same operators act on every cross-sector coherence block; the eight-dimensional carrier and its coherences are retained.

*Proof.* Write $\Psi=\Phi^*$. Trace preservation and covariance give, for every matrix $X$,
$$
\operatorname{Tr}[X\rho(g)^*\rho(g)]
=\operatorname{Tr}\Phi(\mathcal C_gX)
=\operatorname{Tr}\mathcal C_g(\Phi X)
=\operatorname{Tr}[X\Psi(\rho(g)^*\rho(g))].
$$
Hence $\Psi$ fixes $\rho(g)^*\rho(g)$. For a traceless Hermitian $A$, put $J=d\rho(A)=J^*$. Taking $g=e^{tA/2}$ and $g=e^{tA}$ shows that $\Psi$ fixes both $B=e^{tJ}$ and $B^2$. For any Kraus family, completeness yields
$$
\sum_\alpha(BK_\alpha-K_\alpha B)^*(BK_\alpha-K_\alpha B)
=\Psi(B^2)-\Psi(B)B-B\Psi(B)+B^2=0.
$$
Every summand is positive, so every commutator vanishes. Differentiating gives commutation with every represented Hermitian boost generator. The commutators of the three Hermitian Pauli generators span $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, so their represented commutators also commute with each $K_\alpha$. These six real generators span $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb C)$ as a real Lie algebra. Polar decomposition gives $K_\alpha\in\mathcal A$. Conversely, Kraus operators in this commutant commute through the two sides of $\mathcal C_g$, proving channel covariance.

The commutant $\mathcal A$ is a finite-dimensional $*$-algebra: it is the common commutant of Hermitian boost generators and anti-Hermitian rotation generators. Choose a Hilbert–Schmidt orthonormal basis $F_0=I/\sqrt d,F_1,\ldots,F_r$ of $\mathcal A$, with $\operatorname{Tr}F_a=0$ for $a\ge1$. By the channel classification, the Choi matrix of each $\Phi_t$ is supported on $\operatorname{vec}(\mathcal A)$. Therefore
$$
\Phi_t(X)=\sum_{a,b=0}^r c_{ab}(t)F_aXF_b^*,
\qquad C(t)=(c_{ab}(t))\succeq0.
$$
At $t=0$, $c_{00}(0)=d$ and every other entry is zero. Finite-dimensional continuous semigroups have bounded generators, so $Q=C'(0)$ exists and is Hermitian. Positivity on vectors with zero zeroth coordinate gives $Q_+=(Q_{ab})_{a,b\ge1}\succeq0$. Put
$$
K=\frac{Q_{00}}{2d}I+\sum_{a\ge1}\frac{Q_{a0}}{\sqrt d}F_a,
\qquad D=\sum_{a,b\ge1}Q_{ab}F_b^*F_a.
$$
Then
$$
\mathcal L(X)=KX+XK^*+\sum_{a,b\ge1}Q_{ab}F_aXF_b^*,
\qquad K+K^*+D=0,
$$
where the last identity is trace preservation. Thus $K=-D/2-i\Omega$, with $\Omega=\Omega^*\in\mathcal A$. Factoring the positive matrix $Q_+$ gives the stated $V_\alpha\in\mathcal A$ and the generator formula.

Conversely, set $K=-i\Omega-\sum_\alpha V_\alpha^*V_\alpha/2$. The norm-convergent Dyson series about $X\mapsto e^{tK}Xe^{tK^*}$ inserts the completely positive map $X\mapsto\sum_\alpha V_\alpha XV_\alpha^*$. Every term is completely positive; their sum is $e^{t\mathcal L}$. The trace derivative vanishes, so this semigroup is CPTP. Every product in the series belongs to $\mathcal A$, giving covariance. On an irreducible complex representation, an eigenspace of any intertwiner is invariant; irreducibility makes the intertwiner scalar. Scalar generator coefficients give $\mathcal L=0$.

For three spins, the symmetric subspace is spin $3/2$ and has dimension four. The magnetic-$1/2$ subspace has dimension three; its two-dimensional subspace orthogonal to the symmetric sum is annihilated by the collective raising operator. Applying the lowering operator produces two independent spin-half partners. The identity $J_+J_-=I$ on these highest spin-half vectors preserves their inner products. These two spin-half copies exhaust the remaining four dimensions. Their Casimir value $3/4$ differs from the spin-$3/2$ value $15/4$, excluding cross-intertwiners. Within each irreducible spin, commuting with the diagonal weights and the nonzero adjacent ladder entries forces a scalar. The displayed multiplicity commutant follows. $\square$

Every channel in this theorem has an equivariant finite Stinespring isometry $V=\sum_\alpha K_\alpha\otimes|\alpha\rangle$ with a spin-zero ancilla. On each irreducible component it is the identity on the representation factor and an isometry on the multiplicity/ancilla factor. Completing finite orthonormal bases extends it to a unitary commuting with $\rho\otimes I$. A Hermitian spectral logarithm is in the same commutant. On the physical three-spin carrier, the six spin-permutation matrices span this commutant with the single relation
$$
I-P_{(12)}-P_{(13)}-P_{(23)}+P_{(123)}+P_{(132)}=0.
$$
The relation is the vanishing third antisymmetric tensor power of $\mathbb C^2$; the trivial and two-dimensional permutation representations give span dimension $1^2+2^2=5$. The exchange-polynomial prescription of Theorem M.6.13n expresses the finite logarithm with actual scalar spin couplings and scalar ancilla coefficients. Adding a scalar energy offset gives a positive finite-time source. Preparation, clock, ancilla, detector and record services retain their declared costs.

This constructs normalized finite-time quantum channels in the stated matrix-cone class. The normalized retained-outcome test is treated in Proposition M.6.5g. The perspective-law bridge and time-consistent source realization remain the entries of Definition M.6.5a. The anisotropic prediction Hamiltonian of Theorem 7.6o retains its own dynamics; its three-spin carrier is the object reused here.

<a id="proposition-m65f-lorentz-extension-census-for-the-three-spin-rotation-carrier"></a>**Proposition M.6.5f (Lorentz-Extension Census for the Three-Spin Rotation Carrier).** Fix the rotation representation $R(u)=u^{\otimes3}$ on the eight-dimensional carrier of Theorem 7.6o. Up to complex-linear representation equivalence, exactly ten continuous complex-linear representations of the fixed real group $SL(2,\mathbb C)$ restrict to this $SU(2)$ representation. With $(p,q)$ denoting the irreducible Lorentz representation of left and right spins $p,q$, the classes are:

- $(3/2,0)$ or $(0,3/2)$, together with two Weyl halves whose chirality multiset is $LL$, $LR$ or $RR$: six classes;
- $(1,1/2)$ or $(1/2,1)$, together with either $(1/2,0)$ or $(0,1/2)$: four classes.

Their complex commutants are $\mathbb C\oplus M_2(\mathbb C)$ in the four first-family classes with repeated Weyl chirality, $\mathbb C^3$ in the two first-family classes with opposite Weyl chiralities, and $\mathbb C^2$ in the four second-family classes. Each class has an inner-product-compatible representative for Theorem M.6.5e.

Requiring each labeled spin-half factor to carry its own Weyl action gives eight labeled assignments and four representation-equivalence types:
$$
\begin{array}{c|l}
LLL&(3/2,0)\oplus2(1/2,0)\\
RRR&(0,3/2)\oplus2(0,1/2)\\
LLR&(1,1/2)\oplus(0,1/2)\\
LRR&(1/2,1)\oplus(1/2,0).
\end{array}
$$
The three permutations in each mixed row are different labeled assignments. The other six classes require an extension beyond three local Weyl assignments. The census classifies mathematical extensions; a physical boost registration additionally fixes the full-carrier intertwiner and experiment transformation of Definition M.6.5a.

*Proof.* Definition G.10.5a gives the complexified Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$. Complete reducibility follows by integrating its compact real form to $SU(2)\times SU(2)$ and averaging a positive Hermitian inner product with normalized Haar measure. The orthogonal complement of any invariant subspace is invariant under the compact group, hence under its complexified Lie algebra. Induction on dimension decomposes the representation into irreducibles.

For one $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ factor, a highest-weight vector $v$ of weight $m$ satisfies
$$
EF^kv=k(m-k+1)F^{k-1}v.
$$
Termination of the lowering chain forces $m$ to be a nonnegative integer, and in an irreducible module the chain spans its $m+1$ dimensions. Decomposing for the first commuting factor leaves multiplicity spaces on which the second factor acts; applying the same argument there gives the outer products $V_p\otimes V_q$. The simply connected group $SL(2,\mathbb C)$ integrates these modules. Restriction to its compact spin subgroup has the branching rule
$$
(p,q)|_{SU(2)}=\bigoplus_{j=|p-q|}^{p+q}V_j,
$$
with unit increments. Multiplication of the two weight characters and telescopic grouping into spin characters proves this rule, with every indicated spin occurring once.

The target rotation character is $V_{3/2}\oplus2V_{1/2}$ by Theorem M.6.5e. A summand containing spin $3/2$ must have $p+q=3/2$ and hence be one of $(3/2,0),(0,3/2),(1,1/2),(1/2,1)$. The first two leave two spin-half summands, each necessarily a left or right Weyl half, giving three chirality multisets for each choice. The last two leave one Weyl half, giving two choices for each choice. Direct-sum multiplicities are nonnegative, so no higher or unwanted spin can cancel. This exhausts the ten classes. Distinct highest-weight pairs have no intertwiners, while a repeated irreducible has the full matrix algebra on its multiplicity space. The commutant types follow. Standard left/right tensor models have unitary compact action and Hermitian boosts.

For a local two-dimensional spin-half factor, the traceless operator space is one spin-one rotation module. Covariance under the fixed rotations forces the three boost generators to be a common scalar multiple of the Pauli spin matrices. The boost-boost Lorentz bracket makes that scalar's square one. These are the left and right Weyl actions, which agree on $SU(2)$. Tensoring their eight labeled assignments and using $V_{1/2}\otimes V_{1/2}=V_1\oplus V_0$ gives exactly the four displayed types. $\square$

<a id="proposition-m65g-spin-scalar-sources-normalized-boosts-and-retained-outcomes"></a>**Proposition M.6.5g (Spin-Scalar Sources, Normalized Boosts and Retained Outcomes).** Let $R$ be a finite unitary $SU(2)$ representation, let $R_L$ be its holomorphic extension, and put $R_R(g)=R_L((g^*)^{-1})$.

1. Every operator commuting with $R(SU(2))$ commutes with both $R_L(SL(2,\mathbb C))$ and $R_R(SL(2,\mathbb C))$. On a nonzero irreducible spin, these two extensions agree on rotations, have opposite boosts and are inequivalent complex-linear representations of the fixed real group. Thus the full-carrier spin-scalar Hamiltonians of Theorems M.6.13n–M.6.13o supply exact algebraic commutators for either global chiral extension.
2. For an invertible matrix $T$ with largest and smallest singular values $a\ge b>0$, every deterministic quantum channel $\Phi$ on that same carrier satisfies
   $$
   \sup_{\|\psi\|=1}\frac12\left\|
   \Phi(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)
   -\frac{|T\psi\rangle\langle T\psi|}{\|T\psi\|^2}
   \right\|_1
   \ge\frac{a^2-b^2}{4(a^2+b^2)}.
   $$
   Exact deterministic realization for all inputs is possible exactly when $T$ is a scalar multiple of a unitary.
3. Among completely positive trace-nonincreasing success maps whose normalized output is the $T$-ray for every pure input, the largest guaranteed success probability is $b^2/a^2$. The normalized instrument with Kraus operators
   $$
   K=T/a,\qquad K_0=(I-T^*T/a^2)^{1/2}
   $$
   attains it, retaining both outcomes. For $T=\rho_n(\operatorname{diag}(e^{t/2},e^{-t/2}))$, the bound in item 2 is $\tfrac14\tanh(n|t|)$ and the optimal guaranteed success probability is $e^{-2n|t|}$.
4. Suppose $T^*T$ is nonscalar and define $Q_T(\rho)=T\rho T^*/\operatorname{Tr}(T\rho T^*)$. If fixed Born effects $E,E'$ obey
   $$
   \operatorname{Tr}[E'Q_T(\rho)]=\operatorname{Tr}(E\rho)
   $$
   for every density matrix $\rho$, then $E$ is scalar. In particular a fixed-label effect has invariant probability under this normalized same-carrier boost exactly when it is scalar.

*Proof.* Differentiating the compact commutation relation gives commutation with the represented $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ generators. Complex linearity and polar decomposition extend it to $R_L$; composition with $g\mapsto(g^*)^{-1}$ gives $R_R$. For unitary $u$, $(u^*)^{-1}=u$, while a positive diagonal boost is sent to its inverse. An intertwiner between the two irreducible extensions must commute with every compact spin matrix. Commutation with the distinct weights makes it diagonal, and commutation with the adjacent nonzero ladder entries makes it scalar. A nonzero scalar cannot intertwine the opposite nontrivial boosts. This proves item 1.

For item 2, choose orthonormal right singular vectors $u,v$ at singular values $a,b$ and the corresponding left singular vectors $u',v'$. The equal-weight ensembles $\{u,v\}$ and $\{(u+v)/\sqrt2,(u-v)/\sqrt2\}$ have the same density matrix. Their desired mean outputs are
$$
M_0=\tfrac12(|u'\rangle\langle u'|+|v'\rangle\langle v'|),\qquad
M_1=\frac{a^2|u'\rangle\langle u'|+b^2|v'\rangle\langle v'|}{a^2+b^2}.
$$
Their trace distance is $(a^2-b^2)/(2(a^2+b^2))$. If the uniform input error is $\epsilon$, linearity and convexity put the channel's common ensemble output within $\epsilon$ of both matrices. The triangle inequality gives the claimed lower bound. Equal singular values give a scalar multiple of a unitary and its exact channel.

For item 3, write a success map as $\sum_r A_r\rho A_r^*$. A positive sum has range in the ray $T\psi$ only when each $A_r\psi$ lies in that ray. Thus $T^{-1}A_r$ maps every vector into its own span. Testing a basis and every sum of two basis vectors makes it scalar. Consequently every such success map is $cT\rho T^*$, with $c\ge0$. Trace nonincrease gives $cT^*T\preceq I$, so $c\le a^{-2}$ and its minimum success probability is $cb^2\le b^2/a^2$. The displayed instrument attains the bound. The symmetric-power boost singular values are $e^{(n-2k)t/2}$, $k=0,\ldots,n$, giving the two explicit formulas.

For item 4, write the affine functionals
$$
q(\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}(T^*T\rho),\quad
r(\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}(E\rho),\quad
h(\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}(T^*E'T\rho).
$$
The asserted equality is $h=qr$. Evaluating it at $s\rho+(1-s)\sigma$ and subtracting the weighted endpoint equalities gives
$$
s(1-s)[q(\rho)-q(\sigma)][r(\rho)-r(\sigma)]=0.
$$
Choose two states with different $q$ values, which exist because $T^*T$ is nonscalar. Their $r$ values agree. Every other state has a $q$ value different from at least one of these two and hence the same $r$ value. Therefore $E=cI$. Scalar $E'=E=cI$ satisfies the equality. $\square$

For a finite instrument satisfying the linear branch covariance in Theorem M.6.5e, item 4 makes its fixed outcome probabilities invariant under normalized boosts for every input exactly when its branch effects are $c_kI$, with $\sum_kc_k=1$. A nonzero single-Kraus branch then has $K_k=\sqrt{c_k}U_k$ with $U_k$ unitary. If these Kraus operators are in the Spin commutant, the flag transitions $F\mapsto U_kF$ form a constant-probability covariant kernel on the full complete-flag carrier.

The full commutant channel class also contains instruments failing this retained-outcome test. In the all-left three-spin decomposition, let
$$
K_0=I_4\oplus(I_2\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|),\qquad
K_1=0_4\oplus(I_2\otimes|1\rangle\langle1|).
$$
They commute with the Spin representation and satisfy $K_0^*K_0+K_1^*K_1=I_8$. On the lower-sector state
$$
\psi=\frac{|+\rangle\otimes|0\rangle+|-\rangle\otimes|1\rangle}{\sqrt2},
$$
where $|\pm\rangle$ are spin-$z$ eigenvectors, outcome zero has probability $1/2$. The normalized $z$ boost changes it to $e^t/(e^t+e^{-t})$. The unconditional channel remains congruence-covariant, and trace preservation makes its normalized-state channel commute with $Q_T$; its individual retained probabilities obey the separate calculation above.

Theorems M.6.5e and M.6.13n–M.6.13o therefore supply matrix couplings and normalized finite-time channels, while the physical observer, perspective-law, readout and clock transformations retain their explicit entries in Definition M.6.5a and Proposition G.1.8g.2.

**Mathematical branch for M.6.5h–M.6.5m.** Fix $G=SL(2,\mathbb C)$, $V=\operatorname{Sym}^7(\mathbb C^2)$ and its full flag manifold $X=\operatorname{Fl}(V)$. This is an explicitly chosen irreducible action on $\mathbb C^8$; its restriction to $SU(2)$ is the single spin $7/2$, so it is not one of the Lorentz extensions of the three-spin rotation carrier in Proposition M.6.5f.

Use a weight basis $e_0,\ldots,e_7$ with diagonal weights $7,5,\ldots,-7$. Let $T$ be the diagonal torus, $B$ the upper triangular subgroup, and $Z=X^T$ the $8!$ coordinate flags. Let $o$ be the highest-weight flag, and let $C=Go$ be the closed osculating sphere already treated in M.6.5d.

<a id="proposition-m65h-exact-full-flag-stabilizers"></a>**Proposition M.6.5h (Exact Full-Flag Stabilizers).** Every stabilizer $G_{F}$ is conjugate to exactly one of the following types:

\[
B,\quad T,\quad C_2,C_4,C_6,C_8,C_{10},C_{12},C_{14}.
\]

Every listed finite type occurs. There is one $B$-stabilizer orbit and $8!/2-1=20{,}159$ $T$-stabilizer orbits. The remaining orbits have the listed finite cyclic stabilizers.

**Proof.** Flag stabilizers are algebraic. A proper positive-dimensional connected subgroup of SL2 is conjugate to T, the upper unipotent subgroup U, or B. This elementary list also follows by classifying the proper Lie subalgebras of sl2 and using algebraicity. The whole group cannot preserve a line in its irreducible eight-dimensional representation. The upper nilpotent generator on Sym7 has a single Jordan block, so U fixes exactly one full flag, o. Its stabilizer contains B and is B. Hence a connected unipotent stabilizer without B does not occur.

If $G_{F}$ has identity component $T$, $F$ is a coordinate flag. Every component normalizes $T$. The nontrivial Weyl element interchanges the distinct nonzero weight lines of weights $m$ and $-m$, so it does not preserve even the first line of a coordinate flag. Thus $G_F=T$. Exactly two coordinate flags have $B$ stabilizer, the highest and lowest flags. They are exactly $C\cap Z$: the only pure seventh-power weight lines are $[e_{0}]$ and $[e_{7}]$, each determining its unique osculating flag. Among the others, two are $G$-equivalent precisely when related by the nontrivial Weyl element: if $gF=F'$, their stabilizers imply $gTg^{-1}=T$. This involution has no fixed coordinate flag. The count follows.

A finite subgroup preserving a full flag has a direct sum decomposition into one-dimensional representations: average an inner product over the finite group and split the invariant flag by invariant orthogonal complements. Its image is therefore abelian. Sym7 is faithful, so the subgroup itself is abelian; finite abelian subgroups of SL2 are conjugate to a finite subgroup of T and hence cyclic. Every stabilizer contains −I, which acts scalarly on V, so write its order as 2q. If $q\ge 8$, the eight weights are distinct modulo 2q. Every invariant full flag is then a weight flag, whose stabilizer contains T, a contradiction. Thus $q\le 7$.

For $2\le q\le 7$, choose $F_1=[e_0+e_q]$ and refine it to a full flag invariant under $C_{2q}\subset T$ by choosing bases in the cyclic eigenspaces. Its first binary form is, up to nonzero coefficient normalization, $x^{7-q}(x^q+cy^q)$. It has at least three distinct projective factor lines; its projective stabilizer is finite because it permutes that finite set and a Möbius transformation fixing three points is the identity. The finite full-flag stabilizer is cyclic, contains a noncentral element of $C_{2q}$, and thus lies in that element's centralizer $T$. Preserving $[e_0+e_q]$ then forces $z^{2q}=1$, proving exact order $2q$.

For $q=1$, take $F_1=[e_1]$ and $F_2=\operatorname{span}(e_1,\sum_{j\ne 1}e_j)$, and complete arbitrarily. The first form has two factor lines of distinct multiplicities 6 and 1, so its stabilizer is $T$. Preservation of the second plane makes all $z^{7-2j}$, $j\ne 1$, equal; the adjacent indices 2 and 3 force $z^{2}=1$. Thus the full stabilizer is exactly $C_2$. ∎

The principal-subgroup orbit statement agrees with Seppänen and Tsanov (2015, Proposition 2.2, pp. 9–10). The finite cyclic order bound and the explicit realizations are proved above.

<a id="corollary-m65h1-stabilizer-invariant-kernel-rows"></a>**Corollary M.6.5h.1 (Stabilizer-Invariant Kernel Rows).** At an orbit representative $F$ with stabilizer $H$, an equivariant kernel row is precisely an $H$-invariant probability $\nu_{F}$; the orbit rows are $K(gF,\cdot)=g_*\nu_F$. On this branch the permissible representative rows are:

- $H=B$: $\nu_F=\delta_F$.
- $H=T$: an arbitrary probability on the $8!$ $T$-fixed flags, after the same conjugation.
- $H=C_{2q}$: an arbitrary $C_{2q}$-invariant probability on $X$, equivalently a measure of the form $(1/(2q))\sum_{h\in C_{2q}}h_*\nu$ for an arbitrary probability $\nu$.

The formula is well-defined on the orbit exactly by stabilizer invariance. Every such row gives a continuous kernel on its single orbit. Across different orbits one must additionally impose Borel measurability, and for a global Feller kernel weak continuity. Orbitwise choices need not satisfy these conditions.

**Proof of invariant-law assertions.** For T, a positive diagonal element has distinct eigenvalues on V. Every subspace has a coordinate limit under its positive powers: the largest Plücker-weight part is decomposable and invariant, hence is a coordinate subspace. Equal exterior-power weights do not invalidate this argument. Recurrence forces every invariant probability onto the finite fixed set Z. For B, its unipotent subgroup fixes only o; invariance of the resulting atomic law kills every other coordinate atom. The finite case is exactly finite averaging. ∎

**Wronski data for full flags.** 
Identify $V$ with sections $H^0(\mathbb{P}^1,\mathcal{O}(7))$, or in one affine chart with polynomials of degree at most 7. The invariant alternating form on $\mathbb{C}^{2}$ identifies the defining representation with its dual, so this section model differs from the symmetric-tensor model only by a fixed equivariant identification. All conclusions are transported by that identification.

For a $k$-plane $W$ with basis $f_1,\ldots,f_k$ define its projective Wronskian

\[
\mathcal W_k(W)=[\det(f_i^{(j-1)})_{i,j=1}^k]
\in \mathbb P H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(m_k)),
\qquad m_k=k(8-k).
\]

The affine polynomial is homogenized to degree $m_{k}$, so its divisor includes any zero at infinity. It never vanishes identically for independent polynomials. One proof puts a basis into distinct-degree echelon form; its leading Wronskian coefficient is the product of nonzero leading coefficients and a Vandermonde determinant in the distinct degrees.

For a fractional linear coordinate change $\phi(z)=(az+b)/(cz+d)$, an $\mathcal{O}(7)$ section transforms as $(cz+d)^7f(\phi(z))$. Successive chain rules give a triangular derivative change: the determinant multiplier is

\[
(cz+d)^{7k}(\phi'(z))^{k(k-1)/2}
=(cz+d)^{k(8-k)}
\]

when $ad-bc=1$. Thus the homogenized Wronskian is a well-defined equivariant section of $\mathcal{O}(m_k)$, up to its basis-dependent nonzero scalar. This calculation also verifies the point-at-infinity convention.

At a point $a$, choose a local coordinate $z$ with $a=0$ and a basis of $W$ with distinct increasing vanishing orders $r_1<\cdots<r_k$. The leading determinant calculation gives

\[
\operatorname{ord}_a\mathcal W_k(W)
=\sum_{i=1}^k r_i-\frac{k(k-1)}2. \tag{M.6.5i.1}
\]

Indeed, after factoring the leading powers, the determinant of the falling factorials $(r_i)_{j-1}$ is the Vandermonde product $\prod_{i<j}(r_j-r_i)$, which is nonzero. The same proof holds in the coordinate $z=1/w$ at infinity.

Now use the positive diagonal one-parameter subgroup acting, up to a common scalar, as $f(z)\mapsto f(e^{-t}z)$. As $t\to\infty$, $W$ tends to the coordinate subspace spanned by the monomials $z^{r_i}$. Applied to all spaces of a full flag $F$, the resulting nested coordinate subspaces form a coordinate flag. Write this Borel limit map as $\pi(F)\in Z$. For a change of coordinate $h_{a}$ bringing $a$ to zero, write $\pi_a(F)=\pi(h_aF)$. Thus $\pi_a(F)$ records all of the local vanishing-order sets, and hence all multiplicities in (M.6.5i.1). Its fibers are locally closed Schubert cells; in particular $\pi_{a}$ is Borel.

<a id="lemma-m65h2-successive-wronski-reconstruction"></a>**Lemma M.6.5h.2 (Successive Wronski Reconstruction).** The full tuple

\[
F\longmapsto(\mathcal W_1(F_1),\ldots,\mathcal W_7(F_7)) \tag{M.6.5i.2}
\]

is injective.

**Proof.** The first component is $F_{1}$ itself. Suppose $F_{k−1}$ is known and choose a basis $f_1,\ldots,f_{k-1}$. The linear map

\[
f\longmapsto\operatorname{Wr}(f_1,\ldots,f_{k-1},f)
\]

has kernel exactly $F_{k−1}$, by polynomial Wronskian nonvanishing. Its projective value therefore determines the one-dimensional subspace $F_k/F_{k-1}$. Induction reconstructs every $F_{k}$. ∎

Wronski equivariance and the polynomial-subspace framework are treated in Crooks and Milson (2009), especially Theorem 4.3. Lemma M.6.5h.2 uses the full tuple of Wronskians; the Wronski map of a single Grassmannian is not injective.

<a id="theorem-m65i-quantitative-global-feller-rigidity"></a>**Theorem M.6.5i (Quantitative Global Feller Rigidity).** Let K be any G-equivariant Feller Markov kernel on X. Set

\[
\epsilon(K)=\max_{z\in Z}\bigl[1-K(z,\{z\})\bigr].
\]

Then

\[
\sup_{F\in X}\bigl[1-K(F,\{F\})\bigr]\le84\epsilon(K),
\qquad \|K-I\|_{C(X)\to C(X)}\le168\epsilon(K). \tag{M.6.5i.3}
\]

In particular, a global equivariant Feller kernel fixing every coordinate flag is the identity on the entire flag manifold.

**Proof.** Fix $F$ and let $\mu=K(F,\cdot)$. Let $A(F)$ be the union of the divisors' supports of its seven Wronskians. Their degrees sum to

\[
\sum_{k=1}^7k(8-k)=7+12+15+16+15+12+7=84,
\]

so $|A(F)|\le 84$, including infinity. For $a\in A(F)$, let $z_a=\pi_a(F)$. For each continuous test $f$,

\[
\begin{aligned}
\int f(\pi_a(Y))\,\mu(dY)
&=\lim_{t\to\infty}\int f(a_t h_aY)\,\mu(dY)\\
&=\lim_{t\to\infty}Kf(a_t h_aF)
=Kf(z_a).
\end{aligned} \tag{M.6.5i.4}
\]

The first equality is dominated convergence: every flag has the stated diagonal limit. The second is covariance, and the last is the Feller property. Thus $(\pi_a)_*\mu=K(z_a,\cdot)$. This equality is of Borel probabilities, not just formal limits of atoms. Consequently

\[
\mu\{Y:\pi_a(Y)=\pi_a(F)\}=K(z_a,\{z_a\})\ge1-\epsilon(K).
\]

By the union bound, all these at most 84 equalities hold simultaneously with probability at least $1-84\epsilon(K)$. For any such $Y$, formula (M.6.5i.1) gives the same vanishing multiplicities for every $W_{k}$ at every root of $W_k(F_k)$. Both sections have divisor degree $m_{k}$, so their divisors are identical, with no additional roots possible. Sections of the same line bundle $\mathcal{O}(m_k)$ with identical divisor are proportional. Lemma M.6.5h.2 now gives $Y=F$, proving the first bound.

For a probability $\mu$ and point $F$, the total-variation norm of $\mu-\delta_F$ is $2[1-\mu(\{F\})]$. The norm as a functional on $C(X)$ is the same by regularity and the Riesz representation theorem. Taking the supremum over $F$ proves the operator-norm bound. ∎

The proof uses all flags, every Borel row law, and all root multiplicities. It makes no smooth-core, diffusion, finite-support or bounded-jump assumption. The estimate is one-sided: distinct nonidentity kernels can have the same restriction to Z (Proposition M.6.5k).

<a id="theorem-m65j-automatic-boundedness-of-covariant-feller-generators"></a>**Theorem M.6.5j (Automatic Boundedness of Covariant Feller Generators).** Every strongly continuous $G$-equivariant Feller Markov semigroup $(P_{t})$ on $C(X)$ is uniformly continuous. Its closed generator $A$ is bounded on all of $C(X)$. It is exactly a bounded conservative jump generator:

\[
Af(F)=\int_{X\setminus\{F\}}[f(Y)-f(F)]q(F,dY), \tag{M.6.5j.1}
\]

where $q$ is a nonnegative Borel kernel of uniformly bounded total mass, $q(F,\{F\})=0$, $q(gF,gE)=q(F,E)$, and

\[
F\longmapsto\int[f(Y)-f(F)]q(F,dY)
\quad\hbox{is continuous for every }f\in C(X). \tag{M.6.5j.2}
\]

Conversely, every $q$ with these properties generates a $G$-equivariant uniformly continuous Feller Markov semigroup. There are no additional semigroup-compatibility conditions. The canonical off-diagonal $q$ in (M.6.5j.1) is unique. Its exit rates $a(F)=q(F,X)$ satisfy

\[
\sup_Fa(F)\le84\max_{z\in Z}a(z),\qquad
\|A\|=2\sup_Fa(F)\le168\max_{z\in Z}a(z). \tag{M.6.5j.3}
\]

At $B$-stabilizer flags $q=0$. At a $T$-stabilizer flag $q$ is supported on its finite fixed-flag set with its own diagonal removed. At $C_{2q}$-stabilizer flags $q$ is an arbitrary invariant finite measure off the diagonal, subject to the global boundedness and continuity conditions (M.6.5j.2).

**Proof.** For $z\in Z$, covariance makes $P_t(z,\cdot)$ $T$-invariant, hence supported on $Z$ by Corollary M.6.5h.1. Choose for each $z$ a continuous function $f_{z}$ equal to 1 at $z$ and 0 at every other member of $Z$. Strong continuity gives $P_tf_z(z)\to 1$, which is exactly $P_t(z,\{z\})\to 1$. There are finitely many $z$, so $\epsilon(P_t)\to 0$. Theorem M.6.5i yields $\lVert P_t-I\rVert\to 0$. The standard norm-continuous semigroup theorem then gives a bounded, everywhere-defined generator $A$.

The norm-continuous semigroup implication is Engel and Nagel (2000, Theorem I.3.7). The jump representation follows from positivity. Evaluation $Af(F)$ is a signed finite measure $\alpha_{F}$ by Riesz representation, with $\alpha_F(X)=A1(F)=0$. For $f\ge 0$ with $f(F)=0$, differentiating $P_tf(F)\ge 0$ at zero gives $Af(F)\ge 0$. Hence the negative part of $\alpha_{F}$ is supported on $\{F\}$. Its restriction $q(F,\cdot)$ to $X\setminus\{F\}$ is nonnegative, and $\alpha_F=q(F,\cdot)-a(F)\delta_F$. The signed-measure field $\alpha_{F}$ is weakly continuous and bounded in variation. To verify measurability of its moving diagonal, fix a compatible metric $d$ on $X$ and use $\phi_m(F,Y)=\max(0,1-m\,d(F,Y))$. The functions $F\mapsto\int\phi_m(F,Y)\alpha_F(dY)$ are continuous and converge to $\alpha_F(\{F\})$, so the latter is Borel. Standard bounded monotone-class approximation also makes $F\mapsto\alpha_F(E)$ Borel for every Borel $E$. Thus $q(F,E)=\alpha_F(E)-\alpha_F(\{F\})1_E(F)$ is a Borel kernel, with $a(F)\le\lVert A\rVert/2$. Equivariance of $A$ gives that of $q$. Equation (M.6.5j.2) is exactly the already-established fact that $Af$ is continuous.

Conversely, let $M\ge\sup_Fa(F)$, with $M>0$, and define the kernel

\[
K(F,dY)=M^{-1}q(F,dY)+(1-a(F)/M)\delta_F(dY).
\]

It is a positive normalized Borel kernel; (M.6.5j.2) makes $Kf=f+Af/M$ continuous. Thus $K$ is Feller and equivariant, and

\[
P_t=e^{tA}=e^{-Mt}\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}\frac{(Mt)^r}{r!}K^r \tag{M.6.5j.4}
\]

converges in operator norm to a covariant Markov Feller semigroup. The zero-rate case gives the identity. This proves both sufficiency and the absence of an extra Chapman–Kolmogorov gate once q is specified.

The finite set $Z$ is closed under every $P_{t}$, so restriction gives a finite-state continuous-time Markov chain. Its diagonal deficits obey $1-P_t(z,\{z\})=t\,a(z)+o(t)$, uniformly on finite $Z$. Divide (M.6.5i.3) by $t$ and use operator-norm differentiability at zero. This gives $\lVert A\rVert\le 168\max_Za$. Riesz evaluation of $\alpha_{F}$ gives $\lVert A\rVert=\sup_F\lVert\alpha_F\rVert=2\sup_Fa$, proving (M.6.5j.3). ∎

**Local-dynamics consequence.** Every generator in this full class that is local is zero. It suffices to assume $Af(F)=0$ whenever a smooth $f$ vanishes on a neighborhood of $F$. Indeed, a nonnegative smooth $f$ supported away from $F$ has $Af(F)=\int f(Y)q(F,dY)=0$. Such functions detect every positive measure on $X\setminus\{F\}$, so $q(F,\cdot)=0$ for every $F$. In particular no nonzero drift or diffusion differential operator can generate an exactly $G$-equivariant Feller semigroup on this full carrier. This is a consequence of the unrestricted Feller theorem, not a restriction of the classification to a smooth core. Nonlocal duality and reset jumps remain allowed.

The same proof supplies a finite uniformization budget: if $a_Z=\max_{z\in Z}a(z)>0$, equation (M.6.5j.4) may use the single Poisson rate $M=84a_Z$. The expected number of candidate jumps in a time interval of length $t$ is at most $84a_Zt$.

Theorem M.6.5j classifies the entire C0 Feller generator class on this branch structurally, with explicit stabilizer rows and a finite escape-rate bound. The cross-orbit continuity condition (M.6.5j.2) is a genuine restriction on orbitwise data, so the global weakly continuous kernel fields are characterized by it, not parametrized.

<a id="proposition-m65k-global-root-and-diffuse-reset-kernels"></a>**Proposition M.6.5k (Global Root and Diffuse Reset Kernels).** On the same full flag branch, the following constructions give global covariant Feller Markov kernels and bounded jump semigroups. Covariant Feller kernels are therefore not exhausted by the identity and the duality of Theorem M.6.5d, and their rows need not have finite support.

**Root-factor reset.**

Write a nonzero $v$ spanning $F_{1}$ as the symmetric product $v=\ell_1\cdots\ell_7$, with projective factor lines counted with multiplicity. Let $c(\ell)$ be the osculating flag with first line $\ell^{7}$. Define

\[
R(F,\cdot)=\frac17\sum_{i=1}^7\delta_{c(\ell_i)}. \tag{M.6.5k.1}
\]

The multiplication map $\operatorname{Sym}^7(\mathbb{P}^1)\to\mathbb{P}(\operatorname{Sym}^7\mathbb{C}^{2})$ is continuous and bijective by unique factorization; compactness of the domain and the Hausdorff target make it a homeomorphism. Therefore the empirical factor law varies weakly continuously, including multiple roots and factors at infinity. Multiplication is $G$-equivariant, so $R$ is a global covariant Feller kernel.

For $F=c(\ell)$, all factors equal $\ell$ and $R(F)=\delta_F$. Hence $R^{2}=R$ and

\[
e^{\lambda t(R-I)}=e^{-\lambda t}I+(1-e^{-\lambda t})R \tag{M.6.5k.2}
\]

is a nonzero global covariant semigroup for $\lambda>0$. For a flag outside $C$, both $F$ and $D_{\mathrm{BF}}$ lie outside $C$, whereas $R(F)$ is supported on $C$. Thus $R$ is not a convex combination of the identity and bilinear duality at that flag. The duality generator of Theorem M.6.5d is a further member of the class.

**Diffuse reset and nonuniqueness at fixed coordinate rows.**

Identify $\mathbb{P}^1$ with the boundary sphere of hyperbolic 3-space. For a seven-atom empirical probability $\mu=(1/7)\sum\delta_{\ell_i}$, either every atom has mass at most $3/7$, or there is a unique atom of mass at least $4/7$. In the first case let $b(\mu)$ be its unique conformal barycenter in the open hyperbolic ball. In the second case let $b(\mu)$ be that majority point on the boundary.

Existence, uniqueness and Möbius equivariance of the interior barycenter follow from Cantarella and Schumacher (2022, Theorem 5.9) and the defining director equation. The extension to the majority locus used here has the following direct continuity proof.

Choose representatives of convergent unordered seven-tuples that converge after relabeling. If stable barycenters $b_{j}$ have an interior limit, the equation that the seven unit directors sum to zero passes to that limit. A majority configuration cannot satisfy it: at least four directors coincide and at most three unit vectors oppose them. If $b_{j}$ approaches a boundary point $\eta$ different from the limiting majority point $\xi$, a ball isometry taking $b_{j}$ to the center sends each of the at least four roots tending to $\xi$ toward the same limiting boundary direction, uniformly away from $\eta$. Again at most three remaining unit vectors cannot cancel them. Hence $b_j\to\xi$. When the limiting configuration is stable, any proposed boundary limit $\eta$ leaves at least four of the seven roots a positive distance from $\eta$, yielding the same contradiction. Every subsequential limit is therefore interior and is the unique barycenter of the limit. Majority configurations themselves have majority points converging to the unique limiting majority point. These arguments prove continuity on the entire odd-seven configuration space.

Let $\omega_{b}$ be normalized visual (harmonic) measure on the boundary sphere viewed from $b$; at a boundary point $\xi$ set $\omega_\xi=\delta_\xi$. The map $b\mapsto\omega_b$ is weakly continuous on the closed ball and equivariant under orientation-preserving hyperbolic isometries. One direct construction is $\omega_b=g_*\omega_0$ for any $g$ taking the center to $b$; rotations fix $\omega_{0}$, so this is well-defined. As $b\to\xi$, these measures concentrate at $\xi$, giving the boundary continuity.

Define

\[
Q(F,\cdot)=c_*\omega_{b(\mu_{F_1})}. \tag{M.6.5k.3}
\]

Then $Q$ is a global equivariant Feller kernel, $Q^{2}=Q$, and it fixes $C$. Whenever the first binary form has no factor of multiplicity four or more, $Q(F)$ is non-atomic and has support all of $C$. Thus covariant Feller kernel rows need not have finite support. The generator $\lambda(Q-I)$ is bounded, as Theorem M.6.5j requires.

The finite coordinate rows do not determine such a nonidentity kernel. To see this concretely, center a stable empirical measure by a Möbius map $g$ taking the hyperbolic center to $b(\mu)$, and write $\nu=g^{-1}_*\mu$. On the round sphere let

\[
h_\nu(\eta)=\int(\eta\mathbin\cdot\xi)^2\nu(d\xi)-\tfrac13,
\qquad r_{\nu,\theta}(\eta)=1+\theta h_\nu(\eta),\quad |\theta|\le1.
\]

The density $r$ is normalized, lies between $1/3$ and $5/3$, and rotates equivariantly with $\nu$. Thus $g_*(r_{\nu,\theta}\omega_0)$ is independent of the centering choice, continuous on the stable configurations, and Möbius-equivariant. At a majority configuration define it to be the majority point mass. Its extension is continuous: the uniformly bounded centered densities are dominated by $(5/3)\omega_0$, while $g_*\omega_0$ concentrates at the majority point. Pushing to $C$ gives another idempotent Feller reset $Q_\theta$. All $Q_\theta$ have exactly the same rows on $Z$, since the first line of a coordinate flag has two factor multiplicities summing to seven and therefore a unique majority. They are not all equal: take seven equally spaced equatorial points, already centered; their second-moment matrix is $\operatorname{diag}(1/2,1/2,0)$, so $h_\nu$ is not identically zero. More generally $\theta$ can be replaced by any continuous rotation-invariant scalar function of the centered configuration with absolute value at most one. This provides genuine compatible freedom not visible in the finite boundary rows.

<a id="proposition-m65l-unbounded-covariant-total-variation-law-semigroup"></a>**Proposition M.6.5l (Unbounded Covariant Total-Variation Law Semigroup).** The law-carrier clause of Definition M.6.5a also permits the following non-Feller example with an unbounded generator.

The automatic boundedness of Theorem M.6.5j depends on the Feller property, as the following example in the broader law class shows.

Let $D=D_B$ be the nonidentity equivariant involution of Theorem M.6.5d. Choose finite-stabilizer flags $F_{m}$ outside $\operatorname{Fix}(D)$, such that the $G$-orbit/duality pairs

\[
E_m=GF_m\cup GD F_m
\]

are pairwise disjoint. Such a sequence exists: $X$ has complex dimension 28, each $G$-orbit dimension at most 3, and $\operatorname{Fix}(D)$ is a proper closed subset. Algebraic orbits are locally closed and Borel. Let $\lambda=m$ on $E_{m}$ and $\lambda=0$ elsewhere. This is a finite-valued-at-every-point, unbounded, $G$-invariant and $D$-invariant Borel function.

For all finite signed Borel measures $\mu$ define

\[
P_t^*\mu=\tfrac12(1+e^{-2t\lambda})\mu
             +\tfrac12(1-e^{-2t\lambda})D_*\mu. \tag{M.6.5l.1}
\]

Here coefficient functions multiply measures. Because $\lambda\circ D=\lambda$, the formula is a semigroup. It is positive and preserves total mass. It commutes with every $G$-pushforward. Moreover

\[
\|P_t^*\mu-\mu\|_{TV}
\le\int(1-e^{-2t\lambda})\,d|\mu|\longrightarrow0
\]

by dominated convergence, so it is strongly continuous on the entire Banach space $M(X)$ with total-variation norm.

Writing $\mu^-=(\mu-D_*\mu)/2$, its generator has domain

\[
\mathcal D(A^*)=\{\mu:\int\lambda\,d|\mu^-|<\infty\},
\qquad A^*\mu=-2\lambda\mu^-.
\]

The finite-rate truncations show density of this domain, and the multiplication-operator description gives closedness. The odd atomic measure $\delta_{F_m}-\delta_{DF_m}$ is an eigenvector of eigenvalue $-2m$, so the generator is unbounded. Its kernels cannot all be Feller: if they were, pointwise stochastic continuity plus the finite coordinate-flag argument and Theorem M.6.5i would give uniform operator continuity and a bounded generator, contradicting these eigenvalues. More directly, every coordinate-flag orbit has stabilizer $T$ or $B$, so if the $F_{m}$ are chosen with finite stabilizer, all of $Z$ is fixed by these kernels, yet nonidentity rows exist; Theorem M.6.5i excludes Feller continuity of each nonzero-time kernel.

Thus the law-carrier clause of Definition M.6.5a cannot be identified with the Feller branch without an additional premise.

<a id="proposition-m65m-conditional-bridge-capacity-bound"></a>**Proposition M.6.5m (Conditional Bridge Capacity Bound).** 
Definition M.6.5a does not require $J$ to cover all flags or all signed-law modes; it does not impose a uniform preimage bound or a separating readout family. It specifies only finitely many readouts, and it does not declare $H$ finite-dimensional. Moreover, its tested inequality is not the operator identity $G^\Sigma J=J\widehat G$. Without these hypotheses the unbounded example gives no no-go theorem for the certificates of Definition M.6.5a.

There is nevertheless an exact conditional capacity bound. Suppose a particular certificate has a bounded lift $\widehat G$ and covers the normalized atoms of the example by $J\psi_m=\delta_{F_m}$. Put

\[
c_m=|s_P(\delta_{F_m}-\delta_{DF_m})|,
\qquad C_P=\|\ell_P\mathfrak q_{\rm PPI}\widehat G\|+\epsilon_{\rm br}(P).
\]

Then the source's actual bridge inequality and $G^\Sigma\delta_{F_m}=-m(\delta_{F_m}-\delta_{DF_m})$ imply

\[
m c_m\le C_P\|\psi_m\|. \tag{M.6.5m.1}
\]

If $c_m\ge c>0$ and the source vectors have uniformly bounded norms, a fixed bounded lift and finite fixed tolerance cannot cover every $m$. Otherwise their necessary norms grow at least linearly, $\lVert\psi_m\rVert\ge mc/C_P$ when $C_{P}>0$. For odd-law modes $J\psi_m=\delta_{F_m}-\delta_{DF_m}$, the same argument has $2m$ in place of $m$.
