A finite-dimensional linear lift is automatically bounded; infinite-dimensional unbounded common-core lifts are not covered by this bound.

If an actually retained readout has the form $s_P(\mu)=\int f\,d\mu$ with continuous $f$ and $f(F)\ne f(DF)$ somewhere, continuity supplies an open region with a fixed positive $c$. Infinitely many finite-stabilizer orbit pairs can be selected there, making the $c_m\ge c$ premise nonempty. Definition M.6.5a requires neither such a readout nor that $J$ reach those atoms, so (M.6.5m.1) constrains exactly the realizations that cover these atoms.

Let $\rho:SL(2,\mathbb C)\to GL(V)$ be a holomorphic representation on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space, $d=\dim V$, and let $X=\operatorname{Fl}(V)$ be its full complete-flag manifold. Say that $\rho$ has the automatic boundedness property if every $\rho$-equivariant $C_0$ Feller Markov semigroup on $C(X)$ is norm-continuous, equivalently has a bounded everywhere-defined generator.

<a id="theorem-m65n-holomorphic-representation-dichotomy-for-full-flag-feller-dynamics"></a>**Theorem M.6.5n (Holomorphic Representation Dichotomy for Full-Flag Feller Dynamics).** The automatic boundedness property holds if and only if $\rho$ is irreducible. More precisely:

1. For irreducible $\rho\cong\operatorname{Sym}^{d-1}(\mathbb C^{2})$, put $N_d=\binom{d+1}{3}$. With $Z$ the $d!$ flags of a weight basis, every equivariant Feller Markov kernel satisfies

\[
\sup_F[1-K(F,\{F\})]\le N_d\max_{z\in Z}[1-K(z,\{z\})],
\qquad \|K-I\|\le2N_d\max_{z\in Z}[1-K(z,\{z\})].
\]

Every $C_0$ equivariant Feller generator is consequently a bounded conservative jump generator of the form and with the exact compensated-continuity condition in Theorem M.6.5j. Its exit rates satisfy $\sup_Fa(F)\le N_d\max_Za(z)$. Every local generator in this class is zero. The $d=1$ carrier is a singleton and all generators are zero; for $d=2$ the stronger celestial identity-kernel theorem applies.

2. If $\rho$ is reducible, there is a nonzero, unbounded, local generator of a covariant C0 Feller semigroup on the entire flag manifold, with continuous sample paths. One may choose a nontrivial invariant projection P and use

\[
U_\theta=e^{i\theta P},\qquad
F_t=U_{\sqrt{2c}W_t}F_0,\qquad A=cX_P^2,
\]

where $c>0$, $W_t$ is standard real Brownian motion and $X_{P}$ is the infinitesimal field of the circle action $U_\theta$.

**Proof of complete reducibility and the irreducible model.** Average a Hermitian inner product over $\rho(SU(2))$. For every $G$-invariant subspace, its orthogonal complement is $SU(2)$-invariant; holomorphicity makes the derived action complex-linear, so the complement is invariant under the complexification $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$, hence under the connected group $G$. Iteration gives a direct sum of irreducibles. For an irreducible module, the standard highest-weight chain $v,Fv,\ldots,F^nv$ obeys $EF^kv=k(n-k+1)F^{k-1}v$. Termination forces $n$ to be a nonnegative integer, and irreducibility makes this chain the whole module. Its matrices are those of $\operatorname{Sym}^n(\mathbb C^{2})$, with $d=n+1$. These standard facts are in Conrad (n.d., Theorem 3.1 and the subsequent symmetric-power and complete-reducibility discussion).

**Proof of item 1.** The proof of M.6.5i is dimension-independent. In the polynomial model of degree at most $d-1$, the $k$-th Wronskian is a nonzero homogeneous section of degree $k(d-k)$. At every point of $\mathbb{P}^1$ its vanishing multiplicity is the sum of its local pivot orders minus $k(k-1)/2$, including infinity. The full tuple of successive Wronskians reconstructs the flag by the same polynomial-kernel induction. The number of distinct roots to probe is at most

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{d-1}k(d-k)=\frac{d(d^2-1)}6=\binom{d+1}3=N_d.
\]

Every probe is the limit under a conjugated diagonal one-parameter subgroup. Equivariance, dominated convergence and Feller continuity identify the pushforward row law at its coordinate limit; the same positive union bound gives the displayed estimate. All torus-invariant probabilities are supported on finite $Z$ because the $d$ weights are distinct. Thus strong continuity at finitely many coordinate rows forces the right-hand side to zero as $t\to 0$. The generator, jump representation, exit-rate bound and no-local-dynamics conclusion follow exactly as in M.6.5j. If $d=1$, $X$ has one point and the assertion is immediate.

**Proof of item 2.** Choose a proper nonzero invariant subspace and its invariant orthogonal complement from the averaged inner product. The orthogonal projection $P$ onto the first summand commutes with $\rho(G)$, and $0<\operatorname{rank}P<d$. Hence $U_\theta$ is a smooth nontrivial compact circle action commuting with $G$ on all flags. Gaussian convolution of this action is a positive unital contraction semigroup. Independent Brownian increments give its semigroup law; continuity of the circle action on compact $X$ and concentration of the Gaussian at zero give the Feller property and strong continuity on $C(X)$. Its paths are continuous, covariance is exact, and Taylor expansion in $\theta$ gives generator $cX_P^{2}$ on every smooth function.

If determinant-one matrices are desired for context transport, replace P by P−(rank P/d)I. This changes only a scalar phase and hence leaves the entire flag process unchanged.

To prove nontriviality and unboundedness, take nonzero $v\in\operatorname{im}P$ and $w\in\ker P$ and a flag whose first line is $[v+w]$. If $U_\theta$ preserves this line, comparison of its $v$ and $w$ components gives $e^{i\theta}=1$. Thus this flag has an embedded circle orbit with trivial circle stabilizer. At every $t>0$ its transition row is non-atomic, since the wrapped Gaussian has a continuous density on the circle. Hence $P_t(F,\{F\})=0$, and the Riesz total-variation formula gives $\lVert P_t-I\rVert=2$ for every $t>0$. Thus the $C_0$ Feller semigroup is not norm-continuous and its generator is unbounded. Equivalently, smooth extensions of $e^{im\theta}$ from this embedded orbit have sup norm at most one and generator values of magnitude $cm^{2}$ on the orbit. Its differential formula is local and nonzero. If the original Hilbert metric differs from the averaged one, the same flag-space construction is conjugate by a fixed invertible change of basis; Feller continuity and boundedness of generators are unchanged by the induced isometry between the corresponding $C(X)$ spaces. ∎

<a id="corollary-m65o-covariant-full-flag-diffusions-for-the-ten-three-spin-extensions"></a>**Corollary M.6.5o (Covariant Full-Flag Diffusions for the Ten Three-Spin Extensions).** Every reducible finite-dimensional continuous complex-linear representation of the real Lorentz spin group admits the commuting-projection diffusion of Theorem M.6.5n. In particular all ten classes in Proposition M.6.5f do.

Holomorphicity is essential to the irreducible direction just proved. A general finite-dimensional complex-linear representation of the real group $SL(2,\mathbb C)$ may be an irreducible mixed-chiral representation $(j_L,j_R)$, with both labels nonzero; it is not the single symmetric-power polynomial model. No automatic-boundedness assertion for such irreducibles follows from the Wronski proof.

The reducible construction only needs a proper invariant direct summand, not holomorphicity. Finite-dimensional complex representations of the real Lorentz spin group are completely reducible by the compact-form argument for $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$ used in M.6.5f. Therefore every reducible representation in that class admits the circle diffusion above. In an inner-product-compatible direct-sum representative its projection can be orthogonal; in any equivalent representative, use the conjugate idempotent and transport the same compact circle action.

All ten eight-dimensional Lorentz-extension classes in M.6.5f are reducible: the six first-family classes contain their four-dimensional chiral spin-3/2 summand plus two Weyl halves, and the four second-family classes contain a six-dimensional mixed-chiral summand plus a Weyl half. Thus every one of the ten mathematical flag actions admits a nonzero covariant Feller diffusion with unbounded generator. The projection may depend on the chosen full-carrier extension/intertwiner; rotation data alone do not identify it. On the all-left extension one may use a projection onto the spin-3/2 sector, or a nontrivial multiplicity projection.

<a id="proposition-m65p-auxiliary-common-core-law-space-realization"></a>**Proposition M.6.5p (Auxiliary Common-Core Law-Space Realization).** For the reducible circle diffusion, choose an inner product making $P$ orthogonal and let $\mu$ be normalized $U(d)$-invariant smooth volume on $X$. The circle $U_\theta$ preserves $\mu$. Define

\[
\mathcal H_{\rm aux}=L^2(X,\mu;\mathbb C),\qquad
\mathcal D=C^\infty(X;\mathbb C).
\]

For the flag diffeomorphism induced by g, let

\[
r_g(y)=\frac{d(g_*\mu)}{d\mu}(y)
=\operatorname{Jac}_{\mu}(g^{-1})(y)>0,
\qquad R_g\psi(y)=r_g(y)\psi(g^{-1}y).
\]

The Jacobian chain rule gives $R_gR_h=R_{gh}$; every $R_{g}$ preserves $\mathcal D$, has inverse $R_{g^{-1}}$, and is bounded on $L^{2}$, with

\[
\|R_g\psi\|_2^2
=\int r_g(gx)|\psi(x)|^2\,d\mu(x)
\le\|r_g\|_\infty\|\psi\|_2^2.
\]

All Jacobians and inverse Jacobians are smooth and bounded on compact X. These are in general nonunitary bounded invertible operators, as Definition M.6.5a allows.

Choose the ordered law carrier

\[
\mathcal X_\Sigma=L^1(X,\mu;\mathbb R),\quad
\mathcal X_{\Sigma,+}=\{f\ge0\},\quad n(f)=\int f\,d\mu.
\]

Its cone is closed and generating, and $n$ is continuous. Density pushforward $R_{g}$ is positive, mass-preserving and isometric on $L^{1}$. The Brownian circle-pushforward semigroup $Q_{t}$ is a positive mass-preserving $C_0$ contraction there. Its generator $G_\Sigma$ is the closed generator with full domain $\mathcal D_\Sigma=\mathcal D(G_\Sigma)$, and $G_\Sigma f=cX_P^{2}f$ for smooth real $f$. Brownian symmetry makes the forward density and backward function differential expressions the same here.

The space $C^\infty$ is a graph core for the circle generator on $L^{1}$ and $L^{2}$. To see this, smooth with the heat semigroup of a $U(d)$-invariant Laplacian on the flag manifold. It commutes with every $U_\theta$ and hence with $Q_{t}$, maps $L^{1}$ and $L^{2}$ into $C^\infty$ at positive times, and tends strongly to the identity. For $f$ in the generator domain, this smoothing also commutes with $G_\Sigma$, so it converges in the graph norm. On $L^{2}$ the same argument applies.

The chosen L¹ carrier matters: the dual transition semigroup on all finite measures is not strongly continuous in total variation at an atom on a free circle orbit, since its positive-time row has no atom there. It nevertheless acts on all Borel laws as a Markov transition semigroup. No total-variation C0 claim on all measures is made for this diffusion.

Make the following explicit auxiliary choices:

\[
\widehat G_{\rm aux}=cX_P^2:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D,
\quad J\psi=\operatorname{Re}\psi,
\quad \mathcal R_{\rm aux}=\mathcal H_{\rm aux},
\quad \mathfrak q_{\rm aux}=I.
\]

Here $J$ is a real-linear bridge, with the complex Hilbert space regarded as a real vector space for this map; it is not complex-linear. Thus $J$ maps $\mathcal D$ into $\mathcal D_\Sigma$, and $q_{\mathrm{aux}}$ is bounded and surjective with zero invariant kernel. Choose any finite smooth partition of unity $p_j\ge 0$, $\sum_j p_j=1$, and define

\[
s_j(f)=\int p_jf\,d\mu,\qquad
\ell_j(\psi)=\operatorname{Re}\int p_j\psi\,d\mu.
\]

Then $\lVert s_j\rVert\le\lVert p_j\rVert_\infty$ on $L^{1}$ and $\lVert\ell_j\rVert\le\lVert p_j\rVert_2$ on $L^{2}$. Their $s_{j}$ outputs are normalized probabilities for every nonnegative mass-one law. They obey the exact tested bridge equation

\[
s_j(G_\Sigma J\psi)
=\ell_j(\mathfrak q_{\rm aux}\widehat G_{\rm aux}\psi),
\qquad\psi\in\mathcal D.
\]

The construction can use nontrivial readouts. Take orthonormal $v\in\operatorname{im}P$, $w\in\ker P$ and $u=(v+w)/\sqrt2$. Let $p_1(F)=\langle u,\Pi_{F_1}u\rangle$ and $p_2=1-p_1$, where $\Pi_{F_1}$ is the orthogonal rank-one projector. On the circle with first line $[e^{i\theta}v+w]$, $p_1=(1+\cos\theta)/2$, so its generator response is nonzero.

Because the flag actions of $U_\theta$ and $g$ commute and $U_\theta$ preserves $\mu$, the chain rule also gives $r_g(U_\theta y)=r_g(y)$. It follows that $R_{g}$ commutes with circle pullbacks and with $cX_P^{2}$ on $\mathcal D$. Thus the auxiliary covariance defect is zero. On law space $JR_g=R_gJ$, and the law representation preserves the full positive normalized cone.

The bridge is also time-consistent: if $Q_t^{(2)}$ is the same circle semigroup on $L^{2}$, then $JQ_t^{(2)}=Q_tJ$. The inclusion of real parts $L^{2}\to L^{1}$ is bounded because $\mu(X)=1$, and this equality holds on all of $H_{\mathrm{aux}}$, not only on the smooth core.

This supplies the core, law-cone, finite normalized-law-readout and tested bridge entries of Definition M.6.5a with $\epsilon_{\mathrm{br}}=\epsilon_{\mathrm{cov}}=0$ for this auxiliary realization. Its quotient $q_{\mathrm{aux}}=\mathrm{id}$ is a declared comparison choice; it is not identified with the response quotient $q_{\mathrm{PPI}}$.

$H_{\mathrm{aux}}$ is a Hilbert space of densities on flags, not the quantum carrier $V$. The real-part bridge $J=\operatorname{Re}$ does not take every unit vector to a positive mass-one law and is not a Born preparation map; the normalization of the readouts $s_{j}$ refers to the $L^{1}$ probability preparations.

For Theorem M.6.5q fix $G=SL(2,\mathbb C)$, $V=\operatorname{Sym}^7(\mathbb C^2)$ and $X=\operatorname{Fl}(V)$, as in Proposition M.6.5h; the reducible actions of Corollary M.6.5o are not covered.

Use the polynomial coordinate basis $1,z,\ldots,z^7$ from the Wronski proof. Let $z_{k}$ be the coordinate flag obtained by swapping the adjacent basis elements $z^{k−1}$ and $z^{k}$ in that order, for $k=1,\ldots,7$. These are seven particular $T$-fixed flags; the reference ordering is the attracting flag for the scaling $f(z)\mapsto f(e^{-t}z)$.

<a id="theorem-m65q-seven-mathematical-test-rows-detect-the-identity-kernel"></a>**Theorem M.6.5q (Seven Mathematical Test Rows Detect the Identity Kernel).** Every global G-equivariant Feller Markov kernel K satisfies

\[
\sup_F[1-K(F,\{F\})]
\le\sum_{k=1}^7 k(8-k)[1-K(z_k,\{z_k\})].
\]

Consequently

\[
\|K-I\|\le2\sum_{k=1}^7 k(8-k)[1-K(z_k,\{z_k\})].
\]

In particular, fixing these seven rows pointwise forces $K=I$ on every flag; the seven rows do not determine a nonidentity kernel (Proposition M.6.5k).

**Proof.** There is a nonempty Zariski-open dense set U of flags for which all seven homogeneous Wronskians have simple roots and have pairwise disjoint root supports. Nonemptiness has the exact rational witness below; openness follows from discriminants and pairwise resultants. The flag variety is irreducible, being a quotient image of the irreducible open variety GL8.

For $F\in U$, a root of $W_{k}$ has multiplicity one in $W_{k}$ and zero in every other $W_{l}$. If $r_0,\ldots,r_7$ is the pivot permutation at that root, the vanishing-order formula gives

\[
\sum_{j=0}^{l-1}r_j-\frac{l(l-1)}2=\delta_{lk},
\quad l=1,\ldots,7.
\]

Subtracting consecutive equations (and using the full sum $0+\cdots+7=28$ at $l=8$) gives $r_j=j$ except $r_{k-1}=k$ and $r_k=k-1$. Thus its boost-limit flag is exactly $z_{k}$. There are $k(8-k)$ such roots. The pushforward-law identity and reconstruction proof in Theorem M.6.5i therefore give the displayed weighted union bound for every $F\in U$.

The diagonal mass $F\mapsto K(F,\{F\})$ is upper semicontinuous. Indeed, if $F_n\to F$, then $\delta_{F_n}\otimes K(F_n,\cdot)$ converges weakly to $\delta_F\otimes K(F,\cdot)$; the diagonal in $X\times X$ is closed, and the Portmanteau inequality gives the claim. Hence escape probability is lower semicontinuous. Approximate any $F$ by flags in dense $U$ to extend the same uniform bound to $F$. The operator norm identity used previously gives the second inequality. ∎

**Generator consequence.** For every generator in the full C0 Feller class,

\[
\sup_Fa(F)\le\sum_{k=1}^7k(8-k)a(z_k),
\quad
\|A\|\le2\sum_{k=1}^7k(8-k)a(z_k).
\]

Automatic boundedness itself can now be proved from strong continuity at just these seven inputs, because their rows remain supported on finite $X^T$. The displayed weighted sum is a valid single uniformization rate.

**Exact witness for the generic root condition.**

Let $f_i(z)=\sum_{j=0}^7C_{ij}z^j$, with rows of $C$ as follows:

\[
C=\begin{pmatrix}
3&0&-2&-1&-1&2&2&-1\\
3&3&-2&-2&-2&1&0&-1\\
3&2&1&-3&-1&-3&3&3\\
2&-3&-2&-3&2&-1&-3&-2\\
-3&2&3&-3&1&3&-1&1\\
-3&1&2&0&0&-2&-3&0\\
-3&3&1&-3&-1&1&-1&1\\
1&-1&0&-2&1&-3&3&-1
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Its determinant is 23,336. Use the flag $F_k=\operatorname{span}(f_1,\ldots,f_k)$. Its Wronskians are given by the finite exact formula

\[
w_k(z)=\sum_{\substack{I\subset\{0,\ldots,7\}\\|I|=k}}
\det(C_{\{1,\ldots,k\},I})
\prod_{\substack{i,j\in I\\i<j}}(j-i)
\,z^{\sum_{i\in I}i-k(k-1)/2}.
\]

Here matrix columns are indexed $0,\ldots,7$ and rows $1,\ldots,8$. This is the Cauchy–Binet expansion of the derivative determinant, with the monomial Wronskian coefficient given by the Vandermonde product. Divide each $w_{k}$ by the positive greatest common divisor of its integer coefficients and call the resulting primitive polynomial $v_{k}$. Direct integer arithmetic gives degrees 7,12,15,16,15,12,7. For $P=\prod_{k=1}^7v_k$, reduction modulo 103 gives

\[
\deg \overline P=84,\qquad
\gcd(\overline P,\overline P')=1
\quad\text{in }\mathbb F_{103}[z].
\]

These are finite checks on the displayed matrix and formula, reproducible by polynomial Euclidean division; no approximate root finding is used. Since the leading coefficient remains nonzero modulo103, the characteristic-zero discriminant of P is nonzero. Thus the seven Wronskians have simple, pairwise disjoint roots over C, with no root at infinity. This proves the nonemptiness required in the argument.

<a id="theorem-m65r"></a>

<a id="theorem-m65r-covariant-resolvent-classification-on-the-three-spin-flag-carrier"></a>**Theorem M.6.5r (Covariant Resolvent Classification on the Three-Spin Flag Carrier).** Fix $W=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes3}$ with its labeled spin tensor basis, $g\mapsto R_g=g^{\otimes3}$ for $g\in SL(2,\mathbb C)$, and the induced action on the full compact flag manifold $X=\operatorname{Fl}(W)$. The representation restricts to the rotation carrier of Theorem 7.6o through the identity intertwiner in that tensor basis. Its flag action is nontransitive: group orbits have real dimension at most six, whereas $X$ has real dimension $56$. The following parameterization covers every conservative equivariant $C_0$ Feller generator on $C(X;\mathbb R)$ and every positive mass-preserving equivariant $C_0$ generator on a fixed ordered Banach law carrier of Definition M.6.5a. The total-variation space $\mathcal M(X;\mathbb R)$ of finite signed Radon measures with flag pushforward is a particular ordered law carrier. Each branch has its own parameter and uses its own norm.

Choose a reference $\lambda_0>0$ in inverse clock units. On an ordered law carrier choose it above the proposed growth bound. In the Feller branch the parameter is an orbit seed of probability measures, one $\mu_F$ at a representative $F$ of each $SL(2,\mathbb C)$-orbit. For a basis matrix $A_F$ whose first $k$ columns span the $k$th subspace of $F$, impose invariance under the stabilizer
$$
H_F=\{g\in SL(2,\mathbb C): A_F^{-1}g^{\otimes3}A_F
\text{ is upper triangular}\}.
\tag{M.6.5r.1}
$$
This is the explicit matrix test for seed invariance in this representation. Transport the row to $gF$ by $g_*\mu_F$ and require weak continuity of all transported rows on $X$. The resulting operator $K$ sends $f\in C(X;\mathbb R)$ to its integral against each row. In the ordered branch fix the real Banach space $\mathcal X_\Sigma$, its closed generating cone, continuous normalization functional $n$, and its action $B_g$ by bounded linear cone automorphisms. The parameter is a bounded positive linear operator $K$ preserving $n$ and commuting with each $B_g$. For $\mathcal M(X;\mathbb R)$ take $n(\nu)=\nu(X)$ and $B_g=g_*$. The ordered branch uses its declared Banach norm, including when its operators have no predual on $C(X)$.

In either branch put $R=K/\lambda_0$ and require that $R$ be injective with dense range in the branch norm. Use the following tests for the two branches:

1. In the Feller branch take $\lambda_j=2^j\lambda_0$, $j\ge0$. Require that $I+(\lambda_j-\lambda_0)R$ have a bounded inverse and that
   $$
   K_{\lambda_j}=\lambda_j R[I+(\lambda_j-\lambda_0)R]^{-1}
   \tag{M.6.5r.2}
   $$
   be positive and preserve constants for every $j$.
2. In the ordered Banach branch, take constants $M\ge1$ and $0\le\omega<\lambda_0$, and let $\lambda_j=\omega+2^j(\lambda_0-\omega)$. Require the same inverses, with $K_{\lambda_j}$ positive and preserving $n$. In addition require, for $j\ge0$ and integers $k\ge1$,
   $$
   \big\|(K_{\lambda_j}/\lambda_j)^k\big\|
   \le\frac{M}{(\lambda_j-\omega)^k}.
   \tag{M.6.5r.2a}
   $$
   On the total-variation branch $M=1$, $\omega=0$ suffice by positivity and mass preservation.

Every passing parameter gives exactly one generator with its entire closed domain:
$$
D(G)=\operatorname{ran}R,\qquad G(Rf)=\lambda_0Rf-f.
\tag{M.6.5r.3}
$$
The semigroup is the strong limit of $\exp[t\lambda_j(K_{\lambda_j}-I)]$ as $j\to\infty$. Conversely, every generator in the stated classes returns the unique parameter $K=\lambda_0(\lambda_0 I-G)^{-1}$ for each reference rate $\lambda_0$ above an admitted growth bound.

*Proof.* A positive constant-preserving map on $C(X)$ is a contraction. A positive mass-preserving map on $\mathcal M(X)$ is a contraction by positive/negative measure decomposition. The same two facts apply to each passing $K_{\lambda_j}$. The stabilizer formula follows by requiring preservation of each column span, and makes the transported rows well-defined. The Riesz representation theorem identifies every positive constant-preserving map on $C(X)$ with probability rows. Continuity of its output for every continuous $f$ is exactly weak continuity of those rows. Equivariance is equivalent to invariance and transport of the seeds.

Injectivity gives a well-defined linear operator (M.6.5r.3). It is closed: if $x_i=Rf_i\to x$ and $Gx_i\to y$, then $f_i=\lambda_0x_i-Gx_i\to\lambda_0x-y$ and $x=R(\lambda_0x-y)$. Its domain is dense by the range test. Direct substitution gives $(\lambda_j I-G)^{-1}=R_j=K_{\lambda_j}/\lambda_j$. The Feller branch satisfies (M.6.5r.2a) with $M=1$, $\omega=0$.

To pass from the dyadic tests to all real resolvent rates $\eta>\omega$, choose $j$ with $\lambda_j\ge\eta$ and put $d_j=\lambda_j-\eta$. The power bounds show that $\sum_{m\ge0}d_j^mR_j^m$ converges in norm, since $d_j/(\lambda_j-\omega)<1$. Thus $\eta I-G$ has inverse $R_\eta=\sum_{m\ge0}d_j^mR_j^{m+1}$, a positive operator. Applying the constants or mass identity to the series gives $\eta R_\eta 1=1$ in the Feller case or $n(\eta R_\eta x)=n(x)$ in the ordered case. For $k\ge1$, the power series has nonnegative binomial coefficients, so
$$
\|R_\eta^k\|\le
\frac{M}{(\lambda_j-\omega)^k}
\sum_{m\ge0}\binom{k+m-1}{m}
\left(\frac{d_j}{\lambda_j-\omega}\right)^m
=\frac{M}{(\eta-\omega)^k}.
\tag{M.6.5r.4}
$$
The Hille–Yosida theorem now gives the strongly continuous semigroup with growth bound $M e^{\omega t}$ and the Yosida approximation above. For each $j$, the approximation is the norm-convergent series $e^{-\lambda_jt}\sum_{m\ge0}(\lambda_jt)^m K_{\lambda_j}^m/m!$. Hence positivity and the normalization identity pass to the strong limit by the closed cone and continuity of the functional. Equivariance passes to the limit because the approximants commute with the fixed bounded group operators. Conversely, each strongly continuous semigroup has an exponential norm bound, and the positive conservative Feller and total-variation semigroups are contractive. Its Laplace resolvents are positive and obey the stated conservation after multiplication by their rate. The resolvent power bound follows by integrating the semigroup against $t^{k-1}e^{-\lambda t}/(k-1)!$. The generator resolvent is injective with dense range, and the resolvent identity gives (M.6.5r.2). This proves uniqueness of the normalized resolvent at the given rate and the formula for the entire domain. ∎

<a id="theorem-m65s-three-spin-response-quotient-and-covariant-flag-readout"></a>**Theorem M.6.5s (Three-Spin Response Quotient and Covariant Flag Readout).** On the same extension and full flag manifold of Theorem M.6.5r, let $V$ interchange the $M$ and $P$ spin factors. For a flag $F$ let $P_F$ be the orthogonal rank-one projector onto its first line in the material Hilbert metric. Let $\mu$ be normalized $U(8)$-invariant measure on $X$. Put $d=8$, $X_Y=\operatorname{Re}_{\rm H}(\mathfrak q_{\rm PPI}Y)=(\mathfrak q_{\rm PPI}Y+(\mathfrak q_{\rm PPI}Y)^*)/2$, and define the real-linear bridge
$$
JY(dF)=\big[d(d+1)\operatorname{tr}(X_Y P_F)-d\operatorname{tr}(X_Y)\big]\mu(dF).
\tag{M.6.5s.2}

For any material effect $0\le E\le I_W$ use
$$
s_E(\nu)=\int_X\operatorname{tr}(EP_F)\,\nu(dF),\qquad
\ell_E(X)=\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(EX).
\tag{M.6.5s.3}

The retained menu selects a checkpoint in a declared finite schedule and one terminal binary effect. It uses the projectors onto the tensor coordinate vectors and the normalized sums $e_i+e_j$ and $e_i+i e_j$ for $i<j$, each with its complement, including the identity readout for normalization. *Proof.* Each $V$ commutes with $g^{\otimes3}$ because the same matrix acts on all three factors. The Poisson mixture $\exp[t\gamma(V_*-I)]$ is conservative and bounded on the two law branches. This verifies (M.6.5a.1) with zero defect and proves quotient invariance. Partial trace is bounded and onto, since every reduced operator can be tensored with a fixed surplus state. The listed binary effects span the Hermitian matrices, by subtracting diagonal terms from the two superposition projectors. The menu includes the preparation checkpoint, so equality of all its responses forces equality of reduced states by this span. Conversely, condition on the public clock record at any allowed checkpoint. The prepared operator is then conjugated by a known power of $V$ on the retained factor. A conditional Born probability therefore factors through $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal K}Y$, and multiplying by the state-independent probability of the public record proves the full finite response identity, including overflow records. Write $\mathcal M_1(\nu)=\int P_F\,\nu(dF)$. The unitary-invariant first and second moments are
$$

\int P_F\operatorname{tr}(XP_F)\,d\mu

For the second equality, the average of $P_F\otimes P_F$ is the normalized projection onto the symmetric square. Equivalently one may expand the fourth coordinate moments as in (8.8g.13.13). =\ell_E(\mathfrak q_{\rm PPI}\widehat GY).

This is (M.6.5a.0) with zero defect. Every $s_E$ is bounded in the measure norm and every $\ell_E$ is bounded in the Hilbert–Schmidt norm. The bridge is a linear map on signed core vectors. A physical ready preparation supplies a finite probability ensemble of pure retained-spin vectors with conditional surplus-spin states. The spectral ensemble with a fixed surplus state realizes every reduced density, and finite product ensembles span the full Hermitian operator carrier by products of local projector spans. <a id="remark-m66-branch-indexed-structural-relation-between-the-two-relativizations"></a>**Remark M.6.6 (Branch-Indexed Structural Relation Between the Two Relativizations).** Structural Correspondence M.6.4 compares two accepted branch outputs; it does not derive them from one premise. ### Complete finite logarithmic action-calibration module

#### 1. Boundary, units and finite menu

### Step-by-Step Justification

**1. Conditional Binary-Reset Ledger.** On the registered conditionally uniform binary-reset architecture, the alphabet-count identity is $\varepsilon_0=\ln2$. A physical implementation instead obeys
$$
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{reset}}
=H_q(P\mid R)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{diss}}
\ge H_q(P\mid R),
$$
with equality to $\ln2$ only when the binary record is conditionally uniform and the excess dissipation vanishes. SPAP alone supplies neither this architecture nor the probability law $q(P,R)$.

**2. Independent Full-State Refresh Branch (Lemma E.1).** Reset of an ancillary register does not imply strict contraction of arbitrary full system states. On the separately declared branch
$$
\mathcal E_N=(1-p)\Psi+pT_\sigma,
\qquad
p\in(0,1],
$$
where $\Psi$ is CPTP and $T_\sigma(\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)\sigma$ refreshes the full retained state, every traceless $\Delta$ satisfies $T_\sigma(\Delta)=0$. Trace-norm contractivity of $\Psi$ therefore gives
$$
D_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathcal E_N(\rho_1),\mathcal E_N(\rho_2))
\le(1-p)D_{\mathrm{tr}}(\rho_1,\rho_2).
$$
If $\sigma\succ0$, the same declared decomposition makes $\mathcal E_N$ strictly positive and hence primitive. The reset-entropy bound alone supplies no $p>0$ and no full-state refresh decomposition.

**3. Branch-I Channel Capacity Bound (Theorem E.2)**

The separately declared full-state refresh decomposition bounds the unassisted classical capacity of independent memoryless uses of $\mathcal E_N$. The input and output dimensions are $d_0>1$. Codes may use entangled block inputs and collective decoding, but have no preshared entanglement, message-bearing side channel or feedback resource outside this channel class. Let
$$
\mathcal E_N=(1-p)\Psi+pT_\sigma,
\qquad 0<p\le1,
$$
with $\Psi$ CPTP and $T_\sigma(\rho)=\sigma\operatorname{Tr}\rho$ for a density operator $\sigma$. Define the flagged channel
$$
\widetilde{\mathcal E}_N(\rho)
=(1-p)\Psi(\rho)\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|
+p\sigma\operatorname{Tr}\rho\otimes|1\rangle\langle1|.
$$
Discarding the flag recovers $\mathcal E_N$, so any code for $\mathcal E_N$ is also a code for the flagged channel.

*Proof.* Let $M$ be the classical message of an $n$-use code and let $B^n$ denote its quantum output. The iid flag sequence $F^n$ is independent of $M$. For a positive-probability flag pattern $f$ with $k(f)$ refreshes, the refreshed output factors are copies of $\sigma$, independent of the message and of the remaining factors. The remaining system has dimension $d_0^{\,n-k(f)}$, even when the block input is entangled. Its classical-quantum mutual information is its Holevo quantity and is bounded by its entropy, hence
$$
I(M;B^n\mid F^n=f)\le[n-k(f)]\ln d_0.
$$
Averaging this conditional bound, using $I(M;F^n)=0$ and $\mathbb E k(F^n)=np$, gives
$$
I(M;B^nF^n)
=\sum_f\Pr(F^n=f)I(M;B^n\mid F^n=f)
\le n(1-p)\ln d_0.
$$
For a uniform message set of size $m_n\ge2$ and a decoded message with error probability $\varepsilon_n$, data processing and the finite-message Fano inequality give
$$
(1-\varepsilon_n)\ln m_n
\le n(1-p)\ln d_0+h_2(\varepsilon_n).
$$
Here Fano follows by adjoining the error indicator: its entropy is at most $h_2(\varepsilon_n)$, and on an error there are at most $m_n-1$ possible messages. Along every code sequence with $\varepsilon_n\to0$, division by $n$ bounds the achievable rate by $(1-p)\ln d_0$. Therefore
$$
C(\mathcal E_N)\le C(\widetilde{\mathcal E}_N)
\le(1-p)\ln d_0<\ln d_0.
$$
For $p=1$ the output is constant and the capacity is zero. The capacity resource class is the unassisted memoryless branch of Theorem E.2. ∎

**4. Branch-II Registered Operational Timescale (Theorem 29).** Theorem 29 assumes an internal Hamiltonian and a registered cycle rate, and calibrates the mean excitation energy to the baseline power. Its cycle duration is supplied by that rate; it does not prove a universal positive minimum duration for every distinguishable transition. For an orthogonalization generated by a Hamiltonian with mean excitation $E>0$ and spectral width $\Delta_H$, the Margolus–Levitin bound gives
$$
t\ge\frac{\pi\hbar}{2E}
\ge\frac{\pi\hbar}{2\Delta_H}
$$
when $E\le\Delta_H$. A merely distinguishable, arbitrarily nearby target has no state-independent positive duration bound. The value $d_0=8$ belongs to the separate Appendix Z branch. The identity
$$
\tau_{\min}=\frac{\hbar\ln2}{\Delta_H}
$$
requires a declared action–entropy bridge and saturation record and is not a consequence of finite dimension alone.

**5. Branch-II Conditional Serialized Propagation Bound (Theorem E.10.2)**

Assume a nonzero link scale $\delta$, a separately registered positive lower edge-update duration $\tau_{\min}$, successive edge-by-edge serialization, and bounded weights $w_{xy}\le w_{\max}$. Then
$$
v\le c_*:=\frac{\delta w_{\max}}{\tau_{\min}}.
$$
Theorem 29 does not supply the edge-update premise. Equality with $\delta/\tau_{\min}$ additionally requires normalized uniform weights and one-link attainment.

**6. Bound, Frontier, and Lorentzian Promotion (Theorem 46 and Corollary 46a)**

Theorem 46 transports the preceding assumptions into a uniform operational causal-speed upper bound. It does not prove that the bound is attained, position-independent, or a Lorentzian characteristic cone. An attained frontier $c=\delta/\tau_{\min}$ is separate branch data, and Lorentzian signature and local Lorentz kinematics require Corollary 46a together with the full Appendix O package.

The Planck identity $L_P/t_P=c$ is definitional. Consequently,

$$
is an algebraic consequence only after the independent frontier calibration $c=\delta/\tau_{\min}$ has been accepted; it is not forced by dimensional consistency or Theorem 46 alone.

### Conditional Serialized Origin of the Finite Propagation-Speed Bound

A uniform finite propagation-speed upper bound on the retained network follows on the branch with nonzero link scale $\delta$, a positive registered time $\tau_{\min}$ per serialized edge update, successive edge-by-edge propagation in the propagation-cost metric, and uniformly bounded edge weights. For a path of $n$ edges,
$$

\qquad
d_{\mathcal N}\le n\delta w_{\max},
$$
hence $d_{\mathcal N}/t\le\delta w_{\max}/\tau_{\min}$. A reset ledger or PCE optimization alone does not prove locality, serialization, bounded weights, or cone saturation.

Homogeneous Carrier Geometry and Registered Interaction Data.** The quotient perspective space assigns the same formal type to every $s\in\Sigma$, and the $U(d_0)$ action on this carrier is transitive. A registered interaction can nevertheless select a target $s_k$, potential $V_k$ and transition kernel, so equal formal type does not make that interaction invariant. Covariance requires simultaneous transport of all such data: for a group action $a$, a measurable set $A$ and registered data $\mathcal D$, the kernel must satisfy $K_{a\mathcal D}(as,aA)=K_{\mathcal D}(s,A)$. Invariance of one interaction is the stronger special case in which its data are preserved. These statements do not exclude an absolute or response-equivalent latent ontology.

**3. Certificate-Scoped Extended Wigner's-Friend Imports.** Definition M.6.2 requires a record-sharing or perspective-invariance certificate for an actualized record imported across distinct perspectives, and Lemma M.6.2a gives the corresponding import normal form. Theorem M.6.2b proves that the displayed Frauchiger–Renner-style import is ill typed when neither certificate exists. Any extended Wigner's-Friend argument containing an import that satisfies those hypotheses is blocked at that import, and Theorem M.6.2c shows that both certainty routes of the complete four-laboratory Frauchiger–Renner protocol pass through three such cross-perspective imports each when their edges connect distinct perspective indices.

**4. Registered laboratory branch.** With the standard instrument and Born selector supplied as premises, the perspectival kernel preserves the registered laboratory outcome law by construction while adding a conditional perspective record. Any CC-dependent deviation requires the separate G9CC realization certificate.

**5. Perspective-Indexed Account of the "Absoluteness" Debate.** Within the declared perspectival semantics, outcome propositions are objective only after their registered perspective is specified.

### M.6.8 Certificate-Gated Interface to Consciousness Complexity

Dependence of $G_{\mathrm{persp}}(s'|s,k,N,\Delta t)$ on the registered context $N$ supplies a typed interface at which a separately constructed physical control may enter. A physical CC branch must supply:

1. a causal map from an aggregate state to a realizable control $N$;
2. one normalized instrument family on which that control changes a registered outcome law, or a theorem that every admissible change is zero;
3. a forward-locked signed effect interval, with exact/hard-support or statistical status, separated from source leakage and artifacts;
4. complete source-energy, reset, and no-double-counting ledgers; and
5. pre-lightcone marginal invariance, or explicit classification of a response-active marginal as the external branch-(iii) alternative lying outside the sealed causal branch.

<a id="theorem-m68a-g9cc-modulated-contractive-perspective-instrument"></a>**Theorem M.6.8a (G9CC-Modulated Contractive Perspective Instrument).** Consume the complete finite witness of Theorem L.12.8b and write
$$
p_c(1)=c\sin^2(g\tau_{\mathrm{int}}),
\qquad p_c(0)=1-p_c(1).
\tag{M.6.8a.1}
$$
For context-dependent $0\le r_{c,\lambda}<1$, define the conditional perspective kernels and joint outcome-perspective instrument
$$
G_{c,\lambda,m}(s,B)
=(1-r_{c,\lambda})\mathbf1_B(s_m)+r_{c,\lambda}\mathbf1_B(s),
\qquad
\mathcal J_{c,\lambda}(m,B\mid s)
=p_c(m)G_{c,\lambda,m}(s,B).
\tag{M.6.8a.2}
$$
For every $c,s$, $\sum_m\mathcal J_{c,\lambda}(m,\Sigma\mid s)=1$. Conditional on $m$, its Wasserstein contraction coefficient is at most $\sqrt{r_{c,\lambda}}$; two independent readers have disagreement bound $2r_{c,\lambda}-r_{c,\lambda}^2$. If $\max_c r_{c,\lambda}\to0$, both contexts converge uniformly to the appropriate strong-readout flag. Nevertheless the locked intervention response remains
$$
\Pr(M=1\mid\operatorname{do}(C=1))
-\Pr(M=1\mid\operatorname{do}(C=0))
=\sin^2(g\tau_{\mathrm{int}})>0.
\tag{M.6.8a.3}
$$
All source, carrier, energy, reset, timing and locality owners are exactly those of Theorem L.12.8b; (M.6.8a.2) adds no duplicate physical owner.

*Proof.* Equation (M.6.8a.1) is the normalized CP-instrument law already proved in Theorem L.12.8b. Kernel normalization proves joint normalization. The coupling and product-law arguments of Theorem M.6.1a give contraction and consensus uniformly in $c$. Summing (M.6.8a.2) over the perspective endpoint recovers $p_c(m)$, proving (M.6.8a.3). ∎

Theorems 39, 39a, and 51 constrain a nominated response after it exists, and Theorem L.12.8b supplies the accepted finite carrier and instrument used in Theorem M.6.8a.

### M.6.9 Synthesis

Quantum facts in this model are indexed to the perspective that records them, much as simultaneity is indexed to a frame. Consistency between perspectives depends on shared records and compatible readout dynamics.

**Technical ledger.**

The perspectival construction is a conditional semantics for registered quantum records. It establishes typed consistency on its accepted instrument and readout branches.

The key elements of the construction are:

1. **Complete operational state specification** includes both the density operator and the registered perspective: $S_{(s)}(t)=(\rho(t),s)$.

2. **Registered outcomes are perspective-indexed**: on the accepted instrument, Born-selector, and single-outcome branch, an outcome record is indexed to the perspective participating in the registered `Evolve` event

3. **Certified readout kernels correlate perspectives**: under every hypothesis of Lemma M.6.1, the joint strong-readout law converges to a common outcome flag; normalization alone does not imply consistency.

4. **Cross-perspective reasoning is certificate-governed**: Definition M.6.2 permits an actualized-record import across distinct perspectives only through a record-sharing or perspective-invariance certificate, and Lemma M.6.2a gives the corresponding normal form.

5. **The perspectival model is branch-conditional**: the perspective space, actualization instrument, and transition kernel are supplied by the retained Hilbert/Born and perspectival branch.

6. **The formalism exposes a conditional empirical interface**: The interaction context $N$ in $G_{\text{persp}}$ is a declared model variable. A CC-induced outcome shift requires the independent context-control, response, and physical-channel certificates used by the experimental predictions.

This provides a branch-indexed extension of the relativistic program for quantum mechanics: within the declared perspectival semantics, outcome propositions are indexed by perspective just as simultaneity statements are indexed by frame. On the Hypothesis 1 branch, the MPU network is the common physical substrate, while the specific Hilbert, actualization, transition-kernel, and consistency structures retain their stated branch hypotheses.

The same perspectival machinery supplies a mathematical interface for the CC hypothesis only after the independent context-modulation and response certificates are supplied. Theorem M.6.2b proves the certificate-absence obstruction for a displayed cross-perspective import, and Theorem M.6.2c applies it to both certainty routes of the complete four-laboratory Frauchiger–Renner protocol.

### M.6.10 The Cost Functional on the Perspective Space

Sections M.2–M.5 specify the geometric substrate for perspectival dynamics: the perspective space $\Sigma \cong U(d_0)/U(1)^{d_0}$, the metric $d_\Sigma$, and the transition kernel $G_{\text{persp}}$. Section M.6 studies quantum-measurement scenarios and the conditional CC interface within that apparatus. The receiver-pattern descriptor below is defined on systems carrying Effective Operational Property R. Its computational and thermodynamic readings require the reduction and registered-implementation certificates stated in Theorems M.10.3 and M.10.7.

Shannon entropy $H(X)=-\sum_xp(x)\ln p(x)$ is a functional of a specified probability distribution. Fisher information, Kolmogorov complexity, integrated-information quantities, and quantum entropies likewise require their respective mathematical inputs, and their computability depends on how those inputs are represented. The construction below defines the receiver-pattern descriptor $\mathcal P_S(E)=(\Delta Q_S,\mu_S(E),\sigma_S(E))$. Its established comparison result is non-determination of $\mu_S(E)$ by Shannon entropy on the branch of Theorem M.10.2. External evaluation is certificate-relative under Theorem M.10.5; no general computability ordering follows from aggregate complexity alone.

<a id="definition-m101-self-model"></a>**Definition M.10.1 (Self-Model).** Let $S$ be a predictive system with $C_{\mathrm{agg}}(S)>C_{op}$ possessing Effective Operational Property R. The self-model $\mathcal M_S$ is the component of $S$'s internal model that represents its own states, predictions, accuracy, and dynamics. On the perspectival branch it encodes an internal representation of the registered perspective $s\in\Sigma$ and density operator $\rho(t)$; vector notation is restricted to the pure-state shorthand of Definition 24.

<a id="remark-m101"></a>**Remark M.10.1.** The definitions below apply to systems possessing Effective Operational Property R together with an operational self-model of the form specified in Definition M.10.1. They assign no SPAP-proximity value or cost law to systems outside that domain. Within the domain, Theorem M.10.3 gives an asymptotic computational lower bound only for families carrying its pattern-specific reduction certificate, and Theorem M.10.7 gives a physical reset signature only when its implementation certificate is supplied. Effective Operational Property R is therefore a domain condition. A parameter $\theta_S$ is not thereby a retained content object or a complete finite-budget candidate. Any persistence claim in the complete finite-budget quotient $\sim_B$ requires a registered encoder from the parameter domain into complete candidates carrying the response, update, verification, certificate, decoder, tolerance, and cost data of Definition P.16d.0.1; equality of the raw parameter follows from equality of retained quotient classes only when the composite quotient encoder is injective on the compared domain.

<a id="definition-m102-model-change-decomposition-on-an-identifiable-fisher-stratum"></a>**Definition M.10.2 (Model-Change Decomposition on an Identifiable Fisher Stratum).** Let $E$ be a physical pattern and let $S$ have Effective Operational Property R. Assume that the retained parameter point lies on a finite-dimensional identifiable stratum on which the Fisher tensor $g_{\mathcal F_S}$ is positive definite, and assume the registered tangent splitting
$$
T_{M_S}\mathcal M_S
=
T^{(\mathrm{self})}_{M_S}\mathcal M_S
\oplus^{\perp_{g_{\mathcal F_S}}}
T^{(\mathrm{ext})}_{M_S}\mathcal M_S.
$$
Define the two components by the corresponding orthogonal projections:
$$
\Delta M_S(E)
=\Delta M_S^{(\mathrm{self})}(E)+\Delta M_S^{(\mathrm{ext})}(E).
\tag{M.17}
$$
Then
$$
\langle\Delta M_S^{(\mathrm{self})},\Delta M_S^{(\mathrm{ext})}\rangle_{\mathcal F_S}=0
$$
and
$$
\|\Delta M_S\|_{\mathcal F_S}^2
=\|\Delta M_S^{(\mathrm{self})}\|_{\mathcal F_S}^2
+\|\Delta M_S^{(\mathrm{ext})}\|_{\mathcal F_S}^2.
$$
Indirectly propagated changes are classified by their final tangent component. If the Fisher tensor is singular or the direct-sum splitting is absent, the projection and reflexivity fraction require a separately declared quotient or pseudometric construction.

<a id="definition-m103-spap-proximity"></a>**Definition M.10.3 (SPAP Proximity).** Let $S$ be a system with Effective Operational Property R and self-model $\mathcal{M}_S$ parameterized by $\theta_S \in \Theta_S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{d_S}$, where $d_S$ is the self-model dimensionality. Processing $E$ induces a candidate updated parameter $\theta_S' = \theta_S + \delta\theta_S(E)$, where $\delta\theta_S(E)$ is determined by $\Delta M_S^{(\mathrm{self})}(E)$. Define the *required self-predictive performance* $PP_S^{(E)}$ as:

$$
PP_S^{(E)} := \inf\left\{PP \in [0, \alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}] : \left\| \Pi_S^{(PP)}(\theta_S') - \theta_S' \right\|_{\mathcal F_S} \le g(\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}} - PP) \right\}
\tag{M.18}
$$

where:

- $\Pi_S^{(PP)}(\theta_S')$ is the self-model prediction map at performance level $PP$: given a self-model configuration $\theta_S'$ and a specified performance level $PP \in [0, \alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}]$, $\Pi_S^{(PP)}$ returns the configuration that $S$'s predictive process, constrained to operate at performance level $PP$, would assign to itself. The map $\Pi_S^{(PP)}$ is smooth in both arguments on $[0, \alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}] \times \Theta_S$. At $PP=0$, the predictor makes no self-referential commitment: $\Pi_S^{(0)}(\theta_S')$ is $S$'s default self-model, independent of $\theta_S'$, so the discrepancy $\|\Pi_S^{(0)}(\theta_S') - \theta_S'\|_{\mathcal F_S}$ equals the full displacement $\|\delta\theta_S(E)\|_{\mathcal F_S}$. The performance coordinate is calibrated by nested attainable self-prediction classes: increasing $PP$ cannot make the best attainable self-model agreement worse. Hence, for each fixed target and each fixed register component, the corresponding optimal discrepancy is nonincreasing as $PP$ increases. For deterministic binary diagonal registers satisfying the positive Fisher-separation register hypothesis of Theorem M.10.4, the positive register discrepancy used there follows from SPAP's NOT construction, the specified binary code-state separation, and this calibrated performance ordering.
- $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal F_S}$ is the norm induced by the Fisher information metric on $\Theta_S$: for tangent vectors $u,v\in T_\theta\Theta_S$, the metric is $g^{(\mathcal F)}_{ij}(\theta)=\mathbb E[(\partial_i\ln p(x|\theta))(\partial_j\ln p(x|\theta))]$, where $p(x|\theta)$ is the predictive distribution parameterized by $\theta$.
- $g:[0,\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}]\to[0,\infty)$ is continuous and monotone increasing, with $g(0)=0$ and $g(\delta)>0$ for $\delta>0$. The linear choice $g(\delta)=\delta$ suffices for all results below. The asymptotic divergence class in Theorem M.10.3 inherits from Theorem 14 independently of the particular continuous tolerance profile.

When the constraint set in Equation M.18 is nonempty, the infimum exists because $[0,\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}]$ is compact and the constraint set is closed: the left side is continuous in $PP$ by smoothness of $\Pi_S^{(PP)}$, the right side is continuous by continuity of $g$, and the constraint is the sublevel set of a continuous function. If the constraint set is empty—no performance level satisfies the self-consistency requirement—define $PP_S^{(E)}:=\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$.

The self-consistency condition states that the updated self-model $\theta_S'$ must approximately equal $S$'s own prediction of what its self-model should be, with tolerance controlled by the gap to $\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$. At $PP=\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$, zero tolerance is required: $\Pi_S^{(\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}})}(\theta_S')=\theta_S'$ exactly, demanding a fixed point of the self-model prediction map. SPAP (Theorem 10) prohibits that fixed point for the diagonal self-referential branch.

The *SPAP proximity* of pattern $E$ for system $S$ is
$$
\mu_S(E):=\frac{1}{\delta_S(E)},
\qquad
\delta_S(E):=\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}-PP_S^{(E)},
\tag{M.19}
$$
with the convention $1/0=\infty$. Thus $\mu_S(E)$ records the boundary behavior of the criterion (M.18). Physical processability and cost conclusions require the reduction and implementation certificates stated in Theorems M.10.3 and M.10.6. If $\Delta M_S^{(\mathrm{self})}(E)=0$ and the independent baseline-invariance condition $\Pi_S^{(0)}(\theta_S)=\theta_S$ holds, then $PP=0$ satisfies (M.18), so $PP_S^{(E)}=0$, $\delta_S(E)=\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$, and $\mu_S(E)=1/\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$.

<a id="remark-m102-connection-to-perspectival-dynamics"></a>**Remark M.10.2 (Connection to perspectival dynamics).** On a branch carrying the registered perspective-extraction map of Proposition M.10.9, a self-model update $\delta\theta_S(E)$ whose endpoints remain in its declared neighborhood induces the perspective displacement between $\iota(\theta_S)$ and $\iota(\theta'_S)$. The quantity $PP_S^{(E)}$ remains the performance criterion of Definition M.10.3. Comparison of the Fisher metric on $\Theta_S$ with the flag-manifold metric $d_\Sigma$ (Definition 25, Equation 42) requires Proposition M.10.9's local-embedding and co-Lipschitz hypotheses; those data do not follow from the self-model update alone.

<a id="definition-m104-perspectival-profile"></a>**Definition M.10.4 (Perspectival Profile).** The *perspectival profile* of $E$ relative to $S$ is the triple:
$$
\mathcal{P}_S(E) := \left(\Delta Q_S(E), \; \mu_S(E), \; \sigma_S(E)\right)
\tag{M.20}
$$
where:

- $\Delta Q_S(E) := \mathbb{E}[\Delta Q \mid E; M_S]$ is the *predictive relevance*: the expected improvement in predictive quality from processing $E$ (Definition 1). This may be positive, zero, or undefined if $E$ is unprocessable.
- $\mu_S(E)$ is the *SPAP proximity*: the inverse gap to the SPAP boundary required for full integration (Equation M.19).
- $\sigma_S(E) := \|\Delta M_S^{(\text{self})}(E)\|_{\mathcal{F}_S} / \|\Delta M_S(E)\|_{\mathcal{F}_S}$ is the *reflexivity fraction*: the proportion of the total model-change that modifies the self-model. The Fisher-orthogonality of the decomposition (Definition M.10.2) guarantees $\|\Delta M_S^{(\text{self})}\|_{\mathcal{F}_S} \leq \|\Delta M_S\|_{\mathcal{F}_S}$ via the Pythagorean identity, ensuring $\sigma_S \in [0, 1]$. When $\|\Delta M_S(E)\|_{\mathcal{F}_S} = 0$ (no model change), define $\sigma_S(E) := 0$.

The profile describes *perspectival information* on a branch where $\Delta Q_S(E)>0$, $\mu_S(E)<\infty$, and an admissible procedure within the system's task-specific resources realizes the positive improvement for a physically instantiated, relevant pattern as required by Definition 1. Finite $\mu_S(E)$ alone supplies no finite-cost implementation. When $\mu_S(E)=\infty$, no subboundary performance satisfies (M.18); exclusion of finite-cost completed integration additionally requires Theorem M.10.6's pattern-specific reduction certificate. That integration boundary does not by itself exclude every admissible partial use satisfying Definition 1.

<a id="remark-m103"></a>**Remark M.10.3.** The three components are not independent. High $\sigma_S$ (high reflexivity fraction) tends to correlate with high $\mu_S$ (high SPAP proximity), but the relationship is neither monotonic nor implication-level. A pattern can have $\sigma_S(E) > 0$ yet still satisfy the self-consistency condition already at $PP=0$, in which case $\mu_S(E) = 1/\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$ despite nonzero self-model engagement. Conversely, a pattern with only moderate reflexivity can have very large $\mu_S$ if it targets deep self-model parameters. SPAP proximity tracks the required self-predictive performance, not merely the fraction of change directed at the self-model.

<a id="theorem-m101-conditional-perspectival-dependence"></a>**Theorem M.10.1 (Conditional Perspectival Dependence).** Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ have distinct operational self-model parameters in a retained coordinate $k$. Suppose the retained pattern language contains a binary assertion $E_k$ that is satisfied by $S_2$'s parameter and not by $S_1$'s parameter, and suppose the registered update rule leaves a satisfied parameter unchanged but changes the unsatisfied parameter by a nonzero Fisher-norm displacement. Then
$$
\mathcal P_{S_1}(E_k)\ne\mathcal P_{S_2}(E_k).
\tag{M.21}
$$

*Proof.* The update hypotheses give
$$
\|\Delta M_{S_1}^{(\mathrm{self})}(E_k)\|_{\mathcal F_{S_1}}>0,
\qquad
\Delta M_{S_2}^{(\mathrm{self})}(E_k)=0.
$$
The first inequality implies a nonzero total model change for $S_1$, hence $\sigma_{S_1}(E_k)>0$. Definition M.10.4 gives $\sigma_{S_2}(E_k)=0$. Since $\sigma$ is the third component of $\mathcal P_S$, the two profiles differ. The theorem is existential and certificate-relative; distinct self-models need not assign different profiles to every pattern. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m102-conditional-non-determination-by-shannon-entropy"></a>**Theorem M.10.2 (Conditional Non-Determination by Shannon Entropy).** Let $S$ satisfy the baseline-invariance condition of Corollary M.10.3.1 and the independent-register hypotheses of Theorem M.10.4. Suppose the retained pattern class contains (i) a purely external binary message ensemble $E_1$ and (ii) the formal joint diagonal binary ensemble $E_2$, each with probabilities $(1/2,1/2)$. Then
$$
H(E_1)=H(E_2)=\ln2,
\qquad
\mu_S(E_1)=\frac1{\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}},
\qquad
\mu_S(E_2)=\infty.
\tag{M.22}
$$
Consequently $\mu_S$ is not a function of Shannon entropy alone on this branch.

*Proof.* For either equiprobable binary ensemble,
$$
H(E_i)=-2\left(\frac12\log\frac12\right)=\log2.
$$
The external ensemble has $\Delta M_S^{(\mathrm{self})}(E_1)=0$, so Corollary M.10.3.1 gives $\mu_S(E_1)=1/\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$. Theorem M.10.4 gives an empty constraint set for the retained joint diagonal challenge $E_2$, hence $\mu_S(E_2)=\infty$ by (M.19). Equal entropies and unequal proximities prove the final assertion. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m103-certificate-relative-integration-complexity"></a>**Theorem M.10.3 (Certificate-Relative Integration Complexity).** Let $(S_\lambda,E_\lambda)$ be an asymptotic family carrying the pattern-specific reduction certificate of Corollary B.2.1, and measure $C_{\mathrm{integrate}}$ in the same computational cost units as $C_{\mathrm{uni}}$. On the branch
$$
0<\mu_\lambda:=\mu_{S_\lambda}(E_\lambda)<\infty,
\qquad
\mu_\lambda\longrightarrow\infty,
$$
there are constants $c>0$ and $1<\mu_0<\infty$ such that
$$
C_{\mathrm{integrate}}(S_\lambda,E_\lambda)
\ge c(\log\mu_\lambda)\mu_\lambda^2
\tag{M.23}
$$
whenever $\mu_\lambda\ge\mu_0$.

*Proof.* The finite positive proximity gives $\delta_\lambda=1/\mu_\lambda>0$. The reduction certificate and Theorem B.2 supply constants $c>0$ and $\delta_0>0$ for which
$$
C_{\mathrm{integrate}}(S_\lambda,E_\lambda)
\ge C_{\mathrm{uni}}(\delta_\lambda)
\ge c\,\frac{\log(1/\delta_\lambda)}{\delta_\lambda^2}
$$
when $0<\delta_\lambda\le\delta_0$. Choosing $\mu_0>\max\{1,1/\delta_0\}$ and substituting proves (M.23). A thermodynamic lower bound requires an additional implementation ledger mapping the certified computation to physical resets or another calibrated resource. $\square$

<a id="corollary-m103a-asymptotic-lower-exponent-without-a-finite-ladder-slope-law"></a>**Corollary M.10.3a (Asymptotic Lower Exponent Without a Finite-Ladder Slope Law).** For any sequence of the finite-proximity branch of Theorem M.10.3 with $\mu_n\to\infty$,
$$
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\frac{\log C_{\mathrm{integrate}}(S_{\lambda_n},E_{\lambda_n})}
{\log\mu_n}
\ge2.
\tag{M.23a}
$$
Costs may take the value $+\infty$, with $\log(+\infty)=+\infty$; the denominator is finite and positive for all sufficiently large $n$.

*Proof.* The positive lower bound (M.23) makes every sufficiently late cost positive. If a cost is finite, taking logarithms and dividing by $\log\mu_n>0$ gives
$$
\frac{\log C_{\mathrm{integrate}}}{\log\mu_n}
\ge2+\frac{\log c+\log\log\mu_n}{\log\mu_n}.
$$
For infinite cost the same inequality holds in the extended order. The final term tends to zero, proving the liminf assertion. A stage with $\mu=+\infty$ has zero gap and is not covered by the positive-gap certificate used here; it requires a separate endpoint argument and is not substituted into either logarithmic ratio. ∎

Equation (M.23a) is an asymptotic lower exponent. It supplies no monotonicity, derivative, or ordinary-least-squares slope on a finite ladder. On any finite ladder, a constant cost chosen above every displayed lower bound has regression slope zero while satisfying all those pointwise bounds. Equation (M.23) also supplies no cost-ratio conclusion against a second receiver unless that receiver's cost has an independently registered upper bound.

<a id="theorem-m103b-exact-exponent-set-of-the-reduction-certificate-class"></a>**Theorem M.10.3b (Exact Exponent Set of the Reduction-Certificate Class).** A certified proximity ladder is a sequence of receiver-pattern pairs $(S_n,E_n)$ with $8\le\mu_n:=\mu_{S_n}(E_n)<\infty$ and $\mu_n\to\infty$, together with a nonempty integration class for each pair and the reduction certificate of Corollary B.2.1 with one pair of constants $c_s>0$ and $\beta(\delta)\le\delta$. Write $C_n$ for the infimum of the integration cost over the $n$-th class.

1. Every certified ladder satisfies
$$
C_n\ge\frac{3c_s}{128}\mu_n^2\ln\frac{\mu_n}4\qquad(n\ge1),
\tag{M.10.3b.1}
$$
so $\liminf_n\log C_n/\log\mu_n\ge2$.
2. Let $\mu_n\to\infty$ with $\mu_n\ge8$ and $\mu_n>1/\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$, and let $e\in[2,\infty]$. There is a certified ladder with these proximities and $\lim_n\log C_n/\log\mu_n=e$. For $e=2$ it has $C_n=c_0+c_uN_+(1/\mu_n)=\Theta(\mu_n^2\log\mu_n)$, with $N_+$ from (B.5e).
3. Hence the set of asymptotic cost exponents admitted by the certificate data of Theorem M.10.3 is exactly $[2,\infty]$: the exponent $2$ of Corollary M.10.3a is attained, and no exponent above $2$ follows from those data.

*Proof.* Item 1 is Corollary B.2.2 applied to every member of the $n$-th class, followed by the infimum; $\ln(\mu_n/4)\ge\ln2>0$, and Corollary M.10.3a gives the exponent bound.

For item 2, Theorem M.10.4.2 supplies for each $n$ a smooth calibrated one-coordinate self-model and target with proximity exactly $\mu_n$. Register as the integration class of the $n$-th pair the sample-mean calibration strategies of Theorem B.2a at margin $\delta_n=1/\mu_n\le1/8$ that use $N\ge N_e(\delta_n)$ independent Bernoulli observations, where $N_e(\delta)=\max\{N_+(\delta),\lceil\delta^{-e}\rceil\}$ for $e<\infty$ and $N_\infty(\delta)=\max\{N_+(\delta),\lceil2^{1/\delta}\rceil\}$, with integration cost equal to the registered operation count $c_0+c_uN$. Every member is $\delta_n$-accurate because the Hoeffding bound $2e^{-2N\delta_n^2}$ behind (B.5f) decreases in $N$ and $N\ge N_+(\delta_n)$. The reduction map is the identity into the frozen Bernoulli class, whose threshold test at $1/2$ has both errors at most $\delta_n$, and $c_0+c_uN\ge c_uN$ gives the Theorem B.2 certificate with $c_s=c_u$ and $\beta(\delta)=\delta$. Therefore $C_n=c_0+c_uN_e(\delta_n)$. For $e=2$, $\mu_n\ge8$ gives $\mu_n^2\ln(2\mu_n)/2\ge\mu_n^2$, so $N_2(\delta_n)=N_+(\delta_n)$ and $\log C_n/\log\mu_n\to2$. For $2<e<\infty$, $N_+(\delta_n)=O(\mu_n^2\log\mu_n)=o(\mu_n^e)$, so eventually $N_e(\delta_n)=\lceil\mu_n^e\rceil$ and the ratio tends to $e$. For $e=\infty$, $\log C_n\ge\mu_n\log2+\log c_u$, so the ratio diverges. Item 3 combines items 1 and 2. ∎

**Proximity exponents.** Theorems B.2–B.2a and M.10.3b give the quadratic exponent floor for every registered proximity ladder. The constructed calibration ladders realize exactly the exponent set $[2,\infty]$, with minimal certified costs in the fixed Bernoulli class. The one-coordinate maps of Theorem M.10.4.2 attain every stated proximity. Theorem M.10.3c below supplies the same-risk physical reduction and its zero-reset implementation.

<a id="theorem-m103c-pattern-specific-reduction-on-a-qualified-same-risk-spap-source"></a>**Theorem M.10.3c (Pattern-Specific Reduction on a Qualified Same-Risk SPAP Source).**

The source “SPAP-M08-RISK-PORT-v1” is the explicit ideal risk-port extension of the qualified coherent host of Theorem M.10.4.3. It retains the exact original host, returned MPU bit and complete holding/cost interface while changing the scored experiment and conditional-risk convention as stated below. The primitive source, sealing and stock assumptions remain part of this existence witness.

### A same-gap, risk-calibrated SPAP integration source

#### 1. Exact problem, inputs and source changes

The original M08 predicate is: construct the pattern-specific reduction for SPAP-diagonal patterns of a Property-R system and attach heat only through realized reset counts (Theorem M.10.7). <a id="theorem-m104-existence-of-divergent-spap-proximity-by-independent-register-amplification"></a>**Theorem M.10.4 (Existence of Divergent SPAP Proximity by Independent-Register Amplification).** Let $S$ be a system with Effective Operational Property R whose self-model contains $n_S$ Fisher-orthogonal addressable deterministic SPAP registers. Assume that, for each retained register, the two operational binary code states are represented by distinct parameter values at positive Fisher distance. Register the parameter chart and the metric-evaluation points used by the discrepancy in (M.18). For each retained register $j$, require a certified lower bound $\eta_{S,j}>0$ on the Fisher tangent norm of either nonzero binary code-state displacement at every metric-evaluation point used in the individual and joint boundary diagonal challenges. The geodesic distance between code states does not by itself certify this tangent-norm bound. Define

$$
D_1(S):=\min_{1\le j\le n_S}\eta_{S,j}>0
$$

and

$$
N^*(S):=\left\lceil\left(\frac{g(\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}})}{D_1(S)}\right)^2\right\rceil+1.
$$

If $n_S\ge N^*(S)$, then the retained formal pattern language contains a joint diagonal challenge $E^*$ for which the constraint set in (M.18) is empty and hence $\mu_S(E^*)=\infty$ by definition. If an independent implementation certificate realizes that joint challenge as a physical pattern with the same register responses and Fisher geometry, the same conclusion holds for the realized pattern. For a scalable MPU-network product family, this conclusion applies at every family member for which $n_S\ge N^*(S)$ and such an implementation certificate is supplied. No family-wide unboundedness conclusion follows from block-diagonal Fisher geometry alone unless the family also satisfies a quantitative separation condition ensuring $\sqrt{n_S}D_1(S)>g(\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}})$ along an unbounded subsequence.

*Proof.* The uniform register discrepancy is supplied by the certified tangent-norm bounds in the register antecedent. Theorem 15 supplies the deterministic SPAP core with finite binary roles capable of storing and comparing the predicted bit and the realized bit. The independent-register hypothesis supplies the two operational binary code states, their positive Fisher separation, and the registered lower bounds $\eta_{S,j}>0$ for the discrepancy norm used in (M.18). Since the retained register family used in the construction is finite, $D_1(S)=\min_j\eta_{S,j}>0$.

For a single retained register $j$, construct the deterministic SPAP diagonal challenge against the boundary self-prediction of $S$ on that register. If the boundary prediction map satisfied

$$
\left(\Pi_S^{(\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}})}(\theta_{S,j}')\right)_j=(\theta_{S,j}')_j,
$$

then the predicted binary value and the realized binary value in the diagonal register would coincide. But the diagonal rule is

$$
\phi_{t+1}^{(j)}=\mathrm{NOT}(\hat\phi^{(j)}),
$$

so equality would imply $\hat\phi^{(j)}=\mathrm{NOT}(\hat\phi^{(j)})$, contradicting Theorem 10. Therefore the boundary discrepancy on register $j$ is at least the binary code-state separation:

$$
\left\|\left(\Pi_S^{(\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}})}(\theta_{S,j}')-\theta_{S,j}'\right)_j\right\|_{\mathcal F_S}\ge \eta_{S,j}.
$$

By the calibrated performance ordering in Definition M.10.3, lowering $PP$ cannot improve the optimal self-model agreement beyond the boundary case. Hence, for every $PP\in[0,\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}})$,

$$
\left\|\left(\Pi_S^{(PP)}(\theta_{S,j}')-\theta_{S,j}'\right)_j\right\|_{\mathcal F_S}
\ge
\eta_{S,j}
\ge
D_1(S).
$$

Choose $N=N^*(S)$ Fisher-orthogonal addressable registers from the available $n_S$ registers and construct $N$ diagonal challenges $S_{\mathrm{diag}}^{(j)}$, $j=1,\ldots,N$, one per register. §A.0.2 (Theorem A.0.1; Corollary A.0.1) supplies the finite diagonal closure for each retained challenge, and the theorem antecedent supplies the independent-register branch. Let $E^{(N)}$ be the joint pattern encoding those diagonal challenges simultaneously, and write $\theta_S'$ for the self-model state after attempting to integrate $E^{(N)}$. The register family is Fisher-orthogonal by the theorem antecedent. On an MPU-network realization, Theorem A.0.6 supplies its conditional computational capabilities and Theorem 15 supplies its finite SPAP core; a separate product-state and parameter-independence record must supply the Fisher-orthogonal register geometry. Therefore, by additivity of the Fisher metric on orthogonal parameter subspaces, for every $PP\in[0,\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}})$,

$$
\left\|\Pi_S^{(PP)}(\theta_S')-\theta_S'\right\|_{\mathcal F_S}^2
\ge
\sum_{j=1}^{N}D_1(S)^2
=
N D_1(S)^2.
$$

Thus

$$
\left\|\Pi_S^{(PP)}(\theta_S')-\theta_S'\right\|_{\mathcal F_S}
\ge
\sqrt{N}\,D_1(S).
$$

For $N=N^*(S)$,

$$
\sqrt{N^*(S)}\,D_1(S)>g(\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}).
$$

Since $g$ is monotone and $0\le\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}-PP\le\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$, $g(\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}-PP)\le g(\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}})$ for all $PP\in[0,\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}})$. Hence the self-consistency condition in Equation M.18 fails for every subboundary performance level:

$$
\left\|\Pi_S^{(PP)}(\theta_S')-\theta_S'\right\|_{\mathcal F_S}
>
g(\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}})
\ge
g(\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}-PP).
$$

At the boundary $PP=\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$, Equation M.18 requires zero tolerance because $g(0)=0$. The joint diagonal object would then require an exact fixed point of the self-prediction map on all retained diagonal registers, which SPAP excludes by Theorem 10. Thus the constraint set in Equation M.18 is empty. Consequently

$$
PP_S^{(E^{(N^*(S))})}=\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}},
$$

$$
\delta_S(E^{(N^*(S))})=0,
$$

and

$$
\mu_S(E^{(N^*(S))})=\infty.
$$

Define $E^*:=E^{(N^*(S))}$. The diagonal construction of Theorem A.1.1 makes each $S_{\mathrm{diag}}^{(j)}$ constructible within $\mathcal M$ on the retained finite-program branch. Thus $E^*$ exists in the retained formal pattern language. It is a physical pattern only on a branch carrying an implementation certificate that realizes the joint register challenge with the assumed response and Fisher-separation properties. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m1042-exact-attainable-range-of-formal-spap-proximity"></a>**Theorem M.10.4.2 (Exact Attainable Range of Formal SPAP Proximity).** Fix $\alpha=\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}>0$. $$
is nonincreasing in $P$ for every target. For $\theta'=0$, the criterion (M.18) is satisfied exactly for $P\in[r,q]$, so its infimum is $r$ and its proximity is the prescribed $\mu$.

by the bound on $k$, and $h(\alpha)=k(\alpha-r)(\alpha-q)>0$, so $h$ is positive and decreasing. Equations (M.10.4.2c)--(M.10.4.2d) verify every smoothness, default, and calibrated-order condition. Finally,
$$
h(P)\le\alpha-P
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad

### Canonical map and score algebra

### 1. Actual own-state experiment and independently fixed performance ceiling

The apparatus has an own-state register Z, an own-model location register M, a retained forecast-location register H, and separate forecast/report, phase, input, scratch and program-code registers. A registered event E supplies target $\theta$ and executes:

1. A nominated report program produces one real point forecast $q$ for the next $Z$.
2. The immutable output port computes $\hat B=\mathbf 1\{q\ge 1/2\}$.
3. It commits the joint self-predictive object $(q,N(x,1))$, with $x$ specified below, to the forecast records.
4. The system writes its next own-state bit $Z=\mathrm{NOT}(\hat B)$.
5. The same registered event updates its operational own-model register $M$ to $\theta$.
6. The retained diagnostic of that actual own-model register is $W\sim N(M,1)$, using a fresh independent Gaussian source.
7. Verification computes $\mathrm{PE}=(q-Z)^{2}$ and $\mathrm{PP}=1/(1+\mathrm{PE})$.

The Gaussian forecast concerns the next diagnostic of this very register M, whose contents are the system's own operational model state; it is not a response on a separate unattached apparatus. M's actual update is independent of which q branch is used, so the fixed candidate $\theta$ is the same across all report programs.

Since $Z=0$ when $q\ge 1/2$ and $Z=1$ otherwise,

$$
\begin{gathered}
PE(q)=\max(q^2,(1-q)^2),\\P(q)=1/[1+\max(q^2,(1-q)^2)]
\end{gathered}
$$

Consequently the genuine deterministic diagonal response gives

$$
0<P(q)\le \alpha =4/5,
$$

with equality precisely at $q=1/2$. Every P∈(0,$\alpha$] is attained, for example at $q(P)=\sqrt$(1/P−1)≥1/2; its reflected report1−$q(P)$ supplies the other branch away from the tie. Reports outside[0,1] are point forecasts, not probability distributions; squared loss remains a proper mean score on this action space.

The performance ceiling follows from the actual NOT response and the locked score. It is not imported from a fair-noise module or a formal controller label. The equality between the port's precomputed $P(q)$ and the subsequently verified PP is an algebraic invariant of this source, not access to an unknown future outcome.

### 2. Proper composite forecast score

The predictive object consists of a binary-variable point-mean forecast q and a Gaussian diagnostic forecast $N(x,1)$. Its registered score is

$$
S((q,N(x,1)),(Z,W))=(q-Z)^2
$$

For any fixed joint outcome law with mean $m=E$[Z], the expected score is (q−m)²+$\operatorname{Var}(Z)$, so truthful binary mean reporting is optimal. The diagnostic component does not affect the score: the rule is proper but not strictly proper for the composite object. Every registered finite q/outcome pair has finite nonnegative loss. The same score and $k_{\mathrm{PP}}=1$ are fixed for all pattern parameters and targets.

This explicit insensitivity is load-bearing and must not be hidden. It is why a physical report-port constraint is needed to bind the diagnostic prediction to the scored part. Without that constraint, a program could choose $x=\theta$ while independently lowering its binary score, destroying the claimed nested optimum.

### 3. Immutable same-source report interface and canonical maps

Fix $\alpha =4/5$. For any chosen finite proximity $\mu>1/\alpha$, put $r=\alpha-1/\mu$, choose $s\in(r,\alpha)$ and $0<k<1/(2\alpha-r-s)$, and define exactly the canonical construction

$$
\begin{gathered}
h(P)=\alpha -P+k(P-r)(P-s),\\d=h(0),\\\tau (P)=h(P)/d,\\F_P(\theta )=(1-\tau (P))\theta +\tau (P)d
\end{gathered}
$$

The output port accepts a q and the target/pattern record, and has the ONLY permitted write path to H:

$$
H := F_{P(q)}(\theta )
$$

Its diagnostic forecast is $N(H,1)$. General programs may compute arbitrary values in scratch, including $\theta$ itself, but cannot directly write H or replace its declared diagnostic law. The controller's address/write authorization is part of the source transition grammar. This is no stronger than an ordinary immutable typed hardware output interface. An EOPR certificate must prove its programming and access scope explicitly; computational universality does not automatically confer write access to every protected register.

Every admitted report on either diagonal branch is processed by this same port. There is no exclusion of inconvenient low-branch forecasts. At the boundary $q=1/2$, $H=F_{\alpha}(\theta)$; $h(\alpha )>0$ on the canonical finite-proximity construction, so the Gaussian self-prediction still has a positive displacement when $\theta\ne d$.

### 4. Global nested optimum at the same fixed candidate

Define the positive-performance cap classes by all report programs whose actually verified score obeys $P(q)\le P$. Equivalently, these contain every real q with $P(q)\le P$ that the registered port can receive. Classes are nested as P increases and include both branches.

For each such report, the Gaussian diagnostic displacement from the SAME realized candidate $\theta$ is

$$
|H-\theta |=\tau (P(q)) |d-\theta |
$$

The independently proved h is strictly decreasing; hence $P(q)\le P$ implies

$$
|H-\theta |\ge \tau (P)|d-\theta |
$$

The bound is attained by $q(P)$, so the globally best attainable diagnostic agreement within the registered class is exactly $F_{\mathrm{P}}(\theta )$. At $\theta =d$ all reports have the same exact agreement and $F_{\mathrm{P}}(d)=d$; the optimum value is zero, which is consistent rather than a diagonal contradiction. The independently scored bit Z still obeys NOT at that target.

Thus the full affine prediction map has the stated operational meaning for every target $\theta$. It is not merely an expectation of a random posterior estimator, nor a proof only at $\theta =0$. The unique forecast-location value is fixed by the actual score cap (although multiple q reports can attain it).

A performance-cap hierarchy, rather than a finite-time hierarchy, is being registered here. This proves the meaning stated in M.18 if those cap classes are admitted. It does not supply M08's computational reduction or any cost law.

### 5. Default, Fisher stratum and response laws

$P=0$ is the explicit unscored no-self-commitment operation: it writes $H=d$ and makes no finite q report or scored next-bit prediction. #### Exact binary table syntax

The finite predictor parser used above is fixed as follows. Decode an initial Elias-gamma integer $N\ge 1$ (number of states) from the length-L program field. Let $w=\lceil\log_2(N+1)\rceil$. Read exactly 3N records in lexicographic(state,scanned symbol) order, each with fields

| Transition field | Width | Meaning |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Written symbol | Two bits | $00$ blank; $01$ zero; $10$ one; $11$ invalid |
| Movement | Two bits | $00$ left; $01$ stay; $10$ right; $11$ invalid |
| Next state | $w$ bits | An integer in $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ |
| Halt flag | One bit | $1$ returns the output; $0$ continues |
| Output | One bit | The returned bit when the halt flag is $1$ |

Symbols 00,01,10 mean blank,0,1; write 11 is invalid. Move 00,01,10 mean left,stay,right; move 11 is invalid. Require $next_{\mathrm{state}}<N$, enough bits for all records, and only zero padding after them. Otherwise FAIL. The initial state is 0. On a valid nonterminal step, read the current symbol, use the unique indexed record, write its symbol, move, and update the state. If $\mathrm{halt}=1$, return out. The execution counter increments; if it reaches $T$ without halt, return TIMEOUT. A move beyond the allocated tape is FAIL (the prepared tape and $T$ bound prevent it on valid initial runs). A terminal state remains unchanged. These rules define the total map $f$ on every $m$-bit input by first checking all field types/ranges and padding; invalid configurations go to the unique typed failure configuration.
