<a id="theorem-m105-certificate-relative-external-evaluation"></a>**Theorem M.10.5 (Certificate-Relative External Evaluation).** Let $A$ hold an external representation of $B$'s self-model data for a specified pattern $E$. Assume that the representation includes:

1. effective finite descriptions of $\theta'_B(E)$, $g_B$, $g$, and $\Pi_B^{(PP)}$ with certified moduli of continuity on $[0,\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}]$;
2. a decision certificate that either isolates the infimum in (M.18) to any requested rational accuracy or certifies that the constraint set is empty; and
3. if a sender-side reflexive-cost conclusion is desired, an insulation certificate stating that this external computation leaves $A$'s self-model component unchanged.

Then $A$ can enclose $PP_B^{(E)}$ to the accuracy supplied by the decision certificate. On a branch with $PP_B^{(E)}<\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$, certified infimum enclosures also compute the finite value $\mu_B(E)$ to any requested rational accuracy. An exact declaration $\mu_B(E)=\infty$ requires a certificate that the constraint set is empty or that its infimum equals $\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$; arbitrarily narrow infimum enclosures alone do not supply that decision. The inequality $C_{\mathrm{agg}}(A)>C_{\mathrm{agg}}(B)$ is neither necessary nor sufficient for these conclusions by itself.

*Proof.* Define the continuous function
$$
F_E(PP)
=
\|\Pi_B^{(PP)}(\theta'_B(E))-\theta'_B(E)\|_{\mathcal F_B}
-g(\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}-PP).
$$
The effective descriptions and moduli permit certified evaluation of $F_E$ on rational interval enclosures. Item 2 either certifies that $\{PP:F_E(PP)\le0\}$ is empty or encloses its infimum. In the empty case Definition M.10.3 assigns $PP_B^{(E)}=\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$ and $\mu_B(E)=\infty$. Write $p=PP_B^{(E)}$ and $\alpha=\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$. If $p<\alpha$, sufficiently narrow certified enclosures $p\in[L,U]$ satisfy $U<\alpha$ and give
$$
\mu_B(E)\in
\left[\frac1{\alpha-L},\frac1{\alpha-U}\right].
$$
Their width is $(U-L)/[(\alpha-L)(\alpha-U)]$, which tends to zero as the infimum enclosure shrinks around $p<\alpha$. Refinement until this computable width is below the requested tolerance therefore terminates on that branch. At $p=\alpha$, this reciprocal estimate gives no finite error enclosure; an endpoint decision is separate. Under item 3, Definition M.10.2 gives $\sigma_A=0$ for the external-evaluation task; without item 3 no such sender-side conclusion follows. No universal reflexive or upward impossibility is proved by this argument. $\square$

<a id="corollary-m1051-no-universal-self-evaluation-on-a-reduction-certified-branch"></a>**Corollary M.10.5.1 (No Universal Self-Evaluation on a Reduction-Certified Branch).** Fix a predictive system $S$ with Effective Operational Property R. Assume there is a total computable reduction $\mathcal R_S$ with the following property: from any internal procedure that returns the exact value of $\mu_S(E)$ for every represented pattern $E$ with $\sigma_S(E)>0$, $\mathcal R_S$ constructs a universal exact self-predictor for the diagonal class excluded by Theorem 10. Then no such universal internal evaluator of $\mu_S$ exists.

*Proof.* Suppose an internal evaluator $\mathcal P_S$ returned the exact value of $\mu_S(E)$ on every represented pattern with $\sigma_S(E)>0$. By the reduction hypothesis, $\mathcal R_S(\mathcal P_S)$ would be a universal exact self-predictor for the diagonal class of Theorem 10. Theorem 10 excludes that predictor. Hence $\mathcal P_S$ cannot exist. ∎

Theorem M.10.5 separately establishes certificate-relative external evaluation for specified represented patterns.

<a id="corollary-m1052-conditional-physical-signature"></a>**Corollary M.10.5.2 (Conditional Physical Signature).** Theorem M.10.3 supplies only its certificate-relative abstract processing-cost lower bound. Neither the computability scope of Theorem M.10.5 nor the computational lower bound alone determines entropy production, metabolic expenditure, or stress-energy.

<a id="theorem-m106-boundary-of-the-certified-integration-criterion"></a>**Theorem M.10.6 (Boundary of the Certified Integration Criterion).** Let $E$ satisfy $\mu_S(E)=\infty$. Then no $PP<\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$ satisfies the integration criterion (M.18). If, in addition, a pattern-specific reduction certificate identifies every completed integration of $E$ with a certified task family of accuracy gap $\delta\downarrow0$ to which Theorem B.2 applies, the certified computational cost has no finite uniform upper bound:
$$
\liminf_{\delta\downarrow0}C_{\mathrm{integrate}}(S,E;\delta)=\infty.
\tag{M.24}
$$
This statement excludes a finite-cost completed integration on that certificate; it does not assert that an aborted physical run dissipates infinite energy.

*Proof.* By (M.19), $\mu_S(E)=\infty$ means $PP_S^{(E)}=\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$. If a subboundary $PP$ satisfied (M.18), the infimum of the nonempty constraint set would be at most that $PP$ and hence strictly less than $\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$, a contradiction. Thus no subboundary level satisfies the criterion. On the additional reduction branch,
$$
C_{\mathrm{integrate}}(S,E;\delta)
\ge C_{\mathrm{uni}}(\delta)
\ge c\frac{\log(1/\delta)}{\delta^2}
$$
for sufficiently small positive $\delta$. The right-hand side tends to infinity, proving (M.24). $\square$

<a id="remark-m106-comparison-with-gödel"></a>**Remark M.10.6 (Comparison with Gödel).** The comparison with Gödel's First Incompleteness Theorem is structural rather than isomorphic. Theorem M.10.4 supplies boundary objects on its independent-register amplification branch. <a id="theorem-m107-conditional-registered-reset-signature"></a>**Theorem M.10.7 (Conditional Registered-Reset Signature).** Let $(S_\lambda,E_\lambda)$ satisfy the pattern-specific reduction certificate of Corollary B.2.1 on stages with $0<\mu_\lambda:=\mu_{S_\lambda}(E_\lambda)<\infty$ and $\mu_\lambda\to\infty$. Suppose a physical implementation certificate assigns a deterministic finite number $n_\lambda$ of completed resets to each stage, with
$$
n_\lambda\ge c\,\log\mu_\lambda\,\mu_\lambda^2
$$
for some $c>0$ and all sufficiently large $\mu_\lambda$. For every counted reset $j$, conditional on its admitted pre-reset history $\mathcal H_{j-1}$, assume the complete classical reset contract of Definition 28: the actual logical and retained records have law $q_{j|\mathcal H_{j-1}}$, the retained records are unchanged, the logical register returns to its ready state, and the bath independence, resource closure and entropy-limit hypotheses hold. All counted baths have the same temperature $T>0$. Assume integrable mean heats $Q_j$ and define
$$
h_j:=\mathbb E\!\left[
H_{q_{j|\mathcal H_{j-1}}}(P_j\mid R_j)
\right],
\qquad
\Delta S_{\mathrm{export}}
:=
\frac1T\sum_{j=1}^{n_\lambda}\mathbb E Q_j.
$$
Here $\Delta S_{\mathrm{export}}$ is a mean heat-export ledger in entropy units. Then
$$
\frac{\Delta S_{\mathrm{export}}}{k_B}
\ge\sum_{j=1}^{n_\lambda}h_j.
\tag{M.25}
$$
If the certificate also supplies $h_j\ge h_{\min}>0$ for every counted reset, then
$$
\Delta S_{\mathrm{export}}
\ge k_Bh_{\min}n_\lambda
\ge k_Bh_{\min}c\,\log\mu_\lambda\,\mu_\lambda^2.
$$
A stress-energy conclusion additionally requires the local energy-density, support and coarse-graining bridge of Definition B.8.

*Proof.* Theorem 31, applied to each history-conditioned reset under the complete Definition 28 contract, gives
$$
\mathbb E[Q_j\mid\mathcal H_{j-1}]
\ge k_BT\,H_{q_{j|\mathcal H_{j-1}}}(P_j\mid R_j).
$$
Taking expectations and summing the finite deterministic sequence proves (M.25). The entropy floor and the independent implementation count bound give the second inequality chain. A positive entropy floor does not follow from register size or from computational complexity alone.

The ledger is neither a pathwise heat floor nor a total entropy-production floor. Identifying it with an actual finite bath's von Neumann entropy change requires an additional entropy-balance certificate; mean heat divided by temperature is not that entropy change by definition. Random stopping, unbounded reset counts, or infinite-resource limits require a justified conditional-summation and convergence certificate before the same conclusion is used. Definition B.8 consumes the physical localization bridge rather than deriving it here. $\square$

The conditional chain is
$$
\mu_\lambda
\xrightarrow{\text{pattern-specific reduction certificate}}
C_{\mathrm{integrate}}
\xrightarrow{\text{registered implementation certificate}}
\{(P_j,R_j,q_{j|\mathcal H_{j-1}})\}_{j=1}^{n_\lambda}
\xrightarrow{\text{conditional reset contract and finite summation}}
\frac{\Delta S_{\mathrm{export}}}{k_B}
\ge\sum_j h_j.
$$

<a id="theorem-m108-certificate-relative-screening-and-replay-bookkeeping"></a>**Theorem M.10.8 (Certificate-Relative Screening and Replay Bookkeeping).** Let $A$ hold the effective model-access and decision certificates of Theorem M.10.5 for each member of a finite family $\mathcal E=\{E_1,\ldots,E_N\}$. <a id="proposition-m109-conditional-local-comparison-of-self-model-and-perspective-metrics"></a>**Proposition M.10.9 (Conditional Local Comparison of Self-Model and Perspective Metrics).** Let $\iota:U\subseteq\Theta_S\to\Sigma$ be a registered $C^1$ perspective-extraction map on a Fisher-normal neighborhood $U$ of $\theta_S$. Assume that $\iota$ is a local embedding and that, on a smaller neighborhood $U_0\Subset U$, it is co-Lipschitz:
$$
d_\Sigma(\iota(\theta),\iota(\theta'))
\ge C_S d_{\mathcal F_S}(\theta,\theta')
\qquad(\theta,\theta'\in U_0)
$$
for a recorded constant $C_S>0$. Then every pattern whose self-model update remains in $U_0$ satisfies
$$
d_\Sigma(\iota(\theta_S),\iota(\theta'_S))
\ge C_Sd_{\mathcal F_S}(\theta_S,\theta'_S).
$$
At the differential level, if
$$
C_{S,0}:=\inf_{\theta\in U_0}\inf_{\|v\|_{\mathcal F_S}=1}\|d\iota_\theta v\|_\Sigma>0,
$$
then the metric inequality is
$$
\iota^*g_\Sigma\succeq C_{S,0}^2g_{\mathcal F_S}.
$$
The reflexivity fraction $\sigma_S(E)$ alone supplies neither injectivity nor either metric bound.

*Proof.* The endpoint inequality is the co-Lipschitz hypothesis evaluated at $\theta_S$ and $\theta'_S$. For every tangent vector $v$,
$$
(\iota^*g_\Sigma)_\theta(v,v)
=\|d\iota_\theta v\|_\Sigma^2
\ge C_{S,0}^2\|v\|_{\mathcal F_S}^2
=C_{S,0}^2g_{\mathcal F_S}(v,v),
$$
which proves the tensor inequality. $\square$

<a id="definition-m109b-typed-semantic-perspective-bridge-certificate"></a>**Definition M.10.9b (Typed Semantic--Perspective Bridge Certificate).**

Let $\mathcal E_0\subseteq P$ be a declared comparison class in a Borel-registered semantic layer and define
$$
p\sim_\lambda q
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Delta_{\mathrm{rel}}(p,q)=0.
$$
Write $\overline{\mathcal E}_0:=\mathcal E_0/\!\sim_\lambda$. A typed semantic--perspective bridge consists of:

1. an injective registered map
   $$
   \bar\iota_P:\overline{\mathcal E}_0\to\Sigma;
   $$
2. constants $0<c_P\le C_P<\infty$ such that, for every $p,q\in\mathcal E_0$,
   $$
   c_P\Delta_{\mathrm{rel}}(p,q)
   \le
   d_\Sigma\!\left(\bar\iota_P[p],\bar\iota_P[q]\right)
   \le
   C_P\Delta_{\mathrm{rel}}(p,q);
   \tag{M.10.9b.1}
   $$
3. a common finite shared active algebra $\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{sh}}$, faithful states
   $$
   \rho_{[p]}>0
   $$
   on that algebra representing $\bar\iota_P[p]$, and the finite frame-pair/channel ledger of Definition M.6.10a.1 for every ordered pair used;
4. one of the following uniform alternatives for every $p,q\in\mathcal E_0$: either a direct directed comparison
   $$
   D(\rho_{[p]}\Vert\rho_{[q]})
   \ge
   c_P^\rightarrow
   \overrightarrow{\Delta}_{\mathrm{rel}}(p\Vert q)
   \tag{M.10.9b.2}
   $$
   with $c_P^\rightarrow>0$, or a trace-separation comparison
   $$
   \|\rho_{[p]}-\rho_{[q]}\|_1
   \ge
   b_P^\rightarrow
   \overrightarrow{\Delta}_{\mathrm{rel}}(p\Vert q)
   \tag{M.10.9b.3}
   $$
   with $b_P^\rightarrow>0$.

The directed discrepancy is well defined on $\overline{\mathcal E}_0$, because replacing either closure profile by a $\lambda$-almost-everywhere equal profile does not change the measure of its set difference. No subset of $P$ is called open unless a compatible topology generating the registered Borel structure is separately chosen.

<a id="proposition-m109c-conditional-transport-across-the-typed-bridge"></a>**Proposition M.10.9c (Conditional Transport Across the Typed Bridge).**

Under Definition M.10.9b,
$$
\Delta_{\mathrm{rel}}(p,q)\ge\epsilon

and

On the direct directed branch,

\!\left(

\right)
\ge
c_P^\rightarrow
\overrightarrow{\Delta}_{\mathrm{rel}}(p\Vert q).
\tag{M.10.9c.3}

On the trace-separation branch, quantum Pinsker gives

D(\rho_{[p]}\Vert\rho_{[q]})
\ge

gives (M.10.9c.4). ∎

These are dimensionless geometric and distinguishability bounds. <a id="proposition-m109e-explicit-finite-typed-bridge-bridge-nonuniqueness-and-the-separated-class-obstruction"></a>**Proposition M.10.9e (Explicit Finite Typed Bridge, Bridge Nonuniqueness and the Separated-Class Obstruction).**

1. Fix integers $n\ge1$ and $d\ge2$, weights $\omega_1>\omega_2>\cdots>\omega_d>0$ with $\sum_i\omega_i=1$, and $0<\theta\le\pi/(2n)$. 2. Distinct $\theta\in(0,\pi/(2n)]$ give populated bridges with distinct images of $p_1$, so Definition M.10.9b does not determine $\bar\iota_P$ from the semantic layer.

<a id="theorem-m109f-infinite-typed-bridge-criterion-and-source-relative-rational-physical-realization"></a>**Theorem M.10.9f (Infinite Typed-Bridge Criterion and Source-Relative Rational Physical Realization).**

#### Infinite metric classes and compact semantic obstruction

#### Scope of the abstract classification

We classify the abstract typed bridge on a fixed finite flag manifold $\Sigma =U(d)/T$ with its normal Riemannian metric, allowing a certificate to register its faithful shared-algebra assignment and pair channels, as the original definition does. This does not classify physical realizability or change a separately fixed physical state assignment. Discrepancies are the original closure-profile discrepancies. Write $X$ for the quotient, $\delta$ for symmetric discrepancy, and $\delta_{\mathrm{arrow}}$ for directed discrepancy. Then $0\le\delta_{\mathrm{arrow}}(x,y)\le\delta (x,y)$.

#### Theorem M.10.9f.1: exact finite-obstruction classification

The following are equivalent for any cardinality of X:

(A) X admits the abstract typed certificate M.10.9b on this $\Sigma$, with free registration of the state assignment and formal pair-channel ledger.

(B) There exist constants 0<$c\le C$<infinity such that, for every finite F subset X, points $z_{x}$ in $\Sigma$ can be chosen satisfying

$$
c \delta (x,y) \le \operatorname{dist}(z_x,z_y) \le C \delta (x,y), x,y\in F
$$

The SAME c,C must work for every finite F. Neither constants depending on F nor total boundedness alone suffice. Equivalently, there exist positive rational c,C with $c\le C$ for which every one of these finite compact feasibility problems is feasible. Thus failure is classified exactly by: for every rational c,C there is a finite infeasible configuration. This is a mathematical criterion, not a claimed terminating decision algorithm on arbitrary input presentations.

Proof. A implies B by restriction of its metric map. Conversely, take the compact product $\Sigma ^X$. For each unordered pair impose the displayed two closed inequalities. Any finite set of constraints involves finitely many points and is feasible by B. The finite-intersection property yields a simultaneous solution. The lower inequality makes it injective. This uses ordinary compactness (including the product compactness theorem for uncountable X), not an effective source of continuum coordinates. Rational constants follow by decreasing c and increasing C.

To supply the remaining abstract certificate, choose once and for all distinct positive weights $\omega_{1}>\dots>\omega_{d}$ with sum one, and define

$$
F(gT)=g \operatorname{diag}(\omega ) g^*, g \mathrm{in} U(d)
$$

This is well-defined and is a smooth embedding into faithful density matrices on $M_{d}(C)$. There is a number $a>0$ such that

$$
||F(s)-F(t)||_1 \ge a \operatorname{dist}(s,t) \quad\text{for all }s,t \mathrm{in} \Sigma
$$

Here is a full justification of the global lower bound. The differential on a horizontal tangent Z is [Z,diag($\omega$)], injective because its off-diagonal entries are $Z_{ij}(\omega _j-\omega _i)$. Compactness gives a uniform positive minimum singular value relative to the tangent and Hilbert-Schmidt norms. Smooth embedding charts then give a positive local inverse-Lipschitz constant on a neighborhood of the diagonal, using a finite chart cover and the inverse function theorem onto the embedded submanifold. On the complementary compact set dist(s,t)>=$\epsilon$, injectivity makes the continuous numerator attain a strictly positive minimum; divide by the finite diameter. Taking the minimum gives the asserted a. Trace norm dominates Hilbert-Schmidt norm. No uniform-faithfulness compactness assumption on a previously assigned state family is used: this is a newly registered fixed-spectrum assignment permitted by the abstract certificate.

Therefore the trace branch holds with $b_{\mathrm{arrow}}=ac$ since $\delta_{\mathrm{arrow}}\le \delta$. For every ordered pair choose representatives $g_{s}$,$g_{t}$ and the unitary channel $\operatorname{Ad}(g_t g_s^*)$, which maps $F(s)$ to $F(t)$. Choose

$$
L_{s,t}=\log F(s)-\log F(t)
$$

It is self-adjoint, satisfies the ledger operator inequality with equality, and has expectation $D(F(s)||F(t))$. These are exactly the zero-overhead formal unitary frame ledgers used by the canonical finite-chain construction. They supply no physical pulse, thermodynamic heat or source units. They claim only the same abstract ND-RID-compatible unitary branch as that construction. This completes B implies A at the declared abstract scope. $\square$

A separately prescribed state assignment or channel capability grammar must be checked in addition. This qualification is part of the distinction between abstract existence and source realization; it is not an extra admission gate.

#### Theorem M.10.9f.2: a continuum of positive Borel semantic examples

Take the Borel semantic carrier $P=[0,1]$, singleton value space, Lebesgue $\nu$, CPA identically zero and, at $p=t$, seed relation $A_{t}\times A_{t}$ with $A_{t}=[0,\sqrt{t}]$. The seed relation in $(t,s,u)$ is Borel. Reflexive transitive closure is $(A_{t}\times A_{t})$ union the diagonal. The diagonal has zero product measure, and the squares are nested. Hence

$$
\begin{gathered}
\delta (t,u)=|t-u|,\\\delta _{\mathrm{arrow}}(t||u)=(t-u)_+
\end{gathered}
$$

Let $\Sigma=U(2)/T$ and $X_{12}$ be the canonical unit-speed plane rotation generator. For $0<\theta<\pi/2$ put $s_{t}=\exp(\theta t\,X_{12})o$. The normal-metric flag distance on this minimizing arc is $\theta|t-u|$ (or the finite-chain lower/upper constants of Proposition M.10.9e suffice without this exact normalization). Let $\rho_{t}=\exp(\theta t\,X_{12})\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{1},\omega_{2})\exp(-\theta t\,X_{12})$, with $\omega_{1}>\omega_{2}>0$ and $\omega_{1}+\omega_{2}=1$. Direct two-by-two diagonalization gives

$$
\begin{gathered}
||\rho _t-\rho _u||_1=2(\omega _1-\omega _2)|\sin(\theta (t-u))|\\\ge 4(\omega _1-\omega _2)\theta |t-u|/\pi
\end{gathered}
$$

The pair channels and ledgers from Theorem M.10.9f.1 populate all formal certificate entries. This is a genuine infinite, indeed uncountable, registered Borel semantic layer, not a limit assertion from finitely many preselected points. It does NOT mean finite digital programs prepare every real t exactly or that the original physical/source $C_{\mathrm{P}}$ gate is discharged.

#### Theorem M.10.9f.3: compactness/total boundedness is not sufficient

There exists a COUNTABLE compact semantic comparison class whose discrepancy metric cannot admit a bridge into ANY finite-dimensional flag manifold. Thus the uniformly-separated obstruction of Proposition M.10.9e is not the only obstruction, even after all infinite separated families have been excluded.

Partition $[0,1]$ into Borel blocks $B_{n,i}$, $n\ge 1$, $1\le i\le n$, each of measure $b_{n}/n$ with $b_{n}=2^{-n}$. Split each block into two equal-measure Borel halves $B_{n,i}^0$ and $B_{n,i}^1$. Let $A_{0}$ be the union of all zero halves. For each $n$ and bit string $x$ in $\{0,1\}^n$, let $A_{n,x}$ agree with $A_{0}$ outside level $n$ and select half $x_{i}$ inside $B_{n,i}$. Every such set has measure $1/2$. Use one semantic label for each distinct set (all all-zero strings denote the single base class); choose these labels as a countable Borel subset of $P=[0,1]$. At those labels use seed $A\times A$; use $A_{0}\times A_{0}$ at every other $p$. The seed in $(p,s,u)$ is a countable union of Borel pieces, including the Borel complement of the label set, so is Borel. Its reflexive-transitive closure is again $(A\times A)$ union the null diagonal.

If $h=\nu$(A symmetric-difference B), then $\nu (A intersection B)=1/2$-h/2. Direct calculation gives

$$
\begin{gathered}
\delta (A,B)=1/2-2(1/2-h/2)^2=h-h^2/2,\\h/2 \le \delta (A,B) \le h
\end{gathered}
$$

Within the level-$n$ cube, $h=(b_{n}/n)\,\mathrm{Hamming}(x,y)$. All its $2^n$ vertices lie in the $\delta$-ball about $A_{0}$ of radius $b_{n}$; any two distinct vertices are separated by at least $b_{n}/(2n)$. The full countable family is compact: for every $\epsilon$, all sufficiently large levels lie in the $\epsilon$-ball about the base, and only finitely many earlier vertices remain. Every sequence either has a constant subsequence or levels tending to infinity and hence converges to the base. In particular no infinite $\epsilon$-separated subset exists.

Suppose there were a (c,C)-bi-Lipschitz bridge into a finite-dimensional compact flag manifold of real dimension m. The cube images lie in a ball of radius $Cb_{n}$ and are separated by at least $cb_{n}/(2n)$. A compact smooth m-dimensional Riemannian manifold has constants $K,r_{0}>0$ such that, for $0<r\le R\le r_{0}$, every r-separated subset of a radius-R ball has at most $K(1+R/r)^m$ elements. To verify this, take a finite collection of bilipschitz coordinate charts with a uniform Lebesgue radius, and compare disjoint Euclidean balls of radius proportional to r with the enclosing ball of radius proportional to R+r. For large n, $Cb_{n}\le r_{0}$; apply this estimate with $r=cb_{n}/(2n)$. It yields

$$
2^n \le K(1+2Cn/c)^m,
$$

which is impossible as n tends to infinity. No finite d works, since $m=d$(d-1) is finite for each such flag. $\square$

This counterexample is not a global no-go for infinite classes: Theorem M.10.9f.2 gives positive ones. Nor does it refute existence on the finite chain of Proposition M.10.9e or on any registered finite source.

The free Hamiltonian on energetic qubits is

<a id="theorem-m109-non-determination-by-shannon-entropy"></a>**Theorem M.10.9 (Non-Determination by Shannon Entropy).** On any branch satisfying Theorem M.10.2, there is no single-valued function $f$ such that

$$
for every retained pattern $E$.

$$

$$
a contradiction. Comparisons with Fisher information, Kolmogorov complexity, quantum information, or integrated information require a separately defined reduction map and are not conclusions of this theorem. ∎

<a id="theorem-m109g-algebraic-and-borel-refinements-of-the-infinite-typed-bridge"></a>**Theorem M.10.9g (Algebraic and Borel Refinements of the Infinite Typed Bridge).**

Let $X=\mathcal E_0/{\sim_\lambda}$ carry $\delta([p],[q])=\Delta_{\rm rel}(p,q)$ and $\delta_+([p],[q])=\overrightarrow{\Delta}_{\rm rel}(p\Vert q)$, so $0\le\delta_+\le\delta\le1$. Fix $d\ge2$ and the normal flag metric on $\Sigma_d=U(d)/U(1)^d$ induced by $\langle Y,Z\rangle=-\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(YZ)$. The following refinements classify intrinsic existence and state explicitly the further measurable-registration premise.

**Part I. The fixed algebraic orbit and its endpoint metric.**

Fix once and for all distinct rational faithful weights
$$
 \omega_i=\frac{2(d+1-i)}{d(d+1)},\quad 1\le i\le d,
 \qquad W=\operatorname{diag}(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_d).
$$
Other strictly decreasing positive weights summing to one work equally well. Define the compact set
$$
 K_\omega=\{A=A^*: \operatorname{Tr}(A^k)=\sum_i\omega_i^k,
                 \ 1\le k\le d\}.
 \tag{M.10.9g.1}
$$
Newton's identities show that a Hermitian matrix satisfying (M.10.9g.1) has characteristic polynomial $\prod_i(z-\omega_i)$. Consequently every member is a faithful density matrix, and
$$
 K_\omega=\{gWg^*:g\in U(d)\}.
$$
The map
$$
 F:\Sigma_d\longrightarrow K_\omega,\qquad F(gT)=gWg^*
 \tag{M.10.9g.2}
$$
is a smooth bijection with smooth inverse: its stabilizer is exactly the diagonal torus. Equivalently, its inverse assigns the ordered one-dimensional eigenspaces, which vary smoothly locally because all eigenvalues are simple.

**Uniform chordal and geodesic comparison.**

There are constants $0<\ell_\omega\le L_\omega<\infty$ such that
$$
 \ell_\omega d_\Sigma(s,t)
 \le \|F(s)-F(t)\|_2
 \le L_\omega d_\Sigma(s,t),
 \qquad L_\omega=\sqrt2(\omega_1-\omega_d).
 \tag{M.10.9g.3}
$$
Here $\|\cdot\|_2$ is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm, not the trace norm.

**Proof.** At the identity flag a horizontal tangent vector $Y$ has

$$
\|Y\|_\Sigma^2=\tfrac12\sum_{i\ne j}|Y_{ij}|^2,
$$

and
$$
 \|[Y,W]\|_2^2
 =\sum_{i\ne j}|Y_{ij}|^2(\omega_i-\omega_j)^2.
$$
If $\gamma=\min_{i\ne j}|\omega_i-\omega_j|>0$, the differential's singular values lie between $\sqrt2\gamma$ and $\sqrt2(\omega_1-\omega_d)$. Invariance gives the same bounds at every point. Integrating the upper bound along a minimizing geodesic proves the upper inequality.

For the lower inequality, compactness and smoothness give a uniform normal-coordinate radius and a uniform second-order remainder bound for $F(\exp_s v)-F(s)-dF_s v$. Shrinking the radius gives
$\|F(\exp_s v)-F(s)\|_2\ge(\gamma/\sqrt2)|v|$ for every base point and sufficiently small $v$. On the compact set of pairs separated by at least that radius, the continuous ratio $\|F(s)-F(t)\|_2/d_\Sigma(s,t)$ has a strictly positive minimum, since $F$ is injective. Take the smaller of this minimum and $\gamma/\sqrt2$. This proves (M.10.9g.3). ∎

This argument concerns chordal endpoint distance. A lower bound on differential speed alone would not justify a global endpoint bound without the local and compact off-diagonal arguments.

**Part II. Uniform finite polynomial tests.**

For a finite list of distinct points $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in X$ and numbers $0<a\le b<\infty$, define the following finite real polynomial feasibility problem $\mathsf{Flag}_d(a,b;x_1,\ldots,x_n)$:

Find Hermitian matrices $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ satisfying
$$
 \operatorname{Tr}(A_i^k)=\sum_j\omega_j^k
 \quad(1\le i\le n,\ 1\le k\le d),
 \tag{M.10.9g.4}
$$
$$
 a^2\delta(x_i,x_j)^2
 \le\operatorname{Tr}((A_i-A_j)^2)
 \le b^2\delta(x_i,x_j)^2
 \quad(1\le i,j\le n).
 \tag{M.10.9g.5}
$$
Write each off-diagonal entry in real and imaginary parts. Equations (M.10.9g.4) and inequalities (M.10.9g.5) are then an explicit real polynomial system in $nd^2$ variables. Positivity need not be separately imposed: (M.10.9g.4) and Hermiticity already fix the positive spectrum.

**The finite-test criterion.**

For **any** metric quotient $X$, including uncountable or incomplete quotients, the following are equivalent:

1. There exists an injective map $f:X\to\Sigma_d$ and uniform constants $0<c\le C<\infty$ with $c\delta\le d_\Sigma\circ(f\times f)\le C\delta$.
2. There exist **one pair** of positive rational constants $a\le b$, independent of the finite list, such that every finite list passes (M.10.9g.4)–(M.10.9g.5).
3. On the mathematical unitary frame-channel branch, the quotient can be equipped with the **intrinsic, set-theoretic** metric, common faithful-state, pair-channel and trace-separation data appearing in Definition M.10.9b. This item does not assert the registered/Borel clause of that definition; Borel registration follows only under Part III. A preassigned state assignment or narrower apparatus grammar is not required to be preserved.

If condition 2 holds with $a,b$, the constructed bridge can use
$$
 c_P=a/L_\omega,\quad C_P=b/\ell_\omega,
 \quad b_P^\rightarrow=a.
 \tag{M.10.9g.6}
$$
The completion of $X$ is compact and embeds with the same constants. In particular $X$ is separable.

**Proof.** If 1 holds, take $A_i=F(f(x_i))$. Part I gives (M.10.9g.5) with $a=\ell_\omega c$, $b=L_\omega C$; choose a smaller positive rational lower constant and a larger rational upper constant. This proves 2.

For 2 implies 1, form the compact product $K_\omega^X$. For each pair $x,y$, impose the closed cylinder condition (M.10.9g.5). Every finite family of these conditions involves finitely many points, and is satisfiable by condition 2; all remaining coordinates can be assigned $W$. The finite-intersection property therefore gives a simultaneous family $(A_x)_{x\in X}$. Put $f(x)=F^{-1}(A_x)$. Equation (M.10.9g.3) proves (M.10.9g.6), and the lower bound makes $f$ injective. No compatibility among independently chosen finite solutions was assumed; compactness supplies it.

Set $\mathfrak A_{\rm sh}=\mathcal B(\mathbb C^d)$ and $\rho_x=A_x$. Then
$$
 \|\rho_x-\rho_y\|_1\ge\|\rho_x-\rho_y\|_2
 \ge a\delta(x,y)\ge a\delta_+(x,y).
 \tag{M.10.9g.7}
$$
Choose unitaries $G_xWG_x^*=A_x$. The unitary channel
$\Phi_{xy}(B)=G_yG_x^*BG_xG_y^*$ sends $A_x$ to $A_y$. Every fixed pair has a finite-dimensional Hamiltonian realization over any declared $\tau>0$: if $G_yG_x^*=e^{iK_{xy}}$, $K_{xy}=K_{xy}^*$, take $H_{xy}=-\hbar K_{xy}/\tau$. This is the same reset-free mathematical unitary branch consumed by M.10.9e, not an independently verified physical control system.

The cost observable
$$
 L_{xy}=\log A_x-\log A_y
 \tag{M.10.9g.8}
$$
satisfies M.6.10a.2 at equality, and
$\operatorname{Tr}(A_xL_{xy})=D(A_x\Vert A_y)$. Thus the dimensionless ledger has zero stipulated overhead and meets the trace alternative of M.10.9b at the intrinsic, set-theoretic level, proving 3. Conversely 3 includes 1 by definition.

Any bi-Lipschitz image in the compact space $\Sigma_d$ is totally bounded. Its metric completion is identified with the closure of its image; the upper and lower inequalities extend by limits. The completion is compact and separable, and so is every subspace as regards separability. ∎

**Quantifiers and finite obstructions.** Condition 2 contains no infinite embedding, no manifold-distance variable, no state-logarithm constraint and no channel unknown. Each test is a specified finite polynomial problem. Failure at fixed $a,b$ has a finite obstruction by the proof. Passing every test with a **common** pair of constants gives a global solution. Merely passing each finite subset with its own constants is insufficient and would make the statement essentially vacuous. The criterion does not assert that one finite test decides an infinite instance or that a finite obstruction rules out all other distortion constants.

**Effectivity boundary.** For algebraic distance data and rational weights/constants, a finite test is decidable by real algebraic quantifier elimination. Arbitrary real distance data need an appropriate exact oracle; computable approximations alone do not decide equality. The infinite universal quantifier is not replaced by a halting algorithm. The compactness construction is an existence theorem, not an effective algorithm for a registered source.

**Part III. Borel registration and an explicit Borel frame section.**

Assume $\mathcal E_0$ is a standard Borel comparison space and that $p\mapsto\Delta_{\rm rel}(p,q)$ is Borel for each $q\in\mathcal E_0$. Then every metric embedding furnished by Part II pulls back to a Borel map $p\mapsto f([p])$, and its states, pair channels and pair cost observables can all be chosen Borel.

**Proof.** By Part II choose a countable dense family $[p_n]$ in $X$. Its rational-radius balls form a countable base, and their pullbacks are the Borel sets $\{p:\Delta_{\rm rel}(p,p_n)<r\}$. Hence the quotient map into the metric space $X$ is Borel, and its composition with the continuous $f$ is Borel. This does not presume that the original set-theoretic quotient carries an independently given standard Borel structure.

For an explicit frame selector, define the rank-one spectral projectors
$$
 P_i(A)=\prod_{j\ne i}\frac{A-\omega_j I}{\omega_i-\omega_j}.
$$
Let $j_i(A)$ be the first coordinate index with $P_i(A)e_{j_i}\ne0$, and take the $i$-th column of $G(A)$ to be
$$
 v_i(A)=P_i(A)e_{j_i(A)}/\|P_i(A)e_{j_i(A)}\|.
 \tag{M.10.9g.9}
$$
The choice partitions the orbit into finitely many Borel sets for each $i$; normalization is continuous on each selected set. Columns are unit orthogonal eigenvectors, so $G(A)$ is unitary, Borel and satisfies $G(A)WG(A)^*=A$. Thus $G(A_y)G(A_x)^*$ and the channel are Borel in the pair. The matrix logarithm in (M.10.9g.8) is continuous on the fixed faithful orbit. If Hamiltonians are needed, finite-dimensional Borel functional calculus with the principal spectral angle yields a Borel Hermitian logarithm of the pair unitary. A global **continuous** frame section is neither assumed nor asserted. ∎

**Scope of the Borel premise.** Definition P.16b.2.8 registers Borel seed/guard sets; Theorem P.16b.2.9 only concludes that the closed global relation is analytic. Analytic section-measure expressions do not automatically give the Borel distance premise above. If the closed global relation itself is Borel, ordinary parameter integration proves the premise. The semantic examples of Theorem M.10.9f have Borel closed relations. For a merely analytic nominated PU layer, Borel registration/effectivity remains an additional source obligation even though the intrinsic metric classification is exact.

**Part IV. Fixed-rank Euclidean tests and a flag-chart sufficient class.**

Schoenberg (1935)'s anchored-Gram criterion gives the finite Euclidean test below; the compactness argument extends it to the entire metric class. Fix $k\ge1$. For bounded $X$, uniform bi-Lipschitz embeddability in $\mathbb R^k$ is equivalent to the existence of $0<a\le b$ such that every finite set $x_0,\ldots,x_n$ has symmetric real numbers $s_{ij}$, $s_{ii}=0$, satisfying
$$
 a^2\delta(x_i,x_j)^2\le s_{ij}\le b^2\delta(x_i,x_j)^2,
 \quad G_{ij}=\tfrac12(s_{i0}+s_{j0}-s_{ij})\succeq0,
 \quad\operatorname{rank}G\le k.
 \tag{M.10.9g.10}
$$
If $k\le d(d-1)$, this condition suffices for Part II. Conversely every bridge into $\Sigma_d$ gives (M.10.9g.10) for $k=d^2-1$. Thus allowing any finite $d$, a bounded metric class admits a bridge exactly when it admits uniformly distorted, uniformly finite-rank Euclidean distance data as in (M.10.9g.10), for some finite $k$.

**Proof.** Necessity of (M.10.9g.10) is the Gram formula. For sufficiency factor $G=VV^T$, append the origin and obtain a realization of the finite distances in $\mathbb R^k$. Include one fixed base point in every finite test and translate its image to zero. All coordinates then lie in the compact Euclidean ball of radius $b\operatorname{diam}X$. The same closed-cylinder finite-intersection argument as in Part II produces a global Euclidean embedding.

A sufficiently small closed coordinate ball inside the $d(d-1)$-dimensional smooth flag manifold is bi-Lipschitz to a Euclidean ball: smooth metric bounds give the upper bound, and the inverse coordinate differential together with the compact off-diagonal argument gives the lower bound. Translate and rescale the bounded Euclidean image into a smaller such ball, and embed $\mathbb R^k$ into its first $k$ coordinates. Conversely, (M.10.9g.2) maps flags bi-Lipschitzly into the trace-one Hermitian affine space, of real dimension $d^2-1$. For variable finite dimension choose $d$ large enough that $d(d-1)\ge k$. ∎

Neither negative-type embeddability into an unrestricted Hilbert space nor total boundedness is a substitute for (M.10.9g.4)–(M.10.9g.5) at fixed $d$. The variable-dimension corollary must not silently enlarge a previously registered active algebra.

<a id="theorem-m109h-clock-weighted-entropy-histories-and-their-kinetic-limit"></a>**Theorem M.10.9h (Clock-Weighted Entropy Histories and Their Kinetic Limit).**

On the two-dimensional plane put
$$
X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\rho_\theta=e^{\theta X}\operatorname{diag}(2/3,1/3)e^{-\theta X},\qquad
\chi=\frac{\log2}{3},\qquad 0<\alpha\le\frac\pi2.
$$
The exact plane-rotation identity of Proposition M.10.9e gives
$$
D(\rho_\theta\Vert\rho_\phi)=\chi\sin^2(\phi-\theta).
$$
The following statements concern this declared entropy ledger and its angle-path interpolation.

**Part I. Unweighted endpoint sums.**

Let $T_0>0$ and let $\theta:[0,T_0]\to[0,\alpha]$ be absolutely continuous with $\dot\theta\in L^2$. For any partition $0=t_0<\cdots<t_m=T_0$, let $|\pi|$ be its maximum interval length. Then
$$
 \sum_i D(\rho_{\theta(t_i)}\Vert\rho_{\theta(t_{i+1})})
 \le \chi\,|\pi|\int_0^{T_0}|\dot\theta|^2dt
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{M.10.9h.1}
$$
For a nonconstant path, a single coarse endpoint cost may be positive. Thus the same endpoint ledger is not a refinement-invariant additive action with that nonzero endpoint value. A nontrivial continuum kinetic ledger requires additional time weights or another history cost.

**Proof.** $\sin^2 x\le x^2$. Cauchy–Schwarz gives $|\theta(t_{i+1})-\theta(t_i)|^2\le(t_{i+1}-t_i)\int_{t_i}^{t_{i+1}}|\dot\theta|^2$. Sum. ∎

**Part II. Positive clock-weighted kinetic limit.**

Fix a clock scale $\tau_c>0$, total duration $T_0>0$, and two endpoint angles in $[0,\alpha]$. For each uniform mesh $h=T_0/m$, let $V_h$ consist of continuous paths affine on each nominated mesh cell, with those endpoints and range in $[0,\alpha]$. On $C([0,T_0])$ with uniform topology define
$$
 \mathscr L_h(\theta)=\chi\tau_c\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}
          \frac{\sin^2(\theta(t_{i+1})-\theta(t_i))}{h},
\tag{M.10.9h.2}
$$
for $\theta\in V_h$, and $+\infty$ otherwise. Then these dimensionless ledgers are equicoercive and Gamma-converge to
$$
 \mathscr L(\theta)=\chi\tau_c\int_0^{T_0}|\dot\theta|^2dt
\tag{M.10.9h.3}
$$
on the corresponding $H^1$ paths, and $+\infty$ otherwise. Minima converge to $\chi\tau_c(\theta(T_0)-\theta(0))^2/T_0$, and all minimizing subsequences converge uniformly to the linear path. In particular, for any fixed $H^1$ path, its nodal interpolants form a recovery sequence.

**Proof.** Write $K_h=\sum_i|\Delta_i\theta|^2/h=\int|\dot\theta_h|^2$. Since $|\Delta_i\theta|\le\alpha\le\pi/2$,
$$
 \tfrac4{\pi^2}\chi\tau_c K_h\le\mathscr L_h\le\chi\tau_c K_h.
$$
A common sublevel has a common derivative $L^2$ bound and the Holder modulus $|\theta_h(t)-\theta_h(s)|\le\sqrt{K_h}|t-s|^{1/2}$. Its ranges are uniformly bounded, so Arzela–Ascoli proves equicoercivity. Moreover, for all $|x|\le\pi/2$, $0\le x^2-\sin^2x\le x^4/3$: integrate $|x|-|\sin x|\le|x|^3/6$ and multiply by $|x|+|\sin x|\le2|x|$. Since $\max_i|\Delta_i\theta_h|^2\le hK_h$,
$$
 0\le\chi\tau_c K_h-\mathscr L_h
 \le(\chi\tau_c/3)hK_h^2.
\tag{M.10.9h.4}
$$
For a uniformly converging sequence with bounded ledger, weak compactness of the derivatives gives an $H^1$ limit with the correct endpoints/range; weak lower semicontinuity and (M.10.9h.4) give the $\Gamma$ liminf. For a fixed admissible $H^1$ path, the derivative of its nodal interpolant is the cell average of its derivative. Cell averages converge strongly in $L^2$ as the maximum mesh size vanishes, by density of continuous functions and contraction of averaging. The interpolants converge uniformly and retain the range/endpoints; (M.10.9h.4) proves the recovery equality. The linear path uniquely minimizes (M.10.9h.3) by Cauchy–Schwarz, proving the minimum and cluster assertions. ∎

The angle path space here is a separately declared continuous interpolation completion; it does not require the semantic label set to be path-connected. The finite ledgers have positive time weights; they are not the unscaled sums in (M.10.9h.1). The factor $\tau_c/h$ is dimensionless. If one separately calibrates an action scale $\kappa_A>0$, positive multiplication gives $\kappa_A\mathscr L_h$ Gamma-converging to $\kappa_A\mathscr L$, as in Q.0. A rotor with inertia $I=2\kappa_A\chi\tau_c$ would have that kinetic expression, but no such mechanical carrier or equality with the original MPU frame process is asserted or used. This supplies the dimensionless variational interface and its exact required clock normalization, while retaining physical-action identification.

<a id="theorem-m109i-a-countable-thermal-bridge-with-exact-nominal-calorimetry-and-retained-responses"></a>**Theorem M.10.9i (A Countable Thermal Bridge with Exact Nominal Calorimetry and Retained Responses).**

All entropy and relative-entropy logarithms in this theorem are natural.

**Part I. A countable compact semantic source.**

Let
$$
 P=\{p_0,p_1,\ldots\}\cup\{p_\infty\},\quad
 V=\{v\},\quad \mu_V=\delta_v,
$$
with the discrete $\sigma$-algebra, $\nu(p_j)=2^{-j-1}$ for $j\ge0$, and $\nu(p_\infty)=0$. Every label has a finite syntax: a binary nonnegative integer or one reserved infinity token. Put CPA identically zero and $\mathcal E_0=P$. Register seeds
$$
 R_{p_n}^{\circ}=\{(p_0,p_j,v,v):1\le j\le n\},\qquad
 R_{p_\infty}^{\circ}=\{(p_0,p_j,v,v):j\ge1\}.
\tag{M.10.9i.2}
$$
The infinity seed has the finite decision procedure “first argument is 0 and second argument is a positive finite integer.” No infinite stored list is presumed.

**Exact closure and metric.**

With the original Seed, Reflexivity, Transitivity and CPA rules,
$$
 \mathsf R_{p_n}=\operatorname{Diag}(P)\cup R_{p_n}^{\circ},
\tag{M.10.9i.3}
$$
where the singleton valuation factors are suppressed. Define
$$
 u_n=\tfrac14(1-2^{-n}),\qquad u_\infty=\tfrac14.
$$
Then
$$
 \delta(p_a,p_b)=|u_a-u_b|,\qquad
 \delta_+(p_a\Vert p_b)=(u_a-u_b)_+.
\tag{M.10.9i.4}
$$
The quotient is injectively labelled by $\{u_n:n\ge0\}\cup\{1/4\}$, an infinite compact metric space. All relations and maps are Borel.

**Proof.** The seeds only have outgoing non-diagonal edges from $p_0$. There is no pair of composable non-diagonal seed edges. Adding the diagonal is therefore already reflexive and transitive, contains the seed and is the least closure. CPA adds nothing. Unlike the Lebesgue construction, the diagonal has positive mass here; it is common to every profile and cancels exactly from every set difference. For $a>b$,
$$
 \lambda(\mathsf R_{p_a}\setminus\mathsf R_{p_b})
 =\nu(p_0)\sum_{j=b+1}^a\nu(p_j)
 =2^{-b-2}-2^{-a-2}=u_a-u_b.
$$
The convergent geometric series gives the infinity case. Reverse differences vanish. Every countable subset is Borel, and the only accumulation point in the displayed metric realization is $1/4$, which is included. ∎

Every implementation statement below uses the declared Gibbs preparation and control family. The rational physical source of Theorem M.10.9f retains its own source and hierarchy scope.

**Part II. Gibbs energies and the semantic dictionary.**

Register a bath temperature $T>0$, energy gap $\epsilon=k_BT\ln2>0$, a clock unit $\tau>0$, and the quantum phase calibration constant $\hbar>0$. These are independent physical-theory input calibrations. The model does not derive any of them from semantic distance, alphabet size or $C_P$. Equivalently, one may first register $\epsilon>0$ and choose the temperature satisfying the displayed ratio.

Set $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$, $p=2/3$, $r=1/3$, $w=p-r=1/3$, choose one computably specified $0<\alpha\le\pi/2$ (for example $\alpha=\pi/4$), and put
$$
 X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
 \theta_a=4\alpha u_a,\quad g_a=e^{\theta_aX},
$$
$$
 H_a=\epsilon g_a|1\rangle\langle1|g_a^*,\quad
 \rho_a=g_a\operatorname{diag}(p,r)g_a^*
       =\frac{e^{-\beta H_a}}{1+e^{-\beta\epsilon}}.
\tag{M.10.9i.5}
$$
The energy zero is fixed: $-k_BT\log\rho_a=H_a+k_BT\ln(3/2)I$ for every $a$. The common scalar cancels in every pair work/ledger difference; it is not silently changed between labels.

The common shared algebra is $\mathcal B(\mathbb C^2)$. The ordered eigenflag is $f(p_a)=g_aU(1)^2$. A label compiles into the explicit Hamiltonian coefficients, Gibbs preparation request and duration; every finite query uses finitely many declared factors. The parameter family is not encoded as orthogonal programs inside one fixed finite register.

For every pair set $\vartheta=\theta_b-\theta_a$. Direct two-by-two algebra gives
$$
 \|\rho_a-\rho_b\|_1=2w|\sin\vartheta|,
 \quad D_{ab}:=D(\rho_a\Vert\rho_b)=w\ln2\sin^2\vartheta,
\tag{M.10.9i.6}
$$
$$
 L_{ab}:=\log\rho_a-\log\rho_b
          =\beta(H_b-H_a),\qquad \mathcal L_{ab}=\operatorname{Tr}\rho_aL_{ab}=D_{ab}.
\tag{M.10.9i.7}
$$
Thus the cost observable meets the original operator inequality at equality; it need not be positive. The nonnegative expectation is relative entropy.

The two-plane calculation of Proposition M.10.9e, with angle coordinate $4\alpha u$, gives valid uniform constants
$$
 C_P^{\rm metric}=4\alpha,\quad c_P^{\rm metric}=8\alpha/\pi,
 \quad b_P^\rightarrow=16\alpha/(3\pi).
\tag{M.10.9i.8}
$$
The superscript distinguishes the metric upper/lower constants from predictive physical complexity. The upper metric bound is the length of the rotation arc. The lower bound follows from $\|F(x)-F(y)\|_1\le2w d_\Sigma(x,y)$ and $\sin z\ge2z/\pi$ for $0\le z\le\pi/2$. In particular the trace branch of M.10.9b is nonvacuous for every distinct pair. No direct linear entropy lower bound is asserted.

**Part III. Exact thermal replacement, heat and driven work.**

**The supplied control grammar.**

The augmented service admits only:

- preparing one supplied fresh two-level Gibbs body with the specified finite Hamiltonian and temperature;
- the explicitly registered instantaneous Hamiltonian quench, understood as the ideal external-control primitive used by this formal branch;
- a positive-duration exchange pulse with the Hamiltonian below, followed by switching that pulse off;
- a nominated finite energy/Pauli instrument, its retained record, and the explicit finite swap-reset family of Part V;
- finite composition, classical outcome-conditioned selection among the registered commands, and the explicitly justified reset limit.

Each ideal quench is an admitted driven-model primitive, not an autonomous finite-clock theorem. This source tag and its calibration leaves are part of the claim. No undocumented switch, fresh bath, ready memory or external controller is made free. Work exchanges with the classical drive are recorded. Theorem M.10.9j constructs finite autonomous approximations using its additional clock state and positive static Hamiltonian family.

**Pairwise calorimetric realization.**

Start the shared qubit $S$ in $\rho_a$ with Hamiltonian $H_a$. Change its Hamiltonian instantaneously to $H_b$, preserving its state. Supply a fresh bath qubit $B$, independently prepared in Gibbs state $\rho_b$, with Hamiltonian $H_b$. Let $F$ be the swap on $S\otimes B$, and on the exchange interval use
$$
 H_0=H_b\otimes I+I\otimes H_b,\quad
 J=\frac{\pi\hbar}{2\tau}(I-F),\quad H_{\rm tot}=H_0+J.
\tag{M.10.9i.9}
$$
Write $V_b=e^{-iH_b\tau/\hbar}$. The final joint state, after switching off $J$, is
$$
 \rho_b\otimes\eta_{ab},\qquad
 \eta_{ab}=V_b\rho_aV_b^*.
\tag{M.10.9i.10}
$$
The exact reduced channel, including arbitrary reference extensions, is
$$
 \Phi_{ab}(\sigma)=\rho_b\operatorname{Tr}\sigma,
\qquad (\Phi_{ab}\otimes\mathrm{id})(\omega_{SR})
       =\rho_b\otimes\omega_R.
\tag{M.10.9i.11}
$$
The following channel response is uniform over inputs; the calorimetric identities below concern the nominated input $\rho_a$. Its complete Heisenberg response is $\Phi_{ab}^*(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_bA)I$. It is a replacement channel, not the earlier unitary frame channel; it has the same required nominated endpoint. The spent bath receives the initial state, rotated by $V_b$, and any initial reference correlations.

The quench, exchange and boundary switches obey
$$
 W^{\rm quench}_{ab}=\operatorname{Tr}\rho_a(H_b-H_a)=k_BT D_{ab},
$$
$$
 Q^{\rm frame}_{ab}=\operatorname{Tr}H_b(\eta_{ab}-\rho_b)
                  =k_BT D_{ab},\quad
 \Delta E_S^{\rm complete}=0,\quad
 W^{\rm exchange}_{ab}=0.
\tag{M.10.9i.12}
$$
Before any energy readout, for the nominal independent input the spent bath has
$$
 S(\eta_{ab})=S(\rho_b),\quad
 D(\eta_{ab}\Vert\rho_b)=D_{ab},\quad
 \Delta F_B=k_BT D_{ab}.
\tag{M.10.9i.13}
$$
Consequently the finite frame heat is an exact energy increment into an initially Gibbs body. It is not a pure-record erasure cost. No claim is made that the spent finite body is again thermal or can be reused as a fresh Gibbs input without a separately paid return.

**Proof.** Swap commutes with $H_0$; its eigenvalues are $\pm1$, so $e^{-iJ\tau/\hbar}=F$. Therefore $U=(V_b\otimes V_b)F$. Because $V_b\rho_bV_b^*=\rho_b$, (M.10.9i.10) and the reference version of (M.10.9i.11) follow. Both $H_0$ and $J$ commute with $H_{\rm tot}$. Switching $J$ on costs its initial expectation and switching it off returns exactly the same expectation, so the **net** exchange-drive work is zero. The nonzero temporary interaction energy is not discarded:
$$
 E_{\rm pulse}=\frac{\pi\hbar}{2\tau}
                  (1-\operatorname{Tr}\rho_a\rho_b).
\tag{M.10.9i.14}
$$
Quench work is (M.10.9i.7) times $k_BT$. Isospectrality gives $\operatorname{Tr}H_a\rho_a=\operatorname{Tr}H_b\rho_b=\epsilon r$, so the complete system energy change vanishes. Since $V_b$ commutes with $H_b$, bath-energy change equals $\operatorname{Tr}H_b(\rho_a-\rho_b)=k_BT D_{ab}$, using equal entropies and (M.10.9i.5). The same commutation and unitary invariance prove (M.10.9i.13). ∎

**Finite-time quench regularization.** The ideal sudden-quench identity has controlled finite-time, finite-slope approximants; no strict band-limited-control theorem is claimed. Over duration $\delta>0$, use the explicit linear ramp $H_\delta(t)=(1-t/\delta)H_a+(t/\delta)H_b$, followed by the same exchange. Since $\|H_\delta(t)\|\le\epsilon$, Duhamel's formula gives $\|U_\delta-I\|\le\epsilon\delta/\hbar$ and
$$
 \|U_\delta\rho_aU_\delta^*-\rho_a\|_1
 \le2\epsilon\delta/\hbar.
$$
The output shared state is still exactly $\rho_b$, but the spent bath receives the ramp-evolved input. Its heat $Q_{ab,\delta}$ and the full ramp work obey
$$
 W_{ab,\delta}=Q_{ab,\delta},\qquad
 |Q_{ab,\delta}-k_BT D_{ab}|
 \le2\epsilon^2\delta/\hbar,
\tag{M.10.9i.14a}
$$
uniformly in every pair. The work bound follows either by the complete first law or directly from $\int\operatorname{Tr}\rho(t)\dot H(t)dt$, comparing with the frozen-state quench and using $\|H_b-H_a\|\le\epsilon$. This proves a justified finite-time, finite-slope approximation to (M.10.9i.12), rather than identifying every finite ramp with that limit. The ramp rate $\|\dot H\|\le\epsilon/\delta$ diverges as $\delta\downarrow0$.

The exchange switches themselves can instead use any nonnegative smooth envelope $j(t)$ of finite duration, zero at its boundaries and with $\int j(t)dt=\pi\hbar/2$, multiplying $I-F$. All generators commute at different times, so the swap is exact and total envelope work is $\int\dot j(t)\langle I-F\rangle dt=0$. The same smooth-envelope observation applies to the readout copy pulse below. Thus no omitted finite switch-work term is needed for the exchange; precision/bandwidth of the quench limit remains visibly charged.

This proves a **total pairwise heat unit map on the declared family**:
$$
 \mathsf U_Q^{\rm frame}(a,b)=k_BT\mathcal L_{ab}.
\tag{M.10.9i.15}
$$
It is established by the independent energy spectrum, Gibbs law and energy balance. It is not obtained by defining “heat” to be $k_BT\mathcal L$.

**Part IV. Retained instruments, pointers and feedback.**

Let $P_j^{(b)}=g_b|j\rangle\langle j|g_b^*$. Read the spent bath energy with a registered nondemolition energy instrument. Its channel on the shared algebra, with retained classical outcome, is
$$
 \mathcal I_j^{ab}(\sigma)=\operatorname{Tr}(P_j^{(b)}\sigma)\rho_b,
 \quad j\in\{0,1\}.
\tag{M.10.9i.16}
$$
For general input the Gibbs bath remains independent initially. The two effects sum to $I$, so the instrument is normalized. The bath energy readout does not change mean bath energy. Register the normalized perspective kernel $G(\cdot\mid j,N)=\delta_{f(p_b)}$. Put the outcome in the full retained state and allow it to choose the next already registered command, for example $p_0$ after outcome 0 and $p_1$ after outcome 1. Thus the full outcome-dependent update is genuinely stochastic while the shared endpoint remains $\rho_b$. This directly instantiates the form of Definition 27/Definition 6 on the supplied instrument branch; it does not derive a Born selector from semantics.

At nominal input the excited-outcome probability is
$$
 z_{ab}=\operatorname{Tr}P_1^{(b)}\rho_a=r+w\sin^2\vartheta\in[1/3,2/3].
\tag{M.10.9i.17}
$$
Every outcome has positive probability. A finite record can be written by an energy-controlled copy into a degenerate ready bit. If a selector/dephasing instrument is used to regard the output as classical, its ancilla/output factors are explicitly retained or exported as spent source resources; an unreturned ready resource is not cyclic. The reset below treats the actual record marginal. It never infers that other copies of the outcome ceased to exist.

An explicit copy pulse into a degenerate ready memory $M$ is
$$
 J_{\rm read}=\frac{\pi\hbar}{2\tau_{\rm read}}
                  P_1^{(b)}\otimes(I-X_M).
\tag{M.10.9i.17a}
$$
It commutes with $H_b\otimes I$, generates controlled-X in duration $\tau_{\rm read}>0$, and has recovered on/off work, by the same commuting-energy argument as (M.10.9i.9). If $\widetilde\eta= e^{-iH_b\tau_{\rm read}/\hbar}\eta_{ab}e^{iH_b\tau_{\rm read}/\hbar}$, its full premeasurement bath-memory state is
$$
 \sum_{j,k}P_j^{(b)}\widetilde\eta P_k^{(b)}
                     \otimes|j\rangle\langle k|_M.
\tag{M.10.9i.17b}
$$
A second energy-degenerate ready pointer $E$, copied from $M$ by the same controlled-X pulse with control $|1\rangle\langle1|_M$, target $X_E$ and its own positive duration, gives the same expression, now redefining $\widetilde\eta$ with the total elapsed readout time to include bath free evolution during both copy pulses, with $|jj\rangle\langle kk|_{ME}$. On the retained classical bath-memory algebra, or after tracing the explicitly spent pointer $E$, the state is
$$
 \sum_jP_j^{(b)}\widetilde\eta P_j^{(b)}\otimes|j\rangle\langle j|_M.
\tag{M.10.9i.17c}
$$
With an initial reference, replace each bath block by the corresponding operator-valued bath-reference block; the same formulas hold. The bath marginal after readout is dephased and generally has larger entropy. Equation (M.10.9i.13) is **pre-readout only**; the post-readout bath, pointers and their correlations, (M.10.9i.17b)–(M.10.9i.17c), replace it in the full inventory. Mean bath energy is unchanged. A single-run classical selector remains the explicitly supplied Born-instrument leaf of the physical theory. Both initial ready pointers and any spent selector/environment output are charged source resources; their global renewal is not silently included in the one-memory reset below.

For a finite verification query, record its semantic labels, fixed control/energy/clock calibration, the nominated effect and outcome counts, and the actual bath/pointer/reset inventory. Repeating a binary effect on independent freshly prepared copies $M$ times gives empirical frequency within $\varepsilon$ of the predicted Born probability with failure at most $2e^{-2M\varepsilon^2}$. This is a finite-tolerance verifier for that retained query, not a certificate that finitely many calibration points prove an exact continuum control law. Each repetition owns its own fresh bath and ready-record resources. The Definition-27 arming predicate is true exactly upon invocation of a well-typed registered pair command; no SPAP threshold is inferred from this schedule. The next-command use of the recorded outcome supplies the required update ordering. All exact response claims remain relative to the declared source equations and admitted control precision.

For any finite sequence of these commands and effects, (M.10.9i.11) and (M.10.9i.16) recursively determine the joint response law. This is response faithfulness over the entire declared finite-word query grammar, including reference correlations. It does not claim faithfulness for extra omitted controls.

**Part V. The actual record-reset cell list and its uniform bounds.**

The frame channel itself has no entropy-reducing binary erasure: $S(\rho_a)=S(\rho_b)$. If its readout bit is retained for reuse, give that bit its own disjoint reset owner. Let its actual excited probability be $z=z_{ab}$. A known degenerate bit flip, when needed, replaces it by $a=\min(z,1-z)\in[1/3,1/2]$ without changing its entropy or exchanging energy. This flip does not consume a random seed.

Fix integer $n\ge1$, put $N=n^3$, $x_0=\ln((1-a)/a)\in[0,\ln2]$, and
$$
 x_j=x_0+j(n-x_0)/N,\quad
 g_j=(1+e^{x_j})^{-1},\qquad j=0,\ldots,N.
\tag{M.10.9i.18}
$$
Thus $g_0=a$ and $g_N=(1+e^n)^{-1}$. Supply exactly $N$ new independent Gibbs qubits with gaps $k_BTx_j$. First raise the degenerate memory gap to $k_BTx_0$. At step $j$, raise it to $k_BTx_j$, then exchange it with fresh bath cell $j$ using (M.10.9i.9) with matching Hamiltonians. At the end restore the memory Hamiltonian to zero. All switch work and the final energy release are included. No bath cell is reused.

**Exact finite response and calorimetry.**

The memory output is $\gamma_n=\operatorname{diag}(1-g_N,g_N)$, independent of every untouched reference after the last swap. For arbitrary reference-correlated inputs on the memory, the fixed protocol (M.10.9i.18), once its nominal marginal has been registered, obeys
$$
 \|\mathcal R_n-\mathcal R_0\|_\diamond=2g_N\le2e^{-n},
\tag{M.10.9i.19}
$$
where $\mathcal R_0$ is ideal ready-state replacement. For the registered nominal memory marginal $\operatorname{diag}(1-a,a)$, allowing arbitrary correlations with untouched references, the actual bath heat and net external work (the memory has zero boundary Hamiltonian) are
$$
 \beta Q^{\rm rec}_{ab,n}
 =\sum_{j=1}^{N}x_j(g_{j-1}-g_j)
 =h(a)-h(g_N)+\sum_{j=1}^{N}d(g_{j-1}\Vert g_j).
\tag{M.10.9i.20}
$$
Here $h$ and $d$ use natural logarithms. Uniformly over all semantic pairs,
$$
 0<\sum_jd(g_{j-1}\Vert g_j)\le\frac1{8n},
 \quad h(g_N)\le(n+2)e^{-n},
\tag{M.10.9i.21}
$$
$$
 \left|\beta Q^{\rm rec}_{ab,n}-h(z_{ab})\right|
 \le(n+2)e^{-n}+\frac1{8n}.
\tag{M.10.9i.22}
$$
Therefore this supplies the actual record heat $Q^{\rm rec}_{ab,n}$, and a justified exact-erasure limit $Q^{\rm rec}_{ab,n}\to k_BT h(z_{ab})$. The frame and record heats add because their bath cells are disjoint:
$$
 Q^{\rm declared}_{ab,n}=k_BT D_{ab}+Q^{\rm rec}_{ab,n}.
\tag{M.10.9i.23}
$$
This is the heat of the declared frame-plus-record strokes. It does not include an unmodeled return of spent baths or an autonomous realization of the external drive.

**Proof of this specialization.** The swap and reference-transfer calculation of Theorem 7.6r applies to the stated list of exactly $N=n^3$ cells: the initial memory content enters cell 1, each preceding Gibbs content enters the next cell, and the final Gibbs state replaces the memory, transferring every old memory-reference correlation to a spent bath. Its bath-energy and boundary-work calculation gives (M.10.9i.20). No initial extra bath at gap $x_0$ is inserted. The Gibbs curvature estimate proved in Theorem E.9.5h gives
$$
0<\sum_{j=1}^{N}d(g_{j-1}\Vert g_j)
\le\frac{N}{8}\left(\frac{n-x_0}{N}\right)^2
=\frac{(n-x_0)^2}{8n^3}\le\frac1{8n}.
$$
Here $0\le x_0\le\ln2<1\le n$, so every step has positive size. The entropy estimate of Theorem 7.6r uses $g_N\le e^{-n}$ and gives $h(g_N)\le(n+2)e^{-n}$. Since $h(a)=h(z)$, (M.10.9i.22) follows. These are the displayed physical cell list and nominal law, rather than a change to the general reset source. $\square$

**Complete side-information rule.** The arbitrary-reference replacement statement is an algebraic quantum-channel result; the Definition-28 bound invoked here is the complete finite classical-side-record specialization. If another unchanged record contains the outcome, it belongs in the Definition-28 side record $R$. The lower bound is then $k_BT H(M\mid R)$, which may be zero. Formula (M.10.9i.20) remains the actual heat of the specified reset, because it depends on the memory marginal and its actual bath-energy changes. It is not claimed to saturate the conditional bound when such side information exists. The construction does not erase every correlated copy while declaring it absent.

**Ready-state reuse.** Exact copies and exact finite-word responses in (M.10.9i.16) use a freshly supplied pure ready pointer, or the justified ideal-reset limit. A finite reset returns $\gamma_n$, with final excited population $(1+e^n)^{-1}$. Reusing it introduces copy/readout noise. For a finite adaptive word with reset precisions $n_1,\ldots,n_m$, trace-norm contractivity and a hybrid replacement argument give the complete query-output channel the diamond-error bound
$$
\min\left\{2,\ 2\sum_{j=1}^m\frac1{1+e^{n_j}}\right\}.
$$
This output includes all retained classical query records after the spent reset baths and selector factors are isolated or exported and never accessed again by the query. Their distinct complementary records remain in the resource inventory; the estimate is not a comparison of those complete microscopic spent outputs. The heat formula (M.10.9i.20) uses the registered actual input marginal and is not automatically the heat of a noisy reused-pointer run with a different marginal.

**Inventory and limit.** A finite reset uses $n^3$ Gibbs qubits, maximum gap $nk_BT$, total bare bath energy capacity at most $n^4k_BT$, and $n^3$ exchange intervals of duration $\tau$. Each exchange has maximum interaction energy $\pi\hbar/\tau$, temporarily supplied and recovered with its state-dependent switch work. These resources are finite for each $n$ and diverge in the exact-erasure limit. Initial Gibbs states, energy references, schedule precision, classical instructions and any ready readout bit remain declared source inputs. No fixed finite device is claimed to attain the limit.

The general finite-Gibbs and conditional-return calculations are Theorem 7.6r, Corollary 7.6r.1 and Theorem E.9.5h; this part fixes the actual cell list and uniform budget for the present thermal readout.

**Part VI. A separately paid phase-response calibration.**

The operator identity $L_{ab}=\beta(H_b-H_a)$ gives a physical work correspondence. Multiplying it by an arbitrarily chosen duration produces energy-times-time units, but no theorem identifies that product with the complete process's Lagrangian action. Likewise, (M.10.9i.14) is a genuine temporarily stored interaction energy, not a license to identify its time $\int$ with $\hbar D_{ab}$.

One can explicitly test the ledger by a separate registered Ramsey probe. For a degenerate probe initialized in $|+\rangle$, use
$$
 H^{\rm probe}_{ab}=|1\rangle\langle1|\otimes E_*L_{ab}
\tag{M.10.9i.24}
$$
with independently calibrated energy $E_*>0$, on a new calibration copy in $\rho_a$. Equation (M.10.9i.24) is the **full** generator on probe and calibration copy during that interval: the original free $H_a$ is switched off or exactly compensated as a separately registered control. A noncommuting free $H_a$ must not be left implicit. After duration $u$, its coherence factor, defined as twice the probe density-matrix entry (1,0), is
$$
 \chi_{ab}(u)=\operatorname{Tr}\rho_a
                  e^{-iE_*uL_{ab}/\hbar},\qquad
 \chi_{ab}'(0)=-i(E_*/\hbar)D_{ab}.
\tag{M.10.9i.25}
$$
For the unshifted Hamiltonian (M.10.9i.24), let $U_L=e^{-iE_*uL_{ab}/\hbar}$ and $\rho'_S=(\rho_a+U_L\rho_aU_L^*)/2$. With bare $H_a$ before and after the probe interval and zero probe bare energy, the switch works are exactly
$$
 W_{\rm on}^{\rm probe}=E_*D_{ab}/2-\epsilon r,\quad
 W_{\rm off}^{\rm probe}=\operatorname{Tr}H_a\rho'_S-E_*D_{ab}/2,
$$
so their sum is $\operatorname{Tr}H_a(\rho'_S-\rho_a)$. This owns the free-Hamiltonian compensation rather than declaring it costless. Probe/readout records and the fresh $|+\rangle$ resource have their own return owners.

This is a total phase-response dictionary on the declared pair family. It is a separately owned calibration probe; its preparation, pulse, readout and reset are not the original frame operation for free. The source matrix is finite, with $\|L_{ab}\|=\ln2|\sin\vartheta|\le\ln2$. If a nonnegative pulse Hamiltonian is wanted, add $E_*\ln2 I$ inside the controlled branch and retain its known, observable reference phase. Removing that phase from analysis does not remove its source energy from the inventory.

The equation $E_*u_* = \hbar$ can choose a probe duration; it does not prove that the original frame's mechanical action equals $\hbar D_{ab}$. The calibration is distinguished from the ledger-specific identification that remains required by M.10.9c.

<a id="theorem-m109j-finite-positive-clock-realization-of-the-thermal-service-with-complete-error-and-resource-bounds"></a>**Theorem M.10.9j (Finite Positive Clock Realization of the Thermal Service with Complete Error and Resource Bounds).**

Use the qubit family $H_a,\rho_a$, gap $\epsilon=k_BT\ln2$ and nominal pair heat
$$
q_{ab}=k_BT D(\rho_a\Vert\rho_b)
=\frac\epsilon3\sin^2(\theta_b-\theta_a)
$$
of Theorem M.10.9i. For each pair and positive absolute state and energy tolerances, the following finite-dimensional positive time-independent Hamiltonian approximates its ramp-plus-SWAP service. The finite initial pure clock, fresh Gibbs bodies, phase/energy calibration and specified static coupling matrix are owned inputs. The channel estimate includes arbitrary reference extensions; all stated nominal bath/debit estimates use the prescribed nominal source input. The Fourier cutoff is denoted $N$ in this theorem, while the reset index is $n$ and its cell count is $m=n^3$.

Construction E.9.5f.32 supplies the smooth multi-clock theorem. Here an $H^1$ packet gives explicit algebraic bounds for Lipschitz profiles and then for bounded measurable profiles; Parts II–VIII apply them to this thermal source, its actual interaction endpoints and its reset word. Exact logarithmic ledgers and exact replacement channels belong to Theorem M.10.9i; the finite clock supplies the displayed controlled approximations.

**Part I. The finite clock and low-regularity comparison.**

Let $\mathcal H_A$ be any finite-dimensional target space. All $L^2$ norms on the time-coordinate circle use its Lebesgue measure $dx$. Fix a time-coordinate circle $\mathbb R/P\mathbb Z$. Let $K(x)$ be a periodic, self-adjoint, Lipschitz operator on $A$, with

$$
\|K(x)\|\le M_0,\qquad \|K'(x)\|\le M_1\quad\text{a.e.}
\tag{M.10.9j.1}
$$

The coordinate has units of time; the ideal clock velocity is one. This convention makes its momentum energy operator $-i\hbar\partial_x$. The infinite ideal clock is only an intermediate proof device, not the implemented source.

Choose $0<w<P/2$ and the normalized real even packet

$$
 f_w(x)=\sqrt{\frac{15}{16w}}(1-x^2/w^2)\mathbf1_{[-w,w]}(x),
 \qquad a:=\|f_w'\|_2=\frac{\sqrt{5/2}}w.
\tag{M.10.9j.2}
$$

Its weak derivative is square-integrable; differentiability at its support endpoints is not required. Let $P_N$ project onto the Fourier modes $e_n(x)=P^{-1/2}e^{2\pi inx/P}$, $-N\le n\le N$, and put

$$
 q_N=\frac{P}{2\pi(N+1)},\quad q_Na<1,\qquad
 |f_N\rangle=\frac{P_Nf_w}{\|P_Nf_w\|_2}.
\tag{M.10.9j.3}
$$

The implemented clock has $d_C=2N+1$, with

$$
 H_{C,N}=\frac{2\pi\hbar}{P}\sum_{n=-N}^N(n+N)|n\rangle\langle n|,
 \quad K_N=(P_N\otimes I)K(x)(P_N\otimes I),
 \quad H_N=H_{C,N}\otimes I+K_N.
\tag{M.10.9j.4}
$$

Here $K(x)$ is multiplication on the circle. In finite matrices,

$$
 \langle n|K_N|m\rangle=\frac1P\int_0^P
   e^{2\pi i(m-n)x/P}K(x)\,dx.
\tag{M.10.9j.5}
$$

Thus no unspecified infinite controller appears in the implementation. When $K(x)\ge0$, $H_N\ge0$. In all cases

$$
 0\le H_{C,N}\le\frac{4\pi\hbar N}{P}I,
 \qquad E_C(0)=\langle f_N|H_{C,N}|f_N\rangle
                =\frac{2\pi\hbar N}{P}.
\tag{M.10.9j.6}
$$

The last equality uses the packet's symmetric Fourier probabilities. The spectral shift is fully included in the supplied energy; it is not discarded as a free resource.

For $t\ge0$ define

$$
 C(t)=a+\frac{\min\{tM_1,2M_0\}}{\hbar}
       +\frac{M_0}{\hbar}\left(at+\frac{\min\{M_1t^2/2,2M_0t\}}{\hbar}\right),
 \quad e_N(t)=q_N C(t)+q_N^2a^2,
 \quad \xi_N(t)=\min\{2,2e_N(t)\},\quad \xi_0=2q_Na.
\tag{M.10.9j.7}
$$

**Reference-uniform finite-clock bound.**

Start the finite clock in $|f_N\rangle$, independently of any state on $A$ and any reference $R$. The finite evolution under (M.10.9j.4), embedded in the circle space, is within trace norm $\xi_N(t)$ of the evolution under

$$
 H_\infty=-i\hbar\partial_x+K(x)
$$

from $|f_w\rangle$ and the same target/reference state. This is a reference-uniform statement. Initial trace distance is at most $\xi_0$. For a pure input, its ideal characteristic solution is

$$
 \Psi_t(x)=f_w(x-t)U(x,x-t)\chi,
\tag{M.10.9j.8}
$$

where $U(v,u)$ is the time-ordered propagator of $K$ from coordinate $u$ to coordinate $v$.

**Proof.** Bounded self-adjoint multiplication perturbs the self-adjoint circle derivative; the characteristic solution (M.10.9j.8) is unitary and gives the evolution. For any reference extension, Duhamel differentiation of the characteristic propagator gives

$$
 \|\partial_x\Psi_t\|_2\le a+\min\{tM_1,2M_0\}/\hbar,
 \quad \|(I-P_N)\Psi_t\|_2\le q_N(a+\min\{tM_1,2M_0\}/\hbar).
\tag{M.10.9j.9}
$$

The additional bound by $2M_0$ follows directly from

$$
 \partial_xU(x,x-t)=-(i/\hbar)K(x)U(x,x-t)
                     +(i/\hbar)U(x,x-t)K(x-t).
$$

The second inequality is Parseval applied to the modes $|n|\ge N+1$. Initially let $s=\|P_Nf_w\|$; then

$$
1-s\le1-s^2\le q_N^2a^2.
$$

Projecting the infinite Schrödinger equation onto $P_N$ leaves residual $P_NK(I-P_N)\Psi_t$. The derivative operator itself commutes with $P_N$, so it generates no residual. Duhamel in the finite space yields

$$
 \|\Psi_{N,t}-P_N\Psi_t\|_2
 \le q_N^2a^2+
 \frac{M_0q_N}{\hbar}\left(at+\frac{\min\{M_1t^2/2,2M_0t\}}{\hbar}\right).
\tag{M.10.9j.10}
$$

Adding the tail (M.10.9j.9) proves the vector bound $e_N(t)$. In this vector comparison remove the scalar shift $2\pi\hbar N/P$ from the finite Hamiltonian, or equivalently align its global phase. Density matrices and all energy differences are unaffected. Pure-state trace distance is at most twice vector distance. Purification and partial trace give the general reference-uniform result. The initial pure-state trace distance is exactly $2\sqrt{1-s^2}\le2q_Na$. ∎

This elementary algebraic-rate bound is deliberately not optimized. In particular it does not claim the stronger asymptotic rate of the quasi-ideal-clock literature.

**Part II. The complete thermal table and observation guards.**

Fix any pair $(a,b)$, any $w,\delta,\tau>0$, and define

$$
 T_f=4w+\delta+\tau,\qquad P=2T_f+4w=12w+2\delta+2\tau.
\tag{M.10.9j.11}
$$

Let $F$ be SWAP on the two qubits $A=S\otimes B$. Define a periodic system Hamiltonian $H_S(x)$ as follows:

- $H_a$ up to coordinate $2w$, including the initial packet support $[-w,w]$;
- the linear ramp $H_a+(x-2w)(H_b-H_a)/\delta$ on $[2w,2w+\delta]$;
- $H_b$ until coordinate $T_f+2w$;
- a linear return to $H_a$ of length $\delta$, beginning at $T_f+2w$;
- $H_a$ for the rest of the period.

The unwrapped description is consistent across coordinate zero because it is constant there. Put $x_s=2w+\delta$,

$$
 j(x)=\begin{cases}
 \dfrac{\pi\hbar}{\tau}\sin^2\!\dfrac{\pi(x-x_s)}\tau,
       &x_s\le x\le x_s+\tau,\\
 0,&\text{elsewhere},
 \end{cases}
 \qquad K(x)=H_S(x)\otimes I+I\otimes H_b+j(x)(I-F).
\tag{M.10.9j.12}
$$

Extend $j$ periodically. No trajectory beginning in $[-w,w]$ reaches the return ramp during $[0,T_f]$; its endpoint lies in $[T_f-w,T_f+w]$, strictly inside the final constant plateau. Periodic completion makes the finite matrix well-defined but is not used as an uncharged reset. Re-running through it is outside the claimed one-shot protocol.

The spectral and Lipschitz constants, uniform in all pairs, are

$$
 K\ge0,\quad M_0=2\epsilon+\frac{2\pi\hbar}{\tau},\qquad
 M_1=\max\left\{\frac\epsilon\delta,
                         \frac{2\pi^2\hbar}{\tau^2}\right\}.
\tag{M.10.9j.13}
$$

The ramp and pulse derivative supports are disjoint. The pulse area is $\pi\hbar/2$, so it produces exact SWAP in the ideal characteristic dynamics. Bath $B$ has the fixed bare Hamiltonian $H_b$ at all times. No heat convention is changed.

There is an endpoint observation window: every
$$
 3w+\delta+\tau\le t<5w+\delta+\tau
\tag{M.10.9j.14}
$$
puts all ideal characteristics after SWAP and before the return ramp. Replace $T_f$ by the selected $t$ in (M.10.9j.7) for its finite-clock error. This window describes output availability; it does not require switching the Hamiltonian off at an exact reading time. No infinite waiting or permanent halting claim is made.

**Exact ideal endpoint for every clock offset.**

Write $A_i=H_a\otimes I+I\otimes H_b$ and $A_f=H_b\otimes I+I\otimes H_b$. For every packet offset $y\in[-w,w]$,

$$
 U(T_f+y,y)=e^{-iA_fy/\hbar}U(T_f,0)e^{iA_iy/\hbar}.
\tag{M.10.9j.15}
$$

This follows from the composition law and the constant endpoint plateaus, including signed $y$. For every input $\omega_{SR}$, with independent bath $\rho_b$, tracing the ideal clock and bath gives exactly

$$
 \rho_b\otimes\omega_R.
\tag{M.10.9j.16}
$$

Indeed each diagonal clock coordinate implements a system-only ramp followed by SWAP, with endpoint free phases; $\rho_b$ is invariant under those phases. Off-diagonal clock coordinates disappear when the clock is traced. This argument does not assert that the untraced ideal joint state is already a product.

For the nominal Gibbs input $\rho_a\otimes\rho_b$, the initial phase in (M.10.9j.15) leaves the state unchanged, and the final phase preserves bath energy. Thus ideal bath heat is independent of the offset and equals

$$
 Q_\delta=\operatorname{Tr}H_b(R_\delta\rho_aR_\delta^*-\rho_b),
 \qquad |Q_\delta-q_{ab}|\le\frac{2\epsilon^2\delta}{\hbar},
\tag{M.10.9j.17}
$$

where $R_\delta$ is the system's finite linear-ramp propagator. The bound follows from $\|R_\delta-I\|\le\epsilon\delta/\hbar$. The complete nominal system energy change from $H_a$ to $H_b$ is zero. The ideal expectation of $K$ increases by precisely $Q_\delta$.

**Part III. Actual bath energy, clock debit and interaction endpoints.**

Prepare the finite clock in $f_N$, the bath independently in its fresh Gibbs state $\rho_b$, and the nominal system in $\rho_a$. No initial clock-target correlation is assumed. Let $\sigma_N(t)$ be the full evolved state. Define actual bath-energy increment and actual mean clock-energy debit by

$$
 Q_N=\operatorname{Tr}H_b(\sigma_{B,N}(T_f)-\rho_b),
 \qquad W_N=-\operatorname{Tr}H_{C,N}(\sigma_{C,N}(T_f)-|f_N\rangle\langle f_N|).
\tag{M.10.9j.18}
$$

The word "debit" here is important: an energy expectation alone is not proof of entropy-free, reusable or extractable work storage.

**Finite source estimates.**

For the finite autonomous Hamiltonian (M.10.9j.4), (M.10.9j.11)–(M.10.9j.13),

$$
 \|\Phi_N-\mathcal R_{\rho_b}\|_\diamond\le\xi_N(T_f),
 \qquad
 |Q_N-q_{ab}|\le\epsilon\xi_N(T_f)+\frac{2\epsilon^2\delta}{\hbar},
\tag{M.10.9j.19}
$$

and

$$
 W_N=\Delta\langle K_N\rangle\quad\text{exactly},\qquad
 |W_N-q_{ab}|\le M_0[\xi_N(T_f)+\xi_0]
                             +\frac{2\epsilon^2\delta}{\hbar}.
\tag{M.10.9j.20}
$$

Here $\mathcal R_{\rho_b}$ is the replacement channel and $\Phi_N$ uses the prescribed independent clock/bath inputs. The state-uniform trace estimate of Part I establishes the displayed diamond bound by the standard state-and-reference characterization for a difference of channels.

**Proof and endpoint interaction inventory.** Equation (M.10.9j.19) follows from Part II, contraction of trace norm, and the bounded bath observable. Total energy conservation for the time-independent finite $H_N$ proves the first identity in (M.10.9j.20). To prove its estimate, compare $K_N$ in the finite state with $K$ in the ideal characteristic state; compression makes these the same observable on the embedded finite state. Its norm is bounded by $M_0$, uniformly in $N$. Initial and final errors are at most $M_0\xi_0$ and $M_0\xi_N(T_f)$; the ideal difference is $Q_\delta$.

For an explicit endpoint decomposition define

$$
 R_i=K_N-I_C\otimes A_i,\quad R_f=K_N-I_C\otimes A_f,
 \quad r_i=\operatorname{Tr}R_i\sigma_N(0),\quad
 r_f=\operatorname{Tr}R_f\sigma_N(T_f).
$$

Then the exact finite ledger is

$$
 W_N=Q_N+\Delta E_{S,N}+r_f-r_i,
 \qquad \Delta E_{S,N}=\operatorname{Tr}H_b\sigma_{S,N}(T_f)-\epsilon r,
\tag{M.10.9j.21}
$$

with

$$
 |\Delta E_{S,N}|\le\epsilon\xi_N(T_f),\quad
 |r_i|\le(M_0+2\epsilon)\xi_0,\quad
 |r_f|\le(M_0+2\epsilon)\xi_N(T_f).
\tag{M.10.9j.22}
$$

Ideal endpoint residuals vanish because of the support guards. Finite Fourier packets have tails, so the finite residuals generally do not vanish. All are retained. Relative to a single fixed bare system Hamiltonian $H_a$, the late conditional term $H_b-H_a$ is part of the interaction energy; it is never silently thrown away. Equation (M.10.9j.21) uses the explicitly nominated effective endpoint Hamiltonians.

No step bounds the growing clock energy by clock norm times trace error. That shortcut would not prove energy convergence. ∎

**Explicit cutoff and tolerance choice.**

For $0<\eta\le1$, take

$$
 N=\left\lceil\frac{2P C(T_f)}{\pi\eta}\right\rceil.
\tag{M.10.9j.23}
$$

Then $q_N C(T_f)\le\eta/4$, $q_Na\le\eta/4$, and
$\xi_N(T_f)\le5\eta/8\le\eta$, $\xi_0\le\eta/2$. Given tolerances $\eta_S>0$ and $\eta_E>0$, choose

$$
 0<\delta\le\frac{\hbar\eta_E}{4\epsilon^2},\qquad
 0<\eta\le\min\{1,\eta_S,\eta_E/(3M_0)\},
\tag{M.10.9j.24}
$$

and use (M.10.9j.23). Both actual energy quantities are within $\eta_E$ of $q_{ab}$, and the channel error is at most $\eta_S$. The complete space has dimension $4(2N+1)$, clock energy (M.10.9j.6), and total Hamiltonian norm at most $4\pi\hbar N/P+M_0$. Every parameter is finite for positive tolerances. All bounds are uniform over the semantic pairs at a fixed absolute tolerance, but the table (M.10.9j.12) is pair-dependent.

Because distinct semantic pairs can have arbitrarily small $q_{ab}>0$, a uniform absolute tolerance is not uniform relative accuracy and does not prove $W_N\ge0$ for every pair. For an individual distinct pair, choosing $\eta_E<q_{ab}$ ensures positive debit. This may require pair-dependent resources. The stipulated replacement channel is retained even for identical labels; it is not replaced by an identity channel. The present construction does not claim exact zero-error finite operation.

**Part IV. Coefficient and preparation precision.**

The Fourier integrals in (M.10.9j.5), the packet coefficients and normalization are computable from the registered pair and scalar data. Exact symbolic matrices are a mathematical specification, not a claim of infinitely precise laboratory manufacture. If the implemented coupling is $K_N+E$, $\|E\|\le\nu$, and the actual prescribed clock/bath resource state has trace error at most $\zeta$, still independent of the target input and reference, Duhamel gives an added final trace error at most $\zeta+2T_f\nu/\hbar$. Equations (M.10.9j.19)–(M.10.9j.20) remain valid with added bounds

$$
 \text{bath: }\epsilon(2\zeta+2T_f\nu/\hbar),\qquad
 \text{clock debit: }M_0(2\zeta+2T_f\nu/\hbar)+2\nu.
\tag{M.10.9j.25}
