$$

Here actual bath heat subtracts its actual initial energy, so preparation error is counted at both endpoints. The clock Hamiltonian calibration itself is held fixed in this perturbation statement. An arbitrary Hermitian error may spoil positivity; adding the declared scalar $\nu I$ to the implemented total Hamiltonian restores nonnegativity without changing dynamics or energy differences, and gives the explicit bound $\|H_N+E+\nu I\|\le\|H_N\|+2\nu$. The debit proof again uses exact conservation of the implemented Hamiltonian, now retaining $\Delta\langle E\rangle$, rather than continuity of an unbounded family of clock observables. A Hermitian entrywise error at most $\nu/[4(2N+1)]$ suffices for the stated operator error. Hence finite coefficient precision suffices for any positive prescribed tolerance.

**Part V. Joint state, entropy and the owned energy limit.**

Under the endpoint guards, (M.10.9j.15) also implies

$$
 \|U(T_f+y,y)-U(T_f,0)\|
 \le (\|A_i\|+\|A_f\|)|y|/\hbar\le4\epsilon w/\hbar.
$$

Integrating the squared vector difference against $|f_w(y)|^2$ gives an ideal joint-state trace distance at most $8\epsilon w/\hbar$ from the product of the translated pure packet and the nominated driven output. Thus the **finite complete state**, with any target reference, is within

$$
 \zeta_N:=\xi_N(T_f)+\xi_0+8\epsilon w/\hbar
\tag{M.10.9j.26}
$$

of
$$
 e^{-iH_{C,N}T_f/\hbar}|f_N\rangle\langle f_N|e^{iH_{C,N}T_f/\hbar}
 \otimes U(T_f,0)\rho_{AR}U(T_f,0)^*.
\tag{M.10.9j.27}
$$

The finite translated packet is compared with the ideal translated packet at cost $\xi_0$. This proves genuine small endpoint correlations, rather than merely separate marginal accuracy. If $p_N=\zeta_N/2\le1-1/d_C$, entropy continuity gives

$$
 S(\sigma_{C,N}(T_f))\le h_2(p_N)+p_N\ln(d_C-1).
\tag{M.10.9j.28}
$$

For a direct proof, set $q=1-\langle f_N^{\rm free}|\sigma_C|f_N^{\rm free}\rangle\le p_N$; its largest eigenvalue is at least $1-q$, and the entropy is maximized by equalizing all remaining eigenvalues. The resulting $h_2(q)+q\ln(d_C-1)$ increases up to $q=1-1/d_C$. Here $h_2$ uses natural logarithms; if the displayed premise fails use the trivial bound $\ln d_C$. For the nominal mixed input, mutual information between clock and target is at most twice the clock entropy.

For an explicit simultaneous limit, fix $\tau>0$, take $w=\delta=\lambda\tau$, $\eta=\lambda^2$, $0<\lambda\le1$, and use (M.10.9j.23). Then

$$
 N=\Theta(\lambda^{-3}),\quad \zeta_N=O(\lambda),\quad
 S(\sigma_{C,N}(T_f))=O(\lambda\ln(1/\lambda))\to0,
\tag{M.10.9j.29}
$$

The lower bound follows from $C(T_f)\ge a=\sqrt{5/2}/(\lambda\tau)$ and $P\ge2\tau$ in (M.10.9j.23); all other scales are bounded above as stated. Meanwhile $Q_N,W_N\to q_{ab}$, and $E_C(0)=\Theta(\lambda^{-3})$ diverges. The exact debit (M.10.9j.18) survives even though the clock becomes trace-close to its free pure orbit: state convergence with growing energy range does not imply energy convergence. No costless reset or catalytic return is inferred. The supplied pure clock, the fresh Gibbs bath, phase/energy calibration, and construction of each finite static table remain resource owners.

**Part VI. Frame-only passive energy and ergotropy.**

One can quantify more than the clock's mean-energy debit, without assuming a source-reset protocol. For a state $\sigma$ on this fixed finite clock define its passive energy and ergotropy by

$$
 E_{\rm pas}(\sigma)=\min_V\operatorname{Tr}(H_{C,N}V\sigma V^*),
 \qquad \mathcal W(\sigma)=\operatorname{Tr}(H_{C,N}\sigma)-E_{\rm pas}(\sigma),
\tag{M.10.9j.29a}
$$

where the minimum is over clock unitaries. This is the standard unitary-orbit notion, following Allahverdyan, Balian and Nieuwenhuizen (2004); it does not certify an available autonomous extractor.

The exact frame starts with a pure clock and a four-dimensional target. Its joint state's rank is at most four, hence the reduced clock rank is at most sixteen. Let $p=\min\{1,\zeta_N/2\}$ and $\Delta_C=2\pi\hbar/P$. Its largest eigenvalue is at least $1-p$. Place this eigenvector at the zero-energy level and the remaining at most fifteen eigenvectors in the next fifteen levels. Their total probability is at most $p$. Therefore

$$
 0\le E_{\rm pas}(\sigma_C(T_f))
       \le\min\{15,2N\}\Delta_Cp,
\tag{M.10.9j.29b}
$$

and since the initial pure clock has zero passive energy,

$$
 W_N\le\mathcal W(|f_N\rangle\langle f_N|)-\mathcal W(\sigma_C(T_f))
       \le W_N+15\Delta_Cp.
\tag{M.10.9j.29c}
$$

Thus its consumed ergotropy also approaches $q_{ab}$ under (M.10.9j.29). This is an exact-frame, finite-dimensional spectral statement. Arbitrary preparation perturbations can spoil the rank bound; the assertion is not imported unchanged into the growing reset target. It supplies neither a cyclic clock nor an autonomous renewal/extraction mechanism or original-source admission.

**Part VII. Bounded measurable profiles and the static sharp step.**

There is also a slightly broader version of Part I. It suffices that $K$ is bounded measurable and self-adjoint; replace $C(t)$ by

$$
 C_{\rm bd}(t)=a+2M_0/\hbar+
                  (M_0/\hbar)(at+2M_0t/\hbar).
\tag{M.10.9j.29d}
$$

To justify this extension, write $U(x,x-t)=U(x,0)U(x-t,0)^*$. Both endpoint propagators are locally absolutely continuous with bounded weak derivatives. Their product therefore has the endpoint derivative used in the proof, bounded by $2M_0/\hbar$ almost everywhere. Multiplication by the $H^1$ packet remains $H^1$; (M.10.9j.9)–(M.10.9j.10) follow with that derivative bound. The circle derivative plus bounded multiplication is self-adjoint on its original $H^1$ domain. Values of $K$ at isolated jumps are measure-zero irrelevant; the endpoint guards avoid them. The product propagator is periodic even though an individual endpoint propagator need not be. No distributional $\delta$ or derivative of a discontinuous $K$ is inserted into the proof.

Consequently set $\delta=0$ in the frame table, with a step from $H_a$ to $H_b$ at $2w$, the same smooth SWAP pulse immediately afterward, and a return step outside the guarded horizon. The finite matrix (M.10.9j.5) remains positive and explicitly defined. Its entries are Fourier integrals of a static step, not an externally actuated infinite-slope pulse. In this sharp-step comparison the ideal endpoint heat is exactly $q_{ab}$, so the $2\epsilon^2\delta/\hbar$ terms disappear from (M.10.9j.19)–(M.10.9j.20). The only approximation is the finite-clock one. The finite device still does not implement an exact step-controlled endpoint or exact heat identity at fixed $N$. The smooth finite-ramp construction above remains available when spatial/control smoothness is part of the admitted source grammar.

**Part VIII. Finite reset words and their autonomous diagonal limit.**

The theorem is dimension-independent in its error constants, but the actual target dimension and energy capacity are always charged. Part IV's entrywise precision statement with dimension $4(2N+1)$ belongs to the four-dimensional frame target; the operator-error condition $\|E\|\le\nu$ applies on the actual larger matrix for a reset word. Consequently it also applies to any **fixed finite** coherent dilation of the declared frame/readout/reset word, after replacing quenches by finite ramps and interaction switches by smooth finite-area pulses. All baths, pointers and controller records in that dilation must be included. Tracing a spent pointer supplies the reduced channel; it does not prove a physical Born selector or destroy the pointer's record. For a general noncommuting word, ordinary finite-ramp errors must be added and cannot be omitted.

For the reset family of Theorem M.10.9i, Part V a more precise specialization is available. Let $m=n^3$, with its registered nominal diagonal memory law and gaps $k_BTx_j$ from Theorem M.10.9i, Part V. Prepare all $m$ fresh Gibbs qubits at once, independently. Their joint Gibbs Hamiltonian is

$$
 H_{B,n}=k_BT\sum_{j=1}^{m}x_j|1\rangle\langle1|_j,
 \quad E_{B,n}:=\|H_{B,n}\|\le k_BT n^4.
\tag{M.10.9j.30}
$$

Use a linear ramp of duration $\delta>0$ for each of the $m+2$ memory-gap changes, and the envelope (M.10.9j.12) of duration $\tau$ for each of the $m$ full swaps. The initial/final memory gap is zero. The target dimension is $2^{m+1}$, before counting any retained spectator reference. The active duration and safe bounds are

$$
 L_n=(n^3+2)\delta+n^3\tau,
 \quad M_{0,n}=k_BT(n^4+n)+2\pi\hbar/\tau,
 \quad M_{1,n}=\max\{nk_BT/\delta,2\pi^2\hbar/\tau^2\}.
\tag{M.10.9j.31}
$$

Add initial/final guards as above, taking $T_n=4w+L_n$, $P_n=2T_n+4w$, and constant $K=I_M\otimes H_{B,n}$ outside the active interval. Because the boundary Hamiltonians agree, no return ramp is needed for periodic completion.

Here the finite ramps do **not** change the nominal heat: memory-gap ramps are diagonal, so they preserve its probabilities; each full swap then transfers the same populations as in the sudden protocol. With any initial memory-reference correlation, the last full swap still makes the reduced memory-reference output exactly $\gamma_n\otimes\rho_R$; the final diagonal ramp leaves $\gamma_n$ unchanged. Initial/final plateaus and (M.10.9j.15) make these assertions independent of the ideal clock offset. Thus the ideal characteristic heat is exactly the quantity $Q_n^{\rm rec}$, even for finite ramp duration.

Apply (M.10.9j.7), (M.10.9j.23) with $M_{0,n},M_{1,n},T_n,P_n$, and write the resulting error as $\xi_{n,N}$. The finite autonomous reset satisfies

$$
 \|\Phi_{n,N}-\mathcal R_0\|_\diamond
       \le2e^{-n}+\xi_{n,N},
 \quad |Q_{n,N}-Q_n^{\rm rec}|\le E_{B,n}\xi_{n,N},
\tag{M.10.9j.32}
$$

$$
 |W_{n,N}-Q_n^{\rm rec}|
       \le M_{0,n}(\xi_{n,N}+\xi_{0,n}).
\tag{M.10.9j.33}
$$

The work quantity is again the actual clock-energy debit; initial and final interaction residuals are retained exactly as in (M.10.9j.21), with zero boundary memory energy. All retained side records remain spectators or are explicitly included. These formulas concern the registered actual nominal marginal, not an assumed marginal after a noisy prior reuse.

There is no uniform-in-$n$ fixed clock. For the following joint limit hold $w,\delta,\tau>0$ fixed independently of $n$. Then (M.10.9j.23) with $\eta_n=(n+1)^{-6}$ gives $\xi_{n,N_n}\le\eta_n$ and $\xi_{0,n}\le\eta_n/2$. Therefore

$$
 \beta|Q_{n,N_n}-k_BT h(a)|
 \le(n+2)e^{-n}+\frac1{8n}+n^4\eta_n\to0,
\tag{M.10.9j.34}
$$

and (M.10.9j.33) gives the same convergence for $\beta W_{n,N_n}$ to $h(a)$. The output approaches pure replacement by (M.10.9j.32). This is a justified diagonal limit of increasingly large sources: $n^3$ fresh cells, growing gaps/capacity, growing target dimension, duration, clock dimension and clock energy. It is not exact erasure by one finite device. No entropy-free clock-renewal statement is needed for this reset extension or inferred from it.

An optional initial deterministic relabeling flip of the degenerate bit can be inserted as one additional finite smooth pulse; it preserves the nominal entropy and bath energy, with its pulse duration/norm included in the table. Full finite adaptive words require their actual branch/control records in the coherent dilation and retain the original source's ready-state and selector qualifications.

<a id="proposition-m109k-exact-finite-program-obstruction-for-the-unitary-branch"></a>**Proposition M.10.9k (Exact Finite-Program Obstruction for the Unitary Branch).**

Let $g_\theta=e^{\theta X}$, with $X$ and $0<\alpha\le\pi/2$ as in Theorem M.10.9i. Suppose one fixed deterministic quantum processor implements every distinct qubit channel $\sigma\mapsto g_\theta\sigma g_\theta^*$, for infinitely many $\theta\in[0,\alpha]$, by changing only a program state in a fixed finite-dimensional register. No such exact processor exists.

**Proof.** For pure program vectors $P,Q$, a fixed unitary dilation of an exact unitary channel must map $|\psi\rangle|P\rangle$ to $U_P|\psi\rangle|e_P\rangle$, with environment vector independent of $\psi$: otherwise a pure input superposition would become mixed. Preservation of inner products gives
$$
 \langle P|Q\rangle I=\langle e_P|e_Q\rangle U_P^*U_Q.
$$
If the two unitary channels are distinct modulo scalar phase, the right matrix cannot equal a nonzero scalar identity. Hence $\langle P|Q\rangle=0$. Mixed programs reduce to their pure support components: extremality of a unitary channel forces every nonzero component to implement that same channel, so supports for distinct channels are orthogonal. A finite program space admits only finitely many nonzero orthogonal supports. The rotations in the stated interval are distinct modulo phase. ∎

This is the no-programming argument of Nielsen and Chuang (1997), specialized to the rotations of Theorem M.10.9i. It does not obstruct the Gibbs-state-programmed replacement channel (M.10.9i.11), which is nonunitary, nor a family of different externally supplied Hamiltonians, longer finite programs, approximate control, or growing resources. The original finite **shared** algebra is not itself a finite program-register bound.

<a id="proposition-m109d-matched-encoding-invariance-and-receiver-relative-scope"></a>**Proposition M.10.9d (Matched-Encoding Invariance and Receiver-Relative Scope).**

Let $W$ be a finite serialized-pattern random variable with preregistered law $Q$, and let a fixed encoding $e$ assign a state $\rho_w$ to every realization $w$. Suppose the same realization $w$, with the same serialization and encoding, is delivered to receivers $S$ and $S'$.

Every registered functional whose arguments are confined to $(Q,e,w)$ has the same value in the two arms. In particular, the arms have the same Shannon entropy $H_Q(W)$, the same fixed-machine Kolmogorov complexity $K_U(w)$, the same fixed-code length, and the same von Neumann entropy of
$$
\bar\rho_Q
:=
\sum_wQ(w)\rho_w.
\tag{M.10.9d.1}
$$
Suppose additionally that a typed receiver-role certificate proves
$$
\Delta M_S^{(\mathrm{self})}(w)\ne0,
\qquad
\Delta M_{S'}^{(\mathrm{self})}(w)=0,
\tag{M.10.9d.2}
$$
and that $S'$ satisfies the baseline-invariance condition of Corollary M.10.3.1. Then
$$
\sigma_S(w)>0,
\qquad
\sigma_{S'}(w)=0,
\qquad
\mu_{S'}(w)=\frac1{\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}}.
\tag{M.10.9d.3}
$$
No value or divergence law for $\mu_S(w)$ follows without evaluating (M.18), and no measured-cost conclusion follows without Theorem M.10.3's reduction certificate and a registered implementation ledger.

*Proof.* The first conclusions follow because every argument of each pattern-side functional is identical. Equation (M.10.9d.2), Definitions M.10.2 and M.10.4, and Corollary M.10.3.1 give (M.10.9d.3). The final scope sentence retains the reduction premise of Theorem M.10.3 and requires a registered implementation ledger; a reset-heat interpretation additionally retains Theorem M.10.7's implementation hypotheses. ∎

A register permutation alone does not establish (M.10.9d.2). The receiver-role certificate must prove that off-target addressing lies in the external Fisher component and that indirect propagation does not return a nonzero component to the self-model subspace.

### M.10.10 Static Entropic Perspective Coupling with Prescribed Endpoint Marginals

<a id="definition-m1010a-entropic-perspective-transport-problem"></a>**Definition M.10.10a (Entropic Perspective-Transport Problem).** Let $(\Sigma,d_\Sigma)$ be the compact perspective space of Appendix M and let $c(s,s')=d_\Sigma(s,s')^2$ be the quadratic perspective-transport cost. For a measurement partition $\{P_k\}$ and pre-measurement state $\rho$, let
$$
p_k=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_k)
$$
be the Born weights supplied by Theorem G.1.11b. Let $\mu_0$ be the pre-interaction perspective distribution and let $\nu_k$ be the normalized endpoint distribution concentrated on perspectives in which outcome $k$ is actual. Define the prescribed endpoint mixture
$$
\nu=\sum_kp_k\nu_k.
$$
Thus the Born weights are input marginal data for this transport problem. The minimization below can select a coupling between $\mu_0$ and $\nu$ but cannot derive the already prescribed coefficients $p_k$.

If the resulting endpoint kernel is used as $G_{\mathrm{persp}}(\,\cdot\,|s,k,N,\Delta t)$, the registered interaction record must fix $\mu_0^{N,\Delta t}$, $\pi_0^{N,\Delta t}$, $\varepsilon_{N,\Delta t}$, and $\nu_k^{N,\Delta t}$ before the minimization. Without those indexed inputs, the static transport problem defines no dependence on $N$ or $\Delta t$.

Let $\pi_0$ be a Borel probability reference measure on $\Sigma\times\Sigma$ and let $\varepsilon>0$. Assume that at least one coupling $\bar\pi\in\Pi(\mu_0,\nu)$ has $\operatorname{KL}(\bar\pi\Vert\pi_0)<\infty$. This holds on a finite carrier when $\pi_0$ assigns positive mass to every pair. The entropic perspective-transport plan is
$$
\pi^\star
=
\operatorname*{argmin}_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu_0,\nu)}
\left[
\int_{\Sigma\times\Sigma}c(s,s')\,d\pi(s,s')
+
\varepsilon\,\operatorname{KL}(\pi\Vert\pi_0)
\right].
\tag{M.10.10.1}
$$
Here $\Pi(\mu_0,\nu)$ denotes couplings with the stated marginals; absolute continuity without finite relative entropy is not the feasibility condition.

<a id="theorem-m1010b-existence-uniqueness-and-conditional-born-endpoint-marginals"></a>**Theorem M.10.10b (Existence, Uniqueness, and Conditional Born Endpoint Marginals).** Under Definition M.10.10a, the minimizer exists, is unique and has finite objective. If pairwise disjoint Borel outcome sectors $A_k$ satisfy $\nu_k(A_k)=1$ and $\nu_j(A_k)=0$ for $j\ne k$, then
$$
\pi^\star(\Sigma\times A_k)=p_k=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_k).
\tag{M.10.10.2}
$$

*Proof.* Compactness of $\Sigma$ makes $\Pi(\mu_0,\nu)$ weakly compact. The bounded continuous transport cost is weakly continuous. Relative entropy is weakly lower semicontinuous; its probability-measure variational formula expresses it as the supremum of the continuous functionals
$$
\pi\longmapsto\int f\,d\pi-\log\int e^f\,d\pi_0,
\qquad f\in C(\Sigma\times\Sigma).
$$
The finite-relative-entropy feasible coupling makes the objective proper, so the direct method gives a finite minimizer. On its finite domain, strict convexity of $x\log x$ gives strict convexity of relative entropy in the density relative to $\pi_0$. Two distinct minimizers would therefore have a midpoint of lower objective. Finally every admissible coupling has second marginal $\nu=\sum_jp_j\nu_j$, whence
$$
\pi^\star(\Sigma\times A_k)=\nu(A_k)
=\sum_jp_j\nu_j(A_k)=p_k.
$$
The Born weights are prescribed marginal inputs to this conclusion. $\square$

<a id="corollary-m1010c-entropic-transport-kernel-with-prescribed-born-endpoint-law"></a>**Corollary M.10.10c (Entropic Transport Kernel with Prescribed Born Endpoint Law).** Let $A_k=\operatorname{supp}\nu_k$ be pairwise disjoint up to $\nu$-null sets, and disintegrate the unique finite-objective plan as
$$
\pi^\star(ds,ds')=\mu_0(ds)\,K^\star(ds'|s).
$$
Put $r_k(s)=K^\star(A_k|s)$. The endpoint weights satisfy
$$
\int_\Sigma r_k(s)\,\mu_0(ds)=p_k.
\tag{M.10.10.3}
$$
For $p_k>0$, the conditional transition kernel is
$$
G_{\mathrm{persp}}(B|s,k,N,\Delta t)
=
\frac{K^\star(B\cap A_k|s)}{r_k(s)}
\quad\text{when }r_k(s)>0.
\tag{M.10.10.4}
$$
Its value on $r_k(s)=0$ is arbitrary for the outcome-$k$ joint law. The starting-perspective law conditional on that outcome is
$$
\mu_{0|k}(ds)=\frac{r_k(s)}{p_k}\,\mu_0(ds),
$$
and the joint endpoint law decomposes as
$$
\pi^\star(ds,ds')
=
\sum_{k:p_k>0}p_k\,\mu_{0|k}(ds)\,
G_{\mathrm{persp}}(ds'|s,k,N,\Delta t).
$$
To use this same plan with the Born-first sampling rule that draws $s$ from $\mu_0$ and then draws $k$ with probability $p_k$ independent of $s$, additionally require
$$
r_k(s)=p_k
\quad\text{for $\mu_0$-almost every $s$ and every $k$}.
$$
Averaged endpoint weights alone do not supply this compatibility condition. The registered $N,\Delta t$ dependence is the indexed input dependence specified in Definition M.10.10a.

*Proof.* Compact standard-Borel $\Sigma$ admits a disintegration with
$$
\pi^\star(C\times B)=\int_C K^\star(B|s)\,\mu_0(ds).
$$
Taking $C=\Sigma$ and $B=A_k$ proves (M.10.10.3). Conditioning the joint law on the sector gives the stated density of $\mu_{0|k}$ and the normalized restriction (M.10.10.4). Multiplying these two expressions and summing the sectors recovers the disintegration; their union has full second-marginal measure. If $p_k=0$, nonnegativity implies $r_k=0$ almost everywhere, so this outcome contributes nothing. For $p_k>0$, the conditional starting law equals $\mu_0$ exactly when $r_k/p_k=1$ almost everywhere. Equivalently, the Born-first joint law agrees with the plan exactly when its starting-perspective/outcome marginal $p_k\mu_0(ds)$ equals $r_k(s)\mu_0(ds)$ for every $k$. This proves the additional compatibility criterion. No time-indexed path measure, reference Markov process, or Schrödinger bridge is constructed by the static problem. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m1010c1-complete-endpoint-simplex-classification-and-born-nonentailment"></a>**Theorem M.10.10c.1 (Complete Endpoint-Simplex Classification and Born Nonentailment).** Retain pairwise disjoint sectors $A_1,\ldots,A_m$ and normalized component laws $\nu_k$ with $\nu_j(A_k)=\delta_{jk}$. For every probability vector $q\in\Delta_{m-1}$ define
$$
\nu_q:=\sum_kq_k\nu_k.
\tag{M.10.10c.1.1}
$$
Then the sector-mixture map $q\mapsto\nu_q$ is affine and injective, with inverse
$$
q_k=\nu_q(A_k).
\tag{M.10.10c.1.2}
$$
For every $q$ for which Definition M.10.10a's finite-relative-entropy feasibility premise holds, the same strict-convexity proof gives a unique entropic transport plan with endpoint-sector weights exactly $q$. Consequently the transport cost, entropy regularizer, sector partition, and component maps do not select Born weights. They force $q=p$ if and only if an independent descent/marginal axiom fixes
$$
q_k=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_k).
\tag{M.10.10c.1.3}
$$
The registered comparison class contains the following fully populated response-distinct feasible instance. Restrict all transport measures to the two-point finite-resolution carrier $\Sigma_2=\{s_1,s_2\}\subset\Sigma$ and take
$$
A_k=\{s_k\},\qquad \nu_k=\delta_{s_k},\qquad
\mu_0=\tfrac12(\delta_{s_1}+\delta_{s_2}),
\tag{M.10.10c.1.4}
$$
Choose orthonormal $e_1,e_2\in\mathcal H_0$, set $P_1=|e_1\rangle\!\langle e_1|$, $P_2=I-P_1$, and take $\rho=(|e_1\rangle\!\langle e_1|+|e_2\rangle\!\langle e_2|)/2$; then $p=(1/2,1/2)$. Set $q=(1/3,2/3)$ and use the full-support reference and candidate couplings
$$
\pi_0=\mu_0\otimes\nu_p,
\qquad
\pi_q=\mu_0\otimes\nu_q.
\tag{M.10.10c.1.5}
$$
The reference gives mass $1/4$ to each atom of $\Sigma_2^2$, while $\pi_q$ gives masses $1/6$ and $1/3$ to $(s_i,s_1)$ and $(s_i,s_2)$, respectively. Hence $\pi_q\in\Pi(\mu_0,\nu_q)$, $\pi_q\ll\pi_0$, and, writing $d_{12}=d_\Sigma(s_1,s_2)$,
$$
\operatorname{KL}(\pi_q\Vert\pi_0)
=\frac13\log\frac23+\frac23\log\frac43<\infty,
\qquad
\int c\,d\pi_q=\frac12d_{12}^2<\infty.
\tag{M.10.10c.1.6}
$$
It therefore satisfies Definition M.10.10a for every $\varepsilon>0$, while $q\ne p$ and $\nu_q\ne\nu_p$. This refutes a derivation from the transport data alone.

*Proof.* Disjoint support gives $\nu_q(A_k)=q_k$, proving injectivity and (M.10.10c.1.2). The existence/uniqueness proof of Theorem M.10.10b uses only the prescribed second marginal and therefore applies with $\nu$ replaced by $\nu_q$ on the feasible domain. Every coupling has second marginal $\nu_q$, so its sector weights are $q$. Equation (M.10.10c.1.3) is therefore necessary and sufficient for the Born endpoint vector. Equations (M.10.10c.1.4)--(M.10.10c.1.6) verify that the feasible domain contains the displayed non-Born point. ∎

<a id="theorem-m1010d-predictive-role-position-equivalence"></a>**Theorem M.10.10d (Predictive Role-Position Equivalence).** Let $S$ be a knowledge system on the predictive-function-space branch. Let $\mathsf{Cont}_S$ be its retained content class, and let
$$
\mathcal R_c^S:\mathsf P_S^{op}\to\mathbf{Set}
$$
or, on probabilistic branches,
$$
\mathcal R_c^S:\mathsf P_S^{op}\to\mathbf{Prob}_{\mathrm{fin}}
$$
be the operational response presheaf of a content item $c$. Define operational equivalence by
$$
c_1\equiv_{\mathrm{op}}^S c_2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal R_{c_1}^S\cong\mathcal R_{c_2}^S,
$$
and define the predictive-function space
$$
\mathcal F_S:=\mathsf{Cont}_S/\!\equiv_{\mathrm{op}}^S,
\qquad
\pi_S(c)=[c]_{\mathrm{op}}.
$$
Then the quantitative position $\pi_S(c)$ and the qualitative predictive role of $c$ are the same operational invariant:
$$
\pi_S(c)
=
[c]_{\mathrm{op}}
=
[\mathcal R_c^S]_{\cong}
=
\operatorname{Role}_S(c).
$$
Consequently,
$$
c_1\equiv_{\mathrm{op}}^S c_2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\pi_S(c_1)=\pi_S(c_2)
$$
as elements of $\mathcal F_S$. An additional group action on $\mathcal F_S$ does not preserve this equivalence merely by being called an internal symmetry. Passing to its orbit quotient defines a coarser relation unless each orbit is a singleton in $\mathcal F_S$.

The perspectival profile
$$
\mathcal P_S(c)=(\Delta Q_S(c),\mu_S(c),\sigma_S(c))
$$
is a finite descriptor on the subset of $\mathcal F_S$ where it is well-defined. It need not separate all operational distinctions, so equality of profiles implies operational equivalence only on a branch where the profile is injective. Descent of the profile to any additional group-orbit quotient requires invariance under that action. The term “coordinate chart” is reserved for a proved injective local parametrization with the requisite topology.

*Proof.* The predictive role of $c$ is the natural-isomorphism class $[\mathcal R_c^S]_{\cong}$. The quotient defining $\mathcal F_S$ identifies exactly the contents in each such class, giving
$$
\pi_S(c)=[c]_{\mathrm{op}}=[\mathcal R_c^S]_{\cong}.
$$
Thus equality in $\mathcal F_S$ is equivalent to the declared operational equivalence. If a group element moves one point of $\mathcal F_S$ to another, its orbit quotient identifies two distinct operational classes; the original equivalence cannot also characterize equality in that further quotient. A function on $\mathcal F_S$ descends to the orbit quotient precisely when it is constant on every orbit. Finally, a finite tuple of descriptors need not be injective, so the profile implication requires the stated separating property. $\square$

<a id="definition-m1010d1-separating-profile-branch"></a>**Definition M.10.10d.1 (Separating-profile branch).** A profile is separating on a retained content class $\mathcal E\subseteq\mathsf{Cont}_S$ if
$$
\mathcal P_S(c_1)=\mathcal P_S(c_2)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
c_1\equiv_{\mathrm{op}}^S c_2
$$
for all $c_1,c_2\in\mathcal E$.

<a id="corollary-m1010d2-certificate-relative-profile-completeness"></a>**Corollary M.10.10d.2 (Certificate-Relative Profile Completeness).** Let $\mathcal C$ be a declared class of patterns. If the separating-profile condition of Definition M.10.10d.1 has been proved on $\mathcal C$, then $(\Delta Q,\mu,\sigma)$ is a complete invariant on $\mathcal C$. If that certificate has not been supplied, the tuple remains a finite descriptor, but equality of descriptors does not license an inference of operational equivalence.

*Proof.* On a certified class, Definition M.10.10d.1 gives
$$
(\Delta Q,\mu,\sigma)(E_1)=(\Delta Q,\mu,\sigma)(E_2)
\Longrightarrow
E_1\sim_{\mathrm{op}}E_2,
$$
which is precisely completeness of the invariant. Without that implication as an available premise, the same conclusion cannot be inferred in a downstream proof. This is a certificate-scope statement and makes no claim that the implication is false on an uncertified class. ∎

<a id="theorem-m1010d2a-profile-fiber-classification-and-global-collision"></a>**Theorem M.10.10d.2a (Profile-Fiber Classification and Global Collision).** Fix a finite retained content class $\mathcal C$ on which $\mathcal P_S$ is defined and invariant under $\equiv_{\mathrm{op}}^S$. Let
$$
Q_{\mathcal C}:=\mathcal C/\!\equiv_{\mathrm{op}}^S,
\qquad
r:\mathcal C\to Q_{\mathcal C},
$$
and let $\overline{\mathcal P}_S:Q_{\mathcal C}\to\mathbb R\times(0,\infty]\times[0,1]$ be the induced profile map. For each attained profile value $z$, write
$$
F_z:=\overline{\mathcal P}_S^{-1}(z).
\tag{M.10.10d.2a.1}
$$
Then a subclass $\mathcal E\subseteq\mathcal C$ is separating exactly when
$$
|r(\mathcal E)\cap F_z|\le1
\quad\text{for every attained }z.
\tag{M.10.10d.2a.2}
$$
The inclusion-maximal separating subclasses are exactly the saturated transversals
$$
\mathcal E=r^{-1}(T),
\qquad
|T\cap F_z|=1
\quad\text{for every attained }z.
\tag{M.10.10d.2a.3}
$$

The full profile map is nonseparating on an admissible finite model. Take an identifiable Fisher stratum whose external tangent summand contains orthonormal vectors $e_1,e_2$, impose the baseline-invariance condition $\Pi_S^{(0)}(\theta_S)=\theta_S$, and register two patterns $E_1,E_2$ with
$$
\Delta M_S^{(\mathrm{self})}(E_i)=0,
\qquad
\Delta M_S^{(\mathrm{ext})}(E_i)=e_i,
\qquad
\Delta Q_S(E_i)=0.
\tag{M.10.10d.2a.4}
$$
Work on the probabilistic response-presheaf branch and include one retained binary response probe $p$ whose outcome laws are $\delta_0$ on $E_1$ and $\tfrac12(\delta_0+\delta_1)$ on $E_2$. Then
$$
\mathcal P_S(E_1)=\mathcal P_S(E_2)
=\left(0,\frac1{\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}},0\right),
\qquad
E_1\not\equiv_{\mathrm{op}}^S E_2.
\tag{M.10.10d.2a.5}
$$

*Proof.* Invariance makes $\overline{\mathcal P}_S$ well defined. Definition M.10.10d.1 says that $\mathcal E$ is separating exactly when two roles represented in $r(\mathcal E)$ cannot lie in the same profile fiber, which is (M.10.10d.2a.2). If a separating class omits a content operationally equivalent to one it contains, adjoining that content preserves separation. If its role image misses a nonempty fiber, adjoining one role from that fiber also preserves separation. Hence every maximal separating class is saturated and meets every fiber. Conversely, a saturated class meeting every fiber in exactly one role obeys (M.10.10d.2a.2), and adjoining any omitted role creates a two-role intersection in its fiber. This proves (M.10.10d.2a.3).

For the displayed model, $\Delta M_S^{(\mathrm{self})}(E_i)=0$ leaves the updated self parameter equal to $\theta_S$. Baseline invariance makes $PP=0$ satisfy (M.18), so the infimum is zero and Definition M.10.3 gives $\mu_S(E_i)=1/\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$. Fisher orthogonality and the nonzero external updates give $\sigma_S(E_i)=0$, while the registered predictive relevance is zero for both. Their profiles therefore agree. The two probability laws at probe $p$ are not isomorphic: a probability-preserving bijection cannot turn one atom of mass one into two atoms of mass one half. Therefore no natural isomorphism of the retained response presheaves exists, and Theorem M.10.10d places the patterns in different operational roles. This proves (M.10.10d.2a.5). ∎

<a id="corollary-m1010d3-compatibility-with-shape-recognition"></a>**Corollary M.10.10d.3 (Compatibility with shape recognition).** Exact shape identity remains typed subdiagram isomorphism plus response-presheaf isomorphism. Predictive role-position equivalence supplies the role-level quotient of that structure; it does not reduce shape identity to equality of the finite tuple $(\Delta Q,\mu,\sigma)$.

*Proof.* Shape identity requires the subdiagram structure and the response-presheaf correspondence. Theorem M.10.10d identifies the role-level quotient represented by response presheaves. A coordinate chart on that quotient does not replace the full subdiagram and presheaf data. ∎

<a id="theorem-m1011-receiver-relative-simulation-criterion"></a>**Theorem M.10.11 (Receiver-Relative Simulation Criterion).** Let a finite simulation exposure to $S$ be
$$
\mathcal O_S(\mathcal H^\tau,I)=(E_1,\ldots,E_N),
\qquad
R_k:=E_1\oplus\cdots\oplus E_k.
$$
If SPAP-admissibility is defined by the existence of a subboundary performance level satisfying (M.18) for every integrated prefix, then
$$
\mathcal H^\tau\text{ admissible}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mu_S(R_k)<\infty
\quad(1\le k\le N).
$$
This criterion depends on the receiver-prefix pairs $(S,R_k)$ and not on the origin label $\tau$. If a family of prefixes also carries the pattern-specific reduction certificate of Theorem M.10.3 and $\mu_S(R_k)\to\infty$, its certified integration complexity obeys (M.23). If $\mu_S(R_k)=\infty$, Theorem M.10.6 excludes a completed integration only on its stated reduction branch.

*Proof.* Definition M.10.3 assigns $PP_S^{(R_k)}$ and $\mu_S(R_k)$ from the candidate update induced by the accumulated prefix. If $\mu_S(R_k)=\infty$, Theorem M.10.6 shows that no $PP<\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$ satisfies (M.18), contradicting the stated admissibility criterion. Hence every admissible prefix has finite $\mu_S(R_k)$. The formula (M.18) contains $S$ and $R_k$ but no temporal-origin label $\tau$, proving origin-label independence. The final two conclusions are direct applications of Theorems M.10.3 and M.10.6 with their reduction hypotheses retained. ∎

<a id="protocol-m1012-matched-encoding-yoked-receiver-audit"></a>**Protocol M.10.12 (Matched-Encoding Yoked-Receiver Audit).**

Let $n\mapsto(S_n,S_n',W_n)$ be a preregistered family of finite classical pattern experiments. For each $n$, the same realized serialization of $W_n$ is delivered to both receivers. An optional crossed extension introduces target labels $T\in\{0,1\}$ and patterns $W_{nT}$, with every realized $W_{nT}$ delivered to both receiver arms. A matched-encoding audit must register before cost data are inspected:

1. the serialization, sampling law, and encoding, with equality of the realized input verified across the two arms;
2. a common operation-count unit and calibrated meter, together with restored initial-state snapshots or an explicit carryover model;
3. a typed receiver-role certificate of the form (M.10.9d.2), including a no-leakage proof for indirect updates;
4. Theorem M.10.5 model-access and decision certificates, obtained independently of the cost measurements;
5. a *finite-proximity ladder certificate*
   $$
   \frac1{\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}}
   \le
   \mu_{S_n}(W_n)<\infty,
   \qquad
   \mu_{S_n}(W_n)\longrightarrow\infty;
   \tag{M.10.12.1}
   $$
6. the uniform pattern-specific reduction certificate of Theorem M.10.3 for the treatment arm;
7. if a ratio or subtractive divergence is claimed, an independent control-cost certificate
   $$
   C_{\mathrm{integrate}}(S_n',W_n)\le K
   \tag{M.10.12.2}
   $$
   with one finite $K$ for the registered family;
8. for a crossed receiver-target claim, randomized target and receiver labels together with role certificates in both target directions; every audit must include an exchange-isomorphism check for instruction semantics, address resolution, memory locality, cross-talk, and order effects.

Theorem M.10.4 does not supply item 5. Its endpoint object has $\mu=\infty$ and is not a completed finite-cost integration datapoint.

<a id="proposition-m1012a-conditional-divergence-of-the-yoked-cost-contrast"></a>**Proposition M.10.12a (Conditional Divergence of the Yoked Cost Contrast).**

Assume Protocol M.10.12, including (M.10.12.1)--(M.10.12.2). Define
$$
D_n
:=
C_{\mathrm{integrate}}(S_n,W_n)
-
C_{\mathrm{integrate}}(S_n',W_n).
\tag{M.10.12.3}
$$
Then, for all sufficiently large $n$,
$$
D_n
\ge
c\log\mu_{S_n}(W_n)\,
\mu_{S_n}(W_n)^2
-K,
\tag{M.10.12.4}
$$
and therefore
$$
D_n\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{M.10.12.5}
$$
If additionally
$$
0<C_{\mathrm{integrate}}(S_n',W_n)\le K,
$$
then the ratio
$$
\rho_n
:=
\frac{
C_{\mathrm{integrate}}(S_n,W_n)
}{
C_{\mathrm{integrate}}(S_n',W_n)
}
$$
satisfies
$$
\rho_n
\ge
\frac cK
\log\mu_{S_n}(W_n)\,
\mu_{S_n}(W_n)^2
\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{M.10.12.6}
$$

*Proof.* Theorem M.10.3 and item 6 give the treatment-arm lower bound. Subtracting (M.10.12.2) gives (M.10.12.4), whose right-hand side diverges by (M.10.12.1). Under the positive-denominator condition, division by a number at most $K$ gives (M.10.12.6). ∎

<a id="remark-m1012b-inference-boundary"></a>**Remark M.10.12b (Inference Boundary).**

Identical serialization fixes only registered pattern-side functionals. It does not remove receiver state, implementation, carryover, address binding, or receiver-by-target interactions. A crossed arm swap tests fixed hardware asymmetry only when the exchange isomorphism in item 8 has been proved. A nonzero finite contrast establishes a receiver-target interaction for the registered implementation; it does not uniquely identify $\mu$, SPAP, CC, the perspectival quantum branch, gravity, or cosmology.

Neither $\mu_{S_n'}=1/\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$ nor $C_{\mathrm{refl}}(S_n',W_n)=0$ supplies (M.10.12.2), because the external cost can remain unbounded. The lower bound (M.23) supplies the asymptotic exponent of Corollary M.10.3a, not a finite-ladder regression slope. Every finite observed ladder is bounded, so finite data cannot establish observed unboundedness. A finite contradiction must instead use the all-path upper-bound audit of Corollary B.2.2. Registered-reset calorimetry is a separate secondary branch requiring Theorem M.10.7's reset-count and conditional-entropy data.

<a id="proposition-m1012c-finite-stage-contrast-floor-and-bounded-contrast-falsifier"></a>**Proposition M.10.12c (Finite-Stage Contrast Floor and Bounded-Contrast Falsifier).** Assume items 5--7 of Protocol M.10.12, with the treatment-arm certificate of item 6 carrying the Corollary B.2.2 constants $c_s>0$ and $\beta(\delta)\le\delta$, and write $\mu_n:=\mu_{S_n}(W_n)$.

1. Every stage with $\mu_n\ge8$ satisfies
$$
D_n\ge\frac{3c_s}{128}\mu_n^2\ln\frac{\mu_n}4-K.
\tag{M.10.12c.1}
$$
2. If a registered bound $D_n\le\bar D$ holds at a stage with $\mu_n\ge8$ and $\frac{3c_s}{128}\mu_n^2\ln\frac{\mu_n}4>\bar D+K$, the conjunction of items 5--7 with these constants is false. Along every ladder satisfying (M.10.12.1) such a stage exists for every finite $\bar D$, so a uniformly bounded contrast falsifies that conjunction at a finite stage, and the strict inequality evaluated from the registered $\mu_n$, $c_s$, $K$ and $\bar D$ certifies that stage. When these values are registered as computable reals, uniformly in $n$, a search over stages that confirms $\mu_n>8$ and the strict inequality at increasing precision halts at such a stage.
3. The conjunction of items 5--7 is satisfiable. With the frozen-Bernoulli treatment classes of Theorem M.10.3b at $e=2$ and, as control class, the sample-mean strategy of Theorem B.2a at the fixed margin $1/8$, one has $c_s=c_u$, $K=c_0+89c_u$ and $D_n=c_u[N_+(1/\mu_n)-89]$, which obeys (M.10.12c.1) and diverges.

*Proof.* Corollary B.2.2 applied to every strategy of the treatment class gives $\operatorname{Cost}_{\mathrm{integrate}}(S_n,W_n)\ge\frac{3c_s}{128}\mu_n^2\ln\frac{\mu_n}4$; subtracting (M.10.12.2) gives (M.10.12c.1). Item 2 is the contrapositive of item 1, and the floor in (M.10.12c.1) diverges under (M.10.12.1), so some stage has $\mu_n>8$ and the strict inequality. A true strict inequality between computable reals is confirmed by approximations of finite precision, so the dovetailed search over stages and precisions halts. For item 3, (B.5e) gives $N_+(1/8)=\lceil32\ln16\rceil=89$, and (B.5f) makes the control strategy $1/8$-accurate, so (M.10.12.2) holds with $K=c_0+89c_u$. Theorem M.10.3b supplies items 5 and 6 for the treatment arm, and subtraction gives $D_n$. Since $N_+(\delta)\ge\ln(2/\delta)/(2\delta^2)\ge\frac3{128}\delta^{-2}\ln(1/(4\delta))$ for $0<\delta\le1/8$, $D_n$ obeys (M.10.12c.1), and it diverges because $N_+(1/\mu_n)\ge\mu_n^2$. ∎

**Paired contrast.** Under items 5–7 of Protocol M.10.12, Proposition M.10.12c gives the finite-stage contrast floor and a finite bounded-contrast failure stage. The strict inequality can be located by a halting search for a uniformly computable registered ladder. The Bernoulli paired construction proves the joint consistency of those hypotheses. Theorem M.10.12d below supplies the matched receivers and the common physical meter and source for protocol items 1–4 and 8.

<a id="theorem-m1012d-matched-qualified-receivers-and-same-pattern-spap-reduction"></a>**Theorem M.10.12d (Matched Qualified Receivers and Same-Pattern SPAP Reduction).** Consume the qualified finite coherent host of Theorem M.10.4.3 with its unchanged prefix machine and original predictive task. The explicit risk-port source below replaces its single-outcome score by conditional future risk, fixes $\alpha =4/7$, and supplies the same-source reduction required by M.10.3. Its paid two-host extension realizes Protocol M.10.12 items 1–4 and 8, with the actual crossed exchange, full capability-grammar receiver-role certificate and same-pattern treatment reduction. No bounded-control-cost or divergent measured contrast is claimed.

*Proof and complete source specification.*

### Same-source risk calibration and reduction

The risk-port source is the source “SPAP-M08-RISK-PORT-v1” of Theorem M.10.3c. Sections 1–7 of its construction apply verbatim, as do its finite same-risk instance (state and bounds, total transition generator) and its complete paid finite ledger. In particular, conditional future risk replaces the single-outcome score, with $\alpha =4/7$; the actual own-state predictive risk controls the protected coherent map; and the nominated instance has $\delta =1/8$, 89 training acquisitions plus one final evaluation, 266 paid slots, $m=4096$ and zero completed resets.

### Matched receiver, no-leakage and exchange proof

### 1. Original scope and source choice

Item 7's uniform control bound applies if ratio/subtractive divergence is claimed; none is claimed here.

Take two isolated copies of the qualified M08 host of Theorem M.10.3c, indexed $i=0$,1. Each retains its own original MPU qualification, returned active bit $B_{i}$, own source registers, immutable scored prediction port and paid finite-window resources. The own-model coordinate of receiver i is $x_{i}$. Receiver i also has an explicitly external model coordinate $e_{i}$ of the peer's Gaussian diagnostic. At readiness all four coordinates equal the public rational $d_{n}$ of that M08 source. Independently prepared coherent states encode these known means; no unknown state is cloned. The predictive statistical family registered for receiver i is $N(x_i,1)$ times $N(e_i,1)$, with independent diagnostics and Fisher tensor $I_{2}$. Its self tangent is the $x_{i}$ axis, external tangent the $e_{i}$ axis. The own-state scored report, program, flags and resource records are retained in the full operational model, but are not incorrectly assigned a regular Gaussian Fisher tensor. This selected-stratum convention is exactly the M09 qualification of Theorem M.10.4.3 and remains load-bearing.

The peer model is operationally external: its target describes the other host's future diagnostic. Its readout and calculation never determine receiver i's own model or its own prediction report. Internal computational universality does not confer access to the immutable protected output ports. This is an explicit source grammar, not a theorem that arbitrary mutually communicating computers are insulated.

### 2. Matched pattern and preregistration

Fix $\delta_{n}=2^{-n-3}$, $\alpha=4/7$, $r_{n}=\alpha-\delta_{n}$, $s_{n}=\alpha-\delta_{n}/2$, $h_{n}(P)=\alpha-P+(P-r_{n})(P-s_{n})$, $d_{n}=h_{n}(0)$. Each finite trial installs the same finite algebraic descriptor in both arms, including n, source bounds and independently fixed price table. It pays for both copies and their installation before the trial. This preinstalled descriptor is context, not a free hidden serialization field.

The serialized pattern is the one-bit target $T$, delivered as the identical orthogonal classical encoding $|T\rangle\langle T|$ to both receivers, from a fair source. An independent fair arm-permutation bit randomizes physical arm labels. Source-private signs are independent of those bits and unavailable at either receiver before its report commitment. All these laws and the exact context are fixed before cost inspection. Byte/frame comparison explicitly verifies equality in both arms. $H(W)=\ln 2$, code length one, and every functional of the same $(Q,e,w)$ agrees. Equality of pattern data does not assert equality of receiver-relative internal state or operating cost.

On receiving $T$, receiver $i$ resolves the global target using its immutable identity: if $i=T$ it executes the M08 own-model update $x_{i}:d_{n}\to 0$ and the scored own-state challenge. If $i\ne T$ it updates $e_{i}:d_{n}\to 0$, storing a model of host $T$'s changed diagnostic; its own coordinate $x_{i}$ stays $d_{n}$. The control need not solve the target's scored own-state prediction. Its external evaluation uses the public certified map, not secret sign inference. Only the target host's sealed source port accepts $Y$ acquisitions for its own challenge. Receivers are physically distinct copies with separate stock and address spaces.

### 3. Roles and no leakage, including continuations

The registered event therefore has treatment displacement $(-d_{n},0)$ and control displacement $(0,-d_{n})$, in each receiver's ordered (self,external) coordinates. Since $d_{n}>0$, their total Fisher norms are $d_{n}$, self norms $d_{n}$ and 0, and reflexivity fractions 1 and 0. The control's baseline no-commitment map remains its own default $d_{n}$ at its unchanged target $d_{n}$. Thus its required self performance is zero and $\mu_{\mathrm{control}}=1/\alpha=7/4$.

All admitted continuations of this pattern consist of the target host's M08 acquisitions, bounded computations and one-way report lock; read-only algebraic evaluation in the peer's external workspace; append-only receipts/audits; and optional further writes to the same addressed external coordinate. There is no write, control, feedback or address-derived edge from the control's external model, audit outputs, costs or computed certificate to its own $x_{i}$ or own scored report. There is no peer-to-treatment edge before treatment lock, and no shared scheduler with secret-dependent timing. Initial peer state and resources are independent of the target sign. All instructions that can change $x_{i}$ carry the immutable own-target capability, which this off-target trial never supplies to i.

Induction over this complete grammar gives $x_{i}=d_{n}$ for the control for every admitted history. Readout randomness and variable internal evaluation time do not alter that invariant. Physical updates of workspace, records, unused optical outputs and clocks remain paid retained responses; the claim is zero update of the registered self-model component, not zero physical change anywhere in the receiver. Any continuation that copies $e_{i}$ into $x_{i}$, routes a certificate into an own forecast, or treats the entire audit state as a new self-model changes the registered scope and invalidates this certificate. It is not silently an admitted continuation of the same trial. Both hosts still have their independent direct finite-task EOPR capability and diagonal programs; the task-selected capability boundary does not remove that host qualification.

### 4. Independent model access and decision certificate

The peer holds finite descriptions of target 0, $\alpha$, $g(t)=t$, metric 1, and $F_{P}(x)=(1-h_{n}(P)/d_{n})x+h_{n}(P)$. Exact rational coefficients and the bound $|h_n'|\le 1+r_{n}+s_{n}$ on $[0,\alpha]$ supply effective moduli. On any declared compact x domain the affine expression gives a computable joint modulus. No source-private sign appears in these descriptions.

At target 0, the criterion is $h_{n}(P)\le\alpha-P$, equivalently $(P-r_{n})(P-s_{n})\le 0$, so its exact closed solution is $[r_{n},s_{n}]$. The infimum is $r_{n}$ and $\mu_{\mathrm{treatment}}=1/\delta_{n}=2^{n+3}$, independently of all operation measurements. The control's unchanged own target $d_{n}$ has zero discrepancy at $P=0$ and exact infimum zero. These are M.10.5 decision certificates, not a guessed PP label or empirical fit. The semantic calibration is the conditional future-risk map proved in the risk-port analysis above; it differs from the single-outcome M09 score. The full continuum calibration retains the newly declared exact classical-control feedforward primitive; the effective nominated finite reports and settings are algebraic. External certificate computation only writes external workspace under section 3, proving the theorem's insulation hypothesis. No peer needs to read or reveal a hidden sign to evaluate proximity.

### 5. Pattern-specific reduction on the same paired source

Condition on the target label, physical arm permutation, fixed public descriptor and any peer randomness. The treatment's complete precommit view is exactly the M08 sign-bearing acquisition transcript of Theorem M.10.3c followed by a sign-independent quantum channel. Extra peer records, input comparisons, charges, snapshots, allocation and shared public random labels are sign-independent. No extra sign-bearing observable is added by pairing the hosts. Every forecast, postcommit private actuator energy, private utilization or sign-dependent verification result stays inaccessible until the target's one-way lock, with a public padded maximum reserve beforehand. Public failure flags and timing are likewise padded or depend only on accessible acquisition history. These obligations cover the complete costs/energy/flag transcript, not merely a nominal sample count.

Consequently the M08 all-controller reduction of Theorem M.10.3c applies unchanged to every admitted target strategy: actual M.18 success forces the correct q threshold for the source's own-state Y; the test is read from the locked report, not imposed as a new success criterion. With essential maximum N acquisitions, the common unit ledger gives $C\ge N$≥(3/128)$\delta_{n}^{-2}\,\ln(1/(4\delta _n))$. Independent peer calculations can be included in the sign-independent channel and cannot defeat this reduction. The finite odd-majority witness from M08 supplies an actual nonempty reliable treatment strategy at each finite stage; no infinite host or infinite sample tape is asserted. This section uses the M08 actual risk-to-M.18 semantics and sealed physical source of Theorem M.10.3c without widening their scope. The complete paired implementation below supplies its source and cost binding.

### 6. Exchange isomorphism and order

$J$ flips host/receiver/source indices $i\mapsto 1-i$ and target $T\mapsto 1-T$, transports each host's own hidden sign and returned MPU bit with its host, swaps external peer labels accordingly, and preserves stage, program contents, numerical controls and costs. It maps the globally addressed write to the corresponding write, own acquisition to own acquisition, external evaluation to external evaluation, and lock to lock. Every primitive kernel, memory partition, paid reservation and padded schedule is identical under that relabeling. $J^{2}$ is identity and its conjugacy extends inductively to the full path law including all flags, private post-lock records, retained modes and receipts. Independent fair target and arm assignments make the crossed law invariant.

Within each trial the same unmodified word T reaches both arms. J changes that target word between the two crossed trials; a fixed-target role-preserving arm swap would be incompatible with nonzero versus zero self displacement. There is no such symmetry claim here.

Disjoint-host operations commute because their gates and stock live on disjoint factors; no computational output is delivered to the other host. Writes to one coordinate follow the explicitly ordered transition schedule and are not claimed to commute. Every trial allocates fresh ready banks, a fresh independent private sign and sources while retaining and disconnecting all previous-trial records. There is exactly one LOCK and one attempt per fresh instance: post-lock audits can reveal the sign and may never be reused as side information for another attempt with that same sign. Neither controller can inspect the treatment conditional-risk circuit, coupler, forecast output or private energy reconciliation before that LOCK. This is a paid fresh-allocation carryover model, not a free reset.

### 7. Calibrated meter and full source ledger

The calibrated meter counts declared packaged source dispatches, including native finite-table calls with their positive tariffs. Every acquisition is a separate counted dispatch, so $C\ge N$. The actual paired trace, meter history, tariff convention and complete finite constructor are specified below; no Boolean-gate count or measured-energy interpretation is asserted.

Let $D_{n}$ be the printed descriptor/readiness primitive trace, V the matched-frame/identity checks, $E_{n}$ the external-coordinate update and certificate trace, $A_{n}$ the treatment integration trace, and R the final receipt trace. Exact per-arm count is |$D_{n}$|+|V|+|$A_{n}$|+|R| on treatment and |$D_{n}$|+|V|+|$E_{n}$|+|R| on control. These quantities are obtained from the actual primitive traces and are not assumed equal to each other. Initial state preparation, descriptor bytes, allocation, delivery, timing/holding, old host retention, phase reference and optical resources are included as separately labeled positive physical charges as in the M08 paid-host source; full processing and full physical resource ledgers must never be conflated. The root lower bound survives all these nonnegative added costs.

The paired source doubles the old host and own-source stock and adds two independent external coherent model/forecast stocks plus their preparation, readout, retained displacement and holding services. All have declared finite expected energy at each finite n; continuous exactness and unbounded number support remain ideal-source premises. Extra external algebraic evaluation uses finite paid digital banks and a computable bounded schedule. No feedback from any resulting charge can leak a sign before lock. All replaced coherent stocks and unused beam-splitter outputs are retained. No completed logical reset is used; reset count is zero and no positive heat statement follows.

There is no uniform bound on total control cost asserted: exact stage-dependent descriptor installation, proof evaluation and paid host size may grow. Thus this certificate deliberately does not invoke M.10.12a/c to claim measured-cost ratio or subtractive divergence. Original items 1–4,8 and a treatment reduction do not require that stronger contrast claim. A constant bounded-control implementation would be a separate optional construction.

### Complete paired execution, source and meter

### Finite wire context and state

Each arm has one immutable identity bit i. The paired 512-bit big-endian descriptor consists of the 32 uint16 fields listed as $paired_{\mathrm{context}}$ in the inventory data of the proof of Theorem M.6.6c, with meanings: magic words, version, n, $\alpha$ numerator/denominator, $\delta$ numerator/denominator, r numerator/denominator, s numerator/denominator, d numerator/denominator, target-location numerator/denominator, N, base J, peripheral m, peripheral J, total external-mode count, arm count, one-shot flag, then reserved zeros. Both receivers receive exactly this context plus the same one-bit T and a framed end marker. Independent fair target and arm-permutation bits are retained. Context transport is paid; the fixed M08 source recipes and giant native tables are already separately paid inventories, not payload secretly omitted from a declared full-source serialization.

The peripheral 1024-bit configuration contains the fields explicitly listed in the descriptor; their lengths sum to 1024. Padding is checked. A read instruction appends its designated input bit to its fixed address. Invalid addresses, malformed frames, unrecognized public constants, nonzero padding or phase violations enter absorbing FAIL. The native transition increments the phase counter and copies its complete prior configuration into a fresh bank. There are 2049 banks, enough for 2048 peripheral transitions and their initial state. Meter history has 2593 distinct 12-bit banks, one per total dispatch plus initial state; its stock is counted separately. The twelve-bit meter suffices because $2592<4096$.

### Total transition definition

The pre-trace has1024 dispatches:512 bit reads; two public target reads; one frame/equality check; one immutable-identity resolution; one certificate verification; two external mode preparations; a conditional external SWAP; one ready commit; and paid padding through slot 1023. The off-target receiver swaps its external $\operatorname{Enc}(d)$ with independently prepared $\operatorname{Enc}(0)$, retaining the displaced stock. The target receiver holds both external modes. Neither operation addresses either own-model coordinate.

The certificate verifier uses exact rational cross multiplication to check $\alpha =4/7$, $\delta =1/8$, $r=\alpha-\delta$, $s=\alpha-\delta/2$, $d=\alpha+rs$, $0<\delta\le 1/8$, $r<s<\alpha$, and $h'(\alpha)<0$. It outputs the exact fractions $r$ and $1/\delta$ in the 128-bit certificate field. In this fixed nominated constructor every allowed tuple is the printed tuple, so a finite constant-comparison truth table implements the same decision; generic stages use the finite arithmetic constructor described below. These are independent source-data checks, never fitted to a cost record.

The base ordered trace has544 dispatches, not merely266:180 fresh E/Z preparations; four coherent stock preparations (the branch-dependent ancilla is prepared only after LOCK and the 16 private slots);266 native/control slots;90 separately metered source calls; and four additional optical calls (own SWAP, actuator, own diagnostic and forecast diagnostic). The M08 source-control slot allocation is:0 validation,1 target SWAP request,2+2k acquisition request and 3+2k counter increment for $k=0$..88,180 majority,181..188 bounded interpreter,189 report assembly,190 LOCK,191..206 private computation,207 actuator request,208 final evaluation request,209..210 diagnostics,211 release,212..265 padding. The default, target and companion stocks are prepared before control slot 0. The ancilla is prepared immediately after private slot 206, when its setting is available, and before the actuator at 207. Other physical calls occur immediately after their request, as printed in the ordered trace. Thus each acquisition and its retained-counter update occupy distinct charged slots. The chosen role determines which typed base function runs.

For $i=T$, those base functions are exactly the imported M08 transition generator and physical services, with the same private sign, own-state prediction and output port. For $i\ne T$, the base functions are paid padded identities on all own-model/report coordinates. Its fresh source stocks are prepared and retained, but the 90 source-call slots run isolated dummy instruments returning zero into the already allocated output-record cells, with no dependence on either host's sign. Its four optical stock preparations occur in the same paid inventory. The own SWAP and actuator slots are identity optical services, and both diagnostic slots use only the already paid unused target/companion dummy modes. The protected own-model mode is never measured in an off-target trial; no non-disturbing readout or QND premise is assumed. No dummy output writes an own predictive coordinate. These identity/dummy kernels are explicitly admitted physical primitives with positive tariffs and retained histories. They add no causal path to the treatment. Registering this role-dependent kernel is essential; it is not a claim that identical receiver contexts imply identical instruction effects.

After base release there are 1024 further peripheral dispatches: base-completion check, external diagnostic, external certificate release, meter receipt, previous-trial disconnection, and identity padding. FAIL is retained, padded and counted; no rejected run leaves the reliability denominator. The full trace has2592 dispatches per arm. Every primitive drives one packaged meter tick, recorded in a fresh12-bit bank. The meter service's physical cost and history stock are separately positive; its internal gate work is included in that primitive's declared packaged tariff, not invoked recursively as an infinite hierarchy of ticks.

Each native peripheral function $f$ is total on 1024-bit inputs, including malformed states. The reversible realization $(x,y)\to(x,y\oplus f(x))$ retains $x$. Construct each table by enumerating the finite input domain and applying the terminating rules above. At most 16 tables of $1024\cdot 2^{1024}$ bits plus $16Jm+4096$ finite routing/control bits are sufficient. The enormous native-lookup price $E(1+ROM)$ is charged for every peripheral slot. This is a physical-source primitive, not a claimed constant-cost Boolean computation. In particular, the join analysis requires no Boolean expansion of the imported native-table primitive. If Boolean expansion is chosen instead, its larger circuit, stock, duration and meter become a different positively charged implementation; no lower bound relies on cheaper execution.

### Complete new and retained inventories

Both full M08 nominated host stocks are paid and retained, even though only one executes an own-model challenge. The paired descriptor embeds and hashes the imported base descriptor. Its exact new-cell sum and ROM count are not replaced by asymptotic notation. Each arm additionally pays the printed peripheral configuration-history, control, receipt, input-frame, identity, meter-history, algebraic-certificate and ROM cell categories. Category sums are exact integers. Two external coherent modes per arm are additional: $\operatorname{Enc}(d)$ and $\operatorname{Enc}(0)$, with total expected excitation $d^{2}/2=25090081/78675968$ and four-mode zero-point contribution $2\hbar\omega$. Initial preparation, SWAP, retained displaced states, readout and 12-mode phase/holding services all have explicit positive tariffs.

All R14 stocks/timers and the same old retained inventory of the source of Definition 2.6e are held for the full2592-dispatch padded window, not just266 slots. All base and peripheral digital stock receives an additional positive holding tariff across that full window. This deliberately over-reserves common resources rather than understating cost. Base core service charges remain fully paid, and peripheral native-table, delivery/frame/identity, external optical and meter services have separate positive charges. Every fee is printed in the descriptor. E,R,$\hbar$,$\omega$ are the fixed positive source units. $N_{\mathrm{old},\mathrm{retained},\mathrm{cells}}$ is the exact immutable stock of the imported host of Definition 2.6e, not an adjustable unpopulated new category.

The full common source window uses3 $\tau$ per dispatch, hence7776 $\tau$ after the original18 $\tau$ qualification window. No old qualification response is overwritten. Public reservations are fixed at the maximum across target directions, source signs and branch settings before LOCK. Actual private drive energy/utilization and any sign-revealing records are released only after the target LOCK; there is exactly one attempt per independent sign. Fresh trials disconnect all old records and have independent initialized sources. The source remains ideal exact coherent/controlled optics with finite expected energy and unbounded number support; no empirical availability follows.

### Generic finite family

For each n, form $\delta =2$^(-n-3), $\alpha =4/7$, rational r,s,d and a finite N satisfying the stated odd-majority bound. Serialize all rational fields with an explicit finite length frame; B denotes their actual complete bit length. A standard terminating integer addition/multiplication/order-test program constructs and verifies the certificate. Fully unroll that program on this finite input into elementary reversible Boolean steps with retained predecessors; let V and W be the actual generated length and maximum workspace. They are computed outputs of that unrolling, not presumed constant.

Choose m as the next power of two above B+W+128+2 $\lceil \log_2 (B+V+128)\rceil$, and $J_{\mathrm{peripheral}}=B$+V+128. Allocate($J_{\mathrm{peripheral}}$+1)m history bits,16m+16J+256 control bits,3J receipt bits,B+2 input bits and the $full16m2^m$+16Jm+4096 ROM. Expand certificate/output fields if their actual encodings exceed 128; include that actual length in W and the cell sum. Base J must be at least T+2N+$J_{\mathrm{private}}$+64 with one retained predecessor bank for every state update; the M08 constructor of Theorem M.10.3c is the dependency. Add2(N+1) diagonal preparations,(N+1) acquisitions and 8 optical dispatches to the base count. Meter width is $\lceil \log_2 (total_{\mathrm{dispatches}}+1)\rceil$ and its history has $total_{\mathrm{dispatches}}$+1 banks. Extend every holding/phase reservation to that actual padded total. This is a total finite family constructor; no uniform finite hardware or constant control cost is asserted.

All copies, predecessor banks, unused outputs and displaced stocks survive. Completed reset count remains zero. Operation ticks and positive supplied energy do not establish positive heat.

∎

**Matched-receiver result.** Theorem M.10.12d fixes the input encoding, common meter, carryover, no-leakage timing, independently computed model access, crossed exchange and same-pattern reduction. It retains all host modes, private and public records, failures, finite-window stock and positive tariffs. One commitment per fresh independent sign and sign-independent precommit resources are hypotheses. The meter counts packaged source dispatches. ### M.6.10a Finite Perspective-Frame Backreaction

<a id="definition-m610a1-finite-perspective-frame-channel"></a>**Definition M.6.10a.1 (Finite Perspective-Frame Channel).** Let $s,s'\in\Sigma$ be two perspectives and let $\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{sh}}$ be the finite shared active protocol algebra on which both perspectives assign faithful density matrices
$$
\rho_s,\rho_{s'}>0.
$$
A finite perspective-frame channel from $s$ to $s'$ is an ND-RID-compatible CPTP channel on states over $\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{sh}}$ whose induced shared-protocol endpoint is $\rho_{s'}$ when initialized at $\rho_s$.

The irreducible frame-change distinguishability is
$$
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{QRF}}(s\to s')
:=
D(\rho_s\Vert\rho_{s'})
=
\operatorname{Tr}\rho_s(\log\rho_s-\log\rho_{s'}).
\tag{M.6.10a.1}
$$
If the support condition fails, set $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{QRF}}(s\to s')=\infty$.

A finite frame-change ledger is a self-adjoint cost observable $L_{s\to s'}$ on the active support satisfying
$$
L_{s\to s'}
\ge
\log\rho_s-\log\rho_{s'}
\tag{M.6.10a.2}
$$
in operator order. Its dimensionless action cost is
$$
\mathcal L_{s\to s'}
:=
\operatorname{Tr}\rho_s L_{s\to s'}.
\tag{M.6.10a.3}
$$

<a id="theorem-m610a2-quantum-reference-frame-cost-and-covariance-defect"></a>**Theorem M.6.10a.2 (Quantum Reference-Frame Cost and Covariance Defect).** For every finite perspective-frame pair of Definition M.6.10a.1:

1. $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{QRF}}(s\to s')\ge0$, with equality if and only if $\rho_s=\rho_{s'}$.

2. For every CPTP coarse-graining $\Lambda$ of the shared protocol algebra,
$$
D(\Lambda\rho_s\Vert\Lambda\rho_{s'})
\le
D(\rho_s\Vert\rho_{s'}).
\tag{M.6.10a.4}
$$

3. For every bounded shared observable $A\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{sh}}$,
$$
\left|
\operatorname{Tr}A(\rho_s-\rho_{s'})
\right|
\le
\lVert A\rVert_\infty
\sqrt{2\mathcal C_{\mathrm{QRF}}(s\to s')}.
\tag{M.6.10a.5}
$$

4. Every finite ledger implementation has the decomposition
$$
\mathcal L_{s\to s'}
=
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{QRF}}(s\to s')
+
\xi_{\mathrm{PCE}}(s\to s'),
\qquad
\xi_{\mathrm{PCE}}(s\to s')\ge0.
\tag{M.6.10a.6}
$$
On a branch whose independent physical-action bridge identifies this finite ledger with $\mathcal S_{s\to s'}^{\mathrm{phys}}/\hbar$, the associated physical action is
$$
\mathcal S_{s\to s'}^{\mathrm{phys}}
=
\hbar\,\mathcal L_{s\to s'}.
\tag{M.6.10a.7}
$$
Without that certificate, $\mathcal L_{s\to s'}$ is only the dimensionless relative-entropy ledger defined in (M.6.10a.3).
The ideal covariance limit is the zero-defect branch $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{QRF}}=0$ or a limiting branch in which the operationally tested observables have vanishing defect under (M.6.10a.5).

*Proof.* Item 1 is Klein's inequality for quantum relative entropy on a finite-dimensional faithful support, with equality exactly when the two density matrices agree.

Item 2 is the data-processing inequality for quantum relative entropy under CPTP maps.

For item 3, trace duality gives
$$
\left|
\operatorname{Tr}A(\rho_s-\rho_{s'})
\right|
\le
\lVert A\rVert_\infty
\lVert\rho_s-\rho_{s'}\rVert_1.
$$
Pinsker's inequality gives
$$
\lVert\rho_s-\rho_{s'}\rVert_1
\le
\sqrt{2D(\rho_s\Vert\rho_{s'})}.
$$
Combining these inequalities gives (M.6.10a.5).

For item 4, (M.6.10a.2) implies
$$
\operatorname{Tr}\rho_s L_{s\to s'}
\ge
\operatorname{Tr}\rho_s(\log\rho_s-\log\rho_{s'})
=
D(\rho_s\Vert\rho_{s'}).
$$
Define
$$
\xi_{\mathrm{PCE}}(s\to s')
:=
\operatorname{Tr}\rho_s
\left(
L_{s\to s'}-(\log\rho_s-\log\rho_{s'})
\right).
$$
The operator inequality (M.6.10a.2) makes $\xi_{\mathrm{PCE}}\ge0$, proving (M.6.10a.6). Equation (M.6.10a.7) is the independent physical-action identification assumed for this finite ledger. Theorem Q.0.1 and Corollary Q.0.1 provide a continuum scaling and calibrated history representation only when their convergence and recovery-history hypotheses are supplied. The final statement follows immediately from (M.6.10a.5). ∎

<a id="corollary-m610a3-perfect-perspective-covariance-as-a-pce-limit"></a>**Corollary M.6.10a.3 (Perfect Perspective Covariance as a PCE Limit).** A finite perspective transformation is exactly covariance-invisible on the shared active algebra if and only if
$$
\rho_s=\rho_{s'}.
$$
Otherwise every implementation has nonzero distinguishability cost on at least one separating shared observable, bounded below by the protocol family that separates $\rho_s$ from $\rho_{s'}$.

*Proof.* If $\rho_s=\rho_{s'}$, then every shared expectation value is identical and $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{QRF}}=0$ by Theorem M.6.10a.2. Conversely, if every shared observable has identical expectation value, finite-dimensional state separation implies $\rho_s=\rho_{s'}$. If the states differ, there exists a bounded observable separating them. Theorem M.6.10a.2 then gives positive relative entropy and a nonzero ledger cost for any finite implementation. ∎

### M.6.11 Blackwell-PCE Classicality

<a id="definition-m611a-finite-predictive-record-experiment"></a>**Definition M.6.11a (Finite Predictive Record Experiment).** Let $\Theta$ be a finite family of operationally distinguishable preparation states relevant to a measurement context, and let $R$ be a finite record alphabet. A record channel is a stochastic map
$$
\mathcal M:\Theta\to\Delta(R),
\qquad
\theta\mapsto p(r\mid\theta).
$$
Let $\pi(\theta)>0$ be the registered prior on the finite preparation family. Discard record letters with $\sum_\theta\pi(\theta)p(r\mid\theta)=0$ and use $R$ for the remaining alphabet; also discard zero-probability outputs of any post-processing when comparing its retained distinctions. Since the prior has full support, a discarded record has $p(r\mid\theta)=0$ for every $\theta$, so this restriction changes no channel response. For each task $j\in\mathcal T$, let $A_j$ be its finite action set and let $\ell_j(\theta,a)$ be its loss. Define the predictive profile of each retained record $r$ by the complete conditional-loss vector
$$
\Pi(r)
=
\left(
\mathbb E[\ell_j(\theta,a)\mid r]
\right)_{j\in\mathcal T,\,a\in A_j}.
\tag{M.6.11.1}
$$
Define
$$
r\sim r'
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Pi(r)=\Pi(r').
\tag{M.6.11.2}
$$
A post-processed record $Z$ is exactly $\mathcal T$-sufficient for $\mathcal M$ when there is a function $h$ such that $\Pi(R)=h(Z)$ almost surely under the registered joint experiment.
The quotient record channel is
$$
\mathcal M_{\min}:\Theta\to\Delta(R/{\sim}),
\qquad
p([r]\mid\theta)=\sum_{r'\in[r]}p(r'\mid\theta).
\tag{M.6.11.3}
$$

<a id="theorem-m611b-classical-quotient-as-the-minimal-sufficient-post-processing"></a>**Theorem M.6.11b (Classical Quotient as the Minimal Sufficient Post-Processing).** For the finite task family $\mathcal T$ and the registered experiment $\mathcal M$:

1. $\mathcal M_{\min}$ preserves every conditional and Bayes risk in $\mathcal T$.
2. $\mathcal M\succeq_B\mathcal M_{\min}$.
3. If $\mathcal N$ is a stochastic post-processing of $\mathcal M$ and is exactly $\mathcal T$-sufficient in the sense of Definition M.6.11a, then $\mathcal N\succeq_B\mathcal M_{\min}$.
4. The output algebra is
$$
\ell^\infty(R/{\sim}).
\tag{M.6.11.5}
$$
5. If PCE cost is strictly increasing under sufficient record refinements that do not reduce any risk in $\mathcal T$, then $\mathcal M_{\min}$ is the unique PCE-minimal sufficient post-processing of $\mathcal M$, up to relabeling.

*Proof.* By (M.6.11.1), every conditional risk $\mathbb E[\ell_j(\theta,a)\mid r]$ is a component of $\Pi(r)$. It is constant on each equivalence class, so every action comparison, conditional optimum, and prior average is unchanged after replacing $r$ by $[r]$. This proves item 1.

The deterministic quotient map $q(r)=[r]$ satisfies $\mathcal M_{\min}=q\circ\mathcal M$, proving item 2. Let $Z$ be the output of a post-processing $\mathcal N$ as in item 3. Exact sufficiency gives $\Pi(R)=h(Z)$ almost surely. Since the equivalence class $[R]$ is precisely the level set label of $\Pi(R)$, there is a function $\bar h$ with $[R]=\bar h(Z)$ almost surely. Thus $\mathcal M_{\min}=\bar h\circ\mathcal N$, so $\mathcal N\succeq_B\mathcal M_{\min}$.

The observables of the finite classical quotient are all bounded functions on $R/{\sim}$, giving item 4. Finally, every exactly sufficient post-processing determines $[R]$ by item 3; any additional retained distinction is a refinement that changes none of the listed risks. Strict PCE monotonicity excludes every strict such refinement, leaving only relabelings of $R/{\sim}$. This proves item 5. ∎

<a id="corollary-m611c-classical-record-quotient-and-conditional-pce-minimality"></a>**Corollary M.6.11c (Classical-Record Quotient and Conditional PCE Minimality).** Given an independently registered classical finite record channel $\mathcal M:\Theta\to\Delta(R)$, its risk-equivalence quotient is exactly sufficient and has commutative output algebra $\ell^\infty(R/{\sim})$. If PCE cost is strictly increasing under every sufficient refinement that changes none of the registered task risks, the quotient is also the unique PCE-minimal sufficient record up to relabeling. A quantum interaction supplies such a classical record only after an independent instrument, dephasing, and readout bridge is registered.

*Proof.* Items 1--3 of Theorem M.6.11b give exact sufficiency. Item 4 identifies the quotient algebra as $\ell^\infty(R/{\sim})$, whose commutativity is inherited from the assumed classical record alphabet rather than derived from minimality. Under the strict-cost hypothesis, item 5 gives PCE minimality and uniqueness up to relabeling. ∎

<a id="definition-m611d-ppi-objective-fragment-family"></a>**Definition M.6.11d (PPI-Objective Fragment Family).** Let $S$ be a finite system with PCE-minimal classical record alphabet $X$ selected by Theorem M.6.11b, and let $E_1,\dots,E_N$ be disjoint finite environmental fragments. A state on
$$
S E_1\cdots E_N
$$
is considered on the occurring record support when its conditional states are inferred from that state: each retained label then has $p_x>0$. A claim over an entire registered input alphabet, including labels absent from one input law, must supply normalized conditional states for those labels as independent family data. Such a family is provided explicitly in Theorem M.6.11g and cannot be inferred from the absent blocks of a single joint state. The state or supplied family is exactly PPI-objective for $X$ when:

1. the system record algebra is
$$
\ell^\infty(X)
$$
with minimal central projectors $\{|x\rangle\langle x|\}_{x\in X}$;

2. for every fragment $E_i$ there exists a POVM $\{M_i^x\}_{x\in X}$ such that
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(M_i^x\rho_{E_i}^{x'})=\delta_{xx'}
\tag{M.6.11.6}
$$
for all $x,x'$;

3. conditioned on $X=x$, the fragments are independent:
$$
\rho_{E_1\cdots E_N}^{x}
=
\rho_{E_1}^{x}\otimes\cdots\otimes\rho_{E_N}^{x};
\tag{M.6.11.7}
$$

4. no strict refinement $X'\to X$ satisfies items 1–3 with the same exterior predictive risks at lower or equal PCE cost.

The associated spectrum-broadcast form is
$$
\rho_{SE_1\cdots E_N}
=
\sum_{x\in X}
p_x
|x\rangle\langle x|_S
\otimes
\rho_{E_1}^{x}\otimes\cdots\otimes\rho_{E_N}^{x},
\tag{M.6.11.8}
$$
with fragment distinguishability
$$
\rho_{E_i}^{x}\rho_{E_i}^{x'}=0
\qquad
(x\ne x').
\tag{M.6.11.9}
$$

<a id="theorem-m611e-spectrum-broadcast-ppi-objectivity-on-the-dephased-branch"></a>**Theorem M.6.11e (Spectrum-Broadcast PPI Objectivity on the Dephased Branch).** Let $X$ be the risk-equivalence quotient output of $\mathcal M_{\min}$ in Theorem M.6.11b, and assume that PCE cost is strictly increasing under every sufficient record refinement that changes none of the registered risks. Assume also that the PCE-compressed joint state is invariant under dephasing in the selected record basis:
$$
(\Delta_X\otimes\operatorname{id}_{E_1\cdots E_N})(\rho)=\rho,
\qquad
\Delta_X(Y)=\sum_x|x\rangle\langle x|Y|x\rangle\langle x|.
$$
For the state-based equivalence, assume $p_x=\operatorname{Tr}[(|x\rangle\langle x|\otimes I)\rho]>0$ for every retained $x$. Then $X$ is exactly PPI-objective in the sense of Definition M.6.11d if and only if the joint state has the spectrum-broadcast form (M.6.11.8)–(M.6.11.9).

Thus the layered structure is:

1. Theorem G.1.7 fixes Born probabilities for a perspective.

2. Theorem M.6.11b selects the PCE-minimal classical record for one measurement context.

3. Theorem M.6.11e characterizes when that record becomes public across many disjoint perspectives.

*Proof.* Suppose first that the state has the spectrum-broadcast form. The system algebra generated by $|x\rangle\langle x|$ is $\ell^\infty(X)$. For fragment $E_i$, let $P_i^x$ be the support projection of $\rho_{E_i}^x$. Condition (M.6.11.9) makes these projections pairwise orthogonal, so
$$
C_i:=I_{E_i}-\sum_x P_i^x\ge0.
$$
Choose a retained label $x_0$ and define
$$
M_i^{x_0}=P_i^{x_0}+C_i,\qquad
M_i^x=P_i^x\quad(x\ne x_0).
$$
These positive effects sum to $I_{E_i}$. The complement $C_i$ annihilates every conditional-state support, so
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(M_i^x\rho_{E_i}^{x'})=\delta_{xx'}.
$$
Thus every fragment recovers $x$ exactly. The conditional product in (M.6.11.8) proves independence. The strict-cost hypothesis and Theorem M.6.11b exclude risk-preserving strict refinements at lower or equal cost. Hence the record is PPI-objective.

Conversely, suppose the record is PPI-objective. Since the system record algebra is $\ell^\infty(X)$, the PCE-compressed state is classical on the selected central record:
$$
\rho_{SE_1\cdots E_N}
=
\sum_{x\in X}
p_x
|x\rangle\langle x|_S
\otimes
\rho_{E_1\cdots E_N}^{x}.
\tag{M.6.11.10}
$$
Item 3 of Definition M.6.11d gives the conditional product decomposition (M.6.11.7), so (M.6.11.10) becomes (M.6.11.8).

It remains to prove orthogonality. Fix a fragment $E_i$. Perfect recovery means that there is a POVM $\{M_i^x\}$ satisfying (M.6.11.6). For $x\ne x'$,
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(M_i^x\rho_{E_i}^{x'})=0.
$$
