Thus (M.6.13l.5) gives $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge\Phi(\eta_Q(\sigma))$ whenever $0<\eta_Q(\sigma)<1$.

Every finite reference in fact has $\eta_Q(\sigma)<1$. For the maximizing finite raising $L$, nilpotence makes $I-L$ invertible, and
$$
I-H_L=\frac{(I-L)^*(I-L)+(I-L)(I-L)^*}{2}>0,
\qquad
1-\eta_Q(\sigma)=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(I-H_L)>0.
\tag{M.6.13l.7}
$$
If $\eta_Q(\sigma)>0$, the maximizing $L$ is nonzero. At $\lambda_* =\kappa/(2\sqrt{\eta_Q(\sigma)})$, where $c(\kappa)=\sqrt{\eta_Q(\sigma)}$, the strict version of Theorem M.6.13k yields $Z_{\lambda_*}<S(\lambda_*)$. Combining this with (M.6.13l.6) gives the stronger pointwise assertion
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)>\Phi(\eta_Q(\sigma))
\quad\text{if}\quad 0<\eta_Q(\sigma)<1.
\tag{M.6.13l.8}
$$
For every original admitted model of error at most $\epsilon$, Theorem M.6.13h gives $\eta_Q(\sigma)\ge1-\epsilon^2=u>0$. Strict increase of $\Phi$ therefore proves (M.6.13l.2) and the lower-infimum bound in (M.6.13l.1). This covers every original finite apparatus, not merely the balanced or Fourier models.

For completeness, the matching exact-error finite family can be restated explicitly from Theorem M.6.13j. For any integer $N\ge3$ with $N>1/\epsilon^2$, let
$$
\begin{aligned}
Q_N&=\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}n|n\rangle\langle n|,
&\theta_j&=2\pi j/N,
&|\theta_j\rangle&=N^{-1/2}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}e^{in\theta_j}|n\rangle,\\
Z_N(k)&=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}e^{k\cos\theta_j},
&w_j(k)&=e^{k\cos\theta_j}/Z_N(k),
&\sigma_{N,k}&=\sum_jw_j(k)|\theta_j\rangle\langle\theta_j|,\\
c_N(k)&=\sum_jw_j(k)\cos\theta_j,
&L_{N,k}&=c_N(k)\sum_{n=0}^{N-2}|n+1\rangle\langle n|.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13l.9}
$$
The Fourier vectors are orthonormal, $\mathcal G_{Q_N}\sigma_{N,k}=I/N$, and each adjacent coherence is $c_N(k)/N$. The imaginary part vanishes by $j\mapsto N-j$. Since $c_N'(k)$ is the strictly positive discrete variance of $\cos\theta_j$, $c_N(0)=0$, and $c_N(k)\to1$, there is a unique finite $k=\kappa_N>0$ for which
$$
(1-1/N)c_N(\kappa_N)^2=u,
\qquad
\epsilon_\infty^2=1-(1-1/N)c_N(\kappa_N)^2=\epsilon^2,
\qquad
\mathcal A_{Q_N}(\sigma_{N,\kappa_N})
=\kappa_Nc_N(\kappa_N)-\log[Z_N(\kappa_N)/N].
\tag{M.6.13l.10}
$$
Both noise eigenvalues of the invariant $B_{L_{N,\kappa_N}}$ in Theorem M.6.13h equal the displayed squared error. Its spectral-projector controlled shift on a pure neutral pointer is a finite conserving dilation with a charge-commuting pointer and exactly these first two moments. Thus the error is exact for the worst case over all inputs. Appending the pure neutral pointer leaves asymmetry unchanged.

Locally uniform Riemann-sum convergence gives $Z_N(k)/N\to I_0(k)$ and $c_N(k)\to c(k)$. To verify convergence of the roots, bracket $\kappa$ by any two positive points on either side of it. Strict increase of $c$ and uniform convergence put $\kappa_N$ between these points for all sufficiently large $N$; shrinking the bracket proves $\kappa_N\to\kappa$. Consequently
$$
\lim_{N\to\infty}\mathcal A_{Q_N}(\sigma_{N,\kappa_N})
=\kappa\sqrt u-\log I_0(\kappa)=\Phi(u).
\tag{M.6.13l.11}
$$
The limit is taken at each fixed $0<\epsilon<1$. It proves the matching upper bound without replacing a finite model by an infinite apparatus. The equivalence between exact-error and at-most-error infima is also the operational reduction (M.6.13h.4).

Finally, (M.6.13h.2) and (M.6.13l.7) imply $e_Q(\sigma)^2\ge1-\eta_Q(\sigma)>0$, proving finite zero-error impossibility. At $\epsilon=1$, take any invariant finite reference, the identity interaction, and the constant zero pointer. Its noise operator is $-X_S$, whose square is the identity, so its worst-case error is exactly one and its asymmetry is zero. Nonnegativity of relative entropy makes this an attaining zero-resource endpoint. The endpoint statement does not extend interior nonattainment to error one. $\square$

<a id="proposition-m613m-finite-spin-one-upper-family-and-fixed-reference-optimum"></a>**Proposition M.6.13m (Finite Spin-One Upper Family and Fixed-Reference Optimum).** Let
$$
Q_S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2),\qquad
X=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\1&0&1\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}.
$$
For every $0\le u\le45/88$, a complete apparatus of dimension $15$ realizes worst-case squared Ozawa error exactly $1-u$, with natural-$\log$ reference asymmetry
$$
A_{15}(u)=H(3/16,5/8,3/16)
-H\left(1/8,\;7/16-\tfrac12\sqrt{9/64+11u/9},\;
7/16+\tfrac12\sqrt{9/64+11u/9}\right).
\tag{M.6.13m.1}
$$
Here $H$ is Shannon entropy in nats, with $0\log0=0$. This is an upper bound on the original arbitrary finite-apparatus entropy frontier. It is also the exact noise optimum at its specified charged ready state, rather than an optimum over all ready states of the same asymmetry.

*Proof.* Use a three-dimensional charged reference with $Q_R=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2)$ and
$$
\sigma_u=\begin{pmatrix}
3/16&\sqrt{11u/72}&1/16\\
\sqrt{11u/72}&5/8&\sqrt{11u/72}\\
1/16&\sqrt{11u/72}&3/16
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13m.2}
$$
The odd reflection vector has eigenvalue $1/8$. In the even reflection sector the remaining matrix is
$$
\begin{pmatrix}1/4&\sqrt{11u}/6\\\sqrt{11u}/6&5/8\end{pmatrix}.
$$
Its eigenvalues are the last two arguments in (M.6.13m.1), and its determinant is $5/32-11u/36$. Thus (M.6.13m.2) is a density matrix exactly for $0\le u\le45/88$ among real nonnegative $u$. Charge dephasing leaves diagonal probabilities $(3/16,5/8,3/16)$, proving the asymmetry formula. At $u=0$ the charge-two coherence remains $1/16$, and $A_{15}(0)=\tfrac18\log(32/27)>0$; no zero-quality optimality is claimed for this seed.

In the system-reference basis $|s,r\rangle$, define an invariant Hermitian observable $B_u$ by
$$
\langle0,1|B_u|1,0\rangle=\langle1,2|B_u|2,1\rangle=a,
\qquad
\langle0,2|B_u|1,1\rangle=\langle1,1|B_u|2,0\rangle=b,
$$
its adjoint entries, and zero elsewhere, with
$$
a=\frac{4\sqrt{11u}}{11},\qquad b=\frac{2\sqrt{11u}}{11}.
\tag{M.6.13m.3}
$$
Every edge preserves total charge. In the orthonormal system basis
$$
e=(|0\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2,\qquad m=|1\rangle,\qquad
o=(|0\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2,
$$
direct multiplication gives the complete conditional noise matrix
$$
K_{\sigma_u}(B_u)=\operatorname{diag}_{e,m,o}(1-u,\;1-u,\;21u/22).
\tag{M.6.13m.4}
$$
This uses both the first and the second pointer moment. Since $45/88<22/43$, the largest eigenvalue is $1-u$ on the whole positivity interval. At $u=45/88$ the first two eigenvalues exceed the third by $1/1936$. Every system state, including the marginal of a state with arbitrary spectators, is tested by this largest-eigenvalue formula.

For $u>0$, the distinct eigenvalues of $B_u$ are $0,+a,-a,+\sqrt2b,-\sqrt2b$, of multiplicities $3,2,2,1,1$. Write $B_u=\sum_{j=0}^4\nu_j\Pi_j$. Append a neutral five-dimensional pointer in $|0\rangle$, with $M_P=\operatorname{diag}(\nu_0,\ldots,\nu_4)$ and cyclic shift $V$ on these same five levels. Then
$$
U=\sum_{j=0}^4\Pi_j\otimes V^j
\tag{M.6.13m.5}
$$
conserves system-plus-reference charge. Ready-state compression of $U^*(I\otimes M_P)U$ and its square gives $B_u$ and $B_u^2$. The full apparatus is $R\otimes P$, of dimension $3\cdot5=15$, charge $Q_R\otimes I_5$ and ready state $\sigma_u\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|$. All five outcomes are retained. The system-inclusive dimension is $45$. At $u=0$ the same dimension bound works with zero pointer calibration.

For the fixed-state lower certificate, parity oddification, simultaneous system/reference reflection, and complex-conjugation averaging preserve the real reflection-invariant $\sigma_u$ and do not increase maximum noise. As in Theorem M.6.13h, operator convexity of the square justifies each averaging. These operations reduce the invariant observable to arbitrary real edges $a',b'$ in the displayed four positions. Direct multiplication yields
$$
\begin{aligned}
K_e&=1-\frac{\sqrt{11u}}3(a'+b')+\frac58(a')^2+\frac14(b')^2,\\
K_m&=1-\frac{\sqrt{11u}}3(a'+b')+\frac38(a')^2+\frac54(b')^2,\\
K_o&=\frac58(a')^2+\frac18(b')^2.
\end{aligned}
$$
The exact square identity
$$
\tfrac13K_e+\tfrac23K_m
=1-u+\frac{11}{24}\left(a'-\frac{4\sqrt{11u}}{11}\right)^2
+\frac{11}{12}\left(b'-\frac{2\sqrt{11u}}{11}\right)^2
\tag{M.6.13m.6}
$$
is a global lower certificate at this fixed seed. Equation (M.6.13m.3) attains it while respecting the third-input constraint. An independent neutral ready-state extension cannot lower this optimum: compressing its invariant observable gives an invariant Hermitian observable on the original system/reference, and its second-moment leakage is positive. An independent mixed neutral append may first be purified with another neutral factor for this lower-bound proof. A correlated neutral extension with the same charged marginal is a different reference state and is outside this fixed-seed claim. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613n-physical-spin-realization-of-the-qubit-entropy-infimum"></a>**Theorem M.6.13n (Physical Spin Realization of the Qubit Entropy Infimum).** For the system qubit with $Q_S=|1\rangle\langle1|$, target $X=\sigma_x$, and each $0<\epsilon<1$, the following finite distinguishable-spin source class has complete ready-state relative-entropy $J_z$ asymmetry infimum $\Phi(1-\epsilon^2)$ of Theorem M.6.13l. Every member conserves actual additive physical $J_z$, has an invariant terminal pointer, tests all system states from a product input, and retains every physical complement sector, the direction carrier, clock and output record. The class permits the explicitly specified bounded finite spin-scalar couplings and the owned scalar state-supply, timing, switching and detector services below. At each interior error the infimum is approached by exact-error finite sources and is not attained by any finite member. The optimization resource is complete ready-state $J_z$ asymmetry; the separate implementation vector is stated in Part VI.

*Proof and construction.*

**I. Qubit reference, induced moments and finite witness.**

Use Definition M.6.13a and Theorems M.6.13b, M.6.13g, M.6.13h, M.6.13j and M.6.13l. The measured quantity is the supremum over **all** input system states of the Ozawa RMS error, including the actual pointer's second moment. The apparatus state is independent of the input. All apparatus factors present or accessible during the run are counted. Entropies use natural logarithms.

For an ideal error $\epsilon'\in(0,1)$, choose $N\ge3$, $N>1/(\epsilon')^2$. Put
$$
\theta_j=2\pi j/N,\quad |\theta_j\rangle=N^{-1/2}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}e^{in\theta_j}|n\rangle,
\quad w_j=\frac{e^{\kappa\cos\theta_j}}{Z_N(\kappa)},\quad
\sigma=\sum_jw_j|\theta_j\rangle\langle\theta_j|.
$$
Choose the unique finite $\kappa>0$ satisfying
$$
c=\sum_jw_j\cos\theta_j,\qquad (1-1/N)c^2=1-(\epsilon')^2.
$$
Then $Q_N=\operatorname{diag}(0,\ldots,N-1)$, $\mathcal G_{Q_N}\sigma=I/N$, and
$$
\mathcal A_{Q_N}(\sigma)=\log N-H(w)=\kappa c-\log(Z_N/N).
\tag{M.6.13n.1}
$$
For $L=c\sum_{n=0}^{N-2}|n+1\rangle\langle n|$, the invariant observable
$$
B=\begin{pmatrix}0&L\\L^*&0\end{pmatrix}
$$
has eigenvalues $0,+c,-c$; its two noise eigenvalues are both $(\epsilon')^2$. These are the finite witnesses of Theorem M.6.13j.

Let $\Pi_0,\Pi_+,\Pi_-$ be the spectral projectors. A four-level neutral pointer has a three-cycle $V:0\to1\to2\to0$, with level 3 fixed. Starting at 0, define
$$
U_N=\Pi_0\otimes I+\Pi_+\otimes V+\Pi_-\otimes V^2,
\quad M_P=c(|1\rangle\langle1|-|2\rangle\langle2|).
\tag{M.6.13n.2}
$$
Its first two ready-state pointer moments are $B,B^2$, $\|M_P\|=c<1$, and $U_N^3=I$.

**II. Complete physical spin encoding.**

The system is one physical spin half. Encode the reference ladder into the symmetric subspace of $N-1$ distinguishable physical spin halves:
$$
E_N|n\rangle=|D_n^{N-1}\rangle,
\quad Q_R=\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}(I-Z_i)/2,
\quad Q_RE_N=E_NQ_N.
\tag{M.6.13n.3}
$$
The physical reference Hilbert space remains all of $(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes(N-1)}$. The isometry intertwines charge twirling, so it preserves (M.6.13n.1) exactly.

Encode each of two pointer bits in the following two four-spin singlets:
$$
|0_L\rangle=(|01\rangle-|10\rangle)_{12}(|01\rangle-|10\rangle)_{34}/2,
$$
$$
|1_L\rangle=\frac{|0011\rangle+|1100\rangle-(|0101\rangle+|0110\rangle+|1001\rangle+|1010\rangle)/2}{\sqrt3}.
$$
Two such blocks encode pointer levels 0,1,2,3, and all $2^8$ physical pointer states remain. Each code vector has total spin zero. Write $P_a$ for the four rank-one code projectors, $P_\perp=I-\sum_aP_a$. Extend (M.6.13n.2) by identity off the reference-symmetric/pointer-code sector. This full-space unitary still obeys $U_N^3=I$ and commutes with physical $J_z$. The pointer is $c(P_1-P_2)$, zero on the complement, and commutes with all three physical spin components.

The signal W has $N+8$ physical spin halves, including the system. Its active code is SU(2)-invariant and has largest spin $j_{\max}=N/2$. For any $\tau>0$, the exact logarithm
$$
K_N=\frac{2\pi\hbar}{3\tau\sqrt3}\,i(U_N-U_N^*),
\quad e^{-i\tau K_N/\hbar}=U_N,
\quad \|K_N\|=\frac{2\pi\hbar}{3\tau}
\tag{M.6.13n.4}
$$
vanishes off that active code and commutes with $J_z^W$. The cubic spectrum proves every identity in (M.6.13n.4), without choosing a numerical logarithm.

**III. Rotation-invariant coupling and uniform error.**

Append $m=2J$ physical spin halves $F$, ready in $|J,J\rangle=|0\rangle^{\otimes m}$. Keep their entire $2^m$-dimensional carrier. This state has exactly zero $J_z$ asymmetry. It does have $SU(2)$ asymmetry $\log(m+1)$, and its polarization and size are real resources retained in the ledger.

Let $R_W(g)$ be physical simultaneous spin rotation, $|J,g\rangle=R_J(g)|J,J\rangle$, and use normalized $SU(2)$ Haar measure. Define
$$
H_J=(m+1)\int R_W(g)K_NR_W(g)^*\otimes|J,g\rangle\langle J,g|\,dg
\tag{M.6.13n.5}
$$
on $W$ times the symmetric $F$ sector, and extend it by zero on nonsymmetric $F$. This is a **single finite specified Hamiltonian**, not a protocol that physically performs continuous averaging. It is Hermitian, commutes with the full physical $SU(2)$ action, preserves the active $W$ code and symmetric $F$, and satisfies $\|H_J\|\le\|K_N\|$.

Here is a complete analytic error estimate. The map on bounded operator-valued functions
$$
\mathcal F(f)=(m+1)\int f(g)\otimes|J,g\rangle\langle J,g|\,dg
$$
is unital CP on the symmetric F sector, because $(m+1)\int|J,g\rangle\langle J,g|dg=I$. For $f(g)=K_g-K_N$, Kadison's inequality gives
$$
(H_J-K_N\otimes I)^2\le\mathcal F((K_g-K_N)^2).
$$
Axial invariance of $K_N$ and an Euler decomposition reduce the difference norm to a polar rotation by $\theta$. On the active sector,
$$
\|K_g-K_N\|\le2j_{\max}\|K_N\|\theta,
\qquad \theta^2\le\pi^2\sin^2(\theta/2).
$$
With $x=\sin^2(\theta/2)$, the ready-state coherent kernel is exactly the normalized density $(m+1)(1-x)^m dx$. Its mean x is $1/(m+2)$. Thus, uniformly over unit signal vectors, also with arbitrary spectators,
$$
\|(H_J-K_N\otimes I)(\psi\otimes|J,J\rangle)\|
\le\frac{2\pi j_{\max}\|K_N\|}{\sqrt{m+2}}.
\tag{M.6.13n.6}
$$
Duhamel's $\int$ compares $e^{-itH_J/\hbar}$ with $e^{-itK_N/\hbar}\otimes I$; the latter keeps the direction state ready and the signal in its active sector throughout. Therefore
$$
\delta:=\|[e^{-i\tau H_J/\hbar}-(U_N\otimes I)](I_W\otimes|J,J\rangle)\|
\le\frac{2\pi^2N}{3\sqrt{m+2}}.
\tag{M.6.13n.7}
$$
This converges to zero for each fixed finite $N$. Exact conservation holds at every finite m, independently of approximation quality.

**Finite coupling coefficients.**

For $n=N+m+8$ physical spins, every operator commuting with collective $SU(2)$ is a finite linear combination of permutation operators on the $n$ distinguishable spin factors (the spin-half Schur–Weyl commutant). Each transposition is the physical rotational scalar
$$
P_{ij}=\tfrac12I+2\mathbf s_i\cdot\mathbf s_j/\hbar^2.
\tag{M.6.13n.8}
$$
Consequently (M.6.13n.5) has a Hermitian finite exchange-polynomial representation on the full physical carrier, not merely on a logical code. With extra scalar factors its coefficients are finite matrices on those factors.

The coefficients are explicitly defined by a finite procedure: enumerate the $n!$ permutation matrices; greedily select a Hilbert–Schmidt-independent spanning subset $P_{\pi_\alpha}$; form the nonsingular Gram matrix $G_{\alpha\beta}=\operatorname{Tr}(P_{\pi_\alpha}^*P_{\pi_\beta})$; and solve $Gc=h$, where $h_\alpha=\operatorname{Tr}(P_{\pi_\alpha}^*H_J)$. For scalar-controller entries perform this solve entrywise, then Hermitian symmetrize. The finite Haar operation in (M.6.13n.5) is evaluated exactly by angular-momentum block decomposition: on each spin-L block replace the magnetic part by its normalized partial trace times $I_{2L+1}$, retaining all multiplicity entries. This specifies exact real/complex coefficients, supports and finite matrices; no stochastic averaging or uncounted orientation control is involved. The representation-theory input is the finite Schur–Weyl decomposition (Bacon, Chuang and Harrow 2006). No efficient or pairwise-pulse synthesis claim is used.

**IV. Positive scalar source, clock and complete record.**

A spin-zero four-level record D starts at 0. Let $V_4$ shift its four levels cyclically. The full-space scalar record-copy unitary is
$$
C=\sum_{a=0}^3P_a\otimes V_4^a+P_\perp\otimes I_D.
$$
It commutes with all physical spin components. Define
$$
W_0=C(e^{-i\tau H_J/\hbar}\otimes I_D),\quad W_1=I,\quad W_2=W_0^*.
$$
A spin-zero three-cell controller starts in 0, and
$$
d_j=|j+1\bmod3\rangle\langle j|\otimes W_j,\quad D_c=\sum_jd_j,\quad A_c=i(D_c-D_c^*).
$$
Then $D_c^3=I$, $\operatorname{spec}A_c=\{0,\pm\sqrt3\}$. For a registered $T>0$ choose
$$
\gamma=\frac{2\pi\hbar}{3\sqrt3T},\qquad
H_{\rm src}=3\sqrt3\gamma I+\gamma A_c.
\tag{M.6.13n.9}
$$
Its spectrum is $\{2\sqrt3\gamma,3\sqrt3\gamma,4\sqrt3\gamma\}$, so it is strictly positive; $e^{-iTH_{\rm src}/\hbar}=D_c$. This follows by evaluating the three cubic eigenvalues and observing that the scalar reserve phase is $e^{-2\pi i}=1$. The source is a full-space finite spin-scalar Hamiltonian, expressible by (M.6.13n.8) with finite scalar-cell/record matrix coefficients. Its physical charge is the ordinary additive $J_z$, not its controller-shift logarithm.

To provide a stable readout window, use a registered continuously differentiable nonnegative scalar envelope $\lambda(t)$, of finite duration $t_g>0$, zero at both ends, with finite supremum and derivative and $\int_0^{t_g}\lambda(t)dt=T$. Set $H(t)=b_0I+\lambda(t)H_{\rm src}$, $b_0\ge0$. For an entirely explicit continuously differentiable choice, let $x=t/t_g$ and
$$
\lambda(t)=\frac{30T}{t_g}x^2(1-x)^2,\quad
\|\lambda\|_\infty=\frac{15T}{8t_g},\quad
\|\dot\lambda\|_\infty=\frac{10\sqrt3T}{3t_g^2},\quad
\operatorname{TV}(\lambda)=\frac{15T}{4t_g}.
$$
Extend it by zero outside the pulse; it is continuously differentiable. The endpoint is $D_c$ up to a global phase. The interaction is then off. A positive-duration spin-zero detector service reads the four record projectors, with pointer
$$
M_D=c(|1\rangle\langle1|-|2\rangle\langle2|).
$$
All four outcome states exist; labels 0 and 3 are separately available even when both receive numerical value zero. The full instrument is the four-projector Born instrument on D, with its duration, storage and service energies entered below. No final collapse is smuggled into the conserving unitary. This uses the terminal-pointer convention of the conserving measurement class. If a further neutral detector/archive factor is used in a chosen service realization, it is appended and its full finite dimension is multiplied into the count.

The unmodulated cyclic source would revive at 3T; no permanent autonomous halt is claimed. The owned scalar envelope supplies isolation before readout. All post-ready services have trivial spin representation, start independently of $\sigma$, and cannot provide a hidden transverse spin-phase standard.

The standard finite Schrödinger action with the specified $H(t)$ is invariant under physical simultaneous spin rotations. Its Noether generator is the actual $J_z=\sum_i s_i^z$ (and similarly x,y); direct commutation proves its conservation. No geometric spatial-translation or electromagnetic identification is inferred.

**V. Complete ready asymmetry and prescribed error.**

The complete ready apparatus is the product of $E_N\sigma E_N^*$, the eight-spin singlet pointer at 0, $|0\rangle^{\otimes m}$, record 0 and clock 0, together with any independent scalar service state. On each ancillary ready factor $J_z$ is scalar. Therefore global charge dephasing acts only on the original ladder state, and entropy additivity gives
$$
\mathcal A_{J_z}^{\rm complete}=\mathcal A_{Q_N}(\sigma)=\log N-H(w).
\tag{M.6.13n.10}
$$
The physical spin charge equals $J_z/\hbar=(N+m+8)/2-Q_{\rm tot}$; on the system it is $1/2-Q_S$. The same nonzero scaling and additive constants on the two sides preserve every covariance, conservation and asymmetry statement. The target remains the actual system $\sigma_x$.

Let $V$ and $V_J$ denote the ideal and compiled ready-input isometries, including purification of $\sigma$ when bounding norms. Such a purification is a proof device, not an added operational reference. Copying the same pointer record is unitary, and the clock endpoint is exact, so (M.6.13n.7) also bounds their difference. For each unit system-plus-spectator vector, the Ozawa noise norm is
$$
\|M_DV\psi-VX\psi\|.
$$
Taking the supremum proves
$$
|\epsilon_\infty(V_J,M_D)-\epsilon_\infty(V,M_D)|
\le(\|M_D\|+\|X\|)\delta\le2\delta.
\tag{M.6.13n.11}
$$
This controls the full all-state Ozawa error, not just outcome probabilities.

Choose $0<\epsilon'<\epsilon<1$ and finite m such that $2\delta<\epsilon-\epsilon'$. The compiled error is then strictly below $\epsilon$. The error obtained by replacing only the displayed numerical pointer by $sM_D$, $0\le s\le1$, is continuous: it is the square root of the largest eigenvalue of a matrix polynomial in s. At $s=0$ it is exactly $\|X\|=1$; at $s=1$ it is below $\epsilon$. Hence some s in (0,1) realizes **exactly** $\epsilon$. This scalar calibration adds no asymmetry or factor. It can be specified as the least crossing in the compact interval; it need not have a closed elementary expression.

For each $\epsilon'$, the original finite N sequence tends to $\Phi(1-(\epsilon')^2)$. Let $\epsilon'\uparrow\epsilon$, choose N sufficiently large for each desired entropy tolerance, then finite $m$ satisfying (M.6.13n.7). Continuity of $\Phi$ gives an upper infimum $\Phi(1-\epsilon^2)$ within the explicitly constructed physical-spin class. Every such source remains in the original complete conserving/Yanase finite class, so Theorem M.6.13l supplies the matching lower bound and its strict finite inequality. Thus this physical subclass has precisely the same infimum and no finite attaining model. The same conclusion holds for error at most $\epsilon$.

**VI. Finite resources and ready boundary.**

For fixed $N,m,\kappa,\tau,T,t_g$ every entry below is finite. No uniform finite bound is claimed as the approximation improves.

| Entry | Exact count or registered quantity |
|---|---|
| System | One physical spin half, excluded from apparatus count |

| Direction $SU(2)$ resource | $\log(m+1)$ standalone $SU(2)$ asymmetry; zero $J_z$ asymmetry |
| Interaction description | Finite matrices (M.6.13n.5),(M.6.13n.9), permutation-basis Gram prescription; at most n! permutation labels per scalar matrix entry,  $n=N+m+8$; full supports retained |
| Timing and control | T, $t_g$, positive detector duration, exact endpoint convention, finite $\|\lambda\|_\infty,\|\dot\lambda\|_\infty$, command/calibration data and their scalar service costs |

| Coupler work | $\operatorname{Tr}\rho H_{\rm src}$ is constant. Signed switching work is zero; absolute switching work is $(2\pi\hbar/T)\operatorname{TV}(\lambda)$ on the ready input, with operator bound $(8\pi\hbar/(3T))\operatorname{TV}(\lambda)$ |
| State-supply service | Supply the declared mixed ladder, singlets, polarized spins and pure scalar ready states; name finite source storage, work/heat, time, calibration and any isolated preparation archive |

The absolute-work identity is $\int|\operatorname{Tr}\rho(t)\dot H(t)|dt$, not dissipated heat. Source/coupler work and resulting stored energy must not be double counted. The finite service energy/power/price inputs are constitutive entries, as declared in this theorem; no microscopic price is inferred from a matrix response. A scalar total cost, if desired, must declare its unit conversions and disjoint holdings/flows. The theorem optimizes only the original ready-state asymmetry, not this larger typed vector.

**Ready boundary.** The supplying factory is permanently isolated before the independent system input arrives and is not available during the run. Its preparation work, stores, orientation resources and waste/records remain separately owned lifecycle entries. The theorem does not assert free symmetric preparation of an asymmetric ladder. In particular, retaining the Fourier label j in the accessible apparatus changes its state to $\sum_jw_j|\theta_j\rangle\langle\theta_j|\otimes|j\rangle\langle j|$, whose asymmetry is $\log N$, not (M.6.13n.10). Such a flagged/purified apparatus is not substituted into this theorem. A microscopic factory that creates the mixed state and releases a product reference needs its own supplied finite service law; the original source convention permits that state-supply law as an input. If one instead defines cost over the factory plus measurement lifecycle, this theorem does not identify its optimum.

An explicit finite **state-transfer** supplier makes the mixed-state boundary operational without a retained Fourier label. Give a second carrier of $N-1$ spins $F_0$ the mixed state $E_N\sigma E_N^*$ and the destination reference the charge eigenstate $|0\rangle^{\otimes(N-1)}$. The whole-register physical swap $S$ is a product of physical spin permutations and commutes with $SU(2)$. For a registered $t_p>0$, $H_p=\pi\hbar(I-S)/(2t_p)\ge0$ has $e^{-it_pH_p/\hbar}=S$, norm action $\pi\hbar$, and produces the exact product of the destination mixed state and a blank supplier. This adds  $N-1$ supplier spins of full dimension $2^{N-1}$ to the lifecycle ledger, time $t_p$, and the displayed state-transfer action plus owned switch/storage service. Their initially supplied mixed state carries (M.6.13n.1); it is not generated for free. The final blank supplier is invariant, uncorrelated, and can either be isolated or explicitly retained with that dimension multiplier and no change in (M.6.13n.10). This construction does not manufacture the initial asymmetric resource from invariant matter; it gives a finite, label-free transfer from the stated resource input. Other pure ready supplies and all scalar services remain declared finite physical-theory inputs.

<a id="theorem-m613o-genuine-spin-systems-and-equality-of-physical-source-infima"></a>**Theorem M.6.13o (Genuine Spin Systems and Equality of Physical-Source Infima).** Fix an irreducible physical spin $j$, with system dimension $2j+1$, actual spin operators $\mathbf S$, registered charge $Q_S=jI-S_z/\hbar$, and a Hermitian target $A$. The system charge eigenvalues are $0,\ldots,2j$, the system carrier is unchanged, and every input state is tested. At each $0<\epsilon<\|A\|$, the infimum of complete ready-state relative-entropy asymmetry in the finite physical-spin source class constructed below equals its infimum in the complete conserving-unitary/Yanase-pointer class of Theorem M.6.13f, allowing arbitrary finite real reference charges, multiplicities, mixed states and all accessible neutral factors. The equality holds for exact error and for error at most $\epsilon$.

Every finite integer-charge apparatus is first encoded with its charge action, mixed ready state, first two pointer moments and asymmetry preserved. The rotation-scalar source then approximates that encoding with exact physical spin conservation at every finite size. A reference with arbitrary real charges is replaced by an integer-charge apparatus preserving its tested noise and not increasing its asymmetry; this replacement may pinch cross-coset coherence and changes the charge labels. The theorem equates optimization infima and does not evaluate their generally unknown value or decide finite attainment. Its spin-one specialization in Part VIII transfers Proposition M.6.13m's upper family with the complete physical apparatus counted.

*Proof and construction.*

**I. Complete apparatus and tested noise.**

An original device has finite reference $R$, Hermitian $Q$, arbitrary density matrix $\sigma$, $[U,Q_S+Q]=0$, and Hermitian $M$ with $[M,Q]=0$. Every charged or neutral subsystem, degeneracy, flag and correlation present during the run belongs to $R$. The system input is independent of $\sigma$ and every system state is tested. Put
$$
 B=U^*(I\otimes M)U,\quad [B,Q_S+Q]=0,
$$
$$
 K_\sigma(B)=A^2-\{A,\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma)B]\}
 +\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma)B^2],\qquad
 \epsilon_\infty^2=\lambda_{\max}K_\sigma(B).
\tag{M.6.13o.1}
$$
Resource is $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)=S(\mathcal G_Q\sigma)-S(\sigma)$ in nats. The spectral-pointer construction in Part III applies to this invariant observable for every finite target. Both pointer moments are retained.

**II. Integer-charge encoding with all degeneracies.**

First assume $Q$ has integer eigenvalues. Write $q_{\min}=\min\operatorname{spec}Q$, $L=\max\operatorname{spec}Q-q_{\min}$, $d=\max_q\dim R_q$, and $k_R=\lceil\log_2d\rceil$, with $k_R=0$ when $d=1$. No assumption of contiguous occupied levels or constant multiplicity is made.

Use $L$ distinguishable physical spin halves and $k_R$ four-spin singlet blocks. A singlet block has the two orthonormal scalar states
$$
|0_L\rangle=(|01\rangle-|10\rangle)_{12}(|01\rangle-|10\rangle)_{34}/2,
$$
$$
|1_L\rangle=\frac{|0011\rangle+|1100\rangle-(|0101\rangle+|0110\rangle+|1001\rangle+|1010\rangle)/2}{\sqrt3}.
$$
The full sixteen-dimensional block is retained. Its two code vectors have total spin zero. Products of $k_R$ blocks supply $2^{k_R}$ independent scalar labels $|\alpha_L\rangle$. For each original charge eigenbasis define the isometry
$$
 E|q,\alpha\rangle=|D^{L}_{q-q_{\min}}\rangle\otimes|\alpha_L\rangle,
 \qquad \alpha=1,\ldots,\dim R_q.
\tag{M.6.13o.2}
$$
The physical reference space has full dimension $2^{L+4k_R}$, not the number of code vectors. Its actual physical spin satisfies
$$
 (q_{\min}+L/2-J_z^R/\hbar)E=EQ.
\tag{M.6.13o.3}
$$
Consequently $E$ intertwines charge twirling and preserves both entropies and asymmetry exactly, including all original degeneracies and correlations. In particular $E\sigma E^*$ is the actual mixed ready state; it is not replaced by a flagged preparation ensemble or purification.

**Code and invariant envelope.** The image of $E$ need not be $SU(2)$-invariant. Missing charge levels and charge-dependent multiplicities generally prevent that. Its larger envelope
$$
 \operatorname{Sym}^{L}(\mathbb C^2)\otimes(\mathbb C^2_{\rm singlet})^{\otimes k_R}
$$
is invariant, however, and has maximal physical spin $L/2$. All unused charge levels, scalar labels and all physical complement sectors remain present.

Embed $B$ as $\widetilde B=(I\otimes E)B(I\otimes E^*)$, zero off the original reference code. It commutes with actual system-plus-reference $J_z$. Its compression on the ready reference yields $B$ and $B^2$ exactly, so (M.6.13o.1) is preserved for every system input, with or without a spectator. This exact intermediate equivalence precedes the finite rotationally invariant approximation below.

**III. Complete neutral pointer and bounded logarithm.**

List the distinct spectral values of $\widetilde B$, adding value zero if necessary, as $\nu_0=0,\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_{p-1}$; let $\Pi_a$ be their projectors. A zero projector is permitted when zero was added formally. Thus $p\le(2j+1)\dim R+1$. Put $k_P=\lceil\log_2p\rceil$. Use $k_P$ additional four-spin singlet blocks to encode the $p$ pointer labels; retain their full dimension $2^{4k_P}$, including unused scalar code labels and all nonsinglet states.

Let $V$ cyclically shift the first $p$ scalar code labels, and be identity on every other physical pointer state. Starting at label $0$, set
$$
 U_0=\sum_{a=0}^{p-1}\Pi_a\otimes V^a,\qquad
 M_P=\sum_{a=0}^{p-1}\nu_a P_a,
\tag{M.6.13o.4}
$$
where $P_a$ are the rank-one pointer code projectors and $M_P$ is zero on the rest. This unitary is identity outside the relevant reference/pointer envelope, satisfies $U_0^p=I$, conserves physical $J_z$, and reproduces precisely $\widetilde B,\widetilde B^2$ on the pointer ready state. All $p$ outcomes are retained.

For $\tau>0$ define the exact spectral logarithm by
$$
 F_l=\frac1p\sum_{a=0}^{p-1}e^{-2\pi i la/p}U_0^a,
 \quad \theta_l=\operatorname{Arg}(e^{2\pi i l/p})\in(-\pi,\pi],
 \quad K=-\frac\hbar\tau\sum_l\theta_l F_l.
\tag{M.6.13o.5}
$$
Then $e^{-i\tau K/\hbar}=U_0$, $K$ is Hermitian, $[K,J_z]=0$, and
$$
 \|K\|\le\kappa_p\hbar/\tau,\qquad
 \kappa_p=\begin{cases}\pi,&p\text{ even},\\\pi(1-1/p),&p\text{ odd}.\end{cases}
\tag{M.6.13o.6}
$$
For $p=1$ use $K=0$. The operator $K$ vanishes outside the invariant larger envelope of the actual spin-$j$ system, symmetric charge ladder, and singlet labels/pointer. On that envelope the maximal spin is $j_*=j+L/2$. The smaller original code need not be rotationally invariant.

**IV. Rotation-scalar source and uniform noise approximation.**

Add $m$ physical spin halves $F$, ready in $|0\rangle^{\otimes m}=|m/2,m/2\rangle$, keeping the complete $2^m$-dimensional carrier. Its $J_z$ asymmetry is exactly zero. Its separate $SU(2)$ asymmetry is $\log(m+1)$, and its size and polarization $m\hbar/2$ are counted resources.

Let $R_W(g)$ be the physical rotation representation on the system and encoded reference/pointer, and let $|F_g\rangle$ rotate the ready direction state. On the symmetric $F$ sector define
$$
 H_m=(m+1)\int_{SU(2)}R_W(g)KR_W(g)^*\otimes|F_g\rangle\langle F_g|\,dg,
\tag{M.6.13o.7}
$$
and extend by zero on nonsymmetric F. It is one fully specified finite Hermitian operator, invariant under all physical simultaneous rotations. It preserves the larger invariant envelope; it may leave the smaller original reference code. That leakage is retained and bounded, not projected away.

For completeness, the uniform bound follows from the unital CP map
$$
 \mathcal F(f)=(m+1)\int f(g)\otimes|F_g\rangle\langle F_g|dg.
$$
Apply Kadison to $f(g)=K_g-K$. The polar angle $\theta$ in an Euler decomposition obeys
$$
 \|K_g-K\|\le2j_*\|K\|\theta,\qquad
 \theta^2\le\pi^2\sin^2(\theta/2).
$$
Axial invariance of $K$ removes the other Euler angles from the norm. On the ready direction, $x=\sin^2(\theta/2)$ has normalized coherent density $(m+1)(1-x)^m\,dx$ and expectation $1/(m+2)$. Therefore
$$
 \|(H_m-K\otimes I)(\psi\otimes F_0)\|
 \le\frac{2\pi j_*\|K\|}{\sqrt{m+2}}.
$$
On the orthogonal complement of the invariant envelope, $K=K_g=0$. Duhamel\'s $\int$, whose comparison evolution keeps the direction state ready, gives the operator-norm ready-input bound
$$
 \delta_m=\|[e^{-i\tau H_m/\hbar}-U_0\otimes I](I\otimes|F_0\rangle)\|
 \le\frac{2\pi j_*\kappa_p}{\sqrt{m+2}}
 \le\frac{2\pi^2(j+L/2)}{\sqrt{m+2}}.
\tag{M.6.13o.8}
$$
It is uniform with arbitrary spectators. For the fixed mixed original ready state, purify only as a mathematical norm device. If $V_0,V_m$ are the two ready-input isometries, the noise vector is $M_PV\psi-VA\psi$. Hence
$$
 |\epsilon_\infty(V_m,M_P)-\epsilon_\infty(V_0,M_P)|
 \le(\|M_P\|+\|A\|)\delta_m.
\tag{M.6.13o.9}
$$
This controls the actual full worst-case Ozawa error and its second moment, not merely an output distribution.

**Finite physical spin polynomial.**

For a genuine spin-$j$ factor, every matrix unit is explicitly a finite polynomial in its actual $S_z,S_+,S_-$: first use
$$
 P_a=\prod_{b\ne a}\frac{S_z/\hbar-bI}{a-b},\qquad a,b\in\{-j,-j+1,\ldots,j\},
$$
then $P_a(S_+/\hbar)^{a-b}P_b$, divided by its nonzero ladder matrix element, gives $|a\rangle\langle b|$ for $a\ge b$; use adjoints otherwise. Tensor these bases over all physical factors, with scalar matrix units for the clock/record.

Expand (M.6.13o.7), or the final source below, in this finite physical polynomial basis. Since the desired operator is invariant, replace each polynomial term by its simultaneous rotational average. Rotations act linearly on spin-vector components, so each averaged finite-degree monomial is still a finite polynomial with invariant tensor coefficients $\int R_{a_1b_1}\cdots R_{a_kb_k}dg$. These coefficients are fixed finite numbers, computable by finite angular-momentum decomposition. Hermitian symmetrization gives an explicitly specified finite sum of Hermitian rotation-scalar physical-spin polynomials. Equivalently, the whole matrix average is evaluated by normalized magnetic partial traces within total-spin blocks, retaining every multiplicity matrix.

This constructs the actual finite coupling law. It uses neither physical continuous averaging nor a hidden orientation control. For all-spin-half factors the permutation/exchange Gram construction of Theorem M.6.13n is available; it is not falsely assumed to cover a fundamental spin-j factor without the displayed polynomial argument. Efficient, pairwise-only or laboratory synthesis is not claimed or required by the original formal-source rules.

**V. Clock, complete outcome record and resources.**

Add a $p$-level physical scalar record $D$ and a three-cell physical scalar clock $C$, both spin zero and independently ready in $0$. If $S_p$ is the record shift, copy the pointer with
$$
 C_P=\sum_{a=0}^{p-1}P_a\otimes S_p^a+
 (I-\sum_aP_a)\otimes I_D.
$$
Let $W_0=C_P(e^{-i\tau H_m/\hbar}\otimes I_D)$, $W_1=I$, $W_2=W_0^*$, and
$$
 D_c=\sum_{a=0}^2|a+1\bmod3\rangle\langle a|\otimes W_a,
 \quad H_{\rm src}=3\sqrt3\gamma I+\gamma i(D_c-D_c^*),
 \quad \gamma=\frac{2\pi\hbar}{3\sqrt3T},\quad T>0.
\tag{M.6.13o.10}
$$
All cyclic products of $W_a$ are identity. Thus $D_c^3=I$, its chiral generator has eigenvalues $0,\pm\sqrt3$, the positive source spectrum is $\{2\sqrt3\gamma,3\sqrt3\gamma,4\sqrt3\gamma\}$, and $e^{-iTH_{\rm src}/\hbar}=D_c$. Every statement holds on the complete physical carrier.

Use the explicit continuously differentiable nonnegative envelope
$$
 \lambda(t)=\frac{30T}{t_g}x^2(1-x)^2,\quad x=t/t_g\in[0,1],
$$
zero outside the pulse, with $H(t)=b_0I+\lambda(t)H_{\rm src}$, $b_0\ge0$. Its $\int$ is $T$, its peak is $15T/(8t_g)$, its derivative maximum is $10\sqrt3T/(3t_g^2)$, and total variation is $15T/(4t_g)$. The endpoint is $D_c$ up to a global phase. The interaction is then off during a positive-duration spin-zero terminal detector service, whose $p$ projectors read the record and whose calibrated pointer is $\operatorname{diag}(\nu_a)$, subsequently scaled when needed. Every output state is retained. The unmodulated source would recur at $3T$.

The finite Schrödinger action for $H(t)$, with the actual physical spin representation above, is SU(2)-invariant. Its actual additive Noether spin, including the direction carrier, is conserved throughout. On the encoded ready reference define
$$
 Q_R^{\rm phys}=q_{\min}+(L+m)/2-J_z^{\rm apparatus}/\hbar.
\tag{M.6.13o.11}
$$
Together with the unchanged $Q_S$ this is a common affine conversion of physical total $J_z$. On (M.6.13o.2) times the new ready factors it intertwines the original $Q$ exactly. Outside that ready code it is defined on every physical sector. The pointer and all scalar record/clock operators commute with it.

The complete core apparatus has
$$
 \boxed{D_{\rm app}=3p\,2^{L+4k_R+4k_P+m}.}
\tag{M.6.13o.12}
$$
There are $L+4k_R+4k_P+m$ physical spin halves, in addition to the unchanged physical spin-$j$ system, plus $3p$ scalar controller/record states. Any optional finite service factor or retained supplier multiplies this count explicitly.

The implementation vector includes the complete mixed encoded input $\sigma$ and its charge span/multiplicities; every scalar label and unused physical sector; the $m$-spin polarization and its separate $SU(2)$ resource; all finite polynomial coefficients/supports and command installation; $T,t_g$, positive detector duration and timing/calibration service; scalar switch/source stores; and all ready-state supply, detector, record/archive, output holding and optional reset services. All service durations, finite energy/storage/work/power bounds and tariffs are physical-theory inputs declared in this theorem. A scalar price must specify units and disjoint inventories/flows.

Exact source accounting is
$$
 \int\|\lambda H_{\rm src}\|dt=8\pi\hbar/3,
\quad \langle H_{\rm src}\rangle_{C=0}=2\pi\hbar/T,
\quad \langle H_{\rm src}-E_{\min}\rangle_{C=0}=2\pi\hbar/(3T).
$$
The actual pulse energies multiply these active terms by $\lambda$, adding $b_0$ to total energy. The $H_{\rm src}$ expectation is constant during the pulse. Signed switching work is zero; the ready-input absolute work transfer is $(2\pi\hbar/T)\operatorname{TV}(\lambda)$, bounded for any input by $(8\pi\hbar/(3T))\operatorname{TV}(\lambda)$. Baseline action $b_0t_g$, detector/switch dissipation and source holdings remain separate. Absolute transferred work is not heat and is not counted again as independent stored energy.

All post-ready services have trivial spin representation and are initially independent of $\sigma$. The new pointer is singlet ready and the direction carrier is a $J_z$ eigenstate. Therefore the complete ready asymmetry is exactly
$$
 \mathcal A_{Q_R^{\rm phys}}(\sigma_{\rm complete})=\mathcal A_Q(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13o.13}
$$
Core ready entropy is $S(\sigma)$; add $S(\omega_{\rm services})$ for independent mixed scalar services. It cancels from (M.6.13o.13). The preparation resources, work and isolated archives have separate lifecycle owners. An accessible purification or ensemble label is part of the reference. A finite label-free transfer can swap the supplied mixed physical resource with a blank identical carrier: $H_p=\pi\hbar(I-\operatorname{SWAP})/(2t_p)$ is positive, implements the swap exactly at $t_p$ and has norm action $\pi\hbar$. The final blank supplier is independent and $J_z$-invariant; isolate it or retain its full dimension. The initial mixed resource is an explicit input.

**VI. Strict error slack at arbitrarily small extra asymmetry.**

This step does not assume continuity of an unknown frontier.

First there are finite integer-reference devices at arbitrarily small positive error for every fixed $A$. On the reference basis $n=0,\ldots,N-1$ take the uniform pure state $\eta_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_n|n\rangle$ and truncated shifts $T_N^k|n\rangle=|n+k\rangle$ when in range, zero otherwise. In a system charge eigenbasis, put
$$
 B_N=\sum_{a,b}A_{ab}|a\rangle\langle b|\otimes T_N^{q_b-q_a}.
\tag{M.6.13o.14}
$$
It is Hermitian and invariant. For $N>\max_{a,b}|q_a-q_b|$,
$$
 \|(T_N^k-I)\eta_N\|=\sqrt{|k|/N},\qquad
 \|(B_N-A\otimes I)(\psi\otimes\eta_N)\|
 \le\frac{C_A}{\sqrt N},
$$
$$
 C_A=\sum_{a,b}|A_{ab}|\sqrt{|q_a-q_b|}.
\tag{M.6.13o.15}
$$
The bound uses $|\psi_b|\le1$ and the triangle inequality; it is uniform over unit $\psi$ and spectators. The finite spectral-pointer dilation realizes this noise exactly, with asymmetry $\log N$. Thus choose a finite witness with squared error $r_h<r$ for any prescribed $r>0$. If $C_A=0$, $B_N=A\otimes I$ already has zero noise.

Now let an arbitrary finite device have $K_0\le rI$ and cost $a_0$. Retain an orthogonal branch flag and form the direct-sum reference
$$
 Q_t=Q_0\oplus Q_h,\quad
 \sigma_t=(1-t)\sigma_0\oplus t\sigma_h,\quad
 B_t=B_0\oplus B_h,\qquad 0<t<1.
$$
All dimensions and flags are retained; both charges are integer. Direct calculation gives
$$
 K_t=(1-t)K_0+tK_h\le[(1-t)r+tr_h]I<rI,
$$
$$
 \mathcal A_{Q_t}(\sigma_t)=(1-t)a_0+t a_h\longrightarrow a_0.
\tag{M.6.13o.16}
$$
The common classical flag entropy cancels in the asymmetry difference. This proves strict feasibility with arbitrarily little additional asymmetry from every finite feasible model.

Compile this strict-slack finite model by Parts II–V and choose finite $m$ so that (M.6.13o.9) is smaller than the RMS slack. Its actual error is below $\epsilon=\sqrt r$. Replacing only the numerical pointer by $sM_D$, $0\le s\le1$, gives a continuous worst-case error: its squared value is the largest eigenvalue of a finite matrix polynomial in $s$. At $s=0$ it is $\|A\|$, and at $s=1$ it is below $\epsilon$. For $0<\epsilon<\|A\|$, the intermediate value theorem supplies exact error $\epsilon$ without changing the ready state or asymmetry. The argument allows arbitrary finite pointer norm and mixed or correlated reference states.

For every feasible cost $a_0$, (M.6.13o.16) and sufficiently large finite $m$ therefore produce exact-error physical sources whose costs approach $a_0$. Taking the infimum proves equality of integer-apparatus and physical-source infima. The reverse inequality holds because each complete physical source is itself an original finite conserving/Yanase device. Exact and at-most physical infima coincide by the same construction; no attainment conclusion follows.

**VII. Real-to-integer optimization replacement.**

Keep the genuine spin-$j$ system, whose gaps are integers. Partition the finite spectrum of an arbitrary real $Q$ into cosets modulo $\mathbb Z$, and let $P_c$ be the corresponding reference projectors. Charge conservation forces $B$ to preserve each $I_S\otimes P_c$: an entry can be nonzero only when $q-q'$ is a system gap, hence an integer. The same holds for $B^2$. Consequently
$$
 \widetilde\sigma=\sum_cP_c\sigma P_c
$$
leaves both conditional moments in (M.6.13o.1), and therefore the entire tested noise matrix, unchanged. The pinching channel commutes with Q dephasing. Relative-entropy data processing gives
$$
 \mathcal A_Q(\widetilde\sigma)\le\mathcal A_Q(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13o.17}
$$
The full retained reference state may change; no arbitrary whole-apparatus state/observable equivalence is asserted.

Within coset $c$ write $q=\theta_c+n$ with integer $n$. Replace $q$ by $n+t_c$, where the finitely many integer translations $t_c$ place the occupied intervals disjointly; they can also be separated by more than $2j$. Keep every reference basis vector, degeneracy and coset branch. This defines a new integer $Q'$. The same $B$ remains invariant: each previously nonzero charge difference lies within one coset and is unchanged. The original $U,M$ can also be retained because their entries preserve the cosets. Dephasing $\widetilde\sigma$ under $Q'$ gives exactly its old within-coset dephasing, so
$$
 K_{\widetilde\sigma,Q'}(B)=K_{\sigma,Q}(B),\qquad
 \mathcal A_{Q'}(\widetilde\sigma)=\mathcal A_Q(\widetilde\sigma)\le\mathcal A_Q(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13o.18}
$$
The original full finite dimension is unchanged. Integer devices already belong to the real-charge class; (M.6.13o.18) proves equality of their resource infima at every tested error. Combining with Part VI proves the claimed equality with the formal physical-spin source infimum.

This is a newly selected integer-charge apparatus in the same optimization problem. It is not an isometric identification of the old arbitrary-real charge, nor preservation of discarded cross-coset coherence. The actual physical identification is subsequently established by (M.6.13o.2)–(M.6.13o.3) for the new integer model.

**VIII. Transfer of the finite spin-one upper family.**

Use Proposition M.6.13m. The system and charged reference can each be a genuine physical spin one, each of dimension three, with $Q=I-S_z/\hbar$. The reference is the actual mixed state
$$
 \sigma_u=\begin{pmatrix}
 3/16&\sqrt{11u/72}&1/16\\
 \sqrt{11u/72}&5/8&\sqrt{11u/72}\\
 1/16&\sqrt{11u/72}&3/16
 \end{pmatrix},\qquad 0\le u\le45/88.
$$
Its four invariant edges have amplitudes $a=4\sqrt{11u}/11$, $b=2\sqrt{11u}/11$, and its full noise eigenvalues are $(1-u,1-u,21u/22)$. The five pointer outputs are $0,\pm a,\pm\sqrt2b$. Their complete mathematical apparatus dimension is $3\cdot5=15$.

Encode the five neutral pointer labels in three four-spin singlet blocks, retaining all $2^{12}$ states and all three unused scalar code labels. Use $m$ directional spin halves, a five-level scalar record and a three-cell scalar clock. The charged reference remains the actual three-dimensional spin-one carrier, so the complete core apparatus dimension is
$$
 \boxed{45\,2^{m+12}.}
\tag{M.6.13o.19}
$$
All nonsinglet pointer states and all nonsymmetric direction states remain. The actual signal envelope has maximal spin $2$; the five-cycle logarithm has norm $4\pi\hbar/(5\tau)$. Thus
$$
 \delta_m\le\frac{16\pi^2}{5\sqrt{m+2}}.
\tag{M.6.13o.20}
$$
The record norm is $a<1$ throughout the positive family range, so the RMS error perturbation is at most $2\delta_m$. The physical-polynomial construction applies directly to the two fundamental spin-one factors and adds no extra system sector.

For a prescribed $0<u<45/88$, choose $u'>u$ in the family. Its ideal error $\sqrt{1-u'}$ is strictly smaller than $\sqrt{1-u}$. Choose finite $m$ by (M.6.13o.20) and calibrate the pointer to the exact latter error. The complete ready asymmetry is $A_{15}(u')$, and continuity of the explicit entropy expression gives
$$
 \inf\{\mathcal A_{\rm physical}:\epsilon_\infty^2=1-u\}\le A_{15}(u).
\tag{M.6.13o.21}
$$
The costs approach this bound as $u'\downarrow u$. Equality at a finite physical source is not asserted. At $u=45/88$, use the retained-flag strict-slack construction (M.6.13o.16), which increases the physical dimensions beyond (M.6.13o.19), then let its cost overhead tend to zero. At $u=0$ the zero pointer directly gives exact error one; the positive $A_{15}(0)$ of this seed is not an entropy optimum.

The bound in (M.6.13o.21) is a physical-source upper infimum bound from this explicit family. It does not evaluate the entropy infimum over all finite references.

<a id="theorem-m613q-global-spin-one-entropy-bracket-and-logarithmic-divergence"></a>**Theorem M.6.13q (Global Spin-One Entropy Bracket and Logarithmic Divergence).** Fix the spin-one charge and target of Proposition M.6.13m. Retain the complete finite apparatus and resource assumptions of Theorem M.6.13l, with the spin-one system carrier unchanged and every spin-one input state tested. For a finite reference $(Q,\sigma)$, let $\eta=\eta_Q(\sigma)$ be (M.6.13h.3). Let $e_{1,Q}(\sigma)$ be the infimum of worst-case Ozawa RMS errors over invariant Hermitian observables on the system and this reference, allowing their pure neutral spectral-pointer realizations. Then
$$
\frac23(1-\eta)\le e_{1,Q}(\sigma)^2\le1-\eta.
\tag{M.6.13q.1}
$$
The upper value is realized by an explicit invariant observable at every finite reference. In particular, finite zero-error spin-one measurement is impossible.

Write $\mathfrak A_1(\epsilon)$ for the infimum of complete ready-state relative-entropy asymmetry at exact worst-case error $\epsilon$. Its value is unchanged when error at most $\epsilon$ is used. With $\Phi$ from Theorem M.6.13l,
$$
\Phi\!\left(1-\frac32\epsilon^2\right)
\le\mathfrak A_1(\epsilon)\le\Phi(1-\epsilon^2),
\qquad 0<\epsilon<\sqrt{2/3}.
\tag{M.6.13q.2}
$$
The upper bound holds throughout $0<\epsilon<1$. Every admitted finite model of error at most $\epsilon<\sqrt{2/3}$ satisfies the strict pointwise lower inequality
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)>\Phi\!\left(1-\frac32\epsilon^2\right).
\tag{M.6.13q.3}
$$
Consequently,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\log(4\pi/3)-1}{2}
&\le\liminf_{\epsilon\downarrow0}
\bigl[\mathfrak A_1(\epsilon)-\log(1/\epsilon)\bigr]\\
&\le\limsup_{\epsilon\downarrow0}
\bigl[\mathfrak A_1(\epsilon)-\log(1/\epsilon)\bigr]
\le\frac{\log(2\pi)-1}{2},\\
\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}
\frac{\mathfrak A_1(\epsilon)}{\log(1/\epsilon)}&=1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13q.4}
$$
These bounds and the sharp leading logarithmic coefficient also hold for the genuine-spin physical-source infimum of Theorem M.6.13o.

*Proof.* An admitted model gives the invariant Hermitian Heisenberg pointer $B=U^*(I\otimes M)U$. Conversely, the neutral spectral-pointer construction in Theorem M.6.13h realizes every invariant Hermitian $B$ with its first two moments preserved and no added asymmetry. Its conditional noise matrix is
$$
K_\sigma(B)=\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma)(B-X\otimes I)^2]\succeq0.
$$
Let $P=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)$. It commutes with $Q_S$ and obeys $PXP=-X$. Replacing $B$ by $[B-(P\otimes I)B(P\otimes I)]/2$ cannot increase the largest eigenvalue of $K_\sigma(B)$: its noise operator is the average of $B-X\otimes I$ and its negative $P$ conjugate, and the square is operator convex. The replacement remains invariant and has the form
$$
B=\begin{pmatrix}0&L_0&0\\L_0^*&0&L_1\\0&L_1^*&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad [Q,L_0]=L_0,\quad [Q,L_1]=L_1.
\tag{M.6.13q.5}
$$
Set
$$
a=\sqrt2\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(L_0+L_1),\qquad
T=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(L_0L_0^*+L_0^*L_0+L_1L_1^*+L_1^*L_1),\qquad
C=(L_0+L_1)/\sqrt2.
$$
Direct expansion, using $\operatorname{Tr}_S X^2=2$, gives
$$
\operatorname{Tr}_S K_\sigma(B)=2-2a+T.
$$
The operator identity
$$
\frac{L_0L_0^*+L_0^*L_0+L_1L_1^*+L_1^*L_1}{2}-K_C
=\frac{(L_0-L_1)(L_0-L_1)^*+(L_0-L_1)^*(L_0-L_1)}4\succeq0
$$
and the variational definition of $\eta$ imply
$$
\eta\ge\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(C+C^*-K_C)
\ge a-T/2
=1-\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_S K_\sigma(B).
\tag{M.6.13q.6}
$$
If the original model has squared error at most $r$, the oddified noise obeys $0\preceq K_\sigma(B)\preceq rI_3$. Hence $\operatorname{Tr}_S K_\sigma(B)\le3r$ and $\eta\ge1-3r/2$. This proves the lower bound in (M.6.13q.1) for every original finite apparatus, including arbitrary charge multiplicities and accessible neutral correlations.

For the upper bound, let $V$ be the supported maximizing raising contraction in Theorem M.6.13h, so $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(V+V^*-K_V)=\eta$. Choose
$$
B_V=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}0&V&0\\V^*&0&V\\0&V^*&0\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13q.7}
$$
Its conditional noise is parity block diagonal. Its middle diagonal entry and the trace of its outer two-dimensional block are both exactly
$$
k=1-2\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}\sigma V+\operatorname{Tr}\sigma K_V=1-\eta.
\tag{M.6.13q.8}
$$
For clarity, the outer off-diagonal entry is
$$
\frac12+\frac12\operatorname{Tr}\sigma V^2-\operatorname{Tr}\sigma V.
$$
The outer block is positive semidefinite because it is a principal block of a conditional square. Its largest eigenvalue is therefore at most its trace $k$. The middle input has error squared $k$, so the complete worst-case error is exactly $k$, including all second-moment and two-charge-coherence terms. The neutral spectral pointer realizes $B_V$ with this error and unchanged asymmetry. This proves the upper bound in (M.6.13q.1).

Every finite reference has $\eta<1$ by (M.6.13l.7). Thus (M.6.13q.1) excludes finite zero error. If $0<\epsilon<\sqrt{2/3}$, (M.6.13q.6) gives $\eta\ge1-3\epsilon^2/2>0$. The strict reference inequality (M.6.13l.8), followed by strict increase of $\Phi$, proves (M.6.13q.3). Taking infima gives the lower bound in (M.6.13q.2); strictness for each finite model is not converted into a strict inequality between infima.

For the matching upper construction, put $u=1-\epsilon^2$ and choose the finite Fourier reference of (M.6.13l.9)–(M.6.13l.10), with $N>1/\epsilon^2$ and $\kappa_N$ chosen there. Its maximizing raising contraction is
$$
V_N=c_N(\kappa_N)\sum_{n=0}^{N-2}|n+1\rangle\langle n|,
\qquad
\eta_{Q_N}(\sigma_{N,\kappa_N})=u.
$$
Equations (M.6.13q.7)–(M.6.13q.8) give exact spin-one error $\epsilon$ at every finite $N$. The reference asymmetry tends to $\Phi(u)$ by (M.6.13l.11). Appending the finite neutral spectral pointer adds zero asymmetry. This proves the upper infimum bound throughout the stated interior interval.

Exact-error and at-most-error infima coincide. For any model with actual error $\epsilon'<\epsilon<1$, replace its numerical terminal pointer by $sM$, $0\le s\le1$. The largest eigenvalue of its conditional noise matrix is continuous in $s$, equals $1=\|X\|^2$ at $s=0$, and equals $(\epsilon')^2$ at $s=1$. The intermediate value theorem gives exact squared error $\epsilon^2$, with the ready state, charge conservation and pointer commutation unchanged.

The expansion proved in Theorem M.6.13j gives
$$
\Phi(1-\delta^2)=\log(1/\delta)+\frac{\log(2\pi)-1}{2}+O(\delta^2)
\quad(\delta\downarrow0).
$$
Use $\delta=\sqrt{3/2}\,\epsilon$ in the lower bound and $\delta=\epsilon$ in the upper bound. Subtracting $\log(1/\epsilon)$ and taking the lower and upper limits proves (M.6.13q.4). Theorem M.6.13o identifies the complete finite-apparatus and stated physical-source infima at each interior error, transferring all displayed bounds without adding an attainment assertion. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613r-parity-entropy-bound-and-the-convex-spin-one-quality-frontier"></a>**Theorem M.6.13r (Parity Entropy Bound and the Convex Spin-One Quality Frontier).** Use the complete spin-one measurement class and resource of Theorem M.6.13q. Define, with natural logarithms,
$$
f(u)=\log2-h_2\!\left(\frac{1+\sqrt u}{2}\right),\qquad
h_2(p)=-p\log p-(1-p)\log(1-p),\qquad 0\le u\le1.
\tag{M.6.13r.1}
$$
Every admitted finite model with worst-case error at most $\epsilon<1$ satisfies
$$
\boxed{\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge f(1-\epsilon^2)\ge\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{2}.}
\tag{M.6.13r.2}
$$
The first bound is the exact entropy frontier of the parity-conserving relaxation, with a finite attaining apparatus for every $0\le u\le1$. The original additive-charge frontier retains the additional constraints of Theorem M.6.13q.

Let $F_1(u)=\mathfrak A_1(\sqrt{1-u})$ for $0<u<1$ and set $F_1(0)=0$. Then $F_1$ is finite, nondecreasing and convex on $[0,1)$. Its endpoint slope exists and obeys
$$
c_1:=\lim_{u\downarrow0}\frac{F_1(u)}u
=\inf_{0<u<1}\frac{F_1(u)}u,
\qquad \frac12\le c_1\le4A_{15}(1/4)<1.
\tag{M.6.13r.3}
$$
Thus the global spin-one entropy cost is of linear order in $1-\epsilon^2$ as $\epsilon\uparrow1$. Retained flags, arbitrary finite charge multiplicities, and singular or varying reference spectra are included in (M.6.13r.2)–(M.6.13r.3). These statements also hold for the physical-source infimum identified in Theorem M.6.13o. Theorem M.6.13cd identifies this same unrestricted slope as $c_1=c_{\mathrm{proj}}=c_{\mathrm{loc}}=0.83487144924356266269\ldots$. Its complete-reference lower bound is additional to the parity argument below.

*Proof.* First construct the parity action without an integer-spectrum assumption. Partition the finite reference charge spectrum by $q\sim q'$ if $q-q'\in\mathbb Z$. Choose a representative $q_\alpha$ in each class, write its charges as $q_\alpha+k$ with $k\in\mathbb Z$, and define the self-adjoint unitary
$$
\Pi_R\big|_{\mathcal H_{q_\alpha+k}}=(-1)^k I,
\qquad P_S=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1).
\tag{M.6.13r.4}
$$
A matrix entry preserving the additive charge has $s+q=t+q'$, so the two reference charges lie in the same class and $s+k=t+k'$. It therefore preserves $P_S\otimes\Pi_R$. The original unitary commutes with this total parity, and the terminal pointer commutes with $\Pi_R$ because it commutes with the reference charge. Consequently its Heisenberg pointer $B$ commutes with total parity.

Put $\tau=(\sigma+\Pi_R\sigma\Pi_R)/2$ and $\tau_Q=\mathcal G_Q(\sigma)$. Charge dephasing fixes $\tau_Q$, removes the same off-charge entries from $\tau$ as from $\sigma$, and obeys $\mathcal G_Q(\tau)=\tau_Q$. The entropy identities for the two pinching channels give
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)
=[S(\tau)-S(\sigma)]+[S(\tau_Q)-S(\tau)]
=D(\sigma\Vert\tau)+\mathcal A_Q(\tau)
\ge D(\sigma\Vert\tau).
\tag{M.6.13r.5}
$$
This argument uses the displayed spectral parity action, not an assertion that it is a single time in the original one-parameter charge group.

Let $W:\mathbb C^2\to\mathbb C^3$ send $|0\rangle$ to $e=(|0\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and $|1\rangle$ to $m=|1\rangle$. Its range reduces $X$, and $W^*XW=\sigma_x$, $P_SW=W\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$. Define $\widetilde B=(W^*\otimes I)B(W\otimes I)$. It is invariant under the compressed system parity times $\Pi_R$. If $C=B-X\otimes I$, compression of a Hermitian square gives
$$
\bigl[(W^*\otimes I)C(W\otimes I)\bigr]^2
\preceq(W^*\otimes I)C^2(W\otimes I).
$$
Hence the compressed qubit noise is at most $\epsilon^2I_2$. Oddifying under its system parity, as in Theorem M.6.13h, gives a Hermitian invariant observable
$$
\widetilde B_{\rm odd}=\begin{pmatrix}0&L\\L^*&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\Pi_RL\Pi_R=-L,
$$
without increasing the error. The average of its two noise entries yields
$$
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma\left(L+L^*-\frac{LL^*+L^*L}{2}\right)\ge u,
\qquad u=1-\epsilon^2.
$$
Write $L=H+iJ$ with $H,J$ Hermitian. Then $H$ is parity odd and $(LL^*+L^*L)/2=H^2+J^2$. Thus
$$
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(2H-H^2)\ge u.
\tag{M.6.13r.6}
$$

The support $P$ of $\tau$ is parity invariant and contains the support of $\sigma$, since $\tau\succeq\sigma/2$. Replace $H$ by $PHP$ and restrict all subsequent matrices to $P$. Compression decreases its quadratic term and preserves its linear expectation, so (M.6.13r.6) remains valid. On this space $\tau$ is positive definite. Put $D=\log\tau$ and
$$
Z_\lambda=\operatorname{Tr}e^{D+\lambda(2H-H^2)},\qquad
S_2(\lambda)=\max_{r\ge0}e^{-\lambda r^2}\cosh(2\lambda r),\qquad \lambda\ge0.
$$
The trace-exponential concavity used in Theorem M.6.13i gives an immediate parity trace bound. For the positive definite matrix $A=e^{\lambda(2H-H^2)}$, the two values of $\operatorname{Tr}e^{D+\log A}$ at $A$ and $\Pi_RA\Pi_R$ are equal, because $D$ is parity invariant. Concavity bounds their common value by its value at their average. Since $H$ is parity odd,
$$
\frac{A+\Pi_RA\Pi_R}{2}
=e^{-\lambda H^2}\cosh(2\lambda H)\preceq S_2(\lambda)I.
$$
Its logarithm is therefore at most $(\log S_2(\lambda))I$ by scalar spectral calculus. Trace-exponential monotonicity, proved by differentiating along a positive Hermitian increment as in Theorem M.6.13k, yields
$$
Z_\lambda\le S_2(\lambda)\operatorname{Tr}e^D=S_2(\lambda).
$$
The relative-entropy identity with $\omega_\lambda=Z_\lambda^{-1}e^{D+\lambda(2H-H^2)}$ now gives
$$
D(\sigma\Vert\tau)
=D(\sigma\Vert\omega_\lambda)
+\lambda\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(2H-H^2)-\log Z_\lambda
\ge\lambda u-\log S_2(\lambda).
\tag{M.6.13r.7}
$$

Here is the complete scalar evaluation. For $\lambda>0$, the logarithmic derivative of the objective defining $S_2$ is $2\lambda[\tanh(2\lambda r)-r]$, which is negative for $r\ge1$. The function $\tanh x/x$ strictly decreases from one to zero for $x>0$: its derivative has the sign of $x-\sinh x\cosh x<0$, and the last inequality follows by differentiating $\sinh x\cosh x-x$. Therefore $S_2(\lambda)=1$ for $0\le\lambda\le1/2$, while for $\lambda>1/2$ its unique positive maximizer solves $r=\tanh(2\lambda r)$. For $0<u<1$, put $r=\sqrt u$, $\kappa=\operatorname{atanh}r$ and $\lambda_u=\kappa/(2r)>1/2$. This $r$ is the global maximizer at $\lambda_u$. Consequently
$$
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\{\lambda u-\log S_2(\lambda)\}
&=r\operatorname{atanh}r+\tfrac12\log(1-r^2)\\
&=\log2-h_2((1+r)/2)=f(u).
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13r.8}
$$
For completeness, no larger value is hidden in the supremum: evaluating $S_2(\lambda)$ at $r=\sqrt u$ gives $\lambda u-\log S_2(\lambda)\le2\lambda u-\log\cosh(2\lambda r)$, whose global maximum occurs at $2\lambda r=\operatorname{atanh}r$. The endpoint extensions are $f(0)=0$ and $f(1)=\log2$. Finally $f'(u)=\operatorname{atanh}(\sqrt u)/(2\sqrt u)\ge1/2$, so $f(u)\ge u/2$. Combining (M.6.13r.5), (M.6.13r.7) and (M.6.13r.8) proves the original-model lower bound.

To verify sharpness for the stated relaxation, take a two-dimensional reference with $\Pi_R=\sigma_z$, $\sigma=(I+\sqrt u\,\sigma_x)/2$ and $H=\sqrt u\,\sigma_x$. The invariant observable $B=X\otimes H$ commutes with $P_S\otimes\Pi_R$. Its noise is $(1-u)X^2$, yielding worst-case squared error $1-u$, and its parity asymmetry is exactly $f(u)$. A pure neutral spectral pointer realizes it with unchanged first two moments and resource. This works at both endpoints as well. It is a parity-conserving realization; it is not substituted for an additive-charge-conserving source.

For the endpoint assertion, use the at-most-error formulation established in Theorem M.6.13q. Given two finite models, retain an orthogonal neutral flag, take the direct sum of their charged reference spaces and conditional interactions, and put their ready states in the two sectors with probabilities $p,1-p$. Their complete reference asymmetry is exactly the weighted average, because the flag entropy cancels between the ready and charge-dephased states. Their noise matrix is the weighted average of the two original noise matrices. Models of qualities $u_1,u_2$ therefore give quality at least $pu_1+(1-p)u_2$. Taking costs arbitrarily close to each infimum proves convexity. The zero pointer supplies $F_1(0)=0$, nested error constraints give monotonicity, and Theorem M.6.13q gives finiteness and $F_1(u)\le\Phi(u)$. Convexity at zero implies $F_1(u)/u\le F_1(v)/v$ for $0<u<v<1$, proving the existence and infimum identity in (M.6.13r.3). The lower bound $f(u)/u\to1/2$ proves the lower endpoint estimate. Convexity and Proposition M.6.13m give $c_1\le F_1(1/4)/(1/4)\le4A_{15}(1/4)$.

The strict upper comparison has an elementary exact certificate. At $u=1/4$, the reference eigenvalues in Proposition M.6.13m are $1/8,(21-\sqrt{257})/48,(21+\sqrt{257})/48$. Write $g(x)=-x\log x$. Since $16<\sqrt{257}<161/10$, monotonicity of $g$ on the relevant intervals gives
$$
S(\sigma_{1/4})>g(1/8)+g(49/480)+g(371/480) >\frac38\frac{69}{100}+\frac{49}{480}\frac{109}{50}
+\frac{371}{480}\frac{218}{851}
=\frac{13873801}{20424000}.
$$
Here $69/100<\log2<347/500$, $\log3>109/100$ and $\log x>2(x-1)/(x+1)$ for $x>1$. These bounds follow directly from the positive series $\log x=2\sum_{k\ge0}z^{2k+1}/(2k+1)$, $z=(x-1)/(x+1)$: retain three terms for $x=2,3$, and bound the remaining $x=2$ tail by $2z^7/[7(1-z^2)]$; retain the first term for the last inequality. On the other hand, $h_2''(p)=-1/[p(1-p)]\le-4$ gives
$$
S(\mathcal G_Q\sigma_{1/4})
=h_2(5/8)+\tfrac38\log2
\le\tfrac{11}{8}\log2-\tfrac1{32}<\frac{923}{1000}.
$$
Consequently $A_{15}(1/4)<4977551/20424000<1/4$, proving the strict upper endpoint bound from the already admitted finite witness. Equality of infima in Theorem M.6.13o transfers the conclusions to the complete physical-spin source class. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613w-quantitative-charge-span-exhaustion"></a>**Theorem M.6.13w (Quantitative Charge-Span Exhaustion).** Retain the spin-one system and complete finite apparatus class of Theorem M.6.13q. For every admitted model with asymmetry $\mathcal A$ and worst-case RMS error $0\le\epsilon\le1$, and every integer $L\ge2$, there is an admitted model whose complete reference charge spectrum lies in $\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$, with
$$
\mathcal A_L\le\mathcal A,\qquad
e_L^2\le\epsilon^2+\frac{3+2\epsilon-\epsilon^2}{2L}
\le\epsilon^2+\frac2L.
\tag{M.6.13w.1}
$$
Let $d$ be the maximum charge multiplicity after applying the integer-reindexing construction of Theorem M.6.13o to the starting model. The new pre-dilation reference carrier can have dimension $N\le6Ld$, with at most six retained cut/interval branches. A pure neutral spectral pointer with $p_{\rm ptr}\le3N$ outcomes gives the complete apparatus bounds
$$
D_{\rm app}\le3N^2\le108L^2d^2,\qquad
\max_q\dim R_q^{\rm complete}\le108Ld^2.
\tag{M.6.13w.2}
$$

Write $F_{\mathrm{quality}}(u)=F_1(u)$ for the quality-parametrized asymmetry infimum of Theorem M.6.13r, and let $F_{L,\mathrm{quality}}(u)$ be its at-most-error version restricted to complete reference charge spectrum in $\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$, with arbitrary finite multiplicity. If $F_{\mathrm{error}}(r)$ denotes $F(r)$ of (M.6.13dc.1) for this same spin-one system, then
$$
F_{\mathrm{quality}}(u)=F_{\mathrm{error}}(1-u).
$$
Here $u$ is quality and $r$ is squared RMS error; they are not the same coordinate. For $0<u<1$ and $u+2/L<1$,
$$
\boxed{F_{\mathrm{quality}}(u)\le F_{L,\mathrm{quality}}(u)\le F_{\mathrm{quality}}(u+2/L).}
\tag{M.6.13w.3}
$$
In particular, with $u_+=(1+u)/2$ and $L\ge4/(1-u)$,
$$
0\le F_{L,\mathrm{quality}}(u)-F_{\mathrm{quality}}(u)\le\frac{4\Phi(u_+)}{L(1-u)},
\qquad \lim_{L\to\infty}F_{L,\mathrm{quality}}(u)=F_{\mathrm{quality}}(u),
\tag{M.6.13w.4}
$$
where $\Phi$ is the exact qubit entropy function of Theorem M.6.13l.

*Proof.* The real-to-integer optimization replacement in Theorem M.6.13o preserves the complete noise and cannot increase asymmetry. Apply it first, then use Theorem M.6.13q to parity oddify the invariant observable without increasing the error. Thus $B$ has the two raising blocks of (M.6.13q.5). Put
$$
\tau=\mathcal G_Q\sigma,\qquad
\mathcal E_\omega(Z)=\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\omega)Z],\qquad
H=\mathcal E_\sigma(B^2),\qquad K=K_\sigma(B).
$$
The all-input bound is $0\preceq K\preceq\epsilon^2I$. For a purification $s$ of $\sigma$ used as a vector in the proof and every system unit vector $\psi$,
$$
\|B(\psi\otimes s)\|
\le\|(B-X\otimes I)(\psi\otimes s)\|+
\|(X\otimes I)(\psi\otimes s)\|\le\epsilon+1.
$$
Consequently
$$
0\preceq H\preceq(1+\epsilon)^2I.
\tag{M.6.13w.5}
$$
System parity makes $H$ a Hermitian outer two-by-two block on $\operatorname{span}\{|0\rangle,|2\rangle\}$ and an independent middle entry.

For each $t=0,\ldots,L-1$, partition the integer reference charges into intervals
$$
I_{t,j}=\{t+jL,\ldots,t+(j+1)L-1\},\qquad j\in\mathbb Z,
$$
and let $P_{t,j}$ be their reference projectors. Empty sectors are omitted. Define
$$
\Lambda_t(Z)=\sum_jP_{t,j}ZP_{t,j},\qquad
\sigma_t=\Lambda_t(\sigma),\qquad
B_t=(\operatorname{id}_S\otimes\Lambda_t)(B),\qquad
D_t=B-B_t.
$$
The pinching is charge covariant and fixes $\tau$, so relative-entropy data processing gives $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_t)\le\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)$. Since $B_t-X\otimes I$ preserves the intervals, its conditional squared noise in $\sigma_t$ equals that in $\sigma$.

Each reference grade-one edge crosses exactly one of the $L$ partitions. The cut edges within one partition are separated by $L\ge2$, so two consecutive raised edges cannot both occur in $D_t$. The grade-two entries of $D_t^2$ vanish, and each grade-zero edge product occurs once in the sum over cuts. These facts give the exact operator identities
$$
\frac1L\sum_tD_t=\frac BL,\qquad
\frac1L\sum_tD_t^2=
\frac1L(\operatorname{id}_S\otimes\mathcal G_Q)(B^2).
\tag{M.6.13w.6}
$$
They include matrix-valued edges between degenerate charge sectors. Expanding the noise square and using total-charge covariance, $\mathcal E_\tau(B^2)=\mathcal G_{Q_S}(H)$, yields
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac1L\sum_tK_{\sigma_t}(B_t)
&=K-\frac1L\mathcal E_\sigma\{B-X\otimes I,B\}
 +\frac1L\mathcal E_\tau(B^2)\\
&=\left(1-\frac1L\right)K+
\frac1L\left[X^2+\mathcal G_{Q_S}(H)-H\right].
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13w.7}
$$

If $0\preceq H\preceq MI$ has this parity block structure, the only nonzero entries of $\mathcal G_{Q_S}(H)-H$ are its outer off-diagonal pair. The two outer-block eigenvalues lie in $[0,M]$ and differ by at least $2|H_{02}|$. Hence $|H_{02}|\le M/2$ and
$$
\|\mathcal G_{Q_S}(H)-H\|\le(1+\epsilon)^2/2.
$$
Together with $X^2\preceq I$, (M.6.13w.7) bounds the largest eigenvalue of the averaged noise by
$$
\left(1-\frac1L\right)\epsilon^2+
\frac{1+(1+\epsilon)^2/2}{L}
=\epsilon^2+\frac{3+2\epsilon-\epsilon^2}{2L}.
$$
The last numerator is at most four for $0\le\epsilon\le1$.

Retain a uniform neutral flag $t$ and take the direct sum of the devices $(\sigma_t,B_t)$. Its complete noise is the average in (M.6.13w.7), and its asymmetry is the mean of the branch asymmetries because the common flag entropy cancels. Within each interval branch replace its charge $q$ by $q-t-jL$. The state and observable already preserve that branch; reindexing preserves its charge differences, charge pinching and full noise. The resulting spectrum lies in $\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$. Both the cut label and interval label remain as neutral branch labels.

Expand this finite construction into its nonzero normalized interval branches, with noises $K_i$ and asymmetries $a_i$. Each $K_i$ commutes with system parity and therefore has five real coordinates: four for its Hermitian outer block and one for its middle entry. If more than six branch weights are positive, the vectors $(1,K_i)\in\mathbb R^6$ are linearly dependent. Perturb the weights along that dependence, choosing the direction in which the linear mean cost does not increase, until one weight becomes zero. Normalization and the complete noise remain unchanged. Iteration leaves at most six branches. Each uses at most $L$ charge values of original multiplicity at most $d$, so their direct-sum carrier has dimension $N\le6Ld$ and charge multiplicity at most $6d$.

The spectral decomposition of its invariant observable on the $3N$-dimensional system-reference carrier has at most $p_{\rm ptr}\le3N$ distinct eigenvalues. Append a pure neutral pointer of that size and use the conserving spectral-pointer unitary of Theorem M.6.13h. This realizes both moments exactly, with unchanged asymmetry and charge span. The complete apparatus dimension is $Np_{\rm ptr}\le3N^2$, and its maximum charge multiplicity is at most $6d\,p_{\rm ptr}\le108Ld^2$. This proves (M.6.13w.1)–(M.6.13w.2), including all retained labels and pointer outcomes.

The left inequality of (M.6.13w.3) is class inclusion. Apply (M.6.13w.1) to finite devices of quality $u+2/L$ and costs approaching $F_{\mathrm{quality}}(u+2/L)$; their new quality is at least $u$. This proves the right inequality. The convexity of $F_{\mathrm{quality}}$ from Theorem M.6.13r, with $\delta=2/L\le u_+-u$, gives
$$
F_{\mathrm{quality}}(u+\delta)-F_{\mathrm{quality}}(u)
\le\frac\delta{u_+-u}[F_{\mathrm{quality}}(u_+)-F_{\mathrm{quality}}(u)]
\le\frac{4\Phi(u_+)}{L(1-u)},
$$
using $F_{\mathrm{quality}}\ge0$ and the qubit upper bound $F_{\mathrm{quality}}(u_+)\le\Phi(u_+)$. Equation (M.6.13w.4) follows. $\square$

Theorem M.6.13w exhausts the positive-error infimum by bounded charge spans, with arbitrary finite neutral multiplicity retained. Theorem M.6.13o transfers the spin-one infimum to its genuine-spin source class, while Theorem M.6.13df supplies the separate complete binary energy-labelled realization of every finite model; (M.6.13w.2) counts the abstract measurement representation before either physical compilation.

<a id="corollary-m613br-exact-entropy-frontier-for-every-two-sector-system-charge"></a>**Corollary M.6.13br (Exact Entropy Frontier for Every Two-Sector System Charge).** Let $Q_S,A$ be Hermitian matrices on any finite-dimensional system, with $Q_S$ having at most two distinct eigenvalues, of arbitrary degeneracy. Optimize over the same complete finite reference and apparatus class as Theorem M.6.13l, with every system input tested. Let $\mathfrak A_{Q_S,A}(\epsilon)$ be the infimum of natural-$\log$ reference asymmetry at exact worst-case Ozawa error $\epsilon$, and put $r=d_{Q_S}(A)$. If $r>0$, then
$$
\mathfrak A_{Q_S,A}(\epsilon)=\Phi(1-\epsilon^2/r^2),
\qquad 0<\epsilon<r.
\tag{M.6.13br.1}
$$
The value is also the infimum for error at most $\epsilon$. Every finite model has strictly larger cost, while finite conserving models of exactly the requested error approach it. No finite exact zero-error model exists when $r>0$. For $\epsilon\ge r$ the exact-error infimum is zero and is attained. If $[Q_S,A]=0$, it is zero and attained for every $\epsilon\ge0$; this includes scalar $Q_S$. In particular the result includes every Hermitian qubit charge and target. No restriction on system degeneracy, diagonal target blocks, reference state, or admitted ancillary correlations is added.

*Proof.* If $Q_S$ is nonscalar, write $Q_S=q_0P_0+q_1P_1$, where $q_0\ne q_1$ and $P_0+P_1=I$. Define
$$
\Delta=q_1-q_0,\qquad
D_A=P_0AP_0+P_1AP_1,\qquad
C=P_0AP_1=\sum_{j=1}^J r_j|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|,
\qquad r=\|C\|=\max_j r_j=d_{Q_S}(A),
\tag{M.6.13br.2}
$$
where the last sum is a singular-value decomposition over positive singular values, with the maximum of the empty list defined as zero, and with orthonormal $u_j\in P_0\mathcal H_S$, $v_j\in P_1\mathcal H_S$. To prove the distance assertion, set $Z=P_0-P_1$. Every Hermitian $T$ commuting with $Q_S$ is block diagonal, and $C+C^*=[(A-T)-Z(A-T)Z]/2$, so $\|C+C^*\|\le\|A-T\|$. Squaring the two-block off-diagonal matrix gives $\|C+C^*\|=\|C\|$. The choice $T=D_A$ attains equality. The commuting case $r=0$ will be treated at the end.

For $r>0$, choose a maximum singular pair $u,v$ with $Cv=ru$ and $C^*u=rv$, and let $P=|u\rangle\langle u|+|v\rangle\langle v|$. This is a charge-invariant two-dimensional projection; it need not reduce $A$. For any original admitted model, let $B$ be its invariant self-adjoint Heisenberg pointer on system and complete reference $R$, with state $\sigma$. Write $E=B-A\otimes I_R$ and $\widehat P=P\otimes I_R$. Compress to the pair: $B_P=\widehat P B\widehat P$ and $A_P=PAP$, regarded on their compressed spaces. Then
$$
E_P=B_P-A_P\otimes I_R=\widehat P E\widehat P,
\qquad
E_P^2\le\widehat P E^2\widehat P,
\qquad
K_P\le PKP,
\qquad\epsilon_\infty(B_P,A_P)\le\epsilon_\infty(B,A).
\tag{M.6.13br.3}
$$
Here $K=\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma)E^2]$ and $K_P$ is the compressed model's conditional noise square. The difference in the first inequality is $\widehat P E(I-\widehat P)E\widehat P\ge0$; positivity of conditional expectation gives the next. Thus no reduction assumption on $A$ is needed. Since $P$ commutes with $Q_S$, $B_P$ is invariant for the compressed additive charge. Its spectral-projector neutral-pointer dilation is finite and admitted, and appending the pure neutral pointer does not change reference asymmetry.

In the ordered pair basis $u,v$, the compressed charge is $q_0I+\Delta|1\rangle\langle1|$ and $A_P=D_P+rX_S$ with $D_P$ diagonal. Put $Z_P=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, suppressing reference tensor identities in the following odd-part formula. The invariant observable $B'=D_P+(B_P-Z_PB_PZ_P)/2$ satisfies
$$
B'-A_P=\frac{E_P-Z_PE_PZ_P}{2},\qquad
(B'-A_P)^2\le\frac{E_P^2+Z_PE_P^2Z_P}{2},
\qquad B_0=\frac{B'-D_P}{r},\qquad Q_{R,0}=Q_R/\Delta.
\tag{M.6.13br.4}
$$
Operator convexity of the square and positive conditional expectation show that the all-input error of $B'$ is no greater than that of $B_P$. The normalized $B_0$ is invariant for $|1\rangle\langle1|+Q_{R,0}$ and has target $X_S$ and error exactly $\epsilon_\infty(B',A_P)/r$. Nonzero real charge scaling preserves charge eigenspaces, twirl and reference asymmetry, including all degeneracies, mixedness, support and neutral correlations. Neutral-pointer dilation implements $B_0$ within the registered class. Every original finite model of error at most $\epsilon<r$ therefore gives a registered finite model of error at most $\epsilon/r$ with the same asymmetry. The strict lower bound of Theorem M.6.13l proves a cost strictly greater than (M.6.13br.1). The forward operations are error-nonincreasing reductions, not a bijection of apparatus descriptions.

For the matching upper bound, put $\delta=\epsilon/r\in(0,1)$. Take the exact-error finite Fourier sequence in (M.6.13l.9)--(M.6.13l.11) at error $\delta$, with reference $(Q_N,\sigma_N)$ and raising $L_N$. Its two conditional noise eigenvalues are both $\delta^2$. Use this same reference for all singular pairs, set $Q_R=\Delta Q_N$, and define the single invariant system-reference observable
$$
B_N=D_A\otimes I+
\sum_{j=1}^Jr_j\bigl(
|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|\otimes L_N+
|v_j\rangle\langle u_j|\otimes L_N^*\bigr).
\tag{M.6.13br.5}
$$
