It conserves $Q_S+Q_R$, since the two system increments are $-\Delta$ and $\Delta$. Although $D_A$ may mix different singular pairs within either sector, it cancels identically from $E_N=B_N-A\otimes I$. Orthogonality of the two singular families then gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
E_N^2={}&\sum_{j=1}^Jr_j^2\bigl[
|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|\otimes(L_N-I)(L_N^*-I)
+|v_j\rangle\langle v_j|\otimes(L_N^*-I)(L_N-I)\bigr],\\
\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma_N)E_N^2]
={}&\delta^2\sum_{j=1}^Jr_j^2
\bigl(|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|+|v_j\rangle\langle v_j|\bigr),
\qquad\epsilon_\infty(B_N,A)=r\delta=\epsilon.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13br.6}
$$
The noise is zero on any unpaired system subspace. The whole observable $B_N$, including $D_A$, has the finite invariant spectral-projector neutral-pointer dilation of Theorem M.6.13h. The single shared reference incurs exactly $\mathcal A_{Q_N}(\sigma_N)$, with no factor for the number of pairs. Scaling its charge and adding a pure neutral pointer leave that cost unchanged. Its cost tends to $\Phi(1-\delta^2)$ while every model has the requested exact error. This proves the matching upper infimum for both error conventions and, together with the strict lower bound, finite nonattainment.

An original finite zero-error model with $r>0$ would reduce through (M.6.13br.3)--(M.6.13br.4) to a registered finite zero-error model, contradicting Theorem M.6.13l. For $\epsilon\ge r$, take the system-only invariant observable
$$
B=D_A+(\epsilon-r)I,
\qquad B-A=(\epsilon-r)I-(C+C^*),
\qquad\|B-A\|=\epsilon.
\tag{M.6.13br.7}
$$
Indeed $C+C^*$ has spectrum $\{\pm r_j\}$ and possible zero eigenvalues, with extreme values $\pm r$. This observable has a finite pure neutral-pointer realization with zero asymmetry. When $[Q_S,A]=0$, instead take the invariant $B=A+\epsilon I$, with constant noise $\epsilon I$. This includes the scalar-charge case without an artificial choice of charge sectors. Relative-entropy nonnegativity proves optimality of these zero-cost models. $\square$
<a id="proposition-m613bs-certified-spin-one-positive-error-upper-witness"></a>**Proposition M.6.13bs (Certified Spin-One Positive-Error Upper Witness).**

For the original unrestricted complete-finite charge-conserving Yanase-apparatus problem with

$$
Q_S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2),\qquad A=J_x=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\1&0&1\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix},
\tag{M.6.13bs.1}
$$

there is a **complete dimension-15 apparatus**, including a charged three-dimensional reference and a neutral five-dimensional pointer, with exact worst-case squared error $3/4$ and ready-state asymmetry $C$ satisfying the certified rational enclosure

$$
\boxed{0.22397763665574495807<C<0.22397763665574495808.}
\tag{M.6.13bs.2}
$$

Let $F_1(u)$ denote the infimum of complete ready-state reference asymmetry for this registered spin-one problem at squared worst-case error $1-u$. Then $F_1(1/4)\le C$. The currently printed family of Proposition M.6.13m has $A_{15}(1/4)>0.2266$, whereas $C<0.224$. The new witness is a strict improvement of that upper bound; it does not determine the global minimum or the minimum within dimension fifteen.

*Proof.* **I. Exact ready state.**

The five defining parameters are

$$
a=\frac{42964054}{10^8},\quad b=\frac{21053777}{10^8},\quad h=\frac{4392547}{10^8},
\tag{M.6.13bs.3}
$$
$$
p=\frac{4b^2-2a^2-2b^2h}{10b^2-8a^2},\qquad
 t=\frac{1/4+4a^2p+4b^2(1-2p)}{4(a+b)}.
\tag{M.6.13bs.4}
$$

All five are exact rationals. On $R=\mathbb C^3$ set

$$
Q_R=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2),\qquad
\sigma=\begin{pmatrix}p&t&h\\t&1-2p&t\\h&t&p\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13bs.5}
$$

This has trace one. Positivity follows from the exact rational inequalities

$$
0<h<p<1/2,\qquad (p+h)(1-2p)>2t^2.
\tag{M.6.13bs.6}
$$

Indeed, its eigenvalue on the antisymmetric outer vector is $p-h>0$; its remaining block is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p+h&\sqrt2t\\\sqrt2t&1-2p\end{smallmatrix}\right)>0$. The nonzero $h$ is reference charge-gap-two coherence and is retained throughout.

**II. The complete noise operator.**

Use the basis $|i,j\rangle$ for system charge $i$ and reference charge $j$, and define

$$
W=\sqrt2a\bigl(|0,1\rangle\langle1,0|+|1,2\rangle\langle2,1|+\mathrm{h.c.}\bigr)
 +\sqrt2b\bigl(|0,2\rangle\langle1,1|+|1,1\rangle\langle2,0|+\mathrm{h.c.}\bigr).
\tag{M.6.13bs.7}
$$

Every displayed transition preserves $i+j$, so $[W,Q_S\otimes I+I\otimes Q_R]=0$. Direct multiplication, followed by the reference conditional expectation, gives

$$
K=\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma)(W-A\otimes I)^2]
=\begin{pmatrix}d&0&c\\0&m&0\\c&0&d\end{pmatrix},
\tag{M.6.13bs.8}
$$

where

$$
d=\frac12+2a^2(1-2p)+2b^2p-2(a+b)t,
\quad c=\frac12+2b^2h-2(a+b)t,
\tag{M.6.13bs.9}
$$
$$
m=1+4a^2p+4b^2(1-2p)-4(a+b)t.
\tag{M.6.13bs.10}
$$

Thus all three system eigenvalues, without restricting the tested input, are

$$
E_e=d+c=1+2a^2(1-2p)+2b^2(p+h)-4(a+b)t,
\tag{M.6.13bs.11}
$$
$$
E_m=m,\qquad E_f=d-c=2a^2(1-2p)+2b^2(p-h).
\tag{M.6.13bs.12}
$$

The defining formula for $p$ makes $E_e=E_m$. The defining formula for $t$ makes $E_m=3/4$. Finally exact rational arithmetic gives

$$
E_f=\frac{312897203685235398969362161856484729957}
 {1291833028657754750000000000000000000000}
\in(0.24221180039834020774,0.24221180039834020775).
\tag{M.6.13bs.13}
$$

It follows that $K\preceq(3/4)I$ with largest eigenvalue exactly $3/4$. An untouched spectator only tensors this operator with its identity.

**III. Complete conserving instrument.**

The five distinct eigenvalues of $W$ are

$$
\nu_0=0,\quad \nu_1=\sqrt2a,\quad \nu_2=-\sqrt2a,\quad \nu_3=2b,\quad \nu_4=-2b.
\tag{M.6.13bs.14}
$$

They follow from the two two-dimensional total-charge blocks, the central three-dimensional path, and the two scalar zero blocks. Let $P_j$ be their orthogonal spectral projections. These can, if desired, be specified without an eigenvector convention by

$$
P_j=\prod_{k\ne j}\frac{W-\nu_k I}{\nu_j-\nu_k}.
\tag{M.6.13bs.15}
$$

Append a neutral five-dimensional pointer $P$ in $|0\rangle\langle0|$. For $j=1,2,3,4$, let $V_j$ be the permutation matrix that swaps pointer vectors $|0\rangle,|j\rangle$ and fixes all others; take $V_0=I$. Define the complete apparatus on $R\otimes P$ by

$$
Q_{\mathrm{app}}=Q_R\otimes I_P,\quad
\sigma_{\mathrm{app}}=\sigma\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|,
\tag{M.6.13bs.16}
$$
$$
U=\sum_{j=0}^4P_j\otimes V_j,\qquad
M=I_R\otimes\sum_{j=0}^4\nu_j|j\rangle\langle j|.
\tag{M.6.13bs.17}
$$

This $U$ is unitary because the $P_j$ are orthogonal and each $V_j$ is unitary. Each $P_j$ commutes with system-plus-reference charge and every pointer operator is neutral, hence $U$ conserves total charge. The pointer obeys $[M,Q_{\mathrm{app}}]=0$.

The ready-pointer compression of $B=U^*(I_S\otimes M)U$ is $W$, and that of $B^2$ is $W^2$. Expanding $(B-A\otimes I)^2$ therefore gives exactly the previously calculated $K$, including both cross terms. This is a complete-apparatus error calculation, not a state-quality proxy or an unimplemented invariant-observable relaxation.

The complete apparatus dimension is $3\cdot5=15$. Its ready asymmetry equals that of $\sigma$: the pure neutral pointer contributes zero entropy and no charge coherence. No neutral flag, clock, purification, hidden controller, or extra state is used. This is a mathematical conserving realization, not a physical hardware or lifecycle-cost claim.

**IV. Entropy certificate.**

Put

$$
\Delta=(3p+h-1)^2+8t^2,\quad
\eta_0=p-h,\quad \eta_\pm=\frac{1-p+h\pm\sqrt\Delta}{2}.
\tag{M.6.13bs.18}
$$

The exact resource is the elementary algebraic-logarithmic constant

$$
C=-2p\log p-(1-2p)\log(1-2p)
 +\eta_0\log\eta_0+\eta_+\log\eta_++\eta_-\log\eta_-.
\tag{M.6.13bs.19}
$$

All inequalities above can be verified by finite rational arithmetic. For the entropy certificate let $D_0=10^{60}$ and put $z=\lfloor D_0\sqrt\Delta\rfloor$; equivalently $z$ is the integer square root of $\lfloor D_0^2\Delta\rfloor$. Squaring verifies
$$
(z/D_0)^2\le\Delta<((z+1)/D_0)^2.
\tag{M.6.13bs.20}
$$
These endpoints enclose $\eta_\pm$ by their displayed formulas. For each positive rational logarithm argument write $x=2^k y$ with integer $k$ and $1\le y<2$. Use $\log x=k\log2+\log y$ and the exact bounds

$$
2\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{w^{2j+1}}{2j+1}
\le\log y\le
2\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{w^{2j+1}}{2j+1}
+\frac{2w^{2N+1}}{(2N+1)(1-w^2)},\qquad
w=\frac{y-1}{y+1},\quad N=100.
\tag{M.6.13bs.21}
$$

Apply these bounds with rational interval arithmetic, using both endpoints for the positive algebraic eigenvalues and all four products when multiplying intervals. They give the displayed strict enclosure for $C$. The same procedure applied to (M.6.13m.1) at $u=1/4$ gives $A_{15}(1/4)>0.2266$. Thus the numerical assertions use only integer square bracketing and the finite positive series with its explicit tail, rather than a floating-point decision. $\square$

By Theorem M.6.13o, $C$ is also an upper bound on the exact-error infimum in its genuine-spin-one physical source class. That transfer can enlarge the apparatus and approach this resource value; it does not identify a physical source of dimension fifteen or an attaining global frontier.
<a id="theorem-m613bt-common-dual-charge-window-reduction"></a>**Theorem M.6.13bt (Common-Dual Charge-Window Reduction).** Use the spin-one target $X$ and charge $Q_S$ of Proposition M.6.13m. Put
$$
e=(|0\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2,\qquad m=|1\rangle,\qquad
\rho_\lambda=(1-\lambda)|e\rangle\langle e|+\lambda|m\rangle\langle m|,
\qquad 0\le\lambda\le1.
\tag{M.6.13bt.1}
$$
For a complete finite reference $(Q,\sigma)$, define its projected weighted gain by
$$
q_\lambda(\sigma)=\sup_{\substack{B=B^*\\[B,Q_S+Q]=0}}
\left\{1-\operatorname{Tr}\bigl[(\rho_\lambda\otimes\sigma)(B-X\otimes I)^2\bigr]\right\}.
\tag{M.6.13bt.2}
$$
Every system input is tested in the underlying apparatus class, and every charged or neutral reference factor, degeneracy, correlation and retained flag is counted. The quantity in (M.6.13bt.2) is a necessary weighted relaxation of that all-input problem: $0\le q_\lambda\le1$, and every actual measurement of quality $u=1-\epsilon_\infty^2$ has $u\le q_\lambda(\sigma)$ for every $\lambda$. It is not an identification of weighted gain with actual operational quality.

For every integer $L\ge3$, there is one finite reference $\sigma_L$, with charges in $\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$ and arbitrary finite charge-sector multiplicities, such that simultaneously for all $0\le\lambda\le1$,
$$
\mathcal A(\sigma_L)\le\mathcal A(\sigma),\qquad
q_\lambda(\sigma_L)\ge(1-2/L)q_\lambda(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13bt.3}
$$
All window labels remain neutral flags in this same reference. Consequently its common-parameter projected gain obeys
$$
\min_\lambda q_\lambda(\sigma_L)\ge(1-2/L)\min_\lambda q_\lambda(\sigma).
$$
For $t\ge0$, let
$$
B_\infty(\lambda,t)=\sup_\sigma\{tq_\lambda(\sigma)-\mathcal A(\sigma)\},
\qquad
B_L(\lambda,t)=\sup_{\substack{\sigma:\,\operatorname{spec}Q\subset\{0,\ldots,L-1\}}}
\{tq_\lambda(\sigma)-\mathcal A(\sigma)\},
\tag{M.6.13bt.4}
$$
where both suprema retain all finite sector multiplicities and neutral factors. Then
$$
0\le B_\infty(\lambda,t)-B_L(\lambda,t)\le\frac{2t}{L}.
\tag{M.6.13bt.5}
$$
This bounds charge range, not complete apparatus dimension or sector multiplicity.

*Proof.* **I. Complete local weighted dual.** Since $\{\rho_\lambda,X\}=X$ and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho_\lambda X^2=1$, expanding the square proves that (M.6.13bt.2) is a linear-minus-quadratic variational problem. The zero observable gives gain zero, and positivity of the square gives its upper bound one. For an actual observable $B$, its weighted noise does not exceed its all-input maximum, proving $u\le q_\lambda$.

Pinch arbitrary real reference charges into cosets modulo $\mathbb Z$. Charge conservation makes every invariant $B$ and $B^2$ preserve these cosets, so the pinching preserves all weighted noise expectations and $q_\lambda$. It commutes with charge dephasing and decreases relative-entropy asymmetry. Translate each coset to an integer chain and retain its label as a neutral flag. Thus write the finite integer reference as $\bigoplus_j\mathcal H_j$, permitting holes and arbitrary multiplicities.

For completeness the local dual is explicit. Let $\mathcal O_j=\mathcal H_{j-1}\oplus\mathcal H_{j+1}$, and let $E_j:\mathcal O_j\to\mathcal H$ and $F_j:\mathcal H_j\to\mathcal H$ be their canonical embeddings. For arbitrary complex maps $T_j:\mathcal H_j\to\mathcal O_j$, put $\alpha=(1-\lambda)/2$ and
$$
\begin{aligned}
K_\lambda(T)=\sum_j\bigl[&\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(E_jT_jF_j^*+F_jT_j^*E_j^*)\\
&-\alpha E_jT_jT_j^*E_j^*-\lambda F_jT_j^*T_jF_j^*\bigr].
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bt.6}
$$
Then
$$
q_\lambda(\sigma)=\sup_T\operatorname{Tr}\sigma K_\lambda(T)
=\sum_j q_{\lambda,j}(\sigma[\{j-1,j,j+1\}]).
\tag{M.6.13bt.7}
$$
Here, with $O_j=E_j^*\sigma E_j$, $B_j=F_j^*\sigma F_j$ and $H_j=E_j^*\sigma F_j$,
$$
q_{\lambda,j}=\sup_{T_j}\left\{\sqrt2\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}H_j^*T_j
-\operatorname{Tr}T_j^*(\alpha O_jT_j+\lambda T_jB_j)\right\}.
\tag{M.6.13bt.8}
$$
To verify these formulas, use system parity $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)$. It commutes with $Q_S,\rho_\lambda$ and reverses $X$. Operator convexity of the square shows that replacing $B$ by $(B-ZBZ)/2$ cannot increase its weighted noise. Each total-charge block of this odd observable couples its middle reference sector only to its two outer sectors. These are precisely the independent rectangular maps $T_j$. Direct block multiplication gives (M.6.13bt.6)–(M.6.13bt.8); their independent finite blocks give the sum. Each local supremum is nonnegative, homogeneous of degree one in its positive source, and depends only on that principal triple. The full complex block $\sigma_{j-1,j+1}$ remains in $O_j$ and in its outer quadratic penalty. No scalarization or gap-two deletion is made. The variational definition and the bound $q_\lambda\le1$ also cover singular weights and both endpoints of the closed parameter interval.

**II. One state for every common parameter.** For each $s\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$, partition the integer chain into intervals
$$
I_{s,k}=\{s+kL,\ldots,s+kL+L-1\},\qquad k\in\mathbb Z,
$$
and let $P_s$ be pinching onto them. Only finitely many intervals meet the reference support. The pinching commutes with charge dephasing and fixes $\mathcal G_Q\sigma$, so
$$
\mathcal A(P_s\sigma)=D(P_s\sigma\Vert\mathcal G_Q\sigma)\le\mathcal A(\sigma).
$$
An intact triple $\{j-1,j,j+1\}$ has exactly the same local dual after pinching. All other local terms remain nonnegative. Exactly $L-2$ of the $L$ shifts keep that triple intact. Therefore
$$
\frac1L\sum_s q_\lambda(P_s\sigma)
\ge\frac1L\sum_s\sum_{j:\,\text{triple intact}}q_{\lambda,j}(\sigma)
=(1-2/L)q_\lambda(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13bt.9}
$$
Form the normalized direct sum
$$
\sigma_L=\frac1L\bigoplus_{s,k}\sigma[I_{s,k}],
$$
translating the charges of each interval to $0,\ldots,L-1$. Retain $(s,k)$ and any original coset label as neutral flags. Asymmetry and the fixed-parameter gain are homogeneous and additive over these retained orthogonal blocks: their common flag entropy cancels in asymmetry, and the independent local variational problems give the gain sum. Thus
$$
\mathcal A(\sigma_L)=\frac1L\sum_s\mathcal A(P_s\sigma)\le\mathcal A(\sigma),
\qquad
q_\lambda(\sigma_L)=\frac1L\sum_s q_\lambda(P_s\sigma),
$$
which proves (M.6.13bt.3). The same state works pointwise for all $\lambda$, so taking one common minimum is legitimate; separate branchwise minimizing parameters are not substituted.

For each original state, $0\le q_\lambda\le1$ and the construction give
$$
tq_\lambda(\sigma)-\mathcal A(\sigma)
\le tq_\lambda(\sigma_L)-\mathcal A(\sigma_L)+\frac{2t}{L}q_\lambda(\sigma)
\le B_L(\lambda,t)+\frac{2t}{L}.
$$
Taking the supremum proves the upper estimate in (M.6.13bt.5); its lower estimate is inclusion of feasible states. $\square$

For every actual measurement of quality $u$ the bound yields
$$
\mathcal A(\sigma)\ge tu-B_\infty(\lambda,t)
\ge tu-B_L(\lambda,t)-2t/L.
\tag{M.6.13bt.10}
$$
A numerical maximization over a selected multiplicity gives a lower bound on $B_L$, whereas this lower-bound certificate needs an upper bound uniform over multiplicity. Alternatively, if a convex nondecreasing $f$ satisfies $\mathcal A(\rho)\ge f(q_\lambda(\rho))$ for every length-$L$ reference with arbitrary multiplicity, apply it to the actual normalized $\sigma_L$ to get
$$
\mathcal A(\sigma)\ge f((1-2/L)q_\lambda(\sigma))\ge f((1-2/L)u).
$$
Neither consequence evaluates the unrestricted frontier.

For $0<\lambda<1$, the conjugates also have the complete finite Gibbs form
$$
B_\infty(\lambda,t)=\sup_{Q,\tau,T}
\log\operatorname{Tr}\exp(\log\tau+tK_\lambda(T)),
\tag{M.6.13bt.11}
$$
where $\tau$ ranges over invariant faithful normalized reference states, and the length-$L$ version has the restricted charge range but still all finite multiplicities. Indeed
$$
D(\sigma\Vert\tau)=\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)+D(\mathcal G_Q\sigma\Vert\tau),
$$
so the infimum over invariant faithful $\tau$ is $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)$, using supported approximation if necessary. Substitute (M.6.13bt.7), and use the finite Gibbs identity obtained from positivity of relative entropy against $e^{\log\tau+tK}/\operatorname{Tr}e^{\log\tau+tK}$. All optimizations being interchanged are suprema. Equation (M.6.13bt.5) bounds these $\log$ partition functions additively; the corresponding partition functions differ by a factor at most $e^{2t/L}$.
<a id="theorem-m613bu-all-input-charge-range-approximation"></a>**Theorem M.6.13bu (All-Input Charge-Range Approximation).** Use the same spin-one system and complete finite conserving measurement class. Given any apparatus with squared all-input Ozawa error $r\le1$ and ready asymmetry $a$, every $0<\delta<1$ and integer $L\ge3$ admit another complete finite apparatus, with reference charges in $\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$, asymmetry at most $a$, and squared all-input error at most
$$
\frac r{1-\delta}+\frac{6(1+\sqrt{3/\delta})^2}{L}.
\tag{M.6.13bu.1}
$$
Charge-sector multiplicities may be arbitrarily large but remain finite; every neutral flag and the complete spectral pointer are counted. In particular, for every $0<\varepsilon\le1$, at most $\lceil180/\varepsilon^2\rceil$ consecutive charge values suffice for error at most $r+\varepsilon$. This bounds charge range, not complete apparatus dimension.

*Proof.* **I. Supported regularization and a bounded observable.** Replace the original model by its invariant Hermitian Heisenberg pointer $N$. Conversely, the finite spectral-pointer dilation of Theorem M.6.13h's proof realizes any such observable with both moments and a pure neutral pointer. Pinch arbitrary real reference charges into integer cosets. All reference entries contributing to
$$
K_\sigma(N)=\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma)(N-X\otimes I)^2]
$$
have gaps in $\{0,\pm1,\pm2\}$. Coset pinching preserves the whole noise matrix and cannot increase asymmetry. Retain the finite coset labels and translate each chain to integers.

For this fixed finite state minimize over invariant Hermitian $N$ the convex function
$$
J_\delta(N)=(1-\delta)\lambda_{\max}K_\sigma(N)
+\frac\delta3\operatorname{Tr}K_\sigma(N)
=\max_{\rho\ \mathrm{state}}\operatorname{Tr}[\tau_\rho K_\sigma(N)],
\quad \tau_\rho=(1-\delta)\rho+\frac\delta3I.
\tag{M.6.13bu.2}
$$
The original device gives $\min J_\delta\le r$. Restrict the reference to the occupied support of $\mathcal G_Q\sigma$ and compress $N$ to that support. Its state and asymmetry are unchanged; the compression preserves the linear noise terms and removes a positive quadratic excursion, so noise can only decrease. This selects a new finite apparatus rather than identifying every unused part of the old apparatus.

On this finite supported space the strictly positive $\delta$ term makes the objective coercive on invariant $N$: its quadratic weight is at least $(\delta/3)I\otimes\mathcal G_Q\sigma>0$. Finite-dimensional epigraph duality supplies a minimizer $N_\delta$ and a saddle state $\tau$ with $(\delta/3)I\le\tau\le I$. It obeys
$$
RN_\delta+N_\delta R=2D,\qquad
R=\mathcal G_{\mathrm{tot}}(\tau\otimes\sigma),\qquad
D=\mathcal G_{\mathrm{tot}}\!\left(\frac{\{\tau,X\}}2\otimes\sigma\right).
\tag{M.6.13bu.3}
$$
The Hermitian part of $\tau^{1/2}X\tau^{-1/2}$ is
$\tau^{-1/2}\{\tau,X\}\tau^{-1/2}/2$, whose norm is at most $M=\sqrt{3/\delta}$ since $\|X\|=1$. Therefore $-MR\le D\le MR$. The positive Sylvester $\int$
$$
N_\delta=2\int_0^\infty e^{-sR}De^{-sR}\,ds
$$
gives $-MI\le N_\delta\le MI$, with charge conservation preserved. Hence
$$
\|N_\delta\|\le\sqrt{3/\delta},\qquad
\lambda_{\max}K_\sigma(N_\delta)\le\frac r{1-\delta}.
\tag{M.6.13bu.4}
$$
No lower eigenvalue bound on $\sigma$ uniform across apparatuses was assumed; coercivity was needed only on its fixed finite occupied twirl support.

**II. Pinching and the full noise matrix.** Use the $L$ shifted length-$L$ interval partitions of Theorem M.6.13bt. Write $P_s$ for reference pinching, $\sigma_s=P_s\sigma$, and $N_s=P_sN_\delta$, with identity on the system in this pinching. These observables are invariant. Kadison's inequality gives $N_s^2\le P_s(N_\delta^2)$. As $\sigma_s$ is block diagonal and $X$ commutes with reference pinching, the linear terms agree, so
$$
K_{\sigma_s}(N_s)\le
\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma_s)(N_\delta-X\otimes I)^2].
\tag{M.6.13bu.5}
$$
Form the retained uniform mixture of these states and observables, split each pinched interval into its own neutral-flag block, and translate its charges to $0,\ldots,L-1$. Its complete noise matrix is the average of the left sides and its asymmetry is at most $a$.

Put $Y=(N_\delta-X\otimes I)^2$. Both $N_\delta$ and $N_\delta^2$ commute with total charge on a system of charge width two. Thus they have reference charge gaps only in $\{0,\pm1,\pm2\}$; multiplication by $X$ does not change a reference gap. The same five-mode statement holds for $Y$. Average window pinching multiplies the reference gap-$d$ part of $\sigma$ by $1-|d|/L$ when $|d|\le2$. Every Fourier projection $\sigma_d$ has trace norm at most $\|\sigma\|_1=1$, since it is a normalized phase average of unitary conjugates with a scalar coefficient of modulus one. For every finite trace-class $\eta$ the vector-matrix-element trace bound gives
$$
\left\|\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\eta)Y]\right\|
\le\|\eta\|_1\|Y\|.
$$
Consequently
$$
\begin{aligned}
\left\|\operatorname{Tr}_R\!\left[\left(I\otimes\frac1L\sum_s\sigma_s-I\otimes\sigma\right)Y\right]\right\|
&\le\sum_{d=\pm1,\pm2}\frac{|d|}{L}\|\sigma_d\|_1\|Y\|\\
&\le\frac{6(M+1)^2}{L}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bu.6}
$$
Combining with (M.6.13bu.4)–(M.6.13bu.5) gives
$$
K_{\mathrm{new}}\le K_\sigma(N_\delta)+\frac{6(M+1)^2}{L}I,
$$
which proves (M.6.13bu.1). All states, flags, charges and the complete neutral spectral dilation are finite. Every asymmetry-bearing factor is inside the counted reference.

For the explicit cutoff take $\delta=\varepsilon/4$ and $L=\lceil180/\varepsilon^2\rceil$. Since $r\le1$, the regularization loss is at most $\delta/(1-\delta)\le\varepsilon/3$. Also $(1+\sqrt{12/\varepsilon})^2<20/\varepsilon$, so the window loss is at most $2\varepsilon/3$. This proves the stated error increase. $\square$

If $C(r)$ and $C_L(r)$ are the corresponding asymmetry infima at squared error at most $r$, with unrestricted and length-$L$ reference charge ranges respectively, the construction gives
$$
C_L\!\left(\frac r{1-\delta}+\frac{6(1+\sqrt{3/\delta})^2}{L}\right)\le C(r),
\qquad C(r)\le C_L(r).
\tag{M.6.13bu.7}
$$
Sector multiplicity remains unrestricted in $C_L$. This range approximation is not a dimension cutoff, a computed frontier or an attainment theorem.

<a id="theorem-m613bv-fixed-weighted-zeeman-sources-for-finite-charge-measurements"></a>**Theorem M.6.13bv (Fixed Weighted-Zeeman Sources for Finite-Charge Measurements).** Let $Q_S,A$ be Hermitian operators on a fixed finite-dimensional system. Write $F_{Q_S,A}(\epsilon)$ for the infimum of complete ready-reference relative-entropy charge asymmetry in the finite conserving-unitary, product-ready, Yanase-pointer class, with arbitrary finite real reference charges, degeneracies, mixed states and internal correlations, and every system input tested. There is one fixed finite physical system carrier, one fixed encoded target $A_{\rm phys}$ and one fixed physical weighted-Zeeman charge $Q_S^{\rm phys}$ such that, for every $0<\epsilon<\|A\|$, the completely counted finite source family below has exact-error asymmetry infimum $F_{Q_S,A}(\epsilon)$. The same equality holds for error at most $\epsilon$.

The system and reference are encoded separately. Every physical system input, including every code complement, is tested. The conserved physical quantity is the specified weighted Zeeman-energy sum, up to a fixed positive energy-unit scale and additive baselines. Other hardware, clock, field, detector, preparation and drive energies retain their own owners. Neutrality for this charge does not mean zero ordinary energy. The source class admits the displayed finite exchange-polynomial matrices, independently registered longitudinal fields and coefficients, prescribed-time pulses, and separately owned preparation, timing, detector, holding and isolation services. The conclusion concerns this explicit fixed-code interpretation and ready-state asymmetry; it supplies neither an unknown entropy formula nor total-hardware-energy conservation, zero error, finite attainment, a price minimum, spatial locality or full postmeasurement-channel equivalence.

*Proof.* **I. The full-input corner and the original observable problem.** For an original apparatus, its Heisenberg pointer $B=U^*(I\otimes M)U$ is Hermitian and invariant for $Q_S+Q_R$. Put
$$
K_\sigma(B)=A^2-\{A,\mathbb E_\sigma B\}+\mathbb E_\sigma B^2,
\qquad \mathbb E_\sigma B=\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma)B],
\qquad \epsilon_\infty^2=\lambda_{\max}K_\sigma(B).
\tag{M.6.13bv.1}
$$
Conversely the counted neutral spectral-pointer dilation of Theorem M.6.13h realizes any finite invariant Hermitian $B$ with both moments $B,B^2$, retaining every output. Thus this observable problem is equivalent to the original complete-apparatus problem.

Suppose an isometry $E:S\to S_{\rm phys}$ obeys $Q_S^{\rm phys}E=E(Q_S+cI)$, and set $A_{\rm phys}=EAE^*$, zero on the complement. Extending $B$ by zero gives an invariant $B_E=(E\otimes I)B(E^*\otimes I)$ and
$$
K_\sigma^{\rm phys}(B_E)=EK_\sigma(B)E^*.
\tag{M.6.13bv.2}
$$
Noise vanishes on the whole system complement, with no cross terms. Conversely compress any invariant physical $B$ to $B_c=(E^*\otimes I)B(E\otimes I)$. With $P=EE^*\otimes I$,
$$
(E^*\otimes I)B^2(E\otimes I)-B_c^2
=(E^*\otimes I)B(I-P)B(E\otimes I)\ge0,
\qquad K_\sigma(B_c)\le E^*K_\sigma^{\rm phys}(B)E.
\tag{M.6.13bv.3}
$$
The complete reference state, charge and asymmetry are unchanged. A counted neutral spectral pointer realizes $B_c$. Consequently the original and enlarged-system at-most-error infima coincide while all physical inputs are tested. Exact errors in the stated positive interior interval follow by continuous pointer calibration toward zero, whose error is $\|A\|$; part VI supplies strict slack where necessary. The same extension and compression preserve the distance of $A$ to the charge commutant. Preparations, observables and spectator pairings intertwine on the code corner, with a complement effect added to any physical POVM. This source interpretation does not supply a free transcoder for a prescribed unrelated physical carrier or a full-observable or postmeasurement-code equivalence.

**II. One fixed integer module and physical system code.** Choose a charge eigenbasis $|a,\alpha\rangle$, with distinct eigenvalues $q_a$ and multiplicities $d_a$. The group
$$
\Lambda_S=\sum_a\mathbb Z(q_a-q_0)
$$
is a finitely generated torsion-free abelian group. Choose a $\mathbb Z$-basis $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_d$, reversing individual signs so $\beta_i>0$. It is rationally independent, since clearing denominators in a rational relation gives an integer relation. Thus
$$
q_a=q_0+\sum_{i=1}^d n_{ai}\beta_i,\qquad n_{ai}\in\mathbb Z.
\tag{M.6.13bv.4}
$$
This is an integer-module basis, not a rational basis with unhandled denominators. A common denominator embeds a finite generator list in $\mathbb Z^d$, and an integer-lattice basis supplies these coordinates. The exact basis and identities are registered data; no uniform decision procedure for arbitrary real equalities or rational independence is asserted.

For $d\ge1$, let $a_i=\min_a n_{ai}$, $L_{Si}=\max_a n_{ai}-a_i$ and $k_S=\lceil\log_2\max_a d_a\rceil$. Use $L_{Si}$ physical spin halves in family $i$, plus $k_S$ four-spin singlet blocks assigned to family 1. Keep every sixteen-dimensional singlet block. Its two orthonormal rotation-scalar code vectors are
$$
|0_L\rangle=\frac{(|01\rangle-|10\rangle)_{12}(|01\rangle-|10\rangle)_{34}}2,
\qquad
|1_L\rangle=\frac{|0011\rangle+|1100\rangle-(|0101\rangle+|0110\rangle+|1001\rangle+|1010\rangle)/2}{\sqrt3}.
$$
Their products encode the degeneracy labels $|\alpha_L\rangle$. With $|D_n^L\rangle$ the normalized symmetric vector of $L$ spins containing $n$ down spins, define
$$
E_S|a,\alpha\rangle=\bigotimes_i|D_{n_{ai}-a_i}^{L_{Si}}\rangle\otimes|\alpha_L\rangle,
\qquad D_S^{\rm phys}=2^{\sum_iL_{Si}+4k_S}.
\tag{M.6.13bv.5}
$$
Let $J_{zi}^S$ be the actual sum of physical spin-$z$ operators in family $i$, including assigned singlet blocks, and set
$$
Q_{Si}^{\rm phys}=a_i+L_{Si}/2-J_{zi}^S/\hbar,
\quad Q_S^{\rm phys}=q_0I+\sum_i\beta_iQ_{Si}^{\rm phys},
\quad A_{\rm phys}=E_SAE_S^*.
\tag{M.6.13bv.6}
$$
Each coordinate has integer spectrum on the whole physical carrier. Singlet blocks contribute zero $J_z$ and only an integer down-spin offset on their unused sectors. On the code the coordinate is $n_{ai}$, so $Q_S^{\rm phys}E_S=E_SQ_S$. Both system and target are fixed before any reference or accuracy is chosen. The smaller code may have holes or nonuniform degeneracies and need not be $SU(2)^d$ invariant. The larger product-symmetric envelope with all singlet labels is invariant, with family-$i$ spin $L_{Si}/2$.

If $d=0$, the charge is scalar. Encode the system in $k_S=\lceil\log_2\dim S\rceil$ singlet blocks, retain all $2^{4k_S}$ states, and measure $A_{\rm phys}$ with a pure neutral spectral pointer at zero asymmetry. For $p$ distinct outputs including zero, encode its labels in $k_P=\lceil\log_2p\rceil$ singlet blocks. The complete clock/record/pointer apparatus has dimension $3p\,2^{4k_P}$. Take $Q_S^{\rm phys}=q_0I$, $Q_R^{\rm phys}=0$ and $H_Z=E_0I\ge0$. The scalar source and services of part V apply without a nonzero field or direction carrier. Henceforth $d\ge1$.

**III. Arbitrary real references on the fixed system module.** Partition the finite real reference spectrum into cosets modulo $\Lambda_S$. This is an algebraic finite partition even if the subgroup is dense in $\mathbb R$. A nonzero matrix entry of $B$ has reference-charge difference equal to a system gap, so $B$ and $B^2$ preserve every occupied coset. The same holds for the original $U,M$. If $P_c$ are the occupied coset projections, then
$$
\widetilde\sigma=\sum_cP_c\sigma P_c,
\qquad \mathcal A_{Q_R}(\widetilde\sigma)\le\mathcal A_{Q_R}(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13bv.7}
$$
Coset pinching preserves both conditional pointer moments and the whole noise matrix. Its asymmetry inequality is relative-entropy data processing for a charge-covariant channel commuting with charge dephasing.

Within coset $c$ write $q_r=\theta_c+\sum_i n_{ri}\beta_i$. Remove $\theta_c$ and choose translations $t_c\in\mathbb Z^d$ so the finitely many occupied integer-coordinate boxes are disjoint, for example by sufficiently separating their first coordinates. Set
$$
q_r'=\sum_i(n_{ri}+t_{ci})\beta_i.
$$
Retain every original basis state, multiplicity and coset block. All previously nonzero within-coset entries keep their charge differences, so $B,U,M$ remain conserving or Yanase for $Q_R'$. The pinched state has no inter-coset coherence, and the new coset labels are distinct. Its dephasing is unchanged. Thus
$$
K_{\widetilde\sigma,Q_R'}(B)=K_{\sigma,Q_R}(B),\qquad
\mathcal A_{Q_R'}(\widetilde\sigma)=\mathcal A_{Q_R}(\widetilde\sigma)\le\mathcal A_{Q_R}(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13bv.8}
$$
This is an optimization replacement preserving noise and not increasing cost, not a whole-state identity or an identification of the old arbitrary real labels with spin eigenvalues.

Write the distinct new charges as unique integer vectors $n_{ri}$. Put $b_i=\min_rn_{ri}$, $L_{Ri}=\max_rn_{ri}-b_i$ and $k_R=\lceil\log_2\max_q\dim R_q\rceil$. Independently of the system encode the reference by
$$
E_R|r,\alpha\rangle=\bigotimes_i|D_{n_{ri}-b_i}^{L_{Ri}}\rangle\otimes|\alpha_L\rangle,
\qquad \dim R_{\rm spin}=2^{\sum_iL_{Ri}+4k_R}.
\tag{M.6.13bv.9}
$$
It preserves the actual mixed state $\widetilde\sigma$, all degeneracies and internal correlations. The weighted charge intertwines $Q_R'$ with the ready-ancilla constants specified in part V; charge twirling and relative-entropy asymmetry are exactly preserved. Alternatively, for one fixed original device a joint module generated by both system and reference gaps gives the same construction without coset pinching. That intermediate encoding preserves its state exactly but can change the system carrier across devices, so it is not used for the fixed-system optimization theorem.

**IV. Complete neutral pointer and product-spin approximation.** Embed $B$ as
$$
B_E=(E_S\otimes E_R)B(E_S^*\otimes E_R^*),
$$
zero off the full code. Rational independence makes scalar total-charge equality equivalent to equality of every integer total coordinate. Thus $B_E$ commutes with every longitudinal coordinate. With the encoded ready reference, the corner noise is $E_SK E_S^*$ and is zero on every extra system direction.

For the $p$ distinct spectral values of $B_E$, including $\nu_0=0$, use $k_P=\lceil\log_2p\rceil$ four-spin singlet pointer blocks in family 1, retaining all $2^{4k_P}$ states; $p\le\dim S\,\dim R+1$. If $\Pi_a$ are the spectral projections and $V$ a $p$-cycle on the code labels, identity elsewhere, put
$$
U_0=\sum_{a=0}^{p-1}\Pi_a\otimes V^a,
\qquad M_P=\sum_a\nu_aP_a.
\tag{M.6.13bv.10}
$$
The pure ready pointer gives exactly $B_E,B_E^2$. The unitary is identity off the relevant system/reference code and pointer envelope, satisfies $U_0^p=I$, and conserves every coordinate. Its finite spectral logarithm, with phases in $(-\pi,\pi]$ and phase $\pi$ at $-1$, gives
$$
e^{-i\tau K/\hbar}=U_0,\qquad K=K^*,\qquad \|K\|\le\pi\hbar/\tau.
\tag{M.6.13bv.11}
$$
Take $K=0$ outside the larger invariant product-symmetric/singlet envelope. Its maximal family-$i$ spin is $j_i=(L_{Si}+L_{Ri})/2$.

Append $m_i$ physical spin halves in the all-up state $F_i$, retaining every $2^{m_i}$ state. These ready directions are weighted-charge eigenstates and add zero charge asymmetry. On their symmetric sectors let $|F_{i,g_i}\rangle$ be the spin-$m_i/2$ coherent orbit, and define the finite matrix
$$
H_F=\prod_i(m_i+1)\int_{SU(2)^d}R(g)KR(g)^*\otimes\bigotimes_i|F_{i,g_i}\rangle\langle F_{i,g_i}|\,dg,
\tag{M.6.13bv.12}
$$
with zero extension on the other direction sectors. This matrix is Hermitian, has norm at most $\|K\|$, and commutes with every full family spin vector. It preserves the larger envelope but may leave the smaller logical code; that leakage is included in the following error bound.

The $\int$ map is unital and completely positive on the symmetric direction sectors, not on the zero-extended complementary sectors. Apply Kadison to $K_g-K$. Axial invariance and product rotations give $\|K_g-K\|\le2\|K\|\sum_i j_i\theta_i$. The ready coherent kernel satisfies $\mathbb E\sin^2(\theta_i/2)=1/(m_i+2)$ and $\theta_i^2\le\pi^2\sin^2(\theta_i/2)$. Minkowski in $L^2$ therefore yields
$$
\|(H_F-K\otimes I)(\psi\otimes F)\|
\le2\pi\|K\|\sum_i\frac{j_i}{\sqrt{m_i+2}}.
$$
Duhamel, with comparison evolution keeping the directions ready, gives the uniform full-input propagator bound
$$
\delta\le\frac{2\pi\tau\|K\|}{\hbar}\sum_i\frac{j_i}{\sqrt{m_i+2}}
\le2\pi^2\sum_i\frac{j_i}{\sqrt{m_i+2}}.
\tag{M.6.13bv.13}
$$
It tensors with arbitrary spectators and holds for every physical system input. Off the larger invariant envelope both comparison generators vanish for ready directions. Purifying a mixed reference is only a proof device. The noise-vector expression gives
$$
|\epsilon_\infty^{\rm compiled}-\epsilon_\infty^{\rm ideal}|
\le(\|M_P\|+\|A_{\rm phys}\|)\delta=(\|M_P\|+\|A\|)\delta.
\tag{M.6.13bv.14}
$$
There is no omitted failure event or postselection.

The product-group commutant is the tensor product of the physical spin-half permutation algebras. Each within-family swap is the physical scalar $P_{ab}=I/2+2\mathbf s_a\cdot\mathbf s_b/\hbar^2$. Hence $H_F$ is a finite Hermitian sum of products of such exchanges. Its coefficient recipe enumerates those products, selects an independent Hilbert--Schmidt basis and solves its nonsingular Gram system against (M.6.13bv.12). Compute the $\int$ matrix by magnetic partial traces in finite total-spin decompositions family by family, retaining every multiplicity matrix and complement. With $n_i$ the full family spin count there are at most $\prod_i n_i!$ permutation labels per scalar matrix entry. No efficient or pairwise-pulse synthesis claim is needed.

**V. Longitudinal fields, actual source, pulse, readout and ledger.** Add a scalar $p$-level record and a scalar three-cell clock, independently ready at zero. Copy each pointer code label to its record by a controlled $p$-cycle, identity on unused pointer sectors. Define $W_0=\mathrm{copy}\circ(e^{-i\tau H_F/\hbar}\otimes I_{\rm record})$, $W_1=I$, $W_2=W_0^*$ and
$$
D_c=\sum_{a=0}^2|a+1\bmod3\rangle\langle a|\otimes W_a,
\qquad H_{\rm src}=3\sqrt3\gamma I+\gamma i(D_c-D_c^*),
\qquad \gamma=\frac{2\pi\hbar}{3\sqrt3T},\quad T>0.
\tag{M.6.13bv.15}
$$
The three cyclic holonomies are identity, so $D_c^3=I$. The positive source spectrum is $\{2\sqrt3\gamma,3\sqrt3\gamma,4\sqrt3\gamma\}$ and $e^{-iTH_{\rm src}/\hbar}=D_c$. The source commutes with every group spin and has the finite product-exchange representation with scalar clock/record coefficients.

Let $J_{zi}^R$ include all physical reference, direction and assigned pointer/singlet spins. Put
$$
Q_{Ri}^{\rm phys}=b_i+(L_{Ri}+m_i)/2-J_{zi}^R/\hbar,
\qquad Q_R^{\rm phys}=\sum_i\beta_iQ_{Ri}^{\rm phys}.
\tag{M.6.13bv.16}
$$
Its whole coordinate spectra are integer. On the encoded reference and all new ready factors it intertwines $Q_R'$ exactly. Fix one positive unit scale $\chi$ and a system-energy baseline at system registration, independently of reference approximations. Choose an additional apparatus baseline for each finite apparatus so that
$$
H_Z=\chi(Q_S^{\rm phys}+Q_R^{\rm phys})+E_0I\ge0.
\tag{M.6.13bv.17}
$$
Its nonconstant terms are $-\sum_i\omega_i(J_{zi}^S+J_{zi}^R)$ with actual calibrated longitudinal angular frequencies $\omega_i=\chi\beta_i/\hbar>0$. Their values and energy/time units are independent source data. Static field stores and calibration are owned services. Scalar clocks, records, detectors and timing degrees have trivial representation of this magnetic charge but retain their actual Hamiltonian energies and work. Conservation or asymmetry of total service energy is a different predicate.

For a physical pulse duration $t_g>0$, set $x=t/t_g$ and
$$
\lambda(t)=\frac{30T}{t_g}x^2(1-x)^2\quad(0\le t\le t_g),
\qquad \lambda(t)=0\quad\text{otherwise}.
\tag{M.6.13bv.18}
$$
It is $C^1$, has $\int$ $T$, maximum $15T/(8t_g)$, derivative maximum $10\sqrt3T/(3t_g^2)$ and total variation $15T/(4t_g)$. The actual positive core Hamiltonian is
$$
H_{\rm total}(t)=H_Z+b_0I+\lambda(t)H_{\rm src},\qquad b_0\ge0.
\tag{M.6.13bv.19}
$$
Since $[H_{\rm src},H_Z]=0$, its endpoint is free Zeeman evolution times $D_c$, up to phase. The scalar record pointer $M_D=\operatorname{diag}(\nu_a)$ commutes with $H_Z$, so free drift cancels from both Heisenberg pointer moments. No transverse-phase compensation is used. The full evolution conserves each longitudinal family spin and $H_Z$; transverse components generally precess. Full product-rotation invariance belongs to $H_{\rm src}$, not the field-containing $H_{\rm total}$. The finite Schrödinger action has these longitudinal symmetries and this physical weighted magnetic Noether charge.

The pulse isolates the interaction before a positive-duration invariant terminal detector reads all $p$ record projectors, retaining every output. A scalar or pointer-diagonal record Hamiltonian and finite readout/storage law are separately supplied. Without pulse isolation the source recurs and uncomputes its record; no autonomous permanent latch is asserted.

The complete core apparatus dimension is
$$
D_R^{\rm phys}=3p\,2^{\sum_i(L_{Ri}+m_i)+4k_R+4k_P}.
\tag{M.6.13bv.20}
$$
The separately fixed system dimension is (M.6.13bv.5). Every optional neutral service factor or retained supplier multiplies its owner's dimension explicitly. No system spin is moved to the reference or conversely.

On the ready clock cell,
$$
\langle H_{\rm src}\rangle=2\pi\hbar/T,
\quad\langle H_{\rm src}-E_{\min}\rangle=2\pi\hbar/(3T),
\quad\int\|\lambda H_{\rm src}\|\,dt=8\pi\hbar/3.
\tag{M.6.13bv.21}
$$
These are active interaction energies and action. Free $H_Z$ and scalar baseline $b_0$ keep their stored-energy and action inventories. The source expectation is constant, hence signed switching work is zero, ready-input absolute work transfer is $(2\pi\hbar/T)\operatorname{TV}(\lambda)$, and its universal norm bound is $(8\pi\hbar/(3T))\operatorname{TV}(\lambda)$. These transfers are not dissipated heat and are not counted again as independent storage.

The finite typed ledger also retains all $L_{Si},L_{Ri}$ and degeneracy labels; every direction count $m_i$, polarization $m_i\hbar/2$ and product-group asymmetry $\sum_i\log(m_i+1)$; finite coupling coefficients, supports and installation; field magnitudes, stores and calibration; $T,t_g$, terminal detector duration and time standard; scalar switching/controller, output holding and all $p$ records; preparation work, heat and stores; isolated archives; and any optional renewal or reset. Each owned finite service has declared finite duration, energy, power, storage, transfer and tariff inputs. No uniform price or cost bound as dimension, frequency precision or calibration vary follows.

The complete ready reference is $E_R\widetilde\sigma E_R^*$ times independent singlet pointer, polarized directions, scalar clock/record and chosen scalar service states. All added factors are weighted-charge eigenstates or trivial representations, whence
$$
\mathcal A_{Q_R^{\rm phys}}(\sigma_{\rm complete})
=\mathcal A_{Q_R'}(\widetilde\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13bv.22}
$$
All old internal correlations are encoded in its first factor. Independent scalar entropies cancel in asymmetry. A preparation supplier must be permanently isolated before the independent system input and keep its lifecycle costs. A live ensemble label or purifier is counted and can change this identity. A finite label-free supply can swap a preloaded mixed resource with a blank identical physical carrier using $H_p=\pi\hbar(I-\mathrm{SWAP})/(2t_p)$, whose endpoint is SWAP and norm action $\pi\hbar$. Its blank output is longitudinal-spin invariant, not generally fully rotationally invariant; retain or isolate it with full ownership and dimension. This optimizes ready-boundary asymmetry, not total lifecycle resource.

**VI. Finite accuracy, cheap strict slack and exact error.** In the system coordinate basis use the product reference vector $\eta_N$ uniform on $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}^d$. Its dimension is $N^d$, charge is $\sum_i\beta_i n_i$ and asymmetry is $d\log N$. Let $T^k$ be the product of truncated shifts. For $N>\max_i|k_i|$,
$$
\|(T^k-I)\eta_N\|^2
=1-\prod_i(1-|k_i|/N)\le\|k\|_1/N.
\tag{M.6.13bv.23}
$$
The finite invariant Hermitian observable
$$
B_N=\sum_{a,\alpha,b,\beta}A_{a\alpha,b\beta}|a,\alpha\rangle\langle b,\beta|
\otimes T^{n_b-n_a},
\qquad C_A=\sum_{a,\alpha,b,\beta}|A_{a\alpha,b\beta}|\sqrt{\|n_b-n_a\|_1}
\tag{M.6.13bv.24}
$$
has all-input RMS noise at most $C_A/\sqrt N$ by the triangle inequality on each system component, also with spectators. A counted finite neutral spectral pointer realizes it. Thus every positive accuracy has a finite model. If $C_A=0$, the target commutes with charge and is measured exactly by an invariant observable.

For any finite device of squared error at most $r>0$, choose one finite stricter device with $r_h<r$. Retain a direct-sum branch flag with weights $1-t,t$. Its noise and asymmetry satisfy
$$
K_t=(1-t)K_0+tK_h\le[(1-t)r+tr_h]I<rI,
\qquad \mathcal A(\sigma_t)=(1-t)\mathcal A(\sigma_0)+t\mathcal A(\sigma_h)
\longrightarrow\mathcal A(\sigma_0)\quad(t\downarrow0).
\tag{M.6.13bv.25}
$$
The flag entropy cancels. This is affinity of the noise matrix, not an assertion that its largest eigenvalue is affine. Every branch and flag stays counted. Applying part III first keeps this mixing in the fixed module.

For each strict-slack device, choose finite $m_i$ so (M.6.13bv.14) keeps compiled error below $\epsilon=\sqrt r$. Scale only the numerical terminal pointer by $s\in[0,1]$. Its noise is a finite matrix polynomial in $s$, so its largest eigenvalue is continuous. At $s=1$ error is below $\epsilon$, and at zero it is $\|A_{\rm phys}\|=\|A\|$. Every prescribed $0<\epsilon<\|A\|$ is therefore reached exactly without changing the ready state or its asymmetry.

Equations (M.6.13bv.8), (M.6.13bv.22) and (M.6.13bv.25) prove that the physical-source infimum is at most the original one. Conversely every such source is a finite conserving/Yanase device on the fixed physical system. Compression (M.6.13bv.3), keeping the complete physical reference and its charge, gives an original at-most-error device with the same asymmetry. Pointer calibration, with strict slack if needed, gives the original exact-error infimum. The reverse inequality follows. This proves both exact and at-most equalities pointwise at every positive interior error, without continuity of the unknown frontier, a uniform apparatus bound, exact finite preservation of every original moment pair, zero-error realizability or finite attainment. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613bw-exact-finite-charge-capacity-error-frontier"></a>**Theorem M.6.13bw (Exact Finite Charge Capacity Error Frontier).** Retain the complete finite measurement class of Theorems M.6.13g–M.6.13h for the registered qubit
$$
Q_S=|1\rangle\langle1|,
\qquad
X_S=|0\rangle\langle1|+|1\rangle\langle0|.
\tag{M.6.13bw.1}
$$
An admitted apparatus consists of a finite complete reference $R$, a state $\sigma_R$ independent of the tested system input, a Hermitian total reference charge $Q_R$, a unitary $U$ on $S\otimes R$, and a self-adjoint pointer $M$ on $R$. Every ancillary factor, flag, and pointer degree of freedom, together with its correlations, belongs to this complete reference. The conservation, Yanase, and all-input error conditions are
$$
\begin{aligned}
[U,Q_S\otimes I_R+I_S\otimes Q_R]&=0,
&[M,Q_R]&=0,\\
B&=U^*(I_S\otimes M)U,
&\epsilon_\infty^2
&=\sup_{\rho_S}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[
(\rho_S\otimes\sigma_R)(B-X_S\otimes I_R)^2
\right],
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bw.2}
$$
where the supremum is over all system density operators. For each integer $N\ge1$, let $e_N$ be the infimum of $\epsilon_\infty$ over this class subject to $|\operatorname{spec}Q_R|\le N$. The cap counts **distinct eigenvalues of the complete total reference charge**, not the total Hilbert dimension. Charge eigenvalues may be arbitrary real numbers; all finite sector degeneracies, mixed states, and neutral ancillary dimensions are allowed and remain parts of the actual apparatus.

For $a,b\ge0$, define
$$
\begin{aligned}
h(a,b)&=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{2ab}{a+b},&a+b>0,\\[2pt]
0,&a=b=0,
\end{cases}\\
H_N(p)&=\sum_{i=0}^{N-2}h(p_i,p_{i+1}),
\qquad
\mu_N=\max_{\substack{p_i\ge0\\ \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}p_i=1}}H_N(p),
\qquad \mu_1=0,
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bw.3}
$$
with the sum empty when $N=1$. Then the apparatus infimum is an attained minimum, and
$$
e_N^2=1-\mu_N.
\tag{M.6.13bw.4}
$$
For every $N\ge2$, the maximizing probability vector $p^{(N)}$ is unique, strictly positive, and reflection-symmetric. The numbers $\mu_N$ are strictly increasing, satisfy $\mu_N<1$ at every finite $N$, and converge to one. The finite recurrence below specifies their unique admissible algebraic root and reconstructs the maximizer.

An attaining complete apparatus is exhibited below with
$$
K_N=2\left\lfloor\frac N2\right\rfloor+1,
\qquad
\dim R=NK_N,
\qquad
|\operatorname{spec}Q_R|=N,
\qquad
\dim(S\otimes R)=2NK_N.
\tag{M.6.13bw.5}
$$
Each reference-charge eigenspace has degeneracy $K_N$. Here $K_N$ is the number of actual neutral pointer levels in the displayed spectral construction. Neither minimal pointer dimension nor minimal total Hilbert dimension is asserted.

More generally, if $\Gamma\subset\mathbb R$ is finite and nonempty and $m(\Gamma)$ is the number of vertices in its longest consecutive unit-step run, the exact best squared error under $\operatorname{spec}Q_R\subseteq\Gamma$ is $1-\mu_{m(\Gamma)}$. The same attained value holds when the complete spectrum is required to equal $\Gamma$. For $0<\epsilon<1$, the least distinct-charge capacity permitting either error at most $\epsilon$ or exact error $\epsilon$ is the finite integer
$$
N_{\min}(\epsilon)
=\min\{N\ge1:\mu_N\ge1-\epsilon^2\}.
\tag{M.6.13bw.6}
$$
At error one a one-dimensional constant-pointer apparatus suffices; error zero is impossible at every finite charge capacity.

*Proof.*

**Reduction from every complete apparatus.**

For a fixed finite reference charge $Q$ and reference state $\sigma$, use the quantities of Theorem M.6.13h. Namely, let $\tau=\mathcal G_Q(\sigma)$, diagonalize each charge block of $\tau$, denote its eigenvalues by $p_{q\alpha}$, and put
$$
\begin{aligned}
c_{q\alpha\beta}
&=\langle q+1,\alpha|\sigma|q,\beta\rangle,\\
F_\sigma(t)
&=\sum_{q,\alpha,\beta}
\frac{|c_{q\alpha\beta}|^2}
{t p_{q+1,\alpha}+(1-t)p_{q,\beta}},
\qquad 0\le t\le1,\\
e_Q(\sigma)^2&=1-\min_{0\le t\le1}F_\sigma(t).
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bw.7}
$$
Only existing charge sectors separated by one occur. A summand with zero numerator and denominator is defined to be zero, including at $t=0$ and $t=1$; positivity makes every coherence incident to a zero block eigenvalue vanish. The last equality allows a pure neutral pointer enlargement. It therefore supplies a lower bound for each actual measurement using the given complete reference, whether or not that measurement already has this enlargement.

The same theorem gives the basis-independent variational identity
$$
\begin{aligned}
\eta_Q(\sigma)&=F_\sigma(1/2)
=\max_{[Q,L]=L}\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma H_L),\\
H_L&=L+L^*-\frac{LL^*+L^*L}{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bw.8}
$$
Since the minimum in (M.6.13bw.7) is at most its value at $t=1/2$, every such measurement satisfies
$$
\epsilon_\infty^2\ge e_Q(\sigma)^2
\ge1-\eta_Q(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13bw.9}
$$
There is also a direct verification on the original complete apparatus, without interpreting a pointer-enlarged optimization as one on a fixed reference. Conservation and the Yanase condition imply that its Heisenberg pointer commutes with the total charge. In the registered system basis write
$$
B=\begin{pmatrix}A&L\\L^*&D\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
A=A^*,\quad D=D^*,\quad [Q,A]=[Q,D]=0,
\quad [Q,L]=L.
\tag{M.6.13bw.10}
$$
Testing the maximally mixed system input and expanding the noise square gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\epsilon_\infty^2
&\ge\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[
\left(\frac{I_S}{2}\otimes\sigma\right)
(B-X_S\otimes I_R)^2\right]\\
&=1+\frac12\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[\sigma(A^2+D^2)\right]
-\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma H_L)\\
&\ge1-\eta_Q(\sigma).
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bw.11}
$$
The second line uses the quadratic terms $LL^*$ and $L^*L$ already present in $H_L$; the last line discards only nonnegative diagonal-square terms and then uses (M.6.13bw.8).

For fixed $Q$, $\eta_Q$ is a supremum of linear functions of $\sigma$ over a state-independent set of raising operators and is therefore convex. For every finite pure-state decomposition,
$$
\eta_Q\!\left(\sum_a\lambda_a|\psi_a\rangle\langle\psi_a|\right)
\le\sum_a\lambda_a\eta_Q(|\psi_a\rangle\langle\psi_a|),
\qquad
\lambda_a\ge0,\quad \sum_a\lambda_a=1.
\tag{M.6.13bw.12}
$$
Thus it suffices to upper-bound $\eta_Q$ on pure states of the whole reference. In particular, this reduction does not remove mixedness, charge degeneracy, or correlations with neutral ancillas from the admitted apparatus class.

Write a unit vector along the distinct charge sectors as
$$
|\psi\rangle=\sum_{q\in\operatorname{spec}Q}|\psi_q\rangle,
\qquad
p_q=\|\psi_q\|^2,
\qquad
p_q\ge0,\quad\sum_qp_q=1.
\tag{M.6.13bw.13}
$$
In every occupied sector choose $|\psi_q\rangle/\sqrt{p_q}$ as the first basis vector. The corresponding twirled block has the single nonzero eigenvalue $p_q$; its remaining eigenvalues vanish. Between adjacent occupied sectors the only nonzero coherence in these bases is $\sqrt{p_qp_{q+1}}$. The variational contribution of a raising entry $z$ between supported basis vectors, with coherence $c$, is maximized by completing the square:
$$
\begin{aligned}
2\operatorname{Re}(\overline c z)
-\frac{p_q+p_{q+1}}2|z|^2
&=\frac{2|c|^2}{p_q+p_{q+1}}
-\frac{p_q+p_{q+1}}2
\left|z-\frac{2c}{p_q+p_{q+1}}\right|^2,\\
\max_z\left\{
2\operatorname{Re}(\overline c z)
-\frac{p_q+p_{q+1}}2|z|^2\right\}
&=\frac{2|c|^2}{p_q+p_{q+1}},
\qquad p_q+p_{q+1}>0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bw.14}
$$
Every other matrix entry has zero linear coefficient and contributes a maximum of zero. If both support weights vanish, the entire contribution is zero. Consequently, with the zero convention in (M.6.13bw.3),
$$
\eta_Q(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)
=\sum_{\substack{q\in\operatorname{spec}Q\\q+1\in\operatorname{spec}Q}}
 h(p_q,p_{q+1}).
\tag{M.6.13bw.15}
$$
Arbitrarily large charge-sector degeneracies do not create more supported directions in a pure state's twirled block.

Form a graph with one vertex for each distinct real charge eigenvalue and an edge joining $q$ to $q+1$ whenever both are present. Each vertex has at most one predecessor and one successor. A cycle is impossible: its largest real charge would have to have two distinct lower neighbors differing from it by one. Equivalently, directed successor steps strictly increase charge and the predecessor and successor are unique. Every connected component is a finite path, including a one-vertex path. On a component $C$ with $n$ vertices and total probability mass $m_C>0$, degree-one homogeneity gives
$$
\sum_{\{q,q+1\}\subset C}h(p_q,p_{q+1})
=m_C H_n\!\left(\left(\frac{p_q}{m_C}\right)_{q\in C}\right)
\le m_C\mu_n.
\tag{M.6.13bw.16}
$$
A component with zero mass contributes zero. Zero extension of a probability vector proves $\mu_n\le\mu_N$ whenever $n\le N$. If the complete charge has at most $N$ eigenvalues, summing component masses and using (M.6.13bw.12) therefore yields
$$
\eta_Q(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)\le\mu_N,
\qquad
\eta_Q(\sigma)\le\mu_N,
\qquad
\epsilon_\infty^2\ge1-\mu_N.
\tag{M.6.13bw.17}
$$
This proves the universal lower bound in (M.6.13bw.4) for arbitrary finite real charge spectra. The graph is that of the complete total reference charge. Adding a neutral factor changes only sector degeneracy; adding a charged ancillary factor is allowed under the cap only when its resulting complete total spectrum still has at most $N$ distinct eigenvalues.

**Existence and shape of the unique path maximizer.**

The function $h$ is continuous on the closed nonnegative quadrant, including the origin, so $H_N$ attains a maximum on the compact probability simplex. For $N\ge2$, the elementary inequality $h(a,b)\le(a+b)/2$ gives
$$
0\le H_N(p)
\le\frac12\sum_{i=0}^{N-2}(p_i+p_{i+1})
=1-\frac{p_0+p_{N-1}}2
\le1.
\tag{M.6.13bw.18}
$$
Suppose that $p$ is a boundary point. Since the path is connected and some coordinate is positive, there is a zero coordinate $j$ with $k\ge1$ positive neighbors. For $0\le\delta<1$, set $p(\delta)=(1-\delta)p+\delta e_j$. Every previously nonzero edge contribution is multiplied by $1-\delta$, while an edge from $j$ to a positive neighboring coordinate of value $a$ contributes
$$
h(\delta,(1-\delta)a)
=\frac{2\delta(1-\delta)a}{\delta+(1-\delta)a}
=2\delta+O(\delta^2),
\qquad a>0.
\tag{M.6.13bw.19}
$$
Edges from $j$ to zero neighbors contribute zero. It follows that
$$
\left.\frac{d}{d\delta}H_N(p(\delta))\right|_{\delta=0+}
=-H_N(p)+2k\ge-1+2>0.
\tag{M.6.13bw.20}
$$
No boundary point can maximize $H_N$. This argument includes disconnected support and both endpoint and interior zero coordinates. Every maximizer is therefore strictly positive, and its positive endpoint masses make the upper bound in (M.6.13bw.18) strictly smaller than one. Thus $\mu_N<1$.

For $a,b>0$, direct differentiation gives
$$
D^2h(a,b)
=-\frac{4}{(a+b)^3}
\begin{pmatrix}b^2&-ab\\-ab&a^2\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13bw.21}
$$
At a positive vector $p$ and a real simplex tangent vector $v$, this yields
$$
v^{\mathsf T}D^2H_N(p)v
=-4\sum_{i=0}^{N-2}
\frac{(p_{i+1}v_i-p_i v_{i+1})^2}{(p_i+p_{i+1})^3},
\qquad \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}v_i=0.
\tag{M.6.13bw.22}
$$
Equality implies that $v_i/p_i$ is constant along the connected path. The tangent constraint then makes this constant zero. Hence the Hessian is strictly negative on every nonzero simplex tangent direction, and $H_N$ is strictly concave on the positive simplex. Concavity on the whole closed simplex follows from the negative semidefinite summand Hessians and continuity at the boundary. As every maximizer is positive, strict concavity gives exactly one maximizer. Reflection preserves the objective, so uniqueness implies
$$
p_i^{(N)}=p_{N-1-i}^{(N)},
\qquad 0\le i\le N-1.
\tag{M.6.13bw.23}
$$
Strict concavity here concerns the simplex tangent space; degree-one homogeneity precludes strict concavity along scaling rays in the whole positive orthant.

Append a zero endpoint to $p^{(N)}$. This preserves its objective in the $(N+1)$-site simplex, and (M.6.13bw.20) strictly improves it there. The argument also applies when the embedded one-site vector is $(1,0)$. The uniform vector supplies the lower bound
$$
\mu_{N+1}>\mu_N,
\qquad
H_N(1/N,\ldots,1/N)=\frac{N-1}{N},
\qquad
1-\frac1N\le\mu_N<1,
\qquad
\lim_{N\to\infty}\mu_N=1.
\tag{M.6.13bw.24}
$$
In particular, $\mu_2=1/2$, while $\mu_N>1/2$ for $N>2$.

**The finite recurrence and its unique admissible root.**

Let $N\ge2$ and $p=p^{(N)}$. Define
$$
a=\sqrt{\frac{\mu_N}{2}},
\qquad
x_i=\frac{p_i}{p_i+p_{i+1}},
\quad 0\le i\le N-2,
\qquad
\frac12\le a<\frac1{\sqrt2},
\quad 0<x_i<1.
\tag{M.6.13bw.25}
$$
At the interior maximizer, all first derivatives equal one Lagrange multiplier. Euler's identity for degree-one homogeneity gives that multiplier as $\sum_i p_i\partial_{p_i}H_N=H_N(p)=\mu_N$. Direct differentiation thus gives the endpoint and interior equations
$$
\begin{aligned}
\partial_{p_0}H_N&=2(1-x_0)^2=\mu_N,\\
\partial_{p_i}H_N&=2x_{i-1}^2+2(1-x_i)^2=\mu_N,
&&1\le i\le N-2,\\
\partial_{p_{N-1}}H_N&=2x_{N-2}^2=\mu_N.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bw.26}
$$
Because all $x_i$ lie strictly between zero and one, these are equivalent to
$$
\begin{aligned}
x_0&=1-a,\\
x_i&=1-\sqrt{a^2-x_{i-1}^2},
&&1\le i\le N-2,\\
x_{N-2}&=a.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bw.27}
$$
The square root is always the nonnegative real root. The admissibility conditions are $a\in[1/2,1/\sqrt2)$, every recurrence step real, and every resulting $x_i\in(0,1)$. At an admissible solution every radical has strictly positive radicand: a zero radicand would give $x_i=1$. For $N=2$ there is no radical update; the two endpoint equations say $x_0=1-a=a$ and give $a=1/2$. For $N>2$, strict increase in (M.6.13bw.24) gives $a>1/2$.

Existence of an admissible root follows from the maximizer. Conversely, any $a$ and fractions satisfying all these branch conditions and the terminal equation reconstruct a unique positive normalized vector. Explicitly, take
$$
\widetilde p_0=1,
\qquad
\widetilde p_{i+1}=\widetilde p_i\frac{1-x_i}{x_i}
\quad(0\le i\le N-2),
\qquad
p_i=\frac{\widetilde p_i}{\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\widetilde p_j}.
\tag{M.6.13bw.28}
$$
Its adjacent ratios are $p_i/p_{i+1}=x_i/(1-x_i)$, and (M.6.13bw.27) makes every derivative in (M.6.13bw.26) equal to $2a^2$. Concavity then implies, for every probability vector $q$,
$$
H_N(q)\le H_N(p)+\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}
\partial_{p_i}H_N(p)(q_i-p_i)
=H_N(p),
\qquad
H_N(p)=2a^2.
\tag{M.6.13bw.29}
$$
The supporting-plane inequality extends to boundary $q$ by continuity. Thus the reconstructed vector is the global maximizer. Uniqueness of that vector, together with $\mu_N=2a^2$ and $a>0$, proves uniqueness of the admissible root. Squaring to eliminate radicals without retaining their branch, reality, positivity, and endpoint conditions can introduce extraneous roots. The recurrence is a finite algebraic specification; it does not assert a uniform elementary closed form for all $N$.

The fractions are also strictly ordered whenever there is a recurrence step. For an admissible input $x\in(0,1)$,
$$
x^2+(1-x)^2\ge\frac12>a^2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\sqrt{a^2-x^2}<1-x
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
1-\sqrt{a^2-x^2}>x.
\tag{M.6.13bw.30}
$$
Consequently,
$$
x_0<x_1<\cdots<x_{N-2}\quad(N>2),
\qquad
x_{N-2-i}=1-x_i\quad(0\le i\le N-2).
\tag{M.6.13bw.31}
$$
The reflection identity follows directly from (M.6.13bw.23). Together with the adjacent ratios, it says that $p$ strictly increases toward its center and then decreases; there is one central maximum for odd $N$ and two equal central entries for even $N$.

**A complete attaining apparatus with its pointer counted.**

For $N\ge2$, let $R_0=\mathbb C^N$ and use the unique maximizing vector $p=p^{(N)}$. Set
$$
\begin{aligned}
Q_0&=\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}i|i\rangle\langle i|,
&|\phi\rangle&=\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\sqrt{p_i}\,|i\rangle,\\
L&=\sum_{i=0}^{N-2}\ell_i|i+1\rangle\langle i|,
&\ell_i&=\frac{2\sqrt{p_ip_{i+1}}}{p_i+p_{i+1}}
=2\sqrt{x_i(1-x_i)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bw.32}
$$
All $\ell_i$ belong to $(0,1]$, and $[Q_0,L]=L$. Define the invariant observable on $S\otimes R_0$ by
$$
B_0=|0\rangle\langle1|\otimes L
+|1\rangle\langle0|\otimes L^*,
\qquad
[B_0,Q_S\otimes I_{R_0}+I_S\otimes Q_0]=0.
\tag{M.6.13bw.33}
$$
The edge subspaces $\operatorname{span}\{|0,i+1\rangle,|1,i\rangle\}$ are pairwise orthogonal. Their eigenvectors and the two remaining endpoint eigenvectors satisfy
$$
\begin{aligned}
|i,\pm\rangle&=\frac{|0,i+1\rangle\pm|1,i\rangle}{\sqrt2},
&B_0|i,\pm\rangle&=\pm\ell_i|i,\pm\rangle,
&&0\le i\le N-2,\\
B_0|0,0\rangle&=0,
&B_0|1,N-1\rangle&=0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bw.34}
$$
This is a full eigenbasis of $S\otimes R_0$.

The function $2\sqrt{x(1-x)}$ strictly increases for $0<x<1/2$ and is invariant under $x\mapsto1-x$. By (M.6.13bw.31), the coefficients $\ell_i$ increase strictly up to the middle and then reflect. If $N=2m$, the unique middle edge has $x_{m-1}=1/2$ and $\ell_{m-1}=1$, and there are exactly $m$ distinct positive coefficients. If $N=2m+1$, the two middle fractions are complementary and strictly on opposite sides of $1/2$, so there are exactly $m$ distinct positive coefficients, all less than one. The single-edge case $N=2$ agrees with the even formula. Positive and negative eigenvalues are disjoint and zero is present, hence
$$
\bigl|\{\ell_i:0\le i\le N-2\}\bigr|
=\left\lfloor\frac N2\right\rfloor,
\qquad
|\operatorname{spec}B_0|
=2\left\lfloor\frac N2\right\rfloor+1=K_N.
\tag{M.6.13bw.35}
$$
List these distinct eigenvalues as $b_0=0,b_1,\ldots,b_{K_N-1}$, and let $\Pi_j$ be their full spectral projectors, combining all repetitions of each edge eigenvalue. Let $P=\mathbb C^{K_N}$ be a neutral pointer with ready vector $|0\rangle_P$, cyclic shift $V$, and pointer observable $M_P$. Define
$$
\begin{aligned}
V|j\rangle_P&=|(j+1)\bmod K_N\rangle_P,
&M_P&=\sum_{j=0}^{K_N-1}b_j|j\rangle_P\langle j|,\\
U&=\sum_{j=0}^{K_N-1}\Pi_j\otimes V^j.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bw.36}
$$
The complete reference, initial state, charge, and pointer are
$$
R=R_0\otimes P,
\qquad
Q_R=Q_0\otimes I_P,
\qquad
\sigma_R=|\phi\rangle\langle\phi|\otimes|0\rangle_P\langle0|,
\qquad
M=I_{R_0}\otimes M_P.
\tag{M.6.13bw.37}
$$
Orthogonality and completeness of the projectors, and invariance of every $\Pi_j$, imply
$$
\begin{aligned}
U^*U=UU^*&=\sum_j\Pi_j\otimes I_P=I_{S\otimes R},\\
{[U,Q_S\otimes I_R+I_S\otimes Q_R]}&=0,
\qquad [M,Q_R]=0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bw.38}
$$
For $k=1,2$, the ready-state compression is exactly
$$
\begin{aligned}
{}_P\langle0|\,
U^*(I_{S\otimes R_0}\otimes M_P^k)U
\,|0\rangle_P
&=\sum_{j=0}^{K_N-1}\Pi_j\,
{}_P\langle0|V^{-j}M_P^kV^j|0\rangle_P\\
&=\sum_{j=0}^{K_N-1}b_j^k\Pi_j
=B_0^k.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bw.39}
$$
Thus this genuine complete apparatus has the same first and second induced moments as $B_0$.

The complete charge spectrum is exactly $\{0,1,\ldots,N-1\}$, every charge sector has degeneracy $K_N$, the complete reference dimension is $NK_N$, and the system-inclusive dimension is $2NK_N$, as asserted in (M.6.13bw.5). Its pointer norm is
$$
\|M\|=\|M_P\|=\max_{0\le i\le N-2}\ell_i\le1.
\tag{M.6.13bw.40}
$$
All pointer, ancillary, and readout capacities in this construction are included in these counts. No reflection direct sum or enlargement of the charged spectrum is needed.

The first moment is computed directly:
$$
\langle\phi|L|\phi\rangle
=\sum_{i=0}^{N-2}\ell_i\sqrt{p_ip_{i+1}}
=\sum_{i=0}^{N-2}\frac{2p_ip_{i+1}}{p_i+p_{i+1}}
=\mu_N.
\tag{M.6.13bw.41}
$$
The two second moments and their average are
$$
\begin{aligned}
\langle\phi|LL^*|\phi\rangle
&=\sum_{i=0}^{N-2}\ell_i^2p_{i+1},
&\langle\phi|L^*L|\phi\rangle
&=\sum_{i=0}^{N-2}\ell_i^2p_i,\\
\frac{\langle\phi|LL^*|\phi\rangle+
\langle\phi|L^*L|\phi\rangle}{2}
&=\sum_{i=0}^{N-2}\frac{\ell_i^2(p_i+p_{i+1})}{2}
=\sum_{i=0}^{N-2}\frac{2p_ip_{i+1}}{p_i+p_{i+1}}
=\mu_N.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bw.42}
$$
Reflection sends $p_i$ to $p_{N-1-i}$ and $\ell_i$ to $\ell_{N-2-i}$, exchanging the two second-moment sums. Their equality and their displayed average show that both equal $\mu_N$. Define the induced system moments using the actual complete measurement by
$$
E^{(k)}
=\operatorname{Tr}_R\!\left[
(I_S\otimes\sigma_R)U^*(I_S\otimes M^k)U\right],
\qquad k=1,2.
\tag{M.6.13bw.43}
$$
Equations (M.6.13bw.39)–(M.6.13bw.42) then give
$$
E^{(1)}=\mu_NX_S,
\qquad
E^{(2)}=\mu_NI_S.
\tag{M.6.13bw.44}
$$
Since $X_S^2=I_S$, the conditional noise-square operator is
$$
I_S-X_SE^{(1)}-E^{(1)}X_S+E^{(2)}
=(1-\mu_N)I_S.
\tag{M.6.13bw.45}
$$
Every system input has squared error $1-\mu_N$. Together with (M.6.13bw.17), this proves the minimum and its attainment in (M.6.13bw.4).

Equivalently, for this pure symmetric vector the function in (M.6.13bw.7) is
$$
F_\phi(t)
=\sum_{i=0}^{N-2}
\frac{p_ip_{i+1}}{t p_{i+1}+(1-t)p_i},
\qquad
F_\phi(t)=F_\phi(1-t),
\qquad
\min_{0\le t\le1}F_\phi(t)=F_\phi(1/2)=\mu_N.
\tag{M.6.13bw.46}
$$
Each reciprocal-affine summand is convex on $[0,1]$, and all denominators are positive. Reflection and convexity put the minimum at $1/2$. The explicit complete-apparatus moment calculation already establishes attainment independently of this observation.

For $N=1$, take $R=\mathbb C$, $Q_R=0$, the identity interaction, and the zero pointer. Its noise is $-X_S$, so
$$
\mu_1=0,
\qquad e_1^2=1,
\qquad K_1=1,
\qquad \dim R=1.
\tag{M.6.13bw.47}
$$
The universal lower bound applies because a one-vertex charge graph has no edge.

**Small exact cases.**

For $N=2$, the recurrence has no radical update. Its endpoint equations give $a=1/2$, $x_0=1/2$, and hence
$$
p^{(2)}=(1/2,1/2),
\qquad
\mu_2=\frac12,
\qquad
e_2^2=\frac12,
\qquad
\ell=(1),
\qquad K_2=3,
\qquad \dim R=6.
\tag{M.6.13bw.48}
$$
For $N=3$, reflection gives $x_1=1-x_0=a$, and the sole interior equation reduces to
$$
2(1-a)^2=a^2,
\qquad
a=2-\sqrt2,
\qquad
\frac{p_0}{p_1}=\frac{1-a}{a}=\frac1{\sqrt2}.
\tag{M.6.13bw.49}
$$
The other algebraic root is outside the admissible range. Normalizing the symmetric weights yields
$$
\begin{aligned}
p^{(3)}&=\left(1-\frac1{\sqrt2},\ \sqrt2-1,\ 1-\frac1{\sqrt2}\right),\\
\mu_3&=12-8\sqrt2,
\qquad e_3^2=8\sqrt2-11,
\qquad K_3=3,
\qquad \dim R=9.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bw.50}
$$
For $N=4$, reflection gives $x_1=1/2$, $x_0=1-a$, and $x_2=a$. The first interior equation becomes
$$
(1-a)^2+\frac14=a^2,
\qquad a=\frac58,
\qquad \frac{p_0}{p_1}=\frac35,
\qquad p_1=p_2.
\tag{M.6.13bw.51}
$$
Consequently,
$$
\begin{aligned}
p^{(4)}&=\frac1{16}(3,5,5,3),
&\mu_4&=\frac{25}{32},
&e_4^2&=\frac7{32},\\
\ell&=\left(\frac{\sqrt{15}}4,1,\frac{\sqrt{15}}4\right),
&K_4&=5,
&\dim R&=20.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bw.52}
$$
All dimensions in these examples are those of the exhibited complete reference, including its neutral pointer.

**Fixed finite spectra and longest unit-step runs.**

Fix a finite nonempty set $\Gamma\subset\mathbb R$. Define its longest consecutive unit-step run length by
$$
m(\Gamma)=\max\left\{m\ge1:
\{q_0,q_0+1,\ldots,q_0+m-1\}\subseteq\Gamma
\text{ for some }q_0\in\Gamma\right\}.
\tag{M.6.13bw.53}
$$
This is the largest component size in the unit-step graph on $\Gamma$. Every component of a spectrum contained in $\Gamma$ has at most $m(\Gamma)$ vertices. The component argument (M.6.13bw.16), convexity, and the original-apparatus lower bound therefore give
$$
\eta_{Q_R}(\sigma_R)\le\mu_{m(\Gamma)},
\qquad
\epsilon_\infty^2\ge1-\mu_{m(\Gamma)}
\qquad
\text{if }\operatorname{spec}Q_R\subseteq\Gamma.
\tag{M.6.13bw.54}
$$
For attainment, choose a longest run $q_0,q_0+1,\ldots,q_0+m-1$ with $m=m(\Gamma)$. Place $p^{(m)}$ on that run and use the same raising coefficients and neutral-pointer construction. Translating all reference charges on the run by $q_0$ changes neither $[Q_0,L]=L$ nor any measurement moment. When $m=1$, use $B_0=0$ and a one-level constant pointer.

If the complete spectrum is required to equal all of $\Gamma$, retain a basis vector for every unused charge. Put the reference state entirely on the selected run and set $B_0$ equal to zero on both system basis states above every unused charge sector. These vectors join the zero spectral projector; they are neither removed from the Hilbert space nor counted as occupied state mass. Tensor the entire reference with the neutral pointer. With one original basis vector per element of $\Gamma$, this construction has
$$
\operatorname{spec}Q_R=\Gamma,
\qquad
\dim R=|\Gamma|K_m,
\qquad
\dim(S\otimes R)=2|\Gamma|K_m,
\qquad
\epsilon_\infty^2=1-\mu_m.
\tag{M.6.13bw.55}
$$
Every retained charge sector has the counted finite pointer degeneracy $K_m$. The unused sectors have no effect on the two induced moments, so the attained optimum is $1-\mu_{m(\Gamma)}$ for both the contained-spectrum and exact-spectrum conventions. The architecture relevant to this error is the longest unit-step run; adding unrelated charge eigenvalues does not lengthen it.

**Exact error thresholds and endpoints.**

Let $0<\epsilon<1$ and $u=1-\epsilon^2\in(0,1)$. Necessity in (M.6.13bw.17) and attainment in (M.6.13bw.45) prove that error at most $\epsilon$ is possible under the cap $N$ exactly when $\mu_N\ge u$. The set in (M.6.13bw.6) is nonempty because $\mu_N\to1$, so its least integer is finite. Every eligible $N$ is at least two, since $\mu_1=0<u$.

The same condition suffices for exact error $\epsilon$. In the complete attaining apparatus for any eligible $N$, scale the pointer labels by
$$
s=1-\sqrt{1-\frac{u}{\mu_N}},
\qquad 0<s\le1.
\tag{M.6.13bw.56}
$$
This uses the nonnegative real square root and is well-defined because $0<u\le\mu_N$. Retain the same unitary, reference state, complete charge spectrum, and neutral pointer space, replacing $M_P$ by $sM_P$. Equivalently the compressed invariant observable replaces $L$ by $sL$. The first and second moments become
$$
E_s^{(1)}=s\mu_NX_S,
\qquad
E_s^{(2)}=s^2\mu_NI_S,
\qquad
I_S-X_SE_s^{(1)}-E_s^{(1)}X_S+E_s^{(2)}
=\bigl[1-\mu_N(2s-s^2)\bigr]I_S
=\epsilon^2I_S.
\tag{M.6.13bw.57}
$$
Thus the error is exactly $\epsilon$ for every input, establishing the equality of exact-error and at-most-error capacity thresholds. Because $s>0$ in the open interval, the $K_N$ displayed pointer labels remain distinct. At the optimum error for that $N$, $s=1$. At $\epsilon=1$, choose the one-dimensional reference with zero pointer instead; no division by $\mu_1$ is needed. At $\epsilon=0$, (M.6.13bw.24) and (M.6.13bw.17) exclude every finite $N$. With the convention that an impossible finite threshold is $+\infty$, the endpoint values are
$$
N_{\min}(1)=1,
\qquad
N_{\min}(0)=+\infty.
\tag{M.6.13bw.58}
$$
This completes all asserted existence, uniqueness, attainment, capacity, and endpoint claims. $\square$

**Scope.**

The theorem optimizes error under a bound on the number of distinct eigenvalues of the complete total reference charge, with arbitrary finite degeneracies allowed and actual pointer factors counted. The dimensions and pointer level counts above describe explicit witnesses; they are not minimum dimensions under a separate Hilbert-dimension or pointer-dimension constraint. The theorem imposes no pointer-norm or charge-variance bound on the optimizing class, although its witnesses have pointer norm at most one.

The exhibited initial reference is pure, and its natural-$\log$ asymmetry is
$$
\mathcal A_{Q_R}(\sigma_R)
=S(\mathcal G_{Q_R}\sigma_R)-S(\sigma_R)
=-\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}p_i^{(N)}\log p_i^{(N)}.
\tag{M.6.13bw.59}
$$
No assertion is made that this entropy is minimal at the attained error. Attainment at a fixed distinct-charge capacity therefore does not contradict Theorem M.6.13l's finite nonattainment of the different all-capacities entropy infimum at a fixed interior error. The result is confined to the registered qubit capacity problem and its fixed finite charge-spectrum version; it supplies no identification or realizability claim for physical charge or apparatus labels, no implementation-cost model, or physical or PPI closure.

<a id="theorem-m613bx-matching-multigap-entropy-frontier"></a>**Theorem M.6.13bx (Matching Multigap Entropy Frontier).** Let $Q_S$ and $A=A^*$ act on a finite-dimensional system, and let $A_{\mathrm{diag}}=\mathcal G_{Q_S}(A)$, where $\mathcal G_Q$ denotes spectral charge dephasing. Suppose that, in some orthonormal charge eigenbasis,
$$
\begin{aligned}
A&=A_{\mathrm{diag}}+\sum_{e\in E}
\left(a_e|l_e\rangle\langle h_e|+\overline{a_e}|h_e\rangle\langle l_e|\right),\\
Q_S|l_e\rangle&=q_e|l_e\rangle,\qquad
Q_S|h_e\rangle=(q_e+\Delta_e)|h_e\rangle,\qquad
\Delta_e>0,\quad a_e\ne0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bx.1}
$$
All vectors $\{|l_e\rangle,|h_e\rangle:e\in E\}$ are mutually orthogonal. Thus the charge-changing part is a literal disjoint matching: no basis vector occurs in two edges. The charge-commuting part $A_{\mathrm{diag}}$ is otherwise arbitrary. In particular it may mix different matching pairs within a degenerate charge eigenspace, need not preserve individual pairs, and need not commute with $A-A_{\mathrm{diag}}$.

Group edges by their distinct positive gaps $\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_m$, write $g(e)$ for the group of $e$, and define
$$
T_g=\sum_{e:g(e)=g}a_e|l_e\rangle\langle h_e|,
\qquad r_g=\|T_g\|=\max_{e:g(e)=g}|a_e|,
\qquad r_*=\max_g r_g.
\tag{M.6.13bx.2}
$$
The equality of norm and maximum amplitude uses the disjoint matching assumption. Set $r_*=0$ when $E$ is empty.

Use the complete finite measurement class of Theorems M.6.13f–M.6.13h: the reference has an arbitrary finite-dimensional Hermitian charge $Q_R$ with real spectrum and arbitrary degeneracies, an arbitrary input-independent state $\sigma_R$, a conserving unitary $U$, and a self-adjoint Yanase pointer $M$, with
$$
[U,Q_S\otimes I_R+I_S\otimes Q_R]=0,
\qquad [M,Q_R]=0,
\qquad B=U^*(I_S\otimes M)U.
\tag{M.6.13bx.3}
$$
All neutral ancillary factors, pointer factors, flags, and their correlations belong to the complete reference cut. Every system input is tested. No bound on reference dimension, charge variance, pointer norm, purity, or spectral multiplicity is imposed. With natural logarithms, put
$$
\begin{aligned}
N&=B-A\otimes I_R,
&\mathcal E_\sigma(Z)&=\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I_S\otimes\sigma_R)Z],\\
\epsilon_\infty(A)^2&=\|\mathcal E_\sigma(N^2)\|
=\sup_{\rho_S}\operatorname{Tr}\rho_S\mathcal E_\sigma(N^2),
&\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)&=S(\mathcal G_Q\sigma)-S(\sigma)
=D(\sigma\Vert\mathcal G_Q\sigma).
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bx.4}
$$
The conditional noise is positive, so its norm is its largest eigenvalue. Write $F_A^{\le}(\epsilon)$ and $F_A^{=}(\epsilon)$ for the infima of reference asymmetry at error at most $\epsilon$ and at error exactly $\epsilon$, respectively, over this complete finite class.

For each fixed $0<\epsilon<r_*$, let
$$
J(\epsilon)=\{g:r_g>\epsilon\},
\qquad u_g=1-\frac{\epsilon^2}{r_g^2}\in(0,1)\quad(g\in J(\epsilon)).
\tag{M.6.13bx.5}
$$
For the explicit additive formula assume only that the active distinct gaps are rationally independent:
$$
\sum_{g\in J(\epsilon)}k_g\Delta_g=0,\quad k_g\in\mathbb Z
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad k_g=0\text{ for every }g\in J(\epsilon).
\tag{M.6.13bx.6}
$$
Independence of all distinct target gaps is sufficient to apply the theorem at every interior error, but is stronger than necessary at a specified error. Define
$$
\begin{aligned}
I_0(\kappa)&=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}e^{\kappa\cos\theta}\,d\theta,
& I_1(\kappa)&=I_0'(\kappa),\\
\frac{I_1(\kappa(u))}{I_0(\kappa(u))}&=\sqrt u\quad(0<u<1),
&\Phi(u)&=\kappa(u)\sqrt u-\log I_0(\kappa(u)),\qquad \Phi(0)=0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bx.7}
$$
The positive root $\kappa(u)$ is unique. Then
$$
\boxed{F_A^{\le}(\epsilon)=F_A^{=}(\epsilon)
=\sum_{g\in J(\epsilon)}\Phi\!\left(1-\frac{\epsilon^2}{r_g^2}\right)}
\qquad(0<\epsilon<r_*).
\tag{M.6.13bx.8}
$$
Every individual finite admitted model with error at most $\epsilon$ has asymmetry strictly greater than this value. Finite conserving models with exact worst-case error $\epsilon$ approach the value. The strict assertion is pointwise in the finite model; it is not a dimension-uniform positive separation from the infimum.

The endpoints require no gap-independence assumption. If $r_*>0$, then
$$
\begin{aligned}
F_A^{\le}(\epsilon)=F_A^{=}(\epsilon)&=0
&&\text{for }\epsilon\ge r_*,\text{ with finite attainment},\\
F_A^{\le}(0)=F_A^{=}(0)&=+\infty
&&\text{because no finite zero-error model exists}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bx.9}
$$
The second line uses $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$. If $E$ is empty, $A$ commutes with $Q_S$ and both frontiers are zero, with finite attainment, at every prescribed nonnegative error.

There is also an exact operational reduction independent of rational independence. For every matching target and every $0<\epsilon<r_*$,
$$
\boxed{F_A^{\le}(\epsilon)=F_A^{=}(\epsilon)
=\inf_{\substack{Q,\sigma\ \mathrm{finite}\\
\eta_{\Delta_g}(\sigma)\ge u_g\ \text{for all }g\in J(\epsilon)}}
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma).}
\tag{M.6.13bx.10}
$$
The quantities $\eta_{\Delta}$ are defined below. Thus the joint constraint reduction applies to any distinct positive gaps. Only its evaluation as the additive expression (M.6.13bx.8) requires (M.6.13bx.6).

*Proof.*

**Gap quantities with support and degeneracy retained.**

Fix a finite reference $(Q,\sigma)$ and put $\tau=\mathcal G_Q\sigma$. Diagonalize $\tau$ within each original charge eigenspace, writing
$$
p_{q\alpha}=\langle q,\alpha|\tau|q,\alpha\rangle,
\qquad c_{q\alpha\beta}^{(\Delta)}
=\langle q+\Delta,\alpha|\sigma|q,\beta\rangle.
\tag{M.6.13bx.11}
$$
Sums below contain only existing sectors separated by $\Delta>0$, and terms with zero numerator and denominator are zero. For any raising matrix $[Q,L]=\Delta L$, define
$$
K_L=\frac{LL^*+L^*L}{2},\qquad H_L=L+L^*-K_L,
\qquad
\eta_\Delta(\sigma)=\sum_{q,\alpha,\beta}
