\frac{2|c_{q\alpha\beta}^{(\Delta)}|^2}{p_{q+\Delta,\alpha}+p_{q,\beta}}
=\max_{[Q,L]=\Delta L}\operatorname{Tr}\sigma H_L.
\tag{M.6.13bx.12}
$$
This is the gap-rescaled quantity of Theorem M.6.13h: replacing $Q$ by $Q/\Delta$ changes neither spectral dephasing nor support nor asymmetry. For direct verification, the entry $z=L_{q+\Delta,\alpha;q,\beta}$ contributes
$$
2\operatorname{Re}(\overline c z)-\frac{p_{q+\Delta,\alpha}+p_{q,\beta}}2|z|^2,
\qquad z_{\max}=\frac{2c}{p_{q+\Delta,\alpha}+p_{q,\beta}},
\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma L_{\max}
=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma K_{L_{\max}}=\eta_\Delta(\sigma)\in\mathbb R.
\tag{M.6.13bx.13}
$$
Indeed $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma L_{\max}$ is the sum of $2|c|^2/(p_{\mathrm{high}}+p_{\mathrm{low}})$, while the quadratic expectation has the same sum. Positivity implies $|\sigma_{ij}|^2\le\sigma_{ii}\sigma_{jj}$ in this basis, so every coherence incident to zero $\tau$-weight vanishes. Consequently $P=\operatorname{supp}\tau$ contains $\operatorname{supp}\sigma$, commutes with $Q$, and supports a maximizing $L$ for every gap simultaneously. No inverse on a zero-weight space is needed.

The maximizing operator is a contraction even with arbitrary charge degeneracies. For an adjacent block let $P_h=\sigma_{q+\Delta,q+\Delta}$, $P_l=\sigma_{q,q}$, and $C=\sigma_{q+\Delta,q}$. Positivity of the corresponding two-by-two block matrix gives $C=P_h^{1/2}VP_l^{1/2}$ with $\|V\|\le1$. On their supports the maximizing block is the Sylvester solution
$$
P_hL+LP_l=2C,
\qquad L=2\int_0^\infty e^{-sP_h}C e^{-sP_l}\,ds.
\tag{M.6.13bx.14}
$$
For arbitrary vectors $x,y$, Cauchy–Schwarz gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
|\langle x,Ly\rangle|
&\le2\left(\int_0^\infty\|P_h^{1/2}e^{-sP_h}x\|^2ds\right)^{1/2}
\left(\int_0^\infty\|P_l^{1/2}e^{-sP_l}y\|^2ds\right)^{1/2}\\
&\le\|x\|\,\|y\|.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bx.15}
$$
Each $\int$ is half the squared norm of the appropriate support projection. Distinct blocks at a fixed gap have orthogonal domains and orthogonal ranges; extending all blocks by zero therefore gives a contraction on the entire reference space. This proves an operator-norm bound, not merely entrywise bounds.

Taking $L=0$ proves $\eta_\Delta\ge0$. In fact $\eta_\Delta<1$ for every finite reference. Every finite positive-gap raising $L$ is nilpotent, since $[Q,L^n]=n\Delta L^n$ and $L^n=0$ once $n\Delta$ exceeds the diameter of $\operatorname{spec}Q$. Hence $I-L$ is invertible and
$$
I-H_L=\frac{(I-L)^*(I-L)+(I-L)(I-L)^*}{2}>0,
\qquad 1-\eta_\Delta(\sigma)=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(I-H_{L_{\max}})>0.
\tag{M.6.13bx.16}
$$
All these statements allow singular $\sigma$, degenerate charges, mixed or correlated neutral factors, and arbitrary finite real charge spectra.

**Simultaneous necessary constraints from one original apparatus.**

Let an admitted model have $\epsilon_\infty(A)\le\epsilon$. Its full Heisenberg pointer $B$ is invariant under total charge. For each group $g$ choose an edge $e$ with $|a_e|=r_g$, and let $P_e$ project onto $\operatorname{span}\{|l_e\rangle,|h_e\rangle\}$. It commutes with $Q_S$, including when its endpoint eigenspaces are degenerate. On the joint system-reference space, projection symbols below include the reference identity. For Hermitian $N$,
$$
P_eN^2P_e-(P_eNP_e)^2=P_eN(I-P_e)NP_e\ge0.
\tag{M.6.13bx.17}
$$
The map $\mathcal E_\sigma$ is positive and is a system bimodule map. Thus
$$
\mathcal E_\sigma[(P_eNP_e)^2]
\le P_e\mathcal E_\sigma(N^2)P_e
\le\epsilon^2P_e.
\tag{M.6.13bx.18}
$$
The leakage term has been bounded by its nonnegative contribution, rather than incorrectly identifying a compressed square with the square of a compression. The compressed target is
$$
P_eAP_e=\begin{pmatrix}\alpha_e&a_e\\\overline{a_e}&\beta_e\end{pmatrix}
\quad\text{in the ordered basis }(|l_e\rangle,|h_e\rangle).
\tag{M.6.13bx.19}
$$
Its diagonal part commutes with the compressed charge. Subtract it from $P_eBP_e$, divide by $r_g$, and rephase the two endpoint vectors to obtain target $X=|0\rangle\langle1|+|1\rangle\langle0|$ and an invariant qubit-reference observable with worst-case error at most $\epsilon/r_g$. Dividing total charge by $\Delta_g$ reduces the two system charges, up to an irrelevant scalar, to $0,1$ while leaving the reference state unchanged.

For completeness, the needed qubit implication can be seen directly. With $Z=|0\rangle\langle0|-|1\rangle\langle1|$, replace a Hermitian invariant qubit observable $C$ by $C'=(C-ZCZ)/2$. If $K=\mathcal E_\sigma[(C-X)^2]$, operator convexity of the square gives a conditional noise at most $(K+ZKZ)/2$, whose norm is at most $\|K\|$. The new observable has form $C'=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&L\\L^*&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with the appropriate raising relation, and its two noise eigenvalues are
$$
\begin{aligned}
k_0(L)&=1+\operatorname{Tr}\sigma LL^*-2\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}\sigma L,\\
k_1(L)&=1+\operatorname{Tr}\sigma L^*L-2\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}\sigma L,\\
\max\{k_0,k_1\}&\ge\frac{k_0+k_1}{2}
=1-\operatorname{Tr}\sigma H_L\ge1-\eta_\Delta(\sigma).
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bx.20}
$$
This bound applies to the invariant observable itself; a neutral-pointer dilation is available if an operational realization of the intermediate observable is wanted. Therefore the original, unchanged reference obeys all the constraints
$$
\eta_{\Delta_g}(\sigma_R)\ge1-\frac{\epsilon^2}{r_g^2}=u_g
\qquad(g\in J(\epsilon)).
\tag{M.6.13bx.21}
$$
These are simultaneous inequalities on one reference, not results of separately optimizing references for different edges. Compression remains valid when $A_{\mathrm{diag}}$ mixes a selected pair with other basis vectors; all such leakage was controlled in (M.6.13bx.17).

**Exact joint $\eta$ reduction without gap independence.**

Conversely, let a finite reference satisfy every constraint in (M.6.13bx.21), with no independence assumption on the gaps. Choose a supported maximizing $L_g$ for each active gap. Reflect and flag the entire reference once, using
$$
\widehat Q=Q\oplus(-Q),\qquad
\widehat\sigma=\frac{\sigma\oplus\sigma}{2},\qquad
\widehat L_g=L_g\oplus L_g^*.
\tag{M.6.13bx.22}
$$
Then $[\widehat Q,\widehat L_g]=\Delta_g\widehat L_g$ for every active $g$. The direct-sum flag is retained in the complete reference. The state has zero off-flag blocks; physical charge dephasing leaves them zero even if numerical charges coincide across summands. Hence the dephased state is $(\tau\oplus\tau)/2$, both entropies acquire the same $\log2$, and
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal A_{\widehat Q}(\widehat\sigma)&=\mathcal A_Q(\sigma),\\
\operatorname{Tr}\widehat\sigma\widehat L_g
&=\operatorname{Tr}\widehat\sigma\widehat L_g\widehat L_g^*
=\operatorname{Tr}\widehat\sigma\widehat L_g^*\widehat L_g
=\eta_{\Delta_g}(\sigma)=:\eta_g.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bx.23}
$$
The linear expectation is real by (M.6.13bx.13), and reflection averages the two quadratic expectations. Set
$$
s_g=1-\sqrt{1-u_g/\eta_g},\qquad
\widetilde L_g=s_g\widehat L_g\quad(g\in J(\epsilon)),
\qquad \widetilde L_g=0\quad(g\notin J(\epsilon)).
\tag{M.6.13bx.24}
$$
The denominator is positive on active groups. Both conditional squared deviations of $\widetilde L_g$ from the identity are exactly
$$
\operatorname{Tr}\widehat\sigma(\widetilde L_g-I)(\widetilde L_g^*-I)
=\operatorname{Tr}\widehat\sigma(\widetilde L_g^*-I)(\widetilde L_g-I)
=1-\eta_g(2s_g-s_g^2)=1-u_g.
\tag{M.6.13bx.25}
$$
Use all these operators in the single observable
$$
\widetilde B=A_{\mathrm{diag}}\otimes I+
\sum_{e\in E}\left(
 a_e|l_e\rangle\langle h_e|\otimes\widetilde L_{g(e)}
+\overline{a_e}|h_e\rangle\langle l_e|\otimes\widetilde L_{g(e)}^*
\right).
\tag{M.6.13bx.26}
$$
Every term has total charge increment zero. Subtracting $A\otimes I$ cancels the entire $A_{\mathrm{diag}}$ before squaring. Orthogonality of all matching endpoints makes every cross-edge product vanish. Consequently its conditional noise is
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal E_{\widehat\sigma}[(\widetilde B-A\otimes I)^2]
={}&\sum_{g\in J(\epsilon)}\sum_{e:g(e)=g}
|a_e|^2(1-u_g)(|l_e\rangle\langle l_e|+|h_e\rangle\langle h_e|)\\
&+\sum_{g\notin J(\epsilon)}\sum_{e:g(e)=g}
|a_e|^2(|l_e\rangle\langle l_e|+|h_e\rangle\langle h_e|).
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bx.27}
$$
All its eigenvalues are at most $\epsilon^2$, and a maximal-amplitude edge in any active group has eigenvalue $\epsilon^2$. The active set is nonempty, so its norm is exactly $\epsilon^2$. The whole-observable neutral-pointer dilation proved below realizes $\widetilde B$ in one original-class finite apparatus with unchanged asymmetry. This proves the upper direction in (M.6.13bx.10); (M.6.13bx.21) proves the other direction. Since exact-error models are a subset of at-most-error models and the construction has exact error, both infima agree. The argument changes the reference by one common reflection. It does not assert simultaneous attainability of the $\eta$ constraints on every fixed unreflected reference, nor does it require the maximizing $L_g$ to commute.

**General matrix circle lemma for an arbitrary Hermitian first argument.**

The tensorized lower proof requires a circle inequality with no charge-commutation condition on its Hermitian first argument. The graded statement of Theorem M.6.13k by itself is insufficient for that iteration. We prove the needed general lemma here. For any finite complex matrix $L$, arbitrary Hermitian $D$, and $\lambda\ge0$, set
$$
X=L+L^*,\qquad Y=i(L-L^*),\qquad
K=\frac{LL^*+L^*L}{2}=\frac{X^2+Y^2}{4},\qquad
\mathsf S(\lambda)=\sup_{r\ge0}e^{-\lambda r^2}I_0(2\lambda r).
\tag{M.6.13bx.28}
$$
Then
$$
\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}
\operatorname{Tr}\exp\!\left[D+\lambda\left(e^{i\theta}L+e^{-i\theta}L^*-K\right)\right]d\theta
\le\mathsf S(\lambda)\operatorname{Tr}e^D.
\tag{M.6.13bx.29}
$$
For $\lambda>0$ the inequality is strict whenever $L$ is nonnormal. At $\lambda=0$ equality is immediate. The constant is sharp even over scalar matrices: a scalar $L$ equal to a maximizing nonnegative radius, with scalar $D$, attains equality. Finiteness and attainment of that scalar maximum for $\lambda>0$ will also follow from the scalar analysis below.

For Hermitian $H,V$, Duhamel differentiation under the finite trace gives
$$
\left.\frac{d}{dz}\operatorname{Tr}e^{H+zV}\right|_{z=0}
=\operatorname{Tr}(e^HV),\qquad
\left.\frac{d^2}{dz^2}\operatorname{Tr}e^{H+zV}\right|_{z=0}
=\int_0^1\operatorname{Tr}(e^{(1-s)H}Ve^{sH}V)\,ds.
\tag{M.6.13bx.30}
$$
In an eigenbasis of $H$, with eigenvalues $h_i$, the second expression is

$$
\sum_{i,j}|V_{ij}|^2\int_0^1e^{(1-s)h_i+sh_j}ds.
$$

The scalar weighted arithmetic–geometric mean inequality, integrated in $s$, gives
$$
\int_0^1e^{(1-s)h_i+sh_j}ds\le\frac{e^{h_i}+e^{h_j}}2,
\qquad
\delta_H(V):=\operatorname{Tr}(e^HV^2)
-\int_0^1\operatorname{Tr}(e^{(1-s)H}Ve^{sH}V)ds\ge0.
\tag{M.6.13bx.31}
$$
The scalar inequality is strict when $h_i\ne h_j$. Since $V$ is Hermitian, its equality condition after summation is exactly $[H,V]=0$. This Hessian estimate is the same finite trace calculation used in M.6.13k, but has no commutation premise concerning $D$ or $K$.

Put
$$
\begin{aligned}
H(x,y,t)&=D+xX+yY-tK,\qquad F(x,y,t)=\operatorname{Tr}e^{H(x,y,t)},\\
R(x,y,t)&=\frac{\delta_{H(x,y,t)}(X)+\delta_{H(x,y,t)}(Y)}4,\\
\left(\partial_t+\frac14\Delta_{x,y}\right)F&=-R\le0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bx.32}
$$
Indeed $\partial_tF=-\operatorname{Tr}(e^HK)$ and the two Hessians sum to $\operatorname{Tr}e^H(X^2+Y^2)-4R$. This establishes the coefficient $1/4$ directly in Cartesian coordinates, including the origin. No radial invariance or commutation of $D$ with any charge is used.

For $\lambda>0$, let $B_t=(W_t^1,W_t^2)/\sqrt2$, with independent standard real Brownian motions, and let $T=\inf\{t\ge0:|B_t|=\lambda\}$. The generator is $\Delta/4$, and $|B_t|^2-t$ is a martingale. Bounded-time stopping gives
$$
\mathbb E(t\wedge T)=\mathbb E|B_{t\wedge T}|^2\le\lambda^2,
\qquad T<\infty\text{ a.s.},\qquad
\mathbb ET=\lambda^2,
\qquad T>0\text{ a.s.}
\tag{M.6.13bx.33}
$$
The first bound and monotone convergence show $\mathbb ET\le\lambda^2$ and almost sure finiteness. Path continuity then gives $|B_T|=\lambda$, and bounded convergence in the same identity proves equality of the mean. Continuity at the initial point proves strict positivity of $T$.

On the entire stopped disk and for all $t\ge0$,
$$
xX+yY=(x+iy)L+(x-iy)L^*,\qquad
\|xX+yY\|\le2\lambda\|L\|,\qquad
0<F(x,y,t)\le e^{2\lambda\|L\|}\operatorname{Tr}e^D.
\tag{M.6.13bx.34}
$$
Here $K\ge0$. We use monotonicity of the trace exponential in Hermitian Loewner order, justified by its nonnegative first derivative along a positive matrix increment. We do not assert operator monotonicity of the exponential. On any bounded time interval all derivatives on the closed disk are bounded, so Itô's formula and (M.6.13bx.32) give a zero-mean stopped stochastic $\int$ and
$$
\mathbb EF(B_{t\wedge T},t\wedge T)
=\operatorname{Tr}e^D-\mathbb E\int_0^{t\wedge T}R(B_s,s)ds,
\qquad
\mathbb EF(B_T,T)\le\operatorname{Tr}e^D.
\tag{M.6.13bx.35}
$$
The terminal inequality follows from almost sure finiteness of $T$ and the uniform bound (M.6.13bx.34). Thus stopping and passage to the limit use a bounded nonnegative supermartingale, with no unproved uniform-integrability condition at unbounded time.

Write $B_T=\lambda(\cos\Theta,\sin\Theta)$. Rotating the entire Brownian path preserves its law and $T$ and adds a constant to $\Theta$. For every Borel time set $E$, the finite circle measure $C\mapsto\mathbb P(T\in E,\Theta\in C)$ is therefore rotation invariant. Its total mass is $\mathbb P(T\in E)$, so
$$
\mathbb P(T\in E,\Theta\in C)
=\mathbb P(T\in E)\frac{|C|}{2\pi}.
\tag{M.6.13bx.36}
$$
This proves uniformity of the exit angle and its independence of the exit time.

The required exit-time transform is derived directly. For $v\ge0$, define on the disk
$$
h_v(z)=\frac{I_0(2\sqrt v\,|z|)}{I_0(2\sqrt v\,\lambda)},\qquad
\frac14\Delta h_v=vh_v,\qquad
h_v|_{|z|=\lambda}=1,\qquad 0<h_v\le1.
\tag{M.6.13bx.37}
$$
Smoothness and the differential equation at the origin follow from the power series $I_0(z)=\sum_{n\ge0}(z^2/4)^n/(n!)^2$. The bounded stopped process $e^{-v(t\wedge T)}h_v(B_{t\wedge T})$ is a martingale by Itô's formula. Passing to its almost surely finite terminal time gives
$$
\mathbb E e^{-vT}=h_v(0)=\frac1{I_0(2\lambda\sqrt v)}.
\tag{M.6.13bx.38}
$$
At $v=0$ this is $1=1$. Both the generator normalization and the reciprocal-$I_0$ transform have thus been checked without an external hitting-time convention.

For each fixed angle $\theta$ let
$$
f_\theta(t)=\operatorname{Tr}\exp\!\left[D+\lambda(\cos\theta X+\sin\theta Y)-tK\right]
=\int_{[0,\|K\|]}e^{-vt}\,d\mu_\theta(v),\qquad t\ge0.
\tag{M.6.13bx.39}
$$
The positive measure is supplied by Stahl's BMV theorem, for that single angle's arbitrary Hermitian first argument and the positive-semidefinite penalty $K$. The support is between the extreme eigenvalues of $K$, hence is contained in the indicated compact interval. Singular penalties and repeated eigenvalues are allowed. Only the identity for nonnegative $t$ is used. The primary source is Stahl (2013, Theorems 1–2 and support statement (1.15)).

From the definition of $\mathsf S$ and (M.6.13bx.38), pointwise for $v\ge0$,
$$
e^{-\lambda v}\le\frac{\mathsf S(\lambda)}{I_0(2\lambda\sqrt v)}
=\mathsf S(\lambda)\mathbb Ee^{-vT},
\qquad f_\theta(\lambda)\le\mathsf S(\lambda)\mathbb E f_\theta(T).
\tag{M.6.13bx.40}
$$
The latter follows by integration against the fixed positive measure $\mu_\theta$ and Tonelli. Now integrate this scalar inequality in $\theta$. The functions $f_\theta(t)$ are continuous in $(\theta,t)$ and bounded by (M.6.13bx.34), so ordinary Fubini and the independent uniform angle give
$$
\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}f_\theta(\lambda)d\theta
\le\mathsf S(\lambda)\mathbb EF(B_T,T)
\le\mathsf S(\lambda)\operatorname{Tr}e^D.
\tag{M.6.13bx.41}
$$
Since $\cos\theta X+\sin\theta Y=e^{i\theta}L+e^{-i\theta}L^*$, this is (M.6.13bx.29). No measurable selection or averaging of BMV measures is required: the comparison was proved for each fixed angle before continuous functions of the angle were integrated. In particular, no joint positive BMV measure has been assumed.

For strictness suppose $L$ is nonnormal. Then $[X,Y]=-2i[L,L^*]\ne0$, and for any fixed $s>0$,
$$
[H(B_s,s),Y]=[D-sK,Y]+B_s^x[X,Y].
\tag{M.6.13bx.42}
$$
The right side can vanish for at most one real value of $B_s^x$, which has a non-atomic Gaussian law. Thus $[H(B_s,s),Y]\ne0$ almost surely for each fixed positive $s$. The equality condition in (M.6.13bx.31) implies $R(B_s,s)>0$ almost surely. Because $T>0$ almost surely, $\mathbb P(T>s)>0$ for all sufficiently small positive $s$. For every $t>0$, Tonelli therefore gives
$$
\mathbb E\int_0^{t\wedge T}R(B_s,s)ds
=\int_0^t\mathbb E[\mathbf1_{\{s<T\}}R(B_s,s)]ds>0,
\qquad
\mathbb EF(B_T,T)<\operatorname{Tr}e^D.
\tag{M.6.13bx.43}
$$
For the final strict inequality first use (M.6.13bx.35) at a fixed positive horizon and then the supermartingale property and bounded terminal limit. Multiplication by the finite positive $\mathsf S(\lambda)$ in (M.6.13bx.41) proves strictness of (M.6.13bx.29). This proof applies to arbitrary $D$ and uses no killed-transition-density estimate or charge grading of $D$.

**Global scalar dual and its domain.**

Write $c(\kappa)=I_1(\kappa)/I_0(\kappa)$. Its derivative is the strictly positive variance of $\cos\theta$ under density proportional to $e^{\kappa\cos\theta}$, so $c$ is strictly increasing, $c(0)=0$, and $0<c(\kappa)<1$ for $\kappa>0$. Also $c(\kappa)\to1$: for any $\delta>0$, compare the $\int$ on $\cos\theta\le1-\delta$ with that on a positive-length arc where $\cos\theta\ge1-\delta/2$. The former probability is bounded by a constant times $e^{-\kappa\delta/2}$. This proves existence and uniqueness of $\kappa(u)$ in (M.6.13bx.7).

The positive power series give, with $x=\kappa^2/4$,
$$
p_n(x)=\frac{x^n/(n!)^2}{\sum_{j\ge0}x^j/(j!)^2},\qquad
\frac{c(\kappa)}\kappa=\frac12\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{p_n(x)}{n+1},\qquad
\frac{d}{dx}\frac{c(\kappa)}\kappa
=\frac1{2x}\operatorname{Cov}_{p(x)}\!\left(n,\frac1{n+1}\right)<0.
\tag{M.6.13bx.44}
$$
Strict negativity follows from two independent copies $J,N$ of this distribution: twice the covariance is the expectation of $(N-J)((N+1)^{-1}-(J+1)^{-1})$, nonpositive everywhere and negative with positive probability. Thus $c(\kappa)/\kappa$ strictly decreases from $1/2$ to $0$; the first limit is the constant-term ratio and the second follows from $c<1$.

For $g_\lambda(r)=\log I_0(2\lambda r)-\lambda r^2$,
$$
g_\lambda'(r)=2\lambda[c(2\lambda r)-r]
=2\lambda r\left[2\lambda\frac{c(2\lambda r)}{2\lambda r}-1\right],
\qquad
g_\lambda(r)\le-\lambda(r-1)^2+\lambda.
\tag{M.6.13bx.45}
$$
For $0<\lambda\le1$ the first derivative is strictly negative at $r>0$, and the unique maximizer is $r=0$, so $\mathsf S(\lambda)=1$. At $\lambda=0$, $\mathsf S(0)=1$ and every radius maximizes. For $\lambda>1$, the bracket decreases strictly from $\lambda-1>0$ to a negative value and is already negative at $r=1$. There is exactly one positive critical radius; it lies in $(0,1)$ and is the unique global maximum. The upper bound in (M.6.13bx.45) proves finiteness and controls the unbounded radial domain. Thus the same $\mathsf S$ is obtained by taking the supremum over $0\le r\le1$.

For fixed $0<u<1$, set $r=\sqrt u$, $\kappa=\kappa(u)$, and $\lambda_*(u)=\kappa/(2r)>1$. The strict inequality follows from $c(\kappa)/\kappa<1/2$. The radius $r$ is the unique global maximizer of $g_{\lambda_*}$, so
$$
\log\mathsf S(\lambda_*)=\log I_0(\kappa)-\lambda_*u,
\qquad \lambda_*u-\log\mathsf S(\lambda_*)=\Phi(u).
\tag{M.6.13bx.46}
$$
For any $\lambda\ge0$, evaluate the radial supremum at $r$ and then maximize $k r-\log I_0(k)$ in $k\ge0$. Its derivative is $r-c(k)$ and changes sign exactly at $\kappa$, whence
$$
\lambda u-\log\mathsf S(\lambda)
\le2\lambda u-\log I_0(2\lambda r)
\le\kappa r-\log I_0(\kappa)=\Phi(u).
\tag{M.6.13bx.47}
$$
Together these prove the global dual identity and monotonicity properties
$$
\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\{\lambda u-\log\mathsf S(\lambda)\}=\Phi(u),
\qquad \Phi'(u)=\frac{\kappa(u)}{2\sqrt u}=\lambda_*(u)>0
\quad(0<u<1).
\tag{M.6.13bx.48}
$$
The derivative is strictly increasing because $c(\kappa)/\kappa$ decreases, so $\Phi$ is strictly convex on $(0,1)$. The power series at zero give the continuous extension $\Phi(0)=0$. At $u=0$ the dual is zero since $\mathsf S(\lambda)\ge1$ and $\lambda=0$ attains zero. These arguments establish a global scalar maximization, rather than relying on a stationary equation alone.

**Tensorization from one physical charge.**

Let $Q,D$ be finite Hermitian matrices satisfying $[Q,D]=0$, and let $[Q,L_g]=\Delta_gL_g$ for a rationally independent selected set of positive gaps $g=1,\ldots,s$. No commutation among the $L_g$ is assumed. For $\lambda_g\ge0$, define
$$
Z(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_s)
=\operatorname{Tr}\exp\!\left[D+\sum_{g=1}^s\lambda_g
\left(e^{i\theta_g}L_g+e^{-i\theta_g}L_g^*-K_{L_g}\right)\right].
\tag{M.6.13bx.49}
$$
Each $K_{L_g}$ commutes with $Q$. Conjugation by $e^{\mathrm{itQ}}$ therefore gives
$$
Z(\theta+t\Delta)=Z(\theta)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),
\qquad \Delta=(\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_s).
\tag{M.6.13bx.50}
$$
The continuous-time subgroup $t\mapsto(e^{it\Delta_1},\ldots,e^{it\Delta_s})$ is dense in the full $s$-torus. Indeed a proper closed subgroup has a nontrivial annihilating integer character; such a character here would require $e^{it\sum_gk_g\Delta_g}=1$ for every real $t$, hence $\sum_gk_g\Delta_g=0$, contrary to independence. There is no requirement of additional independence from the number $1$. Continuity of $Z$ thus makes it constant on the full torus, and
$$
Z(0)=\int_{[0,2\pi]^s}Z(\theta)\prod_{g=1}^s\frac{d\theta_g}{2\pi}.
\tag{M.6.13bx.51}
$$
For the first angular $\int$ apply (M.6.13bx.29) with $L=L_1$ and arbitrary Hermitian first argument
$$
D_1=D+\sum_{g=2}^s\lambda_g
\left(e^{i\theta_g}L_g+e^{-i\theta_g}L_g^*-K_{L_g}\right).
\tag{M.6.13bx.52}
$$
Neither $[Q,D_1]=0$ nor commutation of $D_1$ with $L_1$ or $K_{L_1}$ is generally true or needed. Integrating the remaining continuous functions on the compact torus and repeating yields
$$
\operatorname{Tr}\exp\!\left[D+\sum_{g=1}^s\lambda_gH_{L_g}\right]
\le\left(\prod_{g=1}^s\mathsf S(\lambda_g)\right)\operatorname{Tr}e^D.
\tag{M.6.13bx.53}
$$
If some $\lambda_g>0$ and $L_g\ne0$, take that index first. It is nilpotent by its positive-gap raising relation and therefore nonnormal, because a normal nilpotent finite matrix is zero. The circle inequality is strict for each fixed choice of the remaining angles. The difference of its right and left sides is a continuous strictly positive function on their compact torus, with strictly positive $\int$. The remaining non-strict estimates preserve strictness, so (M.6.13bx.53) is strict in that case.

This calculation averages a trace already supplied by the original single-charge system. It does not postulate a physical torus reference, independent symmetry generators, commuting raising matrices, or a multivariable BMV measure.

**Entropy lower bound and finite nonattainment.**

For any finite reference, let $\tau=\mathcal G_Q\sigma$ and restrict to the single support $P=\operatorname{supp}\tau$. On this finite space $\tau$ is faithful, $D=\log\tau$ is Hermitian and commutes with the restricted charge, and all supported maximizing $L_g$ retain their raising relations. The restriction loses neither $\sigma$ nor any gap coherence. With a rationally independent selected gap set put
$$
Z_{\boldsymbol\lambda}
=\operatorname{Tr}\exp\!\left[\log\tau+\sum_g\lambda_gH_{L_g}\right],
\qquad
\omega_{\boldsymbol\lambda}
=Z_{\boldsymbol\lambda}^{-1}\exp\!\left[\log\tau+\sum_g\lambda_gH_{L_g}\right].
\tag{M.6.13bx.54}
$$
Both $\omega_{\boldsymbol\lambda}$ and $\tau$ are faithful on $P$, so singular $\sigma$ causes no difficulty. Substituting the logarithm of $\omega_{\boldsymbol\lambda}$ into relative entropy gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)
&=D(\sigma\Vert\omega_{\boldsymbol\lambda})
+\sum_g\lambda_g\eta_{\Delta_g}(\sigma)-\log Z_{\boldsymbol\lambda}\\
&\ge\sum_g\lambda_g\eta_{\Delta_g}(\sigma)-\log Z_{\boldsymbol\lambda}\\
&\ge\sum_g\left[\lambda_g\eta_{\Delta_g}(\sigma)-\log\mathsf S(\lambda_g)\right].
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bx.55}
$$
The last line uses (M.6.13bx.53) and $\operatorname{Tr}\tau=1$. It is strict whenever a selected $\eta_{\Delta_g}>0$ has $\lambda_g>0$, since its maximizing $L_g$ is nonzero.

Each finite $\eta$ lies in $[0,1)$ by (M.6.13bx.16). For each positive $\eta$ choose its optimizing multiplier from (M.6.13bx.48), and assign zero multiplier to $\eta$ zero. This proves the state-only result
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge\sum_{g=1}^s\Phi(\eta_{\Delta_g}(\sigma)),
\quad\text{strictly if at least one selected eta is positive}.
\tag{M.6.13bx.56}
$$
This state inequality needs no matching assumption. For the measurement target, apply (M.6.13bx.55) only to the active gaps, use their simultaneous constraints (M.6.13bx.21), and take $\lambda_g=\lambda_*(u_g)>0$. Since the active set is nonempty,
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma) >\sum_{g\in J(\epsilon)}\left[\lambda_g u_g-\log\mathsf S(\lambda_g)\right]
=\sum_{g\in J(\epsilon)}\Phi(u_g).
\tag{M.6.13bx.57}
$$
This proves the lower half of (M.6.13bx.8) and strict nonattainment by every finite admitted apparatus, including arbitrary correlated references and charge degeneracies.

**Independent lower proof by coordinate dephasing and data processing.**

A second proof of the additive entropy bound uses only the one-gap consequence of the circle lemma and commuting dephasing channels. It does not use (M.6.13bx.53). Fix rationally independent positive selected gaps $\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_s$ and define their free abelian subgroup
$$
\Gamma=\left\{\sum_{g=1}^sn_g\Delta_g:n\in\mathbb Z^s\right\},
\qquad q\sim q'\iff q-q'\in\Gamma.
\tag{M.6.13bx.58}
$$
Partition the finite spectrum of $Q$ into represented cosets. Choose one representative $b_c$ in each such coset. Independence supplies unique integer coordinates for every represented charge,
$$
q=b_c+\sum_{g=1}^sn_g(q)\Delta_g.
\tag{M.6.13bx.59}
$$
The coordinates can be negative; they need not populate a rectangular lattice; different cosets may use the same integer tuple. Each whole original charge eigenspace, with all its degeneracy, is assigned the same coordinates.

Let $P_c$ sum the original charge projections in coset $c$ and pinch first in these cosets:
$$
\sigma^0=\mathcal C(\sigma)=\sum_cP_c\sigma P_c,
\qquad\mathcal C(\tau)=\tau,
\qquad
D(\sigma\Vert\tau)\ge D(\sigma^0\Vert\tau)=\mathcal A_Q(\sigma^0).
\tag{M.6.13bx.60}
$$
The inequality is relative-entropy data processing. This pinching preserves every original coherence separated by any selected $\Delta_g$, because its two endpoints belong to the same coset; it also preserves $\tau$. Define commuting Hermitian coordinate operators and their dephasings on the same finite Hilbert space by
$$
Q_g=\sum_{q\in\operatorname{spec}Q}n_g(q)P_q,
\qquad\mathcal T_g=\mathcal G_{Q_g},
\qquad \mathcal T_1\cdots\mathcal T_s(\sigma^0)=\tau.
\tag{M.6.13bx.61}
$$
All $\mathcal T_g$ commute, are idempotent, and commute with $\mathcal C$, because all are spectral pinchings in compatible diagonal decompositions. After $\mathcal C$ removes cross-coset coherences, equality of all coordinates is equivalent to equality of original charge. This proves the last identity despite missing grid points or repeated coordinate tuples across cosets. These $Q_g$ are mathematical devices on the same space, without a tensor factorization, additional physical conservation law, or new apparatus resource.

Set
$$
\sigma^{(g)}=\left(\prod_{h\ne g}\mathcal T_h\right)(\sigma^0),
\qquad\mathcal T_g(\sigma^{(g)})=\tau,
\qquad
\eta_{Q_g,\,1}(\sigma^{(g)})=\eta_{Q,\,\Delta_g}(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13bx.62}
$$
To verify the last equality, choose the common basis diagonalizing $\tau$ inside each original charge block. An entry surviving in $\sigma^{(g)}$ has endpoints in one coset and equal coordinates $n_h$ for all $h\ne g$. Its increment in $Q_g$ is one precisely when its original charge increment is $\Delta_g$. Conversely an original $\Delta_g$ coherence has exactly those coordinate differences and survives. Thus every relevant numerator in (M.6.13bx.12) is preserved. Since $\mathcal T_g\sigma^{(g)}=\tau$, the same basis is also a valid diagonalization of $\tau$ inside the potentially larger $Q_g$ eigenspaces, so every denominator agrees. Extra coordinate degeneracies create no spurious contributions: off-coset entries and entries with different other coordinates are zero. Zero denominators remain zero under the same support convention.

For the entropy comparison define $\rho_0=\sigma^0$ and $\rho_j=\mathcal T_j\cdots\mathcal T_1(\sigma^0)$, so $\rho_s=\tau$. Every state is supported in $P=\operatorname{supp}\tau$. It is also supported in the support of its own pinching; hence all pinching relative-entropy identities below are finite. Since the logarithm of a pinched state lies in the pinching algebra, $D(\rho\Vert\mathcal T\rho)=S(\mathcal T\rho)-S(\rho)$. Therefore
$$
D(\sigma^0\Vert\tau)
=\sum_{j=1}^s[S(\rho_j)-S(\rho_{j-1})]
=\sum_{j=1}^sD(\rho_{j-1}\Vert\mathcal T_j\rho_{j-1}).
\tag{M.6.13bx.63}
$$
Apply data processing to the $j$th summand with the remaining channel $\mathcal E_j=\mathcal T_s\cdots\mathcal T_{j+1}$, taking $\mathcal E_s$ to be the identity. Commutation and idempotence give the exact images and inequality direction
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal E_j(\rho_{j-1})&=\sigma^{(j)},&
\mathcal E_j(\mathcal T_j\rho_{j-1})&=\tau,\\
D(\rho_{j-1}\Vert\mathcal T_j\rho_{j-1})
&\ge D(\sigma^{(j)}\Vert\tau).
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bx.64}
$$
Summing gives
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)
\ge D(\sigma^0\Vert\tau)
\ge\sum_{j=1}^sD(\sigma^{(j)}\Vert\tau)
=\sum_{j=1}^s\mathcal A_{Q_j}(\sigma^{(j)}).
\tag{M.6.13bx.65}
$$
For each summand use the one-gap supported Gibbs proof: charge conjugation makes the single-angle trace constant, (M.6.13bx.29) bounds its partition function, and (M.6.13bx.48) gives $\mathcal A_{Q_j}(\sigma^{(j)})\ge\Phi(\eta_{Q_j,1}(\sigma^{(j)}))$, strictly when its $\eta$ is positive. This is the $s=1$ argument and does not rely on tensorization. Equations (M.6.13bx.62) and (M.6.13bx.65) yield (M.6.13bx.56), including its strictness. The simultaneous measurement constraints then give (M.6.13bx.57).

This alternative proof explicitly handles cross-coset coherences, incomplete charge lattices, negative coordinates, all original or coordinate degeneracies, singular states, and correlated neutral factors. No flag has been discarded from resource accounting. Its entropy inequality follows from an ordered telescoping sum and ordinary data processing with identified images, not an assumed general quantum entropy-submodularity assertion.

**Product Fourier witnesses and the exact all-input noise operator.**

Assume now the active gaps satisfy (M.6.13bx.6). For each $g\in J(\epsilon)$ put $\delta_g=\epsilon/r_g\in(0,1)$ and choose an integer $N_g\ge3$ with $N_g>1/\delta_g^2$. On one reference factor for that distinct active gap define
$$
\begin{aligned}
Q_{N_g}&=\sum_{n=0}^{N_g-1}n|n\rangle\langle n|,
&\theta_{gj}&=\frac{2\pi j}{N_g},\\
|\theta_{gj}\rangle&=N_g^{-1/2}\sum_{n=0}^{N_g-1}e^{in\theta_{gj}}|n\rangle,
&Z_{N_g}(\kappa)&=\sum_{j=0}^{N_g-1}e^{\kappa\cos\theta_{gj}},\\
w_{gj}(\kappa)&=\frac{e^{\kappa\cos\theta_{gj}}}{Z_{N_g}(\kappa)},
&\sigma_g&=\sum_{j=0}^{N_g-1}w_{gj}(\kappa_g)|\theta_{gj}\rangle\langle\theta_{gj}|,\\
c_{N_g}(\kappa)&=\sum_{j=0}^{N_g-1}w_{gj}(\kappa)\cos\theta_{gj}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bx.66}
$$
The Fourier vectors are orthonormal; the charge diagonal of $\sigma_g$ is $I_{N_g}/N_g$. Symmetry $j\mapsto N_g-j$ removes the imaginary part of its adjacent coherence. The discrete cosine mean starts at zero, tends to one as $\kappa\to\infty$, and has strictly positive derivative equal to the variance of the nonconstant discrete cosine values at every finite $\kappa$. The strict dimension condition says $u_g<1-1/N_g$. Therefore there is a unique finite $\kappa_g>0$ such that, writing $c_g=c_{N_g}(\kappa_g)$,
$$
\left(1-\frac1{N_g}\right)c_g^2=u_g,
\qquad L_g^{\mathrm{loc}}=c_g\sum_{n=0}^{N_g-2}|n+1\rangle\langle n|.
\tag{M.6.13bx.67}
$$
Use the single product reference
$$
\mathcal H_R=\bigotimes_{g\in J(\epsilon)}\mathbb C^{N_g},\qquad
Q_R=\sum_{g\in J(\epsilon)}\Delta_gQ_{N_g}^{(g)},\qquad
\sigma_R=\bigotimes_{g\in J(\epsilon)}\sigma_g.
\tag{M.6.13bx.68}
$$
Here superscript $(g)$ means the local operator tensored with identities on every other factor. Let $L_g=(L_g^{\mathrm{loc}})^{(g)}$ for active groups and $L_g=0$ on this same reference for inactive groups. There is precisely one Fourier factor for each distinct active gap, irrespective of the number of matching edges with that gap. Direct calculation of flat diagonal and adjacent coherence gives
$$
[Q_R,L_g]=\Delta_gL_g,
\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_RL_g
=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_RL_gL_g^*
=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_RL_g^*L_g
=\frac{N_g-1}{N_g}c_g^2=u_g
\quad(g\in J(\epsilon)).
\tag{M.6.13bx.69}
$$
For example the linear expectation sums $N_g-1$ adjacent entries $c_g/N_g$, each multiplied by $c_g$, and both quadratic expectations sum $N_g-1$ equal diagonal weights $c_g^2/N_g$.

Define one Hermitian observable on the entire system and reference:
$$
B=A_{\mathrm{diag}}\otimes I_R+
\sum_{e\in E}\left(
 a_e|l_e\rangle\langle h_e|\otimes L_{g(e)}
+\overline{a_e}|h_e\rangle\langle l_e|\otimes L_{g(e)}^*
\right),\qquad [B,Q_S+Q_R]=0.
\tag{M.6.13bx.70}
$$
The notation $Q_S+Q_R$ includes the appropriate identity tensors. Subtraction gives
$$
N=B-A\otimes I_R
=\sum_{e\in E}\left(
 a_e|l_e\rangle\langle h_e|\otimes(L_{g(e)}-I_R)
+\overline{a_e}|h_e\rangle\langle l_e|\otimes(L_{g(e)}^*-I_R)
\right).
\tag{M.6.13bx.71}
$$
All of $A_{\mathrm{diag}}$ cancels before squaring. Matching orthogonality eliminates every product involving two different edges, even for reference operators that do not commute. Substituting (M.6.13bx.69) therefore yields the exact operator identity
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal E_\sigma(N^2)
={}&\sum_{g\in J(\epsilon)}\sum_{e:g(e)=g}
|a_e|^2\frac{\epsilon^2}{r_g^2}
\left(|l_e\rangle\langle l_e|+|h_e\rangle\langle h_e|\right)\\
&+\sum_{g\notin J(\epsilon)}\sum_{e:g(e)=g}
|a_e|^2\left(|l_e\rangle\langle l_e|+|h_e\rangle\langle h_e|\right),
\qquad \|\mathcal E_\sigma(N^2)\|=\epsilon^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bx.72}
$$
It is zero on unmatched system vectors. Each displayed eigenvalue is at most $\epsilon^2$, with equality on a maximal-amplitude edge in each active group. Hence every system input has squared error at most $\epsilon^2$, and the supremum over all inputs is exactly $\epsilon^2$. This includes coherent superpositions across pairs and inputs mixed by $A_{\mathrm{diag}}$. It does not say that every input has error exactly $\epsilon$: unmatched vectors and smaller-amplitude edges can have strictly smaller error.

**One neutral pointer dilation of the whole observable.**

To implement any of the single invariant observables used above, including the full $B$ in (M.6.13bx.70), diagonalize the whole observable as
$$
B=\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}b_j\Pi_j,\qquad
[\Pi_j,Q_S+Q_R]=0.
\tag{M.6.13bx.73}
$$
Here $K=|\operatorname{spec}B|$ is the number of distinct eigenvalues of the whole $B$, and the $\Pi_j$ are their full spectral projections. Append one neutral $K$-dimensional pointer $P$ in ready state $|0\rangle_P$, let $V|j\rangle=|j+1\pmod K\rangle$, and put
$$
\begin{aligned}
U&=\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}\Pi_j\otimes V^j,
&M_P&=\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}b_j|j\rangle\langle j|,\\
Q_{R,\mathrm{complete}}&=Q_R\otimes I_P,
&\sigma_{R,\mathrm{complete}}&=\sigma_R\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|_P,
& M_{\mathrm{complete}}&=I_R\otimes M_P.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bx.74}
$$
Orthogonality and completeness of the $\Pi_j$ make $U$ unitary, and their charge commutation makes it conserve total charge. The complete pointer commutes with the complete reference charge. Its ready-state compressed moments satisfy
$$
{}_P\langle0|U^*(I_{SR}\otimes M_P^k)U|0\rangle_P=B^k
\qquad(k=1,2).
\tag{M.6.13bx.75}
$$
These identities reproduce the full noise moment: the second pointer moment gives $B^2$, the cross terms with $A$ use the first moment $B$, and the target-square term is unchanged. Thus the actual Heisenberg pointer in the enlarged apparatus has precisely the conditional noise (M.6.13bx.72), or (M.6.13bx.27) in the reflection construction. The pure neutral ready state contributes zero to both entropies, so
$$
\mathcal A_{Q_R\otimes I_P}(\sigma_R\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|)
=\mathcal A_{Q_R}(\sigma_R).
\tag{M.6.13bx.76}
$$
For the product Fourier witness the complete reference has dimension $K\prod_{g\in J(\epsilon)}N_g$, including the neutral pointer of dimension $K$; this is an explicit finite construction and makes no minimal-dimension claim. The pointer is counted in the complete reference, rather than removed from the model. This is one conserving measurement of the whole $B$, including all of $A_{\mathrm{diag}}$. No separate pairwise measurements, preliminary pair identification, system dephasing, or uncounted reference factors are used. The same construction also justifies the invariant-observable uses in the exact operational reduction and endpoints.

**Entropy of the finite witnesses and the limiting value.**

Rational independence of the active gaps makes the product charge labels $\sum_g\Delta_g n_g$ distinct for distinct integer tuples. Therefore physical dephasing by the single $Q_R$ of (M.6.13bx.68) is, on this product state,
$$
\mathcal G_{Q_R}(\sigma_R)
=\bigotimes_{g\in J(\epsilon)}\frac{I_{N_g}}{N_g}.
\tag{M.6.13bx.77}
$$
The equality follows from the chosen finite charge spectrum; it was not postulated as product dephasing in the lower proof. Since the Fourier eigenvalues of $\sigma_g$ are $w_{gj}$, exact entropy addition gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal A_{Q_R}(\sigma_R)
&=\sum_{g\in J(\epsilon)}[\log N_g-S(\sigma_g)]\\
&=\sum_{g\in J(\epsilon)}
\left[\kappa_gc_g-
\log\left(\frac1{N_g}\sum_{j=0}^{N_g-1}e^{\kappa_g\cos\theta_{gj}}\right)\right].
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bx.78}
$$
The neutral pointer leaves this unchanged by (M.6.13bx.76).

Let all $N_g\to\infty$ along integers obeying the strict dimension conditions. There are finitely many active gaps, so independent sequences or one sufficiently large common increasing integer both suffice. The Riemann sums for $N^{-1}Z_N(\kappa)$ and its derivative converge locally uniformly in $\kappa$ to $I_0(\kappa)$ and $I_1(\kappa)$. Consequently $c_N\to c$ locally uniformly. The tuning condition gives $c_g=\sqrt{u_g/(1-1/N_g)}\to\sqrt{u_g}$. Strict increase of $c$ brackets each tuned $\kappa_g$ between fixed points on either side of $\kappa(u_g)$ for all sufficiently large $N_g$, and shrinking this bracket proves
$$
\kappa_g\longrightarrow\kappa(u_g),\qquad
c_g\longrightarrow\sqrt{u_g},\qquad
\mathcal A_{Q_R}(\sigma_R)
\longrightarrow\sum_{g\in J(\epsilon)}\Phi(u_g).
\tag{M.6.13bx.79}
$$
Every member of the sequence is a finite original-class apparatus with exact worst-case error $\epsilon$, not merely an error converging to $\epsilon$. This proves the upper half of (M.6.13bx.8). Together with (M.6.13bx.57), it establishes equality of the infima and strict finite nonattainment at every stated interior error.

**Endpoints and the exact zero-resource distance.**

Let $A_{\mathrm{off}}=A-A_{\mathrm{diag}}$. By matching orthogonality it is a direct sum of Hermitian two-by-two matrices with eigenvalues $\pm|a_e|$ and zero unmatched blocks. Hence
$$
\|A_{\mathrm{off}}\|=r_*,\qquad
 d_{Q_S}(A):=\inf_{\substack{C=C^*\\ {[C,Q_S]=0}}}\|A-C\|=r_*.
\tag{M.6.13bx.80}
$$
For the lower bound on distance, compress $A-C$ to a maximal-amplitude edge. Its off-diagonal entry is $a_e$, since the endpoint charges differ and $C$ commutes with charge. The norm of this compression is at least the modulus of that matrix entry, namely $r_*$. The reverse bound is attained by $C=A_{\mathrm{diag}}$. This proof allows arbitrary mixing by $A_{\mathrm{diag}}$ within degenerate eigenspaces.

For $r_*>0$, the invariant system-only observable $B=A_{\mathrm{diag}}$ has exact error $r_*$ and a zero-asymmetry neutral-pointer realization. For any $\epsilon\ge r_*$ set
$$
B=A_{\mathrm{diag}}+tI_S,\qquad t=\epsilon-r_*\ge0,
\qquad \|B-A\|=\|tI_S-A_{\mathrm{off}}\|=t+r_*=\epsilon.
\tag{M.6.13bx.81}
$$
The last equality uses an eigenvalue $-r_*$ of $A_{\mathrm{off}}$. The neutral-pointer realization has zero asymmetry and exact prescribed error. The at-most frontier is already attained by $B=A_{\mathrm{diag}}$. Nonnegativity of asymmetry proves the zero values in (M.6.13bx.9).

At zero error, any nonzero edge and the compression argument would force $\eta_{\Delta_e}(\sigma_R)\ge1$, contrary to (M.6.13bx.16). Thus finite zero-error infeasibility holds throughout the original apparatus class, without any independence assumption and not just for the Fourier witnesses. If $E$ is empty, take instead the invariant observable $B=A+tI_S$: its error is $|t|$ and its neutral-pointer implementation has zero asymmetry. This covers every nonnegative error for the commuting target and avoids a maximum over an empty edge set. The theorem follows. $\square$

**Nonvacuity and boundaries of the theorem.**

A concrete target with three distinct charge eigenvalues has basis $(|0,a\rangle,|0,b\rangle,|1\rangle,|\sqrt2\rangle)$ and
$$
\begin{aligned}
Q_S&=\operatorname{diag}(0,0,1,\sqrt2),\\
A-A_{\mathrm{diag}}
&=r_1|0,a\rangle\langle1|+r_2|0,b\rangle\langle\sqrt2|+\mathrm{adjoints},
\qquad r_1,r_2>0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bx.82}
$$
The zero-charge block of $A_{\mathrm{diag}}$ may be any Hermitian two-by-two matrix mixing $|0,a\rangle$ and $|0,b\rangle$; its other charge blocks are arbitrary scalars. The gaps $1,\sqrt2$ are rationally independent, and for $0<\epsilon<\min(r_1,r_2)$ the frontier is the sum of two nonzero $\Phi$ terms. Thus this is a nonempty family genuinely reaching more than two distinct system charge sectors, including targets whose commuting and off-charge parts do not commute.

The following boundaries are part of the statement.

1. Arbitrary targets with three or more charge sectors need not have a matching charge-changing part. Shared transition vertices generally create cross-edge terms in the noise square. The exact upper identity (M.6.13bx.72) and hence the asserted frontier are not extended to such targets here.
2. Distinct gaps need not be rationally independent. With dependent active gaps the physical phase orbit can be a proper subtorus, and both the independent-angle identification (M.6.13bx.51) and simple product-charge dephasing (M.6.13bx.77) can fail. No additive exact formula is asserted there; the exact joint constraint reduction (M.6.13bx.10) still holds.
3. Equal-gap edges must be grouped before using the formula. One shared factor serves all edges in a group; its hardest amplitude is $r_g$. An entropy term for each edge would generally overcount the attainable cost.
4. Only gaps with $r_g>\epsilon$ need independence at the specified error. Inactive groups use $L_g=0$ and incur bare error $|a_e|\le\epsilon$. At thresholds $r_g=\epsilon$ the group is inactive; the omitted contribution would be $\Phi(0)=0$.
5. The lower proofs admit arbitrary original charge degeneracy and arbitrary mixed or correlated complete references. Product states occur only in the explicit upper witnesses. Neutral pointers and flags remain in the complete reference accounting, although the specified neutral enlargements do not change asymmetry.
6. The result is an exact theorem for this matching family, together with the state-only inequality (M.6.13bx.56). It does not close the unrestricted general-system frontier or supply a physical identification of the mathematical charge and apparatus.

<a id="theorem-m613by-exact-charge-capacity-for-arbitrary-two-sector-targets"></a>**Theorem M.6.13by (Exact Charge Capacity for Arbitrary Two Sector Targets).** Retain the complete finite apparatus assumptions of Theorems M.6.13g–M.6.13h and M.6.13bw. Let the finite system have two nonzero charge sectors and an arbitrary Hermitian target, written
$$
\begin{aligned}
Q_S&=q_0I_{H_0}\oplus q_1I_{H_1},\qquad q_0<q_1,\qquad \Delta=q_1-q_0>0,\\
A&=\begin{pmatrix}A_{00}&C\\C^*&A_{11}\end{pmatrix},\qquad
D=A_{00}\oplus A_{11},\qquad O=A-D=C+C^*,\\
r&=\|C\|=\|O\|=d_{Q_S}(A),\qquad d=\dim H_S.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13by.1}
$$
Here $C:H_1\to H_0$ is extended by zero to $H_S$. The diagonal target blocks are arbitrary and need not commute with the off-charge part. A complete apparatus has an input-independent state $\sigma_R$, Hermitian complete reference charge $Q_R$, conserving unitary $U$, and Hermitian Yanase pointer $M$. Every neutral pointer, ancillary factor, flag, sector degeneracy and correlation is retained in $R$. Explicitly,
$$
\begin{aligned}
[U,Q_S\otimes I_R+I_S\otimes Q_R]&=0,\qquad [M,Q_R]=0,\\
B&=U^*(I_S\otimes M)U,\\
\epsilon_\infty(A)^2
&=\sup_{\rho_S}\operatorname{Tr}[(\rho_S\otimes\sigma_R)(B-A\otimes I_R)^2],
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13by.2}
$$
where every system density operator is tested.

Let $\mu_N$ be the harmonic-path statistic of Theorem M.6.13bw, including $\mu_1=0$. Under a cap of $N\ge1$ distinct eigenvalues of the complete reference charge, the exact minimum worst-case error is attained and equals
$$
e_N(A)=r\sqrt{1-\mu_N}.
\tag{M.6.13by.3}
$$
For any finite nonempty allowed reference-charge set $\Gamma\subset\mathbb R$, let $m_\Delta(\Gamma)$ be the number of vertices in its longest consecutive $\Delta$-step run. Under either spectrum containment or exact spectrum equality, the exact attained minimum is
$$
e_\Gamma(A)=r\sqrt{1-\mu_{m_\Delta(\Gamma)}}.
\tag{M.6.13by.4}
$$
These are distinct-charge-eigenvalue-count optima, with arbitrary finite degeneracies permitted and counted, rather than fixed-total-Hilbert-dimension or entropy optima. For $r>0$ and $0<\epsilon<r$, the least distinct-charge capacity permitting exact error $\epsilon$, equivalently error at most $\epsilon$, is
$$
N_{\min}(A,\epsilon)=\min\{N\ge1:\mu_N\ge1-(\epsilon/r)^2\}.
\tag{M.6.13by.5}
$$
For $\epsilon\ge r$ this capacity is one. For $r>0$, exact zero error is impossible at finite capacity. If $r=0$, exact error $\epsilon$ is attainable with one distinct reference charge for every $\epsilon\ge0$.

*Proof.*

**Distance and compression lower bound.** Nilpotence gives $C^2=(C^*)^2=0$ and $O^2=CC^*+C^*C$, hence $\|O\|=\|C\|$. To verify distance to the full self-adjoint commutant, put $Z=I_{H_0}\oplus(-I_{H_1})$. Every self-adjoint $T$ commuting with $Q_S$ obeys $ZTZ=T$, and
$$
O=\frac{(A-T)-Z(A-T)Z}{2},\qquad \|O\|\le\|A-T\|.
\tag{M.6.13by.6}
$$
Choosing $T=D$ proves (M.6.13by.1), including unequal sector dimensions, repeated singular values and kernels.

Assume $r>0$. Finite-dimensional singular-value decomposition supplies unit vectors $u\in H_0$ and $v\in H_1$ with $Cv=ru$ and $C^*u=rv$. Let $J:\mathbb C^2\to H_S$ send the two standard basis vectors to $u,v$. Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
J^*AJ&=D_c+rX,\qquad X=|0\rangle\langle1|+|1\rangle\langle0|,\\
D_c&=\operatorname{diag}(\langle u,A_{00}u\rangle,\langle v,A_{11}v\rangle),\\
Q_SJ&=J(q_0I+\Delta|1\rangle\langle1|).
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13by.7}
$$
For any admitted apparatus set $W=J\otimes I_R$, $E=B-A\otimes I_R$, and $E_c=W^*EW$. Compression satisfies
$$
W^*E^2W-E_c^2=W^*E(I-WW^*)EW\ge0.
\tag{M.6.13by.8}
$$
Therefore every qubit density operator $\rho$ satisfies
$$
\operatorname{Tr}[(\rho\otimes\sigma_R)E_c^2]
\le\operatorname{Tr}[(J\rho J^*\otimes\sigma_R)E^2]
\le\epsilon_\infty(A)^2.
\tag{M.6.13by.9}
$$
The embedded state is among the required system inputs. The positive term in (M.6.13by.8) retains all leakage: neither the arbitrary diagonal target blocks nor the full pointer need preserve the singular-pair subspace.

Define the Hermitian compressed observable
$$
\widehat B=\frac{W^*BW-D_c\otimes I_R}{r},\qquad
[\widehat B,|1\rangle\langle1|\otimes I_R+I_2\otimes Q_R/\Delta]=0,\qquad
\widehat B-X\otimes I_R=E_c/r.
\tag{M.6.13by.10}
$$
The direct invariant-observable lower bound proved in Theorem M.6.13bw applies to $\widehat B$ without physically dilating this compressed operator. In the notation of that theorem,
$$
\frac{\epsilon_\infty(A)^2}{r^2}
\ge1-\eta_{Q_R/\Delta}(\sigma_R)
\ge1-\mu_N.
\tag{M.6.13by.11}
$$
Dividing the charge by $\Delta$ preserves its number of distinct eigenvalues and every degeneracy. Unit-step paths for the normalized charge are precisely the original $\Delta$-step paths. The longest-run bound in Theorem M.6.13bw replaces $N$ by $m_\Delta(\Gamma)$ and proves (M.6.13by.4)'s lower bound. No apparatus factor, new charge value, or untested input has been added.

**Attaining whole observable and exact moments.** On $R_0=\mathbb C^N$ use the positive reflection-symmetric optimizer $p^{(N)}$ from Theorem M.6.13bw and set
$$
\begin{aligned}
Q_0&=\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}i\Delta|i\rangle\langle i|,\qquad
|\phi\rangle=\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\sqrt{p_i^{(N)}}|i\rangle,\\
L&=\sum_{i=0}^{N-2}\frac{2\sqrt{p_ip_{i+1}}}{p_i+p_{i+1}}|i+1\rangle\langle i|.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13by.12}
$$
For $N=1$ the sum is empty and $L=0$. All expectations below are in $|\phi\rangle$. The harmonic-path construction of Theorem M.6.13bw, including its reflection symmetry, gives
$$
[Q_0,L]=\Delta L,\qquad
\langle L\rangle=\langle L^*\rangle=\langle LL^*\rangle=\langle L^*L\rangle=\mu_N.
\tag{M.6.13by.13}
$$
Since $[Q_S,C]=-\Delta C$, the single full observable
$$
B_0=D\otimes I+C\otimes L+C^*\otimes L^*,\qquad
[B_0,Q_S\otimes I+I\otimes Q_0]=0
\tag{M.6.13by.14}
$$
is invariant. It is implemented as a whole; no sequential measurement of potentially noncommuting target pieces is assumed. Subtracting the full target first gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
B_0-A\otimes I&=C\otimes(L-I)+C^*\otimes(L^*-I),\\
(B_0-A\otimes I)^2
&=CC^*\otimes(L-I)(L^*-I)+C^*C\otimes(L^*-I)(L-I),\\
\mathcal E_\phi[(B_0-A\otimes I)^2]
&=(1-\mu_N)(CC^*+C^*C)=(1-\mu_N)O^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13by.15}
$$
Here $\mathcal E_\phi$ is the partial expectation in the reference vector. The operator norm of the final positive matrix is $r^2(1-\mu_N)$, proving the all-input worst-case value. This noise need not be constant on every input. The induced moments independently read
$$
E^{(1)}=D+\mu_NO,\qquad
E^{(2)}=D^2+\mu_NO^2+\mu_N(DO+OD).
\tag{M.6.13by.16}
$$
Substitution in $A^2-AE^{(1)}-E^{(1)}A+E^{(2)}$ reproduces (M.6.13by.15) without assuming $DO=OD$.

**Original finite apparatus and retained dimensions.** Spectrally decompose the whole observable as
$$
B_0=\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}b_j\Pi_j,\qquad K=|\operatorname{spec}B_0|\le dN.
\tag{M.6.13by.17}
$$
Take a neutral pointer $P=\mathbb C^K$ with ready vector $|0\rangle$ and cyclic shift $V|j\rangle=|j+1\pmod K\rangle$. Set
$$
\begin{aligned}
M_P&=\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}b_j|j\rangle\langle j|,\qquad
U=\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}\Pi_j\otimes V^j,\\
R&=R_0\otimes P,\qquad Q_R=Q_0\otimes I_P,\\
\sigma_R&=|\phi\rangle\langle\phi|\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|,\qquad
M=I_{R_0}\otimes M_P.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13by.18}
$$
Spectral orthogonality proves unitarity. Each projector commutes with total charge, so $U$ conserves it, and pointer neutrality gives the Yanase condition. If $\iota$ adjoins the ready state, then
$$
\begin{aligned}
[U,Q_S\otimes I_R+I_S\otimes Q_R]&=0,\qquad [M,Q_R]=0,\\
\iota^*U^*(I_{H_S\otimes R_0}\otimes M_P^k)U\iota
&=\sum_j b_j^k\Pi_j=B_0^k,\qquad k=1,2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13by.19}
$$
The embedding intertwines the system target, so both physical pointer moments and all mixed terms in the original noise square equal those in (M.6.13by.15)–(M.6.13by.16). The ready-state label does not require $b_0=0$.

The displayed complete dimensions and charge counts are
$$
\dim R=NK\le dN^2,\qquad
\dim(H_S\otimes R)=dNK,\qquad
|\operatorname{spec}Q_R|=N.
\tag{M.6.13by.20}
$$
Each reference charge has degeneracy $K$. The actual pointer capacity is the number of distinct eigenvalues of the whole $B_0$, not the special qubit count from Theorem M.6.13bw. No minimum-pointer or minimum-total-dimension assertion follows. For $N=1$ this measures $D$ with $K=|\operatorname{spec}D|\le d$ and has error $r$; if $r=0$, it measures $A$ exactly.

**Fixed allowed spectrum with every unused sector retained.** Choose a longest $\Delta$-run of length $m=m_\Delta(\Gamma)$ and translate the preceding $m$-ladder to its starting charge. This attains the lower bound under spectrum containment. For exact equality, give $R_0$ one basis vector for every charge in $\Gamma$, support the state on the chosen run, use the displayed whole observable on that run, and extend it by zero on all unused reference sectors. The run and its complement reduce total charge and the target, so the extension remains invariant and the initially zero-weight sectors do not alter the error. Dilate this entire extended observable, retaining and counting those sectors. Then
$$
\dim R=|\Gamma|K,\qquad
\dim(H_S\otimes R)=d|\Gamma|K,\qquad
\operatorname{spec}Q_R=\Gamma,
\tag{M.6.13by.21}
$$
with degeneracy $K$ at each charge. The actual $K$ is the distinct spectral count of the displayed full observable; $K\le dm$ if no unused sector exists and $K\le dm+1$ otherwise, since zero is its only possible additional eigenvalue. These are witness capacities, not optimal dimensions. The construction includes $m=1$ and invariant targets.

**Exact errors and endpoints.** If $r>0$ and $0<\epsilon<r$, put $u=1-(\epsilon/r)^2$. For an eligible $N$ in (M.6.13by.5), $0<u\le\mu_N$, so $N\ne1$ and
$$
\begin{aligned}
s&=1-\sqrt{1-u/\mu_N}\in(0,1],\\
B_{0,s}&=D\otimes I+sC\otimes L+sC^*\otimes L^*,\\
\mathcal E_\phi[(B_{0,s}-A\otimes I)^2]
&=[1-\mu_N(2s-s^2)]O^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13by.22}
$$
The last norm is exactly $\epsilon^2$. Dilate the whole new observable with its own spectral pointer; its finite capacity obeys $K_s\le dN$. Scaling the entire old pointer would generally also scale $D$ and is not the construction used here. The lower bound proves necessity, and $\mu_N\to1$ ensures the minimum in (M.6.13by.5) exists.

For $\epsilon\ge r>0$, take the charge-invariant observable $B=D+tI$, with $t=\epsilon-r\ge0$. The nonzero spectrum of $O$ is paired, includes $\pm r$, and gives
$$
\|B-A\|=\|tI-O\|=t+r=\epsilon.
\tag{M.6.13by.23}
$$
A neutral spectral pointer and a one-dimensional base reference realize it with one distinct reference charge. Finite exact zero error for $r>0$ is excluded by $\mu_N<1$ for every finite $N$. If $r=0$, the invariant observable $B=A+\epsilon I$ realizes every exact error $\epsilon\ge0$ with one distinct reference charge, including zero. The one-sector system case is likewise invariant. This completes every endpoint and the proof. $\square$

This theorem uses the original complete finite apparatus class. Its two-sector restriction is essential to the compression and nilpotent-block calculation. It supplies no arbitrary higher-charge-system frontier, fixed-total-dimension optimum, entropy optimum, physical charge labels, hardware service, or new measurement postulate.

<a id="theorem-m613bz-finite-higher-charge-precision-gain-and-attainable-spin-upper-slopes"></a>**Theorem M.6.13bz (Finite Higher Charge Precision Gain and Attainable Spin Upper Slopes).** Retain the original complete finite conserving-unitary and Yanase-pointer class of Theorems M.6.13g–M.6.13h, with an input-independent complete reference and the supremum over every system input. Asymmetry uses natural logarithms. Every charged level, neutral pointer, ancillary factor, flag, sector degeneracy and correlation is included in the complete reference. Write $\mathfrak A^{=}_{Q_S,A}(\epsilon)$ and $\mathfrak A^{\le}_{Q_S,A}(\epsilon)$ for the infima of initial complete-reference asymmetry at exact error and error at most $\epsilon$, respectively.

Let the system have charge and target

$$
Q_S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2,3),\qquad A=X=J_x/(3/2).
\tag{M.6.13bz.1}
$$

There is a complete finite admitted apparatus with exactly five distinct reference-charge eigenvalues, reference dimension 45 (including a nine-level neutral pointer), natural-$\log$ asymmetry

$$
\mathcal A\le\frac{161}{16000},
\tag{M.6.13bz.2}
$$

and exact worst-case squared error and quality

$$
\epsilon_\infty^2=\frac{625+4\sqrt{14887}}{1125},\qquad
u=1-\epsilon_\infty^2=\frac{500-4\sqrt{14887}}{1125}.
\tag{M.6.13bz.3}
$$

Both $\|A\|$ and its distance $d_{Q_S}(A)$ to the full self-adjoint charge commutant equal one. The strict certified separation is

$$
\mathcal A\le\frac{161}{16000}
<\frac{492}{46875}\le u\le\Phi(u),
\qquad
\frac{492}{46875}-\frac{161}{16000}=\frac{867}{2000000}>0.
\tag{M.6.13bz.4}
$$

Here $\Phi$ is the previously proved exact normalized binary entropy/error infimum. Thus that formula cannot be extended to arbitrary targets using only normalized error $\epsilon/d_Q(A)$. This does not refute the binary theorem: this target has four system-charge sectors and a connected three-edge path with shared vertices, outside both the two-sector and disjoint-matching target classes.

The state-only one-gap entropy inequality is also unaffected. For this reference the standard charge-one functional is

$$
\eta_1(\sigma)=\sum_{n=0}^3\frac{2|\sigma_{n+1,n}|^2}{\sigma_{nn}+\sigma_{n+1,n+1}}
=\frac45c^2=\frac1{125}<u.
\tag{M.6.13bz.5}
$$

Its existing bound is $\mathcal A>\Phi(\eta_1)$, compatible with the example. The binary operational implication $u\le\eta_1$ is the part that does not extend to this target. Tensoring the pure neutral ready state leaves this functional unchanged; its added zero-support terms contribute zero.

The distinction can be made with exactly the same system charge: the target

$$
A_{\mathrm{match}}=|0\rangle\langle1|+|1\rangle\langle0|
             +|2\rangle\langle3|+|3\rangle\langle2|
\tag{M.6.13bz.6}
$$

also has norm and commutant distance one, but its exact asymmetry infimum is $\Phi(1-\epsilon^2)$. Compressing to the first charge pair proves its binary lower bound; using the same one-gap binary reference on both orthogonal pairs proves the matching upper bound. The pairs' cross terms vanish. Consequently target structure matters even with the system charge spectrum, target norm, and commutant distance fixed.

The spin family below additionally gives the one-sided bound

$$
\limsup_{u\downarrow0}
\frac{\mathfrak A^{=}_{Q_S,J_x/J}(\sqrt{1-u})}{u}
\le \frac{2J+1}{4J}<1,
\qquad J\in\{3/2,2,5/2,\ldots\}.
\tag{M.6.13bz.7}
$$

The same bound holds for the at-most-error infimum. It is an achievable upper slope, not an exact frontier or a matching lower bound.

*Proof.*

**System matrices and distance to the full commutant.**

Order the standard spin basis by $m_z=-3/2,-1/2,1/2,3/2$, and put

$$
C=\frac{J_-}{2J}=\frac13
\begin{pmatrix}
0&\sqrt3&0&0\\0&0&2&0\\0&0&0&\sqrt3\\0&0&0&0
\end{pmatrix},\qquad
X=C+C^*,\qquad Y=i(C-C^*).
\tag{M.6.13bz.8}
$$

Then $J=3/2$, $[Q_S,C]=-C$, and $X=J_x/J$, $Y=J_y/J$ with the usual spin convention. In particular $C$ lowers the system charge. The eigenvalues of $X$ are $-1,-1/3,1/3,1$, so its norm is one.

Set $Z=e^{i\pi Q_S}=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,-1)$. Then $ZXZ^*=-X$. For every self-adjoint $T$ commuting with $Q_S$, $ZTZ^*=T$, and

$$
X=\frac{(X-T)-Z(X-T)Z^*}{2},\qquad \|X\|\le\|X-T\|.
\tag{M.6.13bz.9}
$$

Taking $T=0$ proves $d_{Q_S}(X)=1$. This uses the full charge commutant, not an artificially restricted diagonal approximation family. The same argument applies to $A_{\mathrm{match}}$.

**Same-charge-spectrum comparison with complete matching proof.** The matching target on the same $Q_S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2,3)$ has two orthogonal charge-one pairs. Let $P_{01}$ be the system projection onto the first pair. For any admitted apparatus with noise $E=B-A_{\mathrm{match}}\otimes I_R$, put $P=P_{01}\otimes I_R$. The compression identity $PE^2P-(PEP)^2=PE(I-P)EP\ge0$ implies that its compressed invariant observable has all-input error at most the original error, including any leakage to the other pair. A neutral whole-observable spectral dilation, as in Theorem M.6.13by, makes that finite binary observable an admitted apparatus without changing initial asymmetry. The binary at-most-error theorem therefore gives the lower bound $\Phi(1-\epsilon^2)$ for $0<\epsilon<1$, for both the exact-error and at-most-error matching infima.

For the upper bound, choose any finite binary exact-error witness in the exact-error approximating family of Theorem M.6.13l, and use its same reference and charge-raising operator on both pairs. On the system direct sum, the resulting invariant observable is the direct sum of two copies of the binary observable. Products of the distinct system-pair supports vanish before reference averaging, so the conditional noise is the direct sum of the two identical binary noise operators and has exactly the prescribed norm $\epsilon^2$. Apply a single neutral spectral-pointer dilation to this whole direct-sum observable. The reference cost is paid once, its complete neutral pointer is retained, and its asymmetry equals the original binary reference asymmetry. Taking that finite exact-error sequence proves equality with $\Phi(1-\epsilon^2)$ for both conventions. At zero error there is no finite model by the same compression; at and above error one the invariant constant system observable $(\epsilon-1)I$ attains exact error $\epsilon$ with zero asymmetry. Thus fixing the charge spectrum, target norm and full commutant distance still leaves different achievable entropy costs for different target structures.

**The complete five-charge reference before readout dilation.**

Let $R_0=\mathbb C^5$, $Q_0=\sum_{n=0}^4n|n\rangle\langle n|$, and define

$$
\theta_j=2\pi j/5,\quad
|\theta_j\rangle=5^{-1/2}\sum_{n=0}^4e^{in\theta_j}|n\rangle,\quad
c=1/10,\quad
w_j=\frac{1+2c\cos\theta_j}{5},\quad
\sigma=\sum_{j=0}^4w_j|\theta_j\rangle\langle\theta_j|.
\tag{M.6.13bz.10}
$$

The Fourier vectors are orthonormal, every $w_j$ is strictly positive, and their sum is one. The full state is retained. If $V|n\rangle=|n+1\pmod5\rangle$, it is equivalently

$$
\sigma=\frac{I+c(V+V^*)}{5},\qquad \tau=\mathcal G_{Q_0}(\sigma)=I/5.
\tag{M.6.13bz.11}
$$

In particular, the charge-four wrap coherence between levels zero and four is present in the state and fully counted in its entropy. It is not silently discarded.

Use the noncyclic raising shift

$$
S=\sum_{n=0}^3|n+1\rangle\langle n|,\qquad [Q_0,S]=S.
\tag{M.6.13bz.12}
$$

Its exact moments are

$$
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma S=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma S^*=\frac45c,
\quad
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma SS^*=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma S^*S=\frac45,
\quad
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma S^2=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(S^*)^2=0.
\tag{M.6.13bz.13}
$$

The first equality sums four adjacent entries $c/5$; the second uses the constant diagonal $1/5$; the last uses the absence of charge-two coherence. The cyclic shift defining the state is not used as a conserving shift in the measurement.

Define one Hermitian invariant observable on $S\otimes R_0$:

$$
B=2c(C\otimes S+C^*\otimes S^*).
\tag{M.6.13bz.14}
$$

The opposite charge increments in each tensor product give $[B,Q_S\otimes I+I\otimes Q_0]=0$. This is a single whole-observable construction, not separate edge measurements.

**Exact noise for every system input.**

Write $\mathcal E_\sigma(T)=\operatorname{Tr}_{R_0}[(I\otimes\sigma)T]$, put $a=4/5$, and set $t=2ac^2=2/125$. Equations (M.6.13bz.13) give

$$
\mathcal E_\sigma(B)=tX,
\quad
\mathcal E_\sigma(B^2)=4ac^2(CC^*+C^*C)=t(X^2+Y^2).
\tag{M.6.13bz.15}
$$

For the noise $E=B-X\otimes I$, bimodularity of conditional expectation yields

$$
K=\mathcal E_\sigma(E^2)
=X^2-X\mathcal E_\sigma(B)-\mathcal E_\sigma(B)X+\mathcal E_\sigma(B^2)
=(1-t)X^2+tY^2.
\tag{M.6.13bz.16}
$$

The original all-input squared RMS error is exactly $\|K\|$, once the moment-preserving dilation below is made. No selected input state or average-input surrogate replaces this supremum.

Direct matrix multiplication gives

$$
K=\frac19
\begin{pmatrix}
3&0&2\sqrt3(1-2t)&0\\
0&7&0&2\sqrt3(1-2t)\\
2\sqrt3(1-2t)&0&7&0\\
0&2\sqrt3(1-2t)&0&3
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13bz.17}
$$

Both parity blocks have the same two eigenvalues, so

$$
\operatorname{spec}K=\left\{
\frac{5+4\sqrt{1-3t+3t^2}}9,
\frac{5-4\sqrt{1-3t+3t^2}}9
\right\},
\tag{M.6.13bz.18}
$$

each with multiplicity two. This proves (M.6.13bz.3).

Since $0<t<1$, the inequality $\sqrt{1-z}\le1-z/2$ at $z=3t(1-t)\in(0,1)$ gives

$$
u=\frac49\left(1-\sqrt{1-3t(1-t)}\right)
\ge\frac23t(1-t)=\frac{492}{46875}.
\tag{M.6.13bz.19}
$$

The inequality is in fact strict, but the weak rational bound suffices.

**An elementary entropy certificate below the binary curve.**

Because the complete Fourier spectrum is retained and the twirl is uniform,

$$
\mathcal A_{Q_0}(\sigma)
=\log5-S(\sigma)
=\frac15\sum_{j=0}^4(1+x_j)\log(1+x_j),
\qquad x_j=2c\cos\theta_j.
\tag{M.6.13bz.20}
$$

Let $\mathbb E$ denote the uniform average over the five angles. Fourier orthogonality gives

$$
\mathbb Ex=\mathbb Ex^3=0,\qquad
\mathbb Ex^2=2c^2,\qquad \mathbb Ex^4=6c^4,\qquad |x_j|\le2c<1.
\tag{M.6.13bz.21}
$$

The absolutely convergent expansion

$$
(1+x)\log(1+x)
=x+\sum_{n=2}^\infty\frac{(-1)^n x^n}{n(n-1)}
\tag{M.6.13bz.22}
$$

therefore gives the rigorous upper bound

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal A_{Q_0}(\sigma)
&\le c^2+\mathbb E\sum_{n=4}^\infty\frac{|x|^n}{n(n-1)}\\
&\le c^2+\frac{\mathbb E|x|^4}{12(1-2c)}
=c^2+\frac{c^4}{2(1-2c)}
=\frac{161}{16000}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13bz.23}
$$

No logarithm is bounded by a floating-point evaluation here. For reference only,

$$
\mathcal A=0.010049645091995741\ldots,\quad
u=0.010622953022277709\ldots,\quad
\epsilon_\infty=0.994674342173217159\ldots.
\tag{M.6.13bz.24}
$$

The binary curve has the scalar Legendre form

$$
\Phi(u)=\sup_{\kappa\ge0}\{\kappa\sqrt u-\log I_0(\kappa)\}.
\tag{M.6.13bz.25}
$$

The defining power series implies $I_0(2\sqrt u)=\sum_{n\ge0}u^n/(n!)^2\le e^u$. Evaluating the supremum at $\kappa=2\sqrt u$ proves $\Phi(u)\ge u$. This scalar comparison and (M.6.13bz.19), (M.6.13bz.23) prove (M.6.13bz.4). The strict separation therefore does not depend on numerical Bessel evaluation.

**Explicit original-class unitary, pointer, and complete accounting.**

The total charge on $S\otimes R_0$ has values zero through seven. On each total-charge eigenspace, $B$ is $2c$ times a contiguous principal submatrix of $X$: the block lengths are $1,2,3,4,4,3,2,1$. Thus its nine distinct eigenvalues are

$$
\{b_0,\ldots,b_8\}
=\left\{0,\ \pm\frac1{15},\ \pm\frac{\sqrt3}{15},\
\pm\frac{\sqrt7}{15},\ \pm\frac15\right\},\qquad b_0=0.
\tag{M.6.13bz.26}
$$

Any fixed ordering of the eight nonzero labels is allowed. The zero eigenspace has dimension four and every nonzero eigenspace dimension two. Equivalently the exact characteristic polynomial is

$$
\lambda^4
(\lambda^2-1/225)^2(\lambda^2-3/225)^2
(\lambda^2-7/225)^2(\lambda^2-9/225)^2.
\tag{M.6.13bz.27}
$$

Let $\Pi_j$ be the complete spectral projector at $b_j$, explicitly definable by

$$
\Pi_j=\prod_{k\ne j}\frac{B-b_kI}{b_j-b_k}.
\tag{M.6.13bz.28}
$$

Take $P=\mathbb C^9$, a neutral pointer with ready state $|0\rangle$, and $W|j\rangle=|j+1\pmod9\rangle$. Define

$$
U=\sum_{j=0}^8\Pi_j\otimes W^j,\quad
M_P=\sum_{j=0}^8b_j|j\rangle\langle j|,
\tag{M.6.13bz.29}
$$

and the complete original apparatus

$$
R=R_0\otimes P,\quad
Q_R=Q_0\otimes I_P,\quad
\sigma_R=\sigma\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|,\quad
M=I_{R_0}\otimes M_P.
\tag{M.6.13bz.30}
$$

The orthogonal projectors sum to the identity, so $U$ is unitary. They commute with $Q_S+Q_0$, so $[U,Q_S+Q_R]=0$. Neutrality gives $[M,Q_R]=0$. With $\iota:\psi\mapsto\psi\otimes|0\rangle$, orthogonality also gives

$$
\iota^*U^*(I_{S\otimes R_0}\otimes M_P^m)U\iota
=\sum_j b_j^m\Pi_j=B^m,\qquad m=1,2.
\tag{M.6.13bz.31}
$$

Since the ready-state compression intertwines $X$, expanding the original Heisenberg noise square proves exactly (M.6.13bz.16). The model therefore realizes the stated error in the original measurement definition, not merely an invariant-POVM surrogate.

All 45 apparatus states and all nine readout outcomes remain present. The system-inclusive dimension is 180. There are exactly five distinct complete reference charges $0,1,2,3,4$, each with degeneracy nine. The pointer norm is exactly $1/5$. No auxiliary charge is hidden in the readout: it is neutral and counted. There is no postselection, conditional normalization, discarded failure branch, or uncounted reference flag.

Finally,

$$
\mathcal G_{Q_R}(\sigma_R)=(I/5)\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|,
\quad
\mathcal A_{Q_R}(\sigma_R)=\mathcal A_{Q_0}(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13bz.32}
$$

The neutral pure factor changes capacity but not initial asymmetry. The construction claims membership in the original mathematical class only; it does not derive a physical service for producing or reading this pointer.

**Spin-J weak-quality upper slopes, with improved scalar calibration.**

Let $J\in\{3/2,2,5/2,\ldots\}$, $d=2J+1$, and

$$
Q_S=J_z+JI,\quad C=J_-/(2J),\quad X=J_x/J=C+C^*,\quad Y=J_y/J=i(C-C^*).
\tag{M.6.13bz.33}
$$

The spectrum of $Q_S$ is $0,\ldots,2J$; $\|X\|=d_{Q_S}(X)=1$ by the same phase-$\pi$ argument. For any fixed integer $N\ge5$ and $0<c<1/2$, repeat (M.6.13bz.10) with $N$ Fourier vectors and weights $(1+2c\cos\theta_j)/N$. Write $a_N=1-1/N$. The full reference is strictly positive, its twirl is $I/N$, and

$$
\mathcal A_N(c)=c^2+O(c^4),\quad
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma S=a_Nc,\quad
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma SS^*=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma S^*S=a_N,\quad
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma S^2=0.
\tag{M.6.13bz.34}
$$

The same elementary entropy estimate as (M.6.13bz.23) bounds the absolute remainder by $c^4/[2(1-2c)]$. These assertions hold for every fixed $N\ge5$; no infinite state is introduced.

For a scalar calibration $\beta>0$, take

$$
B_{\beta,c}=\beta c(C\otimes S+C^*\otimes S^*),\qquad s=a_Nc^2.
\tag{M.6.13bz.35}
$$

The exact all-input conditional noise is

$$
K_\beta(s)
=X^2+sD_\beta,\quad
D_\beta=(\beta^2/2-2\beta)X^2+(\beta^2/2)Y^2.
\tag{M.6.13bz.36}
$$

Let $P$ project onto the two extreme $J_x$-eigenvectors $m_x=\pm J$. They are precisely the top eigenspace of $X^2$. The standard spin second moment and the quadratic selection rule give

$$
PX^2P=P,\quad PY^2P=\frac1{2J}P,\quad
PD_\beta P=-\gamma_\beta P,\qquad
\gamma_\beta=2\beta-\frac{\beta^2}{2}\left(1+\frac1{2J}\right).
\tag{M.6.13bz.37}
$$

For clarity, the diagonal second moment follows from rotational symmetry around the x-axis and $J_x^2+J_y^2+J_z^2=J(J+1)I$: each transverse second moment in an extreme x-eigenvector is $J/2$. The off-diagonal entry vanishes because $J_y^2$, expressed using the x-axis raising and lowering operators, changes $m_x$ by at most two, whereas the two extreme values differ by $2J\ge3$. This is why this argument does not include spin one.

Here is an elementary finite-matrix estimate avoiding any unproved differentiability of a degenerate eigenvalue. Put

$$
\delta=1-((J-1)/J)^2=\frac{2J-1}{J^2}>0,
\quad v=\|D_\beta\|.
\tag{M.6.13bz.38}
$$

The complementary restriction of $X^2$ is at most $(1-\delta)I$. If $\gamma_\beta>0$ and $s(v+\gamma_\beta)\le\delta/2$, decomposing any unit vector into its P and complementary parts, and completing a scalar square, yields

$$
1-\gamma_\beta s
\le\lambda_{\max}K_\beta(s)
\le1-\gamma_\beta s+\frac{2v^2}{\delta}s^2.
\tag{M.6.13bz.39}
$$

Indeed the lower bound tests a unit P-vector. For the upper bound, writing the complementary norm as r, the excess over $1-\gamma_\beta s$ is at most

$$
[-\delta+(v+\gamma_\beta)s]r^2+2svr\sqrt{1-r^2}
\le-\tfrac\delta2r^2+2svr\le2s^2v^2/\delta.
\tag{M.6.13bz.40}
$$

Thus its exact quality is

$$
u(s)=1-\|K_\beta(s)\|=\gamma_\beta s+O(s^2).
\tag{M.6.13bz.41}
$$

The matrix is positive semidefinite because it is a conditional expectation of an original noise square. Let $C_0=2v^2/\delta$ and $\gamma=\gamma_\beta>0$. The displayed bounds give $\gamma s-C_0s^2\le u(s)\le\gamma s$. For every sufficiently small prescribed $u>0$, put $s_0=u/\gamma$ and $s_1=u/\gamma+Lu^2$, choosing a fixed $L>C_0/\gamma^3$. Then $u(s_0)\le u$ and, for all sufficiently small $u$, $u(s_1)\ge u$. Continuity of the largest eigenvalue supplies an exact root between them. Decreasing $u$ if necessary ensures $c=\sqrt{s/a_N}<1/2$ and the perturbation smallness condition. Consequently every sufficiently small requested quality is attained with $s=u/\gamma+O(u^2)$, without assuming monotonicity or differentiability of a degenerate eigenvalue.

The whole-observable neutral-pointer dilation works as before. Its number of pointer levels is the finite number $K\le dN$ of distinct eigenvalues of $B_{\beta,c}$; complete reference dimension is $NK\le dN^2$. The charge spectrum still has exactly N eigenvalues, each with degeneracy K, and the pure neutral factor preserves $\mathcal A_N(c)$.

For each fixed $N$ and $\gamma_\beta>0$, equations (M.6.13bz.34), (M.6.13bz.41) imply

$$
\limsup_{u\downarrow0}
\frac{\mathfrak A^{=}_{Q_S,X}(\sqrt{1-u})}{u}
\le\frac1{a_N\gamma_\beta}.
\tag{M.6.13bz.42}
$$

The calibration $\beta=2$ has $\gamma_2=2-1/J$, so it gives the valid upper slope $J/(2J-1)$ after taking the infimum over finite N.

A better scalar calibration is

$$
\beta_* =\frac{4J}{2J+1},\qquad
\gamma_{\beta_*}=\frac{4J}{2J+1}.
\tag{M.6.13bz.43}
$$

It maximizes the scalar quadratic $\gamma_\beta$. Equation (M.6.13bz.42) holds for every finite $N$, so letting N grow only in this numerical upper bound proves (M.6.13bz.7). For $J=3/2$, the improved finite $N=5$ slope is at most 5/6, and the all-finite-reference upper slope is at most 2/3. The corresponding $\beta=2$ values are 15/16 and 3/4. These are upper bounds, without claims of optimality among other calibrations, reference states, invariant observables, or complete apparatuses.

The family of bounds $(2J+1)/(4J)$ tends to 1/2 as $J$ grows. This is a limit of explicit finite-target upper bounds, not a universal lower-slope theorem and not an assertion about one fixed infinite spin system.

Exact-error witnesses also qualify for the at-most-error infimum, so its stated upper slope follows. The construction proves target-structure-dependent achievable advantage and a spin-family upper bound only. It does not give the exact positive-budget frontier of the connected target, an optimal fixed-capacity entropy frontier, a fixed-total-dimension optimum, physical labels, hardware realization, preparation or readout services, implementation prices, PPI or whole-program closure. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613ca-all-finite-spin-one-pressure-bounds-and-a-high-accuracy-lower-curve"></a>**Theorem M.6.13ca (All-Finite Spin-One Pressure Bounds and a High-Accuracy Lower Curve).** Fix $Q_S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2)$ and $X=J_x$ with adjacent entries $1/\sqrt2$. Let $F(r)$ be the complete finite conserving-unitary/Yanase-pointer asymmetry infimum at squared all-input error at most $r$, $0<r<1$. Every finite real reference charge, sector multiplicity, mixed state, internal correlation, neutral factor and outcome remains admitted and counted. All logarithms are natural.

Put $e=(|0\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $m=|1\rangle$, $o=(|0\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, and $T_{\lambda,\mu}=(1-\lambda)|e\rangle\langle e|+\lambda|m\rangle\langle m|+\mu|o\rangle\langle o|$. For $0\le\lambda\le1$, $\mu\ge0$, this positive tester satisfies $\operatorname{Tr}T=1+\mu$, $\operatorname{Tr}TX^2=1$ and $\{T,X\}=X$. Oddification by $P=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)$ removes the even observable part without increasing its all-input error: operator convexity of the square gives $K(N_o)\le[K(N)+PK(N)P]/2$. The tested square is exactly $1-\operatorname{Tr}\sigma\mathcal K_{\lambda,\mu}(N)$ for the operator below. Thus every actual device of error at most $r$ gives $q_{\lambda,\mu}(\sigma)\ge1-r(1+\mu)$; this is a necessary weighted relaxation, not an identification with actual quality.

Define $q_{\lambda,\mu}(\sigma)=\sup_N\operatorname{Tr}\sigma\mathcal K_{\lambda,\mu}(N)$, and define $\Psi(\kappa,\lambda,\mu)$ as the supremum of $\log\operatorname{Tr}\exp[\log\tau+\kappa\mathcal K_{\lambda,\mu}(N)]$ over all finite integer-charge references, arbitrary finite multiplicities, invariant faithful normalized states $\tau$ and odd invariant Hermitian $N$. The zero observable and positivity of the tested square give $0\le q\le1$ and $\Psi\ge0$. Integer charges suffice for this pressure class: pinching arbitrary real charges into cosets modulo $\mathbb Z$ preserves the two pointer moments and cannot increase asymmetry; translate and separate the finitely occupied chains, retaining all coset labels and multiplicities. No physical energy labels are identified by this replacement.

The results are the exact pressure slice (M.6.13ca.8), the all-finite region bound (M.6.13ca.16), and the strictly finite-device lower curve (M.6.13ca.21). These do not evaluate the full spin-one frontier.

*Proof.*

**I. Exact reference-operator form.**

Let the finite integer-charge reference have charge $Q$. Every odd conserving observable has the system-block form

$$
N=\begin{pmatrix}0&A&0\\A^*&0&B\\0&B^*&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad [Q,A]=A,\quad [Q,B]=B.
\tag{M.6.13ca.1}
$$

Here $A,B$ are arbitrary complex charge-raising operators on the entire reference, with arbitrary rectangular blocks between charge sectors separated by one. No simultaneous diagonalization is used. The operator identities and all lower-bound implications below work directly for arbitrary finite real $Q$, since they require only the two commutator identities in (M.6.13ca.1). The pressure itself uses the integer-coset representation specified above. Direct multiplication of this complete matrix gives

$$
\mathcal K_{\lambda,\mu}(N)
=\frac{A+A^*+B+B^*}{\sqrt2}-\mathcal Q_{\lambda,\mu}(A,B),
\tag{M.6.13ca.2}
$$

$$
\begin{split}
\mathcal Q_{\lambda,\mu}(A,B)
={}&\lambda(A^*A+BB^*)\\
&+\frac{1-\lambda}{2}(A+B^*)(A^*+B)
+\frac\mu2(A-B^*)(A^*-B).
\end{split}
\tag{M.6.13ca.3}
$$

Thus the complete gap-two products $AB$ and $B^*A^*$ have coefficient $(1-\lambda-\mu)/2$. Equation (M.6.13ca.3), not a scalar replacement for its factors, is used below. It is the direct expansion against the complete tester defined above.

For a raising operator $L$, define the one-gap potential and pressure constant

$$
H_L=L+L^*-K_L,\qquad K_L=\frac{LL^*+L^*L}{2},
\qquad S(t)=\max_{0\le s\le1}e^{-ts^2}I_0(2ts).
\tag{M.6.13ca.4}
$$

Theorem M.6.13k proves, for every finite $Q$, every invariant Hermitian $D$, every arbitrary raising $L$, and every $t\ge 0$,

$$
\operatorname{Tr}e^{D+tH_L}\le S(t)\operatorname{Tr}e^D.
\tag{M.6.13ca.5}
$$

Its constant is sharp over all finite dimensions, and the inequality is strict for $t>0,L\ne 0$. The constant is taken over all finite reference dimensions.

**II. An exact positive-pressure slice.**

At $\lambda=\mu=1/2$, the tested system matrix is $I_3/2$. Put

$$
L=(A+B)/\sqrt2,\qquad C=(A-B)/\sqrt2.
$$

The complete operator identity is

$$
\boxed{\mathcal K_{1/2,1/2}(N)=H_L-K_C.}
\tag{M.6.13ca.6}
$$

Since $K_C\ge0$, trace-exponential monotonicity and (M.6.13ca.5), with $D=\log\tau$, give

$$
\operatorname{Tr}e^{\log\tau+\kappa\mathcal K_{1/2,1/2}(N)}
\le S(\kappa).
\tag{M.6.13ca.7}
$$

This is an all-finite-dimensional upper bound, including every faithful invariant $\tau$. Conversely every one-gap witness $L$ is obtained exactly by taking $A=B=L/\sqrt2$; then $C=0$. The finite truncated shifts in M.6.13k.16, with $\tau=I/n$, show sharpness within the present original pressure class. Therefore

$$
\boxed{\Psi(\kappa,1/2,1/2)=\log S(\kappa)\quad(\kappa\ge0).}
\tag{M.6.13ca.8}
$$

There is no fixed-dimension approximation in the upper bound. The increasing finite dimensions are used only for the separately proved sharpness direction. In particular $\Psi=0$ on this slice for $0\le \kappa\le 1$, while $\Psi>0$ for $\kappa>1$.
