For completeness the sharpness sequence is explicit. Set $Q_n=\operatorname{diag}(0,\ldots,n-1)$ and $L_n=s\sum_{j=0}^{n-2}|j+1\rangle\langle j|$. Then

$$
K_{L_n}=s^2\left(I-\frac{P_0+P_{n-1}}2\right),
\quad
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\operatorname{Tr}e^{\kappa H_{L_n}}
=e^{-\kappa s^2}I_0(2\kappa s).
\tag{M.6.13ca.9}
$$

The boundary correction has rank two and a trace-exponential interpolation bound of order $1/n$, as proved in (M.6.13k.16). Choosing a maximizing $s$ proves (M.6.13ca.8).

The same identity gives the exact fixed-state variational equality

$$
q_{1/2,1/2}(\sigma)
=\sup_{[Q,L]=L}\operatorname{Tr}\sigma H_L
=\eta_1(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13ca.10}
$$

To check normalization independently, diagonalize only the charge blocks of $\mathcal G_Q\sigma$, with eigenvalues $p_i$. The last supremum is

$$
\eta_1(\sigma)=\sum_{q_i-q_j=1}\frac{2|\sigma_{ij}|^2}{p_i+p_j},
\tag{M.6.13ca.11}
$$

where a zero denominator contributes zero. This is the one-gap state functional of Theorem M.6.13h. Equation (M.6.13ca.10) is not an identification with the actual spin-one operational quality.

**III. A pressure upper bound throughout the positive-penalty region.**

Suppose $0<\lambda<1$ and $\mu>0$. Define

$$
a=\min\{1-\lambda,\mu\},\qquad b=\lambda,
\qquad h=\frac{4ab}{a+b}>0.
\tag{M.6.13ca.12}
$$

The two complete outer products in (M.6.13ca.3) give the operator bound

$$
\mathcal Q_{\lambda,\mu}(A,B)
\ge a(AA^*+B^*B)+b(A^*A+BB^*).
\tag{M.6.13ca.13}
$$

Indeed subtract $a/2$ times each product; the two remaining coefficients are nonnegative, while the sum of the two products is $2(AA^*+B^*B)$. This explicitly controls the full complex gap-two terms before any comparison.

The following weighted square identities are valid for arbitrary noncommuting matrices:

$$
\begin{split}
aAA^*+bBB^*
-\frac{ab}{a+b}(A+B)(A^*+B^*)
&=\frac{(aA-bB)(aA-bB)^*}{a+b},\\
bA^*A+aB^*B
-\frac{ab}{a+b}(A^*+B^*)(A+B)
&=\frac{(bA-aB)^*(bA-aB)}{a+b}.
\end{split}
\tag{M.6.13ca.14}
$$

With $L=(A+B)/\sqrt2$, summing (M.6.13ca.14) proves

$$
\mathcal Q_{\lambda,\mu}\ge hK_L,
\qquad
\mathcal K_{\lambda,\mu}(N)
\le L+L^*-hK_L=\frac1h H_{hL}.
\tag{M.6.13ca.15}
$$

Applying (M.6.13ca.5) yields the promised explicit global pressure bound

$$
\boxed{\Psi(\kappa,\lambda,\mu)\le\log S(\kappa/h),
\quad h=\frac{4\lambda\min\{1-\lambda,\mu\}}
{\lambda+\min\{1-\lambda,\mu\}}.}
\tag{M.6.13ca.16}
$$

In particular the right side is zero for $0\le \kappa\le h$, hence the actual pressure is zero there. Also $h\le 1$: since $a\le 1-\lambda$ and $4\lambda a/(\lambda+a)$ increases with $a$, one has $h\le 4\lambda(1-\lambda)\le 1$. Since positivity of the tested square for every state gives $\mathcal K_{\lambda,\mu}(N)\le I$, one also has $\Psi\le\kappa$; thus one may use $\min\{\kappa,\log S(\kappa/h)\}$ at all these parameters. The bound is not claimed sharp away from the exact slice (M.6.13ca.8).

On the cancellation line $\mu=1-\lambda$, (M.6.13ca.13) is an equality and $h=4\lambda(1-\lambda)$. The two gap-two terms have cancelled identically, because the full tested system matrix is $\operatorname{diag}(1-\lambda,\lambda,1-\lambda)$. This is an exact choice of tester, not removal of an input or a scalar ansatz.

**IV. Explicit original-frontier consequence.**

Let $r$ denote the squared worst-case original error and let $\Phi$ be the one-gap entropy curve of Theorem M.6.13l, equivalently

$$
\Phi(v)=\sup_{t\ge0}\{tv-\log S(t)\},\quad 0\le v<1.
\tag{M.6.13ca.17}
$$

For $0<v<1$, it is $z\sqrt v-\log I_0(z)$ with $I_1(z)/I_0(z)=\sqrt v$, and $\Phi(0)=0$. The direct tested-noise implication below, combined with (M.6.13ca.16), gives

$$
F(r)\ge\Phi\bigl(h[1-r(1+\mu)]_+\bigr).
\tag{M.6.13ca.18}
$$

Here the plus applies to the bracket. Equivalently the actual feasibility condition implies $q_{\lambda,\mu}\ge 1-r(1+\mu)$, whereas (M.6.13ca.15) implies $q_{\lambda,\mu}\le \eta_1/h$; then the one-gap entropy inequality of Theorems M.6.13k and M.6.13l gives (M.6.13ca.18). This alternative derivation makes the absence of any $q=u$ substitution explicit. Since $h\le 1$ and $0<r<1$, every argument to $\Phi$ in (M.6.13ca.18) lies in $[0,1)$.

For fixed $\mu$, the largest $h$ in (M.6.13ca.12), optimized over $\lambda$, is $4\mu(1-\mu)$ when $0<\mu\le 1/2$, attained at $\lambda=1-\mu$; for $\mu\ge 1/2$ it is one, attained at $\lambda=1/2$. In the latter range the error bracket decreases with $\mu$, so optimizing (M.6.13ca.18) reduces exactly to

$$
v(r)=\max_{0\le\mu\le1/2}
4\mu(1-\mu)[1-r(1+\mu)].
\tag{M.6.13ca.19}
$$

For $0<r<1$, its unique positive global maximizer is

$$
\mu_r=\frac{1-\sqrt{1-3r+3r^2}}{3r},
\qquad
\lambda_r=1-\mu_r
=\frac{3r-1+\sqrt{1-3r+3r^2}}{3r},
\tag{M.6.13ca.20}
$$

and $0<\mu_r<1/2$. Consequently

$$
\boxed{F(r)\ge\Phi(v(r)),\qquad
v(r)=4\mu_r(1-\mu_r)[1-r(1+\mu_r)].}
\tag{M.6.13ca.21}
$$

For the derivative check, divide the objective by four: it is $(1-r)\mu-\mu^2+r\mu^3$, whose derivative is $(1-r)-2\mu+3r\mu^2$. This upward quadratic has positive value at zero and negative value $-r/4$ at $1/2$. Therefore its smaller root lies strictly between zero and $1/2$, and its larger root is strictly above $1/2$. The displayed smaller root is the unique maximum on the required interval. Its value is positive. For $r<2/3$, it is strictly greater than the symmetric-slice argument $1-3r/2$, since that endpoint is not maximizing; for $r\ge 2/3$ it is strictly greater than its positive part zero.

An exact checkpoint is $r=1/2$: $\lambda_r=2/3$, $\mu_r=1/3$, $v(r)=8/27$. Near high accuracy,

$$
\mu_r=\frac12-\frac r8+O(r^2),\qquad
v(r)=1-\frac32r+\frac1{16}r^2+O(r^3).
\tag{M.6.13ca.22}
$$

Every individual finite original device satisfying the error threshold in fact has $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)>\Phi(v(r))$ for $0<r<1$. Indeed $v(r)>0$, feasibility and (M.6.13ca.15) give $\eta_1(\sigma)\ge v(r)>0$, and the finite one-gap entropy theorem of Theorem M.6.13l gives the strict inequality $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)>\Phi(\eta_1(\sigma))\ge \Phi(v(r))$. This proves strictness against the displayed lower curve only; it does not prove nonattainment of the unknown original frontier.

The pressure and lower bounds retain the complete complex gap-two products, every reference dimension and multiplicity, and all three input directions. They supply neither a finite-dimensional cutoff nor an exact spin-one entropy frontier or its attainment theorem. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613cb-finite-spin-one-phase-upper-curve-and-high-accuracy-sandwich"></a>**Theorem M.6.13cb (Finite Spin-One Phase Upper Curve and High-Accuracy Sandwich).** Let $Q_S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2)$, let $X=J_x$ have adjacent entries $1/\sqrt2$, and let $F(r)$ be the original complete-apparatus entropy-asymmetry infimum with all-input squared Ozawa error at most $r$. All finite real charge spectra, degeneracies, mixed states, complex conserving unitaries, unrestricted finite self-adjoint Yanase pointers, neutral factors and correlations remain allowed in this infimum.

For every $0<r<1$,
$$
\boxed{F(r)\le\Phi(1-r).}
\tag{M.6.13cb.1}
$$
Here $\Phi(v)=z\sqrt v-\log I_0(z)$, where $I_1(z)/I_0(z)=\sqrt v$, is the one-gap entropy curve of Theorem M.6.13l. Every approximating witness is finite and has exactly the prescribed error.

A realization uses $N$ distinct charges, one three-level neutral pointer, complete apparatus dimension $3N$, and system-inclusive dimension $9N$. All pointer outputs $0,\pm\sqrt{1-r}$ are retained; the ready state belongs to that same pointer.

This is a constructive upper bound, not an exact positive-error frontier or finite-attainment theorem.

*Proof.* **I. Three-level neutral pointer.**

Set $a=\sqrt{1-r}$ and choose an integer $N\ge3$ with
$$
N>\frac1{1-a}.
\tag{M.6.13cb.2}
$$
Write $\theta_l=2\pi l/N$, $b_k=1-k/N$, and let
$$
p_l=\frac{e^{z_N\cos\theta_l}}{Z_N},
\quad Z_N=\sum_l e^{z_N\cos\theta_l},
\quad \sum_l p_l\cos\theta_l=\frac a{b_1}.
\tag{M.6.13cb.3}
$$
There is a unique positive $z_N$: the finite cosine mean increases continuously from zero to one, with derivative equal to its strictly positive variance. The required moment lies in $(0,1)$.

Use $Q_N=\operatorname{diag}(0,\ldots,N-1)$ and the full circulant Fourier state
$$
(\sigma_N)_{jk}=\frac1N\sum_l p_l e^{i(j-k)\theta_l}.
\tag{M.6.13cb.4}
$$
It has diagonal $I_N/N$; all wrap coherences are retained. If $S_N$ is the truncated raising shift, put $S_N=\sum_{n=0}^{N-2}|n+1\rangle\langle n|$ and $c_{k,N}=\sum_lp_l\cos(k\theta_l)$; its two relevant moments are
$$
m_1=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_NS_N=b_1c_{1,N}=a,
\qquad m_2=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_NS_N^2=b_2c_{2,N}.
\tag{M.6.13cb.5}
$$

Let $P_-,P_0,P_+$ be the spectral projections of $X$, and define the three finite effects
$$
F_j=\mathcal G_{Q_S+Q_N}
 (P_j\otimes|\Omega_N\rangle\langle\Omega_N|),
\qquad |\Omega_N\rangle=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}|k\rangle.
\tag{M.6.13cb.6}
$$
The unnormalized vector is only a matrix-definition device. Each effect is positive and charge invariant; their sum is identity. Append a neutral pointer with basis $|-\rangle,|0\rangle,|+\rangle$, initially $|0\rangle$. The isometry
$$
Wv=\sum_j\sqrt{F_j}\,v\otimes|j\rangle
\tag{M.6.13cb.7}
$$
extends by orthonormal-basis completion to a unitary in each total-charge block of the same $9N$-dimensional space. Its input ready subspace and output image have equal dimension. This gives a conserving unitary with pointer $M=a\operatorname{diag}(-1,0,+1)$. No extra ready level or ancillary factor is required. 

For verification, the effects also equal the phase integrals of
$P_{j,\theta}\otimes|\theta\rangle\langle\theta|$, against $d\theta/(2\pi)$, where $P_{j,\theta}=e^{iQ_S\theta}P_je^{-iQ_S\theta}$ and $|\theta\rangle=\sum_ke^{ik\theta}|k\rangle$. This is an identity of finite matrices, not a continuous physical register. Entrywise integration enforces total charge conservation.

The normalized nonnegative finite density $\langle\theta|\sigma_N|\theta\rangle$, against $d\theta/(2\pi)$, is reflection symmetric and has moments $m_1,m_2$. The induced system moments are exactly
$$
B=am_1X,\qquad
C=a^2\left[\frac{1+m_2}{2}X^2+
                 \frac{1-m_2}{2}Y^2\right],\qquad Y=J_y.
\tag{M.6.13cb.8}
$$
In the orthonormal basis $e=(|0\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $m=|1\rangle$, $o=(|0\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, the complete noise $K=C-BX-XB+X^2$ has eigenvalues
$$
r_e=1-2am_1+\frac{a^2(1+m_2)}2,\quad
r_m=1-2am_1+a^2,\quad
r_o=\frac{a^2(1-m_2)}2,
\qquad r_m=r_e+r_o.
\tag{M.6.13cb.9}
$$
All are nonnegative: $K$ is the phase average of $(aX_\theta-X)^2$. Thus the middle input is maximally noisy and
$$
\|K\|=r_m=1-a^2=r.
\tag{M.6.13cb.10}
$$
This operator identity covers every input and entangled spectator, since $K\otimes I$ has the same norm. No state-quality quantity has been substituted for operational accuracy.

The complete initial state is $\sigma_N\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|$, with exact asymmetry
$$
A_N=\log N-H(p)=z_Nc_{1,N}-\log(Z_N/N).
\tag{M.6.13cb.11}
$$
At fixed $r$, strict-monotone-root bracketing and uniform compact Riemann-sum convergence imply $z_N\to z$, where $I_1(z)/I_0(z)=a$. Therefore
$$
A_N\longrightarrow za-\log I_0(z)=\Phi(1-r).
\tag{M.6.13cb.12}
$$
This proves the upper infimum using only finite exact-error apparatuses.

**II. High-accuracy interval.**

Put $c_0=[\log(2\pi)-1]/2$. The Bessel expansion (M.6.13j.6) gives $\Phi(1-s)=\tfrac12\log(1/s)+c_0+O(s)$ as $s\downarrow0$. Combining this upper bound with the all-finite lower curve of Theorem M.6.13ca, $\Phi(v(r))$, where $v(r)=1-\tfrac32r+\tfrac1{16}r^2+O(r^3)$, gives
$$
c_0-\tfrac12\log(3/2)
\le\liminf_{r\downarrow0}[F(r)-\tfrac12\log(1/r)]
\le\limsup_{r\downarrow0}[F(r)-\tfrac12\log(1/r)]
\le c_0.
\tag{M.6.13cb.13}
$$
The endpoints are approximately 0.2162059791505905 and 0.4189385332046727 nats. The remaining gap is exactly $\tfrac12\log(3/2)=0.2027325540540822\ldots$. Existence of an additive limit or equality at either endpoint is not asserted.

**III. Five-level neutral-pointer alternative.**

Put $C=(|0\rangle\langle1|+|1\rangle\langle2|)/\sqrt2$. For $N\ge3$, let $Q_N=\operatorname{diag}(0,\ldots,N-1)$, let $S_N$ be the truncated raising shift, and take the real symmetric circulant finite Fourier state

$$
\sigma_N=\sum_{\ell=0}^{N-1}\frac{e^{\kappa_N\cos\theta_\ell}}{Z_N}
|f_\ell\rangle\langle f_\ell|,
\quad \theta_\ell=2\pi\ell/N,\quad
Z_N=\sum_\ell e^{\kappa_N\cos\theta_\ell}.
\tag{M.6.13cb.14}
$$

Here $|f_\ell\rangle=N^{-1/2}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}e^{in\theta_\ell}|n\rangle$. All wrap coherences are retained. Its charge diagonal is exactly $I_N/N$. Write $c_k=Z_N^{-1}\sum_\ell e^{\kappa_N\cos\theta_\ell}\cos(k\theta_\ell)$, $b_1=1-1/N$, and $b_2=1-2/N$. Then

$$
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_NS_N=b_1c_1,\quad
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_NS_N^2=b_2c_2,\quad
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_NS_N^*S_N
=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_NS_NS_N^*=b_1.
\tag{M.6.13cb.15}
$$

For real $a$, use the whole invariant observable

$$
B_a=a(C\otimes S_N+C^*\otimes S_N^*).
\tag{M.6.13cb.16}
$$

Write $\mathbb E_{\sigma_N}(T)=\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma_N)T]$. Direct multiplication and conditional expectation give the full squared-noise spectrum in the orthonormal system basis $e=(|0\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2,m=|1\rangle,o=(|0\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
r_m&=1+b_1a^2-2ab_1c_1,\\
r_o&=\tfrac12a^2(b_1-b_2c_2),\\
r_e&=r_m-r_o.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13cb.17}
$$

These are the actual eigenvalues of $\mathbb E_{\sigma_N}(B_a-X\otimes I)^2$, not selected-state estimates. Consequently $r_e,r_o\ge0$ for every positive real symmetric circulant state, independently of the von Mises property, and $r_m=r_e+r_o$ is the largest eigenvalue. There is no missing odd-input condition. In particular, at $a=c_1$,

$$
r=\epsilon_\infty^2=1-b_1c_1^2.
\tag{M.6.13cb.18}
$$

For any prescribed $0<r<1$, choose any sufficiently large integer $N>1/r$ and the unique positive $\kappa_N$ satisfying

$$
c_1=\sqrt{(1-r)/b_1}<1.
\tag{M.6.13cb.19}
$$

The discrete cosine mean is continuous and strictly increasing from 0 to 1, since its derivative is the positive cosine variance. Thus this is an exact finite construction at the specified error, with no posterior error adjustment needed.

The characteristic polynomial of $B_a$ is

$$
z^N(z^2-a^2)^{N-2}(z^2-a^2/2)^2.
\tag{M.6.13cb.20}
$$

Indeed each interior total-charge block is a three-site spin-one path; the two boundary nontrivial blocks are two-site paths, and there are two isolated charge states. Thus for $N\ge3,a>0$, the five distinct spectral outputs are $0,\pm a,\pm a/\sqrt2$. The neutral spectral-pointer dilation of Theorem M.6.13h has charged reference dimension and distinct charge count $N$, neutral pointer dimension five including its ready vector, complete reference dimension $5N$ with charge degeneracy five, and system-inclusive dimension $15N$. Its complete ready state is $\sigma_N\otimes|\mathrm{rdy}\rangle\langle\mathrm{rdy}|$ and its unchanged asymmetry is
$$
\mathcal A_N=\kappa_Nc_1-\log(Z_N/N).
\tag{M.6.13cb.21}
$$

No additional ready level, flag, continuous phase register, or uncounted purifying system is physically appended.

At fixed $r$, let $N\to\infty$. The finite root converges to the unique $\kappa$ with $I_1(\kappa)/I_0(\kappa)=\sqrt{1-r}$, by Riemann-sum convergence and strict monotonicity. Consequently

$$
\lim_{N\to\infty}\mathcal A_N
=\kappa\sqrt{1-r}-\log I_0(\kappa)=\Phi(1-r).
\tag{M.6.13cb.22}
$$

Every member is finite and has exactly the required full all-input error. This proves the upper infimum bound, not finite attainment of it. For these particular states $\eta_1(\sigma_N)=b_1c_1^2=1-r$; that identity is a property of this calibrated family and is not asserted for arbitrary states.

**IV. A finite sine-state capacity family.**

Use the pure sine vector

$$
\psi_N(n)=\sqrt{2/(N+1)}\sin[\pi(n+1)/(N+1)].
\tag{M.6.13cb.23}
$$

Its phase moment is $m_1=\cos\alpha$, $\alpha=\pi/(N+1)$. The three-output construction of part I with $a=m_1$ therefore has exact squared error $r_N=\sin^2\alpha$. For any sufficiently small prescribed RMS error $\epsilon$, choose

$$
N=\left\lceil\pi/\arcsin\epsilon\right\rceil-1.
\tag{M.6.13cb.24}
$$

Then $r_N\le\epsilon^2$, and a scalar translation of the whole pointer reaches exactly $\epsilon$ if required: its conditional noise is a finite matrix polynomial, its norm is continuous and tends to infinity, and it starts below the requested error. The intermediate value theorem therefore reaches the prescribed value without changing state, dimension, charge count or the three distinct output count. The complete reference has dimension $3N$, system-inclusive dimension $9N$, and $N\sim\pi/\epsilon$ distinct charges.

The exact asymmetry is the displayed finite charge-probability Shannon entropy. Its asymptotic follows by a Riemann sum:

$$
H_N=\log(N+1)-\int_0^1 2\sin^2(\pi x)\log[2\sin^2(\pi x)]dx+o(1)
=\log(N+1)+\log2-1+o(1).
\tag{M.6.13cb.25}
$$

Thus this dimension-efficient pure family has additive entropy constant $\log(2\pi)-1=0.8378770664093453$, above the mixed-family constant $c_0$. It proves useful finite dimensions, not sharp capacity constants or sharp entropy.

The three-level construction uses the finite root $c_1=\sqrt{1-r}/b_1$, whereas the five-level alternative uses $c_1=\sqrt{(1-r)/b_1}$; their respective finite charge thresholds and complete dimensions remain distinct. All input states, outcomes and ready-state coherences are counted. These constructions do not evaluate the original frontier or optimize apparatus or physical service costs. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613cc-sharp-spin-one-complete-dimension-two-endpoint-and-budget-witnesses"></a>**Theorem M.6.13cc (Sharp Spin-One Complete-Dimension-Two Endpoint and Budget Witnesses).** Let

$$
 Q_S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2),\qquad
 X=2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\1&0&1\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13cc.1}
$$

A complete apparatus of dimension two consists of arbitrary Hermitian charge $Q_R$, arbitrary mixed initial state $\sigma$, a unitary $U$ commuting with $Q_S\otimes I+I\otimes Q_R$, and a Hermitian pointer $M$ commuting with $Q_R$. Its initial state is independent of the tested input; all system states and all correlations with an untouched spectator are tested. Its squared worst-case Ozawa error is

$$
 r=\lambda_{\max}K,\quad
 K=X^2+E^{(2)}-\{X,E^{(1)}\},\quad
 E^{(j)}=\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma)U^*(I\otimes M^j)U].
\tag{M.6.13cc.2}
$$

Every charged or neutral factor and every readout direction is part of the two dimensions. There is no additional pointer, purification, flag, controller, omitted outcome, or postselection.

Over that entire class, including every real apparatus charge gap and arbitrary pointer calibration,

$$
 \boxed{\min r=\frac{3\sqrt3}{8}.}
\tag{M.6.13cc.3}
$$

The explicit conserving device in part V below attains the minimum. Every minimizing two-dimensional device has a nondegenerate charge gap of magnitude one and a pure apparatus state balanced between its two charge eigenspaces. Consequently its full relative-entropy asymmetry is exactly $\log2$.

Thus no complete apparatus of dimension at most two can achieve squared error below $3\sqrt3/8$, at any asymmetry budget. Dimension one has error at least one. At budget at least $\log2$, the complete minimum dimension is exactly two for every prescribed squared error in $[3\sqrt3/8,1)$, in both exact-error and at-most-error conventions. The endpoint is the global two-dimensional optimum and its resource is forced.

This theorem does not evaluate the unrestricted-apparatus frontier, the dimension-three frontier, or the exact two-dimensional positive-budget curve below $\log2$. No physical implementation or lifecycle-cost identification is supplied.

**I. All real charge gaps.**

Diagonalize the entire apparatus charge. If its eigenvalues are distinct, subtract their common offset and order them, giving $Q_R=\operatorname{diag}(0,g)$, $g>0$. Conservation permits an off-diagonal system entry of an induced moment only when its charge gap is zero or $\pm g$. The system charge gaps are $0,\pm1,\pm2$.

If $g\ne1$, the induced first and second moments commute with

$$
 P=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1).
\tag{M.6.13cc.4}
$$

This includes the resonant case $g=2$: the only possible off-diagonal system entries connect charges 0 and 2 and are parity even. For nonresonant gaps the moments are diagonal. If the apparatus charge is degenerate, total-charge conservation makes $U$ block diagonal in the three distinct system charges; the induced moments are again diagonal, even though the charge-commuting pointer can then be an arbitrary two-by-two Hermitian matrix.

Let $|x_+\rangle,|x_-\rangle$ be the target eigenstates of eigenvalues $+1,-1$, chosen with $|x_-\rangle=P|x_+\rangle$. Their first-moment expectations agree when the first moment commutes with $P$. Their average squared error is therefore

$$
 \frac{\langle x_+|K|x_+\rangle+\langle x_-|K|x_-\rangle}{2}
 =1+\frac{\langle x_+|E^{(2)}|x_+\rangle+
 \langle x_-|E^{(2)}|x_-\rangle}{2}\ge1.
\tag{M.6.13cc.5}
$$

Hence every strict improvement on one must use $g=1$. This is a direct reduction preserving the original arbitrary-real-charge scope, not an assumed lattice restriction or discarded-coherence argument.

**II. Complete gap-one parameterization.**

Set $Q_R=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)$, $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$. Write

$$
 \sigma=\begin{pmatrix}p&c\\\bar c&q\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 p,q\ge0,\quad p+q=1,\quad |c|^2\le pq,
 \qquad M=aI+\beta Z,
\tag{M.6.13cc.6}
$$

where $a,\beta$ are arbitrary real numbers. In ordered basis
$(|0,0\rangle,|0,1\rangle,|1,0\rangle,|1,1\rangle,|2,0\rangle,|2,1\rangle)$,
$H=U^*(I\otimes Z)U$ has fixed endpoint values $+1,-1$ and two independent blocks

$$
 H_1=\begin{pmatrix}-A&w\\\bar w&A\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 H_2=\begin{pmatrix}-B&v\\\bar v&B\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad A^2+|w|^2=B^2+|v|^2=1.
\tag{M.6.13cc.7}
$$

Every conserving unitary gives exactly such blocks. Conversely every pair of such Hermitian involutions is unitarily conjugate to $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1)$ within its own total-charge block and therefore has a conserving-unitary implementation on the same six-dimensional joint space. Endpoint unitary phases do not change $H$.

Its conditional moment $F=\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma)H]$ is exactly

$$
 F=\begin{pmatrix}
 p-qA&cw&0\\
 \bar c\bar w&pA-qB&cv\\
 0&\bar c\bar v&pB-q
 \end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{M.6.13cc.B1}
$$

No balance, purity, phase alignment, equal-block, or centered-pointer ansatz has been imposed. Because $M^2=(a^2+\beta^2)I+2a\beta Z$, the complete noise is

$$
 K=X^2+(a^2+\beta^2)I-2aX+2a\beta F-\beta\{X,F\}.
 \tag{M.6.13cc.B2}
$$

The map defining $F$ is unital and positive, so $-I\le F\le I$.

There is an exact sign reduction for $\beta$. Let $J$ reverse system charges 0 and 2, so $JXJ=X$. The replacement

$$
 p'=q,\ c'=\bar c,\ A'=B,\ B'=A,\ w'=-\bar v,\ v'=-\bar w
\tag{M.6.13cc.8}
$$

is admissible and yields $F'=-JFJ$. Thus the model with pointer $(a,-\beta)$ and moment $F'$ has noise $JKJ$. It is sufficient to establish the lower bound for $\beta\ge0$, without changing any resource or dimension.

**III. A universal single-input ellipse.**

Define

$$
 T=\frac{\sqrt3}{2},\quad s=T-\frac12=\frac{\sqrt3-1}{2},\quad
 h=\frac{1-T}{2},\quad C=\frac{\sqrt T}{2},\quad
 k=\frac{\sqrt{T(1-T)}}2=Cs,\quad L=\frac{T}{\sqrt2}.
\tag{M.6.13cc.9}
$$

Here $s^2=1-T$, $s^2+s=1/2$, $L^2/C^2=2T$, and $T-C^2=3\sqrt3/8$.

Use the fixed system input

$$
 |\psi\rangle=\sqrt T\,|1\rangle-
 \sqrt{1-T}\,(|0\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2.
\tag{M.6.13cc.10}
$$

It obeys $\langle X\rangle_\psi=0$ and $\langle X^2\rangle_\psi=T$. Set

$$
 b=\langle F\rangle_\psi\in[-1,1],\qquad
 d=\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi|XF|\psi\rangle.
\tag{M.6.13cc.11}
$$

**Lemma.** For every model (M.6.13cc.B1),

$$
 d\le C\sqrt{1-b^2}.\tag{M.6.13cc.B3}
$$

This is one-sided; the analogous claim with $|d|$ would be false.

**Exact support reduction.**

For an arbitrary real support parameter $\xi$, maximize $d-\xi b$ over the two independent blocks and the apparatus coherence at fixed $p$. The maxima of each linear form on $A^2+|w|^2=1$ and $B^2+|v|^2=1$ are Euclidean norms. They increase with $|c|$, so their common maximum occurs at $|c|=\sqrt{pq}$; independent block phases realize both maxima. Completing each norm's square gives the exact support

$$
 \begin{split}
 f_\xi(p)={}&-k+\xi h(q-p)\\
 &+\sqrt{[\xi(hq+Tp)+kq]^2+L^2pq}\\
 &+\sqrt{[\xi(Tq+hp)-kp]^2+L^2pq}.
 \end{split}\tag{M.6.13cc.B4}
$$

The support reduction can also be checked directly from the complete moment matrix:
$$
\begin{aligned}
b&=h(p-q)+(Tp-hq)A+(hp-Tq)B+\sqrt2\sqrt T\,s\operatorname{Re}(cv-cw),\\
d&=\frac T{\sqrt2}\operatorname{Re}(cw+cv)-\frac{\sqrt T\,s}{2}(1-qA-pB).
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13cc.12}
$$
The first raw block norm is $\sqrt{[\xi(hq-Tp)+kq]^2+[L+\sqrt2\sqrt T\,s\xi]^2pq}$; using $k^2=Th/2$ gives its displayed completed square. The second block is analogous. Thus the certificate bounds the full physical block optimization, including arbitrary phases, rather than an unrelated radical inequality.

The next section supplies a finite exact polynomial certificate for

$$
 f_\xi(p)\le\sqrt{C^2+\xi^2}
 \quad(0\le p\le1,\ \xi\in\mathbb R),\tag{M.6.13cc.B5}
$$

with finite-parameter equality only when $\xi=0,p=1/2$. Taking the infimum of $\sqrt{C^2+\xi^2}+\xi b$ over $\xi$ gives (M.6.13cc.B3), including its continuous endpoint values when $b=\pm1$.

**IV. Exact polynomial/Bernstein certificate.**

The following four exact Bernstein coefficient matrices provide the finite polynomial certificate. No numerical optimization is used.

The symmetry $f_{-\xi}(1-p)=f_\xi(p)$ permits $\xi\ge0$. Put

$$
 x=\xi/C,\quad y=\sqrt{1+x^2},\quad z=2p-1,\quad
 \begin{array}{ll}
 A_0=x(hq+Tp)+sq,&B_0=x(Tq+hp)-sp,\\
 C_0=2Tpq,&W=y+s+xhz.
 \end{array}
\tag{M.6.13cc.13}
$$

Dividing (M.6.13cc.B5) by $C$ reduces it to

$$
 \sqrt{A_0^2+C_0}+\sqrt{B_0^2+C_0}\le W.\tag{M.6.13cc.B6}
$$

Here $W>0$, since $y\ge x\ge0$, $|z|\le1$, and $h<1$. Define

$$
 E=W^2-A_0^2-B_0^2-2C_0,\qquad
 D=E^2-4(A_0^2+C_0)(B_0^2+C_0).
\tag{M.6.13cc.14}
$$

It is enough to prove $E\ge0,D\ge0$; both squarings then preserve the inequality direction. Rationalize

$$
 x=\frac{2u}{1-u^2},\qquad y=\frac{1+u^2}{1-u^2},\qquad 0\le u<1,
\tag{M.6.13cc.15}
$$

and set $\widehat E=(1-u^2)^2E$, $\widehat D=(1-u^2)^4D$. Reducing coefficients by $s^2+s=1/2$ gives polynomials of bidegrees $(4,2)$ and $(8,4)$.

On $(u,v)\in[0,1]^2$, the following four polynomials have the indicated exact tensor-product Bernstein certificates:

- $\widehat E(u,v)$: all 15 degree-$(4,2)$ coefficients strictly positive.
- $\widehat E(u,-v)$: all 15 degree-$(4,2)$ coefficients strictly positive.
- $\widehat D(u,v)$: all 45 degree-$(8,4)$ coefficients nonnegative.
- $\widehat D(u,-v)-(T/2)(u-v)^2$: all 45 degree-$(8,4)$ coefficients nonnegative.

Every coefficient is affine in $s$. Its sign is certified by rational arithmetic using

$$
 366/1000<s<367/1000,
\tag{M.6.13cc.16}
$$

which follows by squaring $2s+1=\sqrt3$. Exact coefficient reconstruction is verified against the polynomial definitions above. Since every Bernstein basis polynomial on the unit square is nonnegative, these are finite algebraic certificates of $E>0,D\ge0$, proving (M.6.13cc.B6) and (M.6.13cc.B5).

For a polynomial of bidegree $(n,m)$, the entry $(i,j)$ below multiplies $\binom ni u^i(1-u)^{n-i}\binom m j v^j(1-v)^{m-j}$. Rows are indexed $i=0,\ldots,n$ and columns $j=0,\ldots,m$. The exact matrices are
$$
\mathcal B[\widehat E(u,v)]=\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{2}s & \frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{2}s & 1+2s \\
\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{2}s & \frac{5}{8}+s & \frac{3}{4}+3s \\
\frac{15}{16}+\frac{5}{6}s & \frac{11}{16}+\frac{11}{6}s & \frac{1}{3}+4s \\
\frac{21}{16}+\frac{3}{2}s & \frac{21}{16}+2s & \frac{1}{2}+3s \\
\frac{21}{8}-s & \frac{29}{8}-3s & 3-4s
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13cc.17}
$$
$$
\mathcal B[\widehat E(u,-v)]=\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{2}s & \frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{2}s & 1+2s \\
\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{2}s & \frac{7}{8} & \frac{5}{4}+s \\
\frac{15}{16}+\frac{5}{6}s & \frac{19}{16}-\frac{1}{6}s & \frac{4}{3} \\
\frac{21}{16}+\frac{3}{2}s & \frac{21}{16}+s & \frac{1}{2}+s \\
\frac{21}{8}-s & \frac{13}{8}+s & -1+4s
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13cc.18}
$$
$$
\mathcal B[\widehat D(u,v)]=\begin{pmatrix}
0 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{3}{2} & 3 \\
0 & \frac{1}{64}+\frac{1}{32}s & \frac{17}{32}+\frac{1}{16}s & \frac{55}{32}-\frac{5}{16}s & \frac{15}{4}-\frac{3}{2}s \\
\frac{13}{112}+\frac{5}{56}s & \frac{33}{224}+\frac{17}{112}s & \frac{109}{168}+\frac{1}{7}s & \frac{55}{28}-\frac{3}{4}s & \frac{127}{28}-\frac{25}{7}s \\
\frac{39}{112}+\frac{15}{56}s & \frac{393}{896}+\frac{143}{448}s & \frac{421}{448}+\frac{5}{32}s & \frac{143}{64}-\frac{257}{224}s & 5-\frac{73}{14}s \\
\frac{197}{280}+\frac{71}{140}s & \frac{1053}{1120}+\frac{37}{80}s & \frac{807}{560}+\frac{31}{168}s & \frac{189}{80}-\frac{219}{280}s & \frac{299}{70}-\frac{134}{35}s \\
\frac{67}{56}+\frac{3}{4}s & \frac{1419}{896}+\frac{345}{448}s & \frac{2537}{1344}+\frac{101}{96}s & \frac{783}{448}+\frac{501}{224}s & \frac{25}{28}+\frac{69}{14}s \\
\frac{47}{28}+\frac{5}{4}s & \frac{845}{448}+\frac{519}{224}s & \frac{1007}{672}+\frac{521}{112}s & -\frac{103}{224}+\frac{1137}{112}s & -\frac{85}{14}+\frac{167}{7}s \\
\frac{3}{2}+\frac{13}{4}s & \frac{3}{2}+\frac{21}{4}s & \frac{5}{6}+\frac{203}{24}s & -2+\frac{127}{8}s & -12+40s \\
5-8s & \frac{69}{8}-\frac{65}{4}s & \frac{53}{4}-\frac{83}{3}s & \frac{65}{4}-36s & 8-16s
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13cc.19}
$$
$$
\mathcal B[\widehat D(u,-v)-(T/2)(u-v)^2]=\begin{pmatrix}
0 & 0 & \frac{11}{24}-\frac{1}{12}s & \frac{11}{8}-\frac{1}{4}s & \frac{11}{4}-\frac{1}{2}s \\
0 & 0 & \frac{11}{24}-\frac{1}{12}s & \frac{77}{64}+\frac{5}{32}s & \frac{33}{16}+\frac{9}{8}s \\
\frac{3}{28}+\frac{1}{14}s & \frac{3}{28}+\frac{1}{14}s & \frac{15}{28}-\frac{1}{12}s & \frac{235}{224}+\frac{47}{112}s & \frac{157}{112}+\frac{121}{56}s \\
\frac{9}{28}+\frac{3}{14}s & \frac{249}{896}+\frac{115}{448}s & \frac{811}{1344}+\frac{1}{672}s & \frac{205}{224}+\frac{3}{8}s & \frac{9}{8}+\frac{45}{28}s \\
\frac{13}{20}+\frac{2}{5}s & \frac{533}{1120}+\frac{319}{560}s & \frac{881}{1680}+\frac{71}{168}s & \frac{179}{280}+\frac{29}{70}s & \frac{43}{40}+\frac{9}{140}s \\
\frac{31}{28}+\frac{4}{7}s & \frac{715}{896}+\frac{317}{448}s & \frac{163}{448}+\frac{229}{224}s & \frac{37}{224}+\frac{7}{8}s & \frac{73}{112}-\frac{23}{56}s \\
\frac{173}{112}+\frac{55}{56}s & \frac{641}{448}+\frac{23}{224}s & \frac{457}{672}+\frac{137}{336}s & \frac{15}{56} & \frac{1}{16}+\frac{1}{8}s \\
\frac{21}{16}+\frac{23}{8}s & \frac{91}{64}+\frac{35}{32}s & \frac{79}{96}+\frac{7}{16}s & \frac{65}{64}-\frac{67}{32}s & 0 \\
\frac{19}{4}-\frac{17}{2}s & \frac{5}{4} & -\frac{31}{24}+\frac{21}{4}s & -\frac{1}{4}+s & 0
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13cc.20}

Expanding these finite Bernstein sums and reducing $s^2=1/2-s$ reconstructs the polynomial definitions exactly. All thirty $E$ coefficients are strictly positive. The $D$ matrices have respectively forty-two and thirty-nine strictly positive coefficients, with three and six zeros. Each nonzero coefficient is positive throughout $366/1000<s<367/1000$, as direct rational endpoint substitution shows. This supplies every coefficient used in the certificate and its equality argument.

For equality: in either $\widehat D$ certificate, its degree-$(8,4)$ coefficient at index $(2,0)$ is strictly positive. For $0<u<1,0\le v<1$ this basis term is strictly positive. At $v=1,u<1$, the coefficient at $(0,4)$ is strictly positive. At $u=0,v>0$, the coefficient at $(0,2)$ is strictly positive. Consequently the only zero for finite $x$, hence $u<1$, is $u=v=0$. The added square on the negative half cannot create other zeros. Thus finite equality in (M.6.13cc.B5) forces $\xi=0,p=1/2$.

**V. Global bound, attainment, and forced endpoint resource.**

For $\beta\ge0$, (M.6.13cc.B2) and the lemma give

$$
 \begin{split}
 r&\ge\langle K\rangle_\psi\\
 &\ge T+a^2+\beta^2+2a\beta b-2\beta C\sqrt{1-b^2}\\
 &=T-C^2+(a+\beta b)^2+
 (\beta\sqrt{1-b^2}-C)^2\\
 &\ge\frac{3\sqrt3}{8}.
 \end{split}\tag{M.6.13cc.B7}
$$

The sign reduction proves the same result for negative $\beta$. Other charge gaps had error at least one.

An attaining device has $p=c=1/2$, $a=0$,

$$
 A=B=2-\sqrt3,\qquad w=v=\sqrt{4\sqrt3-6},\qquad
 \beta=C=\sqrt{\sqrt3/8}.
\tag{M.6.13cc.21}
$$

Its full noise spectrum is

$$
 \frac{3\sqrt3-4}{8},\qquad
 \frac{5\sqrt3-4}{8},\qquad
 \frac{3\sqrt3}{8}.
\tag{M.6.13cc.22}
$$

For completeness the same two-dimensional apparatus carries its actual readout. Set $Q_R=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)$, $\sigma=|+\rangle\langle+|$ and $M=C\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$. In the ordered six-dimensional basis used above let $U_\theta$ be identity on the two endpoint total-charge spaces and the real rotation
$$
R_\theta=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}
\tag{M.6.13cc.23}
$$
on each ordered pair $(|0,1\rangle,|1,0\rangle)$ and $(|1,1\rangle,|2,0\rangle)$, where $\cos(2\theta)=2-\sqrt3$ and $\sin(2\theta)=\sqrt{4\sqrt3-6}>0$. The identity $\cos^2(2\theta)+\sin^2(2\theta)=1$ gives such a rotation. Its total-charge blocks prove conservation. Its two retained outcomes are the actual charged-qubit projectors $P_j=|j\rangle\langle j|$; the subnormalized joint output is $(I\otimes P_j)U_\theta(\rho\otimes\sigma)U_\theta^*(I\otimes P_j)$. No renormalization, postselection or neutral pointer is appended.

This matches (M.6.13cc.B7), with both recorded outcomes retained on the same charged qubit.

Equality in (M.6.13cc.B7) cannot have $|b|=1$, since then its last square equals $C^2>0$. Otherwise equality in (M.6.13cc.B3) uses the finite minimizing support parameter $\xi=-Cb/\sqrt{1-b^2}$. Equality in (M.6.13cc.B5) forces $\xi=0,p=1/2$, hence $b=0,a=0,\beta=C$. At $\xi=0,p=1/2$, the support is strictly increasing in $|c|$, so equality also forces $|c|=1/2$. The reference state is therefore pure and balanced; full charge dephasing gives $I/2$, and its exact asymmetry is $\log2$. Negative $\beta$ is covered by the resource-preserving sign symmetry.

For any untouched spectator, the tested noise is $K\otimes I$, whose largest eigenvalue is the same. Thus the proof imposes the original all-input/spectator error rather than a selected-state surrogate: one fixed state supplies a valid universal lower bound, and the matching witness's entire spectrum supplies the upper bound.

**VI. Explicit positive-budget witnesses.**

Write

$$
 r_0=3\sqrt3/8,\quad C^2=\sqrt3/8,\quad
 s_0=(\sqrt3-1)/2,\quad \alpha_0=(3-\sqrt3)/2.
\tag{M.6.13cc.24}
$$

Keep the same charge gap, total-charge rotations, two retained outcomes and complete dimension two as the endpoint witness. For $0\le t\le1$, set

$$
 \sigma_t=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&\sqrt t\\\sqrt t&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 M_t=C\sqrt t\,Z.
\tag{M.6.13cc.25}
$$

For this family $h_2(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$, with $0\log0=0$. To verify the entire operational error, set $z(t)=1-\alpha_0t$. In the $(e,m,o)$ basis the singleton block on $e$ is $z(t)+C^2t$, and the block on $\operatorname{span}\{m,o\}$ is
$$
\begin{pmatrix}z(t)+C^2t&-C\sqrt t\,s_0\\
-C\sqrt t\,s_0&C^2t\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13cc.32}
$$
Its plus eigenvalue dominates the singleton because $\sqrt{z(t)^2+4C^2s_0^2t}\ge z(t)$. Thus the next formula is the actual all-input noise norm, including its third direction.

The actual full asymmetry and actual squared all-input error are exactly

$$
 b(t)=\log2-h_2\left(\frac{1+\sqrt t}{2}\right),
\tag{M.6.13cc.26}
$$

$$
 r(t)=C^2t+\frac{1-\alpha_0 t+\sqrt{(1-\alpha_0 t)^2+4C^2s_0^2t}}2.
 \tag{M.6.13cc.C1}
$$

No state-quality substitute appears in (M.6.13cc.C1). Its entire noise spectrum is evaluated by the full two-by-two noise block of this same device; the remaining third eigenvalue is no larger.

**Uniform positive-budget interval.**

The entropy has the convergent nonnegative series

$$
 b(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{t^n}{2n(2n-1)}\le t\log2.
\tag{M.6.13cc.27}
$$

For the square root in (M.6.13cc.C1), write $\zeta=4C^2s_0^2$, so its radicand is
$1+(\zeta-2\alpha_0)t+\alpha_0^2t^2$. It is positive on $[0,1]$. Its square-root second derivative has the sign of

$$
 4\alpha_0^2-(\zeta-2\alpha_0)^2=\zeta(4\alpha_0-\zeta)>0.
\tag{M.6.13cc.28}
$$

Thus $r(t)$ is convex. Since $r(0)=1$ and $r(1)=r_0$,

$$
 r(t)\le1-(1-r_0)t.\tag{M.6.13cc.C2}
$$

Given any budget $b>0$, choose

$$
 t=\min\{b/\log2,1\}.
\tag{M.6.13cc.29}
$$

This is an actual dimension-two device of asymmetry at most $b$, with squared error at most the explicit threshold

$$
 R_{\rm explicit}(b)=1-(1-r_0)\min\{b/\log2,1\}<1.
\tag{M.6.13cc.30}
$$

At complete dimension one the pointer is a scalar $m$, so its Heisenberg pointer is $mI$ for every unitary. Its squared worst-case noise is $\|mI-X\|^2=\max\{(m-1)^2,m^2,(m+1)^2\}\ge1$. This proves the strict lower dimension bound for every error below one.

Consequently, for every prescribed squared error

$$
 R_{\rm explicit}(b)\le r<1,
\tag{M.6.13cc.31}
$$

the minimum complete apparatus dimension is exactly two, for both at-most-error and exact-error conventions. The lower dimension bound is the scalar-pointer floor at dimension one. For exact errors, keep $\sigma_t$ and the conserving unitary fixed and continuously recalibrate the two original retained labels from $M=0$ to $M_t$; the error moves continuously from one to $r(t)\le R_{\rm explicit}(b)$, so every intervening error is attained.

The exact expression $r(t)$ in (M.6.13cc.C1), or choosing the unique $t$ satisfying $b(t)=b$ for $0<b<\log2$, generally gives a stronger interval. Neither refinement proves that this family minimizes error at its budget.

**Lower boundary.**

The endpoint bound above proves $r\ge r_0$ for every two-dimensional apparatus, independently of budget, and forces asymmetry $\log2$ at equality. Therefore no dimension-two device at budget $b<\log2$ attains $r_0$. No numerical gap between its budget-constrained infimum and $r_0$ is supplied by this corollary.

This is a complete-dimension restriction, distinct from a charge-range cap or the unrestricted entropy infimum. It does not determine the global spin-one entropy curve or the optimum budget-dependent two-dimensional error curve. $\square$

### M.6.13cd Exact unrestricted spin-one operational coefficient

<a id="theorem-m613cd-exact-unrestricted-spin-one-operational-coefficient"></a>**Theorem M.6.13cd (Exact Unrestricted Spin-One Operational Coefficient).** Let $z_*$ be the unique root in $(1/\sqrt5,1)$ of
$$
3(1-z^2)\operatorname{atanh}z=\sqrt{9z^2-1},
\quad
\lambda_* =\frac{4z_*}{\sqrt{9z_*^2-1}}-1,
\quad
\chi_* =\frac{1-\sqrt{1-z_*^2}}{1+\sqrt{1-z_*^2}},
\quad
c_* =\frac{4\operatorname{atanh}z_*}{3z_*+\sqrt{9z_*^2-1}}=c_{\mathrm{loc}}.
\tag{M.6.13cd.1}
$$
Then every finite complete reference in the unrestricted spin-one class satisfies
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge c_*\mathfrak q_{\lambda_*}(\sigma)\ge c_*u,
\qquad c_{\mathrm{proj}}=c_{\mathrm{loc}}
=0.83487144924356266269\ldots.
\tag{M.6.13cd.2}
$$
Arbitrary real charges, degeneracies, complex gap-two coherences, mixed states, correlations, charged pointers, neutral factors and retained flags are included. The same $\lambda_*$ is used in every retained block. No finite-quality optimizer or uniqueness assertion is made. The equality uses the reflected-qubit operational upper construction below; the unrestricted lower bound is proved by the complete rational certificate below.

**Complete reference and normalized source.** The system charge and observable are
$$
Q_S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2),\qquad
X=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\1&0&1\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad u=1-\epsilon_\infty^2.
\tag{M.6.13cd.S1}
$$
Here $\epsilon_\infty$ is the worst-case, all-input Ozawa RMS error. The complete finite reference contains every charged or neutral pointer, initial correlation and retained flag. Its charge $Q$ may have arbitrary finite real eigenvalues, and
$\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)=D(\sigma\Vert\mathcal G_Q\sigma)$ uses natural logarithms. Put
$|e\rangle=(|0\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $|m\rangle=|1\rangle$, and
$\rho_\lambda=(1-\lambda)|e\rangle\langle e|+\lambda|m\rangle\langle m|$.
Since $\{\rho_\lambda,X\}=X$ and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho_\lambda X^2=1$, every actual conserving model obeys
$$
u\le\mathfrak q_\lambda(\sigma):=
\sup_{N=N^*,\,[N,Q_S+Q]=0}
\bigl\{\operatorname{Tr}[(X\otimes\sigma)N]
-\operatorname{Tr}[(\rho_\lambda\otimes\sigma)N^2]\bigr\}.
\tag{M.6.13cd.S2}
$$
Compression of an initially pure neutral pointer preserves the first moment and decreases the second moment to at least the square of the first. Thus the variational expression is a valid relaxation for complete actual pointers. It is not the separate state-discrimination quality.

**Weighted source and heat identities.** For a smooth positive definite matrix source $F_\theta$ on the circle, normalized by $\int\operatorname{Tr}F=1$, let $\tau=\int F$, $U_\theta=e^{iQ_S\theta}$, and
$$
R(F)=\int U_\theta\rho_\lambda U_\theta^*\otimes F_\theta,\qquad
D(F)=\frac12\int U_\theta XU_\theta^*\otimes F_\theta,
\quad
\mathfrak q_\lambda(F)=\sup_{N=N^*}\{2\operatorname{Tr}DN-\operatorname{Tr}RN^2\}.
\tag{M.6.13cd.S5}
$$
Here $\rho_\lambda=(1-\lambda)|e\rangle\langle e|+\lambda|m\rangle\langle m|$, with the system vectors just defined. On $\operatorname{span}\{e,m\}$, the inequality
$$
-M_\lambda\rho_\lambda\le X/2\le M_\lambda\rho_\lambda,
\qquad M_\lambda=\frac1{2\sqrt{\lambda(1-\lambda)}}
\tag{M.6.13cd.S6}
$$
is an elementary positive $2\times2$ determinant test, and both sides vanish on the orthogonal complement. Hence $-M_\lambda R\le D\le M_\lambda R$. For faithful $F$, $R>0$, because its lower bound contains the strictly positive system average $\operatorname{diag}((1-\lambda)/2,\lambda,(1-\lambda)/2)$. The Sylvester optimizer satisfies
$$
RN+NR=2D,\qquad
N=2\int_0^\infty e^{-sR}De^{-sR}\,ds,\qquad
-M_\lambda I\le N\le M_\lambda I.
\tag{M.6.13cd.S7}
$$
System parity makes $R$ even and $D$ odd, so uniqueness makes $N$ odd. The same conclusions on the support of a singular $R$, followed by zero extension, show that the supremum may always be restricted to this fixed compact norm ball. Thus $\mathfrak q_\lambda$ is continuous in every finite-dimensional source, including singular limits. For a total-charge-twirled source the supported optimizer also commutes with total charge, so this matrix variational quantity equals the conserving dual.

For a system-coefficient matrix $T$, write
$$
\Xi_\theta(T)=\operatorname{Tr}_S[(U_\theta XU_\theta^*\otimes I)T],\qquad
\Psi_\theta(T)=\operatorname{Tr}_S[(U_\theta\rho_\lambda U_\theta^*\otimes I)T],\qquad
\delta T=i[Q_S\otimes I,T].
$$
Put $K_N=\Xi(N)-\Psi(N^2)$, $M_N=\Psi((\delta N)^2)$, and $W_N=K_N''+M_N$. The map $\Psi$ is positive. Writing
$$
N=\begin{pmatrix}0&a&0\\a^*&0&b\\0&b^*&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
a=\sqrt2\alpha,\quad b=\sqrt2\beta,
$$
ordered multiplication gives, for general $\lambda$,
$$
\begin{split}
W_0&=(1-\lambda)\alpha\alpha^*+2\lambda\alpha^*\alpha
       +2\lambda\beta\beta^*+(1-\lambda)\beta^*\beta,\\
W_1&=-(\alpha+\beta),\qquad W_2=3(1-\lambda)\alpha\beta,
\qquad W_{-n}=W_n^*.
\end{split}
\tag{M.6.13cd.S8}
$$
All other modes vanish. For example, the mode-two coefficient of $-\Psi(N^2)$ is $-(1-\lambda)ab/2$; differentiating twice and adding the mode-two coefficient $-(1-\lambda)ab/2$ of $M_N$ gives $3(1-\lambda)ab/2$. No block commutativity is used.

Sylvester stationarity says $\int\operatorname{Tr}F[\Xi(T)-\Psi(NT+TN)]=0$ for every Hermitian $T$. Use $T=\delta^2N$ and
$\delta^2(N^2)=(\delta^2N)N+N\delta^2N+2(\delta N)^2$ to obtain
$$
\int\operatorname{Tr}F(K_N''+2M_N)=0.
\tag{M.6.13cd.S9}
$$
For $F_t=e^{t\partial_\theta^2}F$, stationarity removes the derivative of the optimizer. If $E(F)=\int\operatorname{Tr}(FM_N)$ and $H(F)=\int\operatorname{Tr}(F\log F)-\operatorname{Tr}(\tau\log\tau)$, integration by parts yields
$$
-\frac d{dt}\mathfrak q_\lambda(F_t)=2E(F_t),\qquad
-\frac d{dt}H(F_t)=I_{\mathrm{BKM}}(F_t).
\tag{M.6.13cd.S10}
$$

**Exact continuum auxiliary.** Let $L_C(T)=CT$, $R_C(T)=TC$, and use the Hilbert–Schmidt inner product, integrated with normalized circle measure for source functions. For faithful $G=\sqrt F>0$, diagonalize $G$ pointwise, with eigenvalues $g_i>0$, and put $t_{ij}=(g_i-g_j)/(g_i+g_j)$. The divided-difference formula is
$$
I_{\mathrm{BKM}}(F)=4\int\sum_{i,j}
 \frac{\operatorname{atanh}t_{ij}}{t_{ij}}|G'_{ij}|^2,
\qquad \left.\frac{\operatorname{atanh}t}{t}\right|_{t=0}:=1.
\tag{M.6.13cd.B1}
$$
For the continuum auxiliary put $S=L_G+R_G$, $A=L_G-R_G$, $C=[G,G']$, and $d\mu(u)=\sqrt u\,du/2$ on $[0,1]$. The commuting spectral representation gives
$$
I_{\mathrm{BKM}}(F)=4\|G'\|_2^2
+4\int_0^1\langle C,(S^2-uA^2)^{-1}C\rangle\,d\mu(u).
\tag{M.6.13cd.3}
$$
The inverse eigenvalues have positive denominators $(x+y)^2-u(x-y)^2$ for $x,y>0$. For fixed $0<\chi<1$, real $\gamma$, and Hermitian $Y$, use the bounded test $Z(u)=i\gamma Y/(1-u\chi)$. Completing the square inside the $\int$ yields
$$
I_{\mathrm{BKM}}\ge4\|G'\|_2^2
+4\int\left[-2id\operatorname{Tr}Y[G,G']-s\|\{G,Y\}\|_2^2+a\|[G,Y]\|_2^2\right],
\tag{M.6.13cd.4}
$$
where, with $L(\chi)=\operatorname{atanh}(\sqrt\chi)/\sqrt\chi$ and $F(\chi)=[L(\chi)-1]/\chi$,
$$
d=\gamma F(\chi),\qquad s=\gamma^2L'(\chi),\qquad a=\gamma^2F'(\chi),
\quad L'(\chi)=\frac{1/(1-\chi)-L(\chi)}{2\chi}.
$$
For nonzero $\gamma$, $0<a<s$. All circle integrals are normalized. This inequality is valid directly for every faithful source, regardless of its dimension or spectrum.

**Rational stationary family.** For formal parameters $(\lambda,\chi)$ near $(\lambda_*,\chi_*)$, define
$$
\begin{gathered}
\ell=1+\lambda,\quad b=3\lambda-1,\quad
T=\ell^2(1+\chi)^2-4b^2\chi,\\
E=\ell^2(\chi^2+1)+(38\lambda^2-20\lambda+6)\chi,
\qquad \overline L=\frac{(1+\chi)T}{(1-\chi)^2E},\\
c=\frac{T\overline L}{2\ell(1+\chi)},\quad\kappa=\frac2c,
\quad\gamma=\frac{T}{16b},\quad
f=\frac{\overline L-1}{\chi},\quad h=\frac{1/(1-\chi)-\overline L}{2\chi},\\
d=\gamma f,\qquad s=\gamma^2h,\qquad a=\gamma^2(h-f)/\chi.
\end{gathered}
\tag{M.6.13cd.5}
$$
These are rational functions used to construct the certificate. Away from the actual saddle, no claim is made that $\overline L$ equals the logarithmic function or that this family supplies an operational coefficient. At the true saddle,
$$
(-\chi^2+34\chi-1)\ell^2=64\chi,
\qquad L(\chi)=\frac{4(1+\chi)}{3\ell(1-\chi)^2}.
$$
The exact identities
$$
4E-3\ell T=b[(-\chi^2+34\chi-1)\ell^2-64\chi],
\quad
T(3\ell+4)-8\ell^2(1+\chi)^2=-b[(-\chi^2+34\chi-1)\ell^2-64\chi]
$$
therefore identify $\overline L=L(\chi_*)$, $c=c_*$, and all three coefficients in (M.6.13cd.5) with the valid continuum coefficients in (M.6.13cd.4). They are verified as polynomial identities, not through decimal substitution.

**Complete Fourier form.** Set $M^2=[4\lambda(1-\lambda)]^{-1}$. With odd optimizer blocks $\sqrt2\alpha,\sqrt2\beta$, use the positive localizers
$$
\Lambda_0=M^2I-2\alpha^*\alpha-2\beta\beta^*,\qquad
\Lambda_1=\begin{pmatrix}M^2I-2\alpha\alpha^*&-2\alpha\beta\\
-2\beta^*\alpha^*&M^2I-2\beta^*\beta\end{pmatrix}.
$$
The exact weighted potential is

$$
W_0=(1-\lambda)\alpha\alpha^*+2\lambda\alpha^*\alpha+2\lambda\beta\beta^*+(1-\lambda)\beta^*\beta,
$$

$W_1=-(\alpha+\beta)$, $W_2=3(1-\lambda)\alpha\beta$, and $W_{-j}=W_j^*$. Put $Y_1=\alpha-\beta,Y_{-1}=Y_1^*$, all other modes zero. The form is
$$
\mathcal Q(G)=\kappa\|G'\|_2^2+\langle G,\mathcal J_WG\rangle
+\kappa\int[-2id\operatorname{Tr}Y[G,G']-s\|\{G,Y\}\|_2^2+a\|[G,Y]\|_2^2].
\tag{M.6.13cd.6}
$$
Here $\mathcal J_C=(L_C+R_C)/2$, $\mathcal S_C=L_C+R_C$, and $\operatorname{ad}_C=L_C-R_C$. Its ordered Fourier blocks are $\mathcal L_{nm}=\kappa n^2\mathbf1_{n=m}+\mathcal U_{nm}+\mathcal V_{nm}$, where
$$
\begin{split}
\mathcal U_{nm}&=\mathcal J_{W_{n-m}}-\kappa d(n+m)\operatorname{ad}_{Y_{n-m}},&&|n-m|=1,\\
\mathcal V_{nm}&=\mathcal J_{W_{n-m}}-\kappa\sum_{j+k=n-m}
(s\mathcal S_{Y_j}\mathcal S_{Y_k}-a\operatorname{ad}_{Y_j}\operatorname{ad}_{Y_k}),&&n-m\in\{0,\pm2\}.
\end{split}
$$
Absent coefficients vanish.

For clarity the complete all-mode constants are reconstructed, rather than inherited from a rounded dual. Let
$$
B=\frac1{1-\lambda}+\frac1{2\lambda},\quad
P_2=\frac9{8\lambda},\quad N_2=\frac3{16\lambda},\quad D_2=32M^2B,
$$
and set
$$
\begin{gathered}
a_0=1-8B\kappa s,\qquad U_0=M^2(1+8B\kappa a),\qquad
c_2=N_2+8\kappa sM^2,\\
\beta_{\rm rel}=\frac{P_2+D_2(\kappa s)^2+32\kappa s}{a_0}.
\end{gathered}
\tag{M.6.13cd.7}
$$
The ordered estimates below give

$$
a_0\mathcal J_{W_0}\le\mathcal V_0\le U_0I,
$$

$\mathcal V_0^2\le U_0\mathcal V_0$, $\|\mathcal V_{\pm2}G\|_2^2\le\beta_{\rm rel}\langle G,\mathcal V_0G\rangle$, and $\|\mathcal V_{\pm2}\|\le c_2$. The parameter box below verifies $a_0>0$, $0<a<s$, and $P_2D_2<256$; thus the cross-term bound $\sqrt{P_2D_2}<16$ is rigorous. It also verifies $2M^2<(153/100)^2$ and $d>0$. The adjacent bound is

$$
\|\mathcal U_{nm}\|\le\sqrt2M\max(1,2\kappa d|n+m|).
$$

The localizers imply $0\le W_0\le M^2I$, $\|\alpha\|,\|\beta\|\le M/\sqrt2$,
$\|W_2\|\le N_2$ and
$W_2^*W_2,W_2W_2^*\le P_2W_0$. To retain the ordered information, use
$$
(A-B)^*(A-B)\le(1/p+1/q)(pA^*A+qB^*B),\qquad p,q>0.
$$
The difference is the square of $\sqrt{p/q}A+\sqrt{q/p}B$. Applying the weights
$(2\lambda,1-\lambda)$ and their reversal to $y=\alpha-\beta$ and $y^*$ gives

$$
y^*y,yy^*\le BW_0,
$$

$\|y\|^2\le2M^2$, and
$\|\mathcal S_yG\|_2^2,\|\operatorname{ad}_yG\|_2^2
\le4B\langle G,\mathcal J_{W_0}G\rangle$.
The two orientations therefore give
$a_0\mathcal J_{W_0}\le\mathcal V_0\le U_0I$ and
$\mathcal V_0^2\le U_0\mathcal V_0$.
For a gap-two block, expand
$s\mathcal S_y^2-a\operatorname{ad}_y^2
=(s-a)(L_y^2+R_y^2)+2(s+a)L_yR_y$.
Using $0<a<s$ and the same ordered estimate gives its squared relative bound
$D_2s^2$ and its operator norm bound $4s\|y\|^2$.
Combining it with the $W_2$ bound gives

$$
\|\mathcal V_{\pm2}G\|_2^2\le\beta_{\rm rel}\langle G,\mathcal V_0G\rangle
$$

and $\|\mathcal V_{\pm2}\|\le c_2$.
The cross term is bounded by $2\sqrt{P_2D_2}\,\kappa s<32\kappa s$.
For an adjacent block put $h=\kappa d(n+m)$. Its exact form is
$$
\mathcal U_{nm}
=L_{-(\alpha+\beta)/2-h(\alpha-\beta)}
+R_{-(\alpha+\beta)/2+h(\alpha-\beta)}.
$$
The identity $|1/2+h|+|1/2-h|=\max(1,2|h|)$ gives

$$
\|\mathcal U_{nm}\|\le\sqrt2M\max(1,2|h|).
$$

All estimates retain arbitrary complex ordered blocks.

Let $P$ project on constants, $Q=I-P$, and $D=-\kappa\partial_\theta^2$ on the mean-zero space. Define the full majorant
$$
K_{nm}=\begin{cases}
(153/100)\max(1,2\kappa d|n+m|)/(\kappa|nm|),&|n-m|=1,\\
c_2/(\kappa|nm|),&|n-m|=2,\\
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}\qquad n,m\ne0.
$$
Use $w_{\pm1}=1,w_{\pm2}=7/10,w_{\pm3}=2/5,w_{\pm4}=1/10$, and $w_n=1/50$ for $|n|\ge5$. Put $r_n=\sum_mK_{nm}w_m/w_n$ and $\rho_n=(1-r_n)^{-1}$. Exact interval arithmetic proves $r_1,\ldots,r_7<9/10$ throughout the box. For $n\ge7$ all neighbor weights agree and each summand decreases; negative rows reflect positive ones. Weighted Young and inverse order give
$$
Q\mathcal LQ\ge D_w\ge D/10,\qquad
(Q\mathcal LQ)^{-1}\le D_w^{-1},\qquad
(D_w^{-1}G)_n=\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa n^2}G_n.
\tag{M.6.13cd.8}
$$
This controls every Fourier mode. The correlated maximum has fixed branches in the box, since $6\kappa d<1<10\kappa d$, so the finite residual coefficients are rational functions there. Fourier-polynomial density supplies the entire $H^1$ form domain.

For constant $H=H^*$, define $(g_1)_n=-\mathcal U_{n0}H/(\kappa n^2)$ at $n=\pm1$ and
$(g_2)_n=-[\mathcal V_{n0}H+\sum_{m=\pm1}\mathcal U_{nm}(g_1)_m]/(\kappa n^2)$ at $n=\pm2$. For $G=H+g_1+g_2$, the exact residual is $Q\mathcal LG=r_3+r_4$, with $r_3=Q(\mathcal Vg_1+\mathcal Ug_2)$ on $\pm1,\pm3$ and $r_4=Q\mathcal Vg_2$ on $\pm2,\pm4$. Put $T_2=\sum_{n=\pm2}\langle(g_2)_n,\mathcal V_0(g_2)_n\rangle$. The diagonal inverse removes the odd/even cross term, and the complete constant Schur complement is bounded below by
$$
\begin{gathered}
\vartheta=\frac{\rho_2U_0/4+\rho_4\beta_{\rm rel}/16}{\kappa},\\
K_6=\mathcal Q(H+g_1+g_2)
-\sum_{n=\pm1,\pm3}\frac{\rho_{|n|}}{\kappa n^2}\|(r_3)_n\|_2^2
-\vartheta T_2.
\end{gathered}
\tag{M.6.13cd.9}
$$
Every residual term is retained; only witness degrees two, four and six occur.

**The exact degree-two face.** Put $A_0=\ell(1+\chi)/4$ and define charge-one polynomials
$$
f_1=A_0[\alpha-\beta,H]+\frac{b\chi}{2}\{\alpha+\beta,H\},\qquad
f_2=A_0\{\alpha-\beta,H\}+\frac b2[\alpha+\beta,H].
$$
The degree-two part $q_2$ of $K_6$ obeys the generic rational identity
$$
q_2=a_1\operatorname{Tr}(f_1^*f_1)+a_2\operatorname{Tr}(f_2^*f_2),
\qquad a_1=\frac{2(\ell/4-1/\kappa)}{b^2\chi^2},\quad a_2=\frac{\ell}{2b^2}.
\tag{M.6.13cd.10}
$$
Here is the cleared polynomial comparison, valid for all formal parameters where the displayed denominators are nonzero. Put
$$
D_f=(1-\chi)^2E,\quad N_f=(1+\chi)T-D_f,\quad
N_p=(1-\chi)E-(1+\chi)T,\quad C_f=\ell^2D_f-T^2.
$$
The off-diagonal and the two antisymmetric quadratic coefficients reduce respectively to
$$
\begin{aligned}
4b^2\chi D_f-TN_f
  &=(1+\chi)(C_f+\ell^2D_f\chi),\\
8b^2\chi-N_p&=2\ell^2\chi(1+\chi)^2,\\
8b^2\chi^2D_f-2N_f^2+(N_p-2N_f)D_f
  &=2C_f(1+\chi)^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13cd.F1}
$$
Each is a polynomial identity after substituting $\ell=1+\lambda$, $b=3\lambda-1$, $T$ and $E$. The symmetric diagonal coefficient follows directly from the definitions of $a_1,a_2$. Expanding the ordered four words $\alpha H,H\alpha,\beta H,H\beta$ and their adjoints therefore proves (M.6.13cd.10). Both face coefficients are strictly positive throughout the box below. This treats the semidefinite endpoint face exactly, including its zero direction.

**Finite parametric certificate.** The exact rational box is
$$
\begin{split}

**Complete rational Gram certificate.** Use the ordered noncommuting alphabet
$(\alpha,\alpha^*,\beta,\beta^*,H)$, coded $(0,1,2,3,4)$, with charges
$(1,-1,1,-1,0)$. Adjoint reverses a word, interchanges $0\leftrightarrow1$ and
$2\leftrightarrow3$, and fixes $4$. Words are ordered lexicographically in this alphabet.
For $d\ge1$ and integer $j$, let $\mathcal W_{d,j}$ be the following ordered list:
run through all length-$d$ words in $(0,1,2,3)$ in lexicographic order, retain charge $j$,
and for each word insert one $H$ at positions $0,1,\ldots,d$, in that order.
Let $\mathcal F_1=(f_1,f_2)$, $\mathcal F_{-1}=(f_1^*,f_2^*)$, and
$\mathcal F_j$ be empty for other $j$.
The four free bases, in order, are
$\mathcal F_1\mathbin\Vert\mathcal W_{3,1}$,
$\mathcal W_{3,3}$, $\mathcal W_{2,0}$, and $\mathcal W_{2,2}$.
Their dimensions are $98,32,24,12$.
For each localizer $\Lambda_r$, $r=0,1$, then each $d=1,2$, then each
$j=-d,-d+2,\ldots,d+2$, list components $s=0,\ldots,r$ in order.
For $d=1$ component $s$ contributes $\mathcal F_{j-2s}$;
for $d=2$ it contributes $\mathcal W_{2,j-2s}$.
Delete only empty combined lists. Each resulting basis vector retains its component $s$.
This gives the remaining twelve dimensions
$2,2,12,24,12,2,4,2,12,36,36,12$ and the names printed in the data below.
For a free block define

$$
\Gamma_{ij}=\operatorname{Tr}(v_i^*v_j);
$$

for a localizer block define

$$
\Gamma_{ij}=\operatorname{Tr}(v_i^*\Lambda_{s_i,s_j}v_j).
$$

All basis vectors have exactly one $H$.

Here is the complete finite reconstruction of the Gram functions.
Every numerator in the following indexed tables is an exact integer.
At the rational center

and fill its upper triangle with zeros.
A real trace word is represented by the lexicographically least cyclic rotation of
itself or its adjoint. A complex cyclic word uses rotations only.
All polynomial additions, products, adjoints and trace reductions below are literal
finite operations in this alphabet.

First form a $2\times2$ matrix $L$ by summing entries of every degree-one localizer
Gram whose two component indices agree, assigning indices $i,j$ to

For the remaining trace classes, enumerate slots in the first four free blocks in
that order; in the first block use indices $2,\ldots,97$, and in the others use all
indices. Within each block enumerate $(i,j)$ in lexicographic order with $i\le j$.
The trace polynomial of each such slot is one unit monomial class.
Assign each class its first such slot. Add its residual coefficient divided by one
for $i=j$, or by two for $i<j$, to that symmetric Gram entry.
This yields the center matrices $Q^0$ exactly, not by rounding a positive matrix.

There are $4,736$ nonzero complex cyclic target coefficients, and this reconstruction
makes every coefficient of the center target minus its Gram sum zero.
Every one of the $2,458$ admissible higher-degree real cyclic classes is covered:
these are all charge-zero words with four or six letters from $(0,1,2,3)$ and exactly
two inserted $H$ letters, reduced by cyclic rotation and adjoint.
The sixteen exact rational residual matrices $Q^0-CC^{\mathsf T}$ have strictly
positive diagonal-dominance margin, with every row margin exceeding $9\cdot10^{-10}$.
Thus every $Q^0$ is strictly positive definite.

For a variable point of (M.6.13cd.11), keep $Q^0$ initially, replace its first

same fixed slot. This does not change any other trace class or any lower degree.
The generic two-square identity proves all degree-two equations exactly.
