**Exact saddle and transfer.** The exact root is isolated $z_*$ in
$$
\left[\frac{543396061494967788075712375250}{10^{30}},
\frac{543396061494967788075712375251}{10^{30}}\right].
$$
Eighty positive terms of the $\operatorname{atanh}$ series and remainder bound $z^{161}/[161(1-z^2)]$ prove opposite signs at the endpoints. For $g(z)=3(1-z^2)\operatorname{atanh}z-\sqrt{9z^2-1}$,
$g'(z)=3-6z\operatorname{atanh}z-9z/\sqrt{9z^2-1}<0$ on $(1/\sqrt5,1)$.
Also $g(1/\sqrt5)>0$ follows from $\operatorname{atanh}z>z$, and
$g(z)\to-\sqrt8$ as $z\uparrow1$. Thus the root is unique. Exact outward square-root bounds then put $(\lambda_*,\chi_*)$ strictly inside (M.6.13cd.11). No decimal root is assumed.

Positive localizers, (M.6.13cd.10), and (M.6.13cd.12) prove $K_6\ge0$, since $\operatorname{Tr}(H^2Z_0^2)\ge0$. Together with the full mean-zero inverse, this proves $\mathcal Q\ge0$ on every Hermitian $H^1$ amplitude. More precisely, the same Schur completion retains $\mathcal Q(G)\ge10^{-5}[q_2(H)+\operatorname{Tr}(H^2Z_0^2)]$, where $H=\int G$. At the actual saddle, (M.6.13cd.5) identifies this form with the valid continuum BKM lower form, hence
$$
I_{\mathrm{BKM}}\ge2c_*E_{\mathrm{source}}.
\tag{M.6.13cd.14}
$$
The exact weighted heat identities $-H'=I_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ and $-\mathfrak q_{\lambda_*}'=2E_{\mathrm{source}}$ integrate to $H\ge c_*\mathfrak q_{\lambda_*}$. The normalized source proof above supplies the supported optimizer bound $M$. For an integer-charge reference the orbit $F_\theta=e^{iQ\theta}\sigma e^{-iQ\theta}$ has mean $\mathcal G_Q\sigma$, entropy $H(F)=\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)$ and the same total-charge-twirled dual. On the invariant mean support, positive heat has a strictly positive scalar kernel minimum, so it makes the source faithful. Finite-dimensional entropy continuity and the common compact optimizer ball then let the initial heat time decrease to zero. For arbitrary real charges, pinch into cosets modulo the integers. The system gaps are integers, so this leaves the dual unchanged; relative-entropy data processing cannot increase asymmetry. Translate each occupied coset to integers, apply the same inequality to its normalized block, and add with its original probability. The same $\lambda_*$ is retained in every flag and all apparatus factors remain counted. Finally $u\le\mathfrak q_{\lambda_*}$ gives the lower bound in (M.6.13cd.2), and the finite reflected family below gives the matching operational upper bound.

**Finite reflected family and matching weak coefficient.** Let the charged reference qubit have charges $(0,1)$ and state
$$
\sigma_t(p)=\begin{pmatrix}p&t\\t&q\end{pmatrix},
\quad q=1-p,
\quad 0\le t\le\sqrt{pq}.
\tag{M.6.13cd.U1}
$$
For real $a,b$, define the invariant observable on system and charged reference
$$
N_t=t\left(a|0,1\rangle\langle1,0|
+b|1,1\rangle\langle2,0|+\mathrm{h.c.}\right).
\tag{M.6.13cd.U2}
$$
Each matrix element preserves total charge. Write $\mathbb E_\sigma$ for conditional expectation over the reference. The exact conditional-noise operator is
$$
E=\mathbb E_{\sigma_t}\bigl[(N_t-X\otimes I)^2\bigr]
=X^2+t^2\operatorname{diag}(qa^2,pa^2+qb^2,pb^2)
-t^2\{X,A\},
\quad
A=\begin{pmatrix}0&a&0\\a&0&b\\0&b&0\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13cd.U3}
$$
Add a neutral two-level flag with equal probabilities. In its first branch use $(p,q,a,b)$; in its second use $(q,p,b,a)$. This exchanges the outer diagonal entries of $E$, leaving all its other entries unchanged. No flag is discarded or omitted from the reference resource.

Put
$$
|e\rangle=(|0\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2,
\quad |m\rangle=|1\rangle,
\quad |o\rangle=(|0\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2,
$$
$$
L=\sqrt2(a+b),\qquad
V_m=pa^2+qb^2,\qquad V_e=(qa^2+pb^2)/2.
\tag{M.6.13cd.U4}
$$
The flagged noise is diagonal in $(e,m,o)$, with eigenvalues
$$
1-t^2(L-V_e),\qquad 1-t^2(L-V_m),\qquad t^2V_e.
\tag{M.6.13cd.U5}
$$
This is a full system-operator calculation, not a calculation on only two selected input states.
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_t(p))
=h_2(p)-h_2\!\left(\frac{1+\sqrt{(q-p)^2+4t^2}}2\right),
\tag{M.6.13cd.U6}
$$
obtained by diagonalizing the two-dimensional reference state.

**Complete spectral-pointer implementation and dimension count.** The observable $N_t$, including both flag branches, has only the five spectral values $0,\pm ta,\pm tb$. Its spectral projections commute with total charge. Append a neutral dimension-five pointer prepared in a fixed pure state $|0_P\rangle$. For each spectral value $\nu$, choose a pointer unitary $V_\nu$ taking $|0_P\rangle$ to its distinct readout state $|\nu\rangle$. Then
$$
\mathcal U=\sum_\nu P_\nu\otimes V_\nu,
\qquad M=\sum_\nu\nu|\nu\rangle\langle\nu|
\tag{M.6.13cd.U7}
$$
is charge conserving and satisfies the neutral-pointer requirement. Compression of $\mathcal U^*(I\otimes M)\mathcal U$ and its square to the initial pointer state gives exactly $N_t$ and $N_t^2$. Consequently (M.6.13cd.U3) is the actual Ozawa-noise operator of this implementation. The complete apparatus has dimension $2\times2\times5=20$; its pure neutral pointer adds no asymmetry. No external clock, purification, controller, or uncounted flag is required.
For positive $p,q$, put
$$
f_\lambda(p,q)=\frac12\left[\frac1{(1-\lambda)p/2+\lambda q}
+\frac1{\lambda p+(1-\lambda)q/2}\right],\qquad
h(p,q)=\frac{\log p-\log q}{p-q},\quad h(p,p)=1/p.
\tag{M.6.13cd.U9}
$$
For $p=(1-z)/2$, $z\ge1/\sqrt5$, direct minimization of $f_\lambda(p,1-p)$ gives $U(p)=3/2+\sqrt{9z^2-1}/(2z)$. At the exact saddle choose
$$
p_*=(1-z_*)/2,\quad q_*=1-p_*,\qquad
a_*=[\sqrt2(\lambda_*p_*+(1-\lambda_*)q_*/2)]^{-1},
$$
$$
b_*=[\sqrt2(\lambda_*q_*+(1-\lambda_*)p_*/2)]^{-1},
\qquad U_*=U(p_*).
\tag{M.6.13cd.U8}
$$
The interior optimality condition gives $V_m=V_e=U_*$, while quadratic completion gives $L=2U_*$. Thus the reflected construction (M.6.13cd.U1)–(M.6.13cd.U7) again has exact noise spectrum $\{U_*t^2,1-U_*t^2,1-U_*t^2\}$ for all sufficiently small $t$, with all norm and positivity conditions satisfied. Equation (M.6.13cd.U6) gives its weak ratio $h(p_*,q_*)/U_*=c_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Its flagged seed at zero is faithful on the fixed charged-reference-and-flag support; the neutral pointer is pure and fixed. This proves the matching weak upper coefficient.

**Projected gain and exact weak limits.** Put $P=X^2$, and for a finite reference state $\sigma$ and invariant Hermitian observable $N$ define
$$
K_\sigma(N)=X^2-\{X,\mathbb E_\sigma N\}+\mathbb E_\sigma(N^2),
$$
$$
s(\sigma,N)=\lambda_{\min}\!\left(
P[X^2-K_\sigma(N)]P\big|_{P\mathcal H_S}\right),
\qquad s_\sigma=\sup_N s(\sigma,N).
\tag{M.6.13cd.P1}
$$
The supremum ranges over finite invariant Hermitian observables on this system and reference, without a pointer-norm restriction. Positivity of the noise gives $s_\sigma\le1$, and $N=0$ gives $s_\sigma\ge0$. Define
$$
c_{\mathrm{proj}}:=
\inf_{\substack{\sigma\ \mathrm{finite}\\
s_\sigma>0}}
\frac{\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)}{s_\sigma}.
\tag{M.6.13cd.P2}
$$
Every retained flag and charge-coset block is part of the reference in this infimum.

**Spin-one oddification and exact finite-state minimax.** Let $Z_S=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)$. It commutes with system charge and $P$, and anticommutes with $X$. For
$N_o=(N-Z_SN Z_S)/2$, operator convexity of the square gives
$$
K_\sigma(N_o)\le\frac12
\left[K_\sigma(N)+Z_SK_\sigma(N)Z_S\right].
\tag{M.6.13cd.P3}
$$
Thus oddification preserves invariance and cannot decrease the minimum projected gain. For odd $N$, the noise is parity even, so its compression to $P\mathcal H_S=\operatorname{span}\{e,m\}$ is diagonal in $(e,m)$.

Write
$$
R_e=\mathcal G_{\mathrm{tot}}(|e\rangle\langle e|\otimes\sigma),\quad
R_m=\mathcal G_{\mathrm{tot}}(|m\rangle\langle m|\otimes\sigma),\quad
D=\tfrac12\mathcal G_{\mathrm{tot}}(X\otimes\sigma).
$$
The two projected gains are
$$
g_e(N)=2\operatorname{Tr}(DN)-\operatorname{Tr}(R_eN^2),
\qquad
g_m(N)=2\operatorname{Tr}(DN)-\operatorname{Tr}(R_mN^2).
\tag{M.6.13cd.P4}
$$
Their linear terms agree because both $\{|e\rangle\langle e|,X\}$ and $\{|m\rangle\langle m|,X\}$ equal $X$.

Set $R=(R_e+R_m)/2$. Since $P\pm X\ge0$, one has $-R\le D\le R$. Hence $D$, $R_e$ and $R_m$ are supported on $E_R=\operatorname{supp}R$. Compressing $N$ to $E_R$ preserves its linear term and can only decrease both quadratic costs. The support projection commutes with total charge and system parity. On the resulting finite real vector space of odd invariant Hermitian observables, $R$ is positive definite, making $(g_e+g_m)/2$ coercive. Since $\min(g_e,g_m)\le(g_e+g_m)/2$, the primal maximum is attained.

The convex program maximizing $s$ subject to $s\le g_e(N)$ and $s\le g_m(N)$ has the strict feasible point $(N,s)=(0,-1)$. Finite-dimensional Slater duality therefore gives the exact identity
$$
s_\sigma=\max_N\min\{g_e(N),g_m(N)\}
=\min_{0\le\lambda\le1}\mathfrak q_\lambda(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13cd.P5}
$$
In the dual, the parity-even part of $N$ has zero linear contribution and only nonnegative quadratic cost, with parity cross terms vanishing. Thus the dual can equivalently take all invariant Hermitian $N$, exactly as in (M.6.13cd.S2). Endpoint values are interpreted as extended-real suprema if needed. The function $\lambda\mapsto\mathfrak q_\lambda$ is lower semicontinuous as a supremum of affine functions, the parameter interval is compact, and its value at $1/2$ is finite. Its minimum is therefore attained.

**Lower bound for ordinary all-input quality.** If a model has $u>0$, then $K\le(1-u)I$. Compression to $P$ gives
$$
u\le s(\sigma,N)\le s_\sigma,
\qquad \mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge c_{\mathrm{proj}}u.
\tag{M.6.13cd.P6}
$$
This holds for actual full pointers; occupied-support or first-moment compression can only improve the relaxed noise.

**Finite rare-flag realization and exact-quality tuning.** Fix any finite seed with $s_\sigma>0$ and a maximizing invariant $N$. Append a retained neutral flag separating this resource-bearing branch of weight $w$ from an invariant zero-resource branch of weight $1-w$, whose measured observable is zero. Its complete asymmetry and conditional noise are exactly
$$
\mathcal A_w=w\mathcal A_Q(\sigma),\qquad
K_w=(1-w)X^2+wK_\sigma(N).
\tag{M.6.13cd.P7}
$$
All branch observables have a finite neutral spectral-pointer dilation by (M.6.13cd.U7); flags and pointer are retained and counted. No assumption that the undiluted seed has positive ordinary all-input quality is required.

Put $D_0=K_\sigma(N)-X^2$, $v=\|D_0\|$, $C=2v^2$. By definition $PD_0P\le-s_\sigma P$, with equality on some unit vector. Whenever $w(v+s_\sigma)\le1/2$, Rayleigh lower bounding on that vector and decomposing a general unit vector into $P$ and $P^\perp$ parts gives
$$
1-ws_\sigma\le\lambda_{\max}(K_w)
\le1-ws_\sigma+Cw^2.
\tag{M.6.13cd.P8}
$$
Indeed, writing $r$ for the complementary component norm, the excess over $1-ws_\sigma$ is at most
$$
[-1+w(v+s_\sigma)]r^2+2wv r\sqrt{1-r^2}
\le-r^2/2+2wv r\le2v^2w^2.
$$
Consequently the actual all-input quality satisfies
$$
ws_\sigma-Cw^2\le u_w\le ws_\sigma.
\tag{M.6.13cd.P9}
$$
For every sufficiently small requested $u>0$, the points
$w_0=u/s_\sigma$ and $w_1=u/s_\sigma+Lu^2$, with any fixed $L>C/s_\sigma^3$, bracket a solution of $u_w=u$. Continuity of the full noise norm yields an exact-quality witness with
$$
w=u/s_\sigma+O(u^2),\qquad
\mathcal A_w/u=\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)/s_\sigma+O(u).
\tag{M.6.13cd.P10}
$$
Taking an upper limit for each finite seed and then the infimum over seeds, together with (M.6.13cd.P6), proves existence and equality of the two unrestricted weak limits. Specifically, let $F_{=,1}(u)$ and $F_{\le,1}(u)$ be the complete spin-one resource infima at exact error $\sqrt{1-u}$ and at most that error. Then
$$
\lim_{u\downarrow0}\frac{F_{=,1}(u)}u
=\lim_{u\downarrow0}\frac{F_{\le,1}(u)}u
=c_{\mathrm{proj}}
=\inf_{\substack{\sigma\ \mathrm{finite}\\\min_\lambda\mathfrak q_\lambda(\sigma)>0}}
\frac{\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)}{\min_{0\le\lambda\le1}\mathfrak q_\lambda(\sigma)},
\qquad c_{\mathrm{proj}}=c_*.
\tag{M.6.13cd.P11}
$$
The endpoint inequality gives the lower coefficient, and the reflected family gives the matching upper coefficient.

The full finite-quality spin-one entropy frontier is not evaluated by this coefficient theorem.

### M.6.13ce Dimension-uniform finite-quality remainder

<a id="theorem-m613ce-dimension-uniform-eighth-power-remainder"></a>**Theorem M.6.13ce (Dimension-Uniform Eighth-Power Remainder).** With the exact endpoint constants $\lambda_*$ and $c_{\mathrm{loc}}$ of M.6.13cd, every finite normalized complete reference satisfies
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge c_{\mathrm{loc}}\mathfrak q_{\lambda_*}(\sigma)
 +10^{-24}\mathfrak q_{\lambda_*}(\sigma)^8.
\tag{M.6.13ce.1}
$$
Consequently every complete spin-one measurement of quality $u>0$ obeys
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge c_{\mathrm{loc}}u+10^{-24}u^8.
\tag{M.6.13ce.2}
$$
The coefficient is uniform in reference dimension, charge range, degeneracies, smallest eigenvalue and retained-flag probabilities. It is deliberately nonsharp; no full finite-quality curve or optimizer is identified.

**Proof.** All integrals over the circle use normalized Haar measure. Write $c=c_{\mathrm{loc}}$, $M^2=[4\lambda_*(1-\lambda_*)]^{-1}$, and retain the endpoint notation of M.6.13cd. Its certified root box gives
$M^2<2$, $c>4/5$, $a_1,a_2>1/2$,
$|r|,|t_f|,|a_f|,|v|<1$, and $T/8>1/4$, where

$$
r=A_0-b\chi_*/2,\quad t_f=A_0+b\chi_*/2,
$$

$a_f=b/2-A_0$, $v=b/2+A_0$,
$A_0=(1+\lambda_*)(1+\chi_*)/4$, and $b=3\lambda_*-1$.

For a faithful normalized source $F$, with $\int\operatorname{Tr}F=1$, put $\tau=\int F$, $G=\sqrt F$, $H=\int G$, and use its actual odd Sylvester optimizer $N$, represented by $\alpha,\beta$ as in M.6.13cd. Set
$Z=\alpha\alpha^*+\alpha^*\alpha$,
$P=q_2(H)+\operatorname{Tr}(H^2Z^2)$, and
$R_H=\operatorname{Tr}(H^2W_0)$.
Operator variance gives $H^2\le\tau$ and $\operatorname{Tr}H^2\le1$.
For
$X=\|\alpha H\|_2^2+\|H\alpha\|_2^2$ and
$Y=\|\beta H\|_2^2+\|H\beta\|_2^2$, weighted Cauchy gives

$$
X\le\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}(H^2Z^2)}.
$$

The two face equations have coefficient matrices
$$
M_\alpha=\begin{pmatrix}t_f&-r\\v&-a_f\end{pmatrix},\qquad
M_\beta=\begin{pmatrix}-r&t_f\\a_f&-v\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\|M_\alpha\|\le2,\quad\|M_\beta^{-1}\|\le8.
\tag{M.6.13ce.3}
$$
The inverse bound follows from $|\det M_\beta|=T/8>1/4$. Hence
$Y\le256q_2(H)+512X$, and the coefficients of $W_0$ give

$$
R_H\le512q_2(H)+1026\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}(H^2Z^2)}\le C(P+\sqrt P),
$$

where $C=2048$.
For the actual optimizer, $W_0\le M^2I$, so $R_H<2$.
Considering $P\le1$ and $P\ge1$ separately proves
$$
P\ge\frac{R_H^2}{4C^2},\qquad
I_{\mathrm{BKM}}-2cE_{\mathrm{source}}\ge2c\,10^{-5}P.
\tag{M.6.13ce.4}
$$
The second inequality is precisely the retained padding and continuum comparison of M.6.13cd. No lower eigenvalue bound for $H$ was used.

We need a noncommutative interpolation estimate. For $0\le A\le B$ and $W\ge0$,
$$
[\operatorname{Tr}(A^2W)]^2
\le\operatorname{Tr}(A^2)\operatorname{Tr}(AWAW)
\le\operatorname{Tr}(A^2)\operatorname{Tr}(BWBW)
\le\operatorname{Tr}(A^2)\|W\|\operatorname{Tr}(B^2W).
\tag{M.6.13ce.5}
$$
The first step is Hilbert--Schmidt Cauchy applied to $A$ and $A^{1/2}WA^{1/2}$. For the middle step apply trace-square monotonicity on positive matrices to $W^{1/2}AW^{1/2}\le W^{1/2}BW^{1/2}$; the last step uses $BWB\le\|W\|B^2$. Thus if $F_t\ge m\tau$, square-root monotonicity and (M.6.13ce.5), with $A=\sqrt m\sqrt\tau$, $B=H_t$, give

$$
R_H(t)\ge m[\operatorname{Tr}(\tau W_0(N_t))]^2/M^2.
$$

This does not require the generally invalid inference $H_t^2\ge m\tau$.

Let $F_t$ be circle heat with initial dual $q_0$. If $q_0=0$, (M.6.13ce.1) follows from M.6.13cd, so assume $q_0>0$. The exact source Fourier identities are
$$
R_t=\overline R+e^{-4t}\Delta,\quad D_t=e^{-t}D_0,\quad
-\overline R\le\Delta\le\overline R,\quad
\overline R=\operatorname{diag}((1-\lambda_*)/2,\lambda_*,(1-\lambda_*)/2)\otimes\tau.
\tag{M.6.13ce.6}
$$
Indeed $\Delta$ has only the outer off-diagonal system block, whose sign is reversed by $\operatorname{diag}(1,1,-1)$. Let $\overline Q$ be the auxiliary variational value with linear term $D_0$ and quadratic weight $\overline R$, rather than the dual of the constant source. Weighted Sylvester Cauchy and the supported initial optimizer bound give

$$
q_0\le M\sqrt{\overline Q}.
$$

Variational comparison and $q_t=\operatorname{Tr}(R_tN_t^2)$ yield
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(\tau W_0(N_t))=\operatorname{Tr}(\overline RN_t^2)
\ge\frac{e^{-2t}\overline Q}{(1+e^{-4t})^2}.
\tag{M.6.13ce.7}
$$
For $1\le t\le2$, the circle heat kernel obeys

$$
p_t\ge1-2e^{-t}/(1-e^{-3t})>1/5,
$$

using $e>8/3$ and $384/485<4/5$. Thus $F_t\ge\tau/5$. Also $e<3$, $e>2$ give

$$
e^{-2t}>1/81,
$$

$e^{-4t}<1/16$, so (M.6.13ce.7) is greater than
$256\overline Q/23409>\overline Q/92\ge q_0^2/(92M^2)$.
Interpolation and (M.6.13ce.4) now give throughout this interval
$$
R_H(t)\ge\frac{q_0^4}{5\cdot92^2M^6},\qquad
P(t)\ge\frac{q_0^8}{100C^2\cdot92^4M^{12}}.
\tag{M.6.13ce.8}
$$
Integrate the exact identities $-\mathcal H'(F_t)=I_{\mathrm{BKM}}$, $-q_t'=2E_{\mathrm{source}}$, retaining the gap on $[1,2]$ and its nonnegativity elsewhere. Since this interval has length one,
$$
\mathcal H(F_0)-cq_0
\ge\frac{c\,10^{-5}}{50C^2\cdot92^4M^{12}}q_0^8 >\frac{q_0^8}{120190794307993600000000} >10^{-24}q_0^8.
\tag{M.6.13ce.9}
$$
The rational denominator uses only $C=2048$, $M^2<2$, $c>4/5$.
For singular initial sources, restrict to the invariant mean support and integrate from $\varepsilon<1$ to a terminal time greater than two. Positive heat is faithful there; finite-dimensional entropy and bounded-optimizer continuity allow $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ and terminal time to infinity while preserving the same fixed interval.

Integer-charge orbit sources identify $\mathcal H(F_0)=\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)$ and $q_0=\mathfrak q_{\lambda_*}(\sigma)$. For arbitrary finite real charges, charge-coset pinching leaves the dual unchanged and cannot increase asymmetry. Apply the normalized-block inequality, sum with the original probabilities, and use $\sum_jp_jq_j^8\ge(\sum_jp_jq_j)^8$. This proves (M.6.13ce.1) with the same common $\lambda_*$, including all correlations, charged pointers, neutral factors, degeneracies and retained flags. The inequality $\mathfrak q_{\lambda_*}\ge u$ and monotonicity of $cq+10^{-24}q^8$ give (M.6.13ce.2). $\square$

**Sharp-slope consequence.** For any sequence of finite complete measurements with $u_n>0$ and $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_n)/u_n\to c_{\mathrm{loc}}$, (M.6.13ce.2) gives $10^{-24}u_n^7\le\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_n)/u_n-c_{\mathrm{loc}}\to0$. Therefore $u_n\to0$ and $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_n)\to0$. This is a necessary weak-quality limit for sharp-slope sequences, not a uniqueness statement for their reference states.

### M.6.13cf Entropy-efficient heat retention and a global quadratic remainder

<a id="theorem-m613cf-dimension-uniform-quadratic-remainder"></a>**Theorem M.6.13cf (Dimension-Uniform Quadratic Remainder).** Let $c=c_*$ and
$\lambda=\lambda_*$ be the exact constants of Theorem M.6.13cd.
Every finite complete spin-one reference obeys
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge c\mathfrak q_\lambda(\sigma)
+10^{-34}\mathfrak q_\lambda(\sigma)^2.
\tag{M.6.13cf.1}
$$
Every actual complete conserving apparatus of positive all-input quality $u$
therefore obeys $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge cu+10^{-34}u^2$.
The coefficient is uniform in finite dimension, eigenvalues, charge range,
sector degeneracy, correlations and retained flags.

**Exact padding and supported source.** All circle means below are normalized.
Start with an integer-charge orbit source $F_0(\theta)$ and its heat evolution
$F_t=e^{t\partial_\theta^2}F_0$. Thus $\operatorname{Tr}F_t(\theta)=1$,
$\tau=\int F_t$ has trace one, and the entropy is

$$
\mathcal H_t=\int D(F_t(\theta)\Vert\tau).
$$

Restrict to the occupied support of $\tau$.
Write $G_t=\int\sqrt{F_t}$ for the mean amplitude, and retain the actual supported
odd Sylvester optimizer $N_t$, its positive activity $W_0(N_t)$,
and $q_t=\mathfrak q_\lambda(F_t)$ from Theorem M.6.13cd.
Theorem M.6.13ce, equation (M.6.13ce.4), gives exactly
$$
I_{\mathrm{BKM}}(F_t)+c q_t'
\ge \frac{c}{2\cdot10^5 C^2}R_H(t)^2,
\qquad R_H(t)=\operatorname{Tr}(G_t^2W_0(N_t)),\quad C=2048.
\tag{M.6.13cf.2}
$$
Indeed the retained face-plus-quartic padding $P_t$ satisfies
$I_{\mathrm{BKM}}+cq_t'\ge2c\,10^{-5}P_t$ and
$P_t\ge R_H(t)^2/(4C^2)$. This fixes the prefactor without changing normalization.
The exact root box also gives $4/5<c<1$ and
$M^2=[4\lambda(1-\lambda)]^{-1}<2$.

For clarity, set $a=(1-\lambda)/2$ and
$$
\rho_\lambda=\begin{pmatrix}a&0&a\\0&\lambda&0\\a&0&a\end{pmatrix},
\quad R_t=\int U_\theta\rho_\lambda U_\theta^*\otimes F_t(\theta),
\quad D_t=\frac12\int U_\theta XU_\theta^*\otimes F_t(\theta),
\quad U_\theta=e^{i\operatorname{diag}(-1,0,1)\theta}.
$$
The scalar shift of the system charge leaves its conjugation unchanged.
The exact source order is $-MR_t\le D_t\le MR_t$, obtained from
$-M\rho_\lambda\le X/2\le M\rho_\lambda$ on the two-dimensional $(e,m)$ subspace.
The supported positive Sylvester inverse supplies
$$
R_tN_t+N_tR_t=2D_t,\quad
\|N_t\|\le M,\quad q_t=\operatorname{Tr}D_tN_t=\operatorname{Tr}R_tN_t^2
\le M^2<2.
\tag{M.6.13cf.3}
$$
The same compact optimizer ball gives continuity at singular sources.
Writing
$N_t=\begin{pmatrix}0&A&0\\A^*&0&B\\0&B^*&0\end{pmatrix}$,
the activity and constant quadratic weight are
$$
W_0=aAA^*+\lambda A^*A+\lambda BB^*+aB^*B,\quad
\overline R=\operatorname{diag}(a,\lambda,a)\otimes\tau.
$$
Thus $0\le W_0\le\|N_t\|^2I$ and
$\operatorname{Tr}\tau W_0=\operatorname{Tr}\overline R N_t^2$.
These are positive partial-trace identities and require no commuting blocks.

**Hellinger comparison.** For normalized positive states $A,B$, with $B$ faithful
on the relevant support,
$$
\|\sqrt A-\sqrt B\|_2^2\le D(A\Vert B).
\tag{M.6.13cf.4}
$$
To prove this, let $x_i,y_j$ be their eigenvalues and use weights
$w_{ij}=x_i|\langle i|j\rangle|^2$, whose sum is one. Jensen's inequality gives

$$
\log\operatorname{Tr}\sqrt A\sqrt B\ge-D(A\Vert B)/2.
$$

Then $-\log x\ge1-x$ yields

$$
D(A\Vert B)\ge2(1-\operatorname{Tr}\sqrt A\sqrt B),
$$

the squared root distance.
Zero eigenvalues follow by continuity.
Relative-entropy data processing under the preparation-and-average map gives

$$
D(R_0\Vert\overline R)\le\mathcal H_0.
$$

Each prepared system factor is normalized, so tensoring with that same factor
leaves relative entropy unchanged; averaging then proves the assertion.

Let $\overline Q$ be the auxiliary variational gain with numerator $D_0$ and
quadratic weight $\overline R$. It is not $q(\tau)$.
Cauchy in the real Sylvester inner product gives

$$
q_0\le\sqrt{\overline Q}\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}\overline R N_0^2}.
$$

The Hilbert–Schmidt triangle inequality and (M.6.13cf.4) give
$$
\begin{aligned}
\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}\overline R N_0^2}
&=\|N_0\sqrt{\overline R}\|_2\\
&\le\|N_0\sqrt{R_0}\|_2
 +M\|\sqrt{\overline R}-\sqrt{R_0}\|_2
\le\sqrt{q_0}+M\sqrt{\mathcal H_0}.
\end{aligned}
$$
Hence, for $q_0>0$,
$$
\overline Q\ge\frac{q_0^2}{(\sqrt{q_0}+M\sqrt{\mathcal H_0})^2}.
\tag{M.6.13cf.5}
$$
In particular $\mathcal H_0\le2q_0$ and $M^2<2$ imply

$$
\overline Q\ge q_0/9.
$$

**Fixed-time entropy contraction.** The circle heat kernel satisfies for $t\ge1$
$$
|p_t-1|\le2\sum_{n\ge1}e^{-n^2t}
\le\frac{2e^{-t}}{1-e^{-3t}}\le3e^{-t},
$$
since $n^2\ge1+3(n-1)$ and $e>2$.
For $t\ge T=\log(2^{14})$ write
$p_t=(1-\alpha_t)+\alpha_t k_t$, where
$\alpha_t=3e^{-t}<1$ and $k_t$ is nonnegative and normalized.
Thus $F_t=(1-\alpha_t)\tau+\alpha_t(k_t*F_0)$.
Joint convexity and averaging circle translations give
$$
\mathcal H_t\le3e^{-t}\mathcal H_0,\qquad t\ge T.
$$
Operator variance gives $\tau-G_t^2\ge0$.
Projection onto constant amplitudes and (M.6.13cf.4), applied pointwise, give
$$
0\le\delta_t:=\operatorname{Tr}(\tau-G_t^2)
\le\int\|\sqrt{F_t}-\sqrt\tau\|_2^2
\le\mathcal H_t\le3e^{-t}\mathcal H_0.
\tag{M.6.13cf.6}
$$
This does not infer $G_t^2\ge m\tau$ from source minorization.

**Two Fourier modes and actual amplitude activity.** The exact supports of
$\rho_\lambda$ and $X$ give
$$
R_t=\overline R+e^{-4t}\Delta,\qquad D_t=e^{-t}D_0,
\qquad-\overline R\le\Delta\le\overline R.
\tag{M.6.13cf.7}
$$
The perturbation has only the outer off-diagonal system block.
Conjugation by $\operatorname{diag}(1,1,-1)$ reverses it, so positivity gives both orders.
Variational comparison and the actual optimizer identity imply
$$
q_t\ge\frac{e^{-2t}\overline Q}{1+e^{-4t}},\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}\tau W_0(N_t)
\ge\frac{q_t}{1+e^{-4t}}
\ge\frac{e^{-2t}\overline Q}{(1+e^{-4t})^2}
\ge\frac{e^{-2t}\overline Q}{4}.
\tag{M.6.13cf.8}
$$
Moreover $\pm D_0\le MR_0\le2M\overline R$ and the positive Sylvester inverse give
$$
\|N_t\|\le\frac{2Me^{-t}}{1-e^{-4t}}\le4Me^{-t},\qquad t\ge1.
\tag{M.6.13cf.9}
$$
Suppose $0<q_0$ and $\mathcal H_0\le2q_0$.
The first activity is at least $e^{-2t}q_0/36$.
Since $\tau-G_t^2$ and $W_0$ are positive, their trace product is at most
$\|W_0\|\delta_t$, without requiring them to commute. By (M.6.13cf.6) and
(M.6.13cf.9), the lost activity is at most
$16M^2e^{-2t}\,3e^{-t}\mathcal H_0\le192e^{-3t}q_0$.
Therefore for every $t\ge T$,
$$
R_H(t)\ge e^{-2t}q_0\left(\frac1{36}-\frac{192}{2^{14}}\right)
\ge\frac{e^{-2t}q_0}{72}.
\tag{M.6.13cf.10}
$$
The bracket is nonnegative before it is squared.

**Integration and the complementary branch.** The exact heat identities are
$-\mathcal H_t'=I_{\mathrm{BKM}}(F_t)$ and $q_t'=-2E_{\mathrm{source}}$.
The padding (M.6.13cf.2) makes the dissipation of $\mathcal H_t-cq_t$ nonnegative;
its terminal value is zero. Retaining only $t\ge T$ gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal H_0-cq_0
&\ge\frac{c}{2\cdot10^5C^2}\frac{q_0^2}{72^2}
 \int_T^\infty e^{-4t}\,dt\\
&=\frac{c\,2^{-56}}{8\cdot10^5C^2\cdot72^2}q_0^2 >\frac{q_0^2}{1566767862220559410419204096000000} >10^{-34}q_0^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13cf.11}
$$
If $\mathcal H_0>2q_0$, then $c<1$ and $q_0<2$ give

$$
\mathcal H_0-cq_0>(2-c)q_0>q_0\ge q_0^2/2.
$$

The case $q_0=0$ follows from nonnegative entropy.
Thus the same lower bound holds on both branches.

**Singular sources and the complete reference.** At positive time the circle heat
kernel has positive minimum, so $F_t$ is faithful on the fixed support of $\tau$.
Integrate from $\varepsilon>0$ without resetting the time origin and retain the
same tail $t\ge T$. Let $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ and the terminal time tend to infinity.
Finite-dimensional entropy continuity and the common compact optimizer ball
preserve $\mathcal H_0,q_0$; no lower eigenvalue constant appears.
For a finite integer-charge orbit, $\mathcal H_0=\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)$ and
$q_0=\mathfrak q_\lambda(\sigma)$.
For arbitrary real charges, pinch into cosets modulo the integers. System gaps
$0,1,2$ make this leave the dual unchanged; asymmetry cannot increase.
Normalize each occupied coset, translate its charges to integers, apply the bound
with the same $\lambda_*$, and add with its original probability.
Homogeneity and $\sum_jp_jq_j^2\ge(\sum_jp_jq_j)^2$ preserve the coefficient.
Every original factor and coset label remains counted and retained.
Finally $0<u\le q$ and monotonicity of $cq+10^{-34}q^2$ give the actual-model bound.
$\square$

### M.6.13cg A tighter uniform quadratic coefficient

<a id="theorem-m613cg-uniform-quadratic-improvement"></a>**Theorem M.6.13cg (Uniform Quadratic Improvement).** In the full finite complete
spin-one class of Theorems M.6.13cd–M.6.13cf, with the same common endpoint dual,
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge c_*\mathfrak q_{\lambda_*}(\sigma)
+\frac{2}{10^{23}}\mathfrak q_{\lambda_*}(\sigma)^2.
\tag{M.6.13cg.1}
$$
Thus every actual apparatus of positive all-input quality $u$ satisfies

$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge c_*u+(2/10^{23})u^2.
$$

This coefficient does not determine the optimal quadratic coefficient or the
full positive-error entropy frontier.

**Proof.** The exact endpoint enclosure in Theorem M.6.13cd gives
$$
\frac45<c<\frac9{10},\qquad M^2<\frac65,\qquad M<\frac{11}{10}.
\tag{M.6.13cg.2}
$$
Use the normalized orbit source, $\mathcal H_t$, $G_t$, $q_t$, $N_t$,
$W_0(N_t)$, $\overline R$ and $\overline Q$ of Theorem M.6.13cf.
In particular the exact padding is (M.6.13cf.2), not a doubled prefactor.
Its Hellinger proof and two-mode identities give, writing $x=e^{-t}$,
$$
\overline Q\ge\frac{q_0^2}{(\sqrt{q_0}+M\sqrt{\mathcal H_0})^2},\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}\tau W_0(N_t)\ge\frac{x^2\overline Q}{(1+x^4)^2},\qquad
\|N_t\|\le\frac{2Mx}{1-x^4}.
\tag{M.6.13cg.3}
$$
The same positive-kernel proof gives
$$
0\le\tau-G_t^2,\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}(\tau-G_t^2)\le\mathcal H_t\le3x\mathcal H_0,
\qquad0\le W_0(N_t)\le\|N_t\|^2I
\tag{M.6.13cg.4}
$$
for $t\ge\log4$. Indeed $2x/(1-x^3)\le3x<1$ there, so the required
kernel mixture is nonnegative and normalized.

Suppose $0<q_0$ and $\mathcal H_0\le q_0$.
Then $\overline Q\ge q_0/(1+M)^2>(100/441)q_0$.
For $t\ge\log4$ we have $x\le1/4$, and the exact rational inequalities
$$
\frac{100}{441}\left(\frac{256}{257}\right)^2>\frac15,
\qquad
\frac{24}{5}\left(\frac{256}{255}\right)^2<5
$$
give $\operatorname{Tr}\tau W_0(N_t)\ge x^2q_0/5$ and $\|N_t\|^2\le5x^2$.
Positivity and (M.6.13cg.4) therefore give
$$
\operatorname{Tr}[(\tau-G_t^2)W_0(N_t)]\le15x^3q_0,\qquad
R_H(t)\ge x^2q_0(1/5-15x).
\tag{M.6.13cg.5}
$$
Retain only $t\ge\log75$, so $x\le1/75$ and the last bracket is nonnegative.
Only on this tail is it squared. Integrating the padding and discarding its
nonnegative contribution outside the tail gives
$$
\mathcal H_0-cq_0
\ge\frac{c}{2\cdot10^5\cdot2048^2}q_0^2
\int_{\log75}^{\infty}e^{-4t}(1/5-15e^{-t})^2\,dt.
\tag{M.6.13cg.6}
$$
The substitution $x=e^{-t}$ evaluates the $\int$ exactly:
$$
\int_0^{1/75}x^3(1/5-15x)^2\,dx
=\frac1{60\cdot5^6\cdot15^4}=\frac1{47460937500}.
$$
Using $c>4/5$, the coefficient in (M.6.13cg.6) is strictly greater than
$$
\frac1{49766400000000000000000}>\frac2{10^{23}}.
\tag{M.6.13cg.7}
$$
On the complementary branch $\mathcal H_0>q_0$, the bounds $c<9/10$ and
$q_0\le M^2<2$ give

$$
\mathcal H_0-cq_0>q_0/10\ge q_0^2/20>(2/10^{23})q_0^2.
$$

At $q_0=0$ nonnegative entropy suffices.

The positive-time support restriction and continuity passage in Theorem M.6.13cf
apply without resetting time and preserve the same tail $t\ge\log75$.
For arbitrary real charges, modulo-integer coset pinching leaves the dual
unchanged and cannot increase asymmetry; homogeneous summation at the same
$\lambda_*$ and Jensen's inequality preserve the quadratic coefficient.
All multiplicities, mixedness, correlations, neutral factors and retained flags
remain inside the reference. Monotonicity of $cq+(2/10^{23})q^2$ and $u\le q$
then give the actual-model bound.

The improved term also dominates the eighth-power addition in Theorem M.6.13ce.
For a normalized reference, square completion gives $0\le\mathfrak q_\lambda\le1$:
$$
\operatorname{Tr}[(X\otimes\sigma)N]
-\operatorname{Tr}[(\rho_\lambda\otimes\sigma)N^2]
=1-\operatorname{Tr}[(\rho_\lambda\otimes\sigma)(N-X\otimes I)^2]\le1,
$$
using $\{\rho_\lambda,X\}=X$ and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho_\lambda X^2=1$.
The zero observable supplies the lower bound.
Thus $q^8\le q^2$ and $(2/10^{23})q^2\ge10^{-24}q^8$.
No finite-quality optimizer or reference-state uniqueness follows. $\square$

### M.6.13ch The complete spin-three-halves discriminator and a fixed ten-dimensional apparatus

<a id="theorem-m613ch-spin-three-halves-discriminator-and-fixed-capacity-precision"></a>**Theorem M.6.13ch (Spin-Three-Halves Discriminator and Fixed-Capacity Precision).** Fix
$Q_S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2,3)$ and $X=J_x/(3/2)$ as displayed below.
Use the input-independent complete finite reference state, an additive-charge-conserving unitary,
a self-adjoint pointer commuting with reference charge, and the Ozawa RMS error supremum over
all system inputs, with $u=1-\epsilon_\infty^2$. Every charged or neutral auxiliary, pointer, initial correlation and retained
flag is counted. The natural-$\log$ asymmetry is $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)=D(\sigma\Vert\mathcal G_Q\sigma)$.
The state-only quantity $q_Q$ defined below lies in $[0,1]$, has the supported finite Sylvester
optimizer, and bounds every actual positive all-input quality by $u\le q_Q$.
It also satisfies the nonlinear entropy bound $\mathcal A_Q\ge F(q_Q)$ below.

There is one fixed complete dimension-ten apparatus, with two distinct reference charges and
five retained neutral pointer levels, tuning every quality
$0\le u\le(29-\sqrt{57})/49$ exactly. Its weak resource ratio is $2/3$.
The infimum of $\mathcal A_Q/q_Q$ on positive-quality two-dimensional seed references is also
$2/3$, allowing arbitrary real charge gap, diagonal imbalance and complex coherence; an independent
neutral product factor leaves it unchanged. The full-reference lower endpoint is proved separately
in Theorem M.6.13ck. No minimal apparatus dimension, optimal positive-error frontier or physical
hardware/service cost is inferred from this finite mathematical realization.

The extreme input vectors are
$$
v_+=\frac{(1,\sqrt3,\sqrt3,1)^T}{\sqrt8},\qquad
v_-=\frac{(1,-\sqrt3,\sqrt3,-1)^T}{\sqrt8},\qquad
\rho_s=v_sv_s^*,\quad \rho_*=(\rho_++\rho_-)/2.
\tag{M.6.13ch.S1}
$$
They satisfy $Xv_s=sv_s$; the other two target eigenvalues are $\pm1/3$.

For any finite reference $(R,Q,\sigma)$, let

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Omega_s&=\mathcal G_{Q_S+Q}(\rho_s\otimes\sigma),\\
R_\sigma&=(\Omega_++\Omega_-)/2,\qquad D_\sigma=(\Omega_+-\Omega_-)/2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13ch.S3}
$$

The notation $R_\sigma$ in (M.6.13ch.S3) denotes a density matrix on the system-reference product, not the reference Hilbert space. Define the finite-dimensional, state-only quadratic discrimination quality

$$
q_Q(\sigma)=\sup_{B=B^*,\ [B,Q_S+Q]=0}
\{2\operatorname{Tr}(D_\sigma B)-\operatorname{Tr}(R_\sigma B^2)\}.
\tag{M.6.13ch.S4}
$$

It is obtained by solving one Sylvester equation, as detailed below. Define

$$
c_*:=\inf_{\substack{R,Q,\sigma\text{ finite}\\q_Q(\sigma)>0}}
\frac{\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)}{q_Q(\sigma)}.
\tag{M.6.13ch.S5}
$$
**The optimal quadratic discriminator is a finite invariant contraction.**

Abbreviate $R_\sigma,D_\sigma$ by $R,D$. Both commute with total charge, $\operatorname{Tr}R=1$, and $-R\le D\le R$. Let $E=\operatorname{supp}R$. Positivity shows that $D$ is supported on $E$. On this support define

$$
B_\sigma=2\int_0^\infty e^{-tR}D e^{-tR}\,dt,
\qquad RB_\sigma+B_\sigma R=2D,
\tag{M.6.13ch.S8}
$$

and set $B_\sigma=0$ on $E^\perp$. The $\int$ converges because $R|_E>0$. It is Hermitian and commutes with total charge. The $\int$ map is positive, and

$$
2\int_0^\infty e^{-tR}R e^{-tR}\,dt=I_E.
\tag{M.6.13ch.S9}
$$

Consequently $-I\le B_\sigma\le I$. Completing the quadratic form gives, for every Hermitian $B$,

$$
2\operatorname{Tr}(DB)-\operatorname{Tr}(RB^2)
=\operatorname{Tr}(RB_\sigma^2)
-\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(R(B-B_\sigma)^2\bigr).
\tag{M.6.13ch.S10}
$$

Thus

$$
q_Q(\sigma)=\operatorname{Tr}(DB_\sigma)
=\operatorname{Tr}(RB_\sigma^2)\in[0,1].
\tag{M.6.13ch.S11}
$$

In an eigenbasis of $R$, with eigenvalues $r_a\ge0$, the completely explicit formula is

$$
(B_\sigma)_{ab}=\frac{2D_{ab}}{r_a+r_b},\qquad
q_Q(\sigma)=\sum_{a,b:r_a+r_b>0}\frac{2|D_{ab}|^2}{r_a+r_b},
\tag{M.6.13ch.S12}
$$

with zero assigned when the denominator vanishes. The supremum in (M.6.13ch.S4) therefore requires only this finite Sylvester calculation. In particular, odd system-charge differences one and three both enter; no adjacent-gap-only restriction is made.
**A global entropy lower bound.**

Let $\tau=\mathcal G_Q\sigma$, and set

$$
T=\operatorname{diag}(1,3,3,1)/8\otimes\tau.
\tag{M.6.13ch.S13}
$$

Since the two system inputs have identical charge diagonals,

$$
\mathcal G_{Q_S+Q}(\rho_s\otimes\tau)=T
\quad(s=\pm1).
\tag{M.6.13ch.S14}
$$

Data processing for finite-dimensional quantum relative entropy gives

$$
D(\Omega_s\Vert T)\le D(\rho_s\otimes\sigma\Vert\rho_s\otimes\tau)
=\mathcal A_Q(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13ch.S15}
$$

Averaging and using the elementary relative-entropy decomposition at the mean state yields

$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge
\frac12D(\Omega_+\Vert R)+\frac12D(\Omega_-\Vert R).
\tag{M.6.13ch.S16}
$$

All terms are finite on their supports; the discarded remainder is $D(R\Vert T)\ge0$.

Measure the spectral projectors $\Pi_j$ of $B_\sigma$, with eigenvalues $b_j\in[-1,1]$. Put $r_j=\operatorname{Tr}(R\Pi_j)$ and $d_j=\operatorname{Tr}(D\Pi_j)$. The Sylvester equation implies $d_j=b_jr_j$. The two outcome distributions are therefore $r_j(1\pm b_j)$. Applying data processing again in (M.6.13ch.S16) gives

$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge\sum_jr_j f(b_j),\qquad
f(b)=\frac{(1+b)\log(1+b)+(1-b)\log(1-b)}2.
\tag{M.6.13ch.S17}
$$

The endpoint convention is $0\log0=0$. The function

$$
F(z)=f(\sqrt z)
=\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{z^n}{2n(2n-1)},\quad 0\le z\le1,
\tag{M.6.13ch.S18}
$$

is increasing and convex. Since $\sum_jr_jb_j^2=q_Q(\sigma)$, Jensen's inequality proves

$$
\boxed{\quad
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge F(q_Q(\sigma))
\ge\frac{q_Q(\sigma)}2+\frac{q_Q(\sigma)^2}{12}.
\quad}
\tag{M.6.13ch.S19}
$$

This is valid for every finite real charge spectrum, every degeneracy, and every mixed state. In particular $c_*\ge1/2$. For positive $q$, each individual ratio in (M.6.13ch.S5) is strictly larger than $1/2$; no uniform gap above $1/2$ is claimed.

**Lower bound for every original complete apparatus.**

For an original admitted apparatus, denote the complete reference by $(R,Q,\sigma)$ and its Heisenberg readout by

$$
O=U^*(I\otimes M)U.
\tag{M.6.13ch.S20}
$$

Conservation and the Yanase condition imply $[O,Q_S+Q]=0$. Let

$$
K=\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma)(O-X\otimes I)^2].
\tag{M.6.13ch.S21}
$$

Its all-input squared RMS error is $\|K\|$. Because $Xv_s=sv_s$, averaging the two extreme-input errors gives exactly

$$
\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_* K)
=1-2\operatorname{Tr}(D_\sigma O)+\operatorname{Tr}(R_\sigma O^2).
\tag{M.6.13ch.S22}
$$

If the error is at most $\sqrt{1-u}$, then $K\le(1-u)I$. Equations (M.6.13ch.S4), (M.6.13ch.S22) imply

$$
u\le2\operatorname{Tr}(D_\sigma O)-\operatorname{Tr}(R_\sigma O^2)
\le q_Q(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13ch.S23}
$$

Thus, for every original apparatus with $u>0$,

$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge c_*q_Q(\sigma)\ge c_*u,
\qquad
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge F(u).
\tag{M.6.13ch.S24}
$$

There is no pointer-norm assumption in this lower bound. It directly applies to the complete reference, including all charged or neutral auxiliary factors and correlated flags.
**Arbitrary real spectra reduce to one integer coset.**

Partition the finite spectrum of $Q$ by $q\sim q'$ if $q-q'\in\mathbb Z$, and let $E_j$ project onto the resulting reference subspaces. Let $\sigma'=\sum_jE_j\sigma E_j$. A system charge difference is always an integer, so every matrix entry of $\rho_s\otimes(\sigma-\sigma')$ is killed by total-charge dephasing. Consequently $\Omega_s(\sigma')=\Omega_s(\sigma)$ and $q_Q(\sigma')=q_Q(\sigma)$.

The reference dephasing $\tau$ is unchanged, while pinching gives

$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)
=D(\sigma\Vert\sigma')+\mathcal A_Q(\sigma')
\ge\mathcal A_Q(\sigma').
\tag{M.6.13ch.S36}
$$

Writing the latter state as $\bigoplus_jp_j\sigma_j$, both asymmetry and the quadratic quality split exactly:

$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma')=\sum_jp_j\mathcal A_{Q_j}(\sigma_j),\qquad
q_Q(\sigma')=\sum_jp_jq_{Q_j}(\sigma_j).
\tag{M.6.13ch.S37}
$$

For the second identity, $R,D$ and their Sylvester solution are block diagonal; zero-weight blocks do not contribute. A ratio with positive denominator is no smaller than the smallest component ratio with positive denominator. On such a component all charges belong to one translate of the integers; subtracting that translate preserves every definition. Thus restricting (M.6.13ch.S5) to finite integer spectra does not change it. Missing integer charge levels can be padded with zero state support if desired. No reduction to pure states, fixed dimension, or trivial degeneracies follows.

*Proof.*

**The fixed apparatus and variable state/readout scale.**

Let

$$
Q_S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2,3),\qquad
X=J_x/(3/2)=\frac13
\begin{pmatrix}
0&\sqrt3&0&0\\
\sqrt3&0&2&0\\
0&2&0&\sqrt3\\
0&0&\sqrt3&0
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13ch.1}
$$

The target spectrum is $\{-1,-1/3,1/3,1\}$, and $\|X\|=d_{Q_S}(X)=1$, by conjugation with $\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,-1)$.

Use the two-dimensional charged reference

$$
R_0=\mathbb C^2,\quad Q_0=|1\rangle\langle1|,\quad
\sigma_c=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&c\\c&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
S=|1\rangle\langle0|,\qquad 0\le c\le1.
\tag{M.6.13ch.2}
$$

Its exact natural-$\log$ asymmetry is

$$
\mathcal A(c)=\frac{(1+c)\log(1+c)+(1-c)\log(1-c)}2,
\qquad\mathcal A(c)=\frac{c^2}2+\frac{c^4}{12}+O(c^6).
\tag{M.6.13ch.3}
$$

The endpoint convention is $0\log0=0$. The state is full rank for $0\le c<1$, pure at $c=1$, and its charge dephasing is $I/2$ throughout. Its only coherence carries charge gap one. There is no cyclic wrap coherence.

Define

$$
D=\begin{pmatrix}
0&\sqrt3/2&0&0\\0&0&1&0\\0&0&0&\sqrt3/2\\0&0&0&0
\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B_1=D\otimes S+D^*\otimes S^*,\qquad B(c)=cB_1.
\tag{M.6.13ch.4}
$$

Because $[Q_S,D]=-D$ and $[Q_0,S]=S$, $B_1$ commutes with total charge. The five total-charge blocks, from zero to four, have dimensions $1,2,2,2,1$. Their nonzero off-diagonal entries are respectively $\sqrt3/2,1,\sqrt3/2$. Hence

$$
\operatorname{spec}B_1=\{0,\pm\sqrt3/2,\pm1\},
\quad
\det(\lambda I-B_1)=\lambda^2(\lambda^2-3/4)^2(\lambda^2-1).
\tag{M.6.13ch.5}
$$

The zero and the two $\pm\sqrt3/2$ eigenvalues each have multiplicity two; each $\pm1$ has multiplicity one.

Let $b_0=0,b_1=\sqrt3/2,b_2=-\sqrt3/2,b_3=1,b_4=-1$, and let $\Pi_j$ be the fixed complete spectral projectors of $B_1$. Equivalently,

$$
\Pi_j=\prod_{k\ne j}\frac{B_1-b_kI}{b_j-b_k}.
\tag{M.6.13ch.6}
$$

Use a neutral five-dimensional pointer $P_0$, ready state $|0\rangle$, and cyclic shift $W|j\rangle=|j+1\bmod5\rangle$. Set

$$
U=\sum_{j=0}^4\Pi_j\otimes W^j,
\quad
M_c=I_{R_0}\otimes\sum_{j=0}^4 cb_j|j\rangle\langle j|,
\tag{M.6.13ch.7}
$$

with complete reference

$$
R=R_0\otimes P_0,\quad Q_R=Q_0\otimes I_{P_0},\quad
\sigma_R(c)=\sigma_c\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|.
\tag{M.6.13ch.8}
$$

The Hilbert spaces, charges, unitary, pointer eigenbasis, and ready state are fixed for the entire family. Only $\sigma_c$ and the pointer's scalar calibration change with $c$. Orthogonality gives exact unitarity; each $\Pi_j$ commutes with total charge; and the pointer is neutral. Thus $[U,Q_S+Q_R]=0$ and $[M_c,Q_R]=0$.

For the ready-state embedding $\iota$,

$$
\iota^*U^*(I\otimes M_c^m)U\iota=B(c)^m,
\qquad m=1,2.
\tag{M.6.13ch.9}
$$

Here the identity factors are understood on the non-pointer spaces. Expanding the Heisenberg noise square and using that the embedding intertwines $X$ makes the original first/second-moment error exactly the conditional error of $B(c)$.

The complete apparatus has dimension exactly ten, two distinct reference charges $0,1$, each of degeneracy five, and five retained pointer levels. Its system-inclusive dimension is forty. For $c>0$ the pointer has five distinct values and norm $c$; at $c=0$ those values coincide, but all five levels and the same unitary remain present. The complete initial asymmetry is exactly (M.6.13ch.3), because the neutral pure factor is retained and its entropy cancels. There is no flag, postselection, failure branch, or hidden charged auxiliary system.

**Exact all-input error.**

Let $C=J_-/(2J)$, with $J=3/2$, so $X=C+C^*$, $Y=i(C-C^*)$, and $D=3C/2$. The exact reference moments are

$$
\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_cS)=c/2,\quad
\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_cSS^*)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_cS^*S)=1/2,
\quad S^2=(S^*)^2=0.
\tag{M.6.13ch.10}
$$

They give

$$
\mathcal E_{\sigma_c}(B(c))=\frac{3c^2}{4}X,
\qquad
\mathcal E_{\sigma_c}(B(c)^2)=\frac{9c^2}{16}(X^2+Y^2).
\tag{M.6.13ch.11}
$$

Therefore the exact conditional squared-noise matrix is

$$
K(c)=\left(1-\frac{15c^2}{16}\right)X^2+\frac{9c^2}{16}Y^2.
\tag{M.6.13ch.12}
$$

Put $z=c^2$, $h=1-3z/8$, and $w=1-3z/2$. Then

$$
K(c)=\frac19
\begin{pmatrix}
3h&0&2\sqrt3w&0\\
0&7h&0&2\sqrt3w\\
2\sqrt3w&0&7h&0\\
0&2\sqrt3w&0&3h
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13ch.13}
$$

Both parity blocks have the same two eigenvalues. Consequently

$$
\boxed{\quad
\epsilon_\infty(c)^2=\|K(c)\|
=\frac{40-15z+2\sqrt{256-624z+441z^2}}{72},\qquad
u(c)=\frac{32+15z-2\sqrt{256-624z+441z^2}}{72}.
\quad}
\tag{M.6.13ch.14}
$$

The second noise eigenvalue is obtained by changing the sign before the square root in the numerator of $\epsilon_\infty^2$; both eigenvalues occur twice. All four eigenvalues are nonnegative because (M.6.13ch.12) is the expectation of a noise square, as also follows from (M.6.13ch.13). This is an operator-norm/all-system-input error, not an average-input error.

The radicand is strictly positive for all real $z$: its discriminant is negative. Expanding (M.6.13ch.14) at zero gives

$$
u(c)=\frac34c^2-\frac{27}{512}c^4+O(c^6).
\tag{M.6.13ch.15}
$$

**Exact error tuning on a nonzero interval.**

The quality is strictly increasing for

$$
0\le z<z_*=\frac{104}{147}+\frac{40\sqrt{57}}{2793}<1,
\tag{M.6.13ch.16}
$$

and reaches its maximum within the full parameter interval $0\le c\le1$ at

$$
u_*=\frac{29-\sqrt{57}}{49},\qquad
\epsilon_{\min}^2=\frac{20+\sqrt{57}}{49}.
\tag{M.6.13ch.17}
$$

To check this directly, differentiating (M.6.13ch.14) gives

$$
\frac{du}{dz}=\frac{15+(624-882z)/\sqrt{256-624z+441z^2}}{72}.
\tag{M.6.13ch.18}
$$

It is positive through $z=104/147$. Thereafter its only zero in $[0,1]$ is $z_*$: squaring the equality with the required positive sign gives

$$
8379z^2-11856z+4096=0,
$$

and the smaller quadratic root has the wrong sign for the unsquared equation. The derivative is negative beyond $z_*$.

For every prescribed $u\in[0,u_*]$, the lower-parameter solution is explicitly

$$
\boxed{\quad
z(u)=\frac{64-40u-16\sqrt{49u^2-58u+16}}{57},\qquad
c(u)=\sqrt{z(u)}.
\quad}
\tag{M.6.13ch.19}
$$

It lies in $[0,z_*]$ and solves (M.6.13ch.14), including both endpoints. This follows either by the preceding monotonicity and squaring (M.6.13ch.14), retaining its nonnegative square-root sign, or directly by substitution. It provides exactly the requested original error $\sqrt{1-u}$ on this entire interval.

At $u=0$, $c=0$, the asymmetry is zero and the error is one. At $u=u_*$, the state remains full rank because $z_*<1$. At the separate state-purity endpoint $c=1$, the resource is $\log2$, and

$$
\epsilon_\infty(1)^2=\frac{25+2\sqrt{73}}{72},\qquad
u(1)=\frac{47-2\sqrt{73}}{72}<u_*.
\tag{M.6.13ch.20}
$$

Thus using the entire state-positivity range does not make the quality monotone; the exact-error inverse (M.6.13ch.19) deliberately uses its monotone branch. No zero-error or interior frontier-optimality assertion follows.

Combining (M.6.13ch.3), (M.6.13ch.15), or substituting (M.6.13ch.19), yields

$$
\boxed{\quad
\lim_{u\downarrow0}\frac{\mathcal A(c(u))}{u}=\frac23.
\quad}
\tag{M.6.13ch.21}
$$

For both original exact-error and at-most-error infima, the upper slope $2/3$ is therefore realizable with a fixed complete reference dimension ten and exactly two reference-charge values. No reference-dimension limit is required. This is not a claim that ten is the minimum possible apparatus dimension or that two is the minimum resource count under any alternative accounting convention.

**Exact discriminator and optimality within qubit seed references.**

For the state-only discrimination quality $q_Q$ defined above, the balanced qubit seed has

$$
q_{Q_0}(\sigma_c)=3c^2/4
\tag{M.6.13ch.22}
$$

exactly, and the invariant observable $B(c)$ in (M.6.13ch.4) is its optimizing Sylvester solution. Put $p=(1,3,3,1)/8$. Indeed every nontrivial total-charge block contains two adjacent system levels. On such a block the mean discrimination state is diagonal, with entries $p_i/2$ and $p_{i+1}/2$, and the difference-state off-diagonal entry is $c\sqrt{p_ip_{i+1}}/2$. The Sylvester solution is therefore $2c\sqrt{p_ip_{i+1}}/(p_i+p_{i+1})$, giving precisely the three weights in (M.6.13ch.4). Summing the three block qualities gives (M.6.13ch.22).

There is also a matching bound for every two-dimensional seed reference, without assuming a balanced diagonal or real coherence. This calculation concerns the two-dimensional seed subclass; Theorem M.6.13ck proves the complete-class lower bound.

For a reference with two distinct charges, write an arbitrary qubit state as

$$
\sigma=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1+a&b e^{i\phi}\\b e^{-i\phi}&1-a\end{pmatrix},
\quad b\ge0,\quad a^2+b^2\le1,
\qquad
\mathcal A(\sigma)=F(a^2+b^2)-F(a^2),
\tag{M.6.13ch.23}
$$

where $F(t)=[(1+\sqrt t)\log(1+\sqrt t)+(1-\sqrt t)\log(1-\sqrt t)]/2$. If the reference charge is fully degenerate, its dephasing is the identity and both $\mathcal A$ and $q$ are zero instead; that case is immediate. For two distinct charges, let their absolute gap be $g$. For gap one, the total-charge block joining system levels $i,i+1$ contributes

$$
\frac{2b^2p_ip_{i+1}}{(1-a)p_i+(1+a)p_{i+1}},\qquad p=(1,3,3,1)/8.
\tag{M.6.13ch.24}
$$

This follows by inserting the two diagonal entries of the mean state and the off-diagonal difference entry into the supported Sylvester formula above. Reversing charge order exchanges the first and last contributions. Their sum, and the single extreme-level pair for gap three, give

$$
q(\sigma)=
\begin{cases}
\frac{3b^2}{8}\frac{8-a^2}{4-a^2},&g=1,\\
 b^2/8,&g=3,\\
0,&g\notin\{1,3\}.
\end{cases}
\tag{M.6.13ch.25}
$$

Only odd system-charge differences contribute to the difference state. A gap of two, an unmatched real gap, or a degenerate reference charge therefore gives zero quality. For gap three only the pair of extreme system charge levels contributes. For gap one the coefficient is the sum of all three adjacent pairs. The phase of the coherence cancels from the squared magnitudes.

If $b=0$, both asymmetry and quality vanish, including at $|a|=1$, so the bound is immediate. If $b>0$, positivity implies $|a|<1$. Convexity and the nonnegative power series for $F$ then give

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal A(\sigma)&\ge b^2 F'(a^2),\\
2F'(a^2)&=\frac{\operatorname{artanh}|a|}{|a|}
=1+\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{a^{2n}}{2n+1}
\ge1+\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{a^{2n}}{2\,4^n}
=\frac{8-a^2}{2(4-a^2)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13ch.26}
$$

The value at $a=0$ is interpreted continuously. The coefficient comparison is elementary: $2\cdot4^n\ge2n+1$ for $n\ge1$. Equations (M.6.13ch.25)–(M.6.13ch.26) imply

$$
q(\sigma)\le\frac32\mathcal A(\sigma)
\qquad\text{for every two-dimensional reference seed.}
\tag{M.6.13ch.27}
$$

For gap three the stronger $q\le\mathcal A/4$ follows from $\mathcal A\ge b^2/2$; zero-quality cases are immediate. The balanced charge-one family approaches equality in (M.6.13ch.27) as $c$ tends to zero. Thus the infimum $\mathcal A/q$ over qubit seeds is exactly $2/3$. This result also permits an independent initially uncorrelated neutral factor. To prove this precisely, let $\eta$ be any finite neutral density matrix. Total-charge dephasing tensors both $\Omega_s$ with $\eta$, hence tensors the mean and difference states with $\eta$. On their joint support the old optimal discriminator $B_\sigma\otimes I$ solves the new Sylvester equation; extending it by zero off that support gives the supported optimizer above. Its quality is $\operatorname{Tr}(R_\sigma B_\sigma^2)\operatorname{Tr}\eta=q_Q(\sigma)$. The entropy $S(\eta)$ cancels from $S(\mathcal G_Q\sigma\otimes\eta)-S(\sigma\otimes\eta)$, so asymmetry is unchanged as well. It does not cover arbitrary correlations with neutral degeneracies, larger reference supports, or the entire complete apparatus class.

The complete finite-quality frontier is not evaluated by this apparatus construction. $\square$

### M.6.13ci Complete-source matrix interface and full-corner mean-zero coercivity

<a id="theorem-m613ci-universal-full-corner-mean-zero-coercivity"></a>**Theorem M.6.13ci (Universal Full-Corner Mean-Zero Coercivity).** The complete spin source
of Theorem M.6.13ch admits the following matrix-source interface. With its canonical Jordan
operator $L_B=-3\partial_\theta^2+\mathcal J_{W_B}$, let $P$ project on constant Fourier
amplitudes, $Q=I-P$, $L_0=-3\partial_\theta^2$ and $R_0=(QL_0Q)^{-1}$.
Here these $P,Q$ are Fourier projections, not charge operators. For every odd Hermitian
contraction $B$ and every finite coefficient dimension, including its independent direct
$0\leftrightarrow3$ corner, the full mean-zero Hermitian form has the bound below.
All circle measures are normalized and all traces are ordinary coefficient traces.

**Normalized matrix sources and the supported optimizer.**

Let $d\ge1$, $d\mu=d\theta/(2\pi)$, and
$$
p=(1,3,3,1)/8,\quad v_\theta=(\sqrt{p_i}e^{ii\theta})_{i=0}^3,\quad V_\theta=v_\theta\otimes I_d,
\quad \widehat Q=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2,3)\otimes I_d,
\quad J=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,-1)\otimes I_d.
$$
For a positive matrix symbol $F$ with $\int\operatorname{Tr}F\,d\mu=1$, set
$$
\tau=\int F\,d\mu,\quad
\Omega_F=\int V_\theta F_\theta V_\theta^*\,d\mu,\quad
R_F=(\Omega_F+J\Omega_FJ)/2,\quad D_F=(\Omega_F-J\Omega_FJ)/2.
$$
Write $\delta X=i[\widehat Q,X]$, and define
$$
q(F)=\sup_{B=B^*,\ JBJ=-B}\{2\operatorname{Tr}(D_FB)-\operatorname{Tr}(R_FB^2)\}.
\tag{M.6.13ci.S1}
$$
If $R_F>0$, its unique optimizer solves
$$
R_FB_F+B_FR_F=2D_F,\qquad
q(F)=\operatorname{Tr}(R_FB_F^2)=\operatorname{Tr}(D_FB_F).
\tag{M.6.13ci.S2}
$$
It is an odd contraction. For smooth uniformly positive $F$, it is a strict contraction and all the matrices in (M.6.13ci.S2) depend smoothly on $F$. Define
$$
E(F)=\operatorname{Tr}R_F(\delta B_F)^2,
\quad H_{\rm mat}(F)=\int\operatorname{Tr}(F\log F)\,d\mu-\operatorname{Tr}(\tau\log\tau),
$$
$$
\mathrm D\log_A[X]=\int_0^\infty(A+sI)^{-1}X(A+sI)^{-1}\,ds,
\quad I_{\rm BKM}(F)=\int\operatorname{Tr}(F'\mathrm D\log_F[F'])\,d\mu,
\quad I_{\rm WY}(F)=4\int\operatorname{Tr}[(\sqrt F\,)'^2]\,d\mu.
\tag{M.6.13ci.S3}
$$
All derivatives and inverses in this display are taken on the stated faithful domain.

**Proof of optimizer facts.** The inequalities $R_F\pm D_F\succeq0$ imply $D_F$ is supported on $E_F=\operatorname{supp}R_F$. On this support,
$$
B_F=2\int_0^\infty e^{-tR_F}D_Fe^{-tR_F}\,dt,
$$
with zero extension on $E_F^\perp$. This solves the Sylvester equation. Positivity and $-R_F\preceq D_F\preceq R_F$ show $-E_F\preceq B_F\preceq E_F$; parity follows by uniqueness on the support. Completing the square gives
$$
2\operatorname{Tr}(D_FB)-\operatorname{Tr}(R_FB^2)
=q(F)-\operatorname{Tr}R_F(B-B_F)^2.
\tag{M.6.13ci.S4}
$$
Thus the supported optimizer suffices, even for singular pairs. In particular the supremum may be restricted to the fixed compact set of odd Hermitian contractions, so $q$ is continuous in $(R,D)$.

If $F_\theta\succeq mI>0$, then $\Omega_F\succeq m\operatorname{diag}(p)\otimes I>0$, since $\int v_\theta v_\theta^*d\mu=\operatorname{diag}(p)$. Hence $R_F\pm D_F>0$. The same $\int$ formula gives
$$
I\mp B_F=2\int_0^\infty e^{-tR_F}(R_F\mp D_F)e^{-tR_F}\,dt>0.
$$
The inverse Sylvester map is smooth where $R_F>0$. These assertions do not require a dimension-uniform or smallest-eigenvalue-uniform bound. $\square$

**Canonical Hermitian/Jordan form.**

For any odd Hermitian contraction $B$, whether or not it optimizes a source, define
$$
K_B(\theta)=V_\theta^*(2B-B^2)V_\theta,\qquad M_B(\theta)=V_\theta^*(\delta B)^2V_\theta,\qquad
\mathscr D_B[H](\theta)=V_\theta^*(2H-BH-HB)V_\theta
$$
for odd Hermitian $H$. If $B=B_{G^2}$, its Sylvester normal equation gives
$$
\int\operatorname{Tr}(G^2 \mathscr D_B[H])d\mu=0.
\tag{M.6.13ci.S5}
$$
Equivalently, its canonical potential is $W_B=2(V_\theta^*BV_\theta)''-(V_\theta^*B^2V_\theta)''+M_B$. The canonical quadratic form is
$$
\mathcal Q_B(G)=3\int\operatorname{Tr}G'^2d\mu+
\int\operatorname{Tr}\{G^2(K_B''+M_B)\}d\mu,
\quad G\in H^1(S^1;\operatorname{Herm}_d).
\tag{M.6.13ci.S8}
$$
The form is defined for every odd Hermitian contraction, including tests that are not the optimizer of a source.

**Proof.** Integrating $\operatorname{Tr}(G^2\mathscr D_B[H])$ expresses it as $\operatorname{Tr}[(2D-RB-BR)H]$, proving (M.6.13ci.S5). The derivation identity $\delta^2(B^2)=(\delta^2B)B+B\delta^2B+2(\delta B)^2$ gives
$$
\mathscr D_B[\delta^2B]=K_B''+2M_B.
$$
At the optimizer, (M.6.13ci.S5) therefore gives
$$
\mathcal Q_B(G)=3\int\operatorname{Tr}G'^2d\mu-E(G^2).
\tag{M.6.13ci.S6}
$$
For $G=\sqrt F$, (M.6.13ci.S6) is exactly $\mathcal Q_B(\sqrt F)=3I_{\rm WY}(F)/4-E(F)$.  The potential $K_B''+M_B$ is a bounded Hermitian trigonometric polynomial of degree at most three. Smooth Hermitian functions are dense in the real $H^1$ space, and both terms of the form are continuous in that topology. Thus proofs of its positivity on smooth amplitudes extend to the displayed full domain. On the real Hermitian HS space the potential acts by Jordan multiplication $X\mapsto(W_BX+XW_B)/2$, $W_B=K_B''+M_B$. Replacing this real Hermitian problem by unrestricted complex left multiplication is a stronger relaxation, not the same statement. $\square$

**Metric ordering.**

For the displayed Fisher convention, put $L(a,b)=(\log a-\log b)/(a-b)$ for $a,b>0$, with $L(a,a)=1/a$. Then
$$
I_{\rm BKM}(F)\ge I_{\rm WY}(F)\ge I_{\rm SLD}(F),\qquad
I_{\rm SLD}(F)=\int\operatorname{Tr}[F'\mathcal J_F^{-1}(F')]d\mu,
\quad\mathcal J_F(X)=(FX+XF)/2.
\tag{M.6.13ci.S7}
$$
**Proof.** In an eigenbasis of $F$, the three coefficients against $|X_{ij}|^2$ are respectively $L(a,b)$, $4/(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)^2$, and $2/(a+b)$. The first comparison follows by setting $r=\sqrt{a/b}\ge1$ in
$\log r\ge2(r-1)/(r+1)$; the difference has derivative $(r-1)^2/[r(r+1)^2]\ge0$. The second is $(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)^2\le2(a+b)$. Continuous diagonal values agree. $\square$

**Full mean-zero statement.**

Use the Hermitian/Jordan operator and Fourier projections just defined. All coefficient dimensions are finite and arbitrary. The four forward odd blocks $a=B_{01},b=B_{12},c=B_{23},e=B_{03}$ are independent; the direct gap-three corner is not removed.

**The complete contraction bound.**

For every odd Hermitian contraction $B$,
$$
\boxed{\quad QL_BQ\ge\frac47QL_0Q\ge\frac{12}{7}Q,
\qquad (QL_BQ)^{-1}\le\frac74R_0.\quad}                 \tag{M.6.13ci.1}
$$
The bound holds on the complete mean-zero Hermitian form domain. It does not assert positivity of the constant Schur operator.

**Proof: potential and contraction bounds.** Put $a=\sqrt3\alpha,c=\sqrt3\gamma$. The ordered four-spin path expansion gives
$$
\begin{split}
W_0={}&\tfrac18(3\alpha\alpha^*+9\alpha^*\alpha+3bb^*+3b^*b
 +9\gamma\gamma^*+3\gamma^*\gamma+9ee^*+9e^*e),\\
W_1={}&-\tfrac34(\alpha+b+\gamma),\\
W_2={}&\tfrac98(\alpha b+b\gamma)+\tfrac{21}{8}(e\gamma^*+\alpha^*e),
\qquad W_3=-\tfrac94e,\qquad W_{-k}=W_k^*.
\end{split}                                             \tag{M.6.13ci.2}
$$
In original variables, $W_2=(\sqrt3/8)[3ab+3bc+7ec^*+7a^*e]$. These are the coefficients of $V^*[2\delta^2B-B\delta^2B-\delta^2BB-(\delta B)^2]V$; all multiplication orders are retained.

The four diagonal compressions of $B^2\le I$ give
$$
aa^*+ee^*\le I,\quad a^*a+bb^*\le I,\quad
b^*b+cc^*\le I,\quad e^*e+c^*c\le I.
$$
Thus $0\le W_0\le3I$: the two outer weighted rows are at most $9I/8$ each, and the two inner rows at most $3I/8$ each.

Each of $ab,bc,ec^*,a^*e$ has norm at most $1/2$. Indeed compress $B$ to the three spin vertices on the relevant two-edge path. That principal compression is still a Hermitian contraction; its square is a positive contraction whose off-diagonal endpoint block is exactly the stated product. An off-diagonal block of a positive contraction has norm at most $1/2$, by centering the contraction at $I/2$. This argument does not assume that deleting an edge preserves the norm of the entire four-spin matrix. Consequently
$$
\|W_1\|\le\frac{13}{8},\qquad
\|W_2\|\le\frac{5\sqrt3}{4}\le\frac{13}{6},\qquad
\|W_3\|\le\frac94,
$$
and
$$
\|W_B\|_\infty\le3+2\left(\frac{13}{8}+\frac{13}{6}+\frac94\right)
=\frac{181}{12}.                                      \tag{M.6.13ci.3}
$$
These scalar norms are used only on the remote tail and its boundary. The central certificate retains all positive corner terms and complete contraction relations.

**Proof: a stronger mean-zero vector statement.** We prove first that for every mean-zero $u\in H^1(S^1;\mathbb C^d)$,
$$
\int(3\|u'\|^2+u^*W_Bu)d\mu\ge\frac{12}{7}\int\|u'\|^2d\mu.
\tag{M.6.13ci.4}
$$
This auxiliary left-vector statement is restricted to mean-zero amplitudes; no unrestricted left-vector form bound is used.

Subtract $(4/7)L_0$ and split the nonzero Fourier indices into
$$
\mathcal C=\{n:0<|n|\le8\},\qquad \mathcal T=\{n:|n|\ge9\}.
$$
On $\mathcal T$, (M.6.13ci.3) gives the positive lower bound
$$
\frac97\,81-\frac{181}{12}=\frac{7481}{84}.            \tag{M.6.13ci.5}
$$
Bandwidth three makes the central-tail coupling vanish on all central modes except
$\mathcal E=\{-8,-7,-6,6,7,8\}$. The positive and negative boundary components are disjoint. Componentwise norms bound each coupling by the scalar triangular matrix
$$
T_0=\begin{pmatrix}9/4&13/6&13/8\\0&9/4&13/6\\0&0&9/4\end{pmatrix}.
$$
The leading principal minors of $(196/9)I-T_0^*T_0$ are
$$
\frac{2407}{144},\qquad\frac{1224571}{6912},\qquad
\frac{2609797}{110592},
$$
all positive, so $\|T_0\|\le14/3$. No commutation of the coefficient matrices is used. The coupling $K$ therefore satisfies $K^*K\le(196/9)P_{\mathcal E}$. Exact tail Schur completion shows that (M.6.13ci.4) follows from the finite central inequality
$$
P_{\mathcal C}(L_{\rm left}-\tfrac47L_0)P_{\mathcal C}
-\frac{5488}{22443}P_{\mathcal E}\ge0,
\qquad L_{\rm left}=-3\partial^2+W_B,                 \tag{M.6.13ci.6}
$$
since $(196/9)/(7481/84)=5488/22443$. This controls every omitted Fourier mode before the finite certificate is applied.

**Proof: complete rational localizers.** In even/odd spin order,
$$
B=\begin{pmatrix}0&C\\C^*&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
C=\begin{pmatrix}\sqrt3\alpha&e\\b^*&\sqrt3\gamma\end{pmatrix}.
$$
Congruences of $I-CC^*$ and $I-C^*C$ by $\operatorname{diag}(I/\sqrt3,I)$ and $\operatorname{diag}(I,I/\sqrt3)$ give positive operator matrices
$$
\Lambda_1=\begin{pmatrix}
I/3-\alpha\alpha^*-ee^*/3&-\alpha b-e\gamma^*\\
-b^*\alpha^*-\gamma e^*&I-b^*b-3\gamma\gamma^*
\end{pmatrix},
$$
$$
\Lambda_2=\begin{pmatrix}
I-3\alpha^*\alpha-bb^*&-\alpha^*e-b\gamma\\
-e^*\alpha-\gamma^*b^*&I/3-e^*e/3-\gamma^*\gamma
\end{pmatrix}.                                       \tag{M.6.13ci.7}
$$
Every corner correlation is retained.

**Proof: the exact finite operator certificate.** For independent vectors $u_n\in\mathbb C^d$, $n\in\mathcal C$, the polynomial in (M.6.13ci.6) is
$$
\mathcal P(u)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal C}
\left(\frac97n^2-\frac{5488}{22443}\mathbf1_{\mathcal E}(n)\right)\|u_n\|^2
+\sum_{n,m\in\mathcal C}u_n^*W_{n-m}u_m.             \tag{M.6.13ci.8}
$$
The complete rational data printed below specify the exact representation
$$
\mathcal P(u)=\sum_{\rm free}\sum_{i,j}Q_{ij}v_i^*v_j
+\sum_{\rm local}\sum_{i,j}Q_{ij}u_{n_i}^*\Lambda_{s_i,s_j}u_{n_j}.
\tag{M.6.13ci.9}
$$
There are sixty-one Gram blocks, with maximum size nine and $1,208$ full rational entries.
The ordered alphabet is $(\alpha,\alpha^*,b,b^*,\gamma,\gamma^*,e,e^*)$, with grades $(1,-1,1,-1,1,-1,3,-3)$. Adjoint reverses multiplication order and interchanges each letter with its adjoint. Each free basis row gives the left word $w_i$ and mode $n_i$, denoting $w_i u_{n_i}$; each local row gives its localizer component $s_i$ and mode $n_i$. The matrix tables give the exact rational $Q$ and $R$, including every basis, component, localizer coefficient and entry.
Expand each free term as $u_{n_i}^*w_i^*w_ju_{n_j}$ and each local term with the displayed
$\Lambda_{s_i,s_j}$. The resulting literal ordered coefficient array is exactly the central
target (M.6.13ci.8), with $356$ nonzero ordered terms. Grouping terms with their adjoints gives $250$ coefficient pairs. The equality holds before grouping.
For each Gram the exact symmetric matrix $Q-RR^{\mathsf T}$ has positive diagonal exceeding
its absolute off-diagonal row sum. Therefore all Grams are positive definite, and the
ordered vector/operator identity is nonnegative under the positive localizers.
It uses no cyclic trace reduction, fixed coefficient dimension or matrix sampling.

**Complete mean-zero rational data.**
These sixty-one Gram blocks specify the finite ordered operator identity (M.6.13ci.9). The full tail estimate now proves (M.6.13ci.4). Apply it columnwise to a Hermitian mean-zero matrix amplitude $G$. Pointwise $\operatorname{Tr}G^*W_BG=\operatorname{Tr}G^2W_B$, and derivative energies coincide. This proves (M.6.13ci.1) on the real Hermitian form domain and its Jordan complexification. Density extends finite Fourier calculations to $H^1$, and the positive kinetic gap yields the inverse order. $\square$

### M.6.13cj The full-corner constant Schur certificate

Use Theorem M.6.13ci's matrix-source and Jordan interface. The constant Schur operator is
$$
\mathfrak F_B=P L_B P-P L_B Q(Q L_B Q)^{-1}Q L_B P.
$$
Its full mean-zero inverse exists by Theorem M.6.13ci. The following exact certificate
retains all four independent odd forward blocks and all finite coefficient dimensions.

<a id="theorem-m613cj-full-odd-discriminator-hermitian-certificate"></a>**Theorem M.6.13cj (Full Odd-Discriminator Hermitian Certificate).** Let $B$ be any odd Hermitian contraction, with independent forward blocks
$$
B_{01}=a,\quad B_{12}=b,\quad B_{23}=c,\quad B_{03}=e
$$
and reverse adjoints. The corner $e$ is unrestricted. Put $Z=bb^*+b^*b$ and
$$
\begin{split}
q_2(H)={}&\tfrac14\|aH-Hc\|^2
+\tfrac1{32}\|\{H,a+c-\sqrt3b\}\|^2
+\tfrac1{16}\|[H,a-c]\|^2+\tfrac3{16}\|[H,b]\|^2\\
&+\tfrac{15}{32}\|\{H,e\}\|^2+\tfrac9{16}\|[H,e]\|^2,
\end{split}
$$
where these are Hilbert–Schmidt norms and $H$ is a Hermitian constant. Then
$$
\boxed{\quad
\langle H,\mathfrak F_BH\rangle
\ge\frac{q_2(H)+\operatorname{Tr}H^2Z^2}{100000}.
\quad}                                                   \tag{M.6.13cj.1}
$$
In particular the full Hermitian form (M.6.13ci.S8) is nonnegative for every odd contraction and every finite coefficient dimension. Inactive directions remain allowed; no normality, commutativity, neutrality, adjacency-only, rank, invertibility, activity-gap or Fourier-cutoff assumption is imposed.

**Proof: ordered potential and complete residual.** Set $a=\sqrt3\alpha$, $c=\sqrt3\gamma$. Direct spin-path expansion gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
W_0={}&\tfrac38(\alpha\alpha^*+3\alpha^*\alpha+bb^*+b^*b+3\gamma\gamma^*+\gamma^*\gamma)
+\tfrac98(ee^*+e^*e),\\
W_1={}&-\tfrac34(\alpha+b+\gamma),\qquad W_3=-\tfrac94e,\\
W_2={}&\tfrac98(\alpha b+b\gamma)+\tfrac{21}{8}(e\gamma^*+\alpha^*e),
\qquad W_{-k}=W_k^*.
\end{aligned}                                            \tag{M.6.13cj.2}
$$
All multiplication orders are retained. Let $U$ contain the coefficients at $\pm1,\pm3$ and $V$ those at $0,\pm2$. For the given $H$, choose $G=H+g_1+g_2$ by
$$
(g_1)_n=-\frac{\mathcal J_{U_n}H}{3n^2},\quad n=\pm1,\pm3,
$$
$$
(g_2)_n=-\frac{\mathcal J_{V_n}H+\sum_k\mathcal J_{U_k}(g_1)_{n-k}}{3n^2},
\quad n=\pm2,\pm4,\pm6.                               \tag{M.6.13cj.3}
$$
Absent coefficients vanish. Ordered expansion gives $G_{-n}=G_n^*$ and cancels all degree-one and degree-two terms in $QL_BG$. Its remaining residual is $r_3+r_4$, where $r_3$ has degree three and frequencies $\pm1,\pm3,\pm5,\pm7,\pm9$, while $r_4=Q\mathcal J_Vg_2$ has degree four and frequencies $\pm2,\pm4,\pm6,\pm8$. The exact finite trial energy is
$$
\mathcal Q_B(G)=3\sum_n n^2\operatorname{Tr}G_n^*G_n
 +\sum_{n,m}\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(G_n^*\mathcal J_{W_{n-m}}G_m\bigr).
\tag{M.6.13cj.4}
$$
Its quadratic coefficient is exactly the six-square $q_2$ above.

**Proof: degree-eight absorption.** The weighted average of the four diagonal blocks of $B^2$ equals $W_0-ee^*-e^*e$. Consequently $0\le W_0\le3I$. In original variables,
$$
W_2=\frac{\sqrt3}{8}(X+Y),\quad
X=3ab+7ec^*=[a,e]\binom{3b}{7c^*},\quad
Y=7a^*e+3bc=[a^*,b]\binom{7e}{3c}.
$$
The displayed rows are contractions. Hence $X^*X\le9b^*b+49cc^*$ and $Y^*Y\le49e^*e+9c^*c$. Apply weighted Cauchy–Schwarz with weight $27/49$ to $X+Y$. After multiplying by $3/64$, the coefficient ratios against the corresponding terms of $W_0$ are $171/98,19/2,931/162,19/2$. For the adjoint expression use contraction rows $[b^*,c]$, $[e^*,c^*]$ and reciprocal weight. Thus
$$
W_2^*W_2\le\tfrac{19}{2}W_0,\qquad W_2W_2^*\le\tfrac{19}{2}W_0.
\tag{M.6.13cj.5}
$$
It follows that $\|\mathcal J_{W_0}Y\|^2\le3\langle Y,\mathcal J_{W_0}Y\rangle$ and $\|\mathcal J_{W_{\pm2}}Y\|^2\le(19/2)\langle Y,\mathcal J_{W_0}Y\rangle$.

For positive even frequencies $2,4,6$, the weighted residual norm is bounded by the scalar matrix
$$
A_*=\begin{pmatrix}
1/2&s/2&0\\s/4&1/4&s/4\\0&s/6&1/6\\0&0&s/8
\end{pmatrix},\qquad s=\sqrt{19/6}.
$$
The leading principal minors of $(11/8)I-A_*^*A_*$ are $89/96$, $1909/20736$, and $199121/7962624$, all positive. The negative-frequency chain is identical; $Q$ removes the zero mode. Therefore, with
$$
T=\sum_{n\ne0,\ n\ \mathrm{even}}\langle(g_2)_n,\mathcal J_{W_0}(g_2)_n\rangle,
$$
one has $\langle r_4,R_0r_4\rangle\le(11/8)T$. Exact Schur completion and the inverse bound $7R_0/4\le16R_0/9$ from Theorem M.6.13ci now give
$$
\langle H,\mathfrak F_BH\rangle\ge K_6,
\quad K_6=\mathcal Q_B(G)-\frac{16}{9}\sum_{n\ \mathrm{odd}}
\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(r_3)_n^*(r_3)_n}{3n^2}-\frac{22}{9}T.
\tag{M.6.13cj.6}
$$
The polynomial $K_6$ has only coefficient degrees two, four and six. Neither residual sectors nor infinite Fourier tails have been omitted.

**Proof: exact rational tracial certificate.** In even/odd spin order $B=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&C\\C^*&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with $C=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\sqrt3\alpha&e\\b^*&\sqrt3\gamma\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Congruences of $I-CC^*$ and $I-C^*C$ give positive localizers
$$
\Lambda_1=\begin{pmatrix}
I/3-\alpha\alpha^*-ee^*/3&-(\alpha b+e\gamma^*)\\
-(b^*\alpha^*+\gamma e^*)&I-b^*b-3\gamma\gamma^*
\end{pmatrix},
$$
$$
\Lambda_2=\begin{pmatrix}
I-3\alpha^*\alpha-bb^*&-(\alpha^*e+b\gamma)\\
-(e^*\alpha+\gamma^*b^*)&I/3-\gamma^*\gamma-e^*e/3
\end{pmatrix}.                                         \tag{M.6.13cj.7}
$$
The full rational data below specify every literal ordered basis, localizer component, Gram entry and positive-definiteness witness.

The exact real-trace identity is
$$
K_6-\frac{q_2+\operatorname{Tr}H^2Z^2}{100000}
=\sum_{\rm free}\sum_{i,j}Q_{ij}\operatorname{Tr}(v_i^*v_j)
+\sum_{\rm local}\sum_{i,j}Q_{ij}\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(v_i^*\Lambda_{s_i,s_j}v_j\bigr).
\tag{M.6.13cj.8}
$$
There are thirty-five strictly positive-definite rational Gram blocks. The nine free dimensions are $509,338,144,36,4,60,45,18,3$; each localizer has blocks of dimensions $2,7,10,7,2,3,21,63,105,105,63,21,3$. Every basis polynomial has exactly one $H$. The degree-one adjacent vectors include $\alpha H-H\gamma$, $\{H,\alpha+\gamma-b\}$, $[H,\alpha-\gamma]$, $[H,b]$, and $[H,\alpha+\gamma]$; the corner vectors are $\{H,e\}$ and $[H,e]$. Phase charges are one for $\alpha,b,\gamma$, three for $e$, opposite for adjoints and zero for $H$. All higher words and component orders are explicit in the data.

For every Gram $Q$, its integer numerator matrix divided by its positive denominator
and its integer factor matrix divided by its positive factor denominator define exact rational
matrices $Q,R$. The matrix $Q-RR^{\mathsf T}$ has positive diagonal exceeding the absolute
sum of every off-diagonal row, so every Gram is strictly positive definite.
The alphabet in the data is
$(\alpha,\alpha^*,b,b^*,\gamma,\gamma^*,e,e^*,H)$, coded $0,\ldots,8$.
Adjoint reverses a word, interchanges the adjacent pairs $0\leftrightarrow1$, $2\leftrightarrow3$,
$4\leftrightarrow5$, $6\leftrightarrow7$, and fixes $8$.
Each basis polynomial is printed explicitly in the indexed tables.
For every block form its ordered products $v_i^*v_j$, or $v_i^*\Lambda_{s_i,s_j}v_j$ for its
printed localizer and component list, and multiply by $Q_{ij}$.
For real trace reduction identify each word with the lexicographically least cyclic rotation
of itself or its adjoint. This preserves the trace of the self-adjoint quadratic forms and
never commutes unrelated letters. The reconstructed sum is exactly (M.6.13cj.8): all
$68,591$ nonzero canonical target coefficients agree, including the independent potential,
Jordan correctors, complete residual, six-square quadratic term and full contraction localizers.
The target polynomial is defined by (M.6.13cj.2)–(M.6.13cj.7); its coefficients follow by finite ordered expansion and real-trace reduction.
Thus this is a real-tracial identity for arbitrary complex matrix coefficients and Hermitian $H$,
not a literal free-operator identity. It is distinct from the ordered vector identity of
Theorem M.6.13ci.

The following tables give every ordered basis, localizer component, rational Gram entry and rational positive-definiteness witness. Symmetry determines the lower Gram triangle; unlisted entries are zero. Thus all finite inputs of the certificate are explicit mathematical objects.

**Complete full-corner rational data.**
The following indexed polynomial and rational matrix tables specify every input of the tracial identity (M.6.13cj.8). All indices start at zero. Products in each basis polynomial retain their printed order. A scalar constant $c$ in an operator polynomial means $cI$. The target polynomial is defined by the displayed finite potential, corrector and residual formulas above, so its coefficients require no additional input. A matrix row lists exact rational numerators, with its denominator stated explicitly.

The localizer used by the tables with index $r=1$ is
$$
\Lambda^{\mathrm{tab}}_1=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{1}{3}-\alpha\,\alpha^*-\frac{1}{3}e\,e^*&-\alpha\,b-e\,\gamma^*\\-b^*\,\alpha^*-\gamma\,e^*&1-b^*\,b-3\gamma\,\gamma^*\end{pmatrix}.
$$

The localizer used by the tables with index $r=2$ is
$$
\Lambda^{\mathrm{tab}}_2=\begin{pmatrix}1-3\alpha^*\,\alpha-b\,b^*&-\alpha^*\,e-b\,\gamma\\-\gamma^*\,b^*-e^*\,\alpha&\frac{1}{3}-\gamma^*\,\gamma-\frac{1}{3}e^*\,e\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**Canonical generation of the expanded basis lists.** Let
$$
\mathcal A=(\alpha,\alpha^*,b,b^*,\gamma,\gamma^*,e,e^*),\qquad
\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal A)=(1,-1,1,-1,1,-1,3,-3)
$$
with the displayed alphabet order. For $d\in\{2,3\}$ and integer $q$, let

in lexicographic order. Define the ordered list
$$
F_{d,q}=\bigl(w_1\cdots w_jH w_{j+1}\cdots w_d\bigr)_
{w\in\mathcal W_{d,q},\;j=0,\ldots,d},
$$
where the word index is outermost and the insertion position $j$ increases first.
An empty charge class gives the empty list. The initial vectors are
$$
\begin{aligned}
u_{0}={}&\alpha\,H-H\,\gamma\\
u_{1}={}&\alpha\,H-b\,H+\gamma\,H+H\,\alpha-H\,b+H\,\gamma\\
u_{2}={}&-\alpha\,H+\gamma\,H+H\,\alpha-H\,\gamma\\
u_{3}={}&-b\,H+H\,b\\
u_{4}={}&-\alpha\,H-\gamma\,H+H\,\alpha+H\,\gamma\\
u_5={}&e\,H+H\,e,\qquad u_6=-e\,H+H\,e.
\end{aligned}
$$
The bases of free blocks $0,\ldots,8$, in that order, are
$$

(u_5,u_6)\mathbin{\Vert}F_{3,3},\quad
F_{3,5},\ F_{3,7},\ F_{3,9},\quad
F_{2,0},\ F_{2,2},\ F_{2,4},\ F_{2,6},
$$
where $\Vert$ means concatenation. Their dimensions are respectively
$509,338,144,36,4,60,45,18,3$.
For each localizer, its eight degree-two blocks use

$$

\bigl((v,1):v\in F_{2,q-2}\bigr).

These are blocks $14,\ldots,21$ for $\Lambda^{\mathrm{tab}}_1$ and
$27,\ldots,34$ for $\Lambda^{\mathrm{tab}}_2$. Their dimensions are
$3,21,63,105,105,63,21,3$ in each case. The degree-one localizer bases remain
explicitly listed below.
