Positive Grams and (M.6.13cj.7) make the right side of (M.6.13cj.8) nonnegative. Combined with (M.6.13cj.6), this proves (M.6.13cj.1). Full Schur completion proves the claimed Hermitian form inequality on $H^1$. $\square$

### M.6.13ck The exact full-reference spin-three-halves coefficient

<a id="theorem-m613ck-exact-complete-reference-spin-three-halves-endpoint"></a>**Theorem M.6.13ck (Exact Complete-Reference Spin-Three-Halves Endpoint).** For every finite coefficient dimension, faithful density $\tau$, odd Hermitian contraction $B$ and $0<c\le2/3$,
$$
Z_c(B,\tau)=\int\operatorname{Tr}\exp(\log\tau+cK_B(\theta))d\mu\le1,
$$
strictly when $B\ne0$. Every bounded normalized positive semidefinite matrix symbol obeys
$$
H_{\rm mat}(F)\ge\tfrac23q(F),
\qquad H_{\rm mat}(F)>\tfrac23q(F)\quad\hbox{if }q(F)>0.
\tag{M.6.13ck.1}
$$
These statements include singular sources; no mean-consistency assumption is imposed on a test Gibbs parameter.

**Proof: strictness and discriminator heat.** If $H>0$ and the right side of (M.6.13cj.1) vanishes, then $ZH=0$ forces $b=0$. The corner anticommutator square forces $e=0$. The other anticommutator square gives $a+c=0$, and $aH-Hc=0$ becomes $\{H,a\}=0$, hence $a=c=0$. Thus, for every smooth uniformly positive $F$ and nonzero contractive test $B$, the full Schur completion of Theorem M.6.13cj and $H=\int\sqrt F>0$ give $\mathcal Q_B(\sqrt F)>0$. No optimizer assumption is used here.

Evolve the discriminator, not the source, by $B_s=e^{s\delta^2}B$. This spin dephasing map is a unital completely positive average of charge conjugations. It preserves oddness and contractivity, multiplies adjacent blocks by $e^{-s}$ and the corner by $e^{-9s}$, and sends $B_s$ to zero. Nonzero $B$ remains nonzero at every finite $s$. Put $Z_s=Z_c(B_s,\tau)$ and $F_s=\exp(\log\tau+cK_{B_s})/Z_s$. Each auxiliary Gibbs source is smooth and faithful, and $Z_s\to1$.

For an arbitrary test write $\mathcal E_B(F)=\operatorname{Tr}R_F(\delta B)^2$. The identities $(\log F_s)'=cK_{B_s}'$ and $\mathscr D_B[\delta^2B]=K_B''+2M_B$ give
$$
\int\operatorname{Tr}(F K_B'')d\mu=-I_{\rm BKM}(F)/c,
\qquad
\mathcal Q_B(\sqrt F)=\tfrac34I_{\rm WY}(F)-I_{\rm BKM}(F)/c+\mathcal E_B(F),
$$
$$
\frac{d}{ds}\log Z_s
=-I_{\rm BKM}(F_s)+2c\mathcal E_{B_s}(F_s)
=I_{\rm BKM}(F_s)-\tfrac{3c}{2}I_{\rm WY}(F_s)
 +2c\mathcal Q_{B_s}(\sqrt{F_s}).                       \tag{M.6.13ck.2}
$$
Metric ordering and $3c/2\le1$ make this nonnegative, strictly positive for nonzero $B$. Hence $\log Z_s$ increases to zero, proving the partition assertion. This calculation uses neither a Sylvester equation nor $\tau=\int F_s$.

**Proof: arbitrary source rank.** Compress a bounded positive symbol $F$ to the support of its actual mean $\tau=\int F$, on which $\tau$ is faithful. Positivity places $F$ on this support almost everywhere. Let $B$ be its supported odd Sylvester optimizer from Theorem M.6.13ci, zero-extended; it is a contraction and attains $q(F)$. For $c=2/3$ define the faithful auxiliary source $F_B=\exp(\log\tau+cK_B)/Z$. Write $D(F\Vert F_B)=\int\operatorname{Tr}[F(\log F-\log F_B)]d\mu$, with supported logarithms. Pointwise Klein inequality, followed by integration and global trace normalization, gives $D(F\Vert F_B)\ge0$. Using the actual mean yields the exact identity
$$
D(F\Vert F_B)=H_{\rm mat}(F)-cq(F)+\log Z,
\qquad H_{\rm mat}(F)=cq(F)-\log Z+D(F\Vert F_B).
\tag{M.6.13ck.3}
$$
If $q(F)>0$ then $B\ne0$, so $Z<1$ and the inequality is strict. The $q=0$ case follows from entropy nonnegativity. No inverse of $F$ or derivative of its square root is used in this singular-source step. Every mean-entropy and even-phase term remains present. $\square$

**Finite-reference and operational consequences.** For every original complete finite reference,
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge\tfrac23q_Q(\sigma),
\qquad\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)>\tfrac23q_Q(\sigma)\quad\hbox{if }q_Q(\sigma)>0.
\tag{M.6.13ck.R1}
$$
Let $F_=(u)$ and $F_\le(u)$ be the infima of complete-reference asymmetry for this same fixed spin-$3/2$ contract at RMS error exactly, or at most, $\sqrt{1-u}$ respectively. Then the unrestricted constant of Theorem M.6.13ch is
$$
\boxed{\quad c_*=\frac23,\qquad
\lim_{u\downarrow0}\frac{F_=(u)}u
=\lim_{u\downarrow0}\frac{F_\le(u)}u=\frac23.\quad}     \tag{M.6.13ck.R2}
$$
The finite-reference ratio infimum at positive $q$ is not attained. The matching operational upper slope uses the already constructed fixed complete dimension ten.

**Proof.** For a finite integer-charge reference put
$F(\theta)=e^{iQ\theta}\sigma e^{-iQ\theta}$ and $\tau=\mathcal G_Q\sigma$.
The $(i,a;j,b)$ matrix entry of $V_\theta F_\theta V_\theta^*$ contains the phase
$e^{i(i-j+q_a-q_b)\theta}$. Normalized integration therefore gives exactly
$\Omega_+$ of Theorem M.6.13ch. Conjugating by the system parity gives $\Omega_-$,
so its matrix-source mean/difference pair is the actual finite pair and $q(F)=q_Q(\sigma)$.
Unitary conjugacy gives $\int\operatorname{Tr}F\log F=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma\log\sigma$,
and $[Q,\tau]=0$ gives

$$
H_{\rm mat}(F)=D(\sigma\Vert\tau)=\mathcal A_Q(\sigma),
$$

at every state rank.
On the support of $\tau$ it is faithful as a mean; no physical zero-state direction
is removed from the apparatus count by this mathematical compression.

The matrix-source theorem above therefore proves the strict positive-quality inequality, including singular states and arbitrary degeneracy.

For any finite real spectrum, use precisely the integer-coset pinching from M.6.13ch. It preserves $q$ and gives
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)=D(\sigma\Vert\sigma')+\sum_jp_j\mathcal A_{Q_j}(\sigma_j),
\qquad q_Q(\sigma)=\sum_jp_jq_{Q_j}(\sigma_j).
$$
Each branch is integer after a scalar charge shift. If total $q>0$, a positive-weight branch has positive $q$ and hence a strict inequality; all other terms are nonnegative. This proves (M.6.13ck.R1) with every real charge, support, cross-coset coherence, correlation and retained flag intact.

The balanced two-charge family in Theorem M.6.13ch approaches $\mathcal A/q=2/3$, while (M.6.13ck.R1) gives the matching lower bound. Thus $c_*=2/3$ and no finite positive-quality reference attains the ratio infimum. For either original frontier, the actual-model inequality $u\le q_Q$ and (M.6.13ck.R1) give the lower slope $2/3$. The explicitly tuned family of Theorem M.6.13ch supplies every sufficiently small exact $u$ and the matching upper slope, hence both limits in (M.6.13ck.R2). Theorem M.6.13ch supplies the fixed dimension-ten complete conserving-unitary/Yanase-pointer witnesses with exact all-input error tuning, including all five neutral pointer levels. No reference-dimension limit or discarded auxiliary supplies this upper slope. $\square$

For each finite operational model with $u>0$, the established $u\le q_Q(\sigma)$ implies $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)>2u/3$. This does not identify $q$ with $u$, evaluate either infimum at a fixed positive error, or assert a dimension-uniform strict gap at fixed $u$.

### M.6.13cl Dimension-independent positive-quality separation for the complete spin discriminator

<a id="theorem-m613cl-dimension-independent-positive-quality-separation"></a>**Theorem M.6.13cl (Dimension-Independent Positive-Quality Separation).** Retain the complete finite-reference contract and normalized spin-$3/2$ target of Theorem M.6.13ch. Use the full odd-Hermitian-contraction Schur bound of Theorem M.6.13cj
$$
\langle H,\mathfrak F_BH\rangle\ge\frac{q_2(H)+\operatorname{Tr}H^2(bb^*+b^*b)^2}{100000},
$$
with its full six-square $q_2$, including the gap-three corner. Define $g(0)=0$ and, for $0<q\le1$,
$$
g(q)=\frac{q^5e^{-72\pi^2/q}}
 {169344000000000\bigl(1+\sqrt{q/(72\pi)}\bigr)^4}.
\tag{M.6.13cl.1}
$$
Every finite reference, allowing arbitrary real charges, degeneracies, mixed states, neutral factors, retained flags and initial correlations, obeys
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge\frac23q_Q(\sigma)+g\bigl(q_Q(\sigma)\bigr).
\tag{M.6.13cl.2}
$$
Thus no sequence of finite references at a fixed positive discriminator quality can approach the linear bound $2q/3$, even with unbounded dimensions or charge widths. The function $g$ is increasing on $[0,1]$. Consequently, every complete operational model in the range $0\le u=1-\epsilon^2\le1$ obeys
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge\frac23u+g(u).
\tag{M.6.13cl.3}
$$
This uses only $u\le q_Q(\sigma)$; it does not identify the state discriminator with worst-case all-input quality. The bound is not claimed sharp and does not determine an exact finite-error frontier or a dimension optimum.

**Proof. I. Exact complete-source heat identities.** Use the supported matrix-source definitions of Theorem M.6.13ci. For a smooth uniformly positive normalized symbol, let $F_t=e^{t\partial_\theta^2}F$. Then
$$
-\frac{d}{dt}q(F_t)=2E(F_t),\qquad
-\frac{d}{dt}H_{\rm mat}(F_t)=I_{\rm BKM}(F_t),
\tag{M.6.13cl.H1}
$$
and
$$
H_{\rm mat}(F)-\frac23q(F)
=\int_0^\infty\left[I_{\rm BKM}(F_t)-\frac43E(F_t)\right]dt.
\tag{M.6.13cl.H2}
$$
Heat preserves the actual mean $\tau$, normalization, and fixed positive upper and lower bounds. Fourier coefficients give $\dot R_F=\delta^2R_F$ and $\dot D_F=\delta^2D_F$. Differentiating the variational expression at its smooth optimizer cancels the optimizer derivative by $2D_F=R_FB_F+B_FR_F$, leaving
$$
\dot q=2\operatorname{Tr}(\delta^2D_F)B_F-\operatorname{Tr}(\delta^2R_F)B_F^2
=2\operatorname{Tr}D_F\delta^2B_F-\operatorname{Tr}R_F\delta^2(B_F^2).
$$
The derivation $\delta$ is skew-adjoint for the real trace pairing, so $\delta^2$ is self-adjoint. Its product rule is
$$
\delta^2(B_F^2)=(\delta^2B_F)B_F+B_F\delta^2B_F+2(\delta B_F)^2.
$$
The Sylvester equation therefore cancels the first two product terms and gives $\dot q=-2\operatorname{Tr}R_F(\delta B_F)^2$. Finite trace differentiation and integration by parts give
$$
\frac{d}{dt}H_{\rm mat}(F_t)=\int\operatorname{Tr}(F_t''\log F_t)d\mu
=-\int\operatorname{Tr}(F_t'\mathrm D\log_{F_t}[F_t'])d\mu.
$$
The trace-linear derivative term integrates to zero and the actual mean is fixed; the Frechet derivative is not replaced by left multiplication by $F_t^{-1}$. At infinity $F_t\to\tau$ uniformly with derivatives, so entropy and quality tend to zero. Integrating the two nonnegative dissipations separately gives (M.6.13cl.H2).

For the actual optimizer, (M.6.13ci.S6) and metric ordering give
$$
I_{\rm BKM}(F)-\frac43E(F)
\ge\frac43\mathcal Q_{B_F}(\sqrt F)\ge0.
\tag{M.6.13cl.H3}
$$
The last inequality follows from the full Hermitian mean-zero and constant Schur results of Theorems M.6.13ci and M.6.13cj. It holds on the complete source class, with the direct gap-three corner retained.

For a retained block-diagonal flag $F=\bigoplus_jp_jF_j$ with normalized branches, $H_{\rm mat},q,E,I_{\rm BKM}$ and $I_{\rm WY}$ are their $p_j$-weighted sums. This follows from block functional calculus, the supported Sylvester equation and cancellation of $\log p_j$ in the mean-subtracted entropy. Zero-weight branches may be omitted; no positive-weight flag or even-phase contribution is discarded.

**Proof. II. Weighted amplitude comparison and the separation modulus.** We first prove the assertion for any bounded positive finite-matrix symbol $F$, normalized by $\int\operatorname{Tr}F\,d\mu=1$, with actual mean $\tau=\int F\,d\mu$. The measure is normalized Haar measure and logarithms are natural. Work on the support of $\tau$.

We use a weighted comparison that does not square a Loewner inequality. If $H,G\ge0$, $\operatorname{Tr}H^2\le1$, $G\le KH$, and $X$ is a contraction, then
$$
\operatorname{Tr}G^2X^*X\le K^2\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}H^2X^*X}.
\tag{M.6.13cl.4}
$$
Indeed, write $G=H^{1/2}CH^{1/2}$ on its support, with $0\le C\le KI$. For $A=X^*X$, Schatten Hölder gives
$$
\|XG\|_2^2\le K^2\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}(HAHA)\operatorname{Tr}H^2}
 \le K^2\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}H^2A}.
$$
The last comparison follows from
$\operatorname{Tr}H^2A^2-\operatorname{Tr}HAHA=\frac12\|[H,A]\|_2^2\ge0$
and $A^2\le A$.

Suppose temporarily that $m\tau\le F_\theta\le M\tau$. Put $G_\theta=\sqrt{F_\theta}$ and $H=\int G_\theta\,d\mu$. Operator monotonicity of square root gives $G_\theta\le\sqrt{M/m}\,H$. Also
$\tau-H^2=\int(G_\theta-H)^2d\mu\ge0$, so $\operatorname{Tr}H^2\le1$. Thus (M.6.13cl.4) applies with $K^2=M/m$.

For any odd Hermitian contraction with forward blocks $a,b,c,e$, define
$$
T=\sum_{x\in\{a,b,c,e\}}(\|xH\|_2^2+\|Hx\|_2^2),\qquad
S=q_2(H)+\operatorname{Tr}H^2Z^2,\quad Z=bb^*+b^*b.
$$
We claim
$$
T\le150q_2(H)+25\sqrt S,\qquad S\ge T^2/30625.
\tag{M.6.13cl.5}
$$
To check every coefficient, set $r=aH-Hc$, $s=\{H,a+c\}$ and $B_w=\operatorname{Tr}H^2Z\le\sqrt S$. In an eigenbasis of $H$, solving
$r_{ij}=h_ja_{ij}-h_ic_{ij}$ and $s_{ij}=(h_i+h_j)(a_{ij}+c_{ij})$ gives
$$
\|aH\|_2^2+\|Ha\|_2^2+\|cH\|_2^2+\|Hc\|_2^2
\le4\|r\|_2^2+2\|s\|_2^2.
$$
The zero denominator case has zero left side. The coefficients $1/4$ and $1/32$ in the first two $q_2$ squares of Theorem M.6.13cj imply
$\|r\|_2^2\le4q_2$ and
$\|s\|_2^2\le64q_2+12B_w$.
The corner anticommutator coefficient $15/32$ gives

$$
\|eH\|_2^2+\|He\|_2^2\le32q_2/15.
$$

Hence $T\le(144+32/15)q_2+25B_w\le150q_2+25\sqrt S$. Since $T\le8$, this implies $T\le175\sqrt S$ both when $S\le1$ and when $S>1$, proving (M.6.13cl.5).

Now take the actual supported Sylvester optimizer $B=B_F$. With the weights $p=(1,3,3,1)/8$ and phase embedding $V_\theta$, its quality is exactly
$$
q(F)=\operatorname{Tr}R_FB_F^2
=\int\|B_FV_\theta G_\theta\|_2^2d\mu.
$$
There are two input blocks per odd row. Their two-term square bound, (M.6.13cl.4), and scalar Cauchy–Schwarz yield
$$
q(F)\le2K^2\sum_{i-j\ \mathrm{odd}}p_j
 \sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}H^2(B_F)_{ij}^*(B_F)_{ij}}
 \le2\sqrt2K^2\sqrt T,
$$
because the sum of these weights is $2$ and the unweighted activity sum is $T$. Therefore
$$
S\ge\frac{q(F)^4}{1960000K^8}.
\tag{M.6.13cl.6}
$$

Apply source heat $F_t=e^{t\partial_\theta^2}F$. The normalized circle kernel satisfies
$$
m(t)\le k_t(\theta)\le M(t),\quad
m(t)=\sqrt{\pi/t}\,e^{-\pi^2/(4t)},\quad
M(t)=1+\sqrt{\pi/t}.
$$
The lower estimate is the nearest term of the periodized Gaussian; the upper estimate follows from
$1+2\sum_{n\ge1}e^{-n^2t}\le1+\sqrt{\pi/t}$.
Hence $m(t)\tau\le F_t\le M(t)\tau$.
At every positive time the source is smooth and faithful on the actual mean support. Its actual optimizer is contractive. Centering the spin charge at $3/2$ gives $\|\delta B_t\|\le3$, so the exact source-heat identities imply
$$
-q_t'=2E_t\le18,\qquad q_t\ge q_0-18t.
\tag{M.6.13cl.7}
$$
For $q_0>0$, restrict to $t\in[q_0/72,q_0/36]$. Here $q_t\ge q_0/2$, $m(t)$ is increasing and $M(t)$ decreasing. The Schur bound and the actual-optimizer Hermitian Fisher identity give
$$
I_{\mathrm{BKM}}(F_t)-\frac43E_t
\ge\frac43\mathcal Q_{B_t}(\sqrt{F_t})
\ge\frac4{300000}S_t.
$$
Use (M.6.13cl.6), integrate on this interval, and use nonnegative defect dissipation at all other times. The exact entropy and quality heat identities yield
$$
H_{\mathrm{mat}}(F)-\frac23q(F)
\ge\frac4{300000}\frac{q_0}{72}
 \frac{(q_0/2)^4}{1960000}
 \left[\frac{m(q_0/72)}{M(q_0/72)}\right]^4
=g(q_0).
$$
For $q_0=0$, entropy convexity suffices. Singular initial symbols are included by starting the faithful heat identities at $s>0$ and taking $s\downarrow0$: heat preserves a fixed finite operator-norm bound, converges in $L^1$, and hence preserves the entropy limit by continuity of $x\log x$ on that bounded spectral interval. The mean is fixed; the supported compact variational formula makes $q$ continuous in its finite matrix pair $(R,D)$. At infinity both entropy and quality tend to zero. No dimension-uniform smallest eigenvalue is assumed.

By Theorem M.6.13ck, for integer reference spectra the exact orbit symbol has $H_{\mathrm{mat}}=\mathcal A_Q$ and $q(F)=q_Q$. For arbitrary real spectra, the integer-coset pinching of Theorem M.6.13ch leaves $q$ unchanged and decomposes the asymmetry into a nonnegative pinching cost plus the weighted branch asymmetries. Assemble all normalized coset orbit symbols as one block-diagonal symbol $\bigoplus_jp_jF_j$ after their harmless charge shifts. Its actual entropy and supported quality are precisely the weighted sums, so the symbol theorem applies to their total quality directly, without assuming convexity of $g$ or discarding a flag. This proves (M.6.13cl.2).

Finally, $m(q/72)$ increases and $M(q/72)$ decreases for $0<q\le1$, so $g$ increases. Combining this with the inequality $u\le q$ of Theorem M.6.13ch gives (M.6.13cl.3). The balanced two-charge comparison has $q=3t^2/4$ and
$A=[(1+t)\log(1+t)+(1-t)\log(1-t)]/2$, hence

$$
A-2q/3=4q^2/27+O(q^3);
$$

the new bound is much weaker and leaves the exact frontier open. $\square$

### M.6.13cm A uniform quadratic remainder above the complete spin-three-halves line

<a id="theorem-m613cm-complete-reference-quadratic-separation"></a>**Theorem M.6.13cm (Complete-Reference Quadratic Separation).** In the complete finite-reference contract of Theorems M.6.13ch and M.6.13ck, fix the normalized spin-$3/2$ target. Set $C=12192768000000000$. Every finite reference, including arbitrary real charges, degeneracies, mixed states, charged and neutral factors, retained flags and initial correlations, satisfies
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge\frac23q_Q(\sigma)+\frac{q_Q(\sigma)^2}{C}.
\tag{M.6.13cm.1}
$$
Consequently, every complete operational model in the domain $0\le u=1-\epsilon^2\le1$ satisfies
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge\frac23u+\frac{u^2}{C}.
\tag{M.6.13cm.2}
$$
Only the established inequality $u\le q_Q(\sigma)$ is used; state quality is not identified with worst-case all-input quality. The quadratic modulus strengthens Theorem M.6.13cl while preserving the exact weak coefficient $2/3$. The exact positive-error frontier, optimal quadratic coefficient and dimension optima remain open.

**Proof.** All circle integrals use normalized Haar measure and logarithms are natural. For a bounded positive finite-matrix symbol $F$ with $\int\operatorname{Tr}F=1$, use the actual mean $\tau=\int F$ and work on its support. Write $A=H_{\mathrm{mat}}(F)$, $q=q(F)$ and $E=E(F)$ in the notation of Theorem M.6.13ci. Let
$$
G_\theta=\sqrt{F_\theta},\qquad H=\int G_\theta\,d\mu,
\qquad V=\int\|G_\theta-H\|_2^2d\mu=1-\operatorname{Tr}H^2.
\tag{M.6.13cm.3}
$$
In particular $H\ge0$ and $0\le V\le1$.

**Entropy and amplitude variance.** Diagonalize $F_\theta$ with eigenvalues $f_i(\theta)$ and $\tau$ with eigenvalues $t_j$. The weights $f_i(\theta)|\langle i(\theta),j\rangle|^2d\mu$ form a probability measure. Their expectation of $\log(t_j/f_i)$ is $-A$. Jensen's inequality, followed by Hilbert–Schmidt Cauchy–Schwarz and $\operatorname{Tr}\tau=1$, gives
$$
e^{-A/2}\le\int\operatorname{Tr}\sqrt{F_\theta}\sqrt\tau\,d\mu
=\operatorname{Tr}H\sqrt\tau\le\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}H^2},
\qquad V\le1-e^{-A}\le A.
\tag{M.6.13cm.4}
$$
Zero weights are omitted. No pointwise trace-one assumption on $F_\theta$ is required.

**Constant-amplitude comparison.** Take the actual supported odd Hermitian contraction $B=B_F$. With $p=(1,3,3,1)/8$, $V_\theta=(\sqrt{p_i}e^{ii\theta})_{i=0}^3\otimes I$ and $\delta B=i[\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2,3)\otimes I,B]$, put
$$
q_c=\int\|BV_\theta H\|_2^2d\mu,
\qquad E_c=\int\|\delta B V_\theta H\|_2^2d\mu.
$$
Since $B^2$ and $(\delta B)^2$ are parity even, the corresponding integrals with $G_\theta$ in place of $H$ are $q$ and $E$. The map $V_\theta$ is an isometry. The $L^2$ triangle inequality, $\|B\|\le1$, and the centered-charge bound $\|\delta B\|\le3$ imply
$$
|\sqrt{q_c}-\sqrt q|\le\sqrt V,
\qquad \sqrt E\le\sqrt{E_c}+3\sqrt V.
\tag{M.6.13cm.5}
$$
For the constant amplitude, Fourier orthogonality gives
$$
q_c=\sum_{i,j}p_j\|B_{ij}H\|_2^2,
\qquad E_c=\sum_{i,j}(i-j)^2p_j\|B_{ij}H\|_2^2\le9q_c.
$$
Therefore
$$
\sqrt E\le3\sqrt q+6\sqrt V.
\tag{M.6.13cm.6}
$$
The comparison $E_c\le9q_c$ is only for the constant amplitude; no corresponding weighted commutator inequality for the original source is assumed.

**A quantitative Fisher gap near the line.** Suppose $A\le3q/4$. Equations (M.6.13cm.4)–(M.6.13cm.6) imply
$$
q_c\ge(1-\sqrt{3/4})^2q\ge q/64,
\qquad E\le(3+6\sqrt{3/4})^2q\le81q.
\tag{M.6.13cm.7}
$$
Here $\sqrt{3/4}<7/8$. Let $a=B_{01},b=B_{12},c=B_{23},e=B_{03}$ be the full forward blocks, including the unrestricted corner. Put
$$
T=\sum_{x\in\{a,b,c,e\}}(\|xH\|_2^2+\|Hx\|_2^2),
\qquad S=q_2(H)+\operatorname{Tr}H^2(bb^*+b^*b)^2,
$$
where $q_2$ is the full six-square form of Theorem M.6.13cj. The eight directional terms in $q_c$ have weights $p_j\le1$; reverse adjoints obey $\|x^*H\|_2=\|Hx\|_2$. Thus $q_c\le T$. The weighted activity estimate (M.6.13cl.5) gives $T^2\le30625S$, since $H\ge0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}H^2\le1$. Schur minimization over the mean-zero Hermitian amplitude, followed by the full bound (M.6.13cj.1), now yields
$$
\mathcal Q_B(G)\ge\langle H,\mathfrak F_BH\rangle
\ge\frac S{100000}
\ge\frac{q^2}{64^2\cdot30625\cdot100000}
=\frac{q^2}{12544000000000}.
\tag{M.6.13cm.8}
$$
This uses the real Hermitian form of Theorem M.6.13ci and its coercive mean-zero block, not an unrestricted complex-vector relaxation. No Loewner inequality is squared.

**A fixed source-heat interval.** First suppose $F$ is smooth and uniformly positive on $\operatorname{supp}\tau$, and let $F_t=e^{t\partial_\theta^2}F$. Write $D_t=A_t-2q_t/3$. The source-heat identities (M.6.13cl.H1)–(M.6.13cl.H3), metric ordering (M.6.13ci.S7), actual-optimizer identity (M.6.13ci.S6) and full Hermitian nonnegativity of Theorem M.6.13cj imply
$$
q_t'=-2E_t,\qquad
D_t'=-I_{\mathrm{BKM}}(F_t)+\frac43E_t
\le-\frac43\mathcal Q_{B_t}(\sqrt{F_t})\le0,
\qquad D_t\ge0.
\tag{M.6.13cm.9}
$$
The last inequality follows also by integrating to infinity, where $A_t,q_t\to0$.

If $q_0=0$, entropy nonnegativity suffices. If $q_0>0$ and $D_0>q_0/24$, then $q_0\le1$ and $C>24$ give the desired result. Otherwise $D_0\le q_0/24$. At every time with $q_t\ge q_0/2$, monotonicity of $D_t$ implies
$$
\frac{A_t}{q_t}=\frac23+\frac{D_t}{q_t}
\le\frac23+\frac{q_0/24}{q_0/2}=\frac34.
$$
Consequently (M.6.13cm.7) gives $q_t'\ge-162q_t$ throughout that region. There is no first crossing $q_{t_c}=q_0/2$ with $t_c\le T_*:=1/324$, because integration up to such a crossing would give

$$
q_{t_c}\ge q_0e^{-162t_c}\ge q_0e^{-1/2}>q_0/2.
$$

Thus $q_t\ge q_0/2$ on $[0,T_*]$. Integrating (M.6.13cm.8)–(M.6.13cm.9) on that interval proves
$$
D_0\ge D_0-D_{T_*}
\ge\frac43\frac1{324}\frac{q_0^2/4}{12544000000000}
=\frac{q_0^2}{12192768000000000}.
\tag{M.6.13cm.10}
$$
All constants are independent of coefficient dimension and charge width.

**Limits and complete-reference transfer.** For a bounded singular initial symbol, apply the proved inequality to $F_s=e^{s\partial_\theta^2}F$ for $s>0$. The positive circle heat kernel makes $F_s$ smooth and faithful on the actual mean support. As $s\downarrow0$, heat preserves a fixed finite operator-norm bound and converges in $L^1$; continuity of $x\log x$ on that bounded spectral interval gives convergence of the entropy. The mean is unchanged, and the supported compact variational formula gives convergence of $q$. No continuity of $E$ or Fisher information at a singular source is asserted.

For integer-charge references, the exact orbit symbol in Theorem M.6.13ck has $A=\mathcal A_Q$ and $q=q_Q$. For arbitrary real charges, use the integer-coset pinching and retained direct-sum construction of Theorems M.6.13ch and M.6.13cl: pinching leaves $q$ unchanged and adds a nonnegative asymmetry cost. Assemble all normalized coset orbit symbols as $\bigoplus_jw_jF_j$ after charge shifts. Its actual entropy and supported quality are the weighted branch sums, so the symbol theorem applies directly to their total quality. This proves (M.6.13cm.1) without removing a flag or requiring an eigenvalue lower bound uniform over references. Finally $x\mapsto2x/3+x^2/C$ increases on $[0,1]$, so $u\le q$ proves (M.6.13cm.2) on its stated domain.

**Comparison and scope.** With $g$ as in Theorem M.6.13cl, for $0<q\le1$,
$$
\frac{g(q)}{q^2/C}
=\frac{72q^3e^{-72\pi^2/q}}
 {(1+\sqrt{q/(72\pi)})^4}
\le72e^{-72\pi^2}<1.
$$
Ordinary binary entropy bounds with expansion $q/2+O(q^2)$, combined by taking a maximum with $2q/3$, do not supply a positive remainder near zero. The balanced two-charge comparison in Theorem M.6.13cl has $A-2q/3=4q^2/27+O(q^3)$; the coefficient here is not claimed optimal. $\square$

### M.6.13cn Quantitative neutral-ladder coercivity

<a id="theorem-m613cn-neutral-constant-schur-coercivity-with-coefficient-1100"></a>**Theorem M.6.13cn (Neutral Constant-Schur Coercivity with Coefficient $1/100$).**

**Source and domain.**

Use the normalized source, Hermitian/Jordan form and Fourier projections of Theorem M.6.13ci. Thus $L_B=-3\partial_\theta^2+\mathcal J_{W_B}$, $\mathcal J_W(X)=(WX+XW)/2$, $P$ projects onto constant Fourier modes, $Q=I-P$, $L_0=-3\partial_\theta^2$, and $R_0=(QL_0Q)^{-1}$. The form domain remains $H^1(S^1;\operatorname{Herm}_d)$, with ordinary coefficient trace and normalized Haar measure. The Schur operator is
$$
\mathfrak F_B=P L_B P-P L_B Q(Q L_B Q)^{-1}Q L_B P.
$$
All finite coefficient dimensions are allowed. The complete-reference, charge, degeneracy, correlation, retained-flag, pointer and all-input conventions of Theorems M.6.13ch–M.6.13ck remain unchanged. In particular $u\le q$; no new operational error equality is asserted.

**Part I. Neutral constant-Schur coercivity.**

Let $b$ be an arbitrary complex $d$-by-$d$ matrix, and let $B$ be the neutral ladder
$$
B_{01}=B_{23}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}b,\qquad B_{12}=b,\qquad B_{03}=0,
$$
with reverse adjoint blocks. If $\|B\|\le1$, then for every Hermitian constant $H$, with $Z=bb^*+b^*b$,
$$
\boxed{\quad
\langle H,\mathfrak F_BH\rangle
\ge\frac1{100}\left(\|[H,b]\|_{\rm HS}^2+\operatorname{Tr}H^2Z^2\right).
\quad}                                                    \tag{M.6.13cn.1}
$$
Consequently $\mathcal Q_B(G)\ge0$ on the full Hermitian $H^1$ domain. No normality, nilpotency, grading, rank, invertibility or activity-gap assumption is imposed on $b$ or $H$.

**Proof: the complete mean-zero inverse.** The neutral potential is
$$
W_b(\theta)=-\frac32(bz+b^*z^{-1})+\frac34Z
 +\frac98(b^2z^2+(b^*)^2z^{-2}),\qquad z=e^{i\theta}.
\tag{M.6.13cn.2}
$$
Compression gives $\|b\|\le1$. Since $0\le B^2\le I$, its $02$ block has norm at most $1/2$. This block equals $(\sqrt3/2)b^2$, so $\|b^2\|\le1/\sqrt3$. The $11$ and $22$ diagonal compressions give
$$
bb^*+\tfrac34b^*b\le I,\qquad b^*b+\tfrac34bb^*\le I,
\qquad Z\le\tfrac87I.
$$
The nonconstant potential coefficients therefore have norms at most $c_1=3/2$ and $c_2=2/3$, while its constant coefficient is positive. Jordan multiplication has HS operator norm at most the coefficient norm.

For nonzero Fourier indices, preconditioning by $\sqrt3|n|$ gives the absolute comparison kernel $c_{|n-m|}/(3|nm|)$, zero unless $|n-m|=1,2$. Use Schur weights $w_n=a_n/|n|$, with $a_n=1$ for odd $n$ and $a_n=4/3$ for nonzero even $n$. Its weighted row sums at $n=1,2,3,4$ are
$$
\frac{67}{162},\quad\frac{31}{72},\quad\frac{791}{1800},\quad\frac{959}{8100},
$$
all below $4/9$. Reflection handles negative indices. For $n\ge5$ the row sum is bounded by
$$
\frac49\left(\frac{3/2}{16}+\frac{3/2}{36}+\frac{2/3}{9}+\frac{2/3}{49}\right)
=\frac{9445}{95256}<\frac1{10}.
$$
Dropping only the positive constant coefficient, the weighted Schur inequality and $H^1$ density yield
$$
A:=QL_BQ\ge\frac59QL_0Q,\qquad A^{-1}\le\frac95R_0.
\tag{M.6.13cn.3}
$$
This covers the complete Fourier tail. Also $W_0=(3/4)Z\le6I/7$ gives the optional upper bound $A\le(109/63)QL_0Q$; this upper bound is not needed for (M.6.13cn.1).

**Proof: a finite exact lower polynomial.** For the given $H$, choose the Hermitian Fourier polynomial
$$
G_0=H,\qquad G_1=\frac{bH+Hb}{4},\qquad
G_2=\frac{-b^2H+bHb-Hb^2}{32},\qquad G_{-n}=G_n^*.
\tag{M.6.13cn.4}
$$
Unlisted coefficients vanish. Write $W_k$ for the coefficients in (M.6.13cn.2), and for $n\ne0$ put
$$
E_n=3n^2G_n+\sum_{k=-2}^{2}\mathcal J_{W_k}(G_{n-k}).
$$
The full residual $E=QL_BG$ is supported on $0<|n|\le4$. Define the real ordered tracial polynomial
$$
\begin{split}
\mathcal T(b,H)={}&3\sum_n n^2\operatorname{Tr}G_n^*G_n
 +\sum_{n,m}\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(G_n^*\mathcal J_{W_{n-m}}(G_m)\bigr)\\
&-\frac95\sum_{n\ne0}\frac{\operatorname{Tr}E_n^*E_n}{3n^2}.
\end{split}                                               \tag{M.6.13cn.5}
$$
Its degree in $b,b^*$ is at most eight, and every word has exactly two $H$'s. Exact Schur completion and (M.6.13cn.3) give
$$
\langle H,\mathfrak F_BH\rangle
=\mathcal Q_B(G)-\langle E,A^{-1}E\rangle
\ge\mathcal T(b,H).                                      \tag{M.6.13cn.6}
$$
Thus a finite polynomial lower bound controls the full inverse; no finite-section positivity assumption is used.

**Proof: rational sum-of-squares certificate.** Grouping even and odd spin indices gives $B=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&C\\ C^*&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, where
$$
C=\begin{pmatrix}(\sqrt3/2)b&0\\b^*&(\sqrt3/2)b\end{pmatrix}.
$$
Congruences of $I-CC^*$ and $I-C^*C$ give the positive rational localizers
$$
\Lambda_1=\begin{pmatrix}\frac43I-bb^*&-b^2\\-(b^*)^2&I-b^*b-\frac34bb^*\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\Lambda_2=\begin{pmatrix}I-bb^*-\frac34b^*b&-b^2\\-(b^*)^2&\frac43I-b^*b\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13cn.7}
$$
Here the congruence factors are respectively $\operatorname{diag}(2I/\sqrt3,I)$ and $\operatorname{diag}(I,2I/\sqrt3)$.

For $k\ge2$, let $\mathcal V_k$ contain every word with $k$ letters independently chosen from $b,b^*$ and one $H$ inserted in every position. Set $\mathcal V_1=(bH-Hb,b^*H-Hb^*)$. Let
$$
v_0=\mathcal V_1\cup\mathcal V_3,\quad v_1=\mathcal V_2\cup\mathcal V_4,
\qquad v'_0=v_0,\quad v'_1=\mathcal V_2.
$$
The complete rational data below contain the exact ordered bases, all six rational symmetric Gram matrices of sizes $34,92,68,24,68,24$, and a rational positive-definiteness witness for each matrix.
They satisfy the exact real-trace identity
$$
\begin{split}
\mathcal T(b,H)-\frac{\|[H,b]\|_{\rm HS}^2+\operatorname{Tr}H^2Z^2}{100}
={}&\sum_{s=0}^{1}\sum_{i,j}(Q_s)_{ij}\operatorname{Tr}(v_{s,i}^*v_{s,j})\\
&+\sum_{r=1}^{2}\sum_{s=0}^{1}\sum_{a,i,c,j}
(Q_{r,s})_{(a,i),(c,j)}
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl((v'_{s,i})^*(\Lambda_r)_{ac}v'_{s,j}\bigr).
\end{split}                                               \tag{M.6.13cn.8}
$$
For each Gram matrix $Q$ the data also specify a rational matrix $R$. Exact integer arithmetic verifies strict diagonal dominance of the symmetric residual $Q-RR^{\mathsf T}$ with positive diagonal. Every row margin is positive, so all six Grams are positive definite. This is an exact PSD proof, not a numerical eigenvalue test.

The finite identity has the following exact interpretation. Code $b,b^*,H$ by $0,1,2$. An adjoint reverses a word, interchanges $0,1$ and fixes $2$. Reduce a real-trace word to the lexicographically least cyclic rotation of the word or of its adjoint. Expanding (M.6.13cn.2), (M.6.13cn.4) and all eight residual modes in (M.6.13cn.5), then subtracting the displayed coercive polynomial divided by $100$, gives exactly $129$ nonzero real cyclic coefficients. Expanding the six Gram expressions in (M.6.13cn.8) gives the same coefficients. No multiplication order of $b,b^*$ is changed.

Every basis polynomial and localizer entry is printed as an ordered noncommutative polynomial. If a local block has $k$ basis vectors, matrix index $ak+i$ means localizer component $a=0,1$ and basis index $0\le i<k$; free blocks have only the basis index. Each matrix table states its denominator and integer numerators, defining the exact Gram $Q$ or rational factor $R$. There are $20,020$ entries in the six Gram matrices and the same number in their factors. For each block form the exact symmetric matrix $Q-RR^{\mathsf T}$. All its strict diagonal-dominance row margins are positive; the minimum over all six blocks is
$$
\frac{1562480313427853}{15625000000000000000000}>0.
$$
Thus all six $Q$ are positive definite and every term on the right of (M.6.13cn.8) is nonnegative under (M.6.13cn.7). Equations (M.6.13cn.6)–(M.6.13cn.8) prove (M.6.13cn.1). Full mean-zero coercivity and exact Schur completion give positivity on the complete Hermitian $H^1$ domain. $\square$

**Part II. Actual optimizers and Gibbs stationary points.**

Let $F$ be smooth, normalized and uniformly positive, and suppose its actual Sylvester optimizer $B_F$ is a neutral contraction as in Part I. With $H_0=\int\sqrt F\,d\mu$ and $Z=bb^*+b^*b$,
$$
\frac34I_{\rm WY}(F)-E(F)
\ge\frac1{100}\left(\|[H_0,b]\|_{\rm HS}^2+\operatorname{Tr}H_0^2Z^2\right).
\tag{M.6.13cn.9}
$$
The right side is strictly positive when $b\ne0$. No faithful Gibbs/Sylvester stationary point at $c=2/3$ has a nonzero neutral optimizer.

**Proof.** Theorem M.6.13ci, Equation (M.6.13ci.S6), identifies the left side with $\mathcal Q_{B_F}(\sqrt F)$. Schur completion bounds it below by $\langle H_0,\mathfrak F_{B_F}H_0\rangle$, to which Part I applies. Uniform positivity makes $H_0$ positive definite, so $\operatorname{Tr}H_0^2Z^2=\|ZH_0\|_{\rm HS}^2>0$ for nonzero $b$. At a Gibbs/Sylvester point with coefficient $c=2/3$, the derivative identity and actual-optimizer normal equation of Theorem M.6.13ci give $I_{\rm BKM}=2cE=4E/3$, whereas its metric ordering gives $I_{\rm WY}\le I_{\rm BKM}$. These contradict the strict gap. The Ward identity does not require the fixed Gibbs parameter to equal the actual mean. $\square$

**Scope.** The bound includes arbitrary nonnormal neutral ladders and inactive directions, with explicit coefficient $1/100$. Part II is a pointwise Fisher statement and stationary exclusion. Neutrality of the actual optimizer has not been shown to be heat invariant, so this neutral theorem alone does not give unrestricted entropy integration. Theorems M.6.13cj–M.6.13ck supply the separate general full-corner results. Their operational distinction $u\le q$, complete source inventories and attainment scopes remain in force.

**Complete rational neutral certificate.**

The indexed polynomial and rational matrix tables cited in this section specify every input of the tracial identity (M.6.13cn.8). All indices start at zero. Products in each basis polynomial retain their printed order. A scalar constant $c$ in an operator polynomial means $cI$. The target polynomial is defined by the displayed finite potential, corrector and residual formulas above, so its coefficients require no additional input. A matrix row lists exact rational numerators, with its denominator stated explicitly.

The localizer used by the tables with index $r=1$ is
$$
\Lambda^{\mathrm{tab}}_1=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{4}{3}-b\,b^*&-b\,b\\-b^*\,b^*&1-\frac{3}{4}b\,b^*-b^*\,b\end{pmatrix}.
$$

The localizer used by the tables with index $r=2$ is
$$
\Lambda^{\mathrm{tab}}_2=\begin{pmatrix}1-b\,b^*-\frac{3}{4}b^*\,b&-b\,b\\-b^*\,b^*&\frac{4}{3}-b^*\,b\end{pmatrix}.
$$

### M.6.13co Strict neutral discriminator-radial Gibbs monotonicity

<a id="theorem-m613co-strict-neutral-gibbs-ray-monotonicity"></a>**Theorem M.6.13co (Strict Neutral Gibbs-Ray Monotonicity).**

Fix a faithful coefficient density $\tau$, a nonzero neutral ladder $B_0$ of Theorem M.6.13cn, and $0<c\le2/3$. For $B_t=tB_0$ on any interval where $\|B_t\|\le1$, define
$$
Z_c(t)=\int\operatorname{Tr}\exp\bigl(\log\tau+cK_{B_t}(\theta)\bigr)d\mu,
\qquad F_t(\theta)=\frac{\exp(\log\tau+cK_{B_t}(\theta))}{Z_c(t)}.
$$
Then $Z_c(0)=1$ and $\frac{d}{dt}\log Z_c(t)<0$ for every $t>0$ in that interval. In particular every nonzero contractive neutral matrix Gibbs test has $Z_c<1$, in every finite coefficient dimension and for every faithful $\tau$.

No assertion that $B_t$ is the actual Sylvester optimizer of $F_t$ is required, and $\tau$ need not equal the actual mean of $F_t$.

**Proof.** To distinguish a test discriminator from an actual optimizer, write
$$
\mathcal E_B(F)=\int\operatorname{Tr}(F M_B)d\mu
=\operatorname{Tr}R_F(\delta B)^2.
$$
For an arbitrary Gibbs test $B$, differentiating its matrix logarithm and integrating by parts gives
$$
\int\operatorname{Tr}(F K_B'')d\mu=-\frac1c I_{\rm BKM}(F).
$$
This calculation uses only $(\log F)'=cK_B'$, not a Sylvester equation. The canonical W12 form consequently obeys
$$
\mathcal Q_B(\sqrt F)=\frac34I_{\rm WY}(F)-\frac1cI_{\rm BKM}(F)+\mathcal E_B(F).
\tag{M.6.13co.1}
$$
Every neutral ladder has only spin gaps one, hence $\delta^2B=-B$. The identity $\mathscr D_B[\delta^2B]=K_B''+2M_B$ from Theorem M.6.13ci therefore gives
$$
t\frac{d}{dt}\log Z_c(t)
=c\int\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_t \mathscr D_{B_t}[B_t]\bigr)d\mu
=I_{\rm BKM}(F_t)-2c\mathcal E_{B_t}(F_t).
$$
Combining this with (M.6.13co.1) yields the exact radial identity
$$
\boxed{\quad
t\frac{d}{dt}\log Z_c(t)
=\frac{3c}{2}I_{\rm WY}(F_t)-I_{\rm BKM}(F_t)
 -2c\mathcal Q_{B_t}(\sqrt{F_t}).
\quad}                                                   \tag{M.6.13co.2}
$$
The metric ordering (M.6.13ci.S7) and $3c/2\le1$ make the first two terms nonpositive. Put $H_t=\int\sqrt{F_t}\,d\mu$. Faithfulness on the compact circle makes $H_t$ positive definite. If the neutral coefficient of $B_t$ is $b_t\ne0$, Theorem M.6.13cn and exact Schur completion give
$$
\mathcal Q_{B_t}(\sqrt{F_t})\ge\frac1{100}
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl[H_t^2(b_tb_t^*+b_t^*b_t)^2\bigr]>0.
$$
Thus (M.6.13co.2) is strictly negative at every positive $t$. Smoothness and continuity at $t=0$, together with $\operatorname{Tr}\tau=1$, give the asserted strict partition inequality. $\square$

This proves strict discriminator-radial monotonicity on the complete neutral matrix family without assuming that the test discriminator is an actual optimizer or that $\tau$ equals the actual mean. The radial identity itself applies to any adjacent-only discriminator; using it on a larger class requires positivity of the corresponding quadratic form on that class. Theorems M.6.13cj–M.6.13ck supply the separate general full-corner statements. Complete operational resources and $u\le q$ retain their declared meanings.

### M.6.13cp Finite-dimensional stationary-witness reduction

<a id="theorem-m613cp-attained-faithful-stationary-witness-normal-form"></a>**Theorem M.6.13cp (Attained Faithful Stationary-Witness Normal Form).** Fix $c>0$ and a finite coefficient dimension $d$. Use $V_\theta$, $R_F,D_F$, the odd Hermitian discriminator and its supported Sylvester optimizer $S(F)$ from Theorem M.6.13ci. For a faithful coefficient density $\tau$ define
$$
K_B(\theta)=V_\theta^*(2B-B^2)V_\theta,\qquad
Z_c(B,\tau)=\int\operatorname{Tr}\exp(\log\tau+cK_B(\theta))\,d\mu,
\qquad F_{B,\tau}=\frac{\exp(\log\tau+cK_B)}{Z_c(B,\tau)}.
\tag{M.6.13cp.1}
$$
Here $d\mu=d\theta/(2\pi)$; $F$ is normalized by its integrated trace. If a finite $d$-dimensional test has $Z_c(B,\tau)>1$, there are $1\le r\le d$, a faithful density $\tau$ on $\mathbb C^r$, and an odd Hermitian strict contraction $B$ on $\mathbb C^4\otimes\mathbb C^r$ such that
$$
Z_c(B,\tau)>1,\qquad B=S(F_{B,\tau}),\qquad
\tau=\int F_{B,\tau}\,d\mu.
\tag{M.6.13cp.2}
$$
This test is a local maximum in every odd Hermitian $B$ direction and every trace-zero Hermitian $\tau$ direction within their faithful domains. The reduction is performed separately for each original finite $d$. Its support compression changes the mathematical coefficient test; it does not remove degrees of freedom from a specified physical apparatus.

**Part I. Fixed-density optimizer improvement and interior margin.**

For faithful $\tau$ and any odd Hermitian $B$, put $F=F_{B,\tau}$ and $C=S(F)$. Then
$$
\log Z_c(C,\tau)\ge\log Z_c(B,\tau)
+c\operatorname{Tr}R_F(B-C)^2.
\tag{M.6.13cp.3}
$$
To verify the Gibbs step directly, let $F_C=F_{C,\tau}$. Integrated Klein nonnegativity and the normalization of both symbols give
$$
\int\operatorname{Tr}F(\log F-\log F_C)\,d\mu\ge0.
$$
Subtracting the two Gibbs logarithms expresses this $\int$ as
$\log Z_c(C,\tau)-\log Z_c(B,\tau)
-c\int\operatorname{Tr}F(K_C-K_B)\,d\mu$.
The parity decomposition gives

$$
\int\operatorname{Tr}FK_B=2\operatorname{Tr}D_FB-\operatorname{Tr}R_FB^2.
$$

The exact variational square (M.6.13ci.S4) therefore proves (M.6.13cp.3).
For this smooth uniformly positive $F$, Theorem M.6.13ci makes $C$ an odd strict contraction, and $R_F$ is faithful. The added term vanishes exactly when $B=C$.

Thus, for fixed faithful $\tau$ and fixed $d$, the maximum over the compact closed ball of odd Hermitian contractions exists, equals the supremum over all odd Hermitian $B$, and each maximizing discriminator is its actual Sylvester optimizer and lies in the interior of the contraction ball.

There is also an explicit margin for a contractive input test. The scalar polynomial $2x-x^2$ on $[-1,1]$ gives $-3I\le K_B\le I$. Eigenvalue $\min$-$\max$, followed by scalar exponentiation, gives
$$
\lambda_{\min}\bigl(e^{\log\tau+cK_B}\bigr)
\ge\lambda_{\min}(\tau)e^{-3c},\qquad
\lambda_{\max}\bigl(e^{\log\tau+cK_B}\bigr)
\le\lambda_{\max}(\tau)e^c.
$$
Consequently, if $mI\le F_\theta\le MI$, one can take

$$
m/M\ge\kappa(\tau)^{-1}e^{-4c},
$$

where

$$
\kappa(\tau)=\lambda_{\max}(\tau)/\lambda_{\min}(\tau).
$$

Since $\Omega_F\ge m\operatorname{diag}(p)\otimes I$ and
$R_F\le M\operatorname{diag}(p)\otimes I$, both
$R_F\pm D_F\ge(m/M)R_F$.
Positivity of the inverse Sylvester map then yields
$$
\|S(F)\|\le1-\kappa(\tau)^{-1}e^{-4c}.
\tag{M.6.13cp.4}
$$
This argument uses scalar eigenvalue bounds, not operator monotonicity of the exponential. The margin belongs to the fixed faithful density in the display.

**Part II. Continuous extension to density supports.**

For a possibly singular density $\tau$, let $P=\operatorname{supp}\tau$ and set
$$
\overline Z_c(B,\tau)
=\int\operatorname{Tr}_{P}
\exp\bigl(\log(\tau|_P)+cP K_B(\theta)P\bigr)\,d\mu.
\tag{M.6.13cp.5}
$$
This is the boundary extension of the faithful partition. The logarithm is taken only on the positive support.

**Joint continuity, including varying supports.** Suppose $B_n\to B$ in the fixed-dimensional contraction ball and $\tau_n\to\tau$ in the full density simplex. Let $r=\operatorname{rank}\tau\ge1$. The top-$r$ spectral projection $P_n$ of $\tau_n$ converges to $P$, because the positive spectrum of $\tau$ is separated from zero. Coefficient unitaries $U_n\to I$ carry $P$ onto $P_n$. Conjugating coefficient matrices by $U_n$ preserves the partition and aligns these blocks. On $P$, $\log\tau_n$ converges to $\log(\tau|_P)$, while the operator norm of the remaining density block tends to zero.

On $\operatorname{supp}\tau_n$, write the aligned logarithmic Gibbs exponent as
$$
H_n(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}A_n(\theta)&C_n(\theta)\\ C_n(\theta)^*&D_n(\theta)\end{pmatrix}.
$$
Uniformly in $\theta$, $A_n$ converges to $\log(\tau|_P)+cPK_BP$,
$\|C_n\|\le k$ for a fixed finite $k$, and
$D_n\le(-L_n+M)I$ with $L_n\to\infty$.
Absent zero-eigenvalue directions are omitted; the lower block has dimension at most $d-r$.
For every fixed $\eta>0$, the block Young inequalities give
$$
\operatorname{diag}(A_n-\eta I,D_n-k^2I/\eta)
\le H_n\le
\operatorname{diag}(A_n+\eta I,D_n+k^2I/\eta).
$$
Trace exponential is monotone in Hermitian order by eigenvalue $\min$-$\max$. Hence
$$
e^{-\eta}\operatorname{Tr}e^{A_n}
\le\operatorname{Tr}e^{H_n}
\le e^\eta\operatorname{Tr}e^{A_n}
+(d-r)e^{-L_n+M+k^2/\eta}.
$$
These bounds are uniform on the circle. Integrating, first taking $n\to\infty$ and then $\eta\downarrow0$, proves joint continuity of $\overline Z_c$ on the fixed-dimensional compact product of the contraction ball and full density simplex. It also proves its unique faithful-limit interpretation.

**Support compression.** Put $\widetilde P=I_4\otimes P$,
$C=\widetilde P B\widetilde P$ on the reduced coefficient space and
$Y=\widetilde P B(I-\widetilde P)$. The compression is odd Hermitian and contractive, and
$$
PK_B(\theta)P=K_C(\theta)-V_{\theta,P}^*YY^*V_{\theta,P}\le K_C(\theta),
\qquad
\overline Z_c(B,\tau)\le Z_c(C,\tau|_P).
\tag{M.6.13cp.6}
$$
The spin charge $\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2,3)$ and all four binomial weights are retained. Only the coefficient support changes.
Conversely, embed a faithful $r$-dimensional test as $B=C\oplus0$ and
$\tau_\varepsilon=(1-\varepsilon)\tau\oplus\varepsilon\omega$ with faithful $\omega$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$. Direct sums give
$$
Z_c(B,\tau_\varepsilon)=(1-\varepsilon)Z_c(C,\tau)+\varepsilon.
$$
Every strict violation therefore survives faithful extension to the larger coefficient space.

**Part III. Attainment, self-consistency and local maximality.**

Start with a strict finite-dimensional violation and, if necessary, apply Part I to make its discriminator contractive. Maximize the continuous boundary extension (M.6.13cp.5) on the compact fixed-$d$ product. Its maximum exceeds one. At a maximizing pair, compress to the support of its density using (M.6.13cp.6). The value cannot decrease. Embedding this reduced test back into dimension $d$ with zero density on the complement is allowed by the supported extension, so its value is exactly the same maximum. It is a global maximizer among $r$-dimensional tests and its density is faithful.

Apply (M.6.13cp.3) in this reduced space. A strict increase would contradict maximality, so $B=S(F)$. Theorem M.6.13ci makes $B$ a strict contraction, allowing every sufficiently small odd Hermitian variation. Faithfulness allows every sufficiently small trace-zero Hermitian variation of $\tau$.

Let $\tau_F=\int F\,d\mu$. For a Hermitian density direction $T$,
$$
D_\tau\log Z_c[T]
=\operatorname{Tr}\tau_F\,\mathrm D\log_\tau[T]
=\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\mathrm D\log_\tau[\tau_F]\bigr)T.
$$
The resolvent derivative (M.6.13ci.S3) is trace-self-adjoint and invertible on the faithful Hermitian space. Vanishing on every trace-zero $T$ implies

$$
\mathrm D\log_\tau[\tau_F]=\lambda I.
$$

Since $\mathrm D\log_\tau[\tau]=I$, invertibility gives

$$
\tau_F=\lambda\tau.
$$

Both densities have trace one, hence $\lambda=1$.
This proves (M.6.13cp.2) and the stated local maximality.

**Part IV. Necessary discriminator stability.**

For an odd Hermitian direction $Y$, write
$\mathscr D_B[Y](\theta)=V_\theta^*(2Y-BY-YB)V_\theta$ as in Theorem M.6.13ci. At the maximizing test its $F$-mean vanishes by the Sylvester normal equation. For a Hermitian matrix function $A$ define
$$
\Omega_F(A,A)=\int\!\int_0^1
\operatorname{Tr}(F_\theta^s A_\theta F_\theta^{1-s}A_\theta)\,ds\,d\mu.
$$
Twice differentiating the finite matrix exponential and the scalar normalization gives
$$
D_B^2\log Z_c[Y,Y]
=c^2\Omega_F(\mathscr D_B[Y],\mathscr D_B[Y])
-2c\operatorname{Tr}R_FY^2\le0.
$$
Here the usual square of the first derivative is zero at the stationary test, and $Y^2$ is parity even, so its $\Omega_F$-state expectation equals its $R_F$ expectation. Therefore every violating witness may be chosen to satisfy
$$
\Omega_F(\mathscr D_B[Y],\mathscr D_B[Y])
\le\frac2c\operatorname{Tr}R_FY^2
\quad\hbox{for every odd Hermitian }Y.
\tag{M.6.13cp.7}
$$
This is a necessary local-maximum condition at the attained witness. At $c=2/3$ its coefficient is three; Theorem M.6.13ck already supplies the separate full-class endpoint result. The present reduction applies to the variational tests for arbitrary $c>0$ at each fixed finite starting dimension. It supplies neither attainment over all dimensions nor a uniform rank or eigenvalue bound across the test family. $\square$

### M.6.13cq High-state-quality entropy boundary for fixed-spin extremal-pair discrimination

<a id="theorem-m613cq-fixed-spin-discriminator-entropy-boundary"></a>**Theorem M.6.13cq (Fixed-Spin Discriminator Entropy Boundary).** Fix an integer $r=2J\ge2$, system charge $Q_S=\operatorname{diag}(0,\ldots,r)$, and the two normalized extremal spin vectors

$$
v_\pm=\sum_{i=0}^r(\pm1)^i\sqrt{\binom ri/2^r}\,|i\rangle.
\tag{M.6.13cq.1}
$$

Allow every finite reference Hilbert space, every Hermitian reference charge $Q$ with arbitrary real spectrum, and every density matrix $\sigma$. Every charged or neutral factor, degeneracy, initial correlation and retained flag is included in this complete reference. Write $\mathcal G_Q$ for full charge pinching and use natural-$\log$ asymmetry $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)=D(\sigma\Vert\mathcal G_Q\sigma)$. Define

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Omega_\pm&=\mathcal G_{Q_S+Q}(|v_\pm\rangle\langle v_\pm|\otimes\sigma),\\
R&=(\Omega_++\Omega_-)/2,\qquad D=(\Omega_+-\Omega_-)/2,\\
q_{r,Q}(\sigma)&=\sup_{B=B^*,\,[B,Q_S+Q]=0}
\{2\operatorname{Tr}(DB)-\operatorname{Tr}(RB^2)\},\\
F_r^=(q)&=\inf_{q_{r,Q}(\sigma)=q}\mathcal A_Q(\sigma),\qquad
F_r^\ge(q)=\inf_{q_{r,Q}(\sigma)\ge q}\mathcal A_Q(\sigma).
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13cq.2}
$$

Both infima range over the entire finite reference class just stated; an empty infimum is $+\infty$. For $0\le q<1$ they coincide and are finite. Their common value satisfies

$$
\boxed{\quad F_r(q)=\frac1{2r}\log\frac1{1-q}+O_r(1),
\qquad
\lim_{q\uparrow1}\frac{F_r(q)}{\log(1/(1-q))}=\frac1{2r}=\frac1{4J}.\quad}
\tag{M.6.13cq.3}
$$

More explicitly, every finite reference obeys $q_{r,Q}(\sigma)<1$ and

$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge
\frac1{2r}\log\frac1{1-q_{r,Q}(\sigma)}-\log\frac r{r-1}.
\tag{M.6.13cq.4}
$$

Put $c_r=\binom{2r}{r}/4^r$ and $C_r=2(2r)^{2r}\pi^{2r}/c_r$. For every integer $N\ge r$ satisfying $C_r/(N+1)^{2r}\le1-q$, there is a finite exactly tuned state-quality witness of cost at most $\log N$. At $q=1$ both infima are $+\infty$.

For $r=3$, (M.6.13cq.2) is precisely the spin-$3/2$ discriminator of Theorem M.6.13ch. Write $F_{\mathrm{disc}}=F_3$. In particular

$$
F_{\mathrm{disc}}(q)=\frac16\log\frac1{1-q}+O(1),\qquad
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge\frac16\log\frac1{1-q_Q(\sigma)}-\log\frac32.
\tag{M.6.13cq.5}
$$

This is a state-discrimination endpoint. It does not identify $q$ with operational all-input quality $u$; for the original spin-$3/2$ measurement problem only the established relation $u\le q$ is used elsewhere. The distinction concerns the complete input-independent reference, with every retained factor counted.

*Proof.*

**Supported discriminator and covariance.** The following supported Sylvester construction applies to this pair. Indeed $-R\preceq D\preceq R$. On $E=\operatorname{supp}R$ set

$$
B=2\int_0^\infty e^{-tR}De^{-tR}\,dt,
\qquad RB+BR=2D,
\tag{M.6.13cq.6}
$$

and set $B=0$ on $E^\perp$. The positive $\int$ map sends $R$ to $I_E$, so $B$ is a Hermitian contraction. It commutes with total charge. Completing the quadratic form gives

$$
q:=q_{r,Q}(\sigma)=\operatorname{Tr}(DB)=\operatorname{Tr}(RB^2)\in[0,1].
\tag{M.6.13cq.7}
$$

Put $\delta=1-q$ and

$$
e_\pm=\operatorname{Tr}\big[(B\mp I)^2(|v_\pm\rangle\langle v_\pm|\otimes\sigma)\big].
\qquad \frac{e_++e_-}{2}=\delta.
\tag{M.6.13cq.8}
$$

The equality follows by replacing the untwirled states by $\Omega_\pm$, using invariance of $B$ and $B^2$, and then (M.6.13cq.7).

Let $U_S(\theta)=e^{i\theta Q_S}$ and $\sigma_\theta=e^{i\theta Q}\sigma e^{-i\theta Q}$. Choose purifications $\xi,\xi_\theta$ of $\sigma,\sigma_\theta$ whose overlap has modulus
$F_{\mathrm{root}}(\sigma,\sigma_\theta)=\|\sqrt\sigma\sqrt{\sigma_\theta}\|_1$; this is the standard fidelity purification theorem. The purification is a mathematical proof device, not an omitted physical resource. For
$a=v_+\otimes\xi$ and $b=U_S(\theta)v_-\otimes\xi_\theta$, their reduced states and $[B,Q_S+Q]=0$ imply
$\|(I-B)a\|^2=e_+$ and $\|(I+B)b\|^2=e_-$. Hermiticity gives

$$
2\langle a,b\rangle
=\langle(I-B)a,b\rangle+\langle a,(I+B)b\rangle,
\qquad
|\langle a,b\rangle|\le\frac{\sqrt{e_+}+\sqrt{e_-}}2\le\sqrt\delta.
\tag{M.6.13cq.9}
$$

The binomial theorem gives $\langle v_+,U_S(\theta)v_-\rangle=(1-e^{i\theta})^r/2^r$. Consequently

$$
F_{\mathrm{root}}(\sigma,\sigma_\theta)|\sin(\theta/2)|^r\le\sqrt\delta.
\tag{M.6.13cq.10}
$$

No pointer dilation is needed for this inequality.

**Entropy from the complete real-charge orbit.** Set $X=\sqrt\sigma$ and
$a(\theta)=\operatorname{Tr}[Xe^{i\theta Q}Xe^{-i\theta Q}]$. This quantity is nonnegative and at most $F_{\mathrm{root}}(\sigma,\sigma_\theta)$. Termwise Cesàro averaging in a charge eigenbasis gives, for every finite real spectrum including arbitrary degeneracies,

$$
\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac1T\int_0^T a(\theta)\,d\theta
=\operatorname{Tr}[(\mathcal G_QX)^2]=:c.
\tag{M.6.13cq.11}
$$

An off-charge entry has a nonzero real frequency and hence zero Cesàro mean. No periodicity of the reference orbit is assumed. The scalar upper envelope in (M.6.13cq.10) is $2\pi$-periodic. Using $\sin(\theta/2)\ge\theta/\pi$ on $[0,\pi]$ and writing $a_0=\delta^{1/(2r)}$ yields

$$
\begin{aligned}
c&\le\frac1\pi\int_0^\pi
\min\{1,\sqrt\delta/\sin^r(\theta/2)\}\,d\theta\\
&\le\int_0^1\min\{1,(a_0/x)^r\}\,dx
=\frac r{r-1}a_0-\frac{a_0^r}{r-1}
\le\frac r{r-1}\delta^{1/(2r)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13cq.12}
$$

The zero-deficit case follows by continuity of the $\int$.

For completeness, the Petz-$1/2$ inequality needed here has a direct finite spectral proof. Put $\tau=\mathcal G_Q\sigma$. Diagonalize $\sigma$ and $\tau$ with eigenvalues $s_i,t_j$ and eigenvectors $i,j$. The weights $s_i|\langle i|j\rangle|^2$ sum to one. Their expectation of $\log(t_j/s_i)$ is $-D(\sigma\Vert\tau)$, so Jensen gives

$$
\operatorname{Tr}\sqrt\sigma\sqrt\tau\ge e^{-D(\sigma\Vert\tau)/2}.
$$

Zero weights are omitted; $\operatorname{supp}\sigma\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\tau$ handles singular states. Charge invariance of $\sqrt\tau$ and Hilbert–Schmidt Cauchy–Schwarz give

$$
\operatorname{Tr}\sqrt\sigma\sqrt\tau
=\operatorname{Tr}[(\mathcal G_Q\sqrt\sigma)\sqrt\tau]\le\sqrt c,
\qquad
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge-\log c.
\tag{M.6.13cq.13}
$$

Equations (M.6.13cq.12)–(M.6.13cq.13) prove (M.6.13cq.4). If $\delta=0$, they force $c=0$, impossible because the positive matrix $\mathcal G_Q\sqrt\sigma$ has nonzero trace. This proves finite $q=1$ impossibility without a rank or commensurability restriction.

**Exact pure-reference block formula.** For any finitely supported integer-charge probability distribution, zero extend $p_n$ and set $\psi=\sum_n\sqrt{p_n}|n\rangle$. In total-charge block $m$, $\Omega_\pm$ is the outer product of the vector with components $(\pm1)^i\sqrt{\binom ri p_{m-i}/2^r}$. The common squared norm and opposite-label overlap are

$$
t_m=2^{-r}\sum_{i=0}^r\binom ri p_{m-i},\qquad
s_m=2^{-r}\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i\binom ri p_{m-i}.
\tag{M.6.13cq.14}
$$

Let $E_m,O_m$ be its even and odd squared norms. In the normalized parity directions, $R_m=\operatorname{diag}(E_m,O_m)$ and $D_m$ has off-diagonal entries $\sqrt{E_mO_m}$. The supported Sylvester solution has off-diagonal entries $2\sqrt{E_mO_m}/(E_m+O_m)$. Thus the block quality is $4E_mO_m/(E_m+O_m)=t_m-s_m^2/t_m$. This remains valid when a parity vanishes; zero blocks contribute zero. Since $\sum_m t_m=1$,

$$
1-q_{r,Q}(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)
=\sum_{m:t_m>0}\frac{s_m^2}{t_m},
\qquad \mathcal A_Q(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)=H(p).
\tag{M.6.13cq.15}
$$

**A boundary-complete sine family.** For $N\ge r$ put $h=\pi/(N+1)$, let $f(x)=\sin^{2r}x$ on $[0,\pi]$ and zero elsewhere, and set

$$
Z_N=\sum_{n=1}^N f(nh)=c_r(N+1),\qquad
p_n=f(nh)/Z_N\quad(1\le n\le N).
\tag{M.6.13cq.16}
$$

The normalization is exact: the Fourier expansion has constant coefficient $c_r$ and only frequencies $2k$ with $|k|\le r$; summing on the $(N+1)$-point grid annihilates every nonconstant frequency because $N+1>r$, and the gridpoint $0$ contributes zero.

The zero extension is $C^{2r-1}$, hence $C^r$. Differentiating a product of $2r$ labelled sine factors $r$ times gives $(2r)^r$ ordered derivative choices. Each term retains at least $r$ undifferentiated sine factors, and all differentiated factors have modulus at most one. All derivatives through order $2r-1$ vanish at the support endpoints. Therefore, on the entire real line,

$$
|f^{(r)}(x)|\le(2r)^r\sqrt{f(x)}.
\tag{M.6.13cq.17}
$$

For $m=1,\ldots,N+r$ put

$$
\begin{aligned}
D_m&=\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i\binom ri f((m-i)h),\\
W_m&=\sum_{i=0}^r\binom ri f((m-i)h),\qquad
M_m=\max_{0\le i\le r}f((m-i)h).
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13cq.18}
$$

Iterated fundamental theorem of calculus gives

$$
D_m=\int_{[0,h]^r}f^{(r)}(mh-u_1-\cdots-u_r)\,du.
$$

On $I_m=[(m-r)h,mh]$ one has $\sup f\le2^rM_m$. If the maximum is not the peak $\pi/2$, monotonicity places it at a sampled interval endpoint; zero exterior pieces cause no exception. If the peak lies in the interval, a gridpoint in that interval lies within $h/2$ of it and has value at least $\cos^{2r}(h/2)\ge2^{-r}$. If all samples vanish, the interval has $f=0$. Hence

$$
D_m^2\le(2r)^{2r}h^{2r}\sup_{I_m}f
\le2^r(2r)^{2r}h^{2r}M_m.
\tag{M.6.13cq.19}
$$

Since $W_m\ge M_m$, equations (M.6.13cq.15)–(M.6.13cq.19) imply

$$
\begin{aligned}
1-q_N
&=\sum_{m=1}^{N+r}\frac{D_m^2}{2^rZ_NW_m}
\le\frac{(N+r)(2r)^{2r}h^{2r}}{Z_N}
\le\frac{C_r}{(N+1)^{2r}},\\
\mathcal A_Q(|\psi_N\rangle\langle\psi_N|)&=H(p)\le\log N.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13cq.20}
$$

Zero denominators contribute zero. The last inequality uses $N+r\le2(N+1)$. All $N+r$ total-charge blocks, including the first and last $r$ boundary blocks, are retained.

**Exact-quality tuning and the limit.** An orthogonally retained neutral flag makes both $q$ and $\mathcal A$ affine under flagged direct sums. Mix a reference of quality $q'$ and cost $A$ with a charge-diagonal zero-quality, zero-cost branch with probabilities $\lambda,1-\lambda$. The supported Sylvester problem splits into homogeneous blocks, giving quality $\lambda q'$. The classical flag entropy cancels between $S(\mathcal G\sigma)$ and $S(\sigma)$, giving cost $\lambda A$. All flag directions remain in the reference. For $q'\ge q>0$, choosing $\lambda=q/q'$ proves $F_r^=(q)\le F_r^\ge(q)$; the reverse inequality follows from inclusion. The case $q=0$ is attained at zero cost.

Given $\delta=1-q>0$, take

$$
N=\max\{r,\lceil(C_r/\delta)^{1/(2r)}\rceil\}.
$$

Equation (M.6.13cq.20) supplies $q_N\ge q$ and the retained flag tunes exact quality without increasing cost. For fixed $r$, $\log N=(2r)^{-1}\log(1/\delta)+O_r(1)$. The lower estimate proves (M.6.13cq.3), and the already proved finite impossibility gives the endpoint statement. Substitution of $r=3$ proves (M.6.13cq.5). $\square$

**The inherited $r=1$ case.** For the two-level pair, diagonalize $\tau=\mathcal G_Q\sigma$ within each charge sector with eigenvalues $p_{q\alpha}$. The mean entries are $p_{q\alpha}/2$ and the difference entries connecting adjacent reference charges are $\sigma_{q+1,\alpha;q,\beta}/2$. The Sylvester formula, including both orientations, gives exactly

$$
q_{1,Q}(\sigma)=\sum_{q,\alpha,\beta}
\frac{2|\sigma_{q+1,\alpha;q,\beta}|^2}{p_{q+1,\alpha}+p_{q,\beta}}
=\eta_Q(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13cq.21}
$$

A term with zero denominator is defined to be zero. Thus (M.6.13h.4), (M.6.13l.1) and the retained-flag exact-quality argument identify $F_1(q)=\Phi(q)$. In particular Theorem M.6.13j gives

$$
F_1(q)=\frac12\log\frac1{1-q}+\frac{\log(2\pi)-1}{2}+O(1-q).
\tag{M.6.13cq.22}
$$

This is identity of state quantities and infima through the previously proved qubit reduction, not equality of state quality and the quality of an arbitrary apparatus. Without that reduction, the orbit argument itself gives the weaker lower estimate
$\frac12\log(1/\delta)-\log(1+\frac12\log(1/\delta))$, which still fixes the leading coefficient.

**Attribution and scope.** Relative entropy of frameness and symmetry-constrained state discrimination use the frameworks of Gour et al. (2009) and Ahmadi et al. (2013). The fidelity purification step is Uhlmann's theorem. The Petz-$1/2$ comparison and all finite-difference and boundary estimates used here are proved above. Sine-amplitude reference constructions have the established precursor in Ahmadi et al. (2013, Section 3.3). The high-quality conclusions concern the fixed extremal-pair state frontier; they do not supply an exact interior curve or an operational realization of those state witnesses.

### M.6.13cr Sharp second-order spin state frontier at bounded reference dimension

<a id="theorem-m613cr-sharp-bounded-dimension-spin-state-curvature"></a>**Theorem M.6.13cr (Sharp Bounded-Dimension Spin State Curvature).** For any fixed integer $d\ge2$, let $F_d(q)$ be the infimum of natural-$\log$ asymmetry at exact spin-$3/2$ state-discriminator quality $q$, over every complete reference of Hilbert dimension at most $d$, allowing arbitrary real charges, degeneracies, mixed states, factors and correlations. Then
$$
F_d(q)=\frac23q+\frac4{27}q^2+o(q^2)\qquad(q\downarrow0).
\tag{M.6.13cr.1}
$$
This is a state-only statement; no prescribed all-input operational quality or pointer dimension is identified with $q$. More generally, every sequence with bounded reference dimension and $q_n>0$, $q_n\to0$ satisfies the lower curvature bound (M.6.13cr.2), even when dephased states lose rank and the numerical real charge spectra vary.

The proof first establishes a faithful-limit lemma with no regularity assumptions, then controls singular limits by a retained heavy/light decomposition.

<a id="lemma-m613cra-state-only-faithful-limit-curvature"></a>**Lemma M.6.13cr.a (State-Only Faithful-Limit Curvature).** Retain the complete finite-reference spin-$3/2$ discriminator contract of Theorems M.6.13ch and M.6.13ck. Fix any finite reference charge $Q$, allowing arbitrary real eigenvalues, degeneracies, mixed states, neutral factors, retained flags and correlations. Let $\sigma_n$ be reference states, with
$$
q_n=q_Q(\sigma_n)>0,\qquad q_n\longrightarrow0,\qquad
\tau_n=\mathcal G_Q\sigma_n\longrightarrow\tau>0
$$
on a fixed finite reference support. Then
$$
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\frac{\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_n)-2q_n/3}{q_n^2}\ge\frac4{27}.
\tag{M.6.13cr.2}
$$
The constant is sharp. It is attained as a limit by balanced unit-gap qubits, for which $q=3c^2/4$ and $\mathcal A_Q=F(c^2)=c^2/2+c^4/12+O(c^6)$, with $F(z)=[(1+\sqrt z)\log(1+\sqrt z)+(1-\sqrt z)\log(1-\sqrt z)]/2$. The same conclusion holds without convergence of $\tau_n$ if their smallest eigenvalues have a common positive lower bound on that fixed support.

In particular this covers every finite-dimensional smooth path through a faithful invariant state, including moving dephased means, nonanalytic or oscillating approaches, arbitrary second-order gap-two coherence and quantum-correlated degeneracies. No path expansion or fixed second derivative is assumed. The assertion is about state quality $q$, not an operational all-input optimum: only the previously established inequality $u\le q$ is available. This intermediate lemma does not by itself control singular dephased limits or supply a dimension-uniform faithful reduction.

**Proof.** All logarithms are natural. Physical zero-state directions can remain in the complete reference; faithfulness is required on a single fixed support containing all the states under consideration. No support is removed differently at different $n$.

**Quadratic forms and their nullspace.** For a charge-invariant faithful state $\nu$, use the linear maps $R_Z,D_Z$ of Theorem M.6.13ch and write
$$
R_\nu=\operatorname{diag}(p)\otimes\nu,
\quad p=(1,3,3,1)/8,
\quad R_\nu B_{\nu,Z}+B_{\nu,Z}R_\nu=2D_Z,
\quad j_\nu(Z)=\operatorname{Tr}(D_ZB_{\nu,Z}).
$$
For charge-off-diagonal Hermitian $Z$, put
$$
a_\nu(Z)=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}[Z\,\mathrm D\log_\nu(Z)],
\qquad E_\nu(Z)=a_\nu(Z)-\tfrac23j_\nu(Z).
\tag{M.6.13cr.3}
$$
The coefficient comparison below gives $E_\nu\ge0$ for the quadratic Taylor forms at $\nu$. The separate hypothesis $R_Z=0$ is needed only to turn the quadratic Taylor expression into the nonlinear identity $q_Q(\nu+Z)=j_\nu(Z)$; it is not imposed here. Explicitly, in a common charge/$\nu$ eigenbasis,
$$
a_\nu(Z)=\sum_{a<b}L(\lambda_a,\lambda_b)|Z_{ab}|^2,
\quad j_\nu(Z)=\sum_{a<b}C_{|e_a-e_b|}(\lambda_a,\lambda_b)|Z_{ab}|^2,
$$
where the sums exclude equal-charge entries, $L(a,b)=(\log a-\log b)/(a-b)$ with $L(a,a)=1/a$, and
$$
C_1(a,b)=\tfrac32\left(\frac1{3a+b}+\frac1{a+b}+\frac1{a+3b}\right),
\quad C_3(a,b)=\frac1{2(a+b)},
\quad C_d=0\quad(d\notin\{1,3\}).
$$

To verify these coefficients directly, choose the common charge/$\nu$ eigenbasis used above and let $p=(1,3,3,1)/8$. The entropy resolvent derivative gives
$$
\mathrm D\log_\nu[Z]=\int_0^\infty(\nu+sI)^{-1}Z(\nu+sI)^{-1}\,ds,
\qquad a_\nu(Z)=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}[Z\,\mathrm D\log_\nu[Z]].
\tag{M.6.13cr.P1}
$$
Each off-charge entry has $\int$ coefficient $L(\lambda_a,\lambda_b)$, with the two orientations cancelling the factor $1/2$. The difference-map entry is
$(D_Z)_{ia,jb}=\sqrt{p_ip_j}Z_{ab}$ when $i+e_a=j+e_b$ and $i-j$ is odd, and is zero otherwise. At $\nu$, the Sylvester optimizer therefore has entries $2(D_Z)_{ia,jb}/(p_i\lambda_a+p_j\lambda_b)$. Both orientations and the factor two in this inverse give
$$
C_d(a,b)=4\sum_{j=0}^{3-d}\frac{p_{j+d}p_j}{p_{j+d}a+p_jb}\quad(d=1,3).
\tag{M.6.13cr.P2}
$$
For $m=(a+b)/2$ and $x=(a-b)/(a+b)$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
L(a,b)&=\frac1m\frac{\operatorname{artanh}x}{x}
=\frac1m\left(1+\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{x^{2n}}{2n+1}\right),\\
C_1(a,b)&=\frac3{2m}\frac{8-x^2}{8-2x^2}
=\frac3{2m}\left(1+\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{x^{2n}}{2\cdot4^n}\right),
\qquad C_3(a,b)=\frac1{4m}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13cr.P3}
$$
The values at $x=0$ are continuous. Since $1/(2n+1)>1/(2\cdot4^n)$ for every $n\ge1$, $C_1\le3L/2$, with equality precisely at $a=b$. For gap three, $L/C_3=4\operatorname{artanh}(x)/x\ge4$. Every other charged entry has positive entropy coefficient and zero discriminator coefficient.

Thus the nullspace of $E_\nu$ consists precisely of the unit-gap matrices commuting with $\nu$. The quadratic forms are orthogonal sums over absolute charge gaps. On the subspace with no unit-gap entries, $E_\nu$ is positive definite. On a compact faithful neighborhood of $\tau$, there is consequently a common $c_0>0$ such that
$$
E_\nu(Y)\ge c_0\|Y\|_2^2
\quad\text{whenever $Y$ has no unit-gap entries.}
\tag{M.6.13cr.4}
$$
This is a finite-dimensional continuity assertion, not a constant uniform over dimensions or eigenvalue lower bounds. Entropy and the inverse Sylvester map have uniformly bounded derivatives of each fixed order on this same neighborhood.

**Forced scale separation.** It suffices to consider a subsequence on which the quotient in (M.6.13cr.2) is bounded above; if none exists, the result is immediate. Put
$$
\Delta_n=\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_n)-2q_n/3=O(q_n^2),
\quad Z_n=\sigma_n-\tau_n,
\quad t_n=\|Z_n\|_2.
$$
Theorem M.6.13ck gives $\Delta_n\ge0$. Since $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_n)=2q_n/3+O(q_n^2)\to0$, Pinsker's inequality gives $Z_n\to0$. Also $t_n>0$ and $q_n=O(t_n^2)$ by the uniformly bounded inverse Sylvester map.

Split $Z_n=X_n+Y_n$, with $X_n$ containing exactly the charge gaps $\pm1$ and $Y_n$ all remaining off-charge blocks. The cubic entropy Taylor term on three copies of $X_n$ vanishes identically for every charge-invariant $\tau_n$: three steps of size $\pm1$ cannot form a closed charge word. Its remaining terms are $O(t_n^2\|Y_n\|_2)$. Also $R_{X_n}=0$, so expansion of the Sylvester inverse around $R_{\tau_n}$ shows
$$
\Delta_n=E_{\tau_n}(Z_n)
 +O(t_n^2\|Y_n\|_2)+O(t_n^4).
\tag{M.6.13cr.5}
$$
All constants are uniform along this subsequence. For clarity, the quadratic-discriminator remainder is $O(\|R_{Y_n}\|\,\|D_{Z_n}\|^2)=O(t_n^2\|Y_n\|_2)$, and the entropy fourth-order remainder is $O(t_n^4)$.

Since $\Delta_n=O(t_n^4)$ and (M.6.13cr.4) gives $E_{\tau_n}(Z_n)\ge c_0\|Y_n\|_2^2$, the quadratic inequality from (M.6.13cr.5) implies
$$
\|Y_n\|_2=O(t_n^2),\qquad E_{\tau_n}(X_n)=O(t_n^4).
\tag{M.6.13cr.6}
$$
Pass to a further subsequence so that
$$
X_n/t_n\longrightarrow H,\qquad Y_n/t_n^2\longrightarrow G.
$$
Then $\|H\|_2=1$, $H$ has only unit gaps, and continuity in (M.6.13cr.6) gives $E_\tau(H)=0$, hence $[\tau,H]=0$. In particular
$$
K=\tau^{-1}H=K^*,\qquad
q_n/t_n^2\longrightarrow j_\tau(H)=\tfrac34\operatorname{Tr}(\tau K^2)>0.
\tag{M.6.13cr.7}
$$
The unit-gap tangent $X_n/t_n$ may vary without a bounded second derivative. Its entire instantaneous Hessian cost has been retained rather than Taylor-expanded.

**Quartic coefficients.** Set
$$
D=\mathcal G_Q(K^2),\quad S=K^2-D.
$$
Here $S$ has only gaps $\pm2$ and $K,D,S$ commute with $\tau$. Project $G$ onto gaps $\pm2$ and then onto blocks preserving each eigenvalue of $\tau$, obtaining $G_{2,=}$. Put $L_2=\tau^{-1}G_{2,=}$, which is Hermitian and commutes with $\tau$.

The uniformly valid expansions are
$$
\begin{split}
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_n)
 &=a_{\tau_n}(Z_n)+t_n^4\left[
 \tfrac1{12}\operatorname{Tr}(\tau K^4)
 -\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(\tau S L_2)\right]+o(t_n^4),\\
q_n&=j_{\tau_n}(Z_n)
 -\tfrac38t_n^4\operatorname{Tr}(\tau S L_2)+o(t_n^4).
\end{split}
\tag{M.6.13cr.8}
$$
We give their coefficients explicitly. For entropy, the three-$X_n$ cubic term is exactly zero. Since $Y_n=O(t_n^2)$, only the two-$X_n$, one-$Y_n$ term remains at fourth order. At the limit $[\tau,H]=0$, its value is $-\operatorname{Tr}(\tau^{-2}H^2G)/2$. Indeed the derivative in direction $G$ at $\tau+sH$ is $\operatorname{Tr}[G(\log(\tau+sH)+I)]$; the coefficient of $s^2$ is $-\operatorname{Tr}(G\tau^{-2}H^2)/2$. Charge and $\tau$-spectral orthogonality leave exactly $G_{2,=}$. The fourth derivative on four copies of $H$ is the commuting coefficient $\operatorname{Tr}(\tau^{-3}H^4)/12$. Continuity of these multilinear derivatives and the bounded fifth derivative justify the entropy remainder in (M.6.13cr.8).

For the second line, write $\mathcal J_R(B)=(RB+BR)/2$. The inverse expansion gives
$$
q_n=j_{\tau_n}(Z_n)
 -\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(R_{Y_n}B_{\tau_n,Z_n}^2\bigr)+O(t_n^6).
$$
Since $B_{\tau_n,Z_n}/t_n\to B_{\tau,H}$, the correction divided by $t_n^4$ converges to $-\operatorname{Tr}(R_GB_{\tau,H}^2)$. In a common charge/$\tau$ eigenbasis, nonzero entries of $H$ preserve the eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $\tau$, and
$$
(B_{\tau,H})_{ia,jb}
 =\frac{2\sqrt{p_ip_j}}{p_i+p_j}K_{ab}
\quad\text{when $|i-j|=1$ and $i+e_a=j+e_b$.}
$$
Two such factors preserve $\lambda$ and change reference charge by zero or two. Since $G$ has no equal-charge block, only $G_{2,=}$ contributes. For either orientation of a two-step charge path the system factor is
$$
\sum_{i=0}^1
\frac{4p_ip_{i+1}p_{i+2}}{(p_i+p_{i+1})(p_{i+1}+p_{i+2})}
=\frac3{16}+\frac3{16}=\frac38.
$$
Thus $\operatorname{Tr}(R_GB_{\tau,H}^2)=3\operatorname{Tr}(\tau S L_2)/8$. This is an ordered block-product computation and applies to arbitrary operator-valued charge blocks; it uses neither scalar balancing nor a transpose of operator entries.

**Completion of squares.** Charge-gap orthogonality, the nonnegative Hessian comparison and its gap-two contribution imply
$$
\liminf_n\frac{E_{\tau_n}(Z_n)}{t_n^4}
\ge a_\tau(G_2)\ge\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(\tau L_2^2).
$$
The second inequality retains the equal-$\tau$-eigenvalue entries explicitly and drops only positive unequal-eigenvalue terms. No commutation of the original second-order matrix $G$ with $\tau$ is assumed. Equations (M.6.13cr.8) now yield
$$
\begin{split}
\liminf_n\frac{\Delta_n}{t_n^4}
&\ge \tfrac1{12}\operatorname{Tr}(\tau K^4)
 +\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(\tau L_2^2)
 -\tfrac14\operatorname{Tr}(\tau S L_2)\\
&=\tfrac1{12}\operatorname{Tr}(\tau D^2)
 +\tfrac5{96}\operatorname{Tr}(\tau S^2)
 +\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}\bigl[\tau(L_2-S/4)^2\bigr]\\
&\ge\tfrac1{12}\bigl[\operatorname{Tr}(\tau K^2)\bigr]^2.
\end{split}
\tag{M.6.13cr.9}
$$
Here $\operatorname{Tr}(\tau K^4)=\operatorname{Tr}(\tau D^2)+\operatorname{Tr}(\tau S^2)$ by charge orthogonality, and the last step is weighted variance nonnegativity with $\operatorname{Tr}\tau=1$. Division by (M.6.13cr.7) proves $4/27$. Every bounded-quotient subsequence has such a further subsequence, which proves (M.6.13cr.2). A common eigenvalue lower bound allows compact subsequence extraction of a faithful mean, proving the stated variant. The balanced-qubit expansion proves sharpness. $\square$

**Proof of the theorem (varying charges and singular limits).** The balanced unit-gap qubit supplies the upper bound and exists within each dimension bound $d\ge2$. It suffices to prove the sequential lower bound. Restrict to a subsequence on which
$$
\Delta_n:=\mathcal A_{Q_n}(\sigma_n)-2q_n/3\le Cq_n^2
$$
for a finite constant $C$. Theorem M.6.13ck gives $\Delta_n\ge0$; hence asymmetry tends to zero.

**Finite charge patterns.** Pass to a fixed reference dimension and diagonalize each charge. For each ordered reference-index pair record whether its charge difference is one of $0,\pm1,\pm2,\pm3$, or none of these. There are finitely many records at fixed dimension, so pass to one fixed record. Both reference dephasing and the spin mean/difference maps $R,D$ depend exactly on this record: a system/reference matrix entry is retained precisely when $i+e_a=j+e_b$ with $0\le i,j\le3$. Choose one representative charge $Q_*$ realizing the record. The numerical values of asymmetry and discriminator quality of every transformed state are unchanged when computed with $Q_*$. The invariant-test restriction adds no further dependence, because the supported Sylvester optimizer is automatically invariant.

Now diagonalize each dephased state $\tau_n$ within the fixed charge eigenspaces by charge-commuting unitaries; these preserve $Q_*$, asymmetry and quality. Pass to a subsequence on which all its diagonal entries converge, obtaining a diagonal limit $\tau_0$. Let $P$ contain exactly the indices with positive limiting eigenvalue, and put $P^\perp=I-P$. In this transformed description $P$ commutes with every $\tau_n$ and with $Q_*$. Equivalently in the original coordinates these are the charge-invariant heavy spectral projections of $\tau_n$; no noncommuting fixed-limit projection is used.

Write
$$
\sigma_n=\begin{pmatrix}A_n&X_n\\X_n^*&C_n\end{pmatrix},
\qquad w_n=\operatorname{Tr}C_n\to0,
\qquad\widehat\sigma_n=A_n\oplus C_n.
$$
Pinsker's inequality gives $\sigma_n-\tau_n\to0$. Choose $m>0$ so that the heavy block of $\tau_n$ is at least $mI$ eventually; then $A_n\ge(m/2)I$ eventually. Also $C_n\le w_nI$. If $w_n=0$ along a subsequence, positivity forces $X_n=0$ and the faithful-limit theorem applies directly to the heavy block. We may therefore assume $w_n>0$.

**Entropy cost of cross-support coherence.** Since $P$ commutes with $Q_*$ and $\tau_n$, the complete charge dephasing of $\widehat\sigma_n$ is still $\tau_n$. The pinching chain rule gives
$$
\mathcal A_{Q_*}(\sigma_n)-\mathcal A_{Q_*}(\widehat\sigma_n)
=D(\sigma_n\Vert\widehat\sigma_n).
$$
Set $H_n=\sigma_n-\widehat\sigma_n$. The involution $P-P^\perp$ commutes with $\widehat\sigma_n$ and anticommutes with $H_n$. The following positive-even resolvent expansion therefore gives
$$
D(\sigma_n\Vert\widehat\sigma_n)
\ge\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}[H_n\,\mathrm D\log_{\widehat\sigma_n}(H_n)].
$$
To prove this inequality, write $T=\widehat\sigma_n$ and $H=H_n$ on $\operatorname{supp}T$. The involution commutes with $T$ and anticommutes with $H$, while $T\pm H\succeq0$. For $s\ge0$ and $|t|<1$ set
$$
K_s=(T+sI)^{-1/2}H(T+sI)^{-1/2},\qquad
M_{2k}=\int_0^\infty\operatorname{Tr}|K_s|^{2k}\,ds,
\qquad f(t)=D(T+tH\Vert T).
\tag{M.6.13cr.P4}
$$
The eigenvalues of $K_s$ occur in pairs $\pm\kappa$ and have $|\kappa|\le1$. The logarithmic resolvent and cyclicity give $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ and
$$
f''(t)=\int_0^\infty\operatorname{Tr}[K_s^2(I+tK_s)^{-2}]\,ds,
\qquad
f(t)=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{t^{2k}M_{2k}}{2k}.
\tag{M.6.13cr.P5}
$$
Indeed, expanding $(1+t\kappa)^{-2}$, pairing opposite eigenvalues and integrating twice gives the displayed coefficient. All even coefficients are nonnegative. Monotone convergence as $t\uparrow1$ and continuity of finite-dimensional $x\log x$ give
$$
D(T+H\Vert T)\ge\frac{M_2}{2}
=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}[H\,\mathrm D\log_T(H)].
\tag{M.6.13cr.P6}
$$
This uses only the involution, not a charge-invariant mean or the additional condition $R_H=0$ for the discriminator. Work on the support of $\widehat\sigma_n$; positivity of $\sigma_n$ forces every cross entry into a zero eigenvector of $C_n$ to vanish. The same positive-coefficient series, followed by its supported endpoint limit, covers singular $C_n$ or $\sigma_n$.

If $a$ is an eigenvalue of $A_n$ and $c>0$ one of $C_n$, then $a\ge m/2$, $c\le w_n$, and $a-c\le1$. For sufficiently large $n$,
$$
\frac{\log a-\log c}{a-c}\ge\log\frac{m}{2w_n}.
$$
Summing the off-block BKM coefficients yields
$$
\mathcal A_{Q_*}(\sigma_n)-\mathcal A_{Q_*}(\widehat\sigma_n)
\ge \log\frac{m}{2w_n}\,\|X_n\|_2^2.
\tag{M.6.13cr.10}
$$

**Uniform cross-support quality gain.** Write $q_n^0=q_{Q_*}(\widehat\sigma_n)$. Then
$$
0\le q_n-q_n^0\le \frac{128}{m}\|X_n\|_2^2.
\tag{M.6.13cr.11}
$$
For completeness, decompose an actual Hermitian contraction optimizer $B$ by the system-tensored heavy/light projection as $B=B_0+B_1$, with $B_0$ block diagonal and $B_1$ off diagonal. Write the upper-right block of $B_1$ as $Y$ and $z=\|Y\|_2$. The diagonal part satisfies $\|B_0\|\le1$. Let $R_0,D_0$ be the mean/difference pair of $\widehat\sigma_n$, and $R_1,D_1$ its off-block corrections for $\sigma_n$.

The heavy block of $R_0$ is at least $(m/16)I$: positivity and $A_n\ge(m/2)I$ give $R_{A_n}\ge(m/2)\operatorname{diag}(p)\otimes I$. Hilbert–Schmidt contractivity of total-charge pinching and $\|\rho_*\|_2=\|(\rho_+-\rho_-)/2\|_2=1/\sqrt2$ give
$$
\|R_1\|_2,\|D_1\|_2\le\|X_n\|_2,
\qquad \|B_1\|_2=\sqrt2z.
$$
In the variational objective $2\operatorname{Tr}(DB)-\operatorname{Tr}(RB^2)$ the diagonal part is at most $q_n^0$. The additional negative term is at most $-(m/16)z^2$, while the two off-block linear terms are bounded above by $4\sqrt2\|X_n\|_2z$. There is no trace contribution from $R_1B_1^2$, which is off-diagonal times diagonal. Completing the scalar square gives the upper bound in (M.6.13cr.11). The lower bound follows by inserting the optimal block-diagonal test for $\widehat\sigma_n$ into the objective for $\sigma_n$.

**Discarding no quality at leading order.** Put
$$
\Delta_n^0=\mathcal A_{Q_*}(\widehat\sigma_n)-2q_n^0/3.
$$
By (M.6.13cr.10)–(M.6.13cr.11),
$$
\Delta_n\ge\Delta_n^0+
\left(\log\frac{m}{2w_n}-\frac{256}{3m}\right)\|X_n\|_2^2.
\tag{M.6.13cr.12}
$$
The coefficient tends to infinity and $\Delta_n^0\ge0$ by the global bound. Hence, eventually,
$$
\Delta_n\ge\Delta_n^0,\qquad
\|X_n\|_2^2=O\!\left(\frac{q_n^2}{\log(1/w_n)}\right),
\qquad q_n-q_n^0=o(q_n^2).
$$

Normalize the heavy and light states as $\sigma_{H,n}=A_n/(1-w_n)$ and $\sigma_{L,n}=C_n/w_n$, with qualities $q_{H,n},q_{L,n}$ and deficits $\Delta_{H,n},\Delta_{L,n}$. The retained orthogonal decomposition is exact for both quantities:
$$
q_n^0=(1-w_n)q_{H,n}+w_nq_{L,n},\quad
\Delta_n^0=(1-w_n)\Delta_{H,n}+w_n\Delta_{L,n}.
$$
Let $C_{\rm cm}=12192768000000000$. Theorem M.6.13cm gives
$$
\Delta_n^0\ge w_n\Delta_{L,n}\ge\frac{w_nq_{L,n}^2}{C_{\rm cm}},
$$
so $w_nq_{L,n}=O(q_n\sqrt{w_n})=o(q_n)$. Therefore
$$
(1-w_n)q_{H,n}=q_n(1-o(1)).
$$
The normalized heavy means converge to the faithful trace-one state $\tau_0|_P$. The already proved faithful-limit theorem gives
$$
\Delta_n\ge(1-w_n)\Delta_{H,n}
\ge\left(\frac4{27}-o(1)\right)(1-w_n)q_{H,n}^2
=\left(\frac4{27}-o(1)\right)q_n^2.
$$
This proves the sequential lower bound, including all rank-loss cases. If the infimum statement (M.6.13cr.1) failed, choose a sequence of admissible states within $o(q_n^2)$ of the defining infima; it would violate the sequential result. Together with the exact-quality balanced-qubit upper family this proves (M.6.13cr.1). $\square$

**Scope and unrestricted-dimension obstruction.** The same sequential lower bound holds when only $\operatorname{rank}(\mathcal G_Q\sigma)$ is bounded: restrict the calculations to the charge-invariant support of $\mathcal G_Q\sigma$. Positivity gives $\operatorname{supp}\sigma\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal G_Q\sigma)$, and the mean/difference pair is supported on the system tensored with that reference support, so asymmetry and quality are unchanged.
