Physical zero-state directions remain counted in every complete resource budget. Consequently any sequence improving the coefficient $4/27$ in the complete finite-reference infimum must have unbounded dimension of the charge-invariant support $\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal G_Q\sigma)$; no claim about $\operatorname{rank}\sigma$ is made. Rank loss, real-charge widths, varying spectra, flags and correlations at bounded dimension cannot provide such an escape. This does not prove that a dimension-growing improvement exists or that the unrestricted second-order expansion has a limit. The dimension-independent quadratic lower coefficient in Theorem M.6.13cm and the balanced-pair upper coefficient are consistent with this bounded-dimension statement.

**Operational lower-bound corollary only.** For complete operational models whose entire reference dimension is bounded, let $0<u_n=1-\epsilon_n^2\to0$. Then
$$
\liminf_n\frac{\mathcal A_{Q_n}(\sigma_n)-2u_n/3}{u_n^2}\ge\frac4{27}.
\tag{M.6.13cr.13}
$$
Indeed, on any subsequence where this quotient is bounded, $u_n\le q_n$ and $\mathcal A\ge2q_n/3$ imply $q_n-u_n=O(u_n^2)$ and $q_n/u_n\to1$. Apply the state theorem and write $\mathcal A-2u_n/3=(\mathcal A-2q_n/3)+2(q_n-u_n)/3$. If no bounded-quotient subsequence exists, the lower bound is immediate. No matching operational upper coefficient, equality $u=q$, optimal pointer size, physical identification, preparation/readout price, or hardware realization follows.

### M.6.13cs Full-boundary pure-packet constants and a non-Gaussian high-quality refinement

<a id="theorem-m613cs-pure-packet-discriminator-constants"></a>**Theorem M.6.13cs (Pure-Packet Discriminator Constants).** Retain the complete finite-reference state-discrimination contract and the infimum $F_r$ of Theorem M.6.13cq, with fixed integer $r=2J\ge2$. Let $\mathcal P_r$ be the class of probability densities supported on a finite interval $[a,b]$, zero extended outside, of the form

$$
f(x)=(x-a)^{2r}(b-x)^{2r}g(x),\qquad a<x<b,
\tag{M.6.13cs.1}
$$

where $g$ is positive and $C^r$ on $[a,b]$. Define

$$
h(f)=-\int f\log f,\qquad
I_r(f)=\int_{a}^{b}\frac{[f^{(r)}(x)]^2}{f(x)}\,dx,\qquad
C_r(f)=h(f)+\frac1{2r}\log\frac{I_r(f)}{4^r},\qquad
C_{\mathrm{packet},r}=\inf_{f\in\mathcal P_r}C_r(f).
\tag{M.6.13cs.2}
$$

For every fixed $f\in\mathcal P_r$ and every sufficiently small $\delta>0$, there is a finite pure simple-integer-charge reference with **exact** state quality $q=1-\delta$ and

$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_\delta)
=\frac1{2r}\log\frac1\delta+C_r(f)+o(1).
\tag{M.6.13cs.3}
$$

Every total-charge boundary block is included. The functional $C_r$ is translation and dilation invariant, and

$$
-\log\frac r{r-1}\le C_{\mathrm{packet},r}<\infty,\qquad
\limsup_{\delta\downarrow0}
\left[F_r(1-\delta)-\frac1{2r}\log\frac1\delta\right]
\le C_{\mathrm{packet},r}.
\tag{M.6.13cs.4}
$$

Writing $\phi(x)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2}$ for the standard Gaussian density, one has the strict comparison

$$
C_{\mathrm{packet},r}<
\frac12\log(2\pi e)+\frac1{2r}\log(r!)-\log2
=C_r(\phi),\qquad r\ge2.
\tag{M.6.13cs.5}
$$

Here the Gaussian functional is defined by the same integrals; it is approached by compact profiles and is not claimed to be a finite reference. For $r=3$, the explicit certified refinement is

$$
\boxed{\quad
\limsup_{q\uparrow1}
\left[F_3(q)-\frac16\log\frac1{1-q}\right]
\le \frac12\log(2\pi e)+\frac16\log\left(\frac{1375776}{64\cdot231125}\right).
\quad}
\tag{M.6.13cs.6}
$$

The right side is approximately $1.023093773451$ nats, strictly below the Gaussian-packet value approximately $1.024417930849$. The exact expression, not a numerical quadrature, is the certificate.

These are state-quality and constructive upper statements. They do not identify the sharp unrestricted additive constant, establish a limit for the unrestricted renormalized frontier, or identify $q$ with operational all-input quality $u$. The exact qubit frontier of Theorem M.6.13l remains a separate result.

*Proof.*

**Exact finite packets and all boundaries.** Fix $0<h_0<b-a$. For $0<h<h_0$ put

$$
Z_h=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}f(nh),\qquad
p_n(h)=\frac{f(nh)}{Z_h},\qquad
|\psi_h\rangle=\sum_n\sqrt{p_n(h)}|n\rangle,\qquad Q|n\rangle=n|n\rangle.
\tag{M.6.13cs.7}
$$

Only the finitely many nonzero samples are retained. The open support interval contains a grid point because $h<b-a$, so $Z_h>0$. Continuity of $f$ and $f\log f$ at the zero endpoints and ordinary Riemann sums give

$$
hZ_h\longrightarrow1,\qquad
H(p(h))=\log(1/h)+h(f)+o(1).
\tag{M.6.13cs.8}
$$

Define the zero-extended differences and binomial sums

$$
D_m(h)=\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i\binom ri f((m-i)h),\qquad
W_m(h)=\sum_{i=0}^r\binom ri f((m-i)h).
\tag{M.6.13cs.9}
$$

The exact pure-reference formula (M.6.13cq.15), including every total-charge block, reads

$$
\delta(h):=1-q_{r,Q}(|\psi_h\rangle\langle\psi_h|)
=\frac1{2^rZ_h}\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}\frac{D_m(h)^2}{W_m(h)}.
\tag{M.6.13cs.10}
$$

Zero-denominator summands are zero. The endpoint form (M.6.13cs.1) implies that its zero extension is $C^r$ and

$$
|f^{(r)}(x)|\le C_f\sqrt{f(x)}\quad(x\in\mathbb R).
\tag{M.6.13cs.11}
$$

Indeed every term of the differentiated product vanishes to at least order $r$ at each endpoint, while $g$ is bounded above and below by positive constants. Repeated fundamental theorem gives

$$
D_m(h)=\int_{[0,h]^r}f^{(r)}(mh-u_1-\cdots-u_r)\,du.
\tag{M.6.13cs.12}
$$

There is a constant $K_f$ such that for all sufficiently small $h$ and all $m$,

$$
\sup_{[(m-r)h,mh]}f
\le K_f\max_{0\le i\le r}f((m-i)h).
\tag{M.6.13cs.13}
$$

To verify this also at the boundary, $f$ is monotone on sufficiently small one-sided endpoint neighborhoods: its logarithmic derivative there is the endpoint pole plus bounded terms. Intervals lying there have their maximum at a sampled endpoint. Exterior zero portions cause no exception. Intervals not contained in these endpoint neighborhoods, but meeting the support, contain a sample in a fixed interior compact interval when $h$ is small, so boundedness and a positive interior minimum give the uniform comparison. No short interval crosses both support endpoints.

Consequently

$$
0\le\frac{D_m(h)^2}{h^{2r}W_m(h)}\le C_f^2K_f.
\tag{M.6.13cs.14}
$$

On compact subsets of $(a,b)$, the quotients $D_m(h)/h^r$ and $W_m(h)$ converge uniformly to $f^{(r)}(mh)$ and $2^rf(mh)$, respectively. At most $O(\eta/h)+O(1)$ indices meet endpoint neighborhoods of length $\eta$, so (M.6.13cs.14) makes their contribution to the corresponding $h$-weighted sum $O(\eta)+O(h)$. Interior Riemann convergence and then $\eta\downarrow0$ prove

$$
\frac{\delta(h)}{h^{2r}}\longrightarrow
\frac{I_r(f)}{4^r}=:k_f>0.
\tag{M.6.13cs.15}
$$

If $I_r(f)=0$, then $f^{(r)}=0$ in the interval; the resulting polynomial of degree at most $r-1$ and its vanishing endpoint derivatives force $f=0$, contradicting normalization. Thus $k_f$ is positive. This argument explicitly retains the first and last partly occupied charge blocks; no edge error is suppressed by a formal denominator expansion.

**Pure exact-quality tuning.** On every compact subinterval of $(0,h_0)$ only finitely many grid indices can contribute. Their probabilities vary continuously, with support changes at zero weights. Since $|D_m|\le W_m$, the function $D_m^2/W_m$ extends continuously by zero where $W_m=0$. Hence $\delta(h)$ is continuous. For any fixed $0<\eta<1$, the scales

$$
h_\pm=(\delta/k_f)^{1/(2r)}(1\pm\eta)
\tag{M.6.13cs.16}
$$

bracket the requested deficit for sufficiently small $\delta$. The intermediate value theorem gives $h_\delta\in[h_-,h_+]$ with $\delta(h_\delta)=\delta$. These roots tend to zero, and (M.6.13cs.15) then gives $h_\delta/(\delta/k_f)^{1/(2r)}\to1$. Combining with (M.6.13cs.8) proves (M.6.13cs.3), without a mixing flag. Pure-state asymmetry is exactly $H(p)$.

For $f_s(x)=s^{-1}f((x-t)/s)$, $s>0$, one has $h(f_s)=h(f)+\log s$ and $I_r(f_s)=s^{-2r}I_r(f)$, proving invariance. The universal lower bound of M.6.13cq applied to (M.6.13cs.3) gives the lower bound in (M.6.13cs.4); any one profile gives finiteness. For each fixed profile, its exact witnesses give the limsup bound with $C_r(f)$, and then taking the infimum gives (M.6.13cs.4).

**Compact approximation of Gaussian-polynomial profiles.** The following argument is only a mathematical approximation for constructing finite packets. Let $f$ be $\phi$ times a strictly positive polynomial, normalized to $\int$ one. Choose a sufficiently smooth fixed transition shape and its rescaling $w_R$, with $0\le w_R\le1$, equal to one on $[-R,R]$, positive on $(-2R,2R)$ and vanishing linearly at $\pm2R$. Put

$$
f_R=c_R f w_R^{2r},\qquad \int f_R=1.
\tag{M.6.13cs.17}
$$

Inside its support $w_R$ is smooth up to the endpoints; its zero extension need not be smooth, but $w_R^{2r}$ has all the endpoint vanishing needed in (M.6.13cs.1). Thus $f_R\in\mathcal P_r$. Differentiating its $2r$ factors gives for $0\le j\le r$

$$
|(w_R^{2r})^{(j)}|\le C_jR^{-j}w_R^{2r-j}.
\tag{M.6.13cs.18}
$$

Leibniz and a finite-square bound dominate $(f_R^{(r)})^2/f_R$, uniformly for large $R$, by a constant times $\sum_{k=0}^r(f^{(k)})^2/f$. This is integrable for a Gaussian times a strictly positive polynomial. Here such a polynomial has a positive global lower bound. Dominated convergence therefore gives $I_r(f_R)\to I_r(f)$. For entropy, use integrability of $f|\log f|$, $c_R\to1$, and boundedness of $t|\log t|$ on $[0,1]$ in the extra factor $w_R^{2r}$. These imply $h(f_R)\to h(f)$ and hence $C_r(f_R)\to C_r(f)$. The limits are used in the order: choose a large fixed compact cutoff, then send the sampling scale to zero.

**Hermite descent.** Define the probabilists' Hermite polynomials by $\phi^{(k)}=(-1)^kH_k\phi$. Repeated integration by parts gives $\int\phi H_jH_k=k!\,\mathbf1_{j=k}$. In particular $I_r(\phi)=r!$, giving the Gaussian value in (M.6.13cs.5). For sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ let

$$
f_\varepsilon=\phi(1+\varepsilon H_{2r}).
\tag{M.6.13cs.19}
$$

The even polynomial $H_{2r}$ has positive leading coefficient and is bounded below, so the density is strictly positive. Orthogonality gives $\int$ one and, since $r\ge2$, mean zero and variance one. Nonnegativity of $D(f_\varepsilon\Vert\phi)$ therefore gives $h(f_\varepsilon)\le h(\phi)$. Gaussian-polynomial domination, with the denominator bounded away from zero for small positive $\varepsilon$, justifies the following right derivatives:

$$
\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}h(f_\varepsilon)\right|_{0+}=0,\qquad
I_r(f_\varepsilon)=\int\phi\frac{(H_r+\varepsilon H_{3r})^2}{1+\varepsilon H_{2r}},\qquad
\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}I_r(f_\varepsilon)\right|_{0+}=-(2r)!.
\tag{M.6.13cs.20}
$$

For the last identity the cross inner product $\int\phi H_rH_{3r}$ vanishes, and $\int\phi H_r^2H_{2r}=(2r)!$: the polynomial $H_r^2-H_{2r}$ has degree less than $2r$ because both summands are monic. Thus

$$
\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}C_r(f_\varepsilon)\right|_{0+}
=-\frac{(2r)!}{2r\,r!}<0.
\tag{M.6.13cs.21}
$$

Compact approximation preserves a sufficiently small strict improvement and proves (M.6.13cs.5). Negative $\varepsilon$ is not required and would fail positivity in the tails.

**Exact spin-three-halves certificate.** The polynomial $H_6=x^6-15x^4+45x^2-15$ has minimum $-40-20\sqrt{10}>-104$. Indeed, $H_6'=6x(x^4-10x^2+15)$, so its stationary points have $x=0$ or $x^2=5\pm\sqrt{10}$, with values $-15$ and $-40\mp20\sqrt{10}$; it tends to $+\infty$ at either infinity. The strict lower estimate follows from $\sqrt{10}<16/5$. Take $\varepsilon=1/7500$. The algebraic identity

$$
\frac{(a+\varepsilon b)^2}{1+\varepsilon c}
=a^2+\varepsilon(2ab-a^2c)
+\frac{\varepsilon^2(b-ac)^2}{1+\varepsilon c}
\tag{M.6.13cs.22}
$$

and $H_3H_6=H_9+18H_7+90H_5+120H_3$ give

$$
\begin{aligned}
I_3(f_\varepsilon)
&=6-720\varepsilon+
\varepsilon^2\int\phi\frac{(H_9-H_3H_6)^2}{1+\varepsilon H_6},\\
\int\phi(H_9-H_3H_6)^2
&=18^2\,7!+90^2\,5!+120^2\,3!=2691360,\\
I_3(f_\varepsilon)
&\le6-\frac{720}{7500}+
\frac{2691360}{7500(7500-104)}
=\frac{1375776}{231125}<6.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13cs.23}
$$

Using $h(f_\varepsilon)\le\frac12\log(2\pi e)$, compact approximation and (M.6.13cs.4) proves (M.6.13cs.6). $\square$

**Retained mixed flags and unrestricted mixed-reference scope.** For finitely many fixed packet profiles and scales with constants $C_i$ and deficits $\delta_i=k_i h^{2r}(1+o(1))$, $k_i>0$, mix with fixed probabilities $\alpha_i$ and an orthogonally retained neutral flag. The supported discriminator and asymmetry direct-sum decompositions of Theorem M.6.13cq make $\delta$ and $\mathcal A$ affine. Their exact renormalized limit is

$$
\sum_i\alpha_i C_i+
\frac1{2r}\left[\log\left(\sum_i\alpha_i k_i\right)
-\sum_i\alpha_i\log k_i\right]
\ge\min_i C_i.
\tag{M.6.13cs.24}
$$

The nonnegative term is Jensen's logarithmic gap. Thus these flags do not improve the best constituent packet constant.

If a zero-quality, zero-cost branch has weight $w$, a packet of deficit $d$ and cost $A$ instead gives

$$
\delta_{\mathrm{mix}}=w+(1-w)d,\qquad A_{\mathrm{mix}}=(1-w)A.
\tag{M.6.13cs.25}
$$

A fixed positive $w$ prevents $q\to1$. For $w=cd+o(d)$, fixed $c\ge0$, the renormalized constant becomes $C_r(f)+(2r)^{-1}\log(1+c)$, so an $O(d)$ flag need not preserve the constant; preservation holds for $w=o(d)$. For any $w\to0$, its extra logarithmic term is nonnegative because

$$
\log\delta_{\mathrm{mix}}-(1-w)\log d\ge0.
\tag{M.6.13cs.26}
$$

Consequently no vanishing zero-quality flag lowers the constituent packet's limiting constant, although some make its renormalized cost diverge.

Unflagged mixed references do not have this affine decomposition. No argument here proves that they cannot improve the packet constant. A lower bound matching $C_{\mathrm{packet},r}$, compactness for arbitrary optimizing pure sequences, a continuum operator principle for genuinely mixed references, exact interior discriminator curves and the sharp unrestricted additive constant remain open. These statements neither change the original apparatus contract nor promote a discriminator witness to an all-input measurement realization.

<a id="theorem-m613ct-uniform-pinching-entropy-resolvents-and-a-rational-logarithmic-grid"></a>**Theorem M.6.13ct (Uniform Pinching-Entropy Resolvents and a Rational Logarithmic Grid).** Let $\mathscr H$ be finite dimensional, let $P_1,\ldots,P_L$ be orthogonal projections summing to $I$, and put $\mathcal E(X)=\sum_{a=1}^L P_aXP_a$. Multiplicities of the projections are arbitrary. For a density matrix $\sigma$ set $\tau=\mathcal E(\sigma)$ and
$$
\mathcal A(\sigma)=D(\sigma\Vert\tau)=S(\tau)-S(\sigma),\qquad
F_t(X)=X+X^*-tX^*X-\mathcal E(XX^*),\qquad
g_\sigma(t)=\sup_X\operatorname{Tr}\sigma F_t(X),\quad t>0.
\tag{M.6.13ct.1}
$$
The auxiliary $X$ is an arbitrary complex operator. It need not be Hermitian. The supremum is attained within
$$
\|X\|\le\frac{\sqrt L}{2\sqrt t},\qquad
0\le g_\sigma(t)-\frac1{1+t},\qquad
g_\sigma(t)\le\min\{L,t^{-1}\}.
\tag{M.6.13ct.2}
$$
For faithful $\sigma$ the unique optimizer solves $\tau X+tX\sigma=\sigma$, and
$$
\mathcal A(\sigma)=\int_0^\infty\left(g_\sigma(t)-\frac1{1+t}\right)dt.
\tag{M.6.13ct.3}
$$
Choose the exact rational constants
$$
\delta=\frac{6931471805599453}{10^{16}},\qquad
\eta=10^{-16},\qquad E_0=\frac3{10^{11}},\qquad
 t_j=2^j\quad(-30\le j\le21),
$$
$$
 c=\delta\sum_{j=-30}^{21}\frac{t_j}{1+t_j}+E_0,\qquad
 \mathcal A_{\mathrm{grid}}(\sigma)
 =\delta\sum_{j=-30}^{21}t_jg_\sigma(t_j)-c.
\tag{M.6.13ct.4}
$$
There are $52$ independent auxiliaries. For every finite $L$ and arbitrary chosen operators $X_j$,
$$
 \operatorname{Tr}\sigma\left[\delta\sum_{j=-30}^{21}t_jF_{t_j}(X_j)-cI\right]
 \le\mathcal A_{\mathrm{grid}}(\sigma)\le\mathcal A(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13ct.5}
$$
If $L\le512$, there is also the uniform two-sided estimate
$$
 \mathcal A_{\mathrm{grid}}(\sigma)\le\mathcal A(\sigma)
 <\mathcal A_{\mathrm{grid}}(\sigma)+\frac{662}{10^9}.
\tag{M.6.13ct.6}
$$
These statements hold for singular states and every finite neutral multiplicity. The two-sided error in (M.6.13ct.6) uses the stated charge count; the one-sided trial inequality (M.6.13ct.5) does not bound that count.

**Part I. Resolvent representation and the operator-norm bound.** Pinching gives $\sigma\le L\tau$: apply Cauchy–Schwarz to $\sum_a\sigma^{1/2}P_av$ for every $v$. Initially assume $\sigma>0$. On Hilbert–Schmidt space put $\Delta=L_\tau R_\sigma^{-1}$ and $\xi=\sigma^{1/2}$. Left and right multiplication commute, so $\Delta$ is positive and
$$
\langle\xi,\log\Delta\,\xi\rangle=-\mathcal A(\sigma).
$$
The scalar $\int$ for $-\log\lambda$ and the quadratic variational identity for $(\Delta+t)^{-1}$, with $Y=X\sigma^{1/2}$, give
$$
\langle\xi,(\Delta+t)^{-1}\xi\rangle
=\max_X\left(2\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}\sigma X
-t\operatorname{Tr}\sigma X^*X-\operatorname{Tr}\tau XX^*\right)
=g_\sigma(t).
\tag{M.6.13ct.7}
$$
The last equality uses trace self-adjointness of $\mathcal E$. Differentiation gives the Sylvester equation above. Write $\sigma=\tau^{1/2}C(t\sigma)^{1/2}$, where
$C=t^{-1/2}\tau^{-1/2}\sigma^{1/2}$ has norm at most $\sqrt{L/t}$. For $H,D>0$ the solution of $HX+XD=H^{1/2}CD^{1/2}$ is
$$
 X=\int_0^\infty e^{-uH}H^{1/2}CD^{1/2}e^{-uD}\,du.
$$
Cauchy–Schwarz on its matrix coefficients gives $\|X\|\le\|C\|/2$, because each squared-norm $\int$ is $1/2$ times the squared norm of its vector. This proves the cap in (M.6.13ct.2).

The spectral measure $\mu$ of $\Delta$ in the unit vector $\xi$ has total mass one and
$$
\int\lambda\,d\mu=1,\qquad
\int\lambda^{-1}\,d\mu=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma\tau^{-1}\sigma\le L,
\qquad g_\sigma(t)=\int\frac{d\mu(\lambda)}{\lambda+t}.
\tag{M.6.13ct.8}
$$
Jensen's inequality and positivity prove the other bounds in (M.6.13ct.2). Integration proves (M.6.13ct.3). Also $0\le\mathcal A\le\log L$, by $\sigma\le L\tau$ and operator monotonicity of the logarithm. No spectral interval for $\Delta$ is asserted by the pinching inequality.

**Part II. Logarithmic-grid aliasing and tails.** For $h>0$ define
$$
 f_\sigma(u)=e^u\left(g_\sigma(e^u)-\frac1{1+e^u}\right),\qquad
 q_h=e^{-2\pi^2/h},\qquad E_h=\frac{8\pi q_h}{(1-q_h)^2}.
\tag{M.6.13ct.9}
$$
Writing $\ell(u)=e^u/(1+e^u)$ gives

$$
f_\sigma(u)=\int[\ell(u-\log\lambda)-\ell(u)]\,d\mu(\lambda).
$$

With Fourier convention $\widehat f(\omega)=\int e^{-i\omega u}f(u)\,du$, the substitution $x=e^u$ gives
$$
\int e^{-i\omega u}\ell'(u)\,du
=\int_0^\infty\frac{x^{-i\omega}}{(1+x)^2}\,dx
=\Gamma(1-i\omega)\Gamma(1+i\omega)
=\frac{\pi\omega}{\sinh(\pi\omega)}.
$$
Taking the difference of the translates and dividing by $i\omega$ therefore gives
$$
\widehat f_\lambda(\omega)
=\frac{\pi(e^{-i\omega\log\lambda}-1)}{i\sinh(\pi\omega)},\qquad
|\widehat f_\sigma(\omega)|\le\frac{2\pi}{|\sinh(\pi\omega)|}.
\tag{M.6.13ct.10}
$$
The value at zero is $-\log\lambda$. For faithful finite matrices the measure has finite positive support. Exponential decay of these functions and their derivatives justifies periodization, whose absolutely convergent Fourier series gives
$$
\left|h\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}f_\sigma(jh)-\mathcal A(\sigma)\right|
\le4\pi\sum_{k\ge1}\frac1{\sinh(2\pi^2k/h)}
\le\frac{8\pi q_h}{(1-q_h)(1-q_h^2)}\le E_h.
\tag{M.6.13ct.11}
$$
Only the total mass of $\mu$ is used for this aliasing bound. Equation (M.6.13ct.2) also gives the pointwise bounds
$0\le f_\sigma(u)\le\min\{Le^u,e^{-u}\}$. Thus, for integers $m,n\ge0$,
$$
 T_{h,m,n}-E_h\le\mathcal A\le T_{h,m,n}+E_h+R_{h,m,n},
$$
$$
 T_{h,m,n}=h\sum_{j=-m}^{n}f_\sigma(jh),\qquad
 R_{h,m,n}=\frac{h[Le^{-(m+1)h}+e^{-(n+1)h}]}{1-e^{-h}}.
\tag{M.6.13ct.12}
$$
The omitted node sum is nonnegative, which establishes the lower inequality without using $L$ or a tail bound.

**Part III. Rational constants and rounding direction.** The following finite rational estimates fix all constants. If
$$
 a_{40}=2\sum_{k=0}^{39}\frac{3^{-(2k+1)}}{2k+1},
$$
then $a_{40}<\log2<a_{40}+2\,3^{-81}/[81(1-1/9)]$, and these two rational endpoints lie strictly between $\delta$ and $\delta+\eta$. For $A_N(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}(-1)^kz^{2k+1}/(2k+1)$, the alternating-series enclosure between $A_N(z)$ and $A_N(z)+(-1)^Nz^{2N+1}/(2N+1)$, applied to
$\pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)$ with $N=40,12$, gives $157/50<\pi<22/7$. Finally
$$
 \sum_{k=0}^{100}\frac{(24649/875)^k}{k!}>10^{12},\qquad
 \frac{2(157/50)^2}{7/10}=\frac{24649}{875}.
$$
At $h=\log2$ these imply $q_h<10^{-12}$ and
$$
 E_h<\frac{8(22/7)10^{-12}}{(1-10^{-12})^2}<E_0.
\tag{M.6.13ct.13}
$$
Since $\delta<h$ and $f_\sigma\ge0$, the truncated $\delta$-weighted sum minus $E_0$ is a lower bound for $\mathcal A$. This is (M.6.13ct.5). For $L\le512$, the two geometric tails in (M.6.13ct.12), with $m=30,n=21$, are bounded by $h2^{-20}$. Moreover
$$
0\le(h-\delta)\sum_{j=-30}^{21}f_\sigma(jh)
\le\frac\eta\delta\,[9(\delta+\eta)+E_0].
$$
Consequently the complete error is smaller than the explicit rational number
$$
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{grid}}
 =2E_0+(\delta+\eta)2^{-20}
 +\frac\eta\delta\,[9(\delta+\eta)+E_0]
 <\frac{662}{10^9}.
\tag{M.6.13ct.14}
$$
The weight of $g_\sigma(t_j)$ is $\delta t_j$. The baseline is subtracted at every node. At an invariant state $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{grid}}=-E_0$; replacing this value by zero is not part of the formula.

**Part IV. Singular states and one-sided operator certificates.** On a fixed finite carrier of dimension $d$, use $\sigma_\epsilon=(1-\epsilon)\sigma+\epsilon I/d$. Entropy is continuous on that carrier. At each positive node the common compact cap in (M.6.13ct.2) makes the maximum continuous in the state: the objective is linear with a uniform finite bound on that ball. For any unrestricted fixed $X$, pass its faithful inequality below the ball maximum to the limit; taking its supremum proves that the singular unrestricted supremum equals the ball maximum. Thus (M.6.13ct.6) follows by taking $\epsilon\downarrow0$ on each fixed finite carrier, with the same numerical error in every dimension. The one-sided trial inequality also follows directly by holding its finitely many chosen $X_j$ fixed during this limit.

If a self-adjoint reward $W$ and chosen auxiliaries satisfy the operator inequality
$$
 W-\delta\sum_{j=-30}^{21}t_jF_{t_j}(X_j)\le uI,
\tag{M.6.13ct.15}
$$
then $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma W-\mathcal A(\sigma)\le u+c$ on every representation where that inequality holds. Uniform validity over a class of representations permits taking its state and representation suprema. This implication needs no interchange of an auxiliary infimum with either supremum. It supplies a certificate format; a fixed numerical trial or a sampled representation alone supplies no universal operator inequality. $\square$

<a id="proposition-m613cu-an-exact-non-hermitian-affine-entropy-certificate"></a>**Proposition M.6.13cu (An Exact Non-Hermitian Affine Entropy Certificate).** Let $Q$ have any finite real spectrum, with full spectral pinching $\mathcal E$, and let $[Q,U]=U$, $[Q,V]=V$. Neutral multiplicities are arbitrary. Define
$$
 T=U^*+V,\qquad P=T^*T=UU^*+V^*V+UV+V^*U^*,\qquad
 R=\mathcal E(TT^*)=U^*U+VV^*,
$$
$$
 x_0=12\log2-8>0,\qquad y_0=6-8\log2>0,\qquad s_0=x_0+y_0=4\log2-2.
\tag{M.6.13cu.1}
$$
For $0<\lambda\le1$ put
$$
 W_\lambda=\frac{\lambda s_0}{\sqrt2}(T+T^*)
 -\frac{\lambda x_0}{2}P-\lambda y_0R.
\tag{M.6.13cu.2}
$$
For every state on this carrier,
$$
 \mathcal A(\sigma)\ge\operatorname{Tr}\sigma
 \left[W_\lambda+\lambda(1-\lambda)
 \left(\frac{x_0}{2}P+y_0R\right)\right].
\tag{M.6.13cu.3}
$$
In particular the supremum of $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma W_\lambda-\mathcal A(\sigma)$ over all these finite representations, operators and states is exactly zero. This assertion imposes neither an operator-norm cap nor a bound on the number of charge values.

**Proof.** In the notation of Theorem M.6.13ct choose
$$
 a_t=\frac1{1+t},\qquad b_t=\frac{\sqrt2\lambda}{(1+t)(1+2t)},\qquad X_t=a_tI+b_tT.
$$
Pinching kills $T$ and the charge-two terms of $TT^*$. Direct expansion gives
$$
 F_t(X_t)-a_tI=\frac{b_t}{1+t}(T+T^*)-b_t^2(tP+R).
\tag{M.6.13cu.4}
$$
The three integrals on $(0,\infty)$ are
$$
 \int\frac{dt}{(1+t)^2(1+2t)}=2\log2-1,\qquad
 4\int\frac{t\,dt}{(1+t)^2(1+2t)^2}=x_0,\qquad
 2\int\frac{dt}{(1+t)^2(1+2t)^2}=y_0.
\tag{M.6.13cu.5}
$$
For the latter two, the respective partial fractions are
$$
\frac{24}{2t+1}-\frac8{(2t+1)^2}-\frac{12}{t+1}-\frac4{(t+1)^2},
\qquad
-\frac{16}{2t+1}+\frac8{(2t+1)^2}+\frac8{t+1}+\frac2{(t+1)^2}.
$$
Every nonconstant coefficient in (M.6.13cu.4) is absolutely integrable. Integrating the variational inequality (M.6.13ct.7), with the scalar baseline subtracted pointwise, yields
$$
 \mathcal A(\sigma)\ge\operatorname{Tr}\sigma
 \left[\frac{\lambda s_0}{\sqrt2}(T+T^*)
 -\frac{\lambda^2x_0}{2}P-\lambda^2y_0R\right].
$$
Subtracting (M.6.13cu.2) gives the positive remainder in (M.6.13cu.3). A charge-invariant state with $U=V=0$ attains zero. Faithful approximation on each fixed carrier extends the integrated inequality to singular states, since its displayed right side is linear and continuous in the state. The divergent scalar baseline is never integrated separately.

There is also a finite-node version with rational quadrature constants. With the nodes, $\delta,E_0$ from Theorem M.6.13ct set
$$
 w_j=\delta t_j,\quad d_j=[(1+t_j)(1+2t_j)]^{-1},\quad
 X_j=(1+t_j)^{-1}I+\sqrt2d_jT,
$$
$$
 x=4\sum_jw_jt_jd_j^2,\quad y=2\sum_jw_jd_j^2,\quad
 J=\sum_j\frac{w_j}{(1+t_j)^2(1+2t_j)},\quad
 C_0=\sum_j\frac{w_j}{1+t_j}.
\tag{M.6.13cu.6}
$$
All sums run from $j=-30$ to $21$. The identity $x+y=2J$ holds termwise. For
$W=(x+y)(T+T^*)/\sqrt2-(x/2)P-yR$, summing (M.6.13cu.4) gives exactly
$$
 W-\sum_jw_jF_{t_j}(X_j)=-C_0I.
\tag{M.6.13cu.7}
$$
Since $c=C_0+E_0$, (M.6.13ct.5) gives the universal upper bound
$\operatorname{Tr}\sigma W-\mathcal A(\sigma)\le E_0$. This finite-node implication is valid at every finite charge count. It follows from an exact operator identity, rather than a fitted coefficient table. $\square$

<a id="proposition-m613cv-centered-schur-lift-certificates-and-exact-word-basis-extensions"></a>**Proposition M.6.13cv (Centered Schur-Lift Certificates and Exact Word-Basis Extensions).** Let $[Q,U]=U$, $[Q,V]=V$ on a finite carrier and let $\mathcal E$ be full charge pinching. Fix $x,y>0$, $z\ge0$, and define
$$
 s=x+y,\quad h=(x+z)/2,\quad k=(x-z)/2,\quad M^2=s^2/(4xy),
$$
$$
 W=\frac{s}{\sqrt2}(U+U^*+V+V^*)-h(UU^*+V^*V)
 -y(U^*U+VV^*)-k(UV+V^*U^*),\qquad
 g=M^2I-U^*U-VV^*.
\tag{M.6.13cv.1}
$$
Consider representations with $g\ge0$. Put $S=(U+V)/\sqrt2$, $D=(U-V)/\sqrt2$. Letters $s,S,d,D$ in the word lists below mean $S,S^*,D,D^*$, respectively. Charge of a word is its number of lowercase letters minus uppercase letters; pinching retains precisely its charge-zero part. Ordered words are retained without commuting their letters.

At each of the $52$ nodes of Theorem M.6.13ct set
$$
 \beta_j=\frac{\delta t_j}{(1+t_j)^2},\qquad a_j=t_j\beta_j,\qquad
 X_j=\frac{I+Y_j}{1+t_j},\qquad
 \mathcal T(Y)=Y+Y^*-\mathcal E(Y+Y^*).
$$
Exact expansion yields
$$
 \delta t_jF_{t_j}(X_j)-\frac{\delta t_j}{1+t_j}I
 =\beta_j\mathcal T(Y_j)-a_jY_j^*Y_j-\beta_j\mathcal E(Y_jY_j^*).
\tag{M.6.13cv.2}
$$
Here $Y_j$ may be any polynomial from a chosen finite word list $w=(w_1,\ldots,w_n)$. For real coefficient vectors $v_j$ and real symmetric matrices $C_j$, impose
$$
 G_j=\begin{pmatrix}C_j&v_j\\v_j^T&1\end{pmatrix}\ge0,\qquad
 Y_j=\sum_av_{ja}w_a,
$$
$$
 A(C)=\sum_{a,b}C_{ab}w_a^*w_b,\qquad
 B(C)=\mathcal E\left(\sum_{a,b}C_{ab}w_aw_b^*\right),
$$
$$
 H_{\mathrm{lift}}=\sum_j[\beta_j\mathcal T(Y_j)-a_jA(C_j)-\beta_jB(C_j)]-E_0I.
\tag{M.6.13cv.3}
$$
Let $b$ and $\ell$ be any finite word lists. If $Q_0,R_0$ are real PSD matrices and the complete ordered-word coefficient identity
$$
 \rho I-W+H_{\mathrm{lift}}
 =\sum_{a,b}(Q_0)_{ab}b_a^*b_b
 +\sum_{a,b}(R_0)_{ab}\ell_a^*g\ell_b
\tag{M.6.13cv.4}
$$
holds, then
$$
 \operatorname{Tr}\sigma W-\mathcal A(\sigma)\le\rho
\tag{M.6.13cv.5}
$$
for every state in every such finite representation, independently of charge count and neutral multiplicity.

**Proof and direction of the lift.** The Schur complement gives $C_j-v_jv_j^T\ge0$. A real PSD matrix factors as a sum of real outer products. Consequently $A(rr^T)=p^*p$ and $B(rr^T)=\mathcal E(pp^*)$ for $p=\sum_ar_aw_a$, so both maps preserve positivity. Therefore $H_{\mathrm{lift}}\le H(Y)$, where $H(Y)$ is the centered trial operator obtained by using $Y_j^*Y_j$ and $\mathcal E(Y_jY_j^*)$ in (M.6.13cv.3). Theorem M.6.13ct gives $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma H(Y)\le\mathcal A(\sigma)$ at every finite charge count. Factoring $Q_0$ and $R_0$ shows that the right side of (M.6.13cv.4) is a sum of $p^*p$ and $q^*gq$, hence is positive. Thus
$$
 \operatorname{Tr}\sigma W-\mathcal A(\sigma)
 \le\operatorname{Tr}\sigma[W-H(Y)]
 \le\operatorname{Tr}\sigma[W-H_{\mathrm{lift}}]\le\rho.
$$
The direction of $H_{\mathrm{lift}}\le H(Y)$ is essential.

**Explicit finite bases and a feasible anchor.** Let $w$ be all words in $s,S$ of lengths $0$ through $4$, including the empty word. It has $31$ entries. Let $\ell$ be the analogous list through degree $3$, of size $15$, and take
$$
 b=w\,\cup\,\{d\ell_a,D\ell_a:1\le a\le15\},\qquad |b|=61.
\tag{M.6.13cv.6}
$$
The $52$ Schur blocks have size $32$, and the two other Gram sizes are $61$ and $15$. Every ordered pair in each Gram expansion is included, with an off-diagonal coefficient contributing both ordered products; only equality of a word and its adjoint coefficient is used in compressing the self-adjoint polynomial identity. The constant coefficient of every $Y_j$ is free, so centering removes no polynomial trial of this degree.

For an explicit anchor set all $Y_j,C_j$ to zero, $R_0=0$, and $\rho=x+y+E_0$. Define
$$
 p_e=(S+S^*-D+D^*)/2-I,\quad p_1=S+D-I,\quad
 p_2=S^*-D^*-I,\quad p_f=(S^*-S+D+D^*)/2.
$$
Direct expansion gives
$$
 (x+y)I-W=xp_e^*p_e+\frac y2(p_1^*p_1+p_2^*p_2)+zp_f^*p_f.
\tag{M.6.13cv.7}
$$
The coefficient Gram of these four factors supplies $Q_0\ge0$ in the stated basis, proving feasibility of this anchor. It is a feasibility construction for (M.6.13cv.4), without an optimality assertion.

**Exact equilibration and extension.** At each node let $c_j$ be the unique positive power of $2$ satisfying $c_j^2\le a_j+\beta_j<4c_j^2$. The rational substitution
$$
 \widetilde v_j=c_jv_j,\qquad \widetilde C_j=c_j^2C_j,\qquad
 \widetilde G_j=\operatorname{diag}(c_jI,1)G_j\operatorname{diag}(c_jI,1)
\tag{M.6.13cv.8}
$$
is an invertible congruence, so preserves the PSD constraint exactly. The weights of $\mathcal T(\widetilde Y_j)$, $A(\widetilde C_j)$ and $B(\widetilde C_j)$ become $\beta_j/c_j$, $a_j/c_j^2$ and $\beta_j/c_j^2$, respectively; the last two sum to a number in $[1,4)$. This exact equivalence gives no convergence or condition-number bound.

Appending $s^5,S^5$ to both $w$ and $b$ changes their sizes to $33,63$ and the Schur size to $34$, while $\ell$ remains of size $15$. Include every new and mixed ordered pair, through degree $10$, in (M.6.13cv.4). The same factorization proof establishes sufficiency. Setting the appended vector coordinates and Gram rows and columns to zero embeds every old feasible identity; the congruence then embeds its equilibrated form. Enlarging these lists therefore preserves every old certificate, without proving strict improvement or completeness. A floating conic coefficient map or a solver status alone supplies neither the exact identity nor PSD of its proposed Gram data. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613cy-boundary-free-finite-window-covariance-and-entropy-compactness"></a>**Theorem M.6.13cy (Boundary-Free Finite-Window Covariance and Entropy Compactness).** Fix $d\ge1$, $M<\infty$, $m>0$ and $0\le K<\infty$. For each $j$ let $N_j\ge3$, $\eta_j=1/N_j\to0$, and let $F_{0,j},\ldots,F_{N_j,j}$ be positive operators of rank at most $d$. Their common feature space may depend on $j$ and have arbitrary finite dimension. Put
$$
\begin{aligned}
w_j&=\sum_{n=0}^{N_j}\operatorname{Tr}F_{n,j}>0,&
\Gamma_j&=w_j^{-1}\sum_{n=0}^{N_j}F_{n,j},&G_{n,j}&=F_{n,j}/(\eta_jw_j),\\
B_{n,j}&=(F_{n,j}+3F_{n-2,j})/8,&C_{n,j}&=(3F_{n-1,j}+F_{n-3,j})/8,\\
\delta_{n,j}&=\langle B_{n,j}-C_{n,j},(L_{B_{n,j}}+R_{C_{n,j}})^\dagger(B_{n,j}-C_{n,j})\rangle_{HS},&
e_j&=w_j^{-1}\sum_{n=3}^{N_j}\delta_{n,j}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13cy.1}
$$
Only complete four-site stencils inside the window enter. Assume at every site, including the endpoints,
$$
\operatorname{Tr}G_{n,j}\le M,\qquad\lambda_d(G_{n,j})\ge m,\qquad e_j\le K\eta_j^6.
\tag{M.6.13cy.2}
$$
Eigenvalues are decreasing and padded by zero, so each site has rank exactly $d$.

After a subsequence there is one isometry $U_j:\operatorname{span}_n\operatorname{ran}F_{n,j}\to\ell^2$ per window, independent of its site, such that the piecewise linear interpolation $G_j$ of $U_jG_{n,j}U_j^*$ at $x=n\eta_j$ converges uniformly on $[0,1]$ in trace norm to a positive trace-norm Lipschitz field $F$. At every point it has rank $d$, $\lambda_d(F(x))\ge m$ and $\operatorname{Tr}F(x)\le M$. Furthermore,
$$
U_j\Gamma_jU_j^*\to\Gamma=\int_0^1F(x)\,dx\quad\text{in trace norm},\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}\Gamma=1,\qquad S(\Gamma_j)\to S(\Gamma).
\tag{M.6.13cy.3}
$$
On $I=(0,1)$ define
$$
J_I(F)=\sup_Y\int_0^1\{-2\operatorname{Tr}(FY''')-\operatorname{Tr}(FY^2)\}\,dx,
\tag{M.6.13cy.4}
$$
using smooth compactly supported Hermitian tests in one finite-dimensional coordinate subspace of $\ell^2$. Then
$$
J_I(F)\le64\liminf_j e_j/\eta_j^6\le64K,\qquad \operatorname{rank}\Gamma=d+r\le2d.
\tag{M.6.13cy.5}
$$
For the original liminf choose a realizing subsequence first; another extracted subsequence uses its own liminf. Every subsequence has a further subsequence with these properties. Thus the whole family obeys
$$
\limsup_j S(\Gamma_j)\le\log(2d),\qquad \sum_{k>2d}\lambda_k(\Gamma_j)\to0.
\tag{M.6.13cy.6}
$$
There is a qualitative modulus $\omega_{d,M,m,K}(t)\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$, uniform over all such finite windows with $\eta\le t$, for which their finite normalized covariance satisfies $S(\Gamma)\le\log(2d)+\omega_{d,M,m,K}(t)$. This imposes no exterior-zero field or endpoint penalty and asserts no finite-window rank bound $2d$.

*Proof. I. Interior variation and endpoint-safe interpolation.* Suppress $j$ and set $A_n=F_n/w=\eta G_n$. Metric homogeneity gives $\delta_n(A)=\delta_n(F)/w$. The supported trace inequality (M.6.13cw.18), followed by scalar Cauchy--Schwarz, gives
$$
\sum_{n=3}^N\operatorname{Tr}(B_n^A+C_n^A)\le1,\qquad
\sum_{n=3}^N\|\nabla^3A_n\|_1\le8\sqrt e,\qquad
V:=\sum_{n=3}^N\|\nabla^3G_n\|_1\le8\sqrt e/\eta\le8\sqrt K\eta^2.
\tag{M.6.13cy.7}
$$
Each site has total binomial coefficient at most one; missing exterior stencils only reduce the sum. Here $\nabla^3z_n=z_n-3z_{n-1}+3z_{n-2}-z_{n-3}$.

For any Banach-valued sequence $z_0,\ldots,z_N$ with $\max\|z_n\|\le M_0$, the exact discrete Taylor formula is
$$
\begin{aligned}
R_n&=\sum_{k=3}^n\binom{n-k+2}{2}\nabla^3z_k,\\
Q_n&=z_n-R_n=z_0+n(z_1-z_0)+\binom n2(z_2-2z_1+z_0).
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13cy.8}
$$
The empty sums vanish. Thus $\max\|R_n\|\le N^2V/2$ and $\max\|R_n-R_{n-1}\|\le NV$. Set $k=\lfloor N/2\rfloor$ and $\theta=k/N\in[1/3,1/2]$. At $0,\theta,1$ the quadratic $q(t)=Q_{Nt}$ has norm at most $A=M_0+N^2V/2$. Its Lagrange polynomials are
$$
\ell_0(t)=\frac{(t-\theta)(t-1)}\theta,\qquad
\ell_1(t)=\frac{t(t-1)}{\theta(\theta-1)},\qquad
\ell_2(t)=\frac{t(t-\theta)}{1-\theta}.
\tag{M.6.13cy.9}
$$
Their derivative suprema are at most $4,9/2,3$, with sum below $12$. Hence $\|q'\|\le12A$, and
$$
\max_{1\le n\le N}\|z_n-z_{n-1}\|\le12M_0/N+7NV.
\tag{M.6.13cy.10}
$$
No initial value was assumed zero. Applied in trace class, this proves a common Lipschitz bound on the entire closed interval,
$$
L=12M+56\sqrt K.
\tag{M.6.13cy.11}
$$
Positivity and the trace bound pass through linear interpolation.

**II. Dimension-free spectral and entropy tails.** The cell-anchor argument (M.6.13cw.19) uses only differences internal to its cells. Apply it with (M.6.13cy.7), without zero padding. Partition the $M_s=N+1$ sites into at most $k$ cells of size at most $\ell=\lceil M_s/k\rceil$. Let $P$ contain each cell's first three site ranges, or every site of a shorter cell. Then $\operatorname{rank}P\le3dk$ and
$$
\operatorname{Tr}((I-P)\Gamma)\le8\binom\ell3\sqrt e\le\frac43\ell^3\sqrt e.
\tag{M.6.13cy.12}
$$
Indeed $g_n=\operatorname{Tr}((I-P)A_n)\ge0$ vanishes at the first three anchors. Formula (M.6.13cy.8) reconstructs it; summing gives the binomial coefficient. Distinct cell stencil sets are disjoint, and no outside value is used.

The eigenvalue-tail variational principle, with $k=\lfloor R/(3d)\rfloor$ as in (M.6.13cw.20), gives
$$
T_R:=\sum_{k>R}\lambda_k(\Gamma)\le\min(1,2304d^3M_s^3\sqrt e\,R^{-3}),\qquad R\ge6d.
\tag{M.6.13cy.13}
$$
For $R\ge dM_s$ the tail is zero. Without any site trace/gap assumption, the same estimate proves
$$
S(\Gamma)\le C+\log\{d[1+M_s e^{1/6}]\},
\tag{M.6.13cy.14}
$$
with one numerical $C$. Choose an integer $n_0\ge\max(6d,[2304d^3M_s^3\sqrt e]^{1/3},1)$ with $n_0\le C_0d(1+M_se^{1/6})$. Above it, $T_R\le(n_0/R)^3$. Group the spectrum into its first $n_0$ terms and dyadic shells of lengths $2^jn_0$. Each tail shell has mass at most $2^{-3j}$, whose entropy is bounded by mass times the logarithm of shell length divided by mass. The series of $2^{-3j}$ and $j2^{-3j}$ converge; bound the initial shell separately by $\log(2n_0)$ plus a numerical constant. This proves (M.6.13cy.14). At most three sites, or zero interior deficit, give rank at most $3d$ by the anchors and the same conclusion after enlarging $C$.

Under (M.6.13cy.2), $M_s\le2/\eta$ gives
$$
T_R\le\min(1,C_*R^{-3}),\quad C_*=18432d^3\sqrt K,\quad R\ge6d.
\tag{M.6.13cy.15}
$$
Averaging decreasing eigenvalues between $\lfloor k/2\rfloor+1$ and $k$ gives $\lambda_k\le C'k^{-4}$ for large $k$. Once that bound is below $e^{-1}$, monotonicity of $-t\log t$ gives
$$
\sup_j\sum_{k>R}-\lambda_k(\Gamma_j)\log\lambda_k(\Gamma_j)
\le C''R^{-3}(1+\log R)\to0.
\tag{M.6.13cy.16}
$$
These constants depend on fixed $d,K$ only. At $K=0$ the tail above $6d$ is zero, with no division by $K$.

**III. One ambient isometry, including endpoints.** Diagonalize each window covariance on the span of all site ranges, and send an ordered eigenbasis to the first coordinates of $\ell^2$. Use that single isometry throughout its window. Let $P_R$ be the first-$R$ coordinate projection and $Q_R=I-P_R$. The exact trapezoidal identity is
$$
\int_0^1G_j(x)\,dx=\Gamma_j-\frac{\eta_j}{2}(G_{0,j}+G_{N_j,j}).
\tag{M.6.13cy.17}
$$
The correction is positive with trace at most $M\eta_j$. The nonnegative $L$-Lipschitz function $g_{R,j}(x)=\operatorname{Tr}(Q_RG_j(x))$ has $\int$ $a_{R,j}\le C_*R^{-3}$. Averaging over an interval of length $r$ containing a specified point gives $g(x)\le a/r+Lr$. Choose $r=\min(1,\sqrt{a/L})$, with immediate limiting cases at $a=0$ or $L=0$, to obtain
$$
\sup_{[0,1]}g\le2a+2\sqrt{La}.
\tag{M.6.13cy.18}
$$
This one-sided-safe bound treats both endpoints. For positive trace-class $A$, writing $A-PAP=(I-P)A+PA(I-P)$ and using Schatten Cauchy--Schwarz proves
$$
\|A-PAP\|_1\le2\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}A\,\operatorname{Tr}((I-P)A)}.
\tag{M.6.13cy.19}
$$
Hence $\sup_x\|G_j-P_RG_jP_R\|_1\le C R^{-3/4}\to0$. Each fixed-coordinate compression is bounded and equicontinuous. Arzelà--Ascoli, a diagonal subsequence and this tail approximation give uniform trace-norm convergence. Positivity, trace and Lipschitz bounds pass to the limit. A point differs from its nearest grid point by at most $L\eta_j$ in trace norm. Operator-norm eigenvalue continuity therefore gives rank exactly $d$ and the lower $d$th eigenvalue bound everywhere, including endpoints. Equation (M.6.13cy.17) gives covariance convergence and trace one. Ordered eigenvalues converge in $\ell^1$; the tails (M.6.13cy.16) and continuity of finitely many leading eigenvalues prove entropy convergence.

**IV. Interior variational action.** The exact supported Sylvester dual inequality is
$$
\delta_n(A)\ge2\operatorname{Tr}((B_n^A-C_n^A)X_n)-\operatorname{Tr}((B_n^A+C_n^A)X_n^2).
$$
It holds for ambient finite-rank Hermitian tests as well: outside the feature span there is no linear reward and only a nonnegative quadratic penalty. Set $X_n=\eta^3Y(n\eta)/8$. Then
$$
\frac e{\eta^6}\ge\frac1{64}\eta\sum_{n=3}^N
\left\{2\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\frac{\nabla^3G_n}{\eta^3}Y(n\eta)\right)-\operatorname{Tr}(W_nY(n\eta)^2)\right\},\quad
W_n=\frac{G_n+3G_{n-1}+3G_{n-2}+G_{n-3}}8.
\tag{M.6.13cy.20}
$$
The test and its first three mesh translates vanish near the window endpoints for small mesh. Summation by parts changes the linear sum to
$$
-2\eta\sum_{n=0}^N\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[G_n\frac{\Delta_\eta^3Y(n\eta)}{\eta^3}\right],\qquad
\Delta_\eta Y(x)=Y(x+\eta)-Y(x).
\tag{M.6.13cy.21}
$$
There is no endpoint term or exterior deficit. The divided test differences converge uniformly to $Y'''$, uniform field convergence permits Riemann summation, and $\|W_n-G_n\|_1\le3L\eta$. Taking the lower limit and then the supremum over tests proves the action bound. Extract a realizing subsequence first when the original family's liminf is intended.

**V. Interior action forces collective rank at most $2d$.** On the real Hilbert space of Hermitian Hilbert--Schmidt fields on $I$, put $\ell(Y)=-\int_I\operatorname{Tr}(FY''')$ and $q(Y)=\int_I\operatorname{Tr}(FY^2)$. Optimization in a real scalar gives
$$
|\ell(Y)|^2\le J_I(F)q(Y)\le J_I(F)M\|Y\|_{L^2(S_2)}^2.
\tag{M.6.13cy.22}
$$
The finite-coordinate smooth compactly supported tests are dense. Riesz gives the distributional derivative $F'''\in L^2(I;S_2)$. Three successive primitives differ from $F$ by a Hilbert-space-valued quadratic polynomial; hence $F\in H^3(I;S_2)$ without an endpoint extension or endpoint vanishing conditions.

The bounded form and (M.6.13cy.22) extend to all Hermitian $L^2$ fields. For $P=\operatorname{supp}F$, $Q=I-P$, choose $Y=QF'''Q$. Then $q(Y)=0$, so
$$
QF'''Q=0\quad\text{almost everywhere on }I.
\tag{M.6.13cy.23}
$$
On a compact interior interval the fixed positive spectral gap permits resolvent calculus, giving $P\in H^3$. The parallel-frame ODE $V'=[P',P]V$ supplies $V\in H^3$, $V^*V=I_d$, $V^*V'=0$ and $F=VMV^*$ with positive $M=V^*FV\in H^3$. This matrix field $M$ is distinct from the scalar trace bound. Put $B=V'$, $G=B^*B$, $C=QB'$, $K_0=BMB^*$ and $L_0=P+K_0$. The weak product rule in (M.6.13cy.23) yields
$$
CMB^*+BMC^*+2BM'B^*=0.
\tag{M.6.13cy.24}
$$
Its terms have continuous representatives. Since $V^*B=0$ and $B'=-VG+C$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
L_0&=[V,B]\begin{pmatrix}I_d&0\\0&M\end{pmatrix}[V,B]^*,\\
L_0'&=[V,B]\begin{pmatrix}0&I_d-GM\\I_d-MG&-M'\end{pmatrix}[V,B]^*.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13cy.25}
$$
On each compact interval the first middle matrix has a positive lower bound and the second is bounded. Thus $-cL_0\le L_0'\le cL_0$. Scalar Gronwall for each fixed ambient quadratic form makes its kernel, and hence its finite-dimensional range $S$, constant. Overlapping intervals give one $S$ on $I$, with
$$
S=\operatorname{ran}V(x)\oplus\operatorname{ran}B(x),\qquad\dim S=d+\operatorname{rank}B(x)\le2d.
\tag{M.6.13cy.26}
$$
The span of the ranges of $V$ is all of $S$: it is a closed subspace of fixed finite-dimensional $S$, and difference quotients put the columns of $V'$ in that span. Endpoint ranges lie in $S$ by continuity. The nonnegative continuous function $\langle v,F(x)v\rangle$ has zero $\int$ precisely when it vanishes on $I$. Consequently $\operatorname{ran}\Gamma=S$, proving the rank bound and $S(\Gamma)\le\log(2d)$. Trace-norm convergence gives the tail conclusion.

**VI. Whole-family statements, uniformity and mass normalization.** A subsequence violating either assertion in (M.6.13cy.6) has a further subsequence contradicting Parts III--V. Define $\omega(t)$ as the supremum of $\max(0,S(\Gamma)-\log(2d))$ over all finite windows satisfying the fixed hypotheses with $\eta\le t$, and zero for an empty class. The entropy tail makes it finite. If it did not vanish, nearly maximizing windows would contradict the whole-family conclusion. This gives no explicit rate.

A useful special case is uniform convergence of the $d$ nonzero eigenvalues of $F_{n,j}/(\eta_jw_j)$ to fixed positive numbers $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_d$ of sum one. It implies the hypotheses, for example with $M=2$ and $m=\mu_d/2$, and gives that exact spectrum in the limit. More generally, if $F_{n,j}/a_j$ has uniformly convergent positive eigenvalues $\nu_k$, let $\tau=\sum_k\nu_k>0$. Then
$$
\frac{\eta_jw_j}{a_j}=\eta_j\sum_n\operatorname{Tr}(F_{n,j}/a_j)\to\tau,\qquad\mu_k=\nu_k/\tau,
\tag{M.6.13cy.27}
$$
since $\eta_j(N_j+1)\to1$. For a physical interval of length $\ell_j=N_jh_j$, the normalized mesh is $h_j/\ell_j=1/N_j$, and the energy hypothesis is exactly $\sum\delta_n/w_j\le K(h_j/\ell_j)^6$. Absolute mass only needs to be positive; the required mass/gap information is normalized. Bounds only away from the window boundary cannot replace the all-site assumptions. The interior collective ceiling is $2d$; an endpoint-dependent improvement requires its own endpoint proof. The global entropy localization and scale conclusion are proved next. ∎

<a id="theorem-m613cz-qualitative-critical-scale-bootstrap-by-entropy-localization"></a>**Theorem M.6.13cz (Qualitative Critical-Scale Bootstrap by Entropy Localization).** Fix $d\ge1$, one normalized $f\in\mathcal P_3$ on $[a,b]$, and one $C^3$ density field $\rho(x)\succeq m_0I_d$ with a fixed $m_0>0$. For every nonempty sample set $Z_h=\sum_nf(nh)$, $p_n=f(nh)/Z_h$, prescribe the complete charge-diagonal block $p_n\rho(nh)$, and otherwise let the finite reference state $\sigma_h$ be arbitrary. Its feature dimension and global rank are unrestricted; all physical neutral directions and actual boundary blocks are retained. Write $\delta_h=1-q_{3,Q}(\sigma_h)$ for its actual spin-$3/2$ state deficit and $\mathcal A_h$ for its complete charge asymmetry.

Suppose $\delta_h\to0$. Then $h\to0$ automatically. With $\kappa_h=\delta_h/h^6$,
$$
\kappa_h\to\infty\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mathcal A_h+\frac16\log\delta_h\to+\infty.
\tag{M.6.13cz.1}
$$
Consequently, any such sequence with bounded-above renormalized cost has $\delta_h=O(h^6)$. This establishes the critical-scale hypothesis of Theorem M.6.13cw, Part IV, on these fixed-profile sequences. It gives no explicit coercivity rate or sharp lower constant, no varying-profile or increasing-multiplicity uniformity, and no identification of state quality with all-input apparatus error.

*Proof. I. Automatic mesh limit and boundary-free finite cells.* The positive samples form a consecutive block of $N_h$ sites. The exact third-variation inequality (M.6.13cw.16), followed by the trace, gives
$$
\sum_n|\nabla^3p_n|\le8\sqrt{\delta_h}.
$$
Start a discrete interpolation cell three zero sites before that positive block and include all its positive sites. The first three scalar values vanish. Discrete quadratic summation, with the reconstruction coefficient bounded by $\binom{N_h+3}{3}$, yields
$$
1\le\binom{N_h+3}{3}\sum_n|\nabla^3p_n|
\le8\binom{N_h+3}{3}\sqrt{\delta_h}.
\tag{M.6.13cz.2}
$$
The differences here are subsets of the actual full-state differences, including its actual exterior-zero boundary blocks. Thus every nonempty finite sample has strictly positive deficit. As it tends to zero, $N_h\to\infty$; since $N_h\le(b-a)/h+1$, necessarily $h\to0$. Positivity and the logarithms require no extra assumption.

Factor the actual full state as in (M.6.13cw.1), with feature matrices $F_n=A_nA_n^*$ of trace $p_n$ and rank at most $d$. Its covariance $\Gamma_h=\sum_nF_n$ has the same nonzero spectrum as $\sigma_h$. In a consecutive cell $I$ of $s$ sites define
$$
m_I=\sum_{n\in I}\operatorname{Tr}F_n>0,\qquad
\Gamma_I=m_I^{-1}\sum_{n\in I}F_n,\qquad
\Delta_I=\sum_{\{n,n-1,n-2,n-3\}\subset I}\delta_n.
\tag{M.6.13cz.3}
$$
For $s\le3$ take $\Delta_I=0$. Each site's total stencil coefficient is at most one. Metric and scalar Cauchy--Schwarz therefore give
$$
\sum_{\text{interior}}\|\nabla^3F_n\|_1\le8\sqrt{m_I\Delta_I}.
\tag{M.6.13cz.4}
$$
The cell-anchor proof and entropy estimate (M.6.13cy.12)--(M.6.13cy.14) apply without any exterior-zero penalty, absolute lower mass bound or eigenvalue gap. With one numerical constant $C$,
$$
S(\Gamma_I)\le C+\log\{d[1+s(\Delta_I/m_I)^{1/6}]\}.
\tag{M.6.13cz.5}
$$
At $s\le3$ or zero interior deficit the anchor rank bound $3d$ gives the same inequality. All cell entropies belong to their original common feature space before using any local isometry.

**II. Mesoscopic cells and their energy densities.** Consider a sequence $\kappa_h\to\infty$, and put $\nu_h=\kappa_h^{1/6}$. Then $\nu_h\to\infty$ and $h\nu_h=\delta_h^{1/6}\to0$. Fix $L\ge1$, independently of $h$, and partition the positive sites into cells of
$$
s_h=\left\lfloor L/\delta_h^{1/6}\right\rfloor
\tag{M.6.13cz.6}
$$
sites, with a possibly shorter final cell. One has $s_h\to\infty$, but each full cell's physical diameter is at most $s_hh\le L/\nu_h\to0$. If $k_h=\lceil N_h/s_h\rceil$, then $N_hh\to b-a$ and $s_h\delta_h^{1/6}\to L$, so
$$
k_hL/\nu_h\to b-a,\qquad
\log k_h=\log\nu_h-\log L+\log(b-a)+o_L(1).
\tag{M.6.13cz.7}
$$
Every limit first holds for this fixed $L$. Define $m_i,\Gamma_i,\Delta_i$ by (M.6.13cz.3) and $t_i=\Delta_i/(\delta_hm_i)$. The disjoint complete-stencil sets and nonnegativity of omitted actual blocks imply
$$
\sum_i m_i=1,\qquad \sum_i m_it_i=\delta_h^{-1}\sum_i\Delta_i\le1,
\qquad S(\Gamma_i)\le C_d+\log(1+Lt_i^{1/6}).
\tag{M.6.13cz.8}
$$
The state and its deficit are unchanged; only nonnegative interior subsets are used for this budget. The bound includes endpoint and short cells.

**III. Uniform entropy of good cells.** Choose an endpoint-strip width $\alpha>0$ so that the $f$-mass of $[a,a+\alpha]\cup[b-\alpha,b]$ is below $1/8$. A cell is good if it is full, lies in $[a+\alpha,b-\alpha]$, and $t_i\le4$. All others are exceptional. By (M.6.13cz.8), cells with $t_i>4$ have mass at most $1/4$. Cells failing the interior condition are contained in the fixed endpoint strips enlarged by at most one cell width at each inner boundary. That added physical width tends to zero, and normalized native Riemann sums converge; their eventual mass is below $1/4$. The short last cell is in the right endpoint strip for small $h$. Thus the union of exceptional cells has mass
$$
e_h\le1/2.
\tag{M.6.13cz.9}
$$
The choice of $\alpha$ is independent of $L$.

Rescale a good cell's $s_h$ sites to $[0,1]$, including both endpoints. Its mesh is exactly $\epsilon_h=1/(s_h-1)$, not $1/s_h$, and
$$
\frac{\Delta_i/m_i}{\epsilon_h^6}
=t_i\delta_h(s_h-1)^6\le4L^6.
\tag{M.6.13cz.10}
$$
The nonzero eigenvalues of its normalized site density $F_n/(\epsilon_hm_i)$ are
$$
\frac{(s_h-1)f(nh)}{\sum_{\text{cell}}f(lh)}\operatorname{spec}\rho(nh).
\tag{M.6.13cz.11}
$$
On the fixed positive interior interval, uniform continuity and a positive lower bound of $f$ make the scalar factor tend uniformly to one as the cell diameter shrinks. The factor $(s_h-1)/s_h$ also tends to one. Hence all its sites, including first and last, have a uniform upper trace bound, for example two, and a positive $d$th eigenvalue bound fixed by $\rho\succeq m_0I_d$. Along convergent cell centers their full $d$-spectra converge uniformly to those of $\rho$ at the limiting center.

Theorem M.6.13cy applies with common $d,M,m$ and energy constant $4L^6$. Its uniform conclusion therefore gives
$$
\sup_{i\,\mathrm{good}}S(\Gamma_i)\le\log(2d)+o_L(1).
\tag{M.6.13cz.12}
$$
Equivalently, a violating sequence of good cells has convergent centers and satisfies the same local hypotheses, contradicting that theorem. Its feature isometries need not agree between cells: entropy is invariant under each, while the mixture identity below is applied to the original covariances. The ceiling here is the boundary-free $2d$, with no endpoint-dependent strengthening assumed.

**IV. Entropy of the mixture and the coercive gain.** In the original common feature space the exact identity is $\Gamma_h=\sum_i m_i\Gamma_i$. The finite-mixture inequality gives
$$
S(\Gamma_h)\le H((m_i))+\sum_i m_iS(\Gamma_i),\qquad H((m_i))\le\log k_h.
\tag{M.6.13cz.13}
$$
It requires no orthogonality or commutation: $\Gamma_h\succeq m_i\Gamma_i$ and logarithm monotonicity on supports, with regularization if necessary, give $S(\Gamma_h)\le-\sum_i m_i\operatorname{Tr}[\Gamma_i\log(m_i\Gamma_i)]$.

For $t\ge0$ and $L\ge1$,
$$
\log(1+Lt^{1/6})\le\log(1+L)+\tfrac16\log(1+t).
$$
Weighted Jensen on the exceptional cells, using their energy budget, yields
$$
\sum_{i\,\mathrm{exceptional}}m_i\log(1+t_i)
\le e_h\log(1+1/e_h)\le\log2,
\tag{M.6.13cz.14}
$$
with value zero at $e_h=0$. Thus arbitrarily small masses and large individual $t_i$ leave no unbounded term. Combining (M.6.13cz.8), (M.6.13cz.12), and $\log(1+L)\le\log L+\log2$ gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_i m_iS(\Gamma_i)\le{}&e_h\log L+e_h(C_d+\log2)\\
&+(1-e_h)\log(2d)+(\log2)/6+o_L(1)\\
\le{}&e_h\log L+C'_d+o_L(1),
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13cz.15}
$$
where $C'_d$ is independent of $L$, $h$ and the actual states. Equations (M.6.13cz.7), (M.6.13cz.9), and (M.6.13cz.13) imply, for every fixed $L\ge1$,
$$
\limsup_{h\to0}\{S(\Gamma_h)-\log\nu_h\}\le C_{f,d}-\tfrac12\log L.
\tag{M.6.13cz.16}
$$
The constant is independent of $L$. For any requested negative threshold, first choose a finite $L$ making the right side smaller, then choose the mesh small enough for this fixed $L$. Hence
$$
S(\sigma_h)-\log\nu_h=S(\Gamma_h)-\log\nu_h\to-\infty.
\tag{M.6.13cz.17}
$$
No mesh-dependent diagonal choice $L_h\to\infty$ or convergence modulus uniform over unbounded local energies has been used.

**V. Exact complete-state entropy identity and conclusion.** The prescribed complete diagonal gives
$$
\mathcal A_h=H(p_h)+\sum_np_nS(\rho(nh))-S(\sigma_h).
\tag{M.6.13cz.18}
$$
The fixed native Riemann limits and $\log(1/h)+(1/6)\log\delta_h=\log\nu_h$ imply
$$
\mathcal A_h+\tfrac16\log\delta_h
=h(f)+\int_a^bf(x)S(\rho(x))\,dx+\log\nu_h-S(\Gamma_h)+o(1).
\tag{M.6.13cz.19}
$$
The constants are finite and fixed. Equation (M.6.13cz.17) proves (M.6.13cz.1). If a sequence of bounded-above renormalized cost had unbounded $\kappa_h$, extract a subsequence tending to infinity and obtain a contradiction. Therefore $\kappa_h$ is bounded and $\delta_h=O(h^6)$.

This is a qualitative theorem for one fixed profile, fixed finite multiplicity and one fixed uniformly faithful density field. Mere finite-mesh full rank with a gap tending to zero does not meet its hypothesis. It gives neither an exact finite-mesh rank bound, weak-profile recovery, equality with an optimized continuum functional, global physical optimum, operational quality identification nor a physical source/heat certificate. The matrices, physical neutral factors and actual boundary deficit have remained intact throughout. ∎

<a id="theorem-m613dc-attained-finite-system-dual-and-sharp-weighted-observable-bound"></a>**Theorem M.6.13dc (Attained Finite-System Dual and Sharp Weighted Observable Bound).** In the complete finite measurement class of Theorem M.6.13g, let $Q_S,A=A^*$ be fixed and let every system input be tested. Reference charges have arbitrary finite real spectra and multiplicities. All reference factors, correlations, flags and pointers belong to the reference. Write
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)=S(\mathcal G_Q\sigma)-S(\sigma),\qquad
K_\sigma(B)=\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma)(B-A\otimes I)^2],
$$
where $B=B^*$ commutes with $Q_S+Q_R$. Define
$$
F(r)=\inf_{K_\sigma(B)\preceq rI}\mathcal A_Q(\sigma),\qquad
b(Z)=\inf_{R,Q_R,\sigma,B}\{\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)+\operatorname{Tr}(ZK_\sigma(B))\},
\quad Z\succeq0.
\tag{M.6.13dc.1}
$$
For every $r>0$, the system-side dual is attained:
$$
F(r)=\max_{Z\succeq0}\{b(Z)-r\operatorname{Tr}Z\}.
\tag{M.6.13dc.2}
$$
If one finite strict model has $K_s\preceq r_sI$, $r_s<r$, and asymmetry $a_s$, a maximizing multiplier can be chosen with
$$
\operatorname{Tr}Z\le a_s/(r-r_s).
\tag{M.6.13dc.3}
$$
This is a compact system-side multiplier bound; all finite reference dimensions and multiplicities remain in the inner infimum.

*Proof and weighted refinement.*

##### I. Complete observable class, flags and strict feasibility

Every measurement gives $B=U^*(I\otimes M)U$. Conversely, if $B=\sum_jb_j\Pi_j$ is invariant, append a pure neutral pointer with a distinct label for each eigenvalue and cyclic shift $V$. The unitary $\sum_j\Pi_j\otimes V^j$ conserves charge. Compressing its first two pointer moments to readiness gives $B,B^2$. Thus it reproduces the entire noise matrix and adds zero ready asymmetry, with the pointer retained and counted. This is the spectral construction in the proof of Theorem M.6.13h, applicable to every finite system dimension.

For a retained direct-sum flag,
$$
\sigma'=\bigoplus_jp_j\sigma_j,\qquad B'=\bigoplus_jB_j,
\quad K_{\sigma'}(B')=\sum_jp_jK_{\sigma_j}(B_j),\quad
\mathcal A(\sigma')=\sum_jp_j\mathcal A(\sigma_j).
\tag{M.6.13dc.4}
$$
Both entropy expressions contain the same Shannon flag entropy, even when charge values coincide across branches. Every flag vector remains present.

Strict finite models exist at each positive error by the explicit finite common-reference construction (M.6.13bv.23)–(M.6.13bv.24): choose its finite $N$ so $C_A/\sqrt N<\sqrt r$ and append its counted spectral pointer. Its finite asymmetry is $d\log N$. If $C_A=0$, the target is invariant and its exact neutral measurement suffices. Hence the following proof uses an actual strict model, without assuming a minimizer of $F$.

##### II. Closure of finite response records and attained duality

Let $\mathscr C$ be the set of pairs $(L,c)\in\operatorname{Herm}(\mathcal H_S)\times\mathbb R$ for which one complete finite model has $K\preceq L$ and $\mathcal A\le c$. It is convex by (M.6.13dc.4) and upward closed. Take its closure only in this finite-dimensional response/cost space. This does not add an infinite reference state.

Put $\Delta=r-r_s>0$. If records approach $(rI,c)$, choose actual models with $K_n\preceq(r+\delta_n)I$, asymmetry at most $c+\delta_n$, and $\delta_n\downarrow0$. Mixing them with the strict model at weight $\delta_n/(\Delta+\delta_n)$ gives error at most $rI$ and cost tending to $c$. Thus closing the record set leaves $F(r)$ unchanged and places $(rI,F(r))$ in the closed set.

The value function $\phi(L)=\inf\{c:(L,c)\in\overline{\mathscr C}\}$ is convex, lower semicontinuous and bounded below by zero. It is finite on $\|L-rI\|<\Delta$, since such $L$ dominate $K_s$. It therefore has a finite subgradient at $rI$. Monotonicity makes that subgradient $-Z$ for $Z\succeq0$. Its inequality on each attainable $(K,a)$ is
$$
a\ge F(r)-\operatorname{Tr}[Z(K-rI)].
$$
Consequently $b(Z)-r\operatorname{Tr}Z\ge F(r)$. Evaluating $b(Z)$ on every feasible finite model gives weak duality in the other direction. This proves (M.6.13dc.2). The strict model gives
$$
b(Z)-r\operatorname{Tr}Z\le a_s-\Delta\operatorname{Tr}Z.
$$
Since $F(r)\ge0$, a maximizing $Z$ has (M.6.13dc.3); at a zero-cost boundary $Z=0$ also suffices. Independently, $b$ is an infimum of continuous affine functions and is upper semicontinuous, so this compact restriction verifies dual attainment.

##### III. Exact noncommutative partition representation

For invariant $B$ put
$$
V_Z(B)=\operatorname{Tr}_S[(Z\otimes I)(B-A\otimes I)^2]\succeq0.
$$
An eigenbasis of $Z$ expresses this partial trace as a sum of positive Hermitian compressions; no commuting-factor assumption is needed. Then $\operatorname{Tr}ZK_\sigma(B)=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma V_Z(B)$. For faithful invariant normalized $\tau$,
$$
D(\sigma\Vert\tau)=\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)+D(\mathcal G_Q\sigma\Vert\tau),\qquad
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)=\inf_{\substack{\tau>0,\ \operatorname{Tr}\tau=1\\[\tau,Q_R]=0}}D(\sigma\Vert\tau).
$$
The second identity follows by approximating $\mathcal G_Q\sigma$ on any missing support with a positive scalar density. The finite Gibbs variational identity, obtained by taking relative entropy against $e^{\log\tau-V_Z}/\operatorname{Tr}e^{\log\tau-V_Z}$, now gives
$$
b(Z)=-\log\sup_{\substack{R,Q_R,B\ \mathrm{finite}\\B=B^*,\ [B,Q_S+Q_R]=0\\\tau>0,\ [\tau,Q_R]=0,\ \operatorname{Tr}\tau=1}}
\operatorname{Tr}e^{\log\tau-V_Z(B)}.
\tag{M.6.13dc.5}
$$
Only joint infima have been interchanged. The supremum is at most one because both terms minimized before the Gibbs identity are nonnegative. It is at least $e^{-\operatorname{Tr}(ZA^2)}>0$, using $B=0$ and a one-dimensional reference. Hence $b$ is finite. A uniform partition bound $\operatorname{Tr}e^{\log\tau-V_Z(B)}\le e^{-\beta}$ proves $F(r)\ge\beta-r\operatorname{Tr}Z$. Evaluating a selected matrix size supplies no such uniform bound.

Equivalently write $Z=t\rho$, with $\rho$ a system density and $t\ge0$, and define
$$
c_\rho=\operatorname{Tr}\rho A^2,\qquad
W_{\rho,B}=\operatorname{Tr}_S[((\rho A+A\rho)\otimes I)B-(\rho\otimes I)B^2],
$$
$$
\Psi_\rho(t)=\sup_{R,Q_R,B,\tau}\log\operatorname{Tr}e^{\log\tau+tW_{\rho,B}}.
$$
The same finite invariant conditions as in (M.6.13dc.5) apply. Since $V_Z=t(c_\rho I-W_{\rho,B})$,
$$
F(r)=\max_{\substack{0\le t\le a_s/\Delta\\\rho\succeq0,\ \operatorname{Tr}\rho=1}}
\{t(c_\rho-r)-\Psi_\rho(t)\}.
\tag{M.6.13dc.6}
$$
At $t=0$ the density is immaterial.

##### IV. Interior finite-attainer conditions

Suppose $A$ does not commute with $Q_S$ and $0<r<r_0=d_Q(A)^2$. Theorem M.6.13g gives $F(r)>0$, while the invariant optimum in Theorem M.6.13f gives $F(r_0)=0$. Mixing their finite models yields
$$
F(r')\le\frac{r_0-r'}{r_0-r}F(r)<F(r),\qquad r<r'<r_0.
\tag{M.6.13dc.7}
$$
Every finite interior attainer therefore has $\|K\|=r$, and every optimal multiplier has positive trace.

Any such attainer is faithful on $E=\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal G_Q\sigma)$. Indeed, put $\tau=\mathcal G_Q\sigma>0$ on $E$. If $\sigma$ has a kernel there, $\sigma_\epsilon=(1-\epsilon)\sigma+\epsilon\tau$ obeys
$$
S(\sigma_\epsilon)-S(\sigma)=k\epsilon\log(1/\epsilon)+O(\epsilon),\qquad
k=\operatorname{Tr}(P_{\ker\sigma}\tau)>0.
$$
On the kernel the eigenvalues are $\epsilon\nu_j+O(\epsilon^2)$, $\nu_j>0$, while the positive eigenvalues change by $O(\epsilon)$; summing $-x\log x$ proves this formula. The twirl is unchanged. Keeping the finite device changes its noise by at most $C\epsilon I$, where $C=\|K_\tau-K_\sigma\|$. Mixing with the strict model at weight $C\epsilon/(\Delta+C\epsilon)$ restores $K\preceq rI$ and changes cost only by $O(\epsilon)$. The strictly larger entropy gain contradicts optimality. Pure neutral ready factors are allowed: this is faithfulness on $E$.

Compress $B$ to $\mathcal H_S\otimes E$. The first moment is unchanged and the discarded second-moment excursion is positive. At an optimum its cost is unchanged and its error remains $r$ by (M.6.13dc.7). For an optimal $Z$ it then satisfies
$$
\operatorname{Tr}[Z(rI-K)]=0,\qquad
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)+\operatorname{Tr}ZK=b(Z),
$$
$$
\sigma=\frac{e^{\log\tau-V_Z(B)}}{\operatorname{Tr}e^{\log\tau-V_Z(B)}},\qquad
\tau=\mathcal G_Q\sigma,\qquad
\log\operatorname{Tr}e^{\log\tau-V_Z(B)}=-b(Z).
\tag{M.6.13dc.8}
$$
These follow from equality in weak duality and the finite Gibbs identity, retaining the full matrix $\tau$. Variation in the invariant Hermitian $B$ gives the supported equation
$$
R_ZB+BR_Z=D_Z,\qquad
R_Z=\mathcal G_{\rm tot}(Z\otimes\sigma),\quad
D_Z=\mathcal G_{\rm tot}((ZA+AZ)\otimes\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13dc.9}
$$
Singular $R_Z$ is treated on its support with its permissible null directions. These stationarity conditions become a global certificate only when accompanied by the uniform partition bound and matching primal value in Part III.

##### V. Full spin-one multiplier, including its dark weight

For $Q_S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2)$ and $A=X=J_x$, use
$$
e=(|0\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2,\quad m=|1\rangle,\quad
f=(|0\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2.
$$
A maximizing multiplier in (M.6.13dc.2) may be chosen
$$
Z=x|e\rangle\langle e|+y|m\rangle\langle m|+z|f\rangle\langle f|,
\qquad x,y,z\ge0.
\tag{M.6.13dc.10}
$$
To prove this, average over system parity $P=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)$ and reflection $J|0\rangle=|2\rangle$, $J|1\rangle=|1\rangle$. Parity reverses $X$ and is accompanied by pointer-sign reversal. Reflection takes $Q_S$ to $2I-Q_S$, preserves $X$, and is accompanied by reference-charge reversal. Both transform the full finite class without changing asymmetry, so $b(gZg^*)=b(Z)$. Concavity of $b$ shows averaging cannot decrease the dual objective. The three displayed vectors have distinct characters under the two commuting symmetries, proving (M.6.13dc.10).

If $t=\operatorname{Tr}Z>0$, write
$$
\rho_{\gamma,\lambda}=\gamma(1-\lambda)|e\rangle\langle e|
+\gamma\lambda|m\rangle\langle m|+(1-\gamma)|f\rangle\langle f|,
\quad 0\le\gamma,\lambda\le1.
$$
Then $\operatorname{Tr}\rho A^2=\gamma$ and $\{\rho,A\}=\gamma A$. Equation (M.6.13dc.6) reduces to maximizing $t(\gamma-r)-\Psi_{\rho_{\gamma,\lambda}}(t)$. Since $B=0$ gives $\Psi\ge0$ and $F(r)>0$ for $0<r<1$, an optimal density has $\gamma>r$, or dark weight $1-\gamma<1-r$. A strict dark-noise slack of a particular finite attainer forces $z=0$ by complementary slackness. At a general fixed positive error the dark weight remains part of the optimization. Positive multipliers approximate every boundary multiplier: $b(Z+\epsilon I)\ge b(Z)$, while evaluating at any fixed finite near-minimizer for $b(Z)$ gives $\limsup_{\epsilon\downarrow0}b(Z+\epsilon I)\le b(Z)$. Thus the same dual value is the supremum over $x,y,z>0$, even when a maximizing multiplier lies on a face.

##### VI. Sharp uniform norm for every nonnegative dark weight

Now fix $x,y>0$, $z\ge0$, $s=x+y$, and a faithful finite reference state. At center charge $q$, put
$$
E_q=\begin{pmatrix}\sigma_{q+1,q+1}&\sigma_{q+1,q-1}\\
\sigma_{q-1,q+1}&\sigma_{q-1,q-1}\end{pmatrix},\quad
V_q=\begin{pmatrix}\sigma_{q+1,q}\\\sigma_{q-1,q}\end{pmatrix},
$$
$$
P_q=\operatorname{diag}(I_{q+1},-I_{q-1}),\quad
H_q=\frac x2E_q+\frac z2P_qE_qP_q,\qquad D_q=y\sigma_{q,q}.
$$
Absent endpoint spaces are omitted. The odd minimizing total-charge block is $\begin{pmatrix}0&T_q\\T_q^*&0\end{pmatrix}$, with
$$
H_qT_q+T_qD_q=\frac{s}{\sqrt2}V_q.
\tag{M.6.13dc.11}
$$
This follows by expanding the weighted square, as in (M.6.13bt.8), now retaining the third multiplier weight. Both $H_q$ and $D_q$ are positive definite, including $z=0$. Parity oddification removes a nonnegative even contribution. The unique weighted minimizing odd observable satisfies the sharp dimension-uniform bound
$$
\|B\|\le M(x,y):=\frac{x+y}{2\sqrt{xy}}.
\tag{M.6.13dc.12}
$$
Indeed positivity of the principal state block gives $V_q\sigma_{q,q}^{-1}V_q^*\preceq E_q$. Thus $V_q=H_q^{1/2}C_qD_q^{1/2}$ with $\|C_q\|\le\sqrt{2/(xy)}$. For positive $H,D$, the solution of $HY+YD=H^{1/2}CD^{1/2}$ is
$$
Y=\int_0^\infty e^{-uH}H^{1/2}CD^{1/2}e^{-uD}\,du.
$$
For unit vectors $v,w$, Cauchy–Schwarz in $u$ and $\int_0^\infty He^{-2uH}du=I/2$ give $|v^*Yw|\le\|C\|/2$. Applying the coefficient $s/\sqrt2$ in (M.6.13dc.11) proves (M.6.13dc.12) on every block and hence on their direct sum.

For sharpness use scalar charges $0,1,2$ and
$$
\psi=(\sqrt{p/2},\sqrt a,\sqrt{p/2}),\qquad
p=\frac{2y}{x+2y},\qquad a=\frac{x}{x+2y}.
$$
At center charge one, $E=p|+\rangle\langle+|$, $V=\sqrt{pa}|+\rangle$,
$H=(xp/2)|+\rangle\langle+|+(zp/2)|-\rangle\langle-|$, and $D=ya=xp/2$. Therefore the solution has norm $s/(2\sqrt{xy})$. Each charge population is positive, so every finite Sylvester sum remains invertible, including at $z=0$. The faithful states
$$
\sigma_\epsilon=(1-\epsilon)|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|
+\epsilon\operatorname{diag}(p/2,a,p/2)
$$
have the same diagonal, and their solutions converge to this norm. Thus the constant is sharp already for three scalar charges.

Finally, finite-dimensional faithful approximation leaves the joint infimum $b(Z)$ unchanged: for any fixed finite $(\sigma,B)$ replace $\sigma$ by a faithful mixture; its entropy and noise converge, and minimizing the weighted observable only improves the value. Hence restricting this inner dual infimum to $\|B\|\le M(x,y)$ is exact. This bounds the solved weighted observable, not an inverse Sylvester norm or a reference eigenvalue floor. It does not replace every primal-feasible device by a norm-capped device at the same error. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613dd-exact-gap-two-window-identities-and-uniform-charge-length-remainders"></a>**Theorem M.6.13dd (Exact Gap-Two Window Identities and Uniform Charge-Length Remainders).** Use the complete spin-one apparatus class and the multiplier $Z=x|e\rangle\langle e|+y|m\rangle\langle m|+z|f\rangle\langle f|$ of Theorem M.6.13dc, with $x,y>0$, $z\ge0$. Put
$$
s=x+y,\qquad h=(x+z)/2,\qquad
M^2=\frac{s^2}{4xy},\qquad C(Z)=s-b(Z).
$$
Let $b_L(Z)$ be the same joint cost-plus-weighted-noise infimum restricted to one charge ladder of length at most $L$, retaining all finite neutral multiplicities, and set $C_L=s-b_L$. For every $L\ge2$,
$$
0\le C(Z)-C_L(Z)\le R_L(Z)
:=\min\{D_*(Z)/L,\ \gamma_LD_{\rm sine}(Z)\},
\tag{M.6.13dd.1}
$$
where
$$
D_0=(s+z)\frac{s^2}{4xy},\qquad
\gamma_L=\frac{L-1}{L+1}\tan^2\frac\pi{L+1},
$$
$$
\begin{array}{ll}
D_* =\min\{D_0,\ s\max(1,h/x,h/z)\},& z>0,\\
D_{\rm sine}=\min\{D_0,\ s\max(1,z/x,x/z)\},& z>0,
\end{array}
\qquad D_*=D_{\rm sine}=D_0\quad(z=0).
\tag{M.6.13dd.2}
$$
These estimates are uniform in the initial charge length, multiplicities, state spectrum and real charge offsets. The sine construction also gives the all-input primal approximation in Part IV below.

*Proof.*

##### I. Integer components and exact random cuts

Oddification uses the system parity $P=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)$ as in (M.6.13cd.P3); the norm cannot increase. An odd invariant observable has reference gaps only $\pm1$. Split an arbitrary real reference spectrum into connected components of its unit-adjacency graph and pinch the state onto them. Both $B$ and $B^2$ preserve these components, so the complete noise matrix is unchanged. The pinching commutes with full charge dephasing and cannot increase asymmetry. Retain the component labels and subtract each irrelevant charge offset. Each component is a contiguous finite integer ladder with arbitrary multiplicities. For the scalar weighted infimum, its normalized blocks have cost and weighted noise averaging to the total, so a single component suffices. For a primal operator inequality, keep every component.

On one ladder, for $a=0,\ldots,L-1$ partition charges into intervals $[a+jL,a+(j+1)L)\cap\mathbb Z$. Write $\mathcal E_a$ for the corresponding pinching and set
$$
\sigma_a=\mathcal E_a\sigma,\qquad B_a=(\operatorname{id}_S\otimes\mathcal E_a)B.
$$
The diagonal reference blocks are unchanged and pinching increases entropy, whence $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_a)\le\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)$. Decompose
$$
B^2=D+O,\qquad D=\mathcal G_{Q_R}(B^2).
$$
In system-charge blocks $D$ is diagonal and $O$ has only the $0$-to-$2$ and $2$-to-$0$ entries. Thus $D\succeq0$ and $D\pm O\succeq0$, since reference conjugation by $e^{i\pi Q_R/2}$ reverses $O$ and preserves $D$.

A gap-one edge and its return path survive $L-1$ cuts. A gap-two path crosses two distinct successive boundaries and survives $L-2$ cuts. This includes matrix-valued edges and finite endpoints, so
$$
\frac1L\sum_aB_a=(1-1/L)B,\qquad
\frac1L\sum_aB_a^2=(1-1/L)D+(1-2/L)O.
\tag{M.6.13dd.3}
$$
Since $B_a,B_a^2$ are block diagonal for $\mathcal E_a$, their moments with $\sigma_a$ equal those with $\sigma$. Expanding the full noise square gives
$$
\frac1L\sum_aK_{\sigma_a}(B_a)
=K_\sigma(B)+\frac1L\mathbb E_\sigma(\{X,B\}-D-2O),
\quad \mathbb E_\sigma(T)=\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma)T].
\tag{M.6.13dd.4}
$$
The correction is a matrix and need not be positive.

Choose the weighted-optimal $B$ for a faithful state. Put
$$
q=\operatorname{Tr}[(Z\otimes\sigma)B^2],\quad
d=\operatorname{Tr}[(Z\otimes\sigma)D],\quad
\ell=\operatorname{Tr}[(Z\otimes\sigma)\{X,B\}].
$$
Scalar-rescaling stationarity gives $\ell=2q$. The weighted noise is $w_Z=s-q\ge0$, so $0\le q\le s$. Pairing (M.6.13dd.4) with $Z$ then yields the exact identity
$$
\frac1L\sum_aw_Z(\sigma_a,B_a)=w_Z(\sigma,B)+d/L.
\tag{M.6.13dd.5}
$$
In the original system charge basis, $Z_{\rm diag}=\operatorname{diag}(h,y,h)$, and
$d=\operatorname{Tr}[(Z_{\rm diag}\otimes\sigma)B^2]$. Theorem M.6.13dc gives $d\le M^2\operatorname{Tr}Z_{\rm diag}=D_0$. For $z>0$, the operator inequality $Z_{\rm diag}\preceq\max(1,h/x,h/z)Z$ gives $d\le s\max(1,h/x,h/z)$. Hence $d\le D_*$.

Split every pinched interval into its normalized nonzero block. Its charge length is at most $L$, and both weighted noise and asymmetry average over these blocks by (M.6.13dc.4). Each block is a competitor for $b_L$. Thus
$$
b_L\le\frac1L\sum_a[\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_a)+w_Z(\sigma_a,B_a)]
\le\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)+w_Z(\sigma,B)+D_*/L.
$$
Taking the faithful infimum, which equals $b$ by Theorem M.6.13dc, proves $b\le b_L\le b+D_*/L$.

##### II. Covariant sine windows and their exact positive correction

Put
$$
\theta=\frac\pi{L+1},\quad c=\cos\theta,\quad
f_j=\sqrt{\frac2{L+1}}\sin(j\theta)\ (1\le j\le L),\quad f_j=0\ \text{otherwise},\quad
\beta=f_1^2=\frac{2\sin^2\theta}{L+1}.
\tag{M.6.13dd.6}
$$
For every integer $a$, let $F_a=f(Q_R-a)$ and let $P_a$ project onto charges $a+1,\ldots,a+L$. Only finitely many windows are nonzero on a finite reference and $\sum_aF_a^2=I$. Set
$$
p_a=\operatorname{Tr}(F_a\sigma F_a),\quad
\sigma_a=F_a\sigma F_a/p_a,\quad
B_a=P_aBP_a/c,
\tag{M.6.13dd.7}
$$
omitting zero-weight branches and retaining the neutral flag $a$. Products are taken on the original spaces before restriction to $P_a$.

The channel $\Phi(\sigma)=\bigoplus_aF_a\sigma F_a$ is CPTP and commutes with charge dephasing. Relative-entropy monotonicity (Lindblad 1975) and the direct-sum entropy identity give
$$
\sum_ap_a\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_a)=\mathcal A_Q(\Phi\sigma)\le\mathcal A_Q(\sigma).
\tag{M.6.13dd.8}
$$
The retained flag's common Shannon term cancels.

The finite sine recurrence gives
$$
\sum_jf_j^2=1,\qquad \sum_jf_jf_{j+1}=c,\qquad
\sum_jf_jf_{j+2}=\cos(2\theta)+\beta.
\tag{M.6.13dd.9}
$$
For a return along an adjacent edge, the sole excluded window has the initial charge at the appropriate endpoint, with squared weight $\beta$. For a gap-two path, inclusion of both endpoints includes the intermediate charge. Therefore, with $C_a=P_aBP_a$,
$$
\sum_aF_aC_aF_a=cB,\qquad
\sum_aF_aC_a^2F_a=(1-\beta)D+[\cos(2\theta)+\beta]O.
\tag{M.6.13dd.10}
$$
Scaling by $1/c$ restores the original first moment. Since
$\cos(2\theta)=2c^2-1$ and $(\sin^2\theta-\beta)/c^2=\gamma_L$, the complete noise identity is
$$
\overline K:=\sum_ap_aK_{\sigma_a}(B_a)
=K_\sigma(B)+\gamma_L\mathbb E_\sigma(D-O).
\tag{M.6.13dd.11}
$$
Let $W=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,-1)$ on the system. Direct block conjugation gives $D-O=WB^2W^*\succeq0$. Identity (M.6.13dd.11) holds for every odd invariant $B$ and every state, without stationarity.

##### III. Sine dual remainder and universal lower certificates

For a weighted-optimal $B$, (M.6.13dc.12) gives $D-O\preceq M^2I$. Pairing (M.6.13dd.11) with $Z$ increases weighted noise by at most $\gamma_LD_0$, while (M.6.13dd.8) decreases averaged cost. For $z>0$, $W^*ZW$ has weights $(z,y,x)$ in the $(e,m,f)$ basis, so
$$
\operatorname{Tr}[(Z\otimes\sigma)(D-O)]
=\operatorname{Tr}[(W^*ZW\otimes\sigma)B^2]
\le s\max(1,z/x,x/z).
$$
Selecting a normalized branch for this scalar objective and taking the faithful infimum gives the sine term in (M.6.13dd.1). Combining it with Part I proves the full statement. In particular $\gamma_L\sim\pi^2/L^2$; the exact finite formula is used in (M.6.13dd.1). At $L=2$, $c=1/2$ and $\gamma_2=1$. The excluded $L=1$ would have $c=0$. The faces $x=0$ or $y=0$ are outside these uniform bounds; the face $z=0$ is included.

If $U_L(Z)\ge C_L(Z)$ is certified uniformly over all finite neutral multiplicities, weak duality yields
$$
F(r)\ge s-r(s+z)-U_L(Z)-R_L(Z).
\tag{M.6.13dd.12}
$$
This remains valid for $z=0$. A scalar-multiplicity numerical maximum is a lower bound on $C_L$, while (M.6.13dd.12) requires an upper bound uniform in multiplicity.

##### IV. Actual all-input relaxed-error approximation and dimensions

Start from any original finite device with $K\preceq rI$. Oddify, pinch into every unit-adjacency component, and apply the sine instrument separately to all components, retaining both component and window flags. The component pinching preserves $K$; it cannot increase asymmetry. In the completely positive conditional expectation seminorm, $B=(B-X)+X$ and $\|X\|=1$ imply
$$
\mathbb E_\sigma(B^2)\preceq(1+\sqrt r)^2I.
$$
This follows by the triangle inequality for each vector applied to $(B-X)(v\otimes\sigma^{1/2})$ and $X(v\otimes\sigma^{1/2})$. It is applied before splitting into normalized components. Averaging all exact corrections first gives
$$
\overline K\preceq[r+\gamma_L(1+\sqrt r)^2]I,
\qquad \mathcal A_{\rm new}\le\mathcal A_{\rm old}.
\tag{M.6.13dd.13}
$$
Translate each occupied branch to $\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$, retaining its orthogonal neutral label. The block-diagonal state and device preserve charge differences, the entire noise matrix and asymmetry.

If the original abstract reference dimension is $d$, each charge vector occurs in exactly $L$ translated supports, giving occupied flagged dimension $d'\le Ld$. An odd observable on system dimension three has off-diagonal parity blocks of sizes $2d'$ and $d'$, so at most $2d'+1$ distinct eigenvalues. One pure neutral spectral pointer therefore gives complete abstract reference dimension at most $d'(2d'+1)$ and occupied system-inclusive dimension at most $3d'(2d'+1)$. These are construction bounds with all flags included. The formal energy realization is supplied in Theorem M.6.13df. No uniform neutral multiplicity cutoff follows. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613de-singular-reference-minimax-norm-control-and-exact-error-charge-approximation"></a>**Theorem M.6.13de (Singular-Reference Minimax Norm Control and Exact-Error Charge Approximation).** Fix a finite $m$-dimensional system, a Hermitian target $A$, and one finite reference charge and state $(Q_R,\sigma)$, allowing singular $\sigma$. If an invariant Hermitian $B_0$ has $K_\sigma(B_0)\preceq rI$, then every $\eta>0$ admits an invariant Hermitian $B_\eta$ on the same reference and state such that
$$
K_\sigma(B_\eta)\preceq r(1+m\eta)I,\qquad
\|B_\eta\|\le\|A\|\sqrt{\frac{1+\eta}{\eta}}.
\tag{M.6.13de.1}
$$
There is no state eigenvalue floor in this bound. On the complete spin-one class, the sine windows of Theorem M.6.13dd can then be repaired to the exact original error, as quantified in Parts III–V below.

*Proof and construction.*

##### I. Minimax existence, including singular references

Minimize
$$
J_\eta(B)=\lambda_{\max}K_\sigma(B)+\eta\operatorname{Tr}K_\sigma(B)
=\max_{\rho\ \mathrm{state}}\operatorname{Tr}[(\rho+\eta I)K_\sigma(B)]
$$
over invariant Hermitian $B$. Write $\mathcal G_{\rm tot}$ for total-charge pinching and
$$
R_0=\mathcal G_{\rm tot}(I\otimes\sigma),\quad
R_Z=\mathcal G_{\rm tot}(Z\otimes\sigma),\quad
D_Z=\mathcal G_{\rm tot}((ZA+AZ)\otimes\sigma).
$$
Direct expansion gives
$$
\operatorname{Tr}ZK_\sigma(B)=\operatorname{Tr}(R_ZB^2)-\operatorname{Tr}(D_ZB)+\operatorname{Tr}(ZA^2).
\tag{M.6.13de.2}
$$
For $Z>0$, $\lambda_{\min}(Z)R_0\preceq R_Z\preceq\lambda_{\max}(Z)R_0$, so their supports agree. The kernel $\mathcal N$ of the quadratic seminorm $\operatorname{Tr}(R_0B^2)$ consists exactly of invariant Hermitian $C$ annihilating $\operatorname{supp}R_0$. Indeed
$$
\operatorname{Tr}[(I\otimes\sigma)C^2]=\operatorname{Tr}(R_0C^2)=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad C(I\otimes\sigma^{1/2})=0.
$$
