Thus adding $C\in\mathcal N$ changes none of the conditional second-moment or cross terms in the entire $K$. Pass to the finite-dimensional quotient by $\mathcal N$, where this seminorm is a norm. The Hilbert–Schmidt reverse triangle inequality gives
$$
\operatorname{Tr}K_\sigma(B)\ge
\left(\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}(R_0B^2)}-\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}A^2}\right)^2.
$$
Since $K\succeq0$, $J_\eta\ge\eta\operatorname{Tr}K$ is coercive on this quotient. It is continuous and convex, being a maximum of positive quadratic forms, and has a minimizer.

At a minimizer, zero belongs to the convex hull of the active gradients. To see this directly, if zero were outside that compact convex hull, a separating direction would decrease all active quadratics. Compactness of the family supplies a common sufficiently small step decreasing their maximum, a contradiction. The gradient is affine in $\rho$, so one density $\rho_*$ realizes this convex combination. With $Z=\rho_*+\eta I$, stationarity is
$$
R_ZB+BR_Z=D_Z.
\tag{M.6.13de.3}
$$
Put
$$
c=\|Z^{-1/2}(ZA+AZ)Z^{-1/2}\|
\le2\|A\|\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(Z)/\lambda_{\min}(Z)}.
$$
The order bounds $-cZ\preceq ZA+AZ\preceq cZ$, tensor positivity and pinching give $-cR_Z\preceq D_Z\preceq cR_Z$. Thus $D_Z$ has no matrix element touching $\ker R_Z$. The canonical supported solution is
$$
B_{\rm can}=\int_0^\infty e^{-tR_Z}D_Ze^{-tR_Z}\,dt
\quad\text{on }\operatorname{supp}R_Z,
\qquad B_{\rm can}=0\quad\text{on }\ker R_Z.
$$
Integrating the order bounds gives $-(c/2)P\preceq B_{\rm can}\preceq(c/2)P$. Every other solution of (M.6.13de.3) differs only by a $\ker R_Z$ block, hence by an element of $\mathcal N$, and has the same $K$. Therefore this canonical solution remains a minimizer. Since $\eta I\preceq Z\preceq(1+\eta)I$, its norm has the claimed bound. Finally
$$
\lambda_{\max}K_\sigma(B_{\rm can})\le J_\eta(B_{\rm can})
\le J_\eta(B_0)\le r(1+m\eta),
$$
proving (M.6.13de.1).

For spin one, oddify $B_\eta$ with $P=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)$. Its norm cannot increase, and the complete square expansion gives
$$
K_\sigma(B_o)=\tfrac12(K_\sigma(B_\eta)+PK_\sigma(B_\eta)P)
-\mathbb E_\sigma(B_e^2)\preceq r(1+3\eta)I.
\tag{M.6.13de.4}
$$
This supplies a primal approximate replacement on the same state; the weighted-dual cap in Theorem M.6.13dc has a different role.

##### II. Exact counted thirty-two-charge strict witness

Fix $r=1/16$. On scalar reference charges $q=0,\ldots,31$, take
$$
|\psi\rangle=\frac1{\sqrt{32}}\sum_{q=0}^{31}|q\rangle,\quad
S=\sum_{q=0}^{30}|q+1\rangle\langle q|,\quad U=V=S/\sqrt2,
$$
$$
B_s=\begin{pmatrix}0&U&0\\U^*&0&V\\0&V^*&0\end{pmatrix}.
$$
Each edge preserves $Q_S+Q_R$. Here
$$
\langle S\rangle=31/32,\quad\langle S^2\rangle=30/32,\quad
\langle S^*S\rangle=\langle SS^*\rangle=31/32.
$$
For example the end-sector off-diagonal entry of the noise is

$$
\langle S^2\rangle/2-\langle S\rangle+1/2=0;
$$

its diagonal entries follow from $B_s^2$ and $\{X,\mathbb E B_s\}$. Thus the full noise and cost are exactly
$$
K_s=\operatorname{diag}(1/64,1/32,1/64)\preceq r_sI,
\qquad r_s=1/32=r/2,\qquad \mathcal A_Q(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)=\log32.
\tag{M.6.13de.5}
$$
Also $\|B_s\|^2=\|U^*U+VV^*\|\le1$. A single neutral spectral pointer needs at most $65$ labels, giving complete abstract reference dimension at most $32\cdot65=2080$ and occupied system-inclusive dimension at most $6240$. The pointer is pure at readiness and contributes zero asymmetry; its carrier and output are retained.

##### III. Exact-error repair of sine localization

For $L\ge32$, use $c_L=\cos(\pi/(L+1))$ and $\gamma_L$ from Theorem M.6.13dd. Put
$$
d_L=\gamma_L(1+\sqrt r)^2=\frac{25}{16}\gamma_L,\qquad
w_L=\frac{d_L}{r-r_s+d_L}=\frac{50\gamma_L}{1+50\gamma_L}.
\tag{M.6.13de.6}
$$
For every original $r$-feasible apparatus of cost $a$, (M.6.13dd.13) gives a retained-flag apparatus on charges $0,\ldots,L-1$ with $K_{\rm loc}\preceq(r+d_L)I$ and cost at most $a$. Mix it with (M.6.13de.5) at retained branch weight $w_L$. Then
$$
K_{\rm mix}\preceq[(1-w_L)(r+d_L)+w_Lr_s]I=rI,
\qquad a_{\rm mix}\le(1-w_L)a+w_L\log32.
\tag{M.6.13de.7}
$$
Both branches fit the same charge range; coincident charges retain orthogonal neutral multiplicities.

Let $F_L(r)$ be the complete original infimum restricted only to charges in $\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$, still with every finite multiplicity and mixed state. Apply (M.6.13de.7) to an arbitrary minimizing sequence, without assuming attainment. Then
$$
F(r)\le F_L(r)\le(1-w_L)F(r)+w_L\log32,\qquad
0\le F_L(r)-F(r)\le w_L\log32=O(L^{-2}).
\tag{M.6.13de.8}
$$
This approximation uses the prescribed $r$, not an enlarged final error.

##### IV. Simultaneous charge-width and norm control

Apply Part I and oddification before localization. For $\eta>0$, set
$$
r_\eta=r(1+3\eta),\qquad M_\eta=\sqrt{(1+\eta)/\eta},
$$
$$
d_{L,\eta}=3r\eta+\gamma_L(1+\sqrt{r_\eta})^2,\qquad
w_{L,\eta}=\frac{d_{L,\eta}}{r-r_s+d_{L,\eta}},\qquad
N_{L,\eta}=M_\eta/c_L.
\tag{M.6.13de.9}
$$
The localized branches are $P_aB_oP_a/c_L$, so their norms are at most $N_{L,\eta}$. Their complete noise is at most $(r+d_{L,\eta})I$. Mixing once with the same strict witness gives
$$
K_{\rm final}\preceq rI,\quad
\mathcal A_{\rm final}\le(1-w_{L,\eta})a+w_{L,\eta}\log32,\quad
\operatorname{spec}Q_R\subseteq\{0,\ldots,L-1\},\quad
\|B_{\rm final}\|\le N_{L,\eta}.
\tag{M.6.13de.10}
$$
Here $L\ge32$, and $N_{L,\eta}>1$ also bounds the strict branch. If exact equality $\|K\|=r$ is prescribed, rescale the entire block-diagonal odd observable by $t\in[0,1]$. Its noise norm is continuous, at $t=1$ is at most $r$, and at $t=0$ equals $\|X^2\|=1>r$. The intermediate value keeps the state, charges and asymmetry unchanged and does not increase the norm.

Let $F_{L,N}(r)$ impose both the charge range and the observable norm cap in the equivalent invariant-observable class. Then
$$
F(r)\le F_{L,N_{L,\eta}}(r)
\le(1-w_{L,\eta})F(r)+w_{L,\eta}\log32.
\tag{M.6.13de.11}
$$
Choosing $\eta=\gamma_L$ gives $d_{L,\eta},w_{L,\eta}=O(L^{-2})$ and $N_{L,\eta}=O(L)$. No exchange over matrix multiplicities is used.

##### V. Complete carrier and energy-host accounting

Pinch arbitrary real charges into every unit-adjacency component, retain each component/window flag and translate its formal charge origin. These changes preserve all difference equations and the block-diagonal state's entire noise and asymmetry. They specify a new finite reference; they do not assert an unpriced alteration of installed hardware. The energy-labelled host in Theorem M.6.13df realizes that new reference.

If the starting abstract reference dimension, including every starting neutral factor, is $d$, localization has occupied dimension at most $Ld$. Adding the strict branch gives $D\le Ld+32$. A single appended neutral spectral pointer has at most $2D+1$ eigenvalue labels, hence complete abstract reference dimension
$$
D_R\le D(2D+1),\qquad D_{S,R}^{\rm occupied}\le3D(2D+1).
\tag{M.6.13de.12}
$$
Its pointer magnitude has the same bound $N_{L,\eta}$. Applying the binary energy host to this complete apparatus uses three system cells and $D_R$ reference cells. The full physical reference and system-inclusive Hilbert dimensions are $2^{D_R}$ and $2^{3+D_R}$, respectively, including all unused excitation sectors. Thus $2^{3+D(2D+1)}$ is a sufficient full-space upper bound. For the strict witness alone it is $2^{2083}$.

These bounds still depend on the original $d$. Arbitrary neutral multiplicity remains in $F_L$ and $F_{L,N}$; bounded width and bounded observable norm do not compactify that variable. The exact unrestricted positive-error value and its finite attainment classification remain separate from these approximation theorems. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613df-complete-binary-energy-rail-realization-of-finite-charge-measurements"></a>**Theorem M.6.13df (Complete Binary Energy-Rail Realization of Finite Charge Measurements).** Every explicitly specified finite conserving-unitary/Yanase-pointer model on system and complete reference dimensions $d_S,d_R$ has a finite two-state-cell host with a bounded-below physical bare-energy charge. It preserves the complete reference asymmetry and all-input noise exactly. The carrier family and its code-preserving controls below have the same at-most-error infimum $F(r)$ as the original finite model class. This formal energy-labelled realization uses the specified finite Hilbert and instrument branch, independently of the physical-spin family in Theorem M.6.13o.

*Proof and full source.*

##### I. Physical units, full carrier and source

Choose charge eigenbases, retaining every multiplicity, and list the real eigenvalues $q_i,r_a$ of $Q_S,Q_R$. All flags, pointers and reference auxiliaries are included in $d_R$ and $\sigma_R$. Fix $E_c>0$ in joules and offsets
$$
e_S\ge-E_c\min_iq_i,\qquad e_R\ge-E_c\min_ar_a.
$$
Install $d_S$ system cells and $d_R$ reference cells, each with basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$ and occupation $n$. Assign
$$
h_i^S=e_S+E_cq_i\ge0,\qquad h_a^R=e_R+E_cr_a\ge0,\qquad
H_0=\sum_ih_i^Sn_i^S+\sum_ah_a^Rn_a^R.
\tag{M.6.13df.1}
$$
The registered system and reference carriers each have exactly one excitation. Their isometries send $|i\rangle,|a\rangle$ to the corresponding occupied-cell vectors and obey
$$
V_S^*H_SV_S=e_SI+E_cQ_S,\qquad
V_R^*H_RV_R=e_RI+E_cQ_R.
\tag{M.6.13df.2}
$$
The full Hilbert dimension is $2^{d_S+d_R}$, while the occupied carrier dimension is $d_Sd_R$. Other excitation sectors remain present, counted and dynamically decoupled. Every system input in the fixed $d_S$-dimensional physical carrier is tested. Taking charge eigenbases is a specification of this source, not an unpriced laboratory basis-change operation.

Supply the actual mixed reference input $V_R\sigma_RV_R^*$, with no substituted pure-state ensemble or external purification. The compact closure of energy time translations has precisely the same eigenspace pinching on this sector, so
$$
\mathcal G_{H_R}(V_R\sigma_RV_R^*)
=V_R\mathcal G_{Q_R}(\sigma_R)V_R^*,\qquad
\mathcal A_{H_R}(V_R\sigma_RV_R^*)=\mathcal A_{Q_R}(\sigma_R).
\tag{M.6.13df.3}
$$
Offsets and nonzero scale preserve equality of charge eigenvalues; isometries preserve both nonzero spectra. The full reference dimension is $2^{d_R}$, with zero ready weight on the unused sectors. Preparing the supplied asymmetric state is the resource being measured, not a free preparation step.

##### II. Whole-unitary conserving control with drift retained

For the original conserving unitary $U$, put $V=V_S\otimes V_R$, $P=VV^*$ and
$$
U_{\rm phys}=VUV^*+(I-P).
$$
The projector commutes with $H_0$, and on $P$, $H_0=(e_S+e_R)I+E_c(Q_S+Q_R)$. Hence $[U_{\rm phys},H_0]=0$. For any $\tau>0$, choose on $[0,\tau]$
$$
g(t)=6t(\tau-t)/\tau^3,\qquad
\int_0^\tau g(t)dt=1,\qquad 0\le g\le3/(2\tau).
$$
On $P$ choose a Hermitian logarithm $L$ with
$$
e^{-iL}=e^{iH_0\tau/\hbar}U_{\rm phys},\qquad
\|L\|\le\pi,
$$
and extend $L$ by zero outside $P$. Functional calculus gives $[L,H_0]=0$. Then
$$
H(t)=H_0+\hbar g(t)L
\tag{M.6.13df.4}
$$
has exact endpoint $U_{\rm phys}$ on $P$; outside it retains the included native free evolution. The code is invariant throughout. The interaction peak and norm action satisfy
$$
\|H(t)-H_0\|\le\frac{3\pi\hbar}{2\tau},\qquad
\int_0^\tau\|H(t)-H_0\|dt\le\pi\hbar.
\tag{M.6.13df.5}
$$
The total Hamiltonian is bounded below by $-3\pi\hbar/(2\tau)$, or may be shifted by that fixed scalar. Its physical registered charge is the bare occupation energy $H_0$, not the complete interacting Hamiltonian or a stress tensor. Since $L$ and $H_0$ are conserved, cyclic switching work is exactly
$$
\int_0^\tau\operatorname{Tr}[\rho(t)\dot H(t)]dt
=\hbar\langle L\rangle[g(\tau)-g(0)]=0.
\tag{M.6.13df.6}
$$
This is an externally scheduled conserving source; every instantaneous interaction commutes with the registered charge. Its schedule, timing and switching apparatus have their own description and implementation account. It supplies no autonomous-clock, spatial-locality or zero-infrastructure-cost claim.

##### III. Explicit finite interaction alphabet and readout

For code configurations $x,y$ representing $|i,a\rangle,|j,b\rangle$, the code matrix unit is the product over every rail $\ell$ of $|x_\ell\rangle\langle y_\ell|$. A changed rail uses raising or lowering; an unchanged occupied rail uses $|1\rangle\langle1|$; an unchanged empty rail uses $|0\rangle\langle0|$. Thus the operator vanishes off its specified code configurations. Each nonzero off-diagonal coefficient of $L$ obeys
$$
q_i+r_a=q_j+r_b.
\tag{M.6.13df.7}
$$
Its Hermitian real and imaginary exchange terms therefore commute with $H_0$ on the full Hilbert space. Diagonal code projectors commute as well. There are at most $(d_Sd_R)^2$ real Hermitian coefficients, with a loose sum-of-absolute-coefficients bound $2(d_Sd_R)^2\pi$. These may be many-body controls, whose addressed support is part of the specification.

Alternatively perform ordinary two-level elimination in each fixed total-charge block. At most $D(D-1)/2$ rotations and $D$ phases, $D=d_Sd_R$, implement the finite unitary. Every rotation joins equal-energy code states and has the same finite conserving cell expression. Its assigned durations and actions add. No fixed-body or spatially local architecture is inferred.

Extend the original pointer by
$$
M_{\rm phys}=V_RMV_R^*
$$
on the reference code and zero outside. It commutes with $H_R$ and preserves the code. Its finite spectral instrument has the original calibrated outcome units. Set $A_{\rm phys}=V_SAV_S^*$. For every system density $\rho$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
&\operatorname{Tr}[(V_S\rho V_S^*\otimes V_R\sigma_RV_R^*)
(U_{\rm phys}^*(I\otimes M_{\rm phys})U_{\rm phys}-A_{\rm phys}\otimes I)^2]\\
&\qquad=\operatorname{Tr}[(\rho\otimes\sigma_R)
(U^*(I\otimes M)U-A\otimes I)^2].
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13df.8}
$$
The squared-noise cross terms are retained, proving equality of worst-case error on the registered carrier. Readout memory remains after the one-shot measurement. A later cyclic erasure requires its actual conditional entropy and heat under Definition 28. Any pure neutral pointer needed to dilate an invariant observable is included before $d_R$ cells are installed.

##### IV. Finite ledger and preservation of the original infimum

The source specifies every finite matrix coefficient, gap, basis label, pulse and calibration. Exact coefficient specification is the same ideal specification as for the original finite certificate; approximate hardware requires explicit errors. The reference stored-energy mean is $e_R+E_c\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_RQ_R)$, between the smallest and largest $h_a^R$ on the occupied sector; its full-register operator norm is $\sum_ah_a^R$. The analogous system energy belongs to the tested input. The complete supplied asymmetry is exactly (M.6.13df.3), including initial correlations; controls have (M.6.13df.5), or the accumulated block-rotation ledger. The full pointer, outcome labels and retained memory are counted.

Register before optimization the system rails, $E_c$, energies, response unit and target. Admit every finite reference rail list and source state on its specified one-excitation sector, and every finite control and pointer of the above code-preserving type. More explicitly, require joint-code invariance for the unitary, and $[M_{\rm phys},P_R]=0$ as well as $[M_{\rm phys},H_R]=0$, with $P_R=V_RV_R^*$. These conditions remain necessary when unused sectors share an energy.

Let $F_{\rm energy}(r)$ be the corresponding asymmetry infimum. Every original finite certificate is hosted with identical cost and error by Parts I–III. Conversely, compress any admitted host to its invariant registered sectors. Joint-code invariance makes the compressed interaction unitary. Reference-code invariance gives both $M_{\rm phys}V_R=V_RM$ and $M_{\rm phys}^2V_R=V_RM^2$. Thus compression preserves the square in (M.6.13df.8), not just its first moment. Subtract offsets and divide by $E_c$ to recover an original finite conserving model. Therefore
$$
F_{\rm energy}(r)=F(r).
\tag{M.6.13df.9}
$$
The same two directions transfer finite attainment or nonattainment for this registered host family. An energy-commuting pointer that mixes the code with an unused degenerate sector is outside this family.

For the spin-one branch take three system cells with energies $(0,E_c,2E_c)$ and transverse transition-amplitude target $X=J_x$ in a fixed response unit. This representation label does not identify an unspecified microscopic magnetic spin. The strict witness of (M.6.13de.5), including its $65$-label pointer, has $d_R\le2080$; the generic host has at most $2^{2083}$ full system-inclusive dimensions, retaining all unused sectors. For the three-charge, five-pointer-label model of Proposition M.6.13m, the complete reference dimension is $15$, so the generic host has $15+3$ cells, full dimension $2^{18}$ and occupied system-inclusive dimension $45$. Encoding the charged reference and neutral pointer in separate one-excitation factors instead uses $3+5$ reference cells and three system cells, giving full dimension $2^{11}$. The pointer rails have equal energies, and every original flag remains present. This factorwise construction uses the tensor product of the same isometries and retains both excitation constraints. The host supplies physical labels for each finite approximation without evaluating the unrestricted multi-charge optimum. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613da-global-relaxed-matrix-profile-lower-limit"></a>**Theorem M.6.13da (Global Relaxed Matrix-Profile Lower Limit).** Fix $d\ge1$, one normalized $f\in\mathcal P_3$ on $[a,b]$ and one $C^3$ density field $\rho(x)\succeq m_0I_d$ with fixed $m_0>0$, as in Theorem M.6.13cw. For $h_j\downarrow0$, let $\sigma_j$ be arbitrary complete finite states with diagonal charge blocks
$$
p_{n,j}\rho(nh_j),\qquad p_{n,j}=f(nh_j)/Z_{h_j},\qquad Z_h=\sum_nf(nh).
$$
All actual charge boundaries and neutral directions remain in these states. Their global ranks and feature dimensions are unrestricted. Assume the actual spin-$3/2$ state deficits satisfy $\delta_j=1-q_{3,Q}(\sigma_j)\le Kh_j^6$ for one fixed finite $K$.

After a subsequence and one isometric feature-space identification for each mesh, there is a positive trace-class field $F$ on $\mathbb R$, supported on $[a,b]$ and globally Lipschitz in trace norm, with
$$
\operatorname{Tr}F(x)=f(x),\qquad
\operatorname{spec}_{>0}F(x)=f(x)\operatorname{spec}\rho(x)\quad(a<x<b).
\tag{M.6.13da.1}
$$
Thus its interior rank is $d$, but its ranges and internal eigenvectors may vary with $x$. The normalized Gram interpolants converge uniformly in trace norm to $F$, and
$$
\Gamma_j\longrightarrow\Gamma:=\int_{\mathbb R}F(x)dx\quad\text{in trace norm},\qquad
S(\sigma_j)=S(\Gamma_j)\longrightarrow S(\Gamma)<\infty.
\tag{M.6.13da.2}
$$
For smooth compactly supported Hermitian test fields $Y$ supported in one finite coordinate subspace of $\ell^2$, define the full distributional action
$$
\mathcal J_{\rm ext}(F)=\sup_Y\int_{\mathbb R}
[-2\operatorname{Tr}(FY''')-\operatorname{Tr}(FY^2)]dx.
\tag{M.6.13da.3}
$$
Then
$$
0<I_3(f)\le\mathcal J_{\rm ext}(F)
\le64\liminf_j\frac{\delta_j}{h_j^6}.
\tag{M.6.13da.4}
$$
On a further subsequence $\delta_j/h_j^6\to\kappa\in(0,K]$, the exact cost limit and lower bound are
$$
\begin{aligned}
\lim_j\left[\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_j)-\frac16\log\frac1{\delta_j}\right]
&=h(f)+\int_a^bf(x)S(\rho(x))dx-S(\Gamma)+\frac16\log\kappa\\
&\ge h(f)+\int_a^bf(x)S(\rho(x))dx-S(\Gamma)
+\frac16\log\frac{\mathcal J_{\rm ext}(F)}{64}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13da.5}
$$
This is a lower limit on the enlarged class with prescribed pointwise eigenvalues. It does not substitute the particular orientation $f\rho$ for an arbitrary limit.

*Proof.*

##### I. Global zero-padded interpolation and fixed-scale bounds

Factor $\sigma_h=T_h^*T_h$, with charge-block columns $A_{n,h}$, and put $F_{n,h}=A_{n,h}A_{n,h}^*$, $G_{n,h}=F_{n,h}/h$. Zero padding outside occupied sites is the actual absence of physical charge blocks. By (M.6.13cw.16),
$$
V_h:=\sum_n\|\nabla^3G_{n,h}\|_1\le\frac{8\sqrt{\delta_h}}h
\le8\sqrt K\,h^2.
\tag{M.6.13da.6}
$$
Here $\nabla G_n=G_n-G_{n-1}$. The sequence and its differences vanish sufficiently far to the left, so
$$
\nabla^2G_n=\sum_{m\le n}\nabla^3G_m,\qquad
\nabla G_n=\sum_{m\le n}(n-m+1)\nabla^3G_m.
$$
The difference support has at most $M_h+3$ sites, where $M_h\le(b-a)/h+1$. On it,
$$
\|\nabla^2G_n\|_1\le V_h,\qquad
\|\nabla G_n\|_1\le(M_h+3)V_h\le Ch.
\tag{M.6.13da.7}
$$
Outside it the first difference is zero. Therefore the piecewise linear interpolant $G_h$ on the whole real line is uniformly trace-norm Lipschitz. It is positive, supported on $[a-h,b+h]$, and its trace interpolates $f(nh)/(hZ_h)$, uniformly converging to $f$. Its exact $\int$ is
$$
\int_{\mathbb R}G_h(x)dx=h\sum_nG_{n,h}=\Gamma_h=\sum_nF_{n,h}.
\tag{M.6.13da.8}
$$
The nonzero spectra of $\Gamma_h$ and $\sigma_h$ agree.

##### II. One feature identification and field tightness

Diagonalize $\Gamma_h$ on the span of all feature-Gram ranges, and map its ordered eigenbasis isometrically to the first coordinate vectors of $\ell^2$. This identification leaves the physical state and charge blocks unchanged. Let $P_N$ be the fixed first-$N$ projection and $Q_N=I-P_N$. Since $M_h^3\sqrt{\delta_h}$ is bounded, the finite spectral estimate (M.6.13cw.16) gives
$$
\int\operatorname{Tr}(Q_NG_h(x))dx
=\operatorname{Tr}(Q_N\Gamma_h)\le CN^{-3}
\tag{M.6.13da.9}
$$
for all sufficiently large $N$, uniformly in $h$.

The nonnegative scalar $g_{N,h}(x)=\operatorname{Tr}(Q_NG_h(x))$ has the same uniform Lipschitz bound as $G_h$. A nonnegative globally $L$-Lipschitz integrable function with maximum $u$ dominates its two triangular slopes of area $u^2/L$. Thus
$$
\sup_xg_{N,h}(x)\le\sqrt{L\int g_{N,h}}\le CN^{-3/2}.
$$
For any positive trace-class $A$ and projection $P$, Schatten Cauchy–Schwarz applied to $(I-P)A+PA(I-P)$ gives
$$
\|A-PAP\|_1\le2\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}A\,\operatorname{Tr}[(I-P)A]}.
$$
Consequently
$$
\sup_x\|G_h(x)-P_NG_h(x)P_N\|_1\le CN^{-3/4}.
\tag{M.6.13da.10}
$$
For each $N$, compressed fields have fixed finite matrix size, uniform bounds and equicontinuity on a common compact interval. Arzelà–Ascoli, a diagonal subsequence and (M.6.13da.10) give uniform trace-norm convergence to a positive globally Lipschitz $F$, zero outside $[a,b]$.

At a fixed $x$, choose a neighboring mesh point $x_h$, so $\|G_h(x)-G_h(x_h)\|_1\le Ch$. At that point the nonzero eigenvalues are
$f(x_h)\operatorname{spec}\rho(x_h)/(hZ_h)$, since $A_{n,h}^*A_{n,h}=p_n\rho(nh)$. Eigenvalue continuity and $hZ_h\to1$ prove (M.6.13da.1), including exact interior rank. Uniform convergence over common compact support proves covariance convergence. The $N^{-3}$ mass tail survives in the limit; (M.6.13cw.21) supplies a uniform $O(N^{-3}(1+\log N))$ entropy tail. Thus entropy converges as in (M.6.13da.2), independently of feature dimension.

##### III. Exact singular-metric variational lower limit

Use the actual finite feature matrices
$$
B_m=(F_m+3F_{m-2})/8,\qquad C_m=(3F_{m-1}+F_{m-3})/8,\qquad D_m=B_m-C_m.
$$
Their exact supported cross-Sylvester formula (M.6.13cw.4) has the quadratic dual inequality
$$
\delta_m\ge2\operatorname{Re}\langle D_m,X_m\rangle_{HS}
-\langle X_m,(L_{B_m}+R_{C_m})X_m\rangle_{HS}.
$$
It holds at singular supports. After embedding the feature space, finite-rank ambient tests remain allowed: orthogonal components give no linear reward and only a nonnegative quadratic penalty. Take $X_m=h^3Y(mh)/8$ for any test in (M.6.13da.3). Using $F_m=hG_m$ gives
$$
\frac{\delta_h}{h^6}\ge\frac1{64}h\sum_m
\left\{2\operatorname{Tr}\left[\frac{\nabla^3G_m}{h^3}Y(mh)\right]
-\operatorname{Tr}[W_mY(mh)^2]\right\},
$$
$$
W_m=(G_m+3G_{m-1}+3G_{m-2}+G_{m-3})/8.
\tag{M.6.13da.11}
$$
All boundary and exterior-zero terms remain. Summation by parts three times changes the first term to
$$
-2h\sum_m\operatorname{Tr}\left[G_m\frac{\Delta_h^3Y(mh)}{h^3}\right],
\qquad \Delta_hY(x)=Y(x+h)-Y(x).
$$
Uniform convergence, the smooth test difference limit and Riemann summation give $-2\int\operatorname{Tr}(FY''')$. Uniform Lipschitz continuity gives $\|W_m-G_m\|_1=O(h)$, yielding the quadratic $\int$. Taking the lower limit and then the supremum proves the upper bound in (M.6.13da.4).

For its positive lower bound take $Y(x)=t(x)P_N$, $t\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)$, and let $N\to\infty$. Trace-norm tightness gives
$$
\int[-2ft'''-ft^2]=\int[2f'''t-ft^2].
$$
The zero extension of $f\in\mathcal P_3$ is $C^3$, so no boundary term is removed. Weighted $L^2$ approximation on compact interior subintervals, followed by endpoint truncation, makes the supremum equal to $I_3(f)=\int(f''')^2/f$. Endpoint order six makes this finite. It is positive because a compactly supported normalized density cannot have $f'''\equiv0$. This proves all of (M.6.13da.4) and the positive lower bound on any limit $\kappa$.

For a smooth faithful finite matrix field, integration by parts recovers $\int\operatorname{Tr}[F'''\mathcal L_F^{-1}(F''')]$. At singular fields, (M.6.13da.3) is the extended action and retains every normal-normal derivative component.

##### IV. Entropy and renormalized cost

The prescribed diagonal blocks give the exact identity
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_h)=H(p_h)+\sum_np_nS(\rho(nh))-S(\Gamma_h).
$$
Riemann convergence gives $H(p_h)=\log(1/h)+h(f)+o(1)$ and $\sum_np_nS(\rho(nh))\to\int fS(\rho)$. Combine these with (M.6.13da.2) and $\delta_h/h^6\to\kappa$ to obtain the equality in (M.6.13da.5); its inequality follows from (M.6.13da.4).

Theorem M.6.13cz supplies critical-scale coercivity on this same fixed-profile, fixed-faithful-density class. The present theorem states the ensuing global limit once the critical bound holds. Neither statement optimizes over varying multiplicities or changing native profiles, identifies state quality with operational all-input quality, or selects a sharp unrestricted additive constant. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613db-minimal-collective-range-and-the-compact-support-covariance-ceiling"></a>**Theorem M.6.13db (Minimal Collective Range and the Compact-Support Covariance Ceiling).** Let $I$ be a nonempty connected open interval in $\mathbb R$, $\mathscr H$ a complex Hilbert space, and $1\le d<\infty$ an integer. Suppose $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathbb C^d,\mathscr H)$ is a $C^3$ isometry, $M:I\to\operatorname{Herm}_d$ is $C^3$ and pointwise positive definite, and
$$
F=VMV^*,\qquad P=VV^*,\quad Q=I-P,\qquad QF'''Q=0.
\tag{M.6.13db.1}
$$
In a parallel frame, $r=\operatorname{rank}V'$ is constant, and
$$
\mathscr S=\operatorname{Ran}V(x)\oplus\operatorname{Ran}V'(x)
=\operatorname{span}_{y\in I}\operatorname{Ran}F(y)
\quad\text{is fixed},\qquad \dim\mathscr S=d+r\le2d.
\tag{M.6.13db.2}
$$
There is no endpoint regularity or uniform endpoint lower bound on $M$ in this interior assertion, and $2d$ is sharp on this class.

For a separable $\mathscr H$ with fixed coordinates, suppose instead that $F:\mathbb R\to\mathcal S_1(\mathscr H)$ is positive and trace-norm continuous, compactly supported on $[a,b]$, bounded in operator norm and in $L^2(\mathbb R;\mathcal S_2)$, with rank exactly $d$ at every $a<x<b$. If the unmodified distributional action (M.6.13da.3) is finite, then
$$
F\in H^3(\mathbb R;\mathcal S_2),\qquad
F(a)=F'(a)=F''(a)=F(b)=F'(b)=F''(b)=0,
\tag{M.6.13db.3}
$$
and the minimal collective range has the stronger bound
$$
\dim\mathscr S=d+r\le2d-1.
\tag{M.6.13db.4}
$$
If $\Gamma=\int F$ has finite trace, then $\operatorname{Ran}\Gamma=\mathscr S$; for normalized $\Gamma$, $S(\Gamma)\le\log(2d-1)$.

*Proof.*

##### I. Parallel gauge, normal-null identity and minimal fixed ambient space

For an initial isometry $V_0$, $\Omega=V_0^*V_0'$ is skew-Hermitian. Solve $R'=-\Omega R$, $R(x_0)=I_d$, on compact interior intervals and continue over $I$. This gives a $C^3$ unitary $R$. Set $V=V_0R$, $M=R^*M_0R$, leaving $F$ fixed and obtaining $V^*V'=0$.

Put
$$
B=V',\qquad G=B^*B,\qquad C=QB',\qquad K=BMB^*.
$$
Then $V^*B=0$, $V^*B'=-G$ and $B'=C-VG$. The exact product rule in the normal-normal corner is
$$
QF'''Q=3(CMB^*+BMC^*+2BM'B^*).
\tag{M.6.13db.5}
$$
Thus (M.6.13db.1) implies $CMB^*+BMC^*=-2BM'B^*$. Let $L=P+K$. Its range is $\operatorname{Ran}V\oplus\operatorname{Ran}B$, since $M>0$ and these two spaces are orthogonal. Differentiation gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
L&=[V,B]\begin{pmatrix}I_d&0\\0&M\end{pmatrix}[V,B]^*,\\
L'&=[V,B]\begin{pmatrix}0&I_d-GM\\I_d-MG&-M'\end{pmatrix}[V,B]^*.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13db.6}
$$
On every compact interior interval $J$, the first middle matrix is uniformly positive and the second is bounded Hermitian. Conjugating the latter by the inverse square root of the former gives a finite $c_J$ and
$$
-c_JL\preceq L'\preceq c_JL,
\qquad
 e^{-c_J|x-y|}L(y)\preceq L(x)\preceq e^{c_J|x-y|}L(y)
\quad(x,y\in J).
\tag{M.6.13db.7}
$$
The second inequality follows by scalar Gronwall on $\langle u,L(x)u\rangle$ in both directions. It uses no inverse of $B,G$ or $L$. Hence $\ker L$ and its finite-dimensional range are constant on $I$, proving constant $r$ and the bound $d+r\le2d$.

Let $\mathscr T$ be the span of all $\operatorname{Ran}V(x)$. It lies in the fixed finite-dimensional range of $L$, hence is closed. Difference quotients of the columns of $V$ show $\operatorname{Ran}B(x)\subseteq\mathscr T$. Thus $\mathscr T=\mathscr S$, proving minimality in (M.6.13db.2). In any other isometric frame, the normal velocity is $(I-P)V'$, so its rank is the same intrinsic $r$.

The corresponding transport description is also explicit. Put $A=BV^*-VB^*$ and solve $U'=AU$. Then
$$
P'=[A,P],\qquad K'=[A,K]-BM'B^*,\qquad
(U^*KU)'=-U^*BM'B^*U.
$$
On compact intervals, $-a_JM\preceq M'\preceq a_JM$ gives the same two-sided Gronwall comparison for $U^*KU$. Its support is a fixed projection $E_0$, so the projection onto $\operatorname{Ran}B$ is $E=UE_0U^*$ with $E'=[A,E]$. The projection $H=P+E$ satisfies $H'=[A,H]=0$, since $AH=HA=A$. This recovers the fixed sum of the physical range and its transported normal range.

If $\Gamma=\int_I F$ has finite trace, its quadratic forms integrate nonnegative continuous functions. A vector is in $\ker\Gamma$ exactly when it is in every $\ker F(x)$. Therefore $\operatorname{Ran}\Gamma=\mathscr S$. The same conclusion holds for any integrable positive almost-everywhere scalar weight in this covariance.

For sharpness of the interior $2d$ bound, in $\mathbb C^{2d}$ take nonzero real $\omega_j$ and
$$
v_j(x)=\cos(\omega_jx)e_j+\sin(\omega_jx)e_{d+j},\quad
V=[v_1,\ldots,v_d],\quad M=\operatorname{diag}(m_1,\ldots,m_d),\quad m_j>0.
\tag{M.6.13db.8}
$$
The coordinate planes are orthogonal, $V^*V'=0$, $\operatorname{rank}B=d$, $B_j'=-\omega_j^2v_j$ and $QB'=0$. Equation (M.6.13db.5) vanishes, and every open interval spans both directions in each coordinate plane. On a bounded interval all derivatives are bounded and the positive $m_j$ are fixed, giving finite interior extended action. This example has no vanishing endpoint profile and does not assert sharpness under (M.6.13db.3).

##### II. Finite extended action gives the full Hilbert–Schmidt third derivative

Now assume the compact-support hypotheses. Work on the real Hilbert space of self-adjoint Hilbert–Schmidt fields. For allowed finite-coordinate tests set
$$
\ell(Y)=-\int\operatorname{Tr}(FY'''),\qquad
q(Y)=\int\operatorname{Tr}(FY^2),\qquad C_0=\|F\|_{L^\infty\mathrm{op}}.
$$
Testing the action on every real multiple $tY$ and optimizing $2t\ell-t^2q$ gives, including $q=0$,
$$
|\ell(Y)|^2\le\mathcal J_{\rm ext}(F)q(Y)
\le\mathcal J_{\rm ext}(F)C_0\|Y\|_{L^2\mathcal S_2}^2.
\tag{M.6.13db.9}
$$
Smooth compactly supported finite-coordinate Hermitian fields are dense in this Hilbert space. Riesz representation gives $H_3\in L^2(\mathbb R;\mathcal S_2^{\rm sa})$, with norm squared at most $C_0\mathcal J_{\rm ext}(F)$, representing $\ell$. Testing a scalar smooth function times each finite-coordinate Hermitian matrix identifies $H_3$ as the distributional $F'''$. Since $F\in L^2\mathcal S_2$, the Hilbert-valued Fourier transform has
$$
\int(1+|\xi|^6)\|\widehat F(\xi)\|_{\mathcal S_2}^2d\xi<\infty.
$$
Lower powers are bounded by a constant times $1+|\xi|^6$, so $F\in H^3$. The one-dimensional $H^1$ representative of $F''$ satisfies
$$
\|F''(x)-F''(y)\|_{\mathcal S_2}\le
\|F'''\|_{L^2\mathcal S_2}|x-y|^{1/2}.
$$
Thus $F$ has a $C^2$ representative agreeing with the original continuous one. Since it is zero outside $[a,b]$, continuity of its first two derivatives proves (M.6.13db.3).

##### III. Normal-null equation and local Sobolev frames

The nonnegative form $q$ extends continuously to all $L^2\mathcal S_2^{\rm sa}$ fields as $\|F^{1/2}Y\|_{L^2\mathcal S_2}^2$. Inequality (M.6.13db.9) extends by density. On the interior let $P(x)=\operatorname{supp}F(x)$ and $Q=I-P$, which are measurable. Choose $Y=QF'''Q$ on $(a,b)$ and zero elsewhere. It is self-adjoint and Hilbert–Schmidt square integrable. Since $FQ=0$, $q(Y)=0$, whereas
$$
\ell(Y)=\int_a^b\|QF'''Q\|_{\mathcal S_2}^2dx.
$$
Therefore
$$
QF'''Q=0\quad\text{almost everywhere on }(a,b).
\tag{M.6.13db.10}
$$
The actual normal-normal block has been controlled, rather than removed from an inverse convention.

On compact $J\subset(a,b)$, continuity and exact positive rank $d$ give a positive lower bound on the nonzero eigenvalues. A contour enclosing all positive eigenvalues and excluding zero defines
$$
P=\frac1{2\pi i}\oint(zI-F)^{-1}dz.
$$
Subtract $z^{-1}I$ inside the contour $\int$ to exhibit its Hilbert–Schmidt resolvent difference; that scalar contour $\int$ is zero. Its first three weak derivatives are products of bounded resolvents with $F',F'',F'''$. The first two derivatives of $F$ are continuous and bounded on $J$, and its third is $L^2$. Hence $P\in H^3(J;\mathcal S_2)$ and is locally $C^2$.

Set $A=[P',P]$, skew-adjoint and locally $H^2$, and solve $V'=AV$ with initial isometry onto $\operatorname{Ran}P(x_0)$. The identities $P'=[A,P]$ and $PAP=0$ give $PV=V$, $V^*V=I_d$ and $V^*V'=0$. Compact-interior continuation defines the frame throughout $(a,b)$, with $V\in H^3_{\rm loc}$; for instance $V'''=A''V+2A'V'+AV''\in L^2_{\rm loc}$. Put $M=V^*FV>0$. Then $M\in H^3_{\rm loc}$ and $F=VMV^*$.

The weak product rule gives (M.6.13db.5). Its normal-null products involve $B=V'\in H^2_{\rm loc}$ and $C=QB'$, and have continuous representatives, so their zero identity holds pointwise. The positive operator $L=P+BMB^*$ is locally $C^1$ and satisfies (M.6.13db.6)–(M.6.13db.7). The same Gronwall and difference-quotient proof gives one fixed minimal $\mathscr S$, with $\dim\mathscr S=d+r$ and constant $r\le d$, at this Sobolev regularity.

##### IV. Endpoint vanishing excludes full normal rank

Suppose $r=d$. Then $G=B^*B>0$ at every interior point. Multiply the normal-null equation by $G^{-1}B^*$ on the left and $BG^{-1}$ on the right. With $T=G^{-1}B^*C$ this gives
$$
TM+MT^*+2M'=0.
$$
Since $G'=B^*C+C^*B$, taking the trace after multiplication by $M^{-1}$ gives
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(G^{-1}G')+2\operatorname{Tr}(M^{-1}M')=0.
$$
Consequently
$$
c_0:=\det G(\det M)^2=\det(MGM)>0
\quad\text{is constant on }(a,b).
\tag{M.6.13db.11}
$$
Arithmetic–geometric mean for the eigenvalues of $MGM$ yields

$$
\|BM\|_{HS}^2=\operatorname{Tr}(MGM)\ge d c_0^{1/d}.
$$

In the parallel frame,
$$
F'=BMV^*+VM'V^*+VMB^*.
$$
These two off-diagonal blocks and the range-range block are Hilbert–Schmidt orthogonal. Therefore
$$
\|F'\|_{HS}^2=\|M'\|_{HS}^2+2\|BM\|_{HS}^2
\ge2d c_0^{1/d}>0.
\tag{M.6.13db.12}
$$
This contradicts $F'(x)\to F'(a)=0$. Thus $r\le d-1$, proving (M.6.13db.4). No endpoint frame bound or inverse-eigenvalue bound was assumed; $G^{-1}$ was used only in this full-rank contradiction, after constant rank was established without it. Positivity of the covariance $\int$ proves its range assertion as in Part I. The usual finite-rank entropy maximum gives $S(\Gamma)\le\log(2d-1)$.

##### V. Consequences for the actual critical-scale reference families

The field supplied by Theorem M.6.13da satisfies all compact-support premises: its trace is bounded, it is trace-norm Lipschitz on compact support and therefore in $L^2\mathcal S_2$, its interior eigenvalues are $f\operatorname{spec}\rho>0$, and (M.6.13da.4) gives finite extended action. Hence every such subsequential covariance has
$$
\operatorname{rank}\Gamma\le2d-1,\qquad S(\Gamma)\le\log(2d-1).
\tag{M.6.13db.13}
$$
If $P_{\mathscr S}$ projects onto this limiting range, covariance convergence gives
$$
\sum_{k>2d-1}\lambda_k(\sigma_j)
\le\operatorname{Tr}[(I-P_{\mathscr S})\Gamma_j]
\le\|\Gamma_j-\Gamma\|_1\longrightarrow0.
$$
Entropy convergence in Theorem M.6.13da gives $S(\sigma_j)\to S(\Gamma)$. Apply the same compactness argument to any subsequence of a family with one fixed $f,\rho,d,m_0$ and one uniform $\delta_j\le Kh_j^6$. A subsequence contradiction yields the whole-family conclusions
$$
\sum_{k>2d-1}\lambda_k(\sigma_j)\longrightarrow0,
\qquad\limsup_j S(\sigma_j)\le\log(2d-1).
\tag{M.6.13db.14}
$$
The approximating finite states may still have additional small eigenvalues, so this is not an exact finite-mesh rank cap. Connected positive support with constant interior rank is essential: separate positive components may span different subspaces, and an interior rank drop removes the local spectral-gap premise. For $d=1$ the collective range is constant and one-dimensional. This theorem does not impose a common $d$-plane when $d>1$, select a physical eigenbasis orientation, or assert entropy sharpness or sharpness for all $d\ge3$. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613di-parity-conditional-entropy-and-the-counted-even-phase-cost"></a>**Theorem M.6.13di (Parity-Conditional Entropy and the Counted Even-Phase Cost).** Fix the normalized spin-$3/2$ target $X=J_x/(3/2)$ and complete reference convention of Theorem M.6.13ch. The phase-preparation channel has sharp complete quadratic contraction coefficient one relative to phase parity. Its parity-conditional entropy has sharp weak-quality slope $1/2$. These are statements about the conditional debit; the complete charge asymmetry retains a separate even-phase debit. In particular they do not contradict the complete-reference endpoint of Theorem M.6.13ck.

##### I. The preparation channel and its exact quadratic problem

Put $d\mu=d\theta/(2\pi)$, $z=e^{i\theta}$ and
$$
v_\theta=\frac1{\sqrt8}(1,\sqrt3z,\sqrt3z^2,z^3)^T,\qquad
\Lambda(F)=\int v_\theta v_\theta^*\otimes F_\theta\,d\mu.
\tag{M.6.13di.1}
$$
Here $F$ is any positive matrix symbol of finite coefficient dimension, normalized by $\int\operatorname{Tr}F\,d\mu=1$. Define $G_\theta=(F_\theta+F_{\theta+\pi})/2$, $H_\theta=(F_\theta-F_{\theta+\pi})/2$, $R=\Lambda(G)$, $D=\Lambda(H)$, and
$$
q_{\rm in}=\sup_{b=b^*}\int\operatorname{Tr}(2Hb-Gb^2)\,d\mu,
\qquad q_{\rm out}=\sup_{B=B^*}\operatorname{Tr}(2DB-RB^2).
\tag{M.6.13di.2}
$$
The measurable input supremum is over finite-$\int$ objectives; singular supports use the supported quadratic problem. For $V_\theta=v_\theta\otimes I$ and $b_\theta=V_\theta^*BV_\theta$,
$$
V_\theta^*B^2V_\theta-b_\theta^2
 =V_\theta^*B(I-V_\theta V_\theta^*)BV_\theta\succeq0.
\tag{M.6.13di.3}
$$
Since $G\succeq0$, insertion in the objective gives $q_{\rm out}\le q_{\rm in}$. This includes every finite neutral coefficient and retained flag; it is a quadratic variational contraction, without an entropy contraction assumption.

##### II. A strictly positive approximation to the sharp localization sequence

For integers $n\ge0$ and $0<t<1$, set
$$
I_n=\frac{\binom{2n}{n}}{4^n},\quad g_n(\theta)=\frac{\cos^{2n}\theta}{I_n},\quad
f_{n,t}=g_n(1+t\cos\theta),\quad r_n=\frac{2n+1}{2n+2}.
\tag{M.6.13di.4}
$$
The even and odd parts are $g_n$ and $t g_n\cos\theta$, so $q_{\rm in}=t^2r_n$. The first three real Fourier coefficients are
$$
a=t r_n,\qquad b=\frac n{n+1},\qquad c=\frac{t r_n n}{n+2}.
\tag{M.6.13di.5}
$$
For completeness the full four-level calculation is explicit. In even/odd order $(0,2;1,3)$ the diagonal blocks of $R$ and the even-to-odd block of $D$ are
$$
A=\frac18\begin{pmatrix}1&\sqrt3b\\\sqrt3b&3\end{pmatrix},\quad
B_0=\frac18\begin{pmatrix}3&\sqrt3b\\\sqrt3b&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
C=\frac18\begin{pmatrix}\sqrt3a&c\\3a&\sqrt3a\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13di.6}
$$
The optimizer is $\begin{psmallmatrix}0&S\\S^*&0\end{psmallmatrix}$, where $AS+SB_0=2C$. For $|b|<1$ its entries are
$$
S=\frac1{4(1-b^2)}
\begin{pmatrix}
\sqrt3(2a-ab-bc)&(b-2)(3ab-bc-2c)\\
4a-2ab-3ab^2+b^2c&\sqrt3(2a-ab-bc)
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13di.7}
$$
Direct multiplication verifies the Sylvester equation. Taking $2\operatorname{Tr}(C^*S)$ gives
$$
q_{\rm out}=\frac{(24-12b-9b^2)a^2+(6b^2-12b)ac+(4-b^2)c^2}{16(1-b^2)}.
\tag{M.6.13di.8}
$$
Substitution of (M.6.13di.5) yields
$$
q_{\rm out}=t^2Q_n,\qquad
Q_n=\frac{(2n+1)(2n^2+6n+3)}{4(n+1)^2(n+2)},\qquad
\frac{q_{\rm out}}{q_{\rm in}}=1-\frac1{2(n+1)(n+2)}.
\tag{M.6.13di.9}
$$
Thus $3/4$ is the uniform-background tangent value ($n=0$), while the sharp coefficient over the full class is one. The isolated zeros cause no restriction: replace $g_n$ by $g_{n,\varepsilon}=(1-\varepsilon)g_n+\varepsilon$. Then $g_{n,\varepsilon}(1+t\cos\theta)\ge\varepsilon(1-t)>0$. At $\varepsilon=0$ the four-level mean is positive definite: no nonzero degree-three vector polynomial vanishes almost everywhere against $g_n$. Consequently its Sylvester inverse and quality are continuous there. First let $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ at fixed $n$, then $n\to\infty$. The same sharp coefficient holds for smooth strictly positive symbols, without treating a limiting infinite phase reference as an admitted finite witness.

##### III. The missing even-phase entropy

Write
$$
\Phi(s)=\frac{(1+\sqrt s)\log(1+\sqrt s)+(1-\sqrt s)\log(1-\sqrt s)}2
 =\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{s^k}{2k(2k-1)}.
\tag{M.6.13di.10}
$$
For a normalized scalar even $g$ the conditional parity entropy is

$$
J(g,t)=\int g\Phi(t^2\cos^2\theta)\,d\mu.
$$

In the sequence above,
$$
0\le J(g_n,t)-\frac{t^2r_n}2\le\frac{t^4}{12(1-t^2)},\qquad
\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{J(g_n,t)}{q_{\rm out}}=\frac1{2\eta_n},\quad
\eta_n=1-\frac1{2(n+1)(n+2)}.
\tag{M.6.13di.11}
$$
The remainder follows term by term from (M.6.13di.10). Conversely $\Phi(s)\ge s/2$ and (M.6.13di.3) give $J(g,t)\ge q_{\rm in}/2\ge q_{\rm out}/2$ in this scalar class. More generally define $J(F)=\int\operatorname{Tr}[F(\log F-\log G)]\,d\mu$, with supported logarithms; $G\succeq F/2$ makes these supports legitimate. The binary-discriminator entropy argument in Theorem M.6.13ch gives the same lower bound with finite matrix coefficients: apply the preparation channel to the parity pair, measure its supported Sylvester optimizer, and apply $\Phi(s)\ge s/2$ to its binary outcome pairs. Thus the sharp parity-conditional slope is $1/2$.

The complete scalar cost $H(f)=\int f\log f\,d\mu$ obeys the exact decomposition
$$
H(f_{n,t})=H(g_n)+J(g_n,t),\qquad
H(g_n)=2n(H_{2n}-H_n)-\log\binom{2n}{n}
 \ge\tfrac12\log(n+1)-1.
\tag{M.6.13di.12}
$$
Here $H_j=\sum_{k=1}^j1/k$ and $H_0=0$. Parity annihilates the odd term multiplying $\log g_n$, proving the decomposition. Differentiating the $\beta$ $\int$ $\int|\cos\theta|^{2x}d\mu$ at integer $x$ gives the stated entropy; equivalently use its integration-by-parts recurrence and $\int\log\cos^2\theta\,d\mu=-2\log2$. For $n\ge1$, comparison of decreasing $1/x$ rectangles with their integrals gives $\log2-\sum_{k=n+1}^{2n}1/k\le1/(2n)$, while induction using $I_n/I_{n-1}=(2n-1)/(2n)$ gives $I_n\le1/\sqrt{n+1}$. Hence $H(g_n)\ge-\log I_n-1$, proving the bound; $n=0$ is immediate. The regularization retains
$$
H(g_{n,\varepsilon})\ge(1-\varepsilon)H(g_n)-h_2(\varepsilon).
\tag{M.6.13di.13}
$$
This is the mixture-entropy inequality with its binary flag entropy counted. A retained rare flag $F_\theta=(1-p)\oplus p f_\theta$ has full, even and conditional matrix costs $pH(f),pH(g),pJ$, and both qualities are multiplied by $p$. Thus a small unweighted total even cost cannot remove the branch's conditional debit. The two-dimensional neutral flag remains part of the reference.

##### IV. An exact positive three-charge witness

On $Q=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2)$ take
$$
\sigma_t=\frac13\begin{pmatrix}1&8t/11&5/11\\8t/11&1&8t/11\\5/11&8t/11&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
E=\sigma_0,\quad 0<t<1.
\tag{M.6.13di.14}
$$
It is the three-site Toeplitz compression of $[1+(10/11)\cos2\theta](1+t\cos\theta)\ge(1-t)/11$. Its eigenvalues are $2/11$ and $(27\pm\sqrt{25+512t^2})/66$, so it is faithful. Its charge diagonal is $I_3/3$ and
$$
J_t=D(\sigma_t\Vert E)=\frac9{11}\!\left[\Phi\!\left(\frac{25+512t^2}{729}\right)-\Phi\!\left(\frac{25}{729}\right)\right],\quad
\mathcal A_Q(E)=\frac23\Phi\!\left(\frac{25}{121}\right),\quad
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_t)=\mathcal A_Q(E)+J_t.
\tag{M.6.13di.15}
$$
The identity follows either from these eigenvalues or from the relative-entropy Pythagoras identity for parity pinching, since $E$ is parity invariant. The six total-charge sectors $0,\ldots,5$ have dimensions $1,2,3,3,2,1$. In their increasing system-charge order the supported optimum is zero on singleton sectors; on sectors one and two it is
$$
B_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&4\sqrt3t/11\\4\sqrt3t/11&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&272\sqrt3t/943&0\\272\sqrt3t/943&0&624t/943\\0&624t/943&0\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{M.6.13di.16}
$$
Sector four has $B_1$ and sector three the reversed $B_2$. Explicitly, with $w=(1,\sqrt3,\sqrt3,1)/\sqrt8$, the sector indexed by pairs $(i,a)$ satisfying $i+a=k$ has entries $R_{ia,jb}=w_iw_j(\sigma_t)_{ab}$ when $i-j$ is even and zero otherwise; $D$ uses the odd entries. Substitution verifies $RB+BR=2D$ in every sector. The nontrivial qualities are $8t^2/121$ and $1792t^2/10373$, with their reflected partners. Thus
$$
q=\frac{54512}{114103}t^2.
\tag{M.6.13di.17}
$$
Since $\Phi'(s)=\operatorname{atanh}(\sqrt s)/(2\sqrt s)\le1/[2(1-s)]$, at $t=1/10$,
$$
J_t\le\frac3{1001},\qquad
\frac23q-J_t\ge\frac{146371}{778752975}>0,\qquad
\mathcal A_Q(E)\ge\frac{25}{363}.
\tag{M.6.13di.18}
$$
These are rational bounds; the strict comparison charges only $J_t$. The complete cost retains the strictly positive even debit in (M.6.13di.15).

##### V. A fully retained thirty-five-dimensional apparatus

Here is the conserving realization, including the operational error estimate. Let $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,-1)$ and $H|i\rangle=|3-i\rangle$. The sector optimum $B$ above is a Hermitian contraction conserving $Q_S+Q$, and $ZBZ=-B$. On the complete pre-meter reference use
$$
R_0=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C^3\oplus\mathbb C^3,\quad Q_0=0\oplus Q\oplus(-Q),\quad
\sigma_p=(1-p)\oplus\tfrac p2\sigma_t\oplus\tfrac p2\sigma_t,\quad
\widetilde B=0\oplus B\oplus(H\otimes I)B(H\otimes I).
\tag{M.6.13di.19}
$$
The inactive zero acts on the full system times its one-dimensional reference branch. Reflection conserves the reflected total charge because $HQ_SH=3I-Q_S$ and $HXH=X$. The five distinct eigenvalues of $\widetilde B$ are
$$
b_j\in\left\{0,\ \pm\frac{4\sqrt3t}{11},\ \pm\frac{\sqrt{611328}\,t}{943}\right\}.
\tag{M.6.13di.20}
$$
Let $\Pi_j$ be their complete spectral projectors, including all zero directions. On a neutral five-level meter let $W|j\rangle=|j+1\bmod5\rangle$, initially $|0\rangle$, and set
$$
U=\sum_{j=0}^4\Pi_j\otimes W^j,\qquad
M=I_{R_0}\otimes\sum_{j=0}^4b_j|j\rangle\langle j|.
\tag{M.6.13di.21}
$$
Orthogonality proves unitarity; spectral conservation gives $[U,Q_S+Q_0]=0$, and the neutral pointer satisfies the Yanase condition. Ready-state compression of its first and second Heisenberg moments gives $\widetilde B$ and $\widetilde B^2$. Consequently this is the actual all-input noise-square measurement. Its reference dimension is $7\cdot5=35$, its system-inclusive dimension $140$, and its charges $-2,-1,0,1,2$ have multiplicities $5,5,15,5,5$. Every pointer and inactive/reflection flag is retained. Direct-sum entropy cancellation gives complete cost $p[\mathcal A_Q(E)+J_t]$ and conditional debit $pJ_t$.

To bound its worst-case quality, put $K_B=\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma_t)(B-X\otimes I)^2]$, $K_{\rm sym}=(K_B+HK_BH)/2$ and let $P$ project onto the two extremal $X$ eigenvectors. Parity makes $K_B$ even. In this extremal basis $Z$ exchanges the two vectors while $H$ has eigenvalues $1,-1$. Since their average error is $1-q$ by the Sylvester equation, parity equalizes the two diagonal entries and reflection cancels the off-diagonal entries. Therefore $PK_{\rm sym}P=(1-q)P$. The complete noise square is
$$
K(p)=(1-p)X^2+pK_{\rm sym},\qquad
pq-36p^2\le u(p)=1-\|K(p)\|\le pq\quad(0\le p\le4/45).
\tag{M.6.13di.22}
$$
Indeed $0\preceq K_{\rm sym}\preceq4I$ and $\|K_{\rm sym}-X^2\|\le4$. The complementary eigenvalue of $X^2$ is $1/9$, with gap $\delta=8/9$. For a unit vector with complementary norm $r_0$, its Rayleigh quotient above $1-pq$ is at most $[-\delta+p(4+q)]r_0^2+8pr_0\sqrt{1-r_0^2}\le-\delta r_0^2/2+8pr_0\le36p^2$. The condition follows from $p\le4/45$ and $q\le1$. Compression to $P$ gives the reverse bound and the noise square is positive.

At $t=1/10$ and $p=10^{-6}$, (M.6.13di.18) and (M.6.13di.22) give
$$
\frac23u(p)-pJ_t\ge p\left(\frac{146371}{778752975}-\frac{24}{10^6}\right)>0.
\tag{M.6.13di.23}
$$
Thus even a complete finite all-input apparatus excludes a parity-only $2/3$ cost bound. Its omitted even cost is at least $25p/363$. The result does not replace complete asymmetry by conditional entropy, improve the full endpoint, or assert an uncounted infinite phase source or a minimum apparatus dimension. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613dj-dimension-free-commuting-curvature-and-the-sharp-scalar-bulk-frontier"></a>**Theorem M.6.13dj (Dimension-Free Commuting Curvature and the Sharp Scalar Bulk Frontier).** Retain the complete finite-reference spin-$3/2$ state discriminator $q_Q(\sigma)$ of Theorems M.6.13ch and M.6.13ck, with $p=(1,3,3,1)/8$ and natural-$\log$ asymmetry $\mathcal A_Q$. The following two statements hold.

1. Let $Q_n$ be arbitrary finite real reference charges, $\sigma_n$ states, $\tau_n=\mathcal G_{Q_n}(\sigma_n)$, and $q_n=q_{Q_n}(\sigma_n)>0$ with $q_n\to0$. On $\operatorname{supp}\tau_n$, suppose
$$
[\sigma_n,\tau_n]=0,\qquad
\varepsilon_n=\|\tau_n^{-1}\sigma_n-I\|_{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{M.6.13dj.1}
$$
Then
$$
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\frac{\mathcal A_{Q_n}(\sigma_n)-2q_n/3}{q_n^2}\ge\frac4{27}.
\tag{M.6.13dj.2}
$$
The constant is sharp. Reference dimensions, positive-support ranks, charge widths, degeneracies and smallest positive eigenvalues may vary without any uniform bound. In particular this includes $\tau_n=I/d_n$, $d_n\to\infty$, whenever $\|d_n\sigma_n-I\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to0$. Arbitrary charge gaps, including gap two, and all quantum correlations satisfying (M.6.13dj.1) are retained.

2. For every normalized scalar circle density $f\ge0$, let $H(f)=\int f\log f\,d\mu$, with normalized Haar measure $\mu$, and let $q_{\mathrm{bulk}}(f)$ be the original scalar spin discriminator of (M.6.13di.1)–(M.6.13di.2). Define the exact-quality infimum over all such densities by
$$
F_{\mathrm{scalar}}(q)=\inf\{H(f):q_{\mathrm{bulk}}(f)=q\}.
$$
Then
$$
F_{\mathrm{scalar}}(q)=\frac23q+\frac7{36}q^2+o(q^2)
\qquad(q\downarrow0).
\tag{M.6.13dj.3}
$$
No boundedness, positive lower bound, Fourier-degree bound or other amplitude regularity is imposed on the original scalar densities.

These are state and scalar-bulk statements. Neither proves the unrestricted state coefficient $4/27$, identifies state quality with operational all-input quality, nor supplies a lower curvature bound for arbitrary jointly varying finite Toeplitz symbols and sizes.

*Proof.* We first establish dimension-free local estimates, retaining the fourth moment until the error terms have been absorbed.

**A normalized tracial algebra and charge modes.** For the first assertion, suppress the index $n$ and work on $\operatorname{supp}\tau$. Positivity gives $\operatorname{supp}\sigma\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\tau$; this is a supported calculation, not removal of physical resource directions. Set
$$
Z=\tau^{-1}\sigma-I,\qquad
\varphi(T)=\operatorname{Tr}(\tau T),\qquad
\mathcal M=\{\tau\}'.
$$
The commutation hypothesis makes $Z$ Hermitian and places it in $\mathcal M$. The functional $\varphi$ is a normalized faithful trace on this algebra, since $\tau$ is central there. Also $Q\in\mathcal M$, $\mathcal G_QZ=0$ and $\varphi(Z)=0$. Charge-mode extraction preserves $\mathcal M$. For arbitrary real charges, the mode at frequency $k$ is the Cesàro limit of
$$
\frac1{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}e^{-ikt}e^{\mathrm{itQ}}Ze^{-itQ}\,dt.
$$
Its operator-norm bound is one, independent of dimension and spectrum. Denote this single-frequency extraction by $Z^{[k]}$; each paired mode $Y_k$ below includes both signs. Distinct charge modes are orthogonal in the $\varphi$ inner product.

Write $Z=X+Y$, where $X$ contains exactly the modes $\pm1$, and let $Y_k$ contain the modes $\pm k$ of $Y$. Put
$$
\begin{gathered}
\varepsilon=\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}},\quad
x=\varphi(X^2),\quad y=\varphi(Y^2),\quad W=Y-Y_2,\\
P_0=\mathcal G_Q(X^2),\qquad P_2=X^2-P_0.
\end{gathered}
\tag{M.6.13dj.4}
$$
Thus $\|X\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\varepsilon$, $\|Y\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le3\varepsilon$, and $\|Y_k\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le6\varepsilon$. Charge sums give
$$
\varphi(X^3)=0,\quad
P_2\text{ has only modes }\pm2,\quad
\varphi(X^2Y)=\varphi(P_2Y_2),\quad
\varphi(X^4)=\varphi(P_0^2)+\varphi(P_2^2).
\tag{M.6.13dj.5}
$$
Every constant denoted $C$ below is finite and universal; it may increase between displays but is independent of $\tau$, dimension and charges.

**Entropy expansion with a retained fourth moment.** Commutation gives $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)=\varphi((I+Z)\log(I+Z))$. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, scalar functional calculus and trace Hölder inequalities imply
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)
=\frac12\varphi(Z^2)-\frac12\varphi(P_2Y_2)
 +\frac1{12}\varphi(X^4)+r_A,
\qquad |r_A|\le C\varepsilon[\varphi(X^4)+y].
\tag{M.6.13dj.6}
$$
Here are the full remainder estimates. The Taylor series of $(1+z)\log(1+z)$ through degree four, after its linear term integrates to zero, has trace remainder at most $C\varepsilon\varphi(Z^4)$. The three-$X$ cubic term is zero by (M.6.13dj.5); the two-$X$, one-$Y$ contribution is $-\varphi(P_2Y_2)/2$. Cubic words with at least two $Y$ factors are bounded by $C\varepsilon y$. Quartic words with at least two $Y$ factors are bounded by $C\varepsilon^2y$, including alternating words by tracial Cauchy–Schwarz. The remaining quartic trace obeys
$$
|\varphi(X^3Y)|
\le\|X\|_{\mathrm{op}}\sqrt{\varphi(X^4)y}
\le\varepsilon[\varphi(X^4)+y].
$$
Finally the trace $L^4$ triangle inequality gives
$\varphi(Z^4)\le8[\varphi(X^4)+\varphi(Y^4)]
\le8\varphi(X^4)+72\varepsilon^2y$.
These estimates establish (M.6.13dj.6) without a dimension-dependent norm comparison.

**Exact inverse identity for the quality remainder.** The spin mean and difference maps preserve the commutant of $I_4\otimes\tau$. Remove their common central factor $\tau$ and denote the resulting maps by $R$ and $D$. In the scaled Sylvester problem,
$$
R=R_0+R_Y,\quad R_0=\operatorname{diag}(p)\otimes I,
\quad D=D_Z,\qquad
\mathcal J_R(B)=\frac{RB+BR}{2}.
$$
Here $R_Y$ depends only on $Y_2$, and $D_Z$ only on $X+Y_3$.

Explicitly, in spin indices $i,j=0,1,2,3$,
$$
(R_Y)_{ij}=\sqrt{p_ip_j}\,Z^{[j-i]}1_{|j-i|=2},\qquad
(D_Z)_{ij}=\sqrt{p_ip_j}\,Z^{[j-i]}1_{|j-i|\in\{1,3\}}.
\tag{M.6.13dj.6a}
$$
 Use the tracial functional $\varphi_4=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{spin}}\otimes\varphi$, whose mass is four. The exact quality is

$$
q=\varphi_4(D_Z\mathcal J_R^{-1}D_Z).
$$

The scaled maps are tensoring with fixed spin matrices followed by total-charge pinching, hence have universal operator-norm and $L^2(\varphi_4)$ bounds. In particular
$$
\|R_Y\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C\varepsilon,\qquad
\|R_Y\|_{2,\varphi_4}\le C\sqrt y.
$$
Because $R_0\ge I/8$, the inverse Jordan map $\mathcal J_{R_0}^{-1}$ has norm at most eight on both spaces, by its positive $\int$ formula. Set
$$
B_0=\mathcal J_{R_0}^{-1}D_Z=B_X+B_3.
$$
Then $\|B_0\|_{\mathrm{op}},\|B_X\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C\varepsilon$ and $\|B_3\|_{2,\varphi_4}\le C\sqrt y$. Positivity of the mean map and $\sigma\ge(1-\varepsilon)\tau$ give $R\ge(1-\varepsilon)R_0\ge I/16$ for $\varepsilon\le1/2$.

For $A=\mathcal J_{R_0}$ and $K=\mathcal J_{R_Y}$, the exact inverse identity is
$$
\begin{split}
q={}&\langle D_Z,A^{-1}D_Z\rangle
 -\langle B_0,KB_0\rangle
 +\langle KB_0,(A+K)^{-1}KB_0\rangle,\\
0\le{}&\langle KB_0,(A+K)^{-1}KB_0\rangle
\le16\|KB_0\|_{2,\varphi_4}^2\le C\varepsilon^2y.
\end{split}
\tag{M.6.13dj.7}
$$
The inner products use $\varphi_4$. The last inequality uses
$\|\mathcal J_{R_Y}B_0\|_2\le\|B_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|R_Y\|_2$.
Traciality identifies the middle term as $-\varphi_4(R_YB_0^2)$. Replacing $B_0^2$ by $B_X^2$ costs at most $C\varepsilon y$: bound each cross term by $\|R_Y\|_2\|B_X\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|B_3\|_2$, and the $B_3^2$ term by $\|R_Y\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|B_3\|_2^2$.

The explicit spin-matrix coefficients below, evaluated on equal-$\tau$-eigenvalue entries, give

$$
\langle D_Z,A^{-1}D_Z\rangle=3x/4+\varphi(Y_3^2)/8.
$$

For the remaining ordered cubic coefficient, the two forward spin paths each contribute $3/16$, since
$$
\sum_{i=0}^{1}
\frac{4p_ip_{i+1}p_{i+2}}
{(p_i+p_{i+1})(p_{i+1}+p_{i+2})}=\frac38.
$$
Two unit-gap steps have charge difference zero or two. The zero component of $Y$ is absent, so the ordered trace is exactly
$\varphi_4(R_YB_X^2)=3\varphi(P_2Y_2)/8$.
Both orientations are already included in this trace; no operator-entry transpose or scalar balancing is used. Consequently
$$
q=\frac34x+\frac18\varphi(Y_3^2)
 -\frac38\varphi(P_2Y_2)+r_q,
\qquad |r_q|\le C\varepsilon y.
\tag{M.6.13dj.8}
$$

**Coercive quartic completion.** The quadratic defect on $Y$ is
$$
E(Y)=\frac12\varphi(Y^2)-\frac1{12}\varphi(Y_3^2)
=\frac12\varphi(Y_2^2)+E(W),\qquad
E(W)\ge\frac5{12}\varphi(W^2).
$$
Subtracting $2q/3$ from (M.6.13dj.6) and completing the square gives, with $\Delta=\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)-2q/3$,
$$
\begin{split}
\Delta&\ge\mathscr P-C\varepsilon[\varphi(X^4)+y],\\
\mathscr P&=\frac1{12}\varphi(P_0^2)
 +\frac5{96}\varphi(P_2^2)
 +\frac12\varphi((Y_2-P_2/4)^2)+E(W).
\end{split}
\tag{M.6.13dj.9}
$$
All four terms are nonnegative. Moreover
$$
\begin{split}
\varphi(X^4)&\le\frac{156}{5}\mathscr P,\\
\varphi(Y_2^2)&\le2\varphi((Y_2-P_2/4)^2)
 +\frac18\varphi(P_2^2)\le\frac{32}{5}\mathscr P,\\
\varphi(W^2)&\le\frac{12}{5}\mathscr P.
\end{split}
$$
Thus $\varphi(X^4)+y\le40\mathscr P$, and
$$
\Delta\ge(1-C\varepsilon)\mathscr P
\ge\frac{1-C\varepsilon}{12}x^2.
\tag{M.6.13dj.10}
$$
The last step is trace variance: $\varphi(P_0^2)\ge\varphi(P_0)^2=x^2$. In particular no upper bound of $\varphi(X^4)$ by a constant times $x^2$ has been assumed.

On any subsequence with $\Delta_n/q_n^2$ bounded above, (M.6.13dj.9)–(M.6.13dj.10) force
$y_n=O(q_n^2)$ and $\varphi_n(X_n^4)=O(q_n^2)$.
Only after this deduction do Cauchy–Schwarz and (M.6.13dj.8) give

$$
q_n=3x_n/4+O(q_n^2).
$$

Therefore $x_n/q_n\to4/3$ and (M.6.13dj.10) proves (M.6.13dj.2). If there is no bounded-above subsequence, the lower bound is immediate. Balanced unit-gap qubits have $q=3c^2/4$ and $\mathcal A=c^2/2+c^4/12+O(c^6)$, proving sharpness. Tensoring them with growing maximally mixed neutral factors preserves both quantities and gives sharp examples with diffuse $\tau=I/d$.

**Explicit scalar Fourier embedding.** We next explain why the same estimates apply to a scalar density close to one. Write $z=e^{i\theta}$, $c_k=\int f(z)z^{-k}d\mu$, $w_i=\sqrt{p_i}$, and
$$
O_{ij}=w_iw_jc_{j-i},\quad
J=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,-1),\quad
R_f=(O+JOJ)/2,\quad D_f=(O-JOJ)/2.
\tag{M.6.13dj.11}
$$
The matrix $O=\int f(z)v(z)v(z)^*d\mu$ with $v_i(z)=w_i z^i$ is positive. The supported bulk quality is exactly
$\operatorname{Tr}(D_f\mathcal J_{R_f}^{-1}D_f)$, so only $c_k$ with $|k|\le3$ enter it, including their imaginary parts.

In the tracial algebra $L^\infty(S^1,\mu)$ let $U(z)=\operatorname{diag}(1,z,z^2,z^3)$. The spin/Fourier embedding has entries $O_{ij}z^{j-i}$ and equals $U(z)^*OU(z)$. It is obtained from the positive matrix function $ww^* f(z)$ by the trace-preserving conditional expectation
$$
\mathbb E(A)(z)=\int U(\zeta)A(\zeta z)U(\zeta)^*d\mu(\zeta).
\tag{M.6.13dj.12}
$$
Indeed the $(i,j)$ entry retains only Fourier mode $j-i$. Its even mean, odd difference and supported Sylvester solution are respectively $U^*R_fU$, $U^*D_fU$ and $U^*B_fU$. Their integrated trace quality is therefore precisely the original constant-matrix $q_{\mathrm{bulk}}(f)$. All preceding operator and trace-$L^2$ bounds apply to this conditional expectation. Scalar multiplication replaces the commutant algebra; circle integration replaces $\varphi$; the entropy functional is $H(f)$. No scalar-to-matrix extrapolation is made.

Consequently (M.6.13dj.6)–(M.6.13dj.10) hold for $Z=f-1$ whenever $\|f-1\|_\infty\to0$. The unit-mode part has the form $X=az+\overline a z^{-1}$ for any complex $a$. In this case
$$
x=2|a|^2,\qquad P_0=x,\qquad
\int P_2^2d\mu=2|a|^4=\frac{x^2}{2},\qquad
\mathscr P\ge\frac7{64}x^2.
\tag{M.6.13dj.13}
$$
Thus every uniformly small scalar perturbation sequence with bounded $\Delta/q^2$ satisfies

$$
\liminf\Delta/q^2\ge(7/64)(4/3)^2=7/36.
$$

**A scalar moment lemma removes all original amplitude assumptions.** Define the six real functions
$$
T(\theta)=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta,\cos2\theta,\sin2\theta,\cos3\theta,\sin3\theta).
$$
For $\lambda\in\mathbb R^6$ put
$$
Z(\lambda)=\int e^{\lambda\cdot T}d\mu,\quad
 g_\lambda=e^{\lambda\cdot T}/Z(\lambda),\quad
 m(\lambda)=\int g_\lambda T\,d\mu.
$$
At zero, $m(0)=0$ and $Dm(0)=\operatorname{Cov}_\mu(T)=I_6/2$. The finite-dimensional inverse-function theorem therefore gives a neighborhood of zero in moment space and a smooth solution $\lambda(m)=O(|m|)$. It follows that $\|g_{\lambda(m)}-1\|_\infty=O(|m|)$. For any normalized density $f$ of finite entropy with these moments, boundedness of $\log g_\lambda$ and moment matching give the exact identity
$$
H(f)-H(g_\lambda)=D(f\Vert g_\lambda)\ge0,
\qquad q_{\mathrm{bulk}}(f)=q_{\mathrm{bulk}}(g_\lambda).
\tag{M.6.13dj.14}
$$
The second identity is (M.6.13dj.11), not a perturbative approximation.

Take any sequence of scalar densities with $q\to0$ and $(H(f)-2q/3)/q^2$ bounded above. The accepted scalar slope bound of (M.6.13di.1)–(M.6.13di.2) gives $H(f)\to0$. Pinsker then implies $\|f-1\|_1\to0$, so all six moments tend to zero. The representative $g_\lambda$ exists and is uniformly close to one. Its quality equals $q$, and its deficit lies between zero and the original deficit, again using that same Gibbs bound.

For clarity that Gibbs bound also covers an originally unbounded scalar density of finite entropy. For its supported finite four-level optimizer $B$, $K_B(\theta)=v_\theta^*(2B-B^2)v_\theta$ is bounded, and Theorem M.6.13ck gives $Z_B=\int e^{(2/3)K_B}d\mu\le1$. Relative entropy against the faithful scalar density $e^{(2/3)K_B}/Z_B$ gives $H(f)=(2/3)q-\log Z_B+D(f\Vert e^{(2/3)K_B}/Z_B)\ge2q/3$. No original amplitude bound enters.
 The local estimate (M.6.13dj.13) applies and proves the lower coefficient $7/36$ for the original sequence. Infinite-entropy densities cannot improve the infimum. Higher harmonics of $g_\lambda$ have not been discarded; they remain in $Y$ and are controlled by its coercivity.

**An exact-quality upper family.** For real $t$ near zero take the positive normalized density
$$
f_t(z)=1+t(z+z^{-1})+\frac{t^2}{4}(z^2+z^{-2}).
\tag{M.6.13dj.15}
$$
Here $X=t(z+z^{-1})$, $P_2=t^2(z^2+z^{-2})$ and $Y=P_2/4$. The analytic entropy and inverse-Jordan expansions give
$$
\begin{split}
H(f_t)&=t^2+\frac5{16}t^4+O(t^6),\\
q_{\mathrm{bulk}}(f_t)&=\frac32t^2-\frac3{16}t^4+O(t^6),\\
H(f_t)-\frac23q_{\mathrm{bulk}}(f_t)&=\frac7{16}t^4+O(t^6).
\end{split}
\tag{M.6.13dj.16}
$$
For the entropy coefficients, the quadratic $Y$ term is $t^4/16$, the two-$X$, one-$Y$ term is $-t^4/4$, and the four-$X$ term is $t^4/2$. For quality, $3\int X^2/4=3t^2/2$ and $-3\int P_2Y/8=-3t^4/16$. Analyticity holds since $R_0>0$; the symmetry $t\mapsto-t$ is the rotation $z\mapsto-z$, so only even powers occur. Equivalently, direct solution of the four real odd-block Sylvester equations gives
$$
q_{\mathrm{bulk}}(f_t)=
\frac{3t^2(3t^4+16t^2-128)}{16(t-2)(t+2)(t^2+4)}.
$$
As a function of $s=t^2$, its derivative at zero is $3/2$. Every sufficiently small exact positive $q$ is therefore attained. The ratio of the last line of (M.6.13dj.16) to $q^2$ tends to $7/36$. Together with the sequential lower bound, choosing approximate infimizers within $o(q^2)$ if necessary, this proves (M.6.13dj.3). $\square$

**Scope and remaining obstruction.** The first assertion extends beyond bounded dephased rank and beyond tightness in a fixed heavy spectral block, but its commutation and relative-operator-norm hypotheses are substantive. Small state quality or entropy alone does not imply them. Relative-norm spikes and noncommuting nonflat means remain outside the proof. In particular no unrestricted $4/27$ theorem, global finite-quality quartic inequality, or growing-dimensional counterexample is obtained.

The second assertion concerns all scalar bulk densities, not arbitrary matrix-valued symbols. Its six-dimensional inverse-function argument is not an operator-valued moment reduction. Fixed-symbol Toeplitz convergence permits a diagonal choice of sizes for the displayed upper family with entropy and quality boundary errors $o(q^2)$. It does not supply a uniform lower estimate for arbitrary jointly varying symbols and sizes: the entropy boundary loss has the opposite sign in the deficit and must be controlled separately. All correlations, flags and neutral factors remain counted wherever the stated hypotheses apply. No operational equality $u=q$, sharp unrestricted operational second-order coefficient, dimension optimum, physical identification, preparation or readout price, or hardware conclusion follows. The complete-reference global bounds in Theorem M.6.13cm, bounded-dimension state curvature in Theorem M.6.13cr and the balanced-qubit upper family retain their stated domains.

<a id="theorem-m613dk-a-fifteen-dimensional-spin-one-upper-curve-with-improved-quadratic-coefficient"></a>**Theorem M.6.13dk (A Fifteen-Dimensional Spin-One Upper Curve with Improved Quadratic Coefficient).** Use the complete spin-one class of Theorem M.6.13cd, with $Q_S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2)$, $X=J_x$, natural-log asymmetry and all system inputs tested. Write
$$
F_{\mathrm{quality}}(u)=F_{\mathrm{error}}(1-u),
\qquad 0<u<1,
$$
where $F_{\mathrm{error}}$ is the at-most-squared-error infimum in (M.6.13dc.1). Let $z_*,c=c_*$ be the exact spin-one constants of Theorem M.6.13cd, and put $\alpha=1-\lambda_*$. Define
$$
\begin{gathered}
p=\frac{1-z_*}{3-z_*},\qquad q=\frac{1+z_*}{3-z_*}=1-2p,
\qquad d=q-p,\qquad g=\frac{\log q-\log p}{d},\\
A=\alpha q+2(1-\alpha)p,\qquad
B=\alpha p+2(1-\alpha)q,\qquad
a_0=\frac{\sqrt2}{A},\quad b_0=\frac{\sqrt2}{B},\quad
\gamma=2\left(\frac1A+\frac1B\right),\\
\ell=\frac{2}{d}\left(g-\frac1p\right)+c\alpha b_0^2,
\qquad k=-\frac p2\ell.
\end{gathered}
\tag{M.6.13dk.1}
$$
For $0\le h\le1/1000$, set
$$
\begin{gathered}
\sigma_h=\begin{pmatrix}p&\sqrt h&kh\\\sqrt h&q&\sqrt h\\kh&\sqrt h&p\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
R_h=\sqrt{\frac{2q-p-kh}{q-2p}},\\
b_h=\frac{R_h+1}{\sqrt2(pR_h^2+q)},\qquad a_h=R_hb_h,
\qquad
u(h)=h\frac{(R_h+1)^2}{pR_h^2+q}.
\end{gathered}
\tag{M.6.13dk.2}
$$
These are positive definite states. A complete finite conserving apparatus with charged-reference dimension three and neutral-pointer dimension five has exactly worst-case squared error $1-u(h)$ and asymmetry
$$
\begin{aligned}
C(h)&=(p-kh)\log(p-kh)+\lambda_+(h)\log\lambda_+(h)
 +\lambda_-(h)\log\lambda_-(h)-2p\log p-q\log q,\\
\lambda_\pm(h)&=\frac{p+q+kh\pm\sqrt{(q-p-kh)^2+8h}}2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13dk.3}
$$
The function $u(h)$ is strictly increasing on this interval and $u(1/1000)>1/200$. Consequently, for every $0<u\le1/200$, its unique inverse $h(u)$ supplies the exact finite-error upper bound
$$
F_{\mathrm{quality}}(u)\le C(h(u))
=cu+K_{15}u^2+O(u^3),
\tag{M.6.13dk.4}
$$
where
$$
\begin{aligned}
K_{15}
&=\frac{1}{\gamma^2}
\left[\frac{2}{d^2}\left(\frac1p+\frac1q-2g\right)-\frac p4\ell^2\right]\\
&=0.2088001364002746834919611594\ldots<\frac{21}{100}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13dk.5}
$$
The parameter $k$ uniquely minimizes this quadratic coefficient among the stated fixed-diagonal qutrit families with order-$h$ gap-two coherence and the balanced observables below. The coefficient is strictly smaller than the $0.2803776091137677879\ldots$ coefficient of the fixed reflected-qubit family in M.6.13cd.U1–U8. In particular, combining this upper family with Theorem M.6.13cg gives
$$
\frac2{10^{23}}\le\liminf_{u\downarrow0}\frac{F_{\mathrm{quality}}(u)-cu}{u^2}
\le\limsup_{u\downarrow0}\frac{F_{\mathrm{quality}}(u)-cu}{u^2}\le K_{15};
$$
existence of a common quadratic limit is not asserted.

*Proof.* **Scalar domain.** The exact root enclosure in Theorem M.6.13cd gives
$$
\frac{18}{100}<p<\frac{19}{100},\quad
\frac{62}{100}<q<\frac{64}{100},\quad
1<k<\frac{11}{10},\quad 6<\gamma<7.
\tag{M.6.13dk.6}
$$
These scalar bounds can be checked without evaluating a matrix certificate. Use the rational enclosure of Theorem M.6.13cd,
$$
\frac{543396061494967788075712375250}{10^{30}}
<z_*<
\frac{543396061494967788075712375251}{10^{30}},
$$
put $s=\sqrt{9z_*^2-1}$, and substitute
$$
\operatorname{atanh}z_* =\frac{s}{3(1-z_*^2)},\quad
\alpha=2-\frac{4z_*}{s},\quad
c=\frac{4s}{3(1-z_*^2)(3z_*+s)},\quad
g=\frac{2s}{3(1-z_*^2)d}
$$
into (M.6.13dk.1). All remaining operations are rational operations and positive square roots. For an explicit rational enclosure rule, round each operation outwards to denominator $2^{192}$; a square root is bounded by the adjacent multiples of $2^{-192}$, found by integer-square comparison. Every division denominator in these formulas has strictly positive lower endpoint. The same finite calculation gives
$$
\frac{1046965914}{10^9}<k<\frac{1046965915}{10^9},\qquad
\frac{20880013640027468}{10^{17}}<K_{15}
<\frac{20880013640027469}{10^{17}}.
\tag{M.6.13dk.7}
$$
The root $z_*$ and its certificate are those of Theorem M.6.13cd.

For the full parameter interval, the coarse rational bounds suffice. They give
$$
\frac{24}{100}<q-2p<\frac{28}{100},\qquad
\frac{105}{100}<2q-p<\frac{110}{100},\qquad
\frac{19}{10}<R_h<\frac{22}{10},
$$
$$
\frac54<pR_h^2+q<\frac85,\qquad
b_h^2<4,\qquad a_h^2<16,\qquad
5< G_h:=\frac{(R_h+1)^2}{pR_h^2+q}<9.
\tag{M.6.13dk.8}
$$
Reflection decomposes $\sigma_h$ into the eigenvalue $p-kh$ and the two-by-two matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p+kh&\sqrt{2h}\\\sqrt{2h}&q\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Here $p-kh>0$ and $q(p+kh)-2h>0$, so the state is faithful; its trace is one. This also proves (M.6.13dk.3).

**Complete noise and exact balancing.** Put $Q_R=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2)$ on the charged reference, and define
$$
\begin{gathered}
L_0=\sqrt h\left(a_h|1\rangle\langle0|+b_h|2\rangle\langle1|\right),\qquad
L_1=\sqrt h\left(b_h|1\rangle\langle0|+a_h|2\rangle\langle1|\right),\\
N_h=\begin{pmatrix}0&L_0&0\\L_0^*&0&L_1\\0&L_1^*&0\end{pmatrix}.
\end{gathered}
\tag{M.6.13dk.9}
$$
The raising commutators make $N_h$ conserve $Q_S+Q_R$. In the system basis $e=(|0\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $m=|1\rangle$, $o=(|0\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, direct multiplication gives the full conditional-noise matrix diagonal entries
$$
\begin{aligned}
K_e&=1-2\sqrt2h(a_h+b_h)+h(qa_h^2+pb_h^2)+kh^2b_h^2,\\
K_m&=1-2\sqrt2h(a_h+b_h)+2h(pa_h^2+qb_h^2),\\
K_o&=h(qa_h^2+pb_h^2)-kh^2b_h^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13dk.10}
$$
Parity and reflection make every off-diagonal entry zero; in particular the gap-two terms have not been dropped. The definition of $R_h$ makes $K_e=K_m$. Maximizing their common gain at this ratio gives the displayed $b_h$ and
$$
K_e=K_m=1-u(h).
$$
By (M.6.13dk.8), $K_o<11h\le11/1000$, whereas $1-u(h)>991/1000$. Thus the worst-case squared error over all system inputs is exactly $1-u(h)$.

The total-charge blocks of $N_h$ have spectral values among
$$
0,\quad\pm\sqrt h\,a_h,\quad\pm\sqrt{2h}\,b_h.
$$
Retain all five labels in a neutral pointer, initially pure. If $N_h=\sum_j\nu_j\Pi_j$ and $V$ is the five-cycle on pointer labels, the conserving unitary $\sum_j\Pi_j\otimes V^j$ and pointer $\sum_j\nu_j|j\rangle\langle j|$ reproduce $N_h,N_h^2$ upon ready-state compression. At $h=0$, coincident labels cause no difficulty. The complete reference dimension is $3\cdot5=15$, and no flag or purification is required. The neutral pointer contributes zero asymmetry but remains counted. Theorem M.6.13df gives, separately, its registered binary energy host with at most $2^{18}$ full system-inclusive dimensions.

For monotonicity, write $G(R)=(R+1)^2/(pR^2+q)$. On (M.6.13dk.8),
$$
G'(R)=\frac{2(R+1)(q-pR)}{(pR^2+q)^2},\qquad
\left|G'(R)\right|<5,\qquad
\left|\frac{dR_h}{dh}\right|=\frac{k}{2(q-2p)R_h}<\frac54.
$$
Hence $u'(h)=G(R_h)+hG'(R_h)R_h'>5-7/1000>0$. Also $u(1/1000)>1/200$. This proves the exact-quality interval and inverse assertion.

**Quadratic improvement.** Temporarily replace $k$ by any fixed real $k'$; for sufficiently small $h$ all the preceding matrices and balancing formulas remain valid. The three eigenvalues of $\sigma_h$ have expansions
$$
\begin{aligned}
\lambda_o&=p-k'h,\\
\lambda_+&=q+\frac{2}{d}h+\left(\frac{2k'}{d^2}-\frac4{d^3}\right)h^2+O(h^3),\\
\lambda_-&=p+\left(k'-\frac2d\right)h+\left(-\frac{2k'}{d^2}+\frac4{d^3}\right)h^2+O(h^3).
\end{aligned}
$$
Taylor expansion of $x\log x$ at the positive numbers $p,q$ yields
$$
C(h)=2gh+\left[
\frac{(k')^2}{p}+\frac{2k'}d\left(g-\frac1p\right)
+\frac2{d^2}\left(\frac1p+\frac1q-2g\right)\right]h^2+O(h^3).
\tag{M.6.13dk.11}
$$
At $h=0$, $R_0=a_0/b_0$ and $G(R_0)=\gamma$. They follow by substituting $R_0=(3z_*+1)/\sqrt{9z_*^2-1}$ into (M.6.13dk.1)–(M.6.13dk.2). The weighted bright gain with fixed weight $\alpha$ is stationary in both amplitudes at $a_0,b_0$. The new gap-two coherence changes only its $e$ contribution, by $-\alpha k'b_0^2h$ after dividing the gain by $h$. Differentiating the balanced gain therefore gives
$$
u(h)=\gamma h-\alpha k'b_0^2h^2+O(h^3),
\qquad 2g=c\gamma.
\tag{M.6.13dk.12}
$$
The same derivative follows directly from the explicit $R_h,G(R_h)$ formulas. Combining (M.6.13dk.11)–(M.6.13dk.12) and inverting $u(h)$ gives the quadratic coefficient
$$
\frac1{\gamma^2}
\left[\frac{(k')^2}{p}+\ell k'
+\frac2{d^2}\left(\frac1p+\frac1q-2g\right)\right].
$$
It is strictly convex in $k'$ and has its unique minimum at $k'=-p\ell/2$, proving (M.6.13dk.5). The entropy and inverse functions are analytic in $h$ near zero, so the remainder in (M.6.13dk.4) is $O(u^3)$ for this fixed family.

For comparison, put $U_*=3/2+\sqrt{9z_*^2-1}/(2z_*)$. The fixed reflected family of M.6.13cd has cost
$$
C_{20}(u)=h_2((1-z_*)/2)
-h_2\left(\frac{1+\sqrt{z_*^2+4u/U_*}}2\right).
$$
Its quadratic coefficient is
$$
K_{20}=\frac{2}{U_*^2z_*^3}
\left[\frac{z_*}{1-z_*^2}-\operatorname{atanh}z_*\right]
=0.2803776091137677879\ldots>K_{15}.
$$
The same rational enclosure rule gives this strict comparison. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613eb-irreducible-reference-block-reduction-and-the-limits-of-flags"></a>**Theorem M.6.13eb (Irreducible Reference-Block Reduction and the Limits of Flags).** Use the spin-one system $Q_S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2)$, $X=J_x$ and the notation of Theorem M.6.13dc. For a finite reference $(R,Q)$, an invariant Hermitian $B$ and $Z\succeq0$ put $V_Z(B)=\operatorname{Tr}_S[(Z\otimes I)(B-X\otimes I)^2]$ and
$$
\beta_Q(B;Z)=\min_\sigma\bigl\{\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)+\operatorname{Tr}\sigma V_Z(B)\bigr\},
\tag{M.6.13eb.1}
$$
the minimum over density matrices on $R$; it exists because the state space is compact and $\mathcal A_Q$ is continuous. Thus $b(Z)=\inf_{R,Q,B}\beta_Q(B;Z)$ in (M.6.13dc.1).

1. Write $B=\sum_{ij}|i\rangle\langle j|\otimes B_{ij}$ in the system charge basis, let $\mathcal C$ be the unital $*$-algebra generated by $Q$ and all $B_{ij}$, and let $P_1,\ldots,P_n$ be orthogonal minimal reducing projections of $\mathcal C$ with $\sum_jP_j=I$. With $Q_j,B_j$ the restrictions of $Q,B$ to $R_j=P_jR$ and $\mathcal H_S\otimes R_j$,
$$
\beta_Q(B;Z)=\min_j\beta_{Q_j}(B_j;Z).
\tag{M.6.13eb.2}
$$
Equivalently, the partition supremum of (M.6.13dc.5) at fixed $(Q,B)$ over invariant $\tau$ equals the largest of its block suprema, also when $\tau$ is allowed coherence between equivalent blocks. Hence $b(Z)$ is the infimum over models on which $\mathcal C$ acts irreducibly.
2. For a model with retained flag branches $j$ of weights $p_j$, $K=\sum_jp_jK_j$ and $\mathcal A=\sum_jp_j\mathcal A_j$, and for block-diagonal invariant $\tau=\bigoplus_jp_j\tau_j$ and $V=\bigoplus_jV_j$, $\operatorname{Tr}e^{\log\tau-V}=\sum_jp_j\operatorname{Tr}e^{\log\tau_j-V_j}$. The partition value of a flagged model is therefore at most its largest branch value. Every finite branch list can be replaced by at most $d_S^2+1=10$ of its branches with the same $K$ and no larger $\mathcal A$; if every $K_j$ is diagonal in the basis $(e,m,f)$ of Theorem M.6.13dc, four branches suffice.
3. If a finite model attains $F(r)$ and $Z$ is a maximizing multiplier in (M.6.13dc.2), then after the pinching of item 1 every occupied branch satisfies
$$
\mathcal A_j+\operatorname{Tr}ZK_j=b(Z).
\tag{M.6.13eb.3}
$$
Consequently $F(r)$ has a finite attainer only if $b(Z)$ is attained by a finite model on which $\mathcal C$ acts irreducibly.
4. For every $d\ge2$ let $R=\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^d$, $Q=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)\otimes I_d$, $J=\sum_{k=1}^{d-1}|k\rangle\langle k+1|$, $L_0=|1\rangle\langle0|\otimes I_d$, $L_1=|1\rangle\langle0|\otimes(I_d+J/2)$, and
$$
B=s\bigl(|0\rangle\langle1|\otimes L_0+|1\rangle\langle2|\otimes L_1+\mathrm{h.c.}\bigr),\qquad s>0.
\tag{M.6.13eb.4}
$$
Then $B$ conserves $Q_S+Q$, $\|B\|\le\frac52s$, and $\mathcal C$ acts irreducibly on the $2d$-dimensional reference. For $0<\epsilon<1$ the state $\sigma=\frac1{2d}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}I_d&\epsilon I_d\\\epsilon I_d&I_d\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is faithful, $\mathcal G_Q\sigma=I/(2d)$, and with $s=2\sqrt2\,\epsilon/25$,
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)=\frac{(1+\epsilon)\log(1+\epsilon)+(1-\epsilon)\log(1-\epsilon)}2,
\qquad
\mathfrak q_\lambda(\sigma)\ge\frac{2\epsilon^2}{25}
\tag{M.6.13eb.5}
$$
for every $\lambda$ in (M.6.13cd.S2), uniformly in $d$. A fixed system, two reference charge values, bounded observable norm, bounded asymmetry and positive weighted gain therefore do not bound the irreducible reference dimension.

*Proof.* Let $\mathcal P(\sigma)=\sum_jP_j\sigma P_j$. Every $P_j$ commutes with $Q$ and with every $B_{ij}$, so $\mathcal P$ commutes with $\mathcal G_Q$, and $(B-X\otimes I)^2$ is block diagonal for $I\otimes P_j$. Hence $K_{\mathcal P(\sigma)}(B)=K_\sigma(B)$, and data processing gives
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\mathcal P(\sigma))=D(\mathcal P(\sigma)\Vert\mathcal P(\mathcal G_Q\sigma))\le D(\sigma\Vert\mathcal G_Q\sigma)=\mathcal A_Q(\sigma),
$$
including singular states. Write $\mathcal P(\sigma)=\bigoplus_jp_j\sigma_j$, omitting zero weights. The Shannon entropy of the block label cancels, so
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\mathcal P(\sigma))=\sum_jp_j\mathcal A_{Q_j}(\sigma_j),\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}\mathcal P(\sigma)V_Z(B)=\sum_jp_j\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_jV_Z(B_j).
$$
Their sum is at least $\min_j\beta_{Q_j}(B_j;Z)$. Conversely, a minimizing state of one block, extended by zero, is a state on $R$ with the same objective, because $\mathcal G_Q$ acts inside $R_j$. This proves (M.6.13eb.2).
