For fixed $(Q,B)$, $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)=\inf_\tau D(\sigma\Vert\tau)$ over faithful invariant $\tau$ and the Gibbs variational identity give $e^{-\beta_Q(B;Z)}=\sup_\tau\operatorname{Tr}e^{\log\tau-V_Z(B)}$, which turns (M.6.13eb.2) into the partition statement without assuming $\tau$ block diagonal. Applying item 1 to every finite model gives the reduction of $b(Z)$.

Item 2 is (M.6.13dc.4) together with $\sum_jp_jx_j\le\max_jx_j$. For the branch count, minimize $\sum_jp_j\mathcal A_j$ over $p\ge0$ subject to $\sum_jp_j=1$ and $\sum_jp_jK_j=K$. These are $1+d_S^2$ real linear equations, so a minimizing basic feasible solution has at most $d_S^2+1$ positive coordinates; diagonal $K_j$ leave $1+3$ equations.

For item 3, a finite attainer has $\mathcal A=F(r)$ and $K\preceq rI$. The pinching of item 1 keeps $K$ and cannot lower $\mathcal A$ below $F(r)$, so it keeps $\mathcal A=F(r)$. With (M.6.13dc.2),
$$
\sum_jp_j\bigl(\mathcal A_j+\operatorname{Tr}ZK_j\bigr)=F(r)+\operatorname{Tr}ZK\le F(r)+r\operatorname{Tr}Z=b(Z),
$$
while each branch is a finite model and has objective at least $b(Z)$. Hence every occupied branch has objective exactly $b(Z)$, and each branch is irreducible by construction.

For item 4, every entry of $B$ moves one unit of system charge against one unit of reference charge, so $B$ conserves $Q_S+Q$. Its two Hermitian off-diagonal system terms have norms $\|L_0\|=1$ and $\|L_1\|\le3/2$, so $\|B\|\le\frac52s$. A reducing projection commutes with $Q$, hence equals $\operatorname{diag}(P_0,P_1)$. Commutation with $L_0$ and $L_0^*$ forces $P_0=P_1=P$, and commutation with $L_1$ and $L_1^*$ then gives $[P,J]=[P,J^*]=0$. The truncated shift and its adjoint generate $M_d(\mathbb C)$: $I-J^*J$ and $I-JJ^*$ are rank-one end projections, and translating them by powers of $J$ gives every matrix unit. So $P$ is $0$ or $I$. The state $\sigma$ has eigenvalues $(1\pm\epsilon)/(2d)$, each $d$ times, and $\mathcal G_Q\sigma=I/(2d)$, which gives the asymmetry in (M.6.13eb.5). Since $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma L_0=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma L_1=\epsilon/2$ (using $\operatorname{Tr}J=0$),
$$
\operatorname{Tr}[(X\otimes\sigma)B]=\sqrt2\,s\epsilon,\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}[(\rho_\lambda\otimes\sigma)B^2]\le\|B\|^2\le\tfrac{25}4s^2.
$$
At $s=2\sqrt2\,\epsilon/25$ the difference is $2\epsilon^2/25$, independent of $d$. $\square$

In item 4 the state is the product of a qubit state with the maximally mixed state of $\mathbb C^d$, so the example says nothing about optimal models; it shows that irreducibility together with the stated bounded data does not bound the reference dimension.

<a id="theorem-m613ec"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613ec-spin-one-zero-pressure-classification-and-finite-attainment"></a>**Theorem M.6.13ec (Spin-One Zero-Pressure Classification and Finite Attainment).** Use the complete finite-reference problem and pressure $b(Z)$ of Theorem M.6.13dc, with $Q_S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2)$, $X=J_x$, and $X_{01}=X_{12}=1/\sqrt2$ as the nonzero upper entries. For a unit vector $v$ in the system charge basis set $j_i(v)=\operatorname{Im}(\bar v_i(Xv)_i)$. For every $Z\succeq0$, the following hold.

1. The pressure is zero exactly when $\operatorname{supp}Z\subseteq\operatorname{span}\{|0\rangle,|2\rangle\}$ or $Z=\lambda|v\rangle\langle v|$ with $\lambda>0$ and $j_i(v)=0$ for every $i$.
2. A finite model attains objective zero exactly when a real diagonal $D$ satisfies $(D-X)\operatorname{supp}Z=0$. Apart from $Z=0$, the finite attainers occur for rank-one testers supported on the dark line $\operatorname{span}(|0\rangle-|2\rangle)$ or on vectors with all three entries nonzero and real after one common phase rotation.
3. If $j_i(v)\ne0$ for some $i$, put $c_i=\operatorname{Im}((Xv)_i/v_i)$ on the nonzero coordinates $I$ of $v$, $V=\sum_{i\in I}|v_i|^2c_i^2$, and $\Delta=\max_{i\in I}c_i-\min_{i\in I}c_i$. Then, for every $\lambda>0$,
$$
b(\lambda|v\rangle\langle v|)\ge V\min\{\lambda,\Delta^{-2}\}>0.
\tag{M.6.13ec.1}
$$
In particular a positive multiplier supported on the middle-state line has zero pressure and no finite attainer. Its score in the dual at positive radius $r$ is $-r\operatorname{Tr}Z$.

*Proof.* Every conserving Hermitian $B$ used below has the neutral, retained spectral-pointer realization of Theorem M.6.13dc. In any finite model attaining zero, charge pinching gives $\sigma=\mathcal G_Q\sigma$ because $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)=D(\sigma\Vert\mathcal G_Q\sigma)$. Conservation then makes the reference expectation $D=\Phi_\sigma(B)$ real diagonal, where $\Phi_\sigma(T)=\operatorname{Tr}_R[(I\otimes\sigma)T]$. The completely positive unital map $\Phi_\sigma$ obeys $\Phi_\sigma(B^2)\succeq D^2$. Hence $K_\sigma(B)\succeq(D-X)^2$ and vanishing tested noise forces $(D-X)\operatorname{supp}Z=0$. The converse uses $B=D$ and a one-dimensional reference. The kernel of $D-X$ has dimension at most one because the tridiagonal equations determine $v_1,v_2$ from $v_0$. If $v_1\ne0$, the endpoint equations force both endpoint coordinates nonzero with real ratios to $v_1$. If $v_1=0$, the middle equation forces $v_2=-v_0$. Each listed vector solves the equations with a suitable real diagonal $D$.

For the zero-infimum constructions, use the pure three-charge reference $|\psi_\delta\rangle=\sqrt\delta|0\rangle+\sqrt{1-2\delta}|1\rangle+\sqrt\delta|2\rangle$, $0<\delta<1/2$. Its asymmetry is $-2\delta\log\delta-(1-2\delta)\log(1-2\delta)$, which tends to zero. For a current-free vector $v$, project $v\otimes\psi_\delta$ and $(Xv)\otimes\psi_\delta$ onto each total-charge sector and denote the vectors by $\chi_q,w_q$. Each inner product $\langle\chi_q,w_q\rangle$ is real, by the assumed coordinate currents. When $\chi_q\ne0$ the Hermitian block
$$
B_q=\frac{|w_q\rangle\langle\chi_q|+|\chi_q\rangle\langle w_q|}{\|\chi_q\|^2}
-\frac{\langle\chi_q,w_q\rangle}{\|\chi_q\|^4}|\chi_q\rangle\langle\chi_q|
$$
sends $\chi_q$ to $w_q$. Take $B_q=0$ otherwise. Any nonzero desired component $(Xv)_i|i,1\rangle$ has some adjacent $v_j\ne0$. The same total-charge sector contains the input component $|j,1+i-j\rangle$ with nonzero amplitude. Thus unfitted components lie only on the reference tail charges $0,2$ and the tested noise is at most $2\delta\|Xv\|^2$.

For all endpoint vectors simultaneously, use only the total-charge-two block of $B$. Couple each of $|0,2\rangle$ and $|2,0\rangle$ to $|1,1\rangle$ by the real matrix element $\sqrt{(1-2\delta)/(2\delta)}$ and include the Hermitian conjugate. On an endpoint input this fits exactly the central-reference component of the target. The two remaining reference charges contribute squared error $2\delta\|Xv\|^2$ for each endpoint vector, giving a vanishing bound uniformly on that plane. These constructions prove the asserted zero pressures on the given supports.

To prove the lower bound, compress the output system to the charge coordinates $I$ on which $v_i\ne0$. This can only lower the tested noise. For each total charge $q$, define the filter $D_q=\sum_{i\in I}v_i|i\rangle\otimes P_{q-i}$, with $P_\ell$ the reference charge projections and absent projections zero. The map $\sigma\mapsto\rho=\bigoplus_qD_q\sigma D_q^*$ is CPTP because $\sum_qD_q^*D_q=I$. Pinching $\rho$ by the system label within each $q$ gives $\mathcal E\rho=\bigoplus_qD_q(\mathcal G_Q\sigma)D_q^*$, so $D(\rho\Vert\mathcal E\rho)\le\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)$. In these sectors the compressed target is multiplication by $H=\operatorname{diag}((Xv)_i/v_i)$. Write $C=\operatorname{Im}H$ for its diagonal imaginary parts and $T=B-\operatorname{Re}H$ for a Hermitian variable. The noise is bounded below by the minimum of
$$
\operatorname{Tr}[(T-iC)\rho(T+iC)]
=V+\operatorname{Tr}(\rho T^2)-\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(i[C,\rho]T\right),
$$
where $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho C^2)=V$. Completing the quadratic using $\mathcal S_\rho(T)=(\rho T+T\rho)/2$ gives the minimum $V-\tfrac14 F_{\mathrm{SLD}}(\rho,C)$, with $F_{\mathrm{SLD}}=\operatorname{Tr}(i[C,\rho]\mathcal S_\rho^{+}(i[C,\rho]))$ and the Moore–Penrose inverse on the full matrix space. The commutator has no entries in the joint kernel of $\mathcal S_\rho$.

Here $F_{\mathrm{SLD}}(\rho,C)\le4\Delta^2D(\rho\Vert\mathcal E\rho)$. In the eigenbasis of $\rho$, $(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)^2\le2(a+b)$ gives $F_{\mathrm{SLD}}(\rho,C)\le4\|[C,\sqrt\rho]\|_{\mathrm F}^2$. The latter commutator is supported on off-pinching blocks and its norm is at most $\Delta\|\sqrt\rho-\mathcal E\sqrt\rho\|_{\mathrm F}$. Jensen's inequality in the eigenbases of $\rho$ and $\mathcal E\rho$ gives $D(\rho\Vert\mathcal E\rho)\ge-2\log\operatorname{Tr}(\sqrt\rho\sqrt{\mathcal E\rho})$. Since $\sqrt{\mathcal E\rho}$ is pinching-invariant with Frobenius norm one, the trace in that bound is at most $\|\mathcal E\sqrt\rho\|_{\mathrm F}$. Orthogonal decomposition and $-\log(1-x)\ge x$ now give $D(\rho\Vert\mathcal E\rho)\ge\|\sqrt\rho-\mathcal E\sqrt\rho\|_{\mathrm F}^2$. These spectral inequalities include singular states. Thus the tested noise is at least $\max\{0,V-\Delta^2\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\}$. The mean of the $c_i$ with weights $|v_i|^2$ is zero, so a nonzero current gives $V,\Delta>0$. Minimization of $a+\lambda\max\{0,V-\Delta^2a\}$ over $a\ge0$ gives (M.6.13ec.1).

If the support of $Z$ contains a vector of nonzero current, $Z$ dominates its rank-one projector times the least positive eigenvalue of $Z$. Monotonicity of the pressure and (M.6.13ec.1) then give positive pressure. A two-dimensional subspace on which all currents vanish must contain $|2\rangle$. Otherwise projection onto coordinates $(0,1)$ is an isomorphism, and the nonzero Hermitian form for $j_0$ on those coordinates could not vanish on every projected vector. Applying the same argument to $j_2$ forces $|0\rangle$. The full three-dimensional space contains a nonzero-current vector. Together with the constructions this exhausts the zero set. ∎

The zero-pressure classification excludes every nonzero tester in that set from maximizing the dual at $r>0$, since the zero tester has score zero. The remaining positive pressures, all-input frontier and finite attainment at positive error require separate bounds.

<a id="theorem-m613ed"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613ed-exact-two-charge-spin-one-threshold-and-entropy-at-the-threshold"></a>**Theorem M.6.13ed (Exact Two-Charge Spin-One Threshold and Entropy at the Threshold).** Use the spin-one system, complete finite reference and squared all-input error of Theorem M.6.13dc. Restrict the reference to at most two distinct charge values, allowing arbitrary finite multiplicities, mixed states, correlations and neutral factors. The least squared error is $1/2$. At this error the least asymmetry is
$$
h_2\!\left(\frac{1-1/\sqrt5}{2}\right),
\tag{M.6.13ed.1}
$$
where $h_2(p)=-p\log p-(1-p)\log(1-p)$. A four-dimensional reference carrying a neutral flag, implemented with a five-level neutral pointer, attains both limits. In particular, every complete apparatus of squared error less than $1/2$ uses at least three distinct charges.

*Proof.* Let $c=1/\sqrt2$. The parity $P=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)$ commutes with the system charge and reverses $X=J_x$. Replace any invariant Hermitian measurement observable $B$ by $(B-PBP)/2$, with $P$ acting trivially on the reference. The square of the resulting error operator is bounded above by the mean of the two original parity-related squares. This preserves the all-input error constraint and the reference asymmetry. The odd observable has the form
$$
B=\begin{pmatrix}0&A&0\\ A^*&0&T\\0&T^*&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad [Q_R,A]=A,\quad [Q_R,T]=T.
$$
With fewer than two charges or with a gap other than one, both raising operators vanish and the squared error is at least one. For a unit gap write the reference state as $\sigma=\begin{pmatrix}C&W^*\\W&D\end{pmatrix}$, lower charge first. Compress to the two diagonal supports. This keeps the entropy and the linear observable moments and can only lower the error square, because the discarded second-moment excursion is positive. On the retained supports the nonempty blocks $C,D$ are positive definite. Positivity gives $W=D^{1/2}VC^{1/2}$ for a contraction $V$ between those supports.

The middle-system noise has the two independent least-squares terms
$$
K_{11}=1+\operatorname{Tr}(C A^*A)+\operatorname{Tr}(DTT^*)-2c\,\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(W^*(A+T)\bigr).
$$
Their minimizers are $A=cWC^{-1}$ and $T=cD^{-1}W$, with an empty block contributing zero. The resulting lower bound is
$$
K_{11}\ge 1-\frac12\left[\operatorname{Tr}(D VV^*)+\operatorname{Tr}(C V^*V)\right]\ge\frac12 .
\tag{M.6.13ed.2}
$$
At squared error $1/2$ every inequality is equality. Both supports are nonempty, and their positivity gives $VV^*=I$ and $V^*V=I$. Identify the upper space with the lower by $V$ and keep the notation $D$ for its transported state block. Then
$$
W=D^{1/2}C^{1/2},\qquad A=cD^{1/2}C^{-1/2},\qquad T=cD^{-1/2}C^{1/2}.
$$
The endpoint diagonal noise entries are
$$
K_{00}=\frac12+\frac12\operatorname{Tr}(D^2 C^{-1})-\operatorname{Tr}D,\qquad
K_{22}=\frac12+\frac12\operatorname{Tr}(C^2 D^{-1})-\operatorname{Tr}C .
\tag{M.6.13ed.3}
$$
In particular $K\preceq I/2$ requires $\operatorname{Tr}(D^2 C^{-1}+C^2 D^{-1})\le2$.

Put $E=C+D$, $L=E^{-1/2}CE^{-1/2}$ and write $L=\sum_j p_j |j\rangle\langle j|$. Here $0<p_j<1$ and $w_j=\langle j|E|j\rangle$ is a probability distribution. Expanding $C=E-D$ and $D=E-C$ under the trace gives
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(D^2 C^{-1}+C^2D^{-1})
=\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(E[L^{-1}+(I-L)^{-1}]\bigr)-3
=\sum_j\frac{w_j}{p_j(1-p_j)}-3 .
\tag{M.6.13ed.4}
$$
The nonzero spectra of $\sigma$ and $E$ coincide because $\sigma=UU^*$ for the column $U=(C^{1/2},D^{1/2})^{\mathsf T}$ with $U^*U=E$. Thus the asymmetry is $S(C\oplus D)-S(E)$, the conditional entropy of a classical charge bit with quantum record given by the subnormalized states $C,D$. This joint state is obtained from a classical record $j$ of weight $w_j$ and conditional charge probability $p_j$ by replacing $j$ with the pure state $E^{1/2}|j\rangle/\sqrt{w_j}$. Data processing of mutual information gives
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge \sum_j w_j h_2(p_j).
\tag{M.6.13ed.5}
$$
For $v\ge4$ define $g(v)=h_2((1-\sqrt{1-4/v})/2)$. It is decreasing and convex. Indeed, with $z=\sqrt{1-4/v}$, its derivative is $-(1-z^2)^2\operatorname{artanh}(z)/(8z)$, continuous at $z=0$. The derivative of $(1-z^2)^2\operatorname{artanh}(z)/z$ has the sign of $z-(1+3z^2)\operatorname{artanh}(z)$, which is negative for $0<z<1$. Equations (M.6.13ed.4)–(M.6.13ed.5) and Jensen's inequality now give $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge g(5)$.

For attainment put $p=(1-1/\sqrt5)/2$ and use the two-charge pure reference $\sqrt p\,|0\rangle+\sqrt{1-p}\,|1\rangle$ with the displayed optimal $A,T$. Its middle noise is $1/2$ and its endpoint diagonal sum is one by (M.6.13ed.4). The endpoint off-diagonal noise is zero. Indeed $AT=0$ on a two-charge reference and $K_{02}=c^2-c\,\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(A+T)=0$ by the minimizing formulas. Parity gives the other off-diagonal zeros. Reflect the system charge labels $0,2$ and reverse the reference charge by $Q_R\mapsto I-Q_R$ to obtain the second branch. The reflected observable still conserves total charge and the reflected model has the endpoint entries interchanged. Take an equal mixture with a retained neutral branch flag. This has $K=I/2$ and retains the asymmetry $h_2(p)$ by (M.6.13dc.4). Both branches use exactly the charge values $0,1$. The observable has two nontrivial two-dimensional total-charge blocks in each branch and has eigenvalues $0,\ \pm c\sqrt{(1-p)/p},\ \pm c\sqrt{p/(1-p)}$. The spectral-pointer construction of Theorem M.6.13dc therefore uses five neutral labels. The complete reference and pointer dimension is twenty, with the same two distinct charges. ∎

<a id="theorem-m613ee"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613ee-exact-three-charge-spin-one-threshold-and-entropy-at-the-threshold"></a>**Theorem M.6.13ee (Exact Three-Charge Spin-One Threshold and Entropy at the Threshold).** Use the system, complete finite reference and squared all-input error of Theorem M.6.13dc. Restrict the reference to at most three distinct charge values, with arbitrary finite multiplicities and mixed states. Let $g$ be the unique root of $8g^4+12g^3-4g^2-8g+1$ in $(7317/10000,3659/5000)$, and put
$$
t=\frac{2g+3}{4g^2+4g-1},\qquad
b=\frac1{1+t},\qquad a=\frac{1-b}{2}.
$$
The least squared error and the least asymmetry at this error are respectively
$$
r_3=btg^2=0.2801200368\ldots,\qquad
H(a,b,a)=-2a\log a-b\log b.
\tag{M.6.13ee.1}
$$
Every state feasible at the threshold has this asymmetry. A three-dimensional ready reference and a five-level neutral pointer attain the threshold. Consequently, every complete apparatus of squared error less than $r_3$ has at least four distinct reference charges.

*Proof.* Write $c=1/\sqrt2$, $m=|1\rangle$, $f=(|0\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and $e=(|0\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$. Parity-oddification as in Theorem M.6.13ed preserves the reference state and can only lower $K$. We may therefore use the same raising operators $A,T$ and their adjoints. Fix $0<y<1$ and test the error on the density $Z_y=y|m\rangle\langle m|+(1-y)|f\rangle\langle f|$.

The reference charge graph has an edge at each positive unit gap. Its components are finite paths with at most three vertices. The odd observable and $X\otimes I$ preserve each component. Their error square thus depends only on the component-diagonal part of the reference state. Decompose each of those diagonal blocks into subnormalized pure states. For a normalized pure state $\psi$ in one component, let $P_\psi$ project onto the span of its nonzero charge vectors, one vector per occupied charge. The compression to $I\otimes P_\psi$ preserves the charge rule and decreases the error in Loewner order. The difference is the Gram matrix of the map
$$
s\longmapsto (I\otimes(I-P_\psi))(B-X\otimes I)(s\otimes\psi).
\tag{M.6.13ee.2}
$$
Translate the component to a subpath of $0,1,2$ and pad missing or unoccupied charges with zero ready populations and zero added couplings. These reductions apply to the weighted error for each pure term, so any lower bound uniform on scalar pure references holds on every original mixed reference.

For the scalar pure reference write its nonnegative amplitudes as $\sqrt{p_j}$ with $\sum_{j=0}^2p_j=1$. Let $A_j,T_j$ denote the raising entries from charge $j$ to $j+1$, with absent entries zero. The tested noise is
$$
y\bigl(\|A\psi-c\psi\|^2+\|T^*\psi-c\psi\|^2\bigr)
+\frac{1-y}{2}\|A^*\psi-T\psi\|^2 .
\tag{M.6.13ee.3}
$$
The constant term is $y$. At boundary center $j=0$ or $2$, square completion in its single variable gives gain
$$
\frac{y^2p_jp_1}{2(yp_j+(1-y)p_1/2)},
$$
where a zero numerator and denominator contribute zero. At center $j=1$, the middle-input contribution in $(A_1,T_0^*)$ has quadratic coefficient $yp_1$ and linear vector $yc\sqrt{p_1}(\sqrt{p_2},\sqrt{p_0})$. Its gain is at most $y(p_0+p_2)/2$ after retaining the nonnegative contribution from the dark input. When $p_0=p_2$ and $p_1>0$, the middle-input minimizer has equal real entries and its dark contribution at the center vanishes, attaining this gain.

For fixed $p_1=\beta>0$, the sum of boundary gains is strictly concave in $(p_0,p_2)$ at fixed sum, because $u\mapsto u/(yu+(1-y)\beta/2)$ is strictly concave. Thus the total gain is bounded by
$$
q_y(\beta)=\frac{y^2\beta(1-\beta)}{(1-y)\beta+y(1-\beta)}
+\frac{y(1-\beta)}2 .
\tag{M.6.13ee.4}
$$
This bound also holds at $\beta=0$, where the actual gain is zero. The second derivative of the first term on $[0,1]$ is $-2y^3(1-y)/[(1-y)\beta+y(1-\beta)]^3$, so the whole function is strictly concave.

Choose $y=g/[1+g(1-t)]$. The defining root interval gives $t>0$ and $0<y<1$. The polynomial takes opposite signs at the two rational endpoints and its derivative is positive throughout that interval. Put $J=4g^2+4g-1$. Substituting $t=(2g+3)/J$ gives the exact identities
$$
\begin{aligned}
t(1+t)g^2-g-\tfrac12
 &=-\frac{(2g+1)(8g^4+12g^3-4g^2-8g+1)}{2J^2},\\
tg^2-(1-tg)^2-\tfrac t2
 &=\frac{(2g+1)(8g^4+12g^3-4g^2-8g+1)}{2J^2},\\
1+\tfrac{t^2}4-2tg
 &=-\frac{(2g-1)(16g^2+30g+13)}{4J^2}<0 .
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13ee.5}
$$
Differentiation of (M.6.13ee.4) gives $q_y'(b)=-g[2g^2t(1+t)-2g-1]/[2(gt-g-1)]=0$. Thus $b$ is the unique maximizing middle population, and the unique pure population profile that can saturate the gain is $(a,b,a)$.

Use this profile for the ready vector $\psi=\sqrt a|0\rangle+\sqrt b|1\rangle+\sqrt a|2\rangle$. Define $u=g\sqrt t$, $v=\sqrt t/2$ and set $(A_0,A_1,T_0,T_1)=(u,v,v,u)$. These are the square-completion minimizers in (M.6.13ee.3) at the chosen $y$. In the basis $(f,m,e)$ the noise is diagonal by parity and reflection. Direct expansion gives
$$
K_f=bu^2=btg^2,\qquad
K_m=b\left[(1-tg)^2+\tfrac t2\right],\qquad
K_e=K_f+b\left[1+\tfrac{t^2}4-2tg\right].
\tag{M.6.13ee.6}
$$
The second and third lines of (M.6.13ee.5) give $K_f=K_m=r_3$ and $K_e<r_3$. Since the scalar device attains the minimum tested value $y-q_y(b)$ and its tested value equals $r_3$, the uniform lower bound is sharp. The nonzero total-charge blocks of $B$ have eigenvalues $\pm u$ and $\pm\sqrt2v$, and the full observable also has eigenvalue zero. The spectral-pointer construction of Theorem M.6.13dc therefore gives a complete apparatus of dimension fifteen with the same three charges.

To characterize the entropy at the threshold, parity-oddify any feasible apparatus and use the decomposition in the lower bound. Every pure term must saturate all the weighted inequalities. Strict concavity forces the positive profile $(a,b,a)$, hence the physical reference spectrum must be one consecutive three-vertex component. For a spectral decomposition $\sigma=\sum_\ell w_\ell|\psi_\ell\rangle\langle\psi_\ell|$, write the normalized charge components of $\psi_\ell$ as $v_{0\ell},v_{1\ell},v_{2\ell}$, with positive amplitudes $\sqrt a,\sqrt b,\sqrt a$. The scalar square-completion minimizers are unique. Both weights in $Z_y$ are positive, so equality in (M.6.13ee.2) annihilates its excursions on $m$ and $f$ for each $\ell$. On $m$, the two system outputs and the separate reference charges give $A_0v_{0\ell}=u v_{1\ell}$ and $T_1^*v_{2\ell}=u v_{1\ell}$. On $f$, the reference boundary charge $0$ receives only $A_0^*v_{1\ell}$ and charge $2$ receives only $-T_1v_{1\ell}$. Vanishing excursions and the scalar minimizers give $A_0^*v_{1\ell}=u v_{0\ell}$ and $T_1v_{1\ell}=u v_{2\ell}$. Since $u>0$, these relations equate the Gram matrices of the three families.

The Gram equalities give isometries $U_j$ from the span of $v_{0\ell}$ to the span of $v_{j\ell}$ with $U_jv_{0\ell}=v_{j\ell}$. The direct sum of these isometries transports $\sigma$ to $|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|\otimes\rho$ and its charge pinching to $\operatorname{diag}(a,b,a)\otimes\rho$, where $\rho=\sum_\ell w_\ell|v_{0\ell}\rangle\langle v_{0\ell}|$. Thus the asymmetry of the original reference is exactly $H(a,b,a)$. ∎

<a id="theorem-m613ef"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613ef-exact-finite-charge-cap-feasibility-for-spin-one"></a>**Theorem M.6.13ef (Exact Finite Charge-Cap Feasibility for Spin One).** Use the spin-one system, complete finite reference and squared all-input error of Theorem M.6.13dc. For each integer $N\ge1$, let $r_N$ be the infimum of squared errors when the complete reference has at most $N$ distinct charge values, allowing arbitrary finite multiplicities. The infimum is attained. It equals the smallest feasible value of the finite real polynomial system below. In particular, $r_N$ is real algebraic, and the formula decides feasibility and returns a complete finite witness at each algebraic budget. An optimizer uses a ready reference of dimension at most $6N$ and a neutral pointer with at most $6N+1$ labels. If a finite nonempty spectrum $\Gamma\subset\mathbb R$ is prescribed, the error minimum is $r_{n(\Gamma)}$, where $n(\Gamma)$ is the length of its longest consecutive unit-step run. This holds for the exact spectrum $\Gamma$ and for spectra contained in $\Gamma$.

*Proof.* Oddify the observable using the system parity as in Theorem M.6.13ed. Use the basis $f,m,e$ of Theorem M.6.13ee. The charge graph of the ready reference has unit-gap edges, and each component is a consecutive path. The odd observable and $X\otimes I$ preserve its components. Take the component-diagonal part of the ready state for the noise calculation and decompose each block into pure states. For each pure state use the one-vector-per-charge compression (M.6.13ee.2). Translate the resulting charge coordinates to a common ladder of length $N$. Missing charge coordinates are padded by zero ready amplitude and zero added couplings. These operations bound the original noise from below in Loewner order by a finite weighted sum of scalar pure-ladder noise matrices.

For any scalar branch, reflect the system basis by interchanging $|0\rangle,|2\rangle$ and reflect the ladder by sending charge $j$ to $N-1-j$. The reflected observable again conserves charge, and its noise is the system reflection of the original. Take the two branches with equal weights and retain a neutral flag. Averaging makes the noise diagonal in $(f,m,e)$, since parity separates $m$ from the endpoints and reflection separates $f$ from $e$. The diagonal entries are the original branch's three tested noise values. Any feasible original apparatus therefore gives a mixture of reflected scalar pairs with diagonal vector at most its error budget in all three entries. Conversely, each such mixture is a finite measurement by the spectral-pointer construction. Reflection uses the same charge set and the flags add multiplicity only.

Let $\mathcal S_N\subset[0,\infty)^3$ be the set of scalar pure-ladder diagonal vectors in that basis. The upward-closed set of attainable diagonal bounds is
$$
\mathscr D_N=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal S_N)+[0,\infty)^3 .
\tag{M.6.13ef.1}
$$
In this formula the scalar amplitudes may be chosen real and nonnegative by charge-basis phase choices. The raising entries may be complex, or may be made real when testing an upper bound, since the squared norms on the three real input vectors do not increase upon taking the real parts of the entries.

We prove $\mathscr D_N$ is closed even when a sequence of raising entries is unbounded. Given a convergent sequence of bounds, represent each as a bound on a combination of at most four scalar triples by Carathéodory's theorem. Pass to a subsequence on which the four flag weights and the four normalized nonnegative ready amplitude vectors converge. For each branch with positive limiting weight, its three test norms remain bounded because all branch contributions are nonnegative. In this branch, the linear maps
$$
L_k:s\longmapsto(B_k-X\otimes I)(s\otimes\psi_k)
\tag{M.6.13ef.2}
$$
therefore have a convergent subsequence on the fixed three-dimensional input. If both endpoint charges of a raising entry have positive limiting ready amplitude, the entry converges. For $A_j$ this follows from the $|0\rangle\otimes|j+1\rangle$ component of $L_k(m)$, which is $A_j^{(k)}(\psi_k)_j-c(\psi_k)_{j+1}$. For $T_j^*$ use the $|2\rangle\otimes|j\rangle$ component and the nonzero limit of $(\psi_k)_{j+1}$. Set all entries incident to a zero-amplitude limit charge to zero. Entries joining a zero-amplitude charge to a positive-amplitude charge remain bounded along the sequence. Each can be isolated from a component of $L_k$ on a single system basis state whose ready amplitude on its domain has positive limit, using the adjoint orientation when needed. Thus after projecting the output of the limiting map onto the positive-amplitude reference charges, all contributions from vanishing-amplitude input charges vanish. The projected map is exactly the error map for the limiting ready vector and the retained entries. Its three squared norms are bounded by those of the limiting map. Branches of zero limiting flag weight may be dropped because their contributions to the upper bound are nonnegative. The remaining branches witness the limiting diagonal bound. This proves closure.

The diagonal line meets $\mathscr D_N$ at $r_N(1,1,1)$. This is a boundary point since smaller diagonal values are infeasible. A supporting hyperplane there has a nonzero nonnegative normal, because $\mathscr D_N$ is upward closed. In a finite realization of this bound, every positive-weight branch has its triple on the supporting plane. Indeed, each has normal value at least the value at the boundary point, and their mean has value at most that value by the upper bound. Carathéodory's theorem within the plane then needs at most three scalar triples to retain their mean. The three reflected pairs give ready dimension at most $6N$. A scalar ladder has at most $N$ nontrivial odd total-charge blocks. Each block couples a single middle-system coordinate to its endpoint-system neighbors, so it has at most one positive and one negative eigenvalue. The reflected copy has the same eigenvalues. The spectral construction for the three pairs therefore uses at most $6N+1$ neutral labels.

For the polynomial formula use three nonnegative flag weights $w_\ell$ with $\sum_\ell w_\ell=1$, three real nonnegative ready vectors $p^{(\ell)}\in\mathbb R^N$ with $\sum_j(p_j^{(\ell)})^2=1$, and two real arrays $A_j^{(\ell)},T_j^{(\ell)}$ for $0\le j<N-1$. Form the corresponding invariant odd matrices $B_\ell$. The three inequalities at budget $r$ are
$$
\sum_{\ell=1}^3 w_\ell
\bigl\|(B_\ell-X\otimes I)(s\otimes p^{(\ell)})\bigr\|^2\le r,
\qquad s=f,m,e .
\tag{M.6.13ef.3}
$$
Real-closed-field quantifier elimination gives the feasible budget set and algebraic sampling gives witnesses (Basu, Pollack and Roy 2006). Equations (M.6.13ef.1)–(M.6.13ef.2) prove that this set is $[r_N,\infty)$, so its endpoint is algebraic. For a prescribed spectrum, each unit-step component compresses to a ladder of length at most $n(\Gamma)$, which gives the lower bound. Translate an optimal ladder to a longest run in $\Gamma$ and, for an exact spectrum, add the remaining charge sectors with zero ready weight and zero observable. These sectors leave the full noise and the spectrum requirement as claimed. ∎

<a id="theorem-m613eg"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613eg-population-resolved-spin-one-entropy-bound"></a>**Theorem M.6.13eg (Population-Resolved Spin-One Entropy Bound).** Use the complete finite spin-one apparatus, squared all-input error $r$ and natural-log asymmetry of Theorem M.6.13dc. Put
$$
u_d(r)=1-\frac{r(3-d)}2,\qquad
v_*(r)=\max_{0\le d\le1}
\frac{(1-d^2)[u_d(r)]_+}{1-d^2[u_d(r)]_+},\qquad 0<r<1.
\tag{M.6.13eg.1}
$$
Every finite apparatus satisfying $K\preceq rI$ obeys
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)>\Phi(v_*(r)),\qquad F(r)\ge\Phi(v_*(r)),
\tag{M.6.13eg.2}
$$
where $\Phi$ is the exact one-gap entropy curve of Theorem M.6.13l. This lower curve is strictly larger than (M.6.13ca.21) for every $0<r<1$. The maximum is attained at the unique root $d_r\in(\max\{0,3-2/r\},1)$ of
$$
r d^3+(1-6r)d^2+(9r-6)d+1=0.
\tag{M.6.13eg.3}
$$
In particular, as $r\downarrow0$,
$$
v_*(r)=1-\frac{3+2\sqrt2}{4}r+O(r^2),\qquad
F(r)\ \ge\ \frac12\log\frac1r+\frac{\log[8\pi/(3+2\sqrt2)]-1}{2}-O(r).
\tag{M.6.13eg.4}
$$

*Proof.* Oddify the invariant observable as in Theorem M.6.13ca. In its notation choose $\lambda=(1+d)/2$ and $\mu=1-\lambda$. The bright and dark tester weights are equal, so the complete gap-two terms in the tested square cancel exactly. Let $g_d(\sigma)=q_{\lambda,\mu}(\sigma)$ denote the fixed-state gain of this tester. Its $X^2$ expectation is one and its trace is $(3-d)/2$, so feasibility gives $g_d(\sigma)\ge u_d(r)$.

Diagonalize the charge blocks of $\mathcal G_Q\sigma$, and let $p_i$ be their eigenvalues with charge labels $q_i$. A sum over edges below counts each pair of eigenvectors with $q_i=q_j+1$ once. Write
$$
\eta_{ij}=\frac{2|\sigma_{ij}|^2}{p_i+p_j},\qquad
z_{ij}=\frac{p_i-p_j}{p_i+p_j},\qquad
\eta=\sum_{\rm edges}\eta_{ij}.
$$
An edge with zero denominator contributes zero. Formula (M.6.13ca.3) on this line gives independent quadratic penalties $\lambda p_j+(1-\lambda)p_i$ and $\lambda p_i+(1-\lambda)p_j$ for the two forward coefficients at each edge. Their identical linear term is $\sqrt2\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\sigma_{ij}}\,x)$ for coefficient $x$. Completing each complex square gives the exact finite-state identity, for $0\le d<1$,
$$
g_d(\sigma)=
\sum_{\rm edges}\frac{|\sigma_{ij}|^2}{2}
\left(\frac1{\lambda p_j+(1-\lambda)p_i}
+\frac1{\lambda p_i+(1-\lambda)p_j}\right)
=\sum_{\rm edges}\frac{\eta_{ij}}{1-d^2z_{ij}^2}.
\tag{M.6.13eg.5}
$$
This calculation keeps all finite charge multiplicities and all complex edge coefficients. Edges missing from the actual charge spectrum contribute nothing.

For each pair of neighboring sectors, positivity of the corresponding principal block factors the off-diagonal block as $D^{1/2}VC^{1/2}$ for a contraction $V$ between the diagonal supports, with $C,D$ the two ready-state diagonal blocks. This follows by the Schur complement on the supports, or by its continuous limit from positive-definite blocks. On that edge of sectors define $w_{ij}=(p_i+p_j)|V_{ij}|^2/2$. Then $\eta_{ij}=w_{ij}(1-z_{ij}^2)$. The sum of the $w_{ij}$ for this pair of sectors is at most $(\operatorname{Tr} C+\operatorname{Tr} D)/2$, by the row and column squared-norm bounds on $V$. Each charge sector has at most two neighbors, regardless of its multiplicity or real-valued charge. Summing gives $\sum w_{ij}\le1$.

The function $f_d(s)=s/(1-d^2+d^2s)$ is concave on $[0,1]$ for $0\le d<1$ and satisfies $f_d(0)=0$. With the missing weight placed at zero, (M.6.13eg.5) and Jensen's inequality give the uniform bound
$$
g_d(\sigma)\le\frac{\eta}{1-d^2+d^2\eta}.
\tag{M.6.13eg.6}
$$
Inverting at $u_d(r)>0$ yields $\eta\ge(1-d^2)u_d(r)/(1-d^2u_d(r))$. The same lower bound with positive part is immediate if $u_d(r)\le0$. At $d=1$ the expression in (M.6.13eg.1) is zero, since $r>0$. Thus $\eta\ge v_*(r)>0$. Since every finite reference obeys the strict one-gap relation $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)>\Phi(\eta)$ at positive $\eta$, and $\Phi$ is increasing, this proves (M.6.13eg.2).

On the open interval where $u_d(r)>0$ and $d<1$, the derivative in $d$ of (M.6.13eg.1)'s objective has the sign of the polynomial in (M.6.13eg.3). Its derivative is $2d-6+3r(3-d)(1-d)$, which is strictly less than $-4d$ on that interval because $r(3-d)<2$. At $d=0$ the polynomial is one. If the positive interval starts at $d=3-2/r>0$, the objective has positive right derivative there, since $u_d$ increases with derivative $r/2$ and $1-d^2>0$. At $d=1$ the polynomial is $-4(1-r)<0$. Thus (M.6.13eg.3) gives the unique maximizer. In (M.6.13ca.19) write $d=1-2\mu$. The old objective is $(1-d^2)u_d(r)$ and its maximizing $d$ satisfies $0<d<1$ and $u_d(r)>0$. At this value the new denominator is strictly less than one. Strict monotonicity of $\Phi$ proves the comparison.

At $r=0$ the smaller root of $d^2-6d+1=0$ is $d_0=3-2\sqrt2$. It is simple, so (M.6.13eg.3) gives $d_r=d_0+O(r)$. For fixed $d$ in a neighborhood of $d_0$ the objective is $1-r(3-d)/(2(1-d^2))+O(r^2)$, uniformly in $d$. Its coefficient at $d_0$ is $(3+2\sqrt2)/4$. The expansion $\Phi(1-s)=\tfrac12\log(1/s)+[\log(2\pi)-1]/2+O(s)$ gives (M.6.13eg.4). ∎

**Sharpness of the fixed-$\eta$ comparison.** For fixed $0<\eta<1$ and $0\le d<1$, the right side of (M.6.13eg.6) is the exact supremum of the tested gain over complete finite ready references with this one-gap value. If $d>0$, no finite reference attains that supremum.

Indeed, take an even integer $N$ with $1-1/N>\eta$ and use the scalar charges $0,\ldots,N-1$. Let the ready state be the pure vector with squared amplitudes alternating between $(1+z_N)/N$ and $(1-z_N)/N$, where $z_N^2=1-\eta/(1-1/N)$. Each of the $N-1$ adjacent pairs has $w_{ij}=1/N$ and imbalance of magnitude $z_N$, so their total one-gap value is exactly $\eta$. Formula (M.6.13eg.5) gives
$$
g_d=\frac{\eta}{1-d^2+d^2\eta/(1-1/N)}
\longrightarrow\frac{\eta}{1-d^2+d^2\eta}.
\tag{M.6.13eg.7}
$$
The weighted gain in each member is realized by its finite square-completion observable and a counted neutral spectral pointer. For the strict finite bound, an edge incident to a zero-population sector contributes no weight. The graph of positive-population sectors with unit-gap edges consists of finite paths, including isolated vertices. At least one occupied sector has degree at most one, so the bound $\sum w_{ij}\le\frac12\sum_q\deg(q)\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_{qq}$ is strictly less than one. For $d>0$, $f_d$ is strictly concave. At $\eta>0$ there is a positive weight on a positive argument and a positive missing weight on zero. Hence (M.6.13eg.6) is strict for every finite reference. This sharpness concerns the tested gain at fixed one-gap value. The alternating pure sequence need not minimize entropy.

<a id="theorem-m613eh"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613eh-singularity-at-every-finite-charge-cap-threshold"></a>**Theorem M.6.13eh (Singularity at Every Finite Charge-Cap Threshold).** Use the complete spin-one measurement class and let $r_N$ be the exact minimum squared error at a cap of $N\ge2$ distinct reference charges in Theorem M.6.13ef. Every complete apparatus attaining $r_N$ under that cap has a ready-state support containing no nonzero vector of definite reference charge. In particular its ready state is singular on the support of its charge twirl. The unrestricted entropy infimum at $r=r_N$ is strictly below the asymmetry of each such capped apparatus. If the unrestricted entropy infimum is attained at $r_N$, its attaining apparatus uses more than $N$ distinct charges. The values $r_N$ form a nonincreasing positive algebraic sequence tending to zero, so they contain infinitely many distinct thresholds. Theorems M.6.13ed and M.6.13ee give the explicit values at $N=2,3$.

*Proof.* First, $0<r_N\le1/2$ for $N\ge2$. The upper bound follows from Theorem M.6.13ed. For the positive lower endpoint, attainment under the cap is Theorem M.6.13ef. Exact zero error would imply
$$
(B-X\otimes I)(s\otimes\psi)=0
$$
for every system input $s$ and every vector $\psi$ in the support of the ready state, by the positive square defining $K$. Choose one such nonzero $\psi$ and its highest occupied charge $q$ with nonzero component $\psi_q$. On input $s=|0\rangle$, project the displayed equality to $|1\rangle\otimes\mathcal H_q$. The target contribution is $\psi_q/\sqrt2$. The contribution of the invariant $B$ must come from the component $|0\rangle\otimes\psi_{q+1}$ in the same total-charge sector, and vanishes by the choice of $q$. This contradiction excludes zero error. The sequence is nonincreasing by inclusion of the capped classes. The finite exact-error family in Theorem M.6.13cb supplies a finite charge cap for every prescribed positive error, so $r_N\to0$. Algebraicity is Theorem M.6.13ef, and positivity then implies infinitely many distinct values.

Let $\mathscr D_N$ be the closed convex upper set of three diagonal noise bounds in Theorem M.6.13ef. Take a supporting hyperplane at its boundary point $r_N(1,1,1)$, with normal $(x,y,z)\ge0$ and $x+y+z=1$. Use the tester $Z=x|e\rangle\langle e|+y|m\rangle\langle m|+z|f\rangle\langle f|$ of Theorem M.6.13dc. The symmetry and flag argument in Theorem M.6.13ef ensures that every capped device's tested noise is at least $r_N$, even when its noise has off-diagonal entries: first oddify the observable, then use reflected branches on the common canonical ladder to obtain its three diagonal bounds with no larger values. Conversely an actual cap optimizer gives equality in the tested value because $K\preceq r_NI$.

Put $s=x+y=\operatorname{Tr}(ZX^2)$. One has $s>0$. Otherwise the tester is supported on the dark vector and the zero observable has zero tested noise, contradicting $r_N>0$. In fact $r_N<s$. To see this, use the two-charge ready vector $(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and one invariant Hermitian coupling between $|1,0\rangle$ and $|0,1\rangle$ of real strength $t>0$. At $t=0$ the tested noise is $s$. Its derivative in $t$ is strictly negative, since $\{Z,X\}=sX$ and the reference gap-one coherence is $1/2$. The quadratic term is finite, so a sufficiently small positive $t$ has tested noise strictly below $s$. Its spectral-pointer realization retains the same two charges. The supporting bound gives $r_N<s$.

Now let $(\sigma,B)$ be any apparatus attaining $r_N$ under the cap. Oddify $B$ by system parity, keeping $\sigma$ and the cap. The resulting all-input noise is still at most $r_NI$ and its tested noise equals $r_N$ by the supporting bound. If a normalized charge eigenvector $\psi$ belongs to $\operatorname{supp}\sigma$, the finite-dimensional positivity of $\sigma$ on its support permits a decomposition $\sigma=t|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|+(1-t)\sigma'$ with $0<t<1$ and a density $\sigma'$. Use the same odd $B$ on these two ready states. Both satisfy the cap, so each has tested noise at least $r_N$. In the charge-eigenvector branch the linear term in $B$ vanishes, since $\{Z,X\}=sX$ and the odd conserving observable has reference charge shifts only $\pm1$. Its tested noise is therefore $s+\operatorname{Tr}[(Z\otimes|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)B^2]\ge s>r_N$. Affinity of the tested noise in the ready state contradicts equality for $\sigma$. Thus its support contains no charge eigenvector.

The support of the charge twirl is a nonzero charge-invariant subspace and contains a charge eigenvector. The preceding exclusion makes the ready state singular on that subspace. Theorem M.6.13dc requires every finite unrestricted entropy attainer at $0<r<1$ to be faithful on the support of its charge twirl. It follows that no cap-optimal apparatus attains the unrestricted entropy infimum at $r_N$. Its actual entropy therefore lies strictly above that infimum. ∎

<a id="theorem-m613ei"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613ei-unique-populations-and-exact-entropy-at-every-spin-one-charge-threshold"></a>**Theorem M.6.13ei (Unique Populations and Exact Entropy at Every Spin-One Charge Threshold).** Use the complete finite spin-one class, squared all-input error and cap thresholds \(r_N\) of Theorems M.6.13dc and M.6.13ef. Then \(r_{N+1}<r_N\) for every \(N\ge1\). For every \(N\ge3\) there is a unique probability vector \(p^{(N)}=(p_0,\ldots,p_{N-1})\) of a pure scalar-ladder apparatus attaining \(r_N\). Each entry is positive, \(p_j=p_{N-1-j}\), and \(p^{(N)}\) is algebraic. One such pure ready vector, with a neutral spectral pointer of at most \(2N+1\) labels, attains \(r_N\). To calculate the vector and observable, use (M.6.13ef.3) with one branch of weight one and the known algebraic error \(r_N\).

Every complete apparatus attaining \(r_N\) with at most \(N\) distinct reference charges uses a consecutive \(N\)-charge spectrum up to translation. On the support \(E\) of its ready state \(\sigma\), the charge projections \(P_j\) satisfy
\[
P_E P_j P_E=p^{(N)}_j I_E,\qquad 0\le j<N.
\tag{M.6.13ei.1}
\]
Its exact asymmetry is
\[
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)=-\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}p^{(N)}_j\log p^{(N)}_j.
\tag{M.6.13ei.2}
\]
In particular the rank of the ready state is at most the least multiplicity of these \(N\) charges. For \(N=2\) the threshold entropy is given by Theorem M.6.13ed. For \(N=3\) (M.6.13ei.2) agrees with Theorem M.6.13ee.

*Proof.* Fix \(N\ge3\). As in Theorem M.6.13eh, take a supporting tester
\[
Z=x|e\rangle\langle e|+y|m\rangle\langle m|+z|f\rangle\langle f|,
\qquad x,y,z\ge0,\quad x+y+z=1
\]
at \(r_N(1,1,1)\) in the closed upper set (M.6.13ef.1). Every capped apparatus has tested noise at least \(r_N>0\), and at least one has equality. If \(y=0\), the three-charge endpoint-plane construction of Theorem M.6.13ec gives tested noise tending to zero. If \(x+z=0\), its three-charge construction for \(m\) gives the same contradiction. Thus \(y>0\), \(a:=(x+z)/2>0\), and \(s:=x+y>0\).

Oddification and the pure scalar-ladder reduction of Theorem M.6.13ef show that a scalar apparatus with tested noise \(r_N\) exists. In that reduction a pure ready vector supported on disconnected positive-population runs can be split further. In detail, compress the output to the occupied reference charges. This can only lower its squared noise, since the target acts identically on the reference. The odd observable compressed to these charges has only unit-gap couplings, so it splits across the positive-population runs. The resulting noise is the weighted sum of their normalized ready-vector noises. If the original branch is optimal for \(Z\), each of the compressed runs has tested noise \(r_N\), because every such run itself respects the cap.

Consider a pure scalar ready vector with real nonnegative amplitudes \(\sqrt{p_q}\), extended by zero outside its consecutive occupied run. In the total-charge sector centered at middle-system charge \(q\) on the reference, write \(P=\operatorname{diag}(p_{q-1},p_{q+1})\), \(p=p_q\), \(\mathbf1=(1,1)^{\mathsf T}\), and
\[
G=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&a\end{pmatrix},\qquad b=(x-z)/2,\qquad g_\pm=G^{1/2}e_\pm .
\]
Here \(e_-,e_+\) are the two coordinate vectors. The weighted square has reference endpoint block \(P^{1/2}GP^{1/2}\), middle weight \(yp\), and linear coefficient \(s\sqrt p\,P^{1/2}\mathbf1/\sqrt2\), as in (M.6.13dc.11). Completing the square over the two couplings gives the maximum gain relative to zero observable, summed over \(q\), as
\[
\mathcal U_Z(p_\bullet)=\frac{s^2}{2}\sum_q u_q(p_\bullet),\qquad
u_q(p_\bullet)=\min_{w\in\mathbb R^2}
\left\{p_q\|w\|^2+\frac1y\sum_{i\in\{-,+\}}p_{q+i}(1-g_i^{\mathsf T}w)^2\right\}.
\tag{M.6.13ei.3}
\]
In the sum \(q-=q-1\) and \(q+=q+1\). To see the identity when \(p_q>0\), set \(C=P^{1/2}G^{1/2}\), \(v=P^{1/2}\mathbf1\), and minimize \(p_q\|w\|^2+y^{-1}\|v-Cw\|^2\). The value is \(p_q v^{\mathsf T}(CC^{\mathsf T}+yp_qI)^{-1}v\), exactly the completed-square expression. If \(p_q=0\), the weighted linear term is zero. A consecutive occupied run gives at most one occupied neighbor of such a \(q\), and \(\|g_i\|^2=a>0\) makes the displayed minimum zero there as well. The optimal tested noise on this population is \(s-\mathcal U_Z(p_\bullet)\).

Each \(u_q\) is concave in the three populations, being the pointwise minimum of affine functions. The minima in (M.6.13ei.3) are attained, since the displayed expression is a finite least-squares problem. Equality in its two-point concavity inequality at an interior averaging weight requires a common minimizing \(w\), because a minimizer for the average must minimize both summands. This remains valid when one of the two center populations is zero.

An optimal run cannot have length less than \(N\). If it did, average its population with its unit translate, both inside a ladder of length at most \(N\). The two populations have the same gain, and their average is positive on the union of their two runs. At the rightmost charge of the translated run, the original population has zero center, only a positive left neighbor, and requires \(g_-^{\mathsf T}w=1\) for its local minimum. The translate has positive center \(p\), positive left neighbor \(t\) if the run length is at least two, and no right neighbor. Its local minimum has
\[
g_-^{\mathsf T}w=\frac{a t}{yp+a t}<1 .
\]
This also holds with \(t=0\) for a one-charge run. There is no common minimizer. Thus the gain strictly increases under the average, contradicting optimality. If \(r_{N+1}=r_N\) for \(N+1\ge3\), apply the same argument to a supporting tester at \(r_{N+1}\). An apparatus attaining \(r_N\) has \(K\preceq r_{N+1}I\) and therefore gives a weighted minimizer with an occupied run of length at most \(N\), a contradiction. The remaining inequality \(r_2<r_1\) follows from \(r_1=1\) and Theorem M.6.13ed. For \(r_1=1\), a single charge has an invariant ready state, and averaging by system parity reduces the optimal observable to its odd part, which must vanish on that reference.

We next prove uniqueness of the maximizing scalar population in the \(N\)-cap problem for this tester. Any two maximizing populations on \(0,\ldots,N-1\) are positive there. Their average has at least the same gain and respects the cap, so the two local minima share a minimizer \(w_q\) at every occupied \(q\). Its stationarity is
\[
y w_q=\sum_{i\in\{-,+\}}\frac{p_{q+i}}{p_q}g_i R_i,\qquad R_i=1-g_i^{\mathsf T}w_q .
\tag{M.6.13ei.4}
\]
All residuals \(R_i\) are strictly positive. Indeed for \(D=\operatorname{diag}(p_{q-1}/(yp_q),p_{q+1}/(yp_q))\) the residual column is \((I+GD)^{-1}\mathbf1\). The determinant is positive since \(\det(I+GD)=\det(I+D^{1/2}GD^{1/2})\ge1\). The two numerators are \(1+(a-b)D_{++}\) and \(1+(a-b)D_{--}\), which are at least one since \(a-b=z\ge0\). At \(q=N-1\) the shared \(w_q\) and positive residual determine the ratio \(p_{N-2}/p_{N-1}\) uniquely in (M.6.13ei.4), using \(g_-\ne0\). At each preceding \(q\), subtract the right-neighbor term, whose ratio is already determined, to determine the next ratio \(p_{q-1}/p_q\) in the same way. Normalization now identifies the entire population.

On this full population every odd total-charge block with a middle coordinate has \(yp_q>0\), hence a unique weighted minimizer by the positive quadratic form in the two couplings. Sectors without a middle coordinate have no odd matrix entries. All coefficient data after the charge-basis phase choices are real, so the unique minimizing observable is real. Joint system and ladder reflection preserves the tester and the objective. Uniqueness implies the claimed palindromic population and covariance of the weighted minimizing observable under this reflection. Its noise matrix is diagonal in \((e,m,f)\), since system parity also preserves the noise after tracing the reference. An actual cap optimizer decomposes as in Theorem M.6.13ef into a convex combination of scalar branches whose average diagonal bounds are at most \(r_N\) in all coordinates. Every occupied branch must minimize tested noise, hence has the unique population and observable just proved. Their common diagonal noise therefore satisfies \(K\preceq r_N I\), proving attainment by one scalar branch. Each odd total-charge block contributes at most one positive and one negative eigenvalue. There are at most \(N\) such blocks, so the spectral-pointer construction needs at most \(2N+1\) labels including zero. The one-branch real polynomial system at the algebraic \(r_N\) has this unique normalized nonnegative ready vector and real observable. Real-closed-field algebraic sampling then gives algebraic coefficients, and hence algebraic populations.

Finally, let \(\sigma\) be any capped optimizer at \(r_N\), and use its oddified observable. Every unit vector \(\psi\in E=\operatorname{supp}\sigma\) can occur with strictly positive weight in a pure-state decomposition of \(\sigma\), since \(\sigma\) is positive definite on \(E\). Affinity of the tested noise at fixed observable forces that pure branch also to attain \(r_N\) in the tested objective. Compressing to its occupied vectors, one vector \(P_j\psi/\|P_j\psi\|\) per occupied charge, and splitting its contiguous runs as above cannot lower the noise below \(r_N\). Each resulting run has the unique full \(N\)-charge population. The cap permits only one such run, so the complete charge spectrum is that run, up to translation. Each unit \(\psi\in E\) consequently satisfies \(\langle\psi,P_j\psi\rangle=p^{(N)}_j\). Polarization gives (M.6.13ei.1). The maps \(V_j=p_j^{-1/2}P_j|_E\) are isometries into the corresponding reference charge spaces, and
\[
\mathcal G_Q\sigma=\bigoplus_{j=0}^{N-1}p_j V_j\sigma V_j^*.
\]
Its entropy is \(H(p^{(N)})+S(\sigma)\), proving (M.6.13ei.2) and the rank bound. The pure scalar model and its counted neutral spectral pointer have the finite conserved-charge and physical realization of Theorems M.6.13dc and M.6.13df. \(\square\)

<a id="theorem-m613ej"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613ej-sharp-large-capacity-spin-one-error"></a>**Theorem M.6.13ej (Sharp Large-Capacity Spin-One Error).** For the complete finite spin-one charge-cap error of Theorem M.6.13ef,
\[
\lim_{N\to\infty}N^2r_N=\pi^2 .
\tag{M.6.13ej.1}
\]
In particular, the least number \(N_{\min}(r)\) of distinct complete reference charges for squared all-input error at most \(r\) satisfies \(\sqrt r\,N_{\min}(r)\to\pi\) as \(r\downarrow0\). The same limit holds with exact error \(r\).

*Proof.* Use the fixed tester \(Z=(|m\rangle\langle m|+|f\rangle\langle f|)/2\). It is positive and has trace one. Thus each \(K\preceq rI\) has \(\operatorname{Tr}ZK\le r\). The oddification, pure scalar compression and splitting into consecutive occupied runs of Theorem M.6.13ei give a lower bound on \(\operatorname{Tr}ZK\) from the tested minima on normalized pure scalar runs of length at most \(N\). Extend a run's population by zero to all integer charges and place it in \(0,\ldots,N-1\).

For this tester \(s=y=z=1/2\), \(x=0\), and \(G=\frac14\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) in (M.6.13ei.3). Put \(L=p_{q-1}\), \(P=p_q\), \(R=p_{q+1}\). Direct inversion of the two-by-two matrix for \(P>0\) gives
\[
u_q=2(L+R)-\frac{2(L-R)^2}{2P+L+R}.
\]
For \(P=0\) there is at most one occupied neighbor, so both the local gain and this expression vanish. A zero denominator contributes zero. Since \(\sum_q(L+R)=2\), the exact minimum of the tested noise for the scalar run is
\[
W(p)=\frac14\sum_{q\in\mathbb Z}\frac{(p_{q-1}-p_{q+1})^2}{2p_q+p_{q-1}+p_{q+1}} .
\tag{M.6.13ej.2}
\]
No restriction on complete ready-state multiplicity was used to obtain the lower bound by these pure branches.

For any real sequence \(h_q\) on the finite index range meeting the sum, complete each scalar square in (M.6.13ej.2). With \(D=p_{q-1}-p_{q+1}\), \(S=2p_q+p_{q-1}+p_{q+1}\), the inequality \(D^2/S\ge2Dh_q-Sh_q^2\) holds whenever \(S>0\), and both sides are zero when \(S=0\). Rearranging the finite sums yields
\[
W(p)\ge\frac14\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}p_j\bigl[
2(h_{j+1}-h_{j-1})-2h_j^2-h_{j+1}^2-h_{j-1}^2\bigr].
\tag{M.6.13ej.3}
\]

Fix \(\eta>0\), let \(k=\pi/(1+2\eta)\), and use \(v(x)=k\tan(k(x-\tfrac12))\). Its poles are at \(-\eta\) and \(1+\eta\). It obeys \(v'-v^2=k^2\). Put \(\delta=1/N\) and \(h_j=\delta v(j\delta)\) for \(-1\le j\le N\). For sufficiently large \(N\), all points and Taylor segments lie in \([-\eta/2,1+\eta/2]\), where the derivatives used below are uniformly bounded. Uniformly in \(0\le j<N\),
\[
\frac14\bigl[
2(h_{j+1}-h_{j-1})-2h_j^2-h_{j+1}^2-h_{j-1}^2\bigr]
=\delta^2(v'(j\delta)-v(j\delta)^2)+O_\eta(\delta^4)
=\delta^2 k^2+O_\eta(\delta^4).
\]
The first difference uses the centered Taylor expansion, and the two shifted square terms use the centered sum for \(v^2\). The uniform bound in (M.6.13ej.3) therefore survives every finite scalar branch and every mixture of branches, including arbitrary neutral multiplicities. It gives \(\liminf_N N^2 r_N\ge k^2\). Letting \(\eta\downarrow0\) gives the lower bound \(\pi^2\).

The pure sine phase-reference family in Theorem M.6.13cb has \(N\) distinct charges and exact squared all-input error \(\sin^2(\pi/(N+1))\). Its counted neutral pointer does not add a charge value. This yields the matching upper bound. Strict decrease to zero from Theorem M.6.13ei gives \(r_{N_{\min}(r)}\le r<r_{N_{\min}(r)-1}\) for small positive \(r\), and applying (M.6.13ej.1) to both indices gives the inverse limit. Exact error is obtained by the same continuous scalar translation of the pointer as in Theorem M.6.13cb. Its charge commutator and its ready entropy stay fixed. \(\square\)

<a id="corollary-m613ek"></a>

<a id="corollary-m613ek-optimal-charge-profile-and-threshold-entropy-at-large-capacity"></a>**Corollary M.6.13ek (Optimal Charge Profile and Threshold Entropy at Large Capacity).** Let \(p^{(N)}\) be the common charge population of all apparatuses attaining the exact cap threshold \(r_N\), as in Theorem M.6.13ei. Let \(f_N\) be the continuous piecewise linear function on \([0,1]\) with zero endpoints and values
\[
f_N\!\left(\frac{j+1}{N+1}\right)=\sqrt{(N+1)p^{(N)}_j},
\qquad 0\le j<N.
\]
Then \(f_N\to\sqrt2\sin(\pi x)\) uniformly on \([0,1]\) and weakly in \(H_0^1(0,1)\). The actual ready asymmetry of every cap-threshold optimizer is
\[
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_N)
=\log N+\log 2-1+o(1)
=\frac12\log\frac1{r_N}+\log(2\pi)-1+o(1).
\tag{M.6.13ek.1}
\]

*Proof.* Extend \(p^{(N)}\) by zero at \(j=-1,N\). For a pure scalar ready vector its one-gap quantity in Theorem M.6.13q is
\[
\eta_N=\sum_{j=0}^{N-2}\frac{2p^{(N)}_jp^{(N)}_{j+1}}{p^{(N)}_j+p^{(N)}_{j+1}}.
\]
Here and below a zero denominator contributes zero. Since \(2ab/(a+b)=(a+b)/2-(a-b)^2/[2(a+b)]\), summing over all edges including the two boundary edges gives
\[
\sum_{j=-1}^{N-1}(\sqrt{p^{(N)}_{j+1}}-\sqrt{p^{(N)}_j})^2
\le
\sum_{j=-1}^{N-1}\frac{(p^{(N)}_{j+1}-p^{(N)}_j)^2}{p^{(N)}_j+p^{(N)}_{j+1}}
=2(1-\eta_N)\le3r_N .
\]
The last step applies (M.6.13q.1) to the scalar threshold model of Theorem M.6.13ei. The interpolation has
\[
\int_0^1|f_N'|^2
=(N+1)^2\sum_{j=-1}^{N-1}(\sqrt{p^{(N)}_{j+1}}-\sqrt{p^{(N)}_j})^2.
\]
Theorem M.6.13ej bounds this uniformly. The endpoint values, the Cauchy–Schwarz continuity bound and Arzelà–Ascoli give a uniformly convergent subsequence of every subsequence, and weak \(H_0^1\) compactness gives the same limit \(f\) in that topology. The grid sum of \(f_N^2/(N+1)\) equals one, so uniform convergence gives \(f\ge0\) and \(\int_0^1f^2=1\).

To identify the limit, use any real \(v\in C^\infty([0,1])\) in (M.6.13ej.3), with \(h_j=(N+1)^{-1}v((j+1)/(N+1))\) for \(-1\le j\le N\). Taylor expansion with the fixed smooth test gives
\[
(N+1)^2W(p^{(N)})\ge
\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}p^{(N)}_j(v'-v^2)\!\left(\frac{j+1}{N+1}\right)+O_v(N^{-2}).
\]
For this scalar optimizer \(W(p^{(N)})\le r_N\), since \(W\) is the minimum of the tested noise and the actual noise is at most \(r_NI\). By uniform convergence and (M.6.13ej.1),
\[
\pi^2\ge\int_0^1 f^2(v'-v^2).
\]
Integration by parts, using \(f\in H_0^1(0,1)\), gives \(\int f^2(v'-v^2)=\int|f'|^2-\int|f'+fv|^2\). An absolutely continuous \(f\) has \(f'=0\) almost everywhere on its zero set, so \(-f'/f\) there may be set to zero and is in \(L^2(f^2\,dx)\) with squared norm \(\int|f'|^2\). Smooth real functions are dense in this weighted \(L^2\) space by continuous approximation for the finite Borel measure \(f^2\,dx\) and then uniform smooth approximation. The supremum of the test integrals is thus \(\int|f'|^2\). The Dirichlet Poincaré inequality gives \(\int|f'|^2\ge\pi^2\int f^2=\pi^2\). Its equality condition, for example by the sine expansion, gives the normalized nonnegative first eigenfunction \(f=\sqrt2\sin(\pi x)\). Every subsequence has this same limit, proving the asserted convergence.

Finally, \(t\mapsto t^2\log t^2\) with zero value at zero is continuous and bounded on the common range of the \(f_N\). Equation (M.6.13ei.2) and uniform convergence give
\[
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_N)-\log(N+1)
=-\frac1{N+1}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} f_N(x_j)^2\log f_N(x_j)^2
\longrightarrow -\int_0^1 2\sin^2(\pi x)\log[2\sin^2(\pi x)]\,dx
=\log2-1,
\]
where \(x_j=(j+1)/(N+1)\). The final integral is the sine-profile integral used in (M.6.13cb) and also follows by differentiating the $\beta$ integral for \(\int_0^\pi\sin^\alpha x\,dx\) at \(\alpha=2\). Equation (M.6.13ej.1) gives the second expression in (M.6.13ek.1). These asymmetries are at the cap thresholds. \(\square\)

<a id="theorem-m613el"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613el-exact-matrix-phase-form-of-the-spin-one-frontier"></a>**Theorem M.6.13el (Exact Matrix Phase Form of the Spin-One Frontier).** Use the complete finite spin-one class and the resource \(\mathcal A_Q\), noise \(K\), and frontier \(F(r)\) of Theorem M.6.13dc. Let \(\mathbb T=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)\) with normalized Lebesgue measure \(d\theta/(2\pi)\), let \(U_\theta=e^{iQ_S\theta}\), and put \(P=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)\). For every finite coefficient dimension \(d\), take a measurable positive matrix density \(J_\theta\) on \(\mathbb C^d\) with \(\int\operatorname{Tr}J_\theta=1\), and a constant Hermitian \(C\) on \(\mathbb C^3\otimes\mathbb C^d\) that is odd under \(P\otimes I\). Define
\[
\tau=\int J_\theta,\qquad
H(J)=\int\operatorname{Tr}(J_\theta\log J_\theta)-\operatorname{Tr}(\tau\log\tau),\qquad
K_{\rm ph}(J,C)=\int\operatorname{Tr}_{d}\!\left[
(I\otimes J_\theta)\bigl((U_\theta\otimes I)C(U_\theta^*\otimes I)-X\otimes I\bigr)^2\right].
\tag{M.6.13el.1}
\]
Use \(0\log0=0\) and allow \(H(J)=+\infty\). Then for every \(0<r<1\),
\[
F(r)=\inf_{\substack{d<\infty,\ J,C\\ K_{\rm ph}(J,C)\preceq rI}}H(J).
\tag{M.6.13el.2}
\]
The infimum is unchanged if the densities \(J\) in (M.6.13el.2) are continuous. The equality is an equivalence of the upper noise and entropy closures for parity-invariant matrix budgets: every complete finite apparatus within such a budget gives a matrix phase pair within the same budget and with no greater entropy, and every matrix phase pair of finite entropy is approximated in noise and entropy by complete finite apparatuses. In the latter direction, one can meet the original budget \(rI\) exactly whenever the phase pair meets it, with a sequence whose asymmetry has limit \(H(J)\).

For a parity- and reflection-symmetric tester \(Z=x|e\rangle\langle e|+y|m\rangle\langle m|+z|f\rangle\langle f|\), with \(x,y>0\), \(z\ge0\), set \(M=(x+y)/(2\sqrt{xy})\) and
\[
V_{Z,C}(\theta)=\operatorname{Tr}_S\!\left[
(Z\otimes I)\bigl((U_\theta\otimes I)C(U_\theta^*\otimes I)-X\otimes I\bigr)^2\right].
\]
For every fixed coefficient dimension \(d\), the phase pressure is the compact optimization
\[
\begin{split}
b_d^{\rm ph}(Z)
&=\inf_{J,C}\left[H(J)+\operatorname{Tr}(ZK_{\rm ph}(J,C))\right]\\
&=-\log\max_{\substack{\tau\succeq0,\ \operatorname{Tr}\tau=1\\
C=C^*,\ (P\otimes I)C(P\otimes I)=-C,\ \|C\|\le M}}
\int\operatorname{Tr}\exp\bigl(\log\tau-V_{Z,C}(\theta)\bigr).
\end{split}
\tag{M.6.13el.3}
\]
For singular \(\tau\) the exponential is on \(\operatorname{supp}\tau\), compressing \(V_{Z,C}(\theta)\) to that support. At a maximum a minimizing density is the normalized matrix Gibbs density proportional to this exponential, with \(\int J_\theta=\tau\). Finally \(b(Z)=\inf_{d\ge1}b_d^{\rm ph}(Z)\). No uniform bound on the needed coefficient dimension is imposed.

*Proof.* Oddify an original invariant finite observable by \(P\) as in Theorem M.6.13dc. The new noise obeys \(K_{\rm odd}\preceq(K+PKP)/2\), so it keeps every scalar budget \(rI\). For an upper matrix budget, this map preserves its parity average. The weighted noise decreases for the testers in (M.6.13el.3). The odd observable has only the two unit charge shifts on the reference. Pinch the ready state by the orthogonal projections onto each fractional charge class modulo \(\mathbb Z\). The observable and the target both preserve these classes on the reference, so this pinching leaves the entire odd noise matrix unchanged. It cannot increase \(\mathcal A_Q\), by relative-entropy data processing since it commutes with charge pinching. Subtract the same fractional charge origin from all charges in each class. Treat the classes as a retained classical direct sum, so the resulting integer charge on each class is twirled independently. Consequently the new block state has exactly the asymmetry of the fractional-class-pinched state. In particular merging integer labels of different classes introduces no cross-class matrix entries. This constructs a new formal finite reference with the same relevant differences and the energy-host realization of Theorem M.6.13df.

For this integer reference take \(d=\dim R\), \(C=B_{\rm odd}\), \(V_\theta=e^{iQ_R\theta}\), and \(J_\theta=V_\theta^*\sigma V_\theta\). Conservation gives
\[
(U_\theta\otimes I)C(U_\theta^*\otimes I)
=(I\otimes V_\theta^*)C(I\otimes V_\theta).
\]
Thus the conditional reference trace in (M.6.13el.1) equals \(K_\sigma(C)\) at every angle, by conjugating the ready state and the full square by the same reference unitary. The mean of \(J\) is the charge twirl, and each \(\operatorname{Tr}(J_\theta\log J_\theta)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma\log\sigma)\). Hence \(H(J)=\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\). The reverse construction below starts with any \(J,C\) and approximates their exact matrix \(K_{\rm ph}\). The forward upper-closure equivalence therefore refers to the parity-invariant noise budgets used here, or to noise matrices of the odd conserving class.

For the reverse direction first suppose \(J\) is continuous. Write \(C=\sum_{k=\pm1} C_k\) for its system charge components \([Q_S\otimes I,C_k]=kC_k\), so \(C_{-k}=C_k^*\). Equivalently \((U_\theta\otimes I)C(U_\theta^*\otimes I)=\sum_k e^{ik\theta}C_k\). On the ladder \(\mathbb C^n\) with charges \(0,\ldots,n-1\), let \(S_n|a\rangle=|a+1\rangle\) for \(a<n-1\) and \(S_n|n-1\rangle=0\). Set
\[
B_n=C_1\otimes S_n^*+C_{-1}\otimes S_n
\]
on system, neutral coefficients and ladder. It is odd, Hermitian and conserves the system plus ladder charge. For \(\theta_\ell=2\pi\ell/n\) and \(|v_\ell\rangle=n^{-1/2}\sum_{a=0}^{n-1}e^{ia\theta_\ell}|a\rangle\), use the ready state on the neutral coefficients and ladder
\[
\sigma_n=\frac1{n c_n}\sum_{\ell=0}^{n-1}J_{\theta_\ell}\otimes |v_\ell\rangle\langle v_\ell|,
\qquad c_n=\frac1n\sum_{\ell=0}^{n-1}\operatorname{Tr}J_{\theta_\ell}.
\]
Here \(c_n\to1\), hence \(c_n>0\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). The twirl is \(\tau_n\otimes I_n/n\), where \(\tau_n=(n c_n)^{-1}\sum_\ell J_{\theta_\ell}\). Diagonalizing the Fourier blocks gives the exact identity
\[
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_n)=\frac1n\sum_{\ell=0}^{n-1}
\operatorname{Tr}\left(\frac{J_{\theta_\ell}}{c_n}\log\frac{J_{\theta_\ell}}{c_n}\right)
-\operatorname{Tr}(\tau_n\log\tau_n).
\tag{M.6.13el.4}
\]
Continuity of \(t\log t\) on the common bounded spectral interval, with value zero at zero, and matrix functional calculus give convergence to \(H(J)\) by Riemann sums. In the noise expansion the ladder words have length at most two in \(S_n,S_n^*\). Their expectations in \(v_\ell\) equal the corresponding products of \(e^{-i\theta_\ell}\) and \(e^{i\theta_\ell}\) multiplied by \(1-k/n\) for \(0\le k\le2\), since at most two starting indices are lost by truncating a word. In particular \(S_n^*\) contributes the sign \(+i\theta_\ell\) required for the \(k=1\) system term. The constant terms and cross terms with \(X\) obey the same rule. The coefficients of the resulting error are bounded in norm by a constant depending on \(C,X\) times the average normalized mass of the ready blocks, which is one. Hence the boundary error is \(O(1/n)\) uniformly on system inputs. Riemann convergence of the matrix-valued terms gives \(K_{\sigma_n}(B_n)\to K_{\rm ph}(J,C)\) in norm.

For measurable \(J\) of finite entropy, convolve it with a nonnegative smooth periodic approximate identity, giving \(J^{(\varepsilon)}\). This has the same mean and normalization, stays positive, is bounded and smooth for each \(\varepsilon>0\), and converges to \(J\) in integrated trace norm. The bounded integrand coefficients in the square give norm convergence of \(K_{\rm ph}\). The trace function \(A\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}(A\log A)\) is convex on positive matrices, by the finite-dimensional entropy variational formula. Jensen and translation invariance give \(H(J^{(\varepsilon)})\le H(J)\). Along every sequence converging in \(L^1\), extract an almost-everywhere convergent subsequence of a subsequence approaching the entropy liminf. Since \(\operatorname{Tr}(A\log A)\ge-d/e\), Fatou's lemma gives \(H(J)\le\liminf H(J^{(\varepsilon)})\). Thus the entropies converge. Taking first the smoothing and then the ladder size sufficiently far along gives an ordinary sequence of finite models with both limits. Each finite conserving observable has the exact neutral spectral pointer of Theorem M.6.13dc, and Theorem M.6.13df supplies its physical realization with the entire reference and pointer included.

If an approximation has \(K_n\preceq(r+\epsilon_n)I\) with \(\epsilon_n\downarrow0\), mix it with a fixed finite strict apparatus at error \(r_s<r\) and weight \(\epsilon_n/(r-r_s+\epsilon_n)\) on the strict branch. The original scalar budget then holds exactly. The direct-sum flags of Theorem M.6.13dc give convergence to the same asymmetry and noise limits. If exact largest eigenvalue \(r\) is required, rescale the odd observable toward zero as in Theorem M.6.13de, keeping its ready state and asymmetry. The continuous-density version can use the corresponding strict actual phase pair from the forward direction and the same classical direct sum, so the budget repair stays within the continuous phase class. These arguments prove (M.6.13el.2). For an arbitrary parity-invariant matrix budget, norm convergence of the finite matrices gives the upper-closure assertion with the budget increased by a scalar tending to zero.

For (M.6.13el.3), at fixed \(J\) minimize the tested square in the constant \(C\). Its quadratic coefficient is
\[
R=\int(U_\theta^* ZU_\theta)\otimes J_\theta,\qquad
D=\int U_\theta^*(ZX+XZ)U_\theta\otimes J_\theta .
\]
The objective is \(\operatorname{Tr}(RC^2)-\operatorname{Tr}(DC)+\operatorname{Tr}(ZX^2)\). The even \(R\) and odd \(D\) give a supported odd Sylvester minimizer \(RC+CR=D\), zero-extended on the kernel. On the system basis \((e,m,f)\), the only nonzero entries of \(ZX+XZ\) are \(x+y\) in the two bright off-diagonals. Therefore \(-2MZ\preceq ZX+XZ\preceq2MZ\), including when \(z=0\). Conjugating, multiplying by \(J_\theta\succeq0\) on the other factor and integrating gives \(-2MR\preceq D\preceq2MR\). The integral Sylvester solution yields \(\|C\|\le M\), so imposing this bound does not change the infimum.

For any constant normalized density \(\omega\), relative-entropy splitting gives
\[
\int\operatorname{Tr}J_\theta(\log J_\theta-\log\omega)
=H(J)+D(\tau\Vert\omega),\qquad \tau=\int J_\theta .
\]
For singular \(\omega\) this holds when \(J_\theta\) is supported there almost everywhere, and otherwise the left side is infinite. Minimizing over \(\omega\) gives exactly \(H(J)\). For fixed \(C,\omega\), minimizing the resulting relative entropy plus \(\int\operatorname{Tr}(J_\theta V_{Z,C}(\theta))\) over normalized positive \(J\) gives \(-\log\int\operatorname{Tr}e^{\log\omega-V_{Z,C}(\theta)}\). Indeed subtracting this scalar value gives the integrated relative entropy to the normalized Gibbs density, which is nonnegative by the trace entropy inequality and the common total mass. Its minimizer is the stated Gibbs density.

The partition integrand, with the support convention, is jointly continuous in \(\omega,C,\theta\) in fixed dimension. To verify continuity at a singular \(\omega\), diagonalize a convergent sequence of density matrices in orthonormal bases converging along a subsequence, using compactness of the finite unitary group. The logs of the positive limiting eigenvalues converge and those of the vanishing eigenvalues tend to \(-\infty\). The perturbations \(-V_{Z,C}(\theta)\) have bounded norm. The min–max principle sends the corresponding number of low eigenvalues of the sum to \(-\infty\). For each of the remaining eigenvalues, the eigenvector equation on the vanishing block bounds its norm there by the off-diagonal norm divided by the diverging separation from that block. These remaining eigenvectors converge along subsequences to an orthonormal basis on the positive block, with eigenvalues of its compressed sum. Terms already outside a sequence member's support contribute zero and may be treated as diverging negative diagonal values for this argument. This proves pointwise trace-exponential convergence to the support prescription. Since \(V_{Z,C}(\theta)\succeq0\), the trace is bounded by \(\operatorname{Tr}\omega=1\), by min–max eigenvalue comparison. Dominated convergence proves continuity of the integrated objective. The feasible matrices form a compact set, hence a maximum exists. At a maximum its Gibbs density must have mean equal to the maximizing \(\omega\): otherwise the relative-entropy splitting strictly lowers the joint objective when \(\omega\) is replaced by that mean. This proves (M.6.13el.3). The forward construction preserves or lowers the weighted objective of every original apparatus, and the reverse construction approximates every finite phase dimension by complete finite apparatuses. This identifies \(b(Z)\) with the infimum over \(d\). \(\square\)

<a id="theorem-m613em"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613em-commuting-phase-frontier-and-a-dimension-uniform-noncommutativity-bound"></a>**Theorem M.6.13em (Commuting Phase Frontier and a Dimension-Uniform Noncommutativity Bound).** Use the matrix phase class of Theorem M.6.13el. Let \(F_{\rm com}(r)\) restrict that phase problem to densities \(J_\theta\) diagonal in one fixed orthonormal basis for almost every \(\theta\), with arbitrary finite coefficient dimension and with all constant odd Hermitian \(C\) still admitted. Then for every \(0<r<1\),
\[
F_{\rm com}(r)=\Phi(1-r).
\tag{M.6.13em.1}
\]
The infimum in this phase class is attained in coefficient dimension one. For every \(Z=x|e\rangle\langle e|+y|m\rangle\langle m|+z|f\rangle\langle f|\), \(x,y,z\ge0\), the commuting phase pressure is
\[
b_{\rm com}^{\rm ph}(Z)
=s-\log\sup_{t\ge0}\int_{\mathbb T}
 \exp\!\left[2st\cos\theta-t^2\bigl(y+x\cos^2\theta+z\sin^2\theta\bigr)\right]\,d\theta,
\qquad s=x+y.
\tag{M.6.13em.2}
\]
The measure \(d\theta\) here is the normalized circle measure of Theorem M.6.13el.

For any full matrix phase pair with \(K_{\rm ph}(J,C)\preceq rI\), let \(\mathcal E\) be pinching in any orthonormal basis of its neutral coefficient space and put
\[
\delta_{\mathcal E}=\int_{\mathbb T}\|J_\theta-\mathcal E(J_\theta)\|_1\,d\theta .
\]
For \(0<a<1\) set \(M_a=1/(2\sqrt{a(1-a)})\). Then
\[
H(J)\ge\Phi\!\left(\left[1-\frac{r+(M_a+1)^2\delta_{\mathcal E}}{1-a}\right]_+\right).
\tag{M.6.13em.3}
\]
In particular, if \(H(J)\le h<\Phi(1-r)\), every such basis satisfies the dimension-independent necessary condition
\[
\delta_{\mathcal E}\ge
\sup_{0<a<1}
\frac{\big[(1-a)(1-\Phi^{-1}(h))-r\big]_+}{(M_a+1)^2} >0.
\tag{M.6.13em.4}
\]
The same obstruction applies to each finite physical apparatus through its matrix phase image from Theorem M.6.13el. The exact unrestricted weak-quality coefficient \(c_*<1\) of Theorem M.6.13cd implies \(F(r)<F_{\rm com}(r)\) for all \(r\) sufficiently close to one.

*Proof.* Suppose first that \(J_\theta\) is diagonal in a fixed basis, and extend that basis pinching by the identity on the system. It commutes with \(\operatorname{Ad}U_\theta\) and fixes \(X\otimes I\). For each angle the conditional expectation is unital and completely positive. Its Kadison inequality for the square, followed by the partial trace against \(J_\theta\), gives
\[
K_{\rm ph}(J,(\operatorname{id}_S\otimes\mathcal E)(C))
\preceq K_{\rm ph}(J,C).
\tag{M.6.13em.5}
\]
Indeed the partial trace against a diagonal \(J_\theta\) is unchanged by inserting the pinching on the complete squared operator. Thus the observable can be taken block diagonal on the neutral basis, with no loss for any upper matrix budget or positive tester. Write \(J_\theta=\bigoplus_i w_i j_i(\theta)\), where \(w_i\ge0\), \(\sum_iw_i=1\), each occupied scalar density has \(\int j_i=1\), and terms of zero weight are omitted. Then
\[
H(J)=\sum_iw_i\int j_i\log j_i,\qquad
K_{\rm ph}(J,C)=\sum_iw_i K_{\rm ph}(j_i,C_i).
\tag{M.6.13em.6}
\]

For a scalar branch write \(A=C_{01}\), \(B=C_{12}\) in the charge basis, and set \(m_1=\int e^{i\theta}j(\theta)\,d\theta\). The middle-input noise is
\[
\int j(\theta)\left(\left|Ae^{-i\theta}-\frac1{\sqrt2}\right|^2+
                   \left|\overline B e^{i\theta}-\frac1{\sqrt2}\right|^2\right)d\theta
\ge 1-|m_1|^2 .
\tag{M.6.13em.7}
\]
Completing the two independent complex squares proves the bound. Taking the Gibbs relative entropy of \(j\) against the scalar density proportional to \(\exp[\kappa\cos(\theta-\arg m_1)]\) and optimizing \(\kappa\ge0\) gives
\[
\int j\log j\ge\Phi(|m_1|^2).
\]
This is the scalar variational formula of Theorem M.6.13l. The function \(\Phi\) is increasing and convex by its supremum-of-affine-functions representation (M.6.13ca.17). For any admissible \(J,C\), the middle-input bound gives \(\sum_iw_i|m_{1,i}|^2\ge1-r\), so convexity in (M.6.13em.6) gives \(H(J)\ge\Phi(1-r)\).

For equality take the even von Mises scalar density \(j(\theta)=e^{\kappa\cos\theta}/I_0(\kappa)\) with cosine mean \(t=\sqrt{1-r}\), and \(C=tX\). To compute its complete noise, use the basis \((e,m,f)\). At angle \(\theta\), the even-to-middle coefficients of the error are \(t\cos\theta-1\) and \(-it\sin\theta\) in the bright and dark channels, respectively. Its square has middle value \(|t\cos\theta-1|^2+t^2\sin^2\theta\), and an endpoint two-by-two block with these two nonnegative diagonal entries. The endpoint off-diagonal is odd in \(\theta\) and vanishes after averaging. Thus the largest eigenvalue is the middle value after averaging, namely \(1+t^2-2t^2=r\). Its entropy is exactly \(\Phi(t^2)\). Theorem M.6.13el supplies finite conserving apparatuses with this limiting cost and the exact original error budget.

For (M.6.13em.2), (M.6.13em.5)–(M.6.13em.6) reduce the objective to a weighted sum of scalar branch objectives, so its infimum is the scalar one. Put \(l=(A+B)/\sqrt2\), \(c=(A-B)/\sqrt2\) and \(h=(x+z)/2\). The full weighted scalar squared error at angle \(\theta\) is
\[
s-2s\operatorname{Re}(le^{-i\theta})
 +(y+h)|l|^2+\frac{x-z}{2}\operatorname{Re}(l^2e^{-2i\theta})
 +(y+h)|c|^2-\frac{x-z}{2}\operatorname{Re}(c^2e^{-2i\theta}).
\]
The \(c\)-quadratic is nonnegative because \(y+h\ge |x-z|/2\). Its minimum occurs at \(c=0\) for all angles simultaneously. Rotate the circle coordinate to make \(l=t\ge0\). The \(l\)-quadratic then equals \(t^2(y+x\cos^2\theta+z\sin^2\theta)\). For fixed \(t\), the scalar Gibbs variational formula gives the negative logarithm of the corresponding partition integral, with the constant \(s\) separated. Taking the infimum in \(t\) proves the formula, including singular testers without a claim of a finite maximizing \(t\) there.

For (M.6.13em.3), keep \(J\) and use \(Z_a=a|e\rangle\langle e|+(1-a)|m\rangle\langle m|\), a positive tester of trace one. Its original weighted noise is at most \(r\). The supported Sylvester minimizer in the proof of Theorem M.6.13el gives an odd \(C_a\) with \(\|C_a\|\le M_a\) and weighted noise at most \(r\). For the resulting bounded angular error, the positive coefficient \(V_{Z_a,C_a}(\theta)\) of (M.6.13el.3) has operator norm at most \((M_a+1)^2\), since \(\|X\|=1\) and \(\operatorname{Tr} Z_a=1\). Hölder's inequality for the integrated trace gives
\[
\operatorname{Tr}[Z_aK_{\rm ph}(\mathcal EJ,C_a)]
\le r+(M_a+1)^2\delta_{\mathcal E}.
\]
Pinch \(C_a\) as well and apply (M.6.13em.5) to \(\mathcal EJ\). The middle weight \(1-a\) now gives a middle-noise budget of \([r+(M_a+1)^2\delta_{\mathcal E}]/(1-a)\), because the bright test contributes nonnegative noise. The scalar-flag argument uses only that middle budget and gives the right side of (M.6.13em.3) as a lower bound on \(H(\mathcal EJ)\). Finally \(H(\mathcal EJ)\le H(J)\) by relative-entropy data processing applied to \(D(J_\theta\Vert\tau)\) and integrated over the circle. All support conventions follow those in Theorem M.6.13el, and if \(H(J)=+\infty\) the inequality is automatic. Inverting the increasing \(\Phi\) proves (M.6.13em.4). Its supremum is positive because \(1-\Phi^{-1}(h)>r\), so the numerator is positive for some \(a>0\) sufficiently small.

Near \(u=1-r=0\), \(\Phi(u)=u+O(u^2)\) from the power series of \(I_0,I_1\). By Theorem M.6.13cd and its complete finite weak-quality upper witnesses, \(F(1-u)=c_*u+o(u)\) with \(c_*<1\).
