The optimizing invariant Hermitian observable at this state admits the complete neutral pointer of Theorem M.6.13dc. This gives $b(tZ)<ts$. No sign at the threshold itself is inferred from the second variation. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613fb"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613fb-exact-pressure-onset-for-bipartite-coherence-without-gap-two-blocks"></a>**Theorem M.6.13fb (Exact Pressure Onset for Bipartite Coherence without Gap-Two Blocks).** Retain the full finite reference and spin-one tester $Z$ of Theorem M.6.13fa, with $y>0$, $h=(x+z)/2>0$, $s=x+y$ and susceptibility $\Gamma(Z)$. Consider the class of references and ready states $\sigma$ satisfying the following two conditions. Their charge-gap-two blocks vanish. Also, with $\tau=\mathcal G_Q\sigma$ and $D=\sigma-\tau$, there is a self-adjoint unitary $J$ on $\operatorname{supp}\tau$ such that
\[
[J,Q]=[J,\tau]=0,\qquad JDJ=-D.
\tag{M.6.13fb.1}
\]
The observable retains the complete finite conserving class. Let $b_{\rm bip}(tZ)$ be the weighted entropy and noise infimum on this ready-state class. Then
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
b_{\rm bip}(tZ)=ts, & 0\le t\le 1/\Gamma(Z),\\
b_{\rm bip}(tZ)<ts, & t>1/\Gamma(Z).
\end{array}
\tag{M.6.13fb.2}
\]
The linear branch is attained by an invariant ready state and the zero observable. At every positive $t$ on that branch, every finite attaining ready state is invariant. The same exact onset holds when the reference is restricted to at most two distinct charge values, with arbitrary finite multiplicities and mixed states.

Condition (M.6.13fb.1) is equivalent to bipartite coloring of the nonzero coherence graph in some common eigenbasis of $Q,\tau$. The vertices are the eigenvectors on $\operatorname{supp}\tau$ and an edge joins two vertices when their $D$-entry is nonzero. The graph may include charge gaps of any size other than two. In particular the theorem applies to integer charge ladders with coherence only between opposite charge parities.

*Proof.* Compress to the faithful support of $\tau$ as in Theorem M.6.13fa. Positivity of $\sigma$ ensures its support is contained there, and the compression can only lower the noise. Since both $Q,\tau$ commute with $J$, diagonalizing $J$ inside their common eigenspaces makes every nonzero $D$-entry connect opposite eigenvalues of $J$. Conversely any bipartite coloring in such an eigenbasis defines $J$ by its signs. This proves the graph statement.

Let $p_i>0$ and $q_i$ be the diagonal eigenvalue and charge of a common eigenbasis of $\tau,Q$. The optimized observable gain of Theorem M.6.13fa is now exactly
\[
g_Z(\sigma)=\frac{s^2}{2}\sum_{q_i=q_j+1}|D_{ij}|^2
\left(\frac1{y p_j+h p_i}+\frac1{y p_i+h p_j}\right).
\tag{M.6.13fb.3}
\]
Indeed oddification retains the optimum, and its two raising blocks have quadratic terms of gap zero or two in the tested error square. Gap zero is tested only against $\tau$, and gap two pairs to zero by the premise. The linear terms pair only to gap one. Thus the independent square completions in (M.6.13fa.3) are exact on this state, without an expansion or a restriction on the size of $D$.

For the entropy, let $H(u)=\operatorname{Tr}[(\tau+uD)\log(\tau+uD)]$ for $0\le u\le1$. The matrices are positive definite for $u<1$, even when $\sigma$ is singular. One has $H'(0)=0$ because $D$ has zero charge-diagonal blocks. For $u<1$, differentiating by the logarithm resolvent gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
H''(u)
&=\int_0^\infty\operatorname{Tr}\bigl[
D(\tau+uD+vI)^{-1}D(\tau+uD+vI)^{-1}\bigr]\,dv\\
&=\int_0^\infty\operatorname{Tr}
\bigl[F_v^2(I+uF_v)^{-2}\bigr]\,dv,\qquad
F_v=(\tau+vI)^{-1/2}D(\tau+vI)^{-1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13fb.4}
\]
The second equality follows by factoring the resolvents and cycling inside the trace. Since $J F_vJ=-F_v$, its nonzero eigenvalues occur in pairs $\lambda,-\lambda$. For each pair and $0<u<1$, positivity gives $1\pm u\lambda>0$, and
\[
\lambda^2\bigl[(1+u\lambda)^{-2}+(1-u\lambda)^{-2}\bigr]>2\lambda^2 .
\]
This is strict convexity of the reciprocal square on the positive line. If $D\ne0$, then $F_v\ne0$ for every finite $v$, so $H''(u)>H''(0)$ at $u>0$. Integrating the second derivative yields
\[
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)=H(1)-H(0)>
\frac12 H''(0)=
\sum_{i<j,\ q_i\ne q_j}|D_{ij}|^2
\frac{\log p_i-\log p_j}{p_i-p_j},
\tag{M.6.13fb.5}
\]
where the equality case $p_i=p_j$ in the quotient is defined by continuity. For a singular endpoint, first integrate up to $u<1$ and then take $u\uparrow1$, using continuity of the trace entropy. Strictness persists by integrating the strict positive difference of second derivatives over a fixed interior subinterval with positive limiting integration weight. The final sum is the same charge-pair calculation as (M.6.13fa.4).

By the pair-ratio maximum in Theorem M.6.13fa, (M.6.13fb.3) is bounded by $\Gamma(Z)$ times the sum in (M.6.13fb.5). Hence $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)-t g_Z(\sigma)>0$ for every non-invariant $\sigma$ and every $0<t\le1/\Gamma(Z)$. An invariant state has zero gain and zero asymmetry. This gives the first line of (M.6.13fb.2), its attainment, and its invariant-ready necessity. For $t>1/\Gamma(Z)$, the maximizing two-charge perturbation from Theorem M.6.13fa has only gap-one coherence and satisfies (M.6.13fb.1). Its actual optimized cost is strictly below $ts$, proving the second line.

For a two-charge reference with unit gap, its two charge blocks provide the bipartite coloring and it has no gap-two coherence. If the two charges have any other gap, no odd conserving raising coefficient is available. Its optimized gain is then zero by oddification, whether or not its state has gap-two coherence. Such references cannot lower the weighted cost below $ts$ by their nonnegative entropy. The same maximizing unit-gap perturbation witnesses the strict inequality above the threshold in the complete two-charge class. $\square$

<a id="corollary-m613fb1"></a>

<a id="corollary-m613fb1-exact-onset-for-all-gap-two-free-ready-states"></a>**Corollary M.6.13fb.1 (Exact Onset for All Gap-Two-Free Ready States).** Retain the complete spin-one tester and finite reference class of Theorem M.6.13fb. Suppose only that the ready state has zero blocks at charge gaps $\pm2$. The exact pressure and attainment conclusions (M.6.13fb.2) hold on this larger class, with no bipartite assumption on its other coherences. In particular, an unrestricted finite model whose tested objective is strictly below $ts$ at $t\le1/\Gamma(Z)$ must have a nonzero charge-gap-two ready-state block.

*Proof.* Pinch first into the fractional charge classes modulo $\mathbb Z$, as in Theorem M.6.13el. This preserves the odd observable noise and its optimum, because the odd blocks and their squares use only integer gaps. It keeps the full charge twirl $\tau=\mathcal G_Q\sigma$ and cannot increase asymmetry. If the pinching changes the state, the loss of asymmetry is strictly positive by the relative-entropy identity for a pinching. Work on the faithful support of $\tau$ after this reduction and denote the pinched ready state again by $\sigma$. Translate the charge origin separately in each retained class. Let $P$ be the integer charge parity on each such class and put
\[
\rho=(\sigma+P\sigma P)/2,\qquad D_o=\sigma-\rho,\qquad D_1=\text{the sum of the gap $+1$ and gap $-1$ blocks of $\sigma$} .
\]
Here $D_o$ is parity odd and supported on $\operatorname{supp}\rho$; $D_1$ is its gap-one part. The two pinchings give
\[
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)=\mathcal A_Q(\rho)+D(\sigma\Vert\rho).
\]
On $\operatorname{supp}\rho$, the parity entropy argument in (M.6.13fb.4) applies with $\rho,D_o$ in place of $\tau,D$. It gives $D(\sigma\Vert\rho)\ge\tfrac12\langle D_o,(\mathrm d\log)_\rho D_o\rangle_{\rm HS}$, strictly if $D_o\ne0$, including a singular $\sigma$ by the same interior-interval limit.

For a positive matrix $R$, write $\Omega_R X=\int_0^1 R^vXR^{1-v}\,dv$ on the full space. On $\operatorname{supp}R$ it is the positive inverse of $(\mathrm d\log)_R$, as seen from the reciprocal divided differences in an eigenbasis. For singular $R$ the same integral gives zero outside its support in the sense that only the supported compression of $X$ contributes. For any Hermitian $X$, completing the corresponding positive square gives
\[
\tfrac12\langle D_o,(\mathrm d\log)_\rho D_o\rangle_{\rm HS}
\ge\langle X,D_o\rangle_{\rm HS}-\tfrac12\langle X,\Omega_\rho X\rangle_{\rm HS}.
\tag{M.6.13fb.6}
\]
Only the supported compression is used in this inequality.

Now let $X$ have only gaps $\pm1$, within the retained fractional classes. The function $R\mapsto\langle X,\Omega_R X\rangle_{\rm HS}$ is concave by integration of the positive-power trace concavity of Lieb (1973). Its first derivative at $\tau>0$ along $\rho-\tau$ vanishes. Indeed the derivative of each matrix power at the charge-diagonal $\tau$ preserves charge gaps, as follows from its spectral divided differences. The other, undifferentiated power of $\tau$ has gap zero. The two factors of $X$ have gaps $\pm1$, so a nonzero trace term would require a differentiated gap $0$ or $\pm2$. The direction $\rho-\tau$ has none of these gaps, by the fixed charge twirl and the hypothesis. Thus concavity yields
\[
\langle X,\Omega_\rho X\rangle_{\rm HS}\le
\langle X,\Omega_\tau X\rangle_{\rm HS}.
\tag{M.6.13fb.7}
\]
For a singular $\rho$ the same bound follows by taking the endpoint limit along $(1-v)\tau+v\rho$, using continuity of the positive powers for exponents strictly between zero and one and bounded convergence in their integral.

Take $X=(\mathrm d\log)_\tau D_1$, which has only gaps $\pm1$ by the same divided-difference formula. Then $\langle X,D_o\rangle_{\rm HS}=\langle X,D_1\rangle_{\rm HS}$ by Hilbert–Schmidt orthogonality of the gap subspaces, and $\Omega_\tau X=D_1$. Combining (M.6.13fb.6)–(M.6.13fb.7) gives
\[
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge
\tfrac12\langle D_1,(\mathrm d\log)_\tau D_1\rangle_{\rm HS}.
\]
If $D_1\ne0$, then $D_o\ne0$, and the entropy comparison before (M.6.13fb.6) makes this bound strict. When $D_1=0$, the gain is zero and any non-invariant state still has strictly positive asymmetry. The exact gain formula (M.6.13fb.3) uses only the absence of gap two and is therefore valid on the entire enlarged class. Its edge ratio is bounded by $\Gamma(Z)$ times the last quadratic form. This proves the linear branch and its invariance condition. The two-charge perturbation of Theorem M.6.13fa again proves strict improvement for $t>1/\Gamma(Z)$. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613fc"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613fc-gap-two-coherence-can-preempt-the-quadratic-pressure-onset"></a>**Theorem M.6.13fc (Gap-Two Coherence Can Preempt the Quadratic Pressure Onset).** Use the complete finite spin-one class of Theorem M.6.13dc and a symmetric tester $Z=x|e\rangle\langle e|+y|m\rangle\langle m|+z|f\rangle\langle f|$. Put $s=x+y$, $h=(x+z)/2$, $d=(x-z)/2$, and suppose
\[
y,h>0,\qquad \left(\frac{y-h}{y+h}\right)^2\le\frac13,\qquad
\frac{d}{y+h}<1-\sqrt2 .
\tag{M.6.13fc.1}
\]
Then there is a nonempty open interval immediately below $t_c=1/\Gamma(Z)=(y+h)/s^2$ on which $b(tZ)<ts$. The inequality also holds at $t_c$. On this interval the pressure restricted to gap-two-free ready states is exactly $ts$ by Corollary M.6.13fb.1. The strict unrestricted inequality has complete finite additive-charge witnesses whose all-input squared error is strictly below one. The conditions hold, for example, at $(x,y,z)=(0,1,2)$, where $t_c=2$, and also on a region with all three weights positive.

*Proof.* For a fixed real $v$ and small real $u>0$ use the scalar phase density and observable
\[
j_u(\theta)=1+2u\cos\theta+2vu^2\cos2\theta,\qquad C=wX
\]
of Theorem M.6.13el. The density is normalized and positive whenever $2u+2|v|u^2<1$. The first and second cosine moments are $u$ and $vu^2$. The square of the odd error has no middle-to-endpoint entries. Its bright–dark cross entry integrates to zero by evenness in $\theta$. Direct multiplication in the $(e,m,f)$ basis gives the three noise eigenvalues
\[
k_e=1-2wu+\tfrac12w^2(1+vu^2),\qquad
k_m=1-2wu+w^2,\qquad
k_f=\tfrac12w^2(1-vu^2).
\tag{M.6.13fc.2}
\]
For example, the two endpoint-to-middle error amplitudes are $w\cos\theta-1$ and a purely imaginary multiple of $w\sin\theta$, and the middle input tests the sum of their squared magnitudes. Thus the tested cost before asymmetry is $s-2swu+(y+h+dvu^2)w^2$. Choosing
\[
w=\frac{su}{y+h+dvu^2}
\]
gives tested gain $g_u=s^2u^2/(y+h+dvu^2)>0$ for sufficiently small $u$.

Write $\xi=2u\cos\theta+2vu^2\cos2\theta$. With normalized angle measure, the entropy is the integral of $(1+\xi)\log(1+\xi)$. Its Taylor series converges uniformly for $u$ small, and its value is even in $u$ by the shift $\theta\mapsto\theta+\pi$. The quadratic entropy term contributes $u^2+v^2u^4$, the cubic term contributes $-vu^4$ at order four by $\int\cos^2\theta\cos2\theta=1/4$, and the quartic term contributes $u^4/2$ by $\int\cos^4\theta=3/8$. Consequently
\[
H(j_u)=u^2+(v^2-v+1/2)u^4+O_v(u^6).
\tag{M.6.13fc.3}
\]
The remainder is bounded on a neighborhood where $2|u|+2|v|u^2\le1/2$, by analyticity of the uniformly convergent integrated series and evenness.

At $t_c=(y+h)/s^2$, expansion of the rational gain gives
\[
H(j_u)-t_c g_u
=\left[v^2-\left(1-\frac{d}{y+h}\right)v+\frac12\right]u^4
+O_{y,h,d,v}(u^6).
\tag{M.6.13fc.4}
\]
Set $v=\tfrac12(1-d/(y+h))$. By (M.6.13fc.1) the bracket equals $1/2-(1-d/(y+h))^2/4<0$. For all sufficiently small $u>0$, the error is strictly negative. Fix such a value of $u$. Then for every $H(j_u)/g_u<t\le t_c$, the scalar phase objective $H(j_u)+t(s-g_u)$ is strictly below $ts$. This is a nonempty interval since $H(j_u)/g_u<t_c$. In the example $(0,1,2)$ one has $v=3/4$ and the coefficient in (M.6.13fc.4) is $-1/16$. Strictness of both inequalities in (M.6.13fc.1) at this example gives a region with positive $x,y,z$ by continuity.

In the same construction $w/u\to s/(y+h)\in(0,1)$, since the last inequality in (M.6.13fc.1) implies $x<h$. By (M.6.13fc.2), both bright eigenvalues are strictly below one for sufficiently small positive $u$, while $k_f$ tends to zero. Choose $u$ small enough for this and for the strict entropy comparison above. Fix any squared budget strictly between the largest of the three phase eigenvalues and one. The continuous phase density and the finite constant observable are admitted by Theorem M.6.13el. Its finite additive-charge ladder approximation converges in entropy and in the entire noise matrix. For any fixed $t$ in the displayed strict interval, a sufficiently accurate finite stage therefore meets the strict budget and retains the strict tested objective inequality. Its neutral pointer and other apparatus records are those in Theorems M.6.13dc and M.6.13df. Because $t\le t_c$, Corollary M.6.13fb.1 then requires nonzero charge-gap-two coherence in that finite ready state. This verifies strict preemption within the original finite class. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613fd"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613fd-uniform-gap-two-coherence-required-for-a-pressure-deficit"></a>**Theorem M.6.13fd (Uniform Gap-Two Coherence Required for a Pressure Deficit).** Use the complete finite spin-one class of Theorem M.6.13dc and a symmetric tester $Z=x|e\rangle\langle e|+y|m\rangle\langle m|+z|f\rangle\langle f|$ with $y>0$, $h=(x+z)/2>0$, $s=x+y$, and the susceptibility $\Gamma(Z)$ of Theorem M.6.13fa. Set $0<t\le1/\Gamma(Z)$. For a ready state $\sigma$ and invariant observable $B$ define the tested deficit and its raising gap-two block by
\[
\Delta=ts-\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)-t\operatorname{Tr}(ZK_\sigma(B)),\qquad
G_2=\sum_{q-q'=2}P_q\sigma P_{q'} .
\]
Here $P_q$ are the actual spectral projections of the reference charge, including all multiplicities. If $\|B\|\le M_0$, then
\[
\Delta\le 2\|G_2\|_1\,
  \left[\log2+t\left((\operatorname{Tr}Z)(M_0+1)^2-s\right)\right].
\tag{M.6.13fd.1}
\]
If $x,y>0$, the same inequality applies to every $B$, without any norm premise, by taking $M_0=M(x,y)=(x+y)/(2\sqrt{xy})$. In particular, on the open positive-weight preemption region of Theorem M.6.13fc, for any fixed $t$ with $b(tZ)<ts$ and $t\le1/\Gamma(Z)$, every minimizing sequence has
\[
\liminf\|G_2\|_1\ge
\frac{ts-b(tZ)}
 {2\left[\log2+t((\operatorname{Tr}Z)(M(x,y)+1)^2-s)\right]}>0.
\tag{M.6.13fd.2}
\]
The bound is uniform over every finite dimension, real charge spectrum, and complete mixed ready state.

*Proof.* For each pair of occupied charge blocks $q,q'$ with $q-q'=2$, let $X=P_q\sigma P_{q'}$ viewed as a rectangular map from the $q'$ block to the $q$ block. On their direct sum define
\[
W_{q,q'}=\begin{pmatrix}
(XX^*)^{1/2}&-X\\
-X^*&(X^*X)^{1/2}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
This matrix is positive semidefinite: in a singular-value decomposition of $X$, each nonzero singular value gives a two-dimensional block proportional to $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, and the remaining blocks vanish. Its trace is $2\|X\|_1$. Extend by zero and sum these positive matrices to obtain $W$. Although their diagonal supports can overlap, their off-diagonal blocks cancel precisely the original gaps $\pm2$. Their trace sum is
\[
w=\operatorname{Tr}W=2\sum_{q-q'=2}\|P_q\sigma P_{q'}\|_1=2\|G_2\|_1.
\]
The final equality holds because each input charge block appears at most once in the directed gap-two sum, as does each output charge block, so the singular values of that sum are the union of those of its rectangular blocks.

If $w>0$, put $\sigma'=(\sigma+W)/(1+w)$. This is a normalized positive state on the same reference with zero gap-two blocks. For a normalized positive state $\omega$ supported on a direct sum of two charge sectors, $\mathcal A_Q(\omega)\le\log2$. To see this, its twirl is the average of $\omega$ and its conjugation by the unitary with signs $+1,-1$ on the two sectors. The entropy of a binary mixture of equal weights is at most the average of the entropies plus $\log2$, and the conjugate has the same entropy. Thus each nonzero $W_{q,q'}$, normalized by its own trace, has asymmetry at most $\log2$. Convexity of $\mathcal A_Q(\omega)=D(\omega\Vert\mathcal G_Q\omega)$, from joint convexity of relative entropy, gives
\[
(1+w)\mathcal A_Q(\sigma')\le\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)+w\log2 .
\]
For the same invariant $B$, the tested noise is linear in the ready state. Since $\|X_{\rm sys}\|=1$ for the spin-one target $X_{\rm sys}=J_x$, its square on the system and reference is bounded by $(M_0+1)^2 I$. Hence
\[
(1+w)\operatorname{Tr}(ZK_{\sigma'}(B))
\le\operatorname{Tr}(ZK_\sigma(B))+w(\operatorname{Tr}Z)(M_0+1)^2 .
\]
Corollary M.6.13fb.1 gives $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma')+t\operatorname{Tr}(ZK_{\sigma'}(B))\ge ts$. Combine these three inequalities and subtract $wts$ to prove (M.6.13fd.1). If $w=0$, that corollary directly gives $\Delta\le0$.

For $x,y>0$ the weighted optimizing observable on a faithful ready state has norm at most $M(x,y)$ by (M.6.13dc.12). For singular $\sigma$ in a fixed finite reference, approximate it by faithful mixtures and take a subsequential limit of their minimizing observables in the compact invariant norm ball. Tested noise is continuous in both arguments on this finite carrier. Comparing with every fixed invariant competitor along the same subsequence shows that the limit minimizes the noise for $\sigma$. It has the same norm bound. Replacing $B$ by that minimizer leaves $\sigma$ and $G_2$ unchanged and cannot decrease $\Delta$. This proves the asserted unconstrained-observable bound in the positive-$x,y$ case. The coefficient in (M.6.13fd.1) is positive, since $\operatorname{Tr}Z=s+z$, $M_0\ge0$, and $\log2>0$. Applying the result to a minimizing sequence proves (M.6.13fd.2). The norm-capped replacement concerns the weighted objective and does not assert preservation of an independent all-input noise budget. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613fe"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613fe-high-accuracy-spin-one-tester-weights-and-high-weight-pressure"></a>**Theorem M.6.13fe (High-Accuracy Spin-One Tester Weights and High-Weight Pressure).** Use the complete finite spin-one apparatus and the entropy frontier $F(r)$ and pressure $b(Z)$ of Theorem M.6.13dc. Write a symmetric tester as $Z=x|e\rangle\langle e|+y|m\rangle\langle m|+z|f\rangle\langle f|$. For each $0<r<1$, choose any such maximizing tester $Z_r$ in (M.6.13dc.2) and write its weights as $x_r,y_r,z_r$. Then
\[
r\operatorname{Tr}Z_r\longrightarrow\tfrac12,\qquad r x_r\longrightarrow 0,
\qquad \limsup_{r\downarrow0}\frac{|y_r-z_r|}{y_r+z_r}\le\frac1{\sqrt3}.
\tag{M.6.13fe.1}
\]
In particular, $\liminf_{r\downarrow0}r\min(y_r,z_r)\ge (1-1/\sqrt3)/4$. These limits apply to every choice of symmetric maximizers.

For fixed $x,y,z>0$, the pressure on the ray $tZ$ obeys
\[
\begin{split}
\tfrac12\log(8\pi\min(y,z))
&\le\liminf_{t\to\infty}\bigl[b(tZ)-\tfrac12\log t\bigr]\\
&\le\limsup_{t\to\infty}\bigl[b(tZ)-\tfrac12\log t\bigr]
\le\tfrac12\log(4\pi(y+z)).
\end{split}
\tag{M.6.13fe.2}
\]
When $x>0$ and $y=z>0$, this determines the exact constant $\tfrac12\log(8\pi y)$. Both statements retain all finite reference dimensions, arbitrary finite real charge spectra and multiplicities, mixed states, and counted reference factors and pointers.

*Proof.* Let $T_r=\operatorname{Tr}Z_r$. The affine support inequality $F(v)\ge F(r)-(v-r)T_r$ follows from (M.6.13dc.2). For any fixed $\lambda>1$, use $v=\lambda r$ and Theorem M.6.13eq to get $\liminf rT_r\ge\log\lambda/[2(\lambda-1)]$. For $0<\lambda<1$, the same argument gives $\limsup rT_r\le-\log\lambda/[2(1-\lambda)]$. Sending $\lambda$ to one gives $rT_r\to1/2$.

Use normalized circle measure in Theorem M.6.13el. For $q>0$ let $f_q(\theta)$ be proportional to $\exp[-\theta^2/(2q)]$ for $-\pi\le\theta\le\pi$. Its normalized angle law has $\mathbb E\theta^2=q+O(q^2)$, $\mathbb E\theta^4=O(q^2)$, and
\[
H(f_q)=\tfrac12\log(1/q)+\tfrac12\log(2\pi/e)+o(1).
\tag{M.6.13fe.3}
\]
These follow by the substitution $\theta=\sqrt q\,u$ in the normalizing integral and moments. The truncated tails decay exponentially in $1/q$ up to polynomial factors. The scalar observable $C=X$ has noise diagonals $k_e=O(q^2)$, $k_m=q+O(q^2)$ and $k_f=q+O(q^2)$, by integrating $(\cos\theta-1)^2$, $2(1-\cos\theta)$ and $\sin^2\theta$, respectively. Take $q=r$ and evaluate this trial in the weighted pressure, using the phase-to-finite approximation of Theorem M.6.13el. The equality $F(r)=b(Z_r)-rT_r$ gives
\[
F(r)\le H(f_r)-rx_r+O(r^2T_r).
\]
Theorem M.6.13eq and (M.6.13fe.3) give $H(f_r)-F(r)=o(1)$. Together with $rT_r\to1/2$, this proves $rx_r\to0$.

Consider a sequence $r\downarrow0$ along which $ry_r\to a$, $rz_r\to b$. Such subsequential limits exist by the trace limit, and $a,b\ge0$, $a+b=1/2$. Set $\eta=(a-b)/(a+b)$. To bound it, choose $p,q_0>0$ with $p+q_0=1$, $p>q_0$, set $\tau=\operatorname{diag}(p,q_0)$, and use $Y=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Let $w$ be any bounded odd real function and let $\rho(u)=\tau+\varepsilon w(u)Y$ with $|\varepsilon|\|w\|_\infty<\sqrt{pq_0}$. The matrix phase density is $J_\theta=f_r(\theta)\rho(\theta/\sqrt r)$. Its mean is $\tau$ by symmetry. Let $\mathbb E$ denote expectation under the full standard real Gaussian and $m=\mathbb E[u w(u)]$. The variable $u=\theta/\sqrt r$ under $f_r$ is that Gaussian restricted to $|u|\le\pi/\sqrt r$ and renormalized. Consequently,
\[
\lim_{r\downarrow0}[H(J)-H(f_r)]
=\mathbb E D(\rho(u)\Vert\tau)
=\varepsilon^2\frac{\log p-\log q_0}{p-q_0}\,\mathbb E[w^2]+O(\varepsilon^4).
\tag{M.6.13fe.4}
\]
The entropy identity follows by splitting the scalar and normalized matrix factors of $J$. The Taylor coefficient follows from the two eigenvalues $[1\pm\sqrt{(p-q_0)^2+4\varepsilon^2w(u)^2}]/2$ and the unchanged diagonal of $\rho$. The remainder is uniform in $u$ for fixed $p,q_0,w$ and small $\varepsilon$, since the eigenvalues stay in a compact positive interval.

Take a real off-diagonal matrix $L$ and the constant odd observable with adjacent upper blocks $C_{01}=(I+i\sqrt r L)/\sqrt2$ and $C_{12}=(I+i\sqrt r L^*)/\sqrt2$. In the $(e,m,f)$ basis the $e,m$ and $f,m$ error blocks are
\[
S=(\cos\theta-1)I+\sqrt r\sin\theta\,L,
\qquad D=i(\sqrt r\cos\theta\,L-\sin\theta\,I).
\]
The three input diagonals are the integrated expectations of $SS^*$, $S^*S+D^*D$ and $DD^*$. Thus $k_e=O(r^2)$, and dominated convergence gives
\[
\lim_{r\downarrow0}\operatorname{Tr}(Z_r K_{\rm ph}(J,C))
=\mathbb E\operatorname{Tr}\rho(u)\bigl[a(L-uI)^*(L-uI)+b(L-uI)(L-uI)^*\bigr].
\tag{M.6.13fe.5}
\]
For domination, $|\sin(\sqrt r\,u)|/\sqrt r\le |u|$, $|1-\cos(\sqrt r\,u)|\le ru^2/2$, and $\rho(u)$ is a normalized density. Completing the real squares in $L_{12}$ and $L_{21}$ minimizes (M.6.13fe.5) to
\[
a+b-\varepsilon^2 m^2(a+b)^2
\left[\frac1{a q_0+b p}+\frac1{a p+b q_0}\right]
=a+b-\frac{2\varepsilon^2 m^2}{1-\eta^2(p-q_0)^2}.
\tag{M.6.13fe.6}
\]
The quadratic coefficients are the two denominators and the two linear coefficients are both $-2\varepsilon m(a+b)$. The denominators are positive even when one of $a,b$ vanishes.

If $\eta^2>1/3$, choose $v=p-q_0>0$ sufficiently small that
\[
\frac{\operatorname{artanh}v}{v}<\frac1{1-\eta^2v^2}.
\]
This follows from the series at zero, whose quadratic coefficients on the two sides are $1/3$ and $\eta^2$. Bounded odd truncations of $u$ converge to $u$ in Gaussian $L^2$, so one can choose $w$ with $m^2/\mathbb E[w^2]$ sufficiently close to one to preserve the strict inequality after multiplying the right side by this ratio. Since $(\log p-\log q_0)/(p-q_0)=2\operatorname{artanh}(v)/v$, the sum of (M.6.13fe.4) and the change from $a+b$ in (M.6.13fe.6) is then strictly negative for some fixed nonzero sufficiently small $\varepsilon$. Each trial has a finite coefficient space and a bounded observable at the chosen $r$. Its finite additive approximations preserve the tested objective in the limit by Theorem M.6.13el, so the defining pressure at $Z_r$ is at most that objective. Subtract $rT_r$ and use $rT_r\to a+b$. The trial would give $\limsup [F(r)-H(f_r)]<0$ along the chosen sequence, contradicting Theorem M.6.13eq. Hence $|\eta|\le1/\sqrt3$ for every such subsequential limit. This proves (M.6.13fe.1).

For (M.6.13fe.2), fix $x,y,z>0$. Let $W=\operatorname{Tr}(ZK_{\rm ph}(J,C))$ for an admitted matrix phase pair. Use the Hermitian coefficient operators $R_\theta,I_\theta$ of (M.6.13eq.2), with its two endpoint-to-middle error blocks. The sum of each pair of ordered squares is twice the sum of the squares of its real and imaginary parts. Weighting those positive ordered squares by the actual $x,y,z$ gives
\[
\int\operatorname{Tr}J_\theta R_\theta^2\le\frac{W}{2\min(x,y)},\qquad
\int\operatorname{Tr}J_\theta I_\theta^2\le\frac{W}{2\min(y,z)}.
\tag{M.6.13fe.7}
\]
All circle integrals here use normalized measure. Put $\alpha=1/[2\min(x,y)]$ and $\beta=1/[2\min(y,z)]$. Apply the two-coordinate bin and conditional tangent argument of Theorem M.6.13eq to (M.6.13fe.7). For a fixed Cartesian mesh $\delta$, the separate cosine and sine estimate errors are now bounded by $(\sqrt\alpha+\sqrt\beta)^2 W$. With collar width $W^{1/3}$, each bin error tends uniformly to zero as $W\downarrow0$, so its finite-alphabet conditional entropy tends uniformly to zero. The conditional tangent error, after clipping and inverting the sine in the bin, is bounded by
\[
W\,\frac{(\sqrt\beta+\sqrt\alpha\sin w_\delta)^2}{\cos^2 w_\delta},\qquad w_\delta=2\arcsin(\delta/\sqrt2).
\]
The Gaussian conditional entropy comparison in Theorem M.6.13eq then gives, taking first $W\downarrow0$ and then $\delta\downarrow0$,
\[
H(J)\ge\tfrac12\log\frac{2\pi}{e\beta W}-o(1)\qquad(W\downarrow0),
\tag{M.6.13fe.8}
\]
with a uniform error over all finite coefficient dimensions. In particular a complete finite positive-weight trial has $W>0$, since $W=0$ would force zero all-input noise and contradict Theorem M.6.13eq. For the pressure upper bound, take $C=X$ and the scalar $f_q$ with $q=1/[2t(y+z)]$. The already computed diagonals give $tW=1/2+o(1)$ and (M.6.13fe.3) yields the stated upper constant. For the lower bound select finite models within $1/t$ of the pressure. Their tested $W$ tends to zero by this upper bound and nonnegative asymmetry. Their matrix phase images have the same or smaller tested $W$ and asymmetry by Theorem M.6.13el. Apply (M.6.13fe.8) to the images and minimize $\tfrac12\log[2\pi/(e\beta W)]+tW$ over $W>0$. Its minimum occurs at $W=1/(2t)$, with value $\tfrac12\log(4\pi t/\beta)$. This proves the lower constant and the equality when $y=z$. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613ff"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613ff-exact-balanced-two-charge-spin-one-pressure"></a>**Theorem M.6.13ff (Exact Balanced Two-Charge Spin-One Pressure).** Use the complete finite spin-one apparatus of Theorem M.6.13dc and let $b_2(Z)$ denote its weighted pressure with at most two distinct reference charge values. Retain every finite multiplicity and mixed ready state, and include the pointer in the reference charge count. Let
\[
 Z=x|e\rangle\langle e|+y|m\rangle\langle m|+z|f\rangle\langle f|,
 \quad x,z\ge0,\quad y=(x+z)/2>0,\quad s=x+y,
 \quad \lambda=\frac{t s^2}{4y}.
\]
For every $t\ge0$, the exact pressure is
\[
 b_2(tZ)=ts+\min_{0\le u\le1}\{f(u)-\lambda u\},
 \qquad f(u)=\log2-h_2((1+\sqrt u)/2).
\tag{M.6.13ff.1}
\]
The pressure is attained by a scalar unit-gap two-charge reference and a counted neutral spectral pointer. When $\lambda\le1/2$ the unique minimizing quality is $u=0$. For $\lambda>1/2$ it is the unique $u\in(0,1)$ satisfying $\operatorname{artanh}\sqrt u=2\lambda\sqrt u$. In particular, all multiplicities and ready-state spectra are exhausted by this scalar optimum throughout the balanced tester plane. If $b(tZ)$ is the unrestricted finite pressure, then
\[
 b(tZ)<b_2(tZ)\qquad\left(t>\frac{60y\log3}{s^2}\right).
\tag{M.6.13ff.2}
\]
This strict comparison already has a three-charge witness.

*Exact observable gain on two charges.* Oddify the system observable as in Theorem M.6.13dc. If there is no unit charge gap in the reference, the odd observable vanishes and the best objective is $ts$. Otherwise write the charge-diagonal ready blocks in their separate eigenbases, with eigenvalues $p_i,q_j$ on the lower and upper sectors. Let $W_{ji}$ be the corresponding ready coherence. Compressing to the supports of the two diagonal blocks keeps the state and cannot increase any input noise, as in Theorem M.6.13ed. In the support the two odd raising blocks of the observable have separate quadratic penalties, since the two-charge spectrum has no gap-two coherence. Equation (M.6.13fb.3), or its two independent square completions, gives the optimized weighted gain over the zero observable as
\[
 g_Z(\sigma)=\frac{s^2}{2}\sum_{ij}|W_{ji}|^2
 \left(\frac1{y p_i+((x+z)/2)q_j}+\frac1{y q_j+((x+z)/2)p_i}\right)
 =\frac{s^2}{y}\sum_{ij}\frac{|W_{ji}|^2}{p_i+q_j}.
\tag{M.6.13ff.3}
\]
All included denominators are positive. When a charge sector is absent the sum is empty.

On the same reference consider a parity-odd Hermitian operator $H$, so its only nonzero blocks connect the two reference charges. Completing the complex squares entry by entry gives
\[
 u(\sigma):=\max_H\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(2H-H^2)
 =4\sum_{ij}\frac{|W_{ji}|^2}{p_i+q_j}.
\tag{M.6.13ff.4}
\]
Indeed the contribution from the $ji$ entry $H_{ji}$ of the raising block is $4\operatorname{Re}(\overline W_{ji}H_{ji})-(p_i+q_j)|H_{ji}|^2$. The maximum is attained in finite dimension. It lies in $[0,1]$ because the zero operator is admitted and $2H-H^2=I-(I-H)^2\preceq I$. In a two-charge reference, the parity pinching in Theorem M.6.13r is precisely charge pinching. Its trace-exponential proof (M.6.13r.6)–(M.6.13r.8) applies to every such $H$ and gives $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge f(u(\sigma))$, by continuous extension at $u=0,1$. Therefore (M.6.13ff.3) bounds the weighted objective below by $ts+f(u(\sigma))-\lambda u(\sigma)$.

For every $u\in[0,1]$ take the scalar unit-gap reference state with diagonal probabilities $1/2,1/2$ and real coherence $\sqrt u/2$. Its asymmetry is $f(u)$, and (M.6.13ff.4) is exactly $u$. Choose both raising blocks to have their square-completion coefficients $s\sqrt u/(2\sqrt2\,y)$. Then (M.6.13ff.3) is attained. The finite invariant observable has the complete neutral spectral pointer of Theorem M.6.13dc and adds no new charge values. The objective is the corresponding scalar value in (M.6.13ff.1), proving equality and physical attainment. The derivative $f'(u)=\operatorname{artanh}\sqrt u/(2\sqrt u)$ increases strictly from $1/2$ to infinity, as follows by integrating the power series of $(1-v^2)^{-1}$ from $0$ to $v=\sqrt u$. This gives the minimizing quality and the endpoint assertions.

*Three-charge separation.* On the scalar charges $0,1,2$, use the pure equal-amplitude vector $\psi$, with asymmetry $\log3$. Write $S|0\rangle=|1\rangle$, $S|1\rangle=|2\rangle$, $S|2\rangle=0$. Set both raising blocks of the odd spin-one observable to $aS$, with $a\ge0$. The linear gain term in (M.6.13ca.2), scaled to the tester $Z$, is $4\sqrt2\,sa/3$ because $\langle\psi,S\psi\rangle=2/3$. In (M.6.13ca.3) the quadratic terms of charge zero give $8ya^2/3$, since $y=(x+z)/2$ and each of $S^*S,SS^*$ has expectation $2/3$. The gap-two term gives $(x-z)a^2/3$, using $\langle\psi,S^2\psi\rangle=1/3$. The total quadratic penalty is $[(8y+x-z)/3]a^2$. It is positive for $a>0$, since $|x-z|\le2y$. Maximizing the gain over $a$ gives $8s^2/[3(8y+x-z)]$, which is at least $4s^2/(15y)$ and exceeds the largest two-charge gain $s^2/(4y)$ by at least $s^2/(60y)$. The finite observable has a counted neutral spectral pointer. Its cost is at most $ts+\log3-t[4s^2/(15y)]$, whereas every two-charge objective is at least $ts-t s^2/(4y)$ by nonnegative entropy. This proves (M.6.13ff.2). $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613fg"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613fg-isotropic-pressure-stability-and-exclusion-of-isotropic-optimal-testers"></a>**Theorem M.6.13fg (Isotropic Pressure Stability and Exclusion of Isotropic Optimal Testers).** Use the complete finite spin-one class and its symmetric pressure $b(Z)$ of Theorem M.6.13dc. Let $Z_0=\kappa I_3/2$ with $\kappa>1$, and let $a\in(0,1)$ be the unique solution of
$$
a=I_1(2\kappa a)/I_0(2\kappa a).
$$
For every sequence of odd conserving observables with a common finite norm bound and weighted objectives converging to $b(Z_0)$, the three noise entries in the $(e,m,f)$ basis converge to
$$
(k_e,k_m,k_f)
=\left(1-a^2-\frac{a^2}{2\kappa},\,1-a^2,\,\frac{a^2}{2\kappa}\right).
\tag{M.6.13fg.1}
$$
There is no bound on the reference dimensions, charge spectra, multiplicities or smallest nonzero ready-state eigenvalues. The restriction of $b$ to symmetric testers is differentiable at $Z_0$ with the noise vector (M.6.13fg.1) as gradient. No nonnegative scalar multiple of $I_3$ maximizes the unrestricted fixed-error dual at any $0<r<1$.

*Exact two-parameter moments.* Compress each model to the support of its charge twirl $\tau$. The weighted cost cannot increase, and its decrease tends to zero because the unrestricted pressure is a lower bound. The discarded excursion is positive in the noise matrix and its trace tends to zero since $Z_0>0$. Thus it suffices to work on this support, with $\tau>0$. Write $A,B$ for the two raising blocks and put $L=(A+B)/\sqrt2$, $C=(A-B)/\sqrt2$. Define $X_L=L+L^*$, $Y_L=i(L-L^*)$ and $K_L=(LL^*+L^*L)/2$, and similarly $K_C$. By (M.6.13ca.6), the objective minus $\kappa$ is
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)-\kappa\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(X_L-K_L)
+\kappa\operatorname{Tr}\sigma K_C .
$$
For independent $u,v>0$ the exact unrestricted infimum of the first two terms in the form $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)-\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(uX_L-vK_L)$ is $-\log S(u^2/v)$. Indeed replace $L$ by $vL/u$ and apply the sharp rotational bound and its finite approximants in Theorem M.6.13k, with the Gibbs variational formula as in Theorem M.6.13ca. This proves the equality on the full finite class. Hence $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma K_C\to0$, and the remaining objective tends to $-\log S(\kappa)$.

For $\kappa>1$ the maximizing scalar in $S(\kappa)$ is $a$. The quotient $I_1(z)/(zI_0(z))$ decreases strictly for positive $z$. In the series in $z^2$, the coefficient ratios of the numerator $I_1(z)/z$ and the denominator $I_0(z)$ are $1/[2(j+1)]$. Differentiating their quotient and pairing terms of different degrees gives strict decrease. The scalar derivative equation therefore has exactly one positive solution for $\kappa>1$, since the derivative is positive for small positive amplitudes and negative at amplitude one. Differentiating the maximum gives $(\log S)'(\kappa)=a^2$. Now test every near-minimizing pair against the exact pressure with $u=\kappa\pm h,v=\kappa$ and then with $u=\kappa,v=\kappa\pm h$. Taking sequence limits and then $h\downarrow0$ sandwiches the two moments between the corresponding difference quotients. This yields
$$
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma X_L\longrightarrow2a^2,\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma K_L\longrightarrow a^2.
\tag{M.6.13fg.2}
$$

*Stability of the angular Duhamel inequality.* On each support put $D=\log\tau$ and $H(x,y,t)=D+xX_L+yY_L-tK_L$. Write $F=\operatorname{Tr}e^H$ and let $\mathcal R$ be the nonnegative remainder in (M.6.13k.6). Use the planar Brownian motion and radius-$\kappa$ exit time $T$ of that theorem. The proof of (M.6.13k.13) gives
$$
F(\kappa,0,\kappa)\le S(\kappa)\,\mathbb E F(B_T,T)
\le S(\kappa).
$$
The variational identity gives
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)-\kappa\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(X_L-K_L)
=D(\sigma\Vert \sigma_G)-\log F(\kappa,0,\kappa),\qquad
\sigma_G=e^{H(\kappa,0,\kappa)}/F(\kappa,0,\kappa).
$$
Near equality implies $F(\kappa,0,\kappa)\to S(\kappa)$ and $D(\sigma\Vert\sigma_G)\to0$. In particular $\|\sigma-\sigma_G\|_1\to0$. It also gives $\mathbb E F(B_T,T)\to1$. The stopped supermartingale identity and its terminal bound imply for each finite $T_0$
$$
0\le \mathbb E\int_0^{T_0\wedge T}\mathcal R(B_t,t)\,dt
\le1-\mathbb E F(B_T,T)\longrightarrow0 .
\tag{M.6.13fg.3}
$$

The remainders are uniformly Lipschitz on every compact space-time box with $t\ge0$, including boxes meeting radius $\kappa$. To see this, $\operatorname{Tr}e^D=1$ and the common bound on $L$ give $\operatorname{Tr}e^H\le\exp(|x|\|X_L\|+|y|\|Y_L\|)$ there. For bounded Hermitian insertions $W_1,\ldots,W_m$, a mixed derivative of $\operatorname{Tr}e^H$ is a sum over permutations of ordered Duhamel integrals. On the simplex the exponential intervals sum to one, so Schatten Hölder bounds the absolute trace of each integrand by $(\operatorname{Tr}e^H)\prod_i\|W_i\|$. The permutation factor cancels the simplex volume. The same estimate with one additional fixed bounded operator under the trace proves the derivative bound for $\operatorname{Tr}(e^H X_L^2)$ and its $Y_L$ counterpart. The Duhamel terms in $\mathcal R$ are second derivatives, so the same bounds through order three establish the stated Lipschitz control independently of the spectrum of $D$.

At any point of radius strictly less than $\kappa$ and time $t>0$, a positive lower bound on $\mathcal R$ along a subsequence would give a positive lower bound on a fixed neighborhood by this Lipschitz estimate. Planar Brownian motion killed at the disk boundary has positive occupation measure on every such space-time neighborhood. For example it has positive probability to follow a sufficiently narrow tube around a piecewise-linear path staying in the disk and then remaining in that neighborhood for a time interval. This contradicts (M.6.13fg.3). Thus the remainder tends to zero at each interior point. The same uniform Lipschitz bound, applied from a fixed interior point and then with its distance to the edge tending to zero, gives $\mathcal R(\kappa,0,\kappa)\to0$.

At the terminal exponent $H=H(\kappa,0,\kappa)$ the two individual deficits are nonnegative. In particular
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(e^H Y_L^2)-\mathcal B_H(Y_L,Y_L)\longrightarrow0.
$$
By the exact angular identity (M.6.13k.5), $\mathcal B_H(Y_L,Y_L)=\operatorname{Tr}(e^H X_L)/\kappa$. Divide by $F(\kappa,0,\kappa)$ and use the Gibbs trace-distance convergence and the bounded insertions. Together with (M.6.13fg.2), this gives
$$
\operatorname{Tr}\sigma Y_L^2\longrightarrow2a^2/\kappa .
\tag{M.6.13fg.4}
$$

*Noise and dual exclusion.* Removing $C$ changes each tested error norm by at most a constant times $\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}\sigma K_C}$. This follows from the Hilbert–Schmidt purification of the ready state, since the sum of the squared norms of $C\sqrt\sigma$ and $C^*\sqrt\sigma$ is $2\operatorname{Tr}\sigma K_C$. All original and modified error norms are bounded on the sequence. With $A=B=L/\sqrt2$, direct substitution gives
$$
k_f=\tfrac14\operatorname{Tr}\sigma Y_L^2,\qquad
k_m=1-\operatorname{Tr}\sigma X_L+\operatorname{Tr}\sigma K_L,\qquad
k_e=k_m-k_f.
$$
This proves (M.6.13fg.1). For a sufficiently small symmetric perturbation of $Z_0$, near minimizers can be odd and chosen with a common finite norm bound by the weighted Sylvester estimate of Theorem M.6.13dc. Their noise vectors are bounded, so as the perturbation vanishes, any such near optimizer with objective error smaller than the perturbation norm also tends to isotropic pressure saturation. The preceding proof fixes the limit of its full three-entry vector. Test it at $Z_0$ for the lower bound on the pressure increment and test an isotropic minimizing sequence at the perturbed tester for the upper bound. The two bounds give the claimed derivative, with the error divided by the perturbation norm tending to zero.

At an active isotropic tester this derivative has $k_m-k_e=a^2/(2\kappa)>0$. A trace-preserving perturbation that increases middle weight and decreases bright weight strictly increases the dual objective, and it is feasible since $Z_0$ is positive definite. For $0\le\kappa\le1$, the isotropic dual objective is $\kappa(1-3r/2)$ by (M.6.13ca.8). If $r\ge2/3$ it cannot maximize, since $F(r)>0$. For $r<2/3$ it is increasing up to one. At one its right derivative is still $1-3r/2>0$, since the scalar maximizer tends to zero as $\kappa\downarrow1$ from above. This excludes the endpoint as well. The argument restricts the maximizing tester in the unrestricted problem. The pressure away from the isotropic tester and finite attainment at the actual maximizing tester retain their tests. $\square$

<a id="theorem-m613fh"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613fh-three-charge-pressure-attainment-with-at-most-four-neutral-dimensions"></a>**Theorem M.6.13fh (Three-Charge Pressure Attainment with at Most Four Neutral Dimensions).** Use the spin-one system $Q_S=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2)$, $X=J_x$, the operator $V_Z$ of (M.6.13dc.5) and the tester $Z=x|e\rangle\langle e|+y|m\rangle\langle m|$ of (M.6.13dc.10) with $x,y>0$, and put $s=x+y$, $\alpha=x/2$. For a ready state $\sigma$ on a finite reference $(R,Q_R)$ write
$$
g_Z(\sigma)=s-\min_B\operatorname{Tr}[\sigma V_Z(B)],\qquad
\mathfrak F_Z(\sigma)=g_Z(\sigma)-\mathcal A_Q(\sigma),
\tag{M.6.13fh.1}
$$
the minimum over Hermitian $B$ on $\mathcal H_S\otimes R$ commuting with $Q_S+Q_R$, as in Theorem M.6.13fa. Since $\operatorname{Tr}ZK_\sigma(B)=\operatorname{Tr}\sigma V_Z(B)$, $s-b(Z)$ is the supremum of $\mathfrak F_Z$ over all finite references and ready states. For $n\ge1$ let $b_{[n]}(Z)$ be the same pressure restricted to references whose charge values are $0,1,2$ with multiplicities $1,n,1$, so that $s-b_{[n]}(Z)$ is the supremum of $\mathfrak F_Z$ over their ready states.

1. Let $\sigma$ be a faithful ready state on a reference with charge values $0,1,2$ of multiplicities $1,n,1$. If $\sigma$ is a stationary point of $\mathfrak F_Z$ on the ready states of that reference and $\mathfrak F_Z(\sigma)>0$, then $n\le4$. On a reference with charge values $0,1$ (or $1,2$) of multiplicities $1,n$ (or $n,1$) the same hypotheses give $n\le2$.
2. Each $b_{[n]}(Z)$ is attained, $b_{[n+1]}(Z)\le b_{[n]}(Z)$, and
$$
\inf_{n\ge1}b_{[n]}(Z)=b_{[4]}(Z),
\tag{M.6.13fh.2}
$$
which is attained on the reference with multiplicities $1,4,1$. If $b_{[n]}(Z)<s$, every attaining ready state, restricted to the support of $\mathcal G_Q\sigma$, is faithful there; its charge-one block has rank at most four, and at most two when only one of the charges $0,2$ is occupied.
3. An attainer of $b_{[4]}(Z)$ has reference dimension at most six. The spectral pointer of Theorem M.6.13dc, Part I, realizes its optimal invariant observable, both moments exactly and with no added asymmetry, on a complete reference of dimension at most $6\cdot18=108$.

*Proof.*

##### I. Gain and asymmetry of a faithful three-charge state

Order the reference as charge $0$, charge $2$, charge $1$, and write a faithful ready state as
$$
\sigma=\begin{pmatrix}O&V^*\\V&D\end{pmatrix},\qquad
O=\begin{pmatrix}p&\omega\\\bar\omega&r\end{pmatrix},\qquad
D=\sum_j\lambda_jP_j,\qquad M_j=V^*P_jV,
$$
where $\lambda_j>0$ are the distinct eigenvalues of the charge-one block, $P_j$ its spectral projections, of ranks $r_j$, and $V$ the $n\times2$ block of coherences between charge one and the charges $0,2$. By (M.6.13dc.11) at $z=0$, each center charge $q$ contributes the optimal value $\frac{s^2}2\langle V_q,\mathcal S_q^{-1}V_q\rangle$ of its odd block, where $\mathcal S_q(T)=\alpha E_qT+yT\sigma_{q,q}$ in the notation of Part VI of that proof. Evaluating the three center charges in eigenbases gives
$$
g_Z(\sigma)=\sum_j\operatorname{Tr}[G(\lambda_j)M_j],\qquad
G(\lambda)=\frac{s^2}2\left[\begin{pmatrix}(\alpha\lambda+yp)^{-1}&0\\0&(\alpha\lambda+yr)^{-1}\end{pmatrix}+(\alpha O+y\lambda I_2)^{-1}\right].
\tag{M.6.13fh.3}
$$
The diagonal terms are the center charges $0$ and $2$. The matrix inverse is the center charge one and contains the gap-two coherence $\omega$. With $O=\sum_{i=1}^2o_iQ_i$ in spectral form, $G$ is a sum of four positive rank-one atoms:
$$
G(\lambda)=\sum_{\ell=1}^4\frac{R_\ell}{\lambda+t_\ell},\qquad
\begin{aligned}
&(t_1,R_1)=\Bigl(\tfrac{yp}\alpha,\tfrac{s^2}{2\alpha}|0\rangle\langle0|\Bigr),\quad
(t_2,R_2)=\Bigl(\tfrac{yr}\alpha,\tfrac{s^2}{2\alpha}|2\rangle\langle2|\Bigr),\\
&(t_{2+i},R_{2+i})=\Bigl(\tfrac{\alpha o_i}y,\tfrac{s^2}{2y}Q_i\Bigr),\quad i=1,2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.13fh.4}
$$
For positive definite $\rho,\tau$ of equal trace, $\operatorname{Tr}\rho\log\rho-\operatorname{Tr}\tau\log\tau=\int_0^\infty\log[\det(\tau+tI)/\det(\rho+tI)]\,dt$, by integrating $\frac{d}{d\mu}\int_0^T\log(\mu+t)\,dt$ and letting $T\to\infty$. With $S(t)=O+tI-\sum_jM_j/(\lambda_j+t)$, the Schur determinant formula gives $\det(\sigma+tI)=\det(D+tI)\det S(t)$, while $\det(\mathcal G_Q\sigma+tI)=\det(D+tI)(p+t)(r+t)$. Hence
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)=\int_0^\infty\log\frac{(p+t)(r+t)}{\det S(t)}\,dt.
\tag{M.6.13fh.5}
$$

##### II. Stationarity equations

For $\lambda>0$ put
$$
E(\lambda)=\int_0^\infty\frac{S(t)^{-1}}{\lambda+t}\,dt,\qquad H(\lambda)=G(\lambda)-E(\lambda).
\tag{M.6.13fh.6}
$$
A variation of $V$ at fixed $O$ and $D$ changes $M_j$ by $\delta M_j$ and $S(t)$ by $-\sum_j\delta M_j/(\lambda_j+t)$, so $\delta\mathcal A_Q=\sum_j\operatorname{Tr}[E(\lambda_j)\delta M_j]$; $G$ depends only on $O$, so $\delta\mathfrak F_Z=\sum_j\operatorname{Tr}[H(\lambda_j)\delta M_j]$. A Hermitian variation $\delta$ of $D$ supported in $\operatorname{ran}P_j$ gives, from (M.6.13fh.4)–(M.6.13fh.5),
$$
\delta\mathfrak F_Z=\operatorname{Tr}[V_jH'(\lambda_j)V_j^*\delta],\qquad V_j=P_jV.
$$
Both $g_Z$ and $\mathcal A_Q$ extend to positive operators as functions homogeneous of degree one, so by Euler's identity the Lagrange multiplier of $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma=1$ is $\mathfrak F_Z(\sigma)$; variations of $V$ leave the trace unchanged. A faithful stationary point therefore satisfies
$$
V_jH(\lambda_j)=0,\qquad V_jH'(\lambda_j)V_j^*=\mathfrak F_Z(\sigma)\,I_{\operatorname{ran}P_j}\quad\text{for every }j.
\tag{M.6.13fh.7}
$$
If $\mathfrak F_Z(\sigma)>0$, then $V_j^*$ is injective on $\operatorname{ran}P_j$. Its range $U_j$ has dimension $r_j$, lies in $\ker H(\lambda_j)$, and $H'(\lambda_j)$ is positive definite on $U_j$, since $u=V_j^*c$ gives $u^*H'(\lambda_j)u=\mathfrak F_Z(\sigma)|c|^2$.

##### III. A finite-negative-rank crossing lemma

<a id="lemma-m613fha-crossings-of-a-stieltjes-perturbed-kernel"></a>**Lemma M.6.13fh.a (Crossings of a Stieltjes-Perturbed Kernel).** Let $H:(0,\infty)\to\operatorname{Herm}(\mathbb C^k)$ be real analytic and negative definite outside a compact interval $[a,b]\subset(0,\infty)$. Write $H[\lambda,\mu]=(H(\lambda)-H(\mu))/(\lambda-\mu)$ and $H[\lambda,\lambda]=H'(\lambda)$, and suppose
$$
H[\lambda,\mu]=\mathcal B(\lambda,\mu)-\sum_{\ell=1}^m\frac{R_\ell}{(\lambda+t_\ell)(\mu+t_\ell)},
\tag{M.6.13fh.8}
$$
where $t_\ell>0$, $R_\ell\succeq0$, and $\mathcal B$ is a positive kernel: $\sum_{a,c}u_a^*\mathcal B(\mu_a,\mu_c)u_c\ge0$ for every finite family of points $\mu_a$ and vectors $u_a$. If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_J$ are distinct and $U_j\subset\ker H(\lambda_j)$ are subspaces of dimension $r_j$ on which $H'(\lambda_j)$ is positive definite, then
$$
\sum_jr_j\le\rho:=\sum_\ell\operatorname{rank}R_\ell .
$$

*Proof.* By analytic perturbation theory for Hermitian families (Kato 1966, Chapter II, §6), on a neighbourhood of $[a,b]$ the eigenvalues of $H$ form finitely many real-analytic branches $e_i$ with analytic orthonormal eigenvectors. A nonconstant branch has finitely many critical points in $[a,b]$. Choose $\epsilon>0$ different from every critical value of a nonconstant branch and from every constant branch; all sufficiently small $\epsilon$ outside a finite set qualify. Then $H-\epsilon I$ is negative definite outside $[a,b]$, and at every zero $\lambda$ of a branch $e_i-\epsilon$ in $[a,b]$ the compression of $H'(\lambda)$ to $\ker(H(\lambda)-\epsilon I)$ is diagonal in the branch eigenvectors, with the nonzero entries $e_i'(\lambda)$. Call such a zero downward if $e_i'(\lambda)<0$ and upward if $e_i'(\lambda)>0$.

Take one unit eigenvector $u_c$ for each downward zero $c$, located at $\lambda_c$. For zeros at distinct points,
$u_c^*H[\lambda_c,\lambda_{c'}]u_{c'}=(\epsilon u_c^*u_{c'}-\epsilon u_c^*u_{c'})/(\lambda_c-\lambda_{c'})=0$; at a common point $u_c^*H'(\lambda_c)u_{c'}=e_c'(\lambda_c)\delta_{cc'}$. Thus the matrix $[u_c^*H[\lambda_c,\lambda_{c'}]u_{c'}]$ is diagonal and negative definite. By (M.6.13fh.8) it is a positive semidefinite matrix minus the Gram matrix of the vectors $(R_\ell^{1/2}u_c/(\lambda_c+t_\ell))_\ell$ in $\bigoplus_\ell\operatorname{ran}R_\ell$, whose rank is at most $\rho$. On the kernel of that Gram matrix the difference is positive semidefinite, so its size is at most $\rho$. There are at most $\rho$ downward zeros.

The number of positive eigenvalues of $H(\lambda)-\epsilon I$ vanishes outside $[a,b]$ and changes only at zeros, by the number of upward minus the number of downward zeros there. Hence there are at most $\rho$ upward zeros. At $\lambda_j$ the compression of $H'(\lambda_j)$ to $\ker H(\lambda_j)$ has at least $r_j$ positive eigenvalues by the min–max principle, and these are the derivatives at $\lambda_j$ of the branches vanishing there. For all sufficiently small admissible $\epsilon$, each of these branches has an upward zero of $e_i-\epsilon$ near $\lambda_j$, and zeros near distinct $\lambda_j$ are distinct. Therefore $\sum_jr_j\le\rho$. $\square$

##### IV. At most four neutral dimensions

The divided differences of (M.6.13fh.6) are
$$
H[\lambda,\mu]=\int_0^\infty\frac{S(t)^{-1}}{(\lambda+t)(\mu+t)}\,dt-\sum_{\ell=1}^4\frac{R_\ell}{(\lambda+t_\ell)(\mu+t_\ell)} .
$$
The integral is a positive kernel, since $\sum_{a,c}u_a^*\mathcal B(\mu_a,\mu_c)u_c=\int_0^\infty\|S(t)^{-1/2}\sum_au_a/(\mu_a+t)\|^2dt$, and $\sum_\ell\operatorname{rank}R_\ell=4$. $H$ is real analytic on $(0,\infty)$. Since $O\preceq I$ and $\sum_jM_j/(\lambda_j+t)\succeq0$, $S(t)\preceq(1+t)I$ and
$$
E(\lambda)\succeq\frac{\log\lambda}{\lambda-1}\,I\qquad(\text{value }1\text{ at }\lambda=1).
$$
With $m=\lambda_{\min}(O)>0$ and $K_0=\frac{s^2}2(\alpha^{-1}+y^{-1})$, the bounds $p,r\ge m$ give $\|G(\lambda)\|\le K_0/m$ and $\|G(\lambda)\|\le K_0/\lambda$. Hence $H(\lambda)\prec0$ for $\lambda<e^{-K_0/m}$ and for $\lambda>e^{K_0}$. Lemma M.6.13fh.a with the subspaces $U_j$ of Part II gives $n=\sum_jr_j\le4$.

On a two-charge reference with one outer charge of population $p$, the center charges at that outer charge and at charge one give $G(\lambda)=\frac{s^2}2[(\alpha\lambda+yp)^{-1}+(\alpha p+y\lambda)^{-1}]$, and (M.6.13fh.5) holds with the single factor $p+t$ and scalar $S(t)$. The same argument with two atoms gives $n\le2$. This proves item 1.

##### V. Attainment

For a faithful ready state, (M.6.13dc.12) gives a minimizing observable with $\|B\|\le M(x,y)=s/(2\sqrt{xy})$. For a singular ready state $\sigma$, take faithful $\sigma_k\to\sigma$ with such minimizers $B_k$ and a limit point $B_0$; upper semicontinuity of $\sigma\mapsto\min_B\operatorname{Tr}\sigma V_Z(B)$ gives $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma V_Z(B_0)\le\min_B\operatorname{Tr}\sigma V_Z(B)$, so the minimum is attained in the same ball. On that ball $0\preceq V_Z(B)\preceq s(M+1)^2I$, so $g_Z$ is Lipschitz on ready states of a fixed reference. $\mathcal A_Q$ is continuous there, hence each $b_{[n]}(Z)$ is attained. Adding a charge-one direction of zero population changes neither $g_Z$ nor $\mathcal A_Q$, so $b_{[n+1]}\le b_{[n]}$; invariant ready states have $\mathfrak F_Z=0$, so $b_{[n]}\le s$.

Let $\sigma$ attain $b_{[n]}(Z)<s$ and let $E=\operatorname{supp}\mathcal G_Q\sigma$. This subspace is charge invariant and contains the support of $\sigma$. Restriction to $E$ leaves $\mathcal A_Q$ unchanged, and it leaves $g_Z$ unchanged: compressing an invariant observable to $\mathcal H_S\otimes E$ removes the expectation of a positive square, and an invariant observable on $\mathcal H_S\otimes E$ extends by zero. The argument of Theorem M.6.13dc, Part IV, applied to $(1-\epsilon)\sigma+\epsilon\mathcal G_Q\sigma$ with $g_Z$ Lipschitz, shows that $\sigma$ is faithful on $E$: otherwise the entropy gain of order $\epsilon\log(1/\epsilon)$ exceeds the $O(\epsilon)$ change of $g_Z$. On $E$ the charges $0,2$ have dimension zero or one. If charge one is absent, or both outer charges are absent, every odd invariant observable vanishes and $g_Z=0$, contradicting $\mathfrak F_Z(\sigma)>0$. Otherwise $\sigma$ is an interior maximizer of $\mathfrak F_Z$ on the ready states of $E$, hence a faithful stationary point, and item 1 bounds the dimension $n'$ of the charge-one part of $E$ by four, or by two when one outer charge is absent. Padding with zero-population directions places it on the reference with multiplicities $1,4,1$. Thus $b_{[4]}\le b_{[n]}$ for every $n$, which with monotonicity proves item 2.

For item 3, the attainer has reference dimension $1+4+1=6$. Its invariant optimal observable on the eighteen-dimensional space $\mathcal H_S\otimes R$ has at most eighteen distinct eigenvalues. The spectral pointer of Theorem M.6.13dc, Part I, uses one pure neutral pointer label per eigenvalue, conserves charge, reproduces both moments and adds no ready asymmetry. The complete reference has dimension at most $6\cdot18=108$. $\square$

Theorem M.6.13fh gives finite attainment of the restricted pressure on the union of the three-charge classes, with explicit reference and pointer dimensions. The value $b_{[4]}(Z)$ and a reduction of general references to these classes remain open.

<a id="theorem-m613fi"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613fi-charge-local-multiplicity-bound-at-positive-stationary-states"></a>**Theorem M.6.13fi (Charge-Local Multiplicity Bound at Positive Stationary States).** Retain $Z$, $s$, $\alpha$ and $\mathfrak F_Z$ of Theorem M.6.13fh. Let $(R,Q_R)$ be a finite reference with arbitrary real charge values, put $d_t=\dim\ker(Q_R-t)$, with $d_t=0$ when $t$ is not an eigenvalue, and let $\sigma$ be a faithful ready state on $R$ that is a stationary point of $\mathfrak F_Z$ on the ready states of $R$ with $\mathfrak F_Z(\sigma)>0$. Then for every eigenvalue $r$ of $Q_R$
$$
d_r\le2\,(d_{r-1}+d_{r+1}).
\tag{M.6.13fi.1}
$$
In particular every occupied charge has an occupied neighbour at distance one. The bound holds for a finite-dimensional maximizer of $\mathfrak F_Z$ with positive value after restriction to the support of its charge twirl, as in Part V of the proof of Theorem M.6.13fh. The inequalities are homogeneous: for every $L\ge2$ and $k\ge1$ the constant vector $d_0=\cdots=d_{L-1}=k$ satisfies all of them, so they bound ratios of neighbouring multiplicities and leave the number of occupied charges and $\dim R$ unbounded.

*Proof.* Fix $r$, write $R=R_r\oplus R_r^c$ with $R_r=\ker(Q_R-r)$, and
$$
\sigma=\begin{pmatrix}D&V\\V^*&O\end{pmatrix},\qquad D=\sum_j\lambda_jP_j,\qquad M_j=V^*P_jV,\qquad S(t)=O+tI-\sum_j\frac{M_j}{\lambda_j+t},
$$
with $M_j$ and $S(t)$ acting on $R_r^c$. The charge twirl acts separately on $R_r$, where it fixes $D$, and on $R_r^c$, so as in (M.6.13fh.5)
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)=\int_0^\infty\log\frac{\det(\mathcal G_QO+tI)}{\det S(t)}\,dt,
$$
and with $E(\lambda)=\int_0^\infty S(t)^{-1}(\lambda+t)^{-1}dt$ the variations of $V$ and of $D$ inside $\operatorname{ran}P_j$ change $\mathcal A_Q$ exactly as in Part II of the proof of Theorem M.6.13fh.

By (M.6.13dc.11) at $z=0$, $g_Z(\sigma)=\frac{s^2}2\sum_q\langle V_q,\mathcal S_q^{-1}V_q\rangle$ with $\mathcal S_q(T)=\alpha E_qT+yT\sigma_{q,q}$. The blocks $D$ and $V$ enter only the terms $q=r$ and $q=r\pm1$.

*Center $r$.* With $N=R_{r-1}\oplus R_{r+1}$, its inclusion $J_N$ into $R_r^c$ and $E_r=\sum_ao_aQ_a$, $o_a>0$, this term equals $\sum_j\operatorname{Tr}[G_c(\lambda_j)M_j]$ with
$$
G_c(\lambda)=\sum_a\frac{s^2}{2y}\,\frac{J_NQ_aJ_N^*}{\lambda+\alpha o_a/y},
$$
of total residue rank at most $\dim N$.

*Centers $q=r+\eta$, $\eta=\pm1$.* Let $\sigma_{q,q}=\sum_l\mu_le_le_l^*$ with $\mu_l>0$, let $F=R_{r+2\eta}$ (possibly zero), $W=\sigma_{r,r+2\eta}$, $B_F=\sigma_{r+2\eta,r+2\eta}$, $u_l=\sigma_{r,q}e_l$, $a_l=\sigma_{r+2\eta,q}e_l$, $A_l=\alpha D+y\mu_lI$ and $K_l=\alpha B_F+y\mu_lI$. In the order $(R_r,F)$ one has $E_q=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}D&W\\W^*&B_F\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, and the term equals $\frac{s^2}2\sum_l\left(\begin{smallmatrix}u_l\\a_l\end{smallmatrix}\right)^*\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A_l&\alpha W\\\alpha W^*&K_l\end{smallmatrix}\right)^{-1}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}u_l\\a_l\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Completing the square in the variational formula for the inverse of a positive definite block matrix gives
$$
\begin{pmatrix}u\\a\end{pmatrix}^*\begin{pmatrix}A&\alpha W\\\alpha W^*&K\end{pmatrix}^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}u\\a\end{pmatrix}
=\max_w\bigl\{(u-\alpha Ww)^*A^{-1}(u-\alpha Ww)+2\operatorname{Re}(a^*w)-w^*Kw\bigr\},
\tag{M.6.13fi.2}
$$
with a unique maximizer, because the negative Hessian $K-\alpha^2W^*A^{-1}W$ is a Schur complement of a positive definite matrix. Freeze the maximizer $w_l$ at $\sigma$. By the envelope theorem the first differential of the term in $(D,V)$ equals that of $\frac{s^2}2\sum_l(V\xi_l)^*(\alpha D+y\mu_lI)^{-1}(V\xi_l)$ with $\xi_l=J_qe_l-\alpha J_Fw_l\in R_r^c$ held fixed, since $u_l-\alpha Ww_l=V\xi_l$. This is the differential of $\sum_j\operatorname{Tr}[G_\eta(\lambda_j)M_j]$ with
$$
G_\eta(\lambda)=\sum_l\frac{s^2}{2\alpha}\,\frac{\xi_l\xi_l^*}{\lambda+y\mu_l/\alpha},
$$
of total residue rank at most $d_{r+\eta}$.

Put $G_r=G_c+G_++G_-$, held fixed, and $H_r=G_r-E$. The first differential of $\mathfrak F_Z$ at $\sigma$ along variations of $D$ and $V$ equals that of $\sum_j\operatorname{Tr}[G_r(\lambda_j)M_j]-\mathcal A_Q$, and $G_r$ is a sum of positive atoms $R_\ell/(\lambda+t_\ell)$ with $t_\ell>0$ and $\sum_\ell\operatorname{rank}R_\ell\le2(d_{r-1}+d_{r+1})$. Part II of the proof of Theorem M.6.13fh gives
$$
V_jH_r(\lambda_j)=0,\qquad V_jH_r'(\lambda_j)V_j^*=\mathfrak F_Z(\sigma)\,I_{\operatorname{ran}P_j},
$$
so $U_j=\operatorname{ran}V_j^*$ has dimension $r_j$, lies in $\ker H_r(\lambda_j)$ and carries a positive definite $H_r'(\lambda_j)$. The divided differences of $H_r$ have the form (M.6.13fh.8) with the positive kernel $\int_0^\infty S(t)^{-1}(\lambda+t)^{-1}(\mu+t)^{-1}dt$. Since $O\preceq I$, $E(\lambda)\succeq(\log\lambda/(\lambda-1))I$, while $G_r$ is bounded on $(0,\infty)$ and $O(1/\lambda)$ at infinity, so $H_r$ is negative definite near $0$ and near $\infty$. Lemma M.6.13fh.a gives $d_r=\sum_jr_j\le2(d_{r-1}+d_{r+1})$. If $d_{r-1}=d_{r+1}=0$, then $G_r=0$ and the lemma gives $d_r=0$, which proves the statement on neighbours. $\square$

Theorem M.6.13dd, Part I, reduces the unrestricted pressure to one connected integer charge ladder; on that ladder (M.6.13fi.1) constrains every faithful positive stationary state at every charge, including both ends.

<a id="theorem-m613fj"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613fj-scalar-toeplitz-surplus-bound-and-strict-separation-at-one-tester"></a>**Theorem M.6.13fj (Scalar Toeplitz Surplus Bound and Strict Separation at One Tester).** Retain $g_Z$ and $\mathfrak F_Z$ of Theorem M.6.13fh at the tester $Z_*=\frac5{16}|e\rangle\langle e|+\frac{11}{16}|m\rangle\langle m|$, so $s=1$, $\alpha=5/32$, and put $\nu=1-\alpha=27/32$.

1. For every real $t$,
$$
P(t)=\log\int_0^{2\pi}e^{2t\cos\theta-\alpha t^2\cos2\theta}\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}-\nu t^2<\frac{49}{2000}.
\tag{M.6.13fj.1}
$$
Equivalently, every even probability density $f$ on the circle with finite entropy, $a_f=\int f\cos\theta\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}$ and $b_f=\int f\cos2\theta\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}$ satisfies $a_f^2/(\alpha(1+b_f)+\frac{11}{16})-\int f\log f\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}<49/2000$.
2. Let $L\ge3$, let $T$ be a real symmetric positive semidefinite Toeplitz $L\times L$ matrix with unit diagonal, and let $\sigma=T/L$ be the ready state of the reference with charges $0,\ldots,L-1$ of multiplicity one. Then
$$
\mathfrak F_{Z_*}(\sigma)<\frac{49}{2000}+\frac7{8L}.
\tag{M.6.13fj.2}
$$
3. The faithful ready state on the scalar charges $0,1,2$
$$
\sigma_*=\begin{pmatrix}0.19&0.212&0.053\\0.212&0.62&0.212\\0.053&0.212&0.19\end{pmatrix}
\tag{M.6.13fj.3}
$$
has $g_{Z_*}(\sigma_*)=49741772/168975625$, $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma_*)=0.2676245328773694\ldots$ and $\mathfrak F_{Z_*}(\sigma_*)=0.0267479365246523\ldots$. Hence $1-b(Z_*)>0.0267$, while every ready state of item 2 with $L\ge500$ has $\mathfrak F_{Z_*}<0.02625$, and every even density of item 1 has value below $0.0245$.

*Proof.* *Item 1.* For an even density put $D_f=\alpha(1+b_f)+\frac{11}{16}\ge\frac{11}{16}$. Then $a_f^2/D_f=\max_\tau(2a_f\tau-D_f\tau^2)$, attained at $\tau=a_f/D_f$, $|\tau|\le16/11$. Exchanging the two suprema and using the Gibbs variational identity $\sup_f\{\int fh-\int f\log f\}=\log\int e^h$, whose maximizer $e^h/\int e^h$ is even when $h$ is even, gives
$$
\sup_f\Bigl\{\frac{a_f^2}{D_f}-\int f\log f\Bigr\}=\sup_{|\tau|\le16/11}P(\tau)=\sup_{\tau\in\mathbb R}P(\tau);
$$
the last equality holds because the Gibbs density at any $\tau$ has value at least $P(\tau)$, using $a^2/D\ge2a\tau-D\tau^2$. The shift $\theta\mapsto\theta+\pi$ gives $P(-t)=P(t)$, so it suffices to bound $P$ on $[0,3/2]$.

For $0\le t\le3/2$ the exponent $h_t(\theta)=2t\cos\theta-\frac5{32}t^2\cos2\theta$ satisfies $|h_t|\le3+\frac{45}{128}<4$. Since $e^4<55$, Taylor's theorem gives $e^{h_t}\le\sum_{k=0}^{32}h_t^k/k!+55\cdot4^{33}/33!$. The integrated polynomial $T_{32}(t)=\sum_{k=0}^{32}\int h_t^k/k!\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}$ has rational coefficients, obtained as constant Fourier coefficients of $h_t^k$ with $h_t=t(w+w^{-1})-\frac5{64}t^2(w^2+w^{-2})$, $w=e^{i\theta}$. Exact rational arithmetic at the $1501$ nodes $t_i=i/1000$, $0\le i\le1500$, gives
$$
T_{32}(t_i)+\frac{55\cdot4^{33}}{33!}<\sum_{j=0}^{24}\frac1{j!}\Bigl(\frac{22}{1000}+\frac{27}{32}t_i^2\Bigr)^j\le\exp\Bigl(\frac{22}{1000}+\frac{27}{32}t_i^2\Bigr),
\tag{M.6.13fj.4}
$$
with smallest margin $4.6\times10^{-4}$. Hence $P(t_i)<0.022$. The derivative $P'(t)=\langle2\cos\theta-2\alpha t\cos2\theta\rangle_t-2\nu t$, with $\langle\cdot\rangle_t$ the Gibbs mean, satisfies $|P'(t)|\le2+2t\le5$ on $[0,3/2]$, and every point of that interval lies within $1/2000$ of a node. Therefore $P<0.022+5/2000=49/2000$ on $[0,3/2]$, which proves (M.6.13fj.1).

*Item 2.* Write $a=T_{i,i+1}$, $b=T_{i,i+2}$ and $D=\alpha(1+b)+\frac{11}{16}=\nu+\alpha b$. Positivity of the leading $3\times3$ block gives $|b|\le1$ and $a^2\le(1+b)/2$. In (M.6.13dc.11) every center charge $1,\ldots,L-2$ has $E_q=\frac1L\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&b\\b&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, $V_q=\frac aL(1,1)^{\mathsf T}$, $\sigma_{q,q}=1/L$, and contributes $a^2/(LD)$; the end center charges $0$ and $L-1$ contribute $a^2/(2L\nu)$ each. Thus
$$
g_{Z_*}(\sigma)=\Bigl(1-\frac2L\Bigr)\frac{a^2}D+\frac{a^2}{L\nu}.
\tag{M.6.13fj.5}
$$
Since $\mathcal G_Q\sigma=I/L$, $\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)$ is the relative entropy of $\sigma$ to $I/L$, and the Gibbs variational inequality with $K=t(S+S^*)-\frac{\alpha t^2}2(S^2+S^{*2})$, $S$ the unilateral shift, gives
$$
\mathcal A_Q(\sigma)\ge\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma K)-\log\frac{\operatorname{Tr}e^K}L
=2ta\Bigl(1-\frac1L\Bigr)-\alpha t^2b\Bigl(1-\frac2L\Bigr)-\log\frac{\operatorname{Tr}e^K}L .
$$
$K$ is the compression of multiplication by $h_t$ on $L^2$ of the circle to the Fourier modes $0,\ldots,L-1$. For an orthonormal eigenbasis $v_i$ of $K$, convexity of the exponential gives $e^{\langle v_i,Kv_i\rangle}=e^{\langle v_i,h_tv_i\rangle}\le\langle v_i,e^{h_t}v_i\rangle$, hence $\operatorname{Tr}e^K\le L\int e^{h_t}\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}$. Choose $t=a/D$. Substituting into (M.6.13fj.5), the coefficient of $1/L$ is $a^2/\nu-2a^2/D+2ta-2\alpha t^2b=t^2(D^2/\nu-2\alpha b)=t^2(\nu+\alpha^2b^2/\nu)$, and
$$
\mathfrak F_{Z_*}(\sigma)\le P(t)+\frac{t^2}L\Bigl(\nu+\frac{\alpha^2b^2}\nu\Bigr).
\tag{M.6.13fj.6}
$$
With $u=(1+b)/2\in[0,1]$, $D=1-\frac5{16}(1-u)\ge\frac{1+u}2\ge\sqrt u\ge|a|$, so $|t|\le1$ and the coefficient is at most $\frac{27}{32}+\frac{25}{864}<\frac78$. Item 1 gives (M.6.13fj.2). Singular $T$ are included, since (M.6.13fj.5) uses only the unit diagonal and the Gibbs inequality holds for every ready state.

*Item 3.* The eigenvalues of $\sigma_*$ are $0.137$ and the two roots of the block $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0.243&0.212\sqrt2\\0.212\sqrt2&0.62\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, namely $0.0773527848\ldots$ and $0.7856472151\ldots$, so $\sigma_*$ is faithful. Formula (M.6.13fh.3) with $n=1$, $p=r=0.19$, $\omega=0.053$, $\lambda=0.62$ and $V=0.212\,(1,1)$ gives the rational value of $g_{Z_*}(\sigma_*)$. The asymmetry is $\sum_i\lambda_i\log\lambda_i-2(0.19\log0.19)-0.62\log0.62$, evaluated to forty digits. Thus $1-b(Z_*)\ge\mathfrak F_{Z_*}(\sigma_*)>0.0267$. For $L\ge500$, (M.6.13fj.2) gives $\mathfrak F_{Z_*}(\sigma)<0.0245+7/4000=0.02625$. $\square$

At $Z_*$ the three-charge state exceeds every real scalar Toeplitz ready state with at least five hundred charges by more than $4\times10^{-4}$ and every even scalar bulk density by more than $2\times10^{-3}$. Optimal references at this tester are therefore not approached by long real translation-invariant scalar chains.

<a id="theorem-m613fk"></a>

<a id="theorem-m613fk-bounded-charge-filters-and-whole-response-compression"></a>**Theorem M.6.13fk (Bounded Charge Filters and Whole-Response Compression).** Retain $g_Z$, $\mathfrak F_Z$, $s$ and $\alpha$ of Theorem M.6.13fh, the susceptibility $\Gamma(Z)$ of Theorem M.6.13fa at $z=0$, and let $A_L$ be the adjacency matrix of the path with $L$ vertices.

1. Suppose $\Gamma(Z)>1$. For every $N\ge1$ there are an even $L>N$, $0<\epsilon<1/2$, a faithful ready state $\sigma$ on the scalar charges $0,\ldots,L-1$ with $\mathfrak F_Z(\sigma)>0$, and $\gamma>0$ with the following property. For every diagonal $K$ with $K\sigma K^*\ne0$ whose normalized output $\sigma_K=K\sigma K^*/\operatorname{Tr}(K\sigma K^*)$ occupies at most $N$ charges, $\mathfrak F_Z(\sigma_K)\le\mathfrak F_Z(\sigma)-\gamma$, and the same holds for every mixture of such outputs with retained flags. At $Z_*$ of Theorem M.6.13fj one may take $L=12(N+1)^2$, $\epsilon=1/(1000(N+1)^2)$, $\sigma=(I+\epsilon A_L)/L$ and $\gamma=1/(5\cdot10^7(N+1)^6)$.
2. At $Z_*$, every uniform path state satisfies $\mathfrak F_{Z_*}((I+\epsilon A_L)/L)\le25/972<0.0258$ for all $L\ge1$ and $|\epsilon|\,\|A_L\|\le1$; this lies below $\mathfrak F_{Z_*}(\sigma_*)$ of (M.6.13fj.3).
3. For $n\ge4$ let $\sigma_n$ be the ready state on charges $0,1,2$ with multiplicities $1,n,1$ given, in the order of Theorem M.6.13fh, by $O=\frac14I_2$, $D=\operatorname{diag}(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ with $m_j=j/(n(n+1))$, and $V$ with columns $(\delta,\ldots,\delta)$ and $(\delta j/(n+1))_j$, $\delta=1/(100n^2)$. It is faithful. For $y=1$ and $x=2w$, $w>0$, the function $H_n(w)=2g_Z(\sigma_n)/(2w+1)^2$ is rational in $w$ with exactly $2n$ distinct simple poles. If a ready state $\sigma'$ on a finite reference of total dimension $D'$ satisfies $g_Z(\sigma')=g_Z(\sigma_n)$ for all $w$ in an open subinterval of $(0,\infty)$, then $D'\ge2\sqrt n$; if its reference has charges $0,1,2$ with multiplicities $1,d,1$, then $d\ge n/2$.

*Proof.* *Item 1.* For a probability vector $p$ on $L$ vertices and $0<\epsilon<1/2$ put $\sigma(p,\epsilon)=\Delta^{1/2}(I+\epsilon A_L)\Delta^{1/2}$, $\Delta=\operatorname{diag}(p)$, on the scalar charges $0,\ldots,L-1$. Its gap-two blocks vanish, so (M.6.13fb.3) at $z=0$ gives
$$
g_Z(\sigma(p,\epsilon))=\epsilon^2\sum_{i=1}^{L-1}\mathcal Q(p_i,p_{i+1}),\qquad
\mathcal Q(a,b)=\frac{s^2ab}2\Bigl(\frac1{\alpha a+yb}+\frac1{\alpha b+ya}\Bigr).
$$
Let $\mathcal E(a,b)=ab(\log a-\log b)/(a-b)$, with $\mathcal E(a,a)=a$ and $\mathcal E(a,0)=0$, and $\mathcal E_{\rm tot}=\sum_i\mathcal E(p_i,p_{i+1})$. With $Y=\Delta^{1/2}A_L\Delta^{1/2}$ one has $-2\Delta\preceq Y\preceq2\Delta$, and $\varphi(u)=\operatorname{Tr}(\Delta+uY)\log(\Delta+uY)$ has $\varphi'(0)=0$ and $\varphi''(u)=\int_0^\infty\operatorname{Tr}[YR_u(t)YR_u(t)]\,dt$, $R_u(t)=(\Delta+uY+tI)^{-1}$. For $0\le u\le\epsilon$, $(1+2\epsilon)^{-1}R_0\preceq R_u\preceq(1-2\epsilon)^{-1}R_0$, and $P\preceq P'$ implies $P^{\mathsf T}\otimes P\preceq P'^{\mathsf T}\otimes P'$, so $\varphi''(u)$ lies between $(1\pm2\epsilon)^{-2}\varphi''(0)=(1\pm2\epsilon)^{-2}\,2\mathcal E_{\rm tot}$. Integrating twice, and using $\mathcal E(a,b)\le\sqrt{ab}\le(a+b)/2$, so that $\mathcal E_{\rm tot}\le1$,
$$
\Bigl|\frac{\mathfrak F_Z(\sigma(p,\epsilon))}{\epsilon^2}-\sum_if(p_i,p_{i+1})\Bigr|\le\eta(\epsilon)=(1-2\epsilon)^{-2}-1,\qquad f=\mathcal Q-\mathcal E,
\tag{M.6.13fk.1}
$$
uniformly in $L$ and $p$, including vanishing populations.

The function $\chi(z)=2f(\frac{1+z}2,\frac{1-z}2)=(1-z^2)\bigl[\frac{s^2}{\alpha+y}(1-kz^2)^{-1}-\operatorname{artanh}(z)/z\bigr]$, $k=((y-\alpha)/(y+\alpha))^2$, is continuous on $[-1,1]$ with $\chi(\pm1)=0$, and $\chi(z)>0$ for some $z$ exactly when $\Gamma(Z)>1$, by (M.6.13fa.1). Put $\mathsf M=\max\chi>0$, attained at $z_*\in(-1,1)$. Homogeneity gives $f(a,b)\le\mathsf M(a+b)/2$. Let $H_N$ be the maximum of $\sum_if(p_i,p_{i+1})$ over probability vectors on at most $N$ vertices of a path. Then $H_N\le\mathsf M(1-(p_1+p_N)/2)$, and $H_N<\mathsf M$: equality would force $p_1=p_N=0$ and equality on every edge, while an edge with one zero and one positive population has $f=0<\mathsf M(a+b)/2$, so all populations would vanish. Put $d_N=\mathsf M-H_N>0$. On an even path with alternating populations $(1\pm z_*)/L$, every edge has $f=\mathsf M/L$, so $\sum_if=\mathsf M(1-1/L)$. Choose $L>N$ even with $\mathsf M/L<d_N/4$ and $\epsilon$ with $\eta(\epsilon)<d_N/4$; then $\mathfrak F_Z(\sigma)/\epsilon^2>\mathsf M-d_N/2>0$. A diagonal filter maps $\sigma(p,\epsilon)$ to $\sigma(p',\epsilon)$ with $p'_i\propto|K_{ii}|^2p_i$, up to a diagonal unitary that commutes with $Q_R$. Its occupied charges split into runs of at most $N$ consecutive charges, and by (M.6.13dc.4) $g_Z$, $\mathcal A_Q$ and $\mathfrak F_Z$ are the weighted averages over the runs and over retained flags. Each run obeys (M.6.13fk.1) with $\sum f\le H_N$, so $\mathfrak F_Z(\sigma_K)/\epsilon^2<\mathsf M-3d_N/4$, and $\gamma=\epsilon^2d_N/4$ works.

At $Z_*$, $s=1$, $r=\frac{s^2}{\alpha+y}-1=5/27$ and $\delta_*=4\alpha y/(\alpha+y)^2=440/729$. With $z=\tanh u$, $2f(a,b)/(a+b)=(r+1)/(1+\delta_*\sinh^2u)-2u/\sinh2u$ for $a/b=e^{2u}$. The coefficient comparison $1/(2j+1)!\le1/(3(2j)!)$ gives $\sinh v/v\le(\cosh v+2)/3$, hence
$$
r-\frac{2f(a,b)}{a+b}\ge\frac{z^2\bigl[(\tfrac{32}{27}\delta_*-\tfrac23)(1-z^2)+\tfrac23\delta_*rz^2\bigr]}{(1-(1-\delta_*)z^2)(1-z^2/3)}\ge\frac{z^2}{25},
$$
since $\frac{32}{27}\delta_*-\frac23=\frac{958}{19683}>\frac1{25}$ and $\frac23\delta_*r=\frac{4400}{59049}>\frac1{25}$. Thus $\mathsf M=r$, and $r(a+b)/2-f(a,b)\ge(a-b)^2/(50(a+b))\ge(\sqrt a-\sqrt b)^2/50$. For $w_i=\sqrt{p_i}$ on at most $N$ vertices, $r/2>1/50$ and the smallest eigenvalue $2(1-\cos\frac\pi{N+1})$ of the Dirichlet path Laplacian give
$$
r-\sum_if(p_i,p_{i+1})\ge\frac1{50}\Bigl[w_1^2+w_N^2+\sum_i(w_i-w_{i+1})^2\Bigr]\ge\frac{1-\cos\frac\pi{N+1}}{25}\ge\frac2{25(N+1)^2}=:d .
$$
For the uniform source, $\sum_if=r(1-1/L)$ with $r/L<1/(60(N+1)^2)<d/4$, and $\eta(\epsilon)<8\epsilon<d/4$. The loss is at least $\epsilon^2d/4=1/(5\cdot10^7(N+1)^6)$.

*Item 2.* For $|\epsilon|\,\|A_L\|<1$ the logarithm series and bipartiteness give $\mathcal A_Q=\frac1L\sum_{k\ge1}\epsilon^{2k}\operatorname{Tr}(A_L^{2k})/(2k(2k-1))$ with nonnegative terms. With $\operatorname{Tr}A_L^2=2(L-1)$, $\operatorname{Tr}A_L^4=6L-10$ for $L\ge2$, and $u=(1-1/L)\epsilon^2$, one gets $\mathcal A_Q\ge u+u^2/3$, because $(6L-10)/(12L)-(1-1/L)^2/3=(L-2)(L+1)/(6L^2)\ge0$. The gain is $(1+r)u$, by (M.6.13fj.5) for $L\ge3$ and by the same computation for $L=2$, so $\mathfrak F_{Z_*}\le ru-u^2/3\le3r^2/4=25/972$. The endpoint $|\epsilon|\,\|A_L\|=1$ follows by continuity, and $L=1$ gives zero.

*Item 3.* $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_n=1$ and $\|V^*D^{-1}V\|\le\operatorname{Tr}V^*D^{-1}V=\delta^2n(n+1)\sum_j(1+j^2/(n+1)^2)/j<2\delta^2n^2(n+1)\le1/16000<1/4$, so the Schur complement is positive definite. By (M.6.13fh.3) with $p=r=1/4$, $\omega=0$,
$$
H_n(w)=\sum_{j=1}^nc_j\Bigl(\frac1{wm_j+\frac14}+\frac1{\frac w4+m_j}\Bigr),\qquad c_j=\delta^2\Bigl(1+\frac{j^2}{(n+1)^2}\Bigr)>0 .
$$
Since $0<m_j<1/4$, the poles $-1/(4m_j)<-1$ and $-4m_j\in(-1,0)$ are $2n$ distinct points with positive residues. For any finite reference, (M.6.13dc.11) at $y=1$, $x=2w$ gives $2g_Z(\sigma')/(2w+1)^2=\sum_q\sum_{a,j}|\langle e_a|V_q|f_j\rangle|^2/(w\omega_a+\mu_j)$, with $\omega_a,\mu_j$ the eigenvalues of $E_q$ and $\sigma'_{q,q}$ after restriction to the support of $\mathcal G_Q\sigma'$, which leaves $g_Z$ unchanged. Its poles are among at most $\sum_q(d_{q-1}+d_{q+1})d_q=2\sum_td_td_{t+1}$ points. The charges differing by one form disjoint paths; coloring each path alternately gives $\sum_td_td_{t+1}\le D_0D_1\le D'^2/4$ with $D_0+D_1=D'$. Two rational functions equal on an open interval coincide, so $2n\le D'^2/2$. In the class with multiplicities $1,d,1$, (M.6.13fh.3) shows that each eigenvalue $\mu_j$ of the charge-one block contributes at most the four denominators $w\mu_j+p_0$, $w\mu_j+p_2$, $wo_1+\mu_j$, $wo_2+\mu_j$, so $2n\le4d$. $\square$

Items 1 and 3 exclude reductions that act on every ready state: a bounded set of charge sectors selected by diagonal filtering, and a bounded-dimensional model reproducing a ready state's gain at all testers. Reductions that act on optimizers at one tester, such as Theorem M.6.13fh, are compatible with both.

<a id="definition-m614a-finite-nd-rid-process-tensor"></a>**Definition M.6.14a (Finite ND-RID Process Tensor).** For a finite $n$-step ND-RID history with intervention times $0,\ldots,n$, let $\mathcal H_k^{\mathrm{in}}$ and $\mathcal H_k^{\mathrm{out}}$ be the retained input and output Hilbert spaces at step $k$. The process tensor is a positive Choi operator
$$
\Upsilon_{n:0}
\in
\mathcal B\left(
\bigotimes_{k=0}^{n}
\mathcal H_k^{\mathrm{out}}\otimes\mathcal H_k^{\mathrm{in}}
\right),
\qquad
\Upsilon_{n:0}\ge0,
\tag{M.6.14a.1}
$$
satisfying the causality constraints
$$
\operatorname{Tr}_{k^{\mathrm{out}}}\Upsilon_{k:0}
=
I_{k^{\mathrm{in}}}\otimes\Upsilon_{k-1:0}
\quad
(k=1,\ldots,n),
\tag{M.6.14a.2}
$$
with the explicit base normalization $\operatorname{Tr}_{0^{\mathrm{out}}}\Upsilon_{0:0}=I_{0^{\mathrm{in}}}$. Together with (M.6.14a.2), this excludes nonunit scalar multiples and fixes a deterministic comb. 

For a sequential tester outcome $\omega$, let $T_\omega\succeq0$ be the dual-comb Choi element obtained by linking the retained CP instrument outcomes to an explicitly normalized initial preparation, memory wiring, and terminal effect. All slotwise transposes dictated by the fixed Choi convention are included in $T_\omega$; it is not an arbitrary tensor product of CPTP Choi matrices. A family $\{T_\omega\}$ is complete exactly when $T_\Omega:=\sum_\omega T_\omega$ belongs to the normalized deterministic dual-tester cone,
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(\Upsilon T_\Omega)=1
\quad
\text{for every deterministic comb }\Upsilon\text{ satisfying Definition M.6.14a}.
$$
The generalized Born rule is then
$$
p(\omega)=\operatorname{Tr}(\Upsilon T_\omega),
\qquad
p(\omega)\ge0,
\qquad
\sum_\omega p(\omega)=1.
\tag{M.6.14a.3}
$$
This dual normalization is the missing boundary datum that prevents the raw channel--channel Choi contraction from being misread as a probability.

**Process-tensor compatibility for reflected modular records.** Whenever $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{Borch}}$ is invoked inside a perspectival branch, the reflection map is compared only against interventions contained in the already retained local past. The process-tensor record must show that replacing a branch by its reflected modular representative preserves the deterministic-control/no-future-to-past condition used elsewhere in this appendix. This prevents the reflected extension from being used as a hidden future-input channel.

<a id="theorem-m614b-nd-rid-histories-are-exactly-normalized-fixed-order-process-tensors"></a>**Theorem M.6.14b (ND-RID Histories are Exactly Normalized Fixed-Order Process Tensors).** Every finite ND-RID history built from an initial state, retained CPTP update kernels, conditional instruments, and finite environment memory defines a unique process tensor satisfying Definition M.6.14a. Conversely, every positive operator satisfying the recursive trace identities and base normalization of Definition M.6.14a, together with the normalized dual-tester pairing of (M.6.14a.3), defines a normalized fixed-order operational history on the retained instruments. Two histories are PPI-equivalent for the retained protocol family if and only if their process tensors give the same multilinear functional (M.6.14a.3) on that family.

*Proof.* Compose the initial state, the finite ND-RID update channels, and the retained memory systems into the multilinear map that sends a sequence of intervention CP maps to the final probability. Applying the Choi-Jamiolkowski isomorphism to every input-output slot gives a unique operator $\Upsilon_{n:0}$. Complete positivity of each update and instrument implies positivity of the Choi operator. Trace preservation of the future update after summing over an intervention gives exactly the recursive partial-trace constraints (M.6.14a.2). This proves that every finite ND-RID history gives a process tensor.

Conversely, positivity makes every positive tester outcome nonnegative. The recursive and base constraints place $\Upsilon$ in the deterministic-comb cone, while normalization of the dual tester makes its complete outcome sum equal to one. The comb trace identities preserve every earlier marginal when a later tester stage is summed out. The normalized dual tester supplies the terminal unit probability. Together they yield a valid fixed-order process with no future-to-past control. Therefore the operator defines a valid finite operational process.
