If two histories give the same process tensor on the retained instrument span, then (M.6.14a.3) gives the same probabilities for every retained finite protocol, so PPI identifies them. If they differ on some retained instrument sequence, the corresponding protocol distinguishes them and they are not PPI-equivalent. ∎

**Corollary M.6.14b.1 (Local Threshold Arming as a Process-Tensor Control).** Let $A_j$ be a finite classical arming or stopping register whose value is a registered function of classical data available in the branch's local past. These data may include retained records, ledger readings and a classically supplied model or estimate of the local reduced process tensor. A nonlinear function of an unknown quantum state or process is not an available control input merely because that state or process has a mathematical description. Adjoining this record-based control gives another causal process tensor satisfying Definition M.6.14a. If the conditional post-arming outcome kernel is unchanged, the Born weights of Theorem 28a are unchanged on that conditioned branch. On the local CPTP branch of Postulate 3(i), summing over all local control outcomes preserves remote unconditional marginals. Theorems 39 and 39a remain deterministic-endpoint and zero-error finite-window gates.

*Proof.* On a classical past-record basis, the map $r\mapsto(r,f(r))$ is an isometry and hence a CP, trace-preserving record extension. Controlled compositions of the registered local instruments are CP; summing their complete outcome family is trace preserving. Composing these instruments with the process tensor therefore preserves positivity and the partial-trace causality constraints. Local trace preservation leaves a remote unconditional marginal unchanged, whereas postselection on one control outcome need not do so. Equality of the conditional outcome kernel preserves its probabilities by definition. $\square$

**Remark M.6.14b.2 (No-Future-to-Past Condition for Metered Actualization).** A metered trigger uses only records available in the local past. Changing later complete trace-preserving choices leaves every earlier unconditional record marginal unchanged. It need not leave the full multi-time joint law unchanged, and conditioning on selected future outcomes is a distinct postselected experiment.

<a id="theorem-m614b3-sharp-single-copy-variance-control-obstruction"></a>**Theorem M.6.14b.3 (Sharp Single-Copy Variance-Control Obstruction).** Let $H$ be a Hermitian operator on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, with two normalized eigenvectors of distinct eigenvalues $E_0,E_1$. Set $\Delta=|E_1-E_0|>0$, $\rho_i=|E_i\rangle\langle E_i|$, and $\rho_m=(\rho_0+\rho_1)/2$. An experiment receives one unknown input state $\rho$, uses a fixed apparatus initially independent of that input, and applies a finite normalized quantum instrument, possibly with adaptive choices based on its own earlier records. For any registered terminal event, its probability has the form
$$
p(\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}(F\rho),\qquad 0\le F\le I.
\tag{M.6.14b.3.1}
$$
Write $\sigma_H(\rho)=\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}(\rho H^2)-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho H)^2}$. For any proposed target probability $b(\sigma_H(\rho))\in[0,1]$, put $u=b(0)$ and $v=b(\Delta/2)$. Then
$$
\inf_{0\le F\le I}\ \max_{\rho\in\{\rho_0,\rho_1,\rho_m\}}
\big|\operatorname{Tr}(F\rho)-b(\sigma_H(\rho))\big|
=\frac{|v-u|}{2}.
\tag{M.6.14b.3.2}
$$
In particular, a deterministic target event $\mathbf1\{t\sigma_H(\rho)/\hbar\ge\theta\}$, with $\theta>0$ and finite $t\ge2\hbar\theta/\Delta$, has unavoidable uniform error $1/2$ on these three states.

*Proof.* Composition and outcome coarse-graining of complete instruments give a trace-nonincreasing CP map for the event. Applying its adjoint to the identity gives the effect $F$; independent fixed ancillas are absorbed into this effect. Adaptation merely selects the CP maps on each retained record branch before summing the event branches, so the same affine expression holds. The endpoint variances vanish and the midpoint variance is $\Delta^2/4$. If all three probability errors are at most $\epsilon$, affinity gives
$$
|v-u|\le |v-p(\rho_m)|
+\frac{|p(\rho_0)-u|+|p(\rho_1)-u|}{2}
\le2\epsilon.
$$
The constant effect $F=(u+v)I/2$ attains the lower bound. The threshold example has $u=0,v=1$. ∎

<a id="theorem-m614b4-finite-two-copy-energy-variance-meter"></a>**Theorem M.6.14b.4 (Finite Two-Copy Energy-Variance Meter).** Let $H$ be a self-adjoint operator on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space with spectral width $\Delta=E_{\max}-E_{\min}>0$. Suppose a registered preparation supplies $2M$ independent copies of the same state $\rho$, with $M\ge1$, and the local apparatus implements the complete spectral measurement of $H$. Measure each copy and retain all energy outcomes. Pair the outcomes as $(E_{j,1},E_{j,2})$ and define
$$
Z_j=\frac{(E_{j,1}-E_{j,2})^2}{2},
\qquad
\widehat v_M=\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M Z_j,
\qquad v=\operatorname{Var}_\rho H.
\tag{M.6.14b.4.1}
$$
Then the measurement is a finite normalized instrument, $\mathbb E\widehat v_M=v$, and, for every $\epsilon>0$,
$$
\Pr\{|\widehat v_M-v|\ge\epsilon\}
\le2\exp\!\left(-\frac{8M\epsilon^2}{\Delta^4}\right).
\tag{M.6.14b.4.2}
$$
On the event $|\widehat v_M-v|\le\epsilon$,
$$
\sqrt{\max(0,\widehat v_M-\epsilon)}
\le\sigma_H(\rho)\le\sqrt{\widehat v_M+\epsilon},
\qquad
|\sqrt{\widehat v_M}-\sigma_H(\rho)|\le\sqrt\epsilon.
\tag{M.6.14b.4.3}
$$
If a separately specified stationary clock has rate $\sigma_H(\rho)/\hbar$ and threshold $\theta>0$, its declared hitting time $\tau=\hbar\theta/\sigma_H(\rho)$ obeys the corresponding interval
$$
\frac{\hbar\theta}{\sqrt{\widehat v_M+\epsilon}}
\le\tau\le
\frac{\hbar\theta}{\sqrt{\max(0,\widehat v_M-\epsilon)}}.
\tag{M.6.14b.4.4}
$$
A zero denominator on the upper side means $+\infty$; $v=0$ gives $\tau=+\infty$. The interval is a confidence statement under the independent preparation law. Any later arming rule formed from the retained outcomes is a local past-record control of Corollary M.6.14b.1.

*Proof.* Independence of the two copies gives
$$
\mathbb E Z_j=\frac12(2\mathbb E E^2-2(\mathbb E E)^2)=v,
\qquad 0\le Z_j\le L:=\Delta^2/2.
$$
For a random variable $Z\in[0,L]$, let $K(t)=\ln\mathbb E e^{t(Z-\mathbb EZ)}$. Its second derivative is the variance under the exponentially tilted law. That law still has support in $[0,L]$, so its variance is at most $L^2/4$: subtracting the midpoint shows $\operatorname{Var}Z\le\mathbb E(Z-L/2)^2\le L^2/4$. Since $K(0)=K'(0)=0$, twice integrating gives $K(t)\le t^2L^2/8$ for every real $t$. Independence, the exponential Markov inequality and minimization over $t>0$ give an upper tail at most $\exp(-2M\epsilon^2/L^2)$. Apply the same argument to the lower tail and add the bounds to obtain (M.6.14b.4.2). Taking square roots of the nonnegative variance interval proves the first part of (M.6.14b.4.3). The inequality $|\sqrt a-\sqrt b|\le\sqrt{|a-b|}$ for $a,b\ge0$ proves its second part. Inversion gives (M.6.14b.4.4), with the stated extended-real convention. Completeness of the spectral projectors makes each measurement trace preserving after all outcomes are summed. The product preparation, product instruments and classical record computation therefore form a normalized fixed-order history. Subsequent arming takes place after the measurement records exist and satisfies the local-past condition. ∎

The two-copy meter replaces an unavailable nonlinear single-copy control input by explicit preparation, measurement and retained-record resources. Its uncertainty, preparation stationarity, energy observable and any clock threshold are registered separately. A classical model supplying the exact variance is another allowed input under Corollary M.6.14b.1 and is outside the unknown-input obstruction of Theorem M.6.14b.3.

<a id="corollary-m614c-markov-memory-and-indefinite-order-gates"></a>**Corollary M.6.14c (Markov, Memory, and Indefinite-Order Gates).** On the finite process-tensor branch:

1. Markovian multi-time dynamics is the tensor-factorization condition for $\Upsilon_{n:0}$ into one-step conditional channels;

2. failure of this factorization witnesses non-Markovian temporal correlations. A finite-memory realization additionally requires a finite ancillary-memory dilation certificate, while all fixed-order comb constraints remain satisfied;

3. coherent or classical control of internal operations within Definition M.6.14a remains a fixed external-order comb. A genuinely indefinite-order resource is outside this definition and requires a separately normalized process-matrix or higher-order-map branch with its own probability and no-loop certificate.

Items 1--2 remain normalized fixed-order histories and obey the same partial-trace comb constraints. Item 3 is a scope boundary, not an existence claim for an indefinite-order PU sector.

*Proof.* One-step Markov dynamics with no retained environment memory has a Choi representation given by the link product of adjacent conditional channels. Conversely, that factorization makes the future conditionally independent of the earlier past given the present slot. Failure of the factorization witnesses non-Markovian temporal correlation; a finite-memory realization additionally requires a finite ancillary dilation. Equation (M.6.14a.2) selects one external order, so every process satisfying it remains an externally ordered comb. A genuinely indefinite-order process belongs to a distinct process-matrix or higher-order-map normalization cone and is not asserted to satisfy (M.6.14a.2). ∎

<a id="theorem-m614c1-temporal-operator-schmidt-memory-bound"></a>**Theorem M.6.14c.1 (Temporal Operator-Schmidt Memory Bound).** Let $\Upsilon_{n:0}$ be a finite normalized process tensor and cut its Choi slots into a temporal past $P$ and future $F$. Let
$$
R_j
=
\operatorname{OSR}_{P|F}(\Upsilon_{n:0})
\tag{M.6.14c.1.1}
$$
be the minimum number of product operators in a decomposition across cut $j$. If every carrier of influence across that cut, including the through-going system when it crosses the cut, classical shared variables, and pre-correlated ancillas, is contained in one complete memory system $M_j$ of Hilbert dimension $d_{M_j}$, then
$$
R_j\le d_{M_j}^2,
\qquad
d_{M_j}\ge\left\lceil\sqrt{R_j}\right\rceil.
\tag{M.6.14c.1.2}
$$
Defining $d_M:=\max_j d_{M_j}$, every exact realization obeys
$$
d_M\ge
\max_j\left\lceil\sqrt{R_j}\right\rceil.
\tag{M.6.14c.1.3}
$$

*Proof.* All dependence crossing cut $j$ factors through $\mathcal B(M_j)$. Expanding that carrier in an operator basis $\{E_a\}_{a=1}^{d_{M_j}^2}$ writes the Choi operator as $\sum_aX_a^P\otimes Y_a^F$, so its operator-Schmidt rank is at most $d_{M_j}^2$. Rearrangement gives the lower bounds. ∎

<a id="remark-m614c1a-lower-bound-scope"></a>**Remark M.6.14c.1a (Lower-Bound Scope).** Equation (M.6.14c.1.2) is not an achievability equality. Positivity, comb normalization, and classical nonnegative-factorization constraints may require larger memory. Omitting the through-going system, a classical seed, or a pre-correlated environment from $M_j$ invalidates the premise rather than evading the bound.

<a id="theorem-m614c2-affine-channel-determinant-and-rank-revival-witness"></a>**Theorem M.6.14c.2 (Affine-Channel Determinant and Rank-Revival Witness).** Represent a finite-dimensional trace-preserving channel on the real affine space of density operators as
$$
x\longmapsto A_tx+b_t
\tag{M.6.14c.2.1}
$$
on traceless Hermitian coordinates reconstructed in one time-independent calibrated affine chart. Suppose $\Lambda_t=V_{t,s}\Lambda_s$ for $t\ge s$, where every $V_{t,s}$ is positive and trace preserving. Then
$$
|\det A_t|\le|\det A_s|,
\qquad
\operatorname{rank}A_t\le\operatorname{rank}A_s.
\tag{M.6.14c.2.2}
$$
Consequently an increase of $|\det A_t|$, revival after a rank loss, or a negative determinant reached continuously from $A_0=I$ witnesses failure of positive divisibility and therefore of CP divisibility, provided the change exceeds the registered tomography interval. Time-dependent coordinate changes are not admissible witnesses. On an absolutely continuous invertible branch with $A_0=I$ and bounded integrable traceless-coordinate generator $L_t$ defined by $\dot A_t=L_tA_t$,
$$
\det A_t
=
\exp\!\left(\int_0^t\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbb R}L_s\,ds\right)>0.
\tag{M.6.14c.2.3}
$$
None of the converse statements holds: nonnegative monotone determinant does not certify Markovianity, and determinant zero is inconclusive without the invertible-generator premise.

*Proof.* Positivity and trace preservation contract trace distance on Hermitian differences, so every eigenvalue of the induced traceless-space propagator has modulus at most one and $|\det A_{t,s}|\le1$. From $A_t=A_{t,s}A_s$, determinant multiplicativity and rank monotonicity prove (M.6.14c.2.2). A continuous determinant starting at $1$ cannot become negative without passing through zero; divisibility then forbids the required rank revival. Equation (M.6.14c.2.3) is Liouville's determinant formula for the fundamental solution of $\dot A_t=L_tA_t$. ∎

<a id="theorem-m614c3-minimal-operator-bond-dimension-and-exact-memory-of-identity-and-dephasing-transmission"></a>**Theorem M.6.14c.3 (Minimal Operator Bond Dimension and Exact Memory of Identity and Dephasing Transmission).** Let $\mathcal S_k=\mathcal B(\mathcal H_k^{\mathrm{out}}\otimes\mathcal H_k^{\mathrm{in}})$ denote the operator space of slot $k$ of Definition M.6.14a.

1. For every finite normalized process tensor, an operator matrix-product representation
$$
\Upsilon_{n:0}=\sum_{\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{n-1}}A^{(0)}_{\alpha_0}\otimes A^{(1)}_{\alpha_0\alpha_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes A^{(n)}_{\alpha_{n-1}},
\qquad A^{(k)}_{\cdots}\in\mathcal S_k,
\tag{M.6.14c.3.1}
$$
whose bond index $\alpha_j$ takes $D_j$ values has $D_j\ge R_j$ at the cut between slots $j$ and $j+1$, and one representation has $D_j=R_j$ at every cut simultaneously. When the retained tester span is the full operator space of the slots, Theorem M.6.14b makes $\Upsilon_{n:0}$ the only member of its PPI class, so the numbers $R_j$ are the minimal bond dimensions over that class.
2. Let the only carrier across a cut be a $d$-dimensional system that a channel $\mathcal C$ transmits from slot $0$ to slot $1$, so that the process tensor is the Choi operator of $\mathcal C$ in the fixed convention. Call $m$ an exact memory dimension when $\mathcal C=\mathcal D\circ\mathcal E$ for CPTP maps $\mathcal E:\mathcal B(\mathbb C^d)\to\mathcal B(\mathbb C^m)$ and $\mathcal D:\mathcal B(\mathbb C^m)\to\mathcal B(\mathbb C^d)$, as in the premise of Theorem M.6.14c.1. For the coherent identity $\mathcal C=\mathrm{id}_d$, $R=d^2$ and the least exact memory dimension is $d=\lceil\sqrt R\rceil$. For the complete dephasing channel $\Delta_d(\rho)=\sum_i\langle i|\rho|i\rangle\,|i\rangle\langle i|$, $R=d$ and the least exact memory dimension is $d$, which exceeds $\lceil\sqrt R\rceil=\lceil\sqrt d\rceil$ for every $d\ge3$.
3. The least exact memory dimension is not a function of the operator-Schmidt rank: $\mathrm{id}_2$ and $\Delta_4$ both have $R=4$, with least exact memory dimensions $2$ and $4$.

*Proof.* Grouping (M.6.14c.3.1) at the cut $j$ writes $\Upsilon_{n:0}$ as a sum of $D_j$ product operators across that cut, so $R_j\le D_j$. For the converse, let $\mathcal P_j\subseteq\mathcal S_0\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal S_j$ be the span of the partial contractions $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\varphi)(\Upsilon_{n:0})$ over linear functionals $\varphi$ on $\mathcal S_{j+1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal S_n$; its dimension is the rank of the unfolding, $R_j$, and $\mathcal P_n=\operatorname{span}\{\Upsilon_{n:0}\}$. For $X=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\varphi)(\Upsilon_{n:0})$ and a functional $\psi$ on $\mathcal S_j$, $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\psi)(X)=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\psi\otimes\varphi)(\Upsilon_{n:0})\in\mathcal P_{j-1}$, so every slot-$j$ slice of an element of $\mathcal P_j$ lies in $\mathcal P_{j-1}$ and $\mathcal P_j\subseteq\mathcal P_{j-1}\otimes\mathcal S_j$. Expanding each vector of a basis of $\mathcal P_j$ in a basis of $\mathcal P_{j-1}$ tensored with $\mathcal S_j$, starting from $\Upsilon_{n:0}\in\mathcal P_n$, produces (M.6.14c.3.1) with $D_j=R_j$ for every $j$. With a full retained tester span, equality of the functional (M.6.14a.3) on that span forces equality of the operators, so the PPI class is a singleton.

For item 2, the Choi operator of $\mathrm{id}_d$ is $\sum_{i,j}|i\rangle\langle j|\otimes|i\rangle\langle j|$ up to the fixed transposes, which preserve operator-Schmidt rank; the $d^2$ operators $|i\rangle\langle j|$ are linearly independent, so $R=d^2$. The Choi operator of $\Delta_d$ is $\sum_i|i\rangle\langle i|\otimes|i\rangle\langle i|$, so $R=d$. Memory $d$ suffices in both cases with $\mathcal E=\mathrm{id}_d$ and $\mathcal D=\mathcal C$. If $\mathrm{id}_d=\mathcal D\circ\mathcal E$, then $\mathcal E$ is injective on $\mathcal B(\mathbb C^d)$ and $d^2\le m^2$. If $\Delta_d=\mathcal D\circ\mathcal E$, then for $i\ne j$ trace-norm contraction under $\mathcal D$ gives $\|\mathcal E(|i\rangle\langle i|)-\mathcal E(|j\rangle\langle j|)\|_1\ge2$; two states at trace distance $2$ have orthogonal supports, so $\mathbb C^m$ contains $d$ mutually orthogonal nonzero subspaces and $m\ge d$. Finally $\lceil\sqrt d\rceil<d$ for $d\ge3$. Item 3 is item 2 with $d=2$ for the identity and $d=4$ for dephasing. ∎

<a id="proposition-m614c4-process-matrix-extensions-of-a-preparation-or-terminal-slot"></a>**Proposition M.6.14c.4 (Process-Matrix Extensions of a Preparation or Terminal Slot).** Let two parties $A,B$ have input and output spaces $A_I,A_O,B_I,B_O$. A normalized process-matrix extension is an operator $W\ge0$ on $A_I\otimes A_O\otimes B_I\otimes B_O$ with $\operatorname{Tr}[W(M_A\otimes M_B)]=1$ for every pair of Choi operators of CPTP maps $A_I\to A_O$ and $B_I\to B_O$ in the fixed convention, so that $\operatorname{Tr}_{A_O}M_A=I_{A_I}$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{B_O}M_B=I_{B_I}$.

1. If $\dim A_I=1$, the normalized extensions are exactly $W=J\otimes I_{B_O}$ with $J\ge0$ on $A_O\otimes B_I$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{B_I}J=I_{A_O}$: the fixed-order combs with $A$ before $B$.
2. If $\dim A_O=1$, they are exactly the operators $W\ge0$ on $A_I\otimes B_I\otimes B_O$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_{A_I}W=\rho_{B_I}\otimes I_{B_O}$ for a state $\rho_{B_I}$: the fixed-order combs with $B$ before $A$.

Consequently, whenever one party has a one-dimensional input or output space, every normalized process-matrix extension of the two slots is a fixed-order comb of Definition M.6.14a, and the extension class contains no indefinite-order process. The same statements hold with $A$ and $B$ exchanged.

*Proof.* A Hermitian $X$ on $B_I\otimes B_O$ satisfies $\operatorname{Tr}(XM)=1$ for every CPTP Choi operator $M$ exactly when $X=Y\otimes I_{B_O}$ with $\operatorname{Tr}Y=1$. Indeed, the Choi operator $I_{B_I}\otimes I_{B_O}/\dim B_O$ of the completely depolarizing map is positive definite, so CPTP Choi operators fill a relative neighborhood of it in the affine space $\{M=M^*:\operatorname{Tr}_{B_O}M=I_{B_I}\}$ and affinely span it. Hence $\operatorname{Tr}(X\Delta)=0$ for every Hermitian $\Delta$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_{B_O}\Delta=0$, which places $X$ in the range $\{Y\otimes I_{B_O}\}$ of the adjoint of $\operatorname{Tr}_{B_O}$, and then $\operatorname{Tr}(XM)=\operatorname{Tr}(Y\operatorname{Tr}_{B_O}M)=\operatorname{Tr}Y$.

For item 1, $M_A$ ranges over all states $\sigma$ on $A_O$. Each $X_\sigma:=\operatorname{Tr}_{A_O}[W(\sigma\otimes I)]$ is Hermitian and satisfies the displayed criterion, so $X_\sigma=Y_\sigma\otimes I_{B_O}$. The map $\sigma\mapsto X_\sigma$ is linear and states span the Hermitian operators on $A_O$, so every slice of $W$ along $A_O$ has this form and $W=J\otimes I_{B_O}$. Then $\operatorname{Tr}[W(\sigma\otimes M_B)]=\operatorname{Tr}[J(\sigma\otimes I_{B_I})]=\operatorname{Tr}[(\operatorname{Tr}_{B_I}J)\sigma]$, which equals one for every state exactly when $\operatorname{Tr}_{B_I}J=I_{A_O}$, and $W\ge0$ exactly when $J\ge0$. For item 2, the only CPTP map $A_I\to\mathbb C$ is the trace, whose Choi operator is $I_{A_I}$, so the condition reads $\operatorname{Tr}[(\operatorname{Tr}_{A_I}W)M_B]=1$ for every $M_B$. The criterion gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{A_I}W=\rho_{B_I}\otimes I_{B_O}$ with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho_{B_I}=1$, and $\rho_{B_I}\ge0$ because $\operatorname{Tr}_{A_I}W\ge0$. In both items the displayed trace identities are the base normalization and recursion (M.6.14a.2) of the corresponding two-tooth comb. Exchanging the party labels proves the final sentence. ∎

**Memory and extension scope.** Operator bond dimensions describe tensor factorizations, while transmitted quantum or classical information determines physical crossing memory. The finite normalized combs include coherent identity and dephasing transmission in every dimension; their least exact crossing memory is that dimension. Preparation-slot and terminal-slot extensions obey the fixed-order classification. Theorems M.6.14c.5–M.6.14c.6 below supply the general peak-memory minimum and full nontrivial two-slot classification.

<a id="theorem-m614c5-exact-peak-memory-of-every-finite-comb"></a>**Theorem M.6.14c.5 (Exact Peak Memory of Every Finite Comb).** Fix the finite external ports $X_k=\mathcal H_k^{\mathrm{in}}$, $Y_k=\mathcal H_k^{\mathrm{out}}$, $k=0,\ldots,n$, of Definition M.6.14a, with dimensions $a_k,b_k$. Fix their temporal cuts and source/tester ownership. At cut $j$, the complete source memory $M_j$ contains every source-owned carrier of influence crossing that cut: a through-going system, carried classical record or shared random seed, and any precorrelated or later-reused ancilla. An independently owned tester wire stays in the normalized dual tester. No source wire is reassigned to that tester during minimization.

Every retained source-instrument outcome is assigned to a crossing classical factor or a declared output before minimization. Unobserved Kraus indices in a permanently isolated local environment are not treated as readable outcomes. An admissible complete-leg realization consists of CPTP maps
$$
\mathcal C_k:\mathcal B(X_k\otimes M_{k-1})
\longrightarrow\mathcal B(Y_k\otimes M_k),\qquad
m_{-1}=m_n=1,\qquad m_j=\dim M_j,
\tag{M.6.14c.5.1}
$$
with the source's fixed external port order. Fresh local environments are allowed within a tooth. Any discarded factor is outside future memory only when no later admitted source coupling or readout accesses it; its preparation and hardware remain resources. A record released as an output has that explicit output role. The optimized scalar is the original peak complete-memory dimension $d_M=\max_{j<n}m_j$, with the trivial no-cut value one. Additional restrictions requiring a particular accessible subsystem, prescribed tensor factor or microscopic coupling are separate constrained problems; they cannot be removed by changing this port convention.

Let $\Upsilon=\Upsilon_{n:0}$ be any finite normalized comb, with causal prefixes $\Upsilon_{j:0}$. The following construction gives its exact minimum, a finite attaining realization and an all-real classification.

1. **Explicit finite factorization test.** For a specified capacity profile $\mathbf m=(m_0,\ldots,m_{n-1})$, introduce one Hermitian Choi matrix $C_k$ of size
$$
\ell_k=(b_km_k)(a_km_{k-1}),\qquad
C_k\succeq0,\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}_{Y_kM_k}C_k=I_{X_kM_{k-1}}.
\tag{M.6.14c.5.2}
$$
Its coordinate convention is
$$
[C_k]^{y\alpha,y'\beta}_{x\gamma,x'\delta}
=\langle y\alpha|\mathcal C_k(|x\gamma\rangle\langle x'\delta|)|y'\beta\rangle,
\tag{M.6.14c.5.3}
$$
with output and memory indices before input and memory indices. Impose, for every external matrix element,
$$
\Upsilon_{\mathbf y,\mathbf x;\mathbf y',\mathbf x'}
=\sum_{\alpha_0,\beta_0,\ldots,\alpha_{n-1},\beta_{n-1}}
\prod_{k=0}^n
[C_k]^{y_k\alpha_k,y'_k\beta_k}_{x_k\alpha_{k-1},x'_k\beta_{k-1}},
\tag{M.6.14c.5.4}
$$
where the two boundary memory indices have their unique value. This is the component form of the Choi link product in the fixed slot order; its contractions already include the required index convention.

Write a Hermitian matrix with real diagonal entries and real/imaginary parts above the diagonal. Positive semidefiniteness is exactly the nonnegativity of all its principal minors. Equations (2)--(4) therefore define a finite polynomial feasibility formula $\mathsf F_{\mathbf m}(\Upsilon)$ with $\sum_k\ell_k^2$ real channel variables, explicit linear trace equations, finite polynomial inequalities and composition equations of degree at most $n+1$ in those variables. It is true exactly when the comb has an implementation with those capacities. It tests one common channel sequence; separately feasible cut minima are not substituted for a jointly feasible profile.

2. **A simultaneous finite upper bound and attainment.** Put
$$
r_j=\operatorname{rank}\Upsilon_{j:0},\qquad
U=\max\left(1,\max_{j<n}r_j\right),\qquad
U_{\mathrm{dim}}=\max\left(1,\max_{j<n}\prod_{k=0}^j a_kb_k\right).
\tag{M.6.14c.5.5}
$$
Then
$$
1\le d_{\min}(\Upsilon)\le U\le U_{\mathrm{dim}},\qquad
d_{\min}(\Upsilon)=\min\{m\in\{1,\ldots,U\}:\mathsf F_{(m,\ldots,m)}(\Upsilon)\}.
\tag{M.6.14c.5.6}
$$
The upper bound is the dimension of the complete internal source-memory leg in a sequential isometric construction, not an environment-only count that omits a source system. The prefix-rank construction is an upper bound for this CPTP optimization, rather than a general equality.

For each fixed profile the feasible channel set is compact. The optimum in (6) is attained by an actual channel sequence. For fixed port dimensions, real quantifier elimination produces finite quantifier-free formulas $\Phi_m(\Upsilon)$ equivalent to $\mathsf F_{(m,\ldots,m)}$ for every $1\le m\le U_{\mathrm{dim}}$. With $\Phi_0$ false, the exact all-real strata are
$$
\{\Upsilon:d_{\min}(\Upsilon)=m\}
=\{\Upsilon:\Phi_m(\Upsilon)\ \wedge\ \neg\Phi_{m-1}(\Upsilon)\}
\tag{M.6.14c.5.7}
$$
inside the normalized comb cone. Thus every finite real comb is classified by a finite semialgebraic condition. A lexicographic minimum of the real channel coefficients in each nonempty compact fiber supplies a total semialgebraic choice of an attaining realization.

For coefficients supplied as real algebraic numbers with defining polynomials and isolating data, the following is a terminating exact algorithm: compute a bound in (5); generate (2)--(4) for $m=1,\ldots,U$ in order; use exact real-algebraic decision until the first feasible case; extract an algebraic sample point in that fiber; and recover the channels and their finite Kraus dilations. The decision and sample-point routines are the effective real-closed-field algorithms of Basu, Pollack and Roy [2006, Chapters 13--14]. This is an exact bounded search, with both positive witnesses and rejected lower capacities, not a conclusion from a failed numerical optimization. The all-real statement (7) is mathematical; approximation-only descriptions of arbitrary real coefficients do not thereby gain a Turing procedure for exact equality. No efficiency bound is asserted.

The formula (2)--(4) also decides every specified finite profile. Enumerating profiles with $1\le m_j\le d_{\min}$ gives all peak-optimal profiles. It does not claim that this box contains every Pareto-minimal profile for other objectives.

3. **Full protocol and quotient preservation.** Every feasible channel tuple reproduces the complete operator $\Upsilon$, so it reproduces $\operatorname{Tr}(\Upsilon T_\omega)$ for every normalized dual tester of Definition M.6.14a, including retained outcomes, spectator systems, causal classical controls and future marginalization. This pairing is the linked dual-tester pairing; raw channel--channel contraction is not substituted for it.

If the declared retained tester span has a supplied finite basis $T_1,\ldots,T_q$, replace (4) by
$$
\operatorname{Tr}[(\Upsilon(C)-\Upsilon)T_l]=0,
\qquad l=1,\ldots,q.
\tag{M.6.14c.5.8}
$$
The same bounded construction gives the exact minimum over that PPI response class. The original $\Upsilon$ provides the upper bound even if another equivalent representative has lower memory. The all-real semialgebraic statement includes the tester coefficients as parameters; an effective algorithm additionally requires their exact input representation. Unitary changes of port or memory bases preserve the feasible capacities and the optimum. A chosen lexicographic representative can depend on that basis. Composing two optimal representatives preserves their operational response but is not asserted to preserve optimality.

Classical records are counted as orthogonal states: a $q_j$-dimensional quantum memory together with a $c_j$-valued carried classical record has dimension $q_jc_j$, or $\sum_c\dim Q_{j,c}$ for a direct-sum realization. A random seed shared between teeth belongs to the same count. This differs from optimization with free classical assistance.

4. **Explicit finite examples.** Identity and dephasing transmission from Theorem M.6.14c.3 are represented by two teeth $d\to1$ and $1\to d$. Their first prefix is $I_d$, so the complete transmitted carrier has prefix rank $d$ and its original exact memory $d$ is counted. In contrast, a tensor product of independently depolarizing teeth has memory one even when its first prefix has full Choi rank; intermediate local discards can strictly improve the isometric upper bound.

A nontrivial three-tooth example has qubit input and output at every tooth and memory two at both cuts. Its maps are
$$
\begin{aligned}
V_0|x\rangle&=|0\rangle_{Y_0}|x\rangle_{M_0},\\
V_1(|x\rangle_{X_1}|m\rangle_{M_0})
&=|m\rangle_{Y_1}|x\rangle_{M_1},\\
\mathcal C_2(X)&=\operatorname{Tr}_{X_2}X
\quad\text{with }M_1\text{ relabeled as }Y_2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.14c.5.9}
$$
In grouped labels its Choi operator is
$$
\Upsilon=
|0\rangle\langle0|_{Y_0}\otimes
|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|_{Y_1X_0}\otimes
|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|_{Y_2X_1}\otimes I_{X_2},
\qquad |\Omega\rangle=|00\rangle+|11\rangle,
\tag{M.6.14c.5.10}
$$
permuted into the registered tooth order. Both prefix ranks are two and both temporal operator-Schmidt ranks are four. Theorem M.6.14c.1 and (9) therefore give the exact peak minimum two.

*Proof.* Consolidate the physical operations between adjacent registered cuts into one channel. Every future-accessible source record or system is an input/output memory factor of that channel. Fresh local environments are absorbed into the CPTP map; an environment subsequently used is included in its output memory instead. The Choi theorem then gives (2)--(3). Evaluating the linked channels on every external matrix unit and summing the paired internal memory indices gives (4), proving necessity. Conversely, positive matrices with the displayed partial traces define CPTP maps on exactly those finite factors. Joining them realizes the component contraction (4). Equality on all matrix units proves equality of the process operator and hence every correctly normalized tester response, proving sufficiency.

To enlarge a capacity, embed its used subspace isometrically. On the larger input memory, first project onto that subspace or its orthogonal complement. Apply the original channel on the first block and send the complement to a fixed normalized output; sum both outcomes and embed the used output. This is a CPTP extension. It kills off-diagonal input blocks outside the used support, and the actual source always remains in the embedded used support. Padding therefore preserves feasibility and proves monotonicity in every capacity, including the uniform capacity in (6).

For the upper bound, choose a minimal purification $|\psi_j\rangle$ of each positive prefix $\Upsilon_{j:0}$ on its external ports and a space $E_j$ of dimension $r_j$. Treat the empty prefix as the scalar one. The causal trace identity says that $|\psi_j\rangle$ and
$|\Omega\rangle_{X_jX'_j}\otimes|\psi_{j-1}\rangle$
purify the same operator $I_{X_j}\otimes\Upsilon_{j-1:0}$ on the earlier external ports and $X_j$. The latter purification is minimal: its purifying leg has dimension $a_jr_{j-1}$, equal to that operator's rank. Purification uniqueness supplies an isometry
$$
V_j:X'_j\otimes E_{j-1}\longrightarrow Y_j\otimes E_j.
$$
This construction can be made directly on matrices. Reshape the two purification vectors as matrices $A,B$ with the common reduced-system index as row index. Then $AA^*=BB^*$ and $A$ has full column rank. With its supported left inverse $A^+$, the matrix $V=(A^+B)^T$ has $V^*V=I$ and maps the first purification to the second. The range inclusion follows from $AA^*=BB^*$, so $A A^+B=B$; the same identity proves the isometry equation. This also treats rank-deficient prefixes on their actual support. Iterating the isometries and tracing the terminal $E_n$ gives $\Upsilon$. Thus every complete internal leg has dimension $r_j$ at its cut, proving (5)--(6). The construction agrees with the finite-network realization theorem of Chiribella, D'Ariano and Perinotti [2009, Theorem 3], with the complete-memory convention fixed here.

For a fixed profile, each local Choi matrix has trace $a_km_{k-1}$. Positivity bounds its norm and every entry by that fixed trace. Its positive, trace-preserving set is therefore compact. The product of these finitely many compact sets remains compact, and the polynomial equality fiber (4) is closed. Nonemptiness at the finite upper bound and the ordered finite search prove attainment of the least integer capacity. Principal-minor positivity and real/imaginary coefficient separation give the stated finite polynomial system. Effective real quantifier elimination produces (7), and exact sample-point algorithms supply algebraic channel entries when the input coefficients are algebraic. Taking the successive minima of the finite coordinate list on a compact fiber gives a lexicographic minimum. Its graph is defined by feasibility and the first-order assertion that no feasible tuple is lexicographically smaller; eliminating its quantifiers proves the all-real selector statement. No approximation oracle is used to decide an exact real equality.

For (8), linearity of the tester pairing makes equality on the supplied span equivalent to every retained response. The original comb has a finite realization at the same upper bound, so the quotient-class feasibility search is nonempty. The feasible fiber remains closed inside the same compact channel product. Basis changes conjugate each local matrix and memory embedding, preserving positivity, trace and linked responses; dimensions are unchanged. The statements about classical memory follow by its orthogonal direct-sum representation. They do not import the different convention in which arbitrary classical assistance is free.

Finally, the three maps (9) are an isometry, a unitary swap and a partial trace. Their total channel sends $X_0,X_1$ to the delayed outputs $Y_1,Y_2$, prepares $Y_0=0$ and isolates $X_2$. This gives (10). Taking the recursive traces leaves a rank-two first prefix and a rank-two second prefix. Across the first cut the only crossing identity Choi factor is $Y_1X_0$, and across the second it is $Y_2X_1$; its four matrix units have operator-Schmidt rank four. All other factors lie on one side. The lower bound two and the displayed attaining realization agree. The two-tooth transmission examples and the independent-channel example follow by the same contraction. ∎

<a id="theorem-m614c6-complete-two-party-process-matrix-classification"></a>**Theorem M.6.14c.6 (Complete Two-Party Process-Matrix Classification).** Use the extension class of Proposition M.6.14c.4 with arbitrary positive finite dimensions
$a=d_{A_I}$, $\alpha=d_{A_O}$, $b=d_{B_I}$ and $\beta=d_{B_O}$. Fix the factor order $A_I,A_O,B_I,B_O$ and the standard Choi coordinates
$M_A=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\mathcal M_A)(|\Omega_a\rangle\langle\Omega_a|)$, and similarly for $B$. Thus the process pairing is exactly $\operatorname{Tr}[W(M_A\otimes M_B)]$. The output-first channel coordinates of Theorem M.6.14c.5 and these input-reference-first coordinates differ by fixed factor permutations, not an unexplained partial transpose.

Let $\mathsf H_X$ denote the real Hermitian space on $X$ and $\mathsf T_X$ its traceless part. The exact allowed linear space is the orthogonal direct sum
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf L={}&\mathsf H_{A_I}\otimes I_{A_O}\otimes\mathsf H_{B_I}\otimes I_{B_O}\\
&\oplus\mathsf H_{A_I}\otimes\mathsf T_{A_O}\otimes\mathsf T_{B_I}\otimes I_{B_O}\\
&\oplus\mathsf T_{A_I}\otimes I_{A_O}\otimes\mathsf H_{B_I}\otimes\mathsf T_{B_O}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{M.6.14c.6.1}
$$
All normalized two-party extensions, and no others, are
$$
\mathsf P=\{W\in\mathsf L:W\succeq0,\ \operatorname{Tr}W=\alpha\beta\}.
\tag{M.6.14c.6.2}
$$
Equivalently the eight allowed Hilbert--Schmidt types are
$$
1,\ A_I,\ B_I,\ A_IB_I,\ A_OB_I,\ A_IA_OB_I,\ A_IB_O,\ A_IB_IB_O,
\tag{M.6.14c.6.3}
$$
where every displayed nonidentity factor is traceless. In bases beginning with the identity, its coefficient is $1/(ab)$; positivity is the remaining constraint on all other real coefficients. The affine dimension is
$$
a^2b^2+a^2(\alpha^2-1)(b^2-1)+(a^2-1)b^2(\beta^2-1)-1.
\tag{M.6.14c.6.4}
$$
In particular it is $87$ for four qubits. This gives a finite spectrahedral test for every normalized extension with nontrivial inputs and outputs, extending the one-dimensional cases of Proposition M.6.14c.4. The general structure agrees with Oreshkov, Costa and Brukner [2012, Appendix C].

Let $\mathcal R_X$ be trace over $X$ followed by replacement with $I_X/d_X$. The fixed-order subclasses are exactly
$$
\mathsf P_{A\prec B}=\{W\in\mathsf P:W=\mathcal R_{B_O}W\},\qquad
\mathsf P_{B\prec A}=\{W\in\mathsf P:W=\mathcal R_{A_O}W\}.
\tag{M.6.14c.6.5}
$$
A process is causally separable exactly when it has a decomposition
$$
W=X+Y,\qquad X,Y\succeq0,\quad X,Y\in\mathsf L,\quad
X=\mathcal R_{B_O}X,\quad Y=\mathcal R_{A_O}Y.
\tag{M.6.14c.6.6}
$$
Their traces divided by $\alpha\beta$ are the nonnegative mixture weights. Thus fixed order, causal separability and causal nonseparability have complete finite tests. Membership in neither fixed-order subclass is not by itself a nonseparability certificate.

The nonseparable class is nonempty whenever all four dimensions are at least two. On four qubits define
$$
P=I\otimes Z\otimes Z\otimes I,\qquad
Q=Z\otimes I\otimes X\otimes Z,
\quad
W_*=\frac14\left[I+\frac{P+Q}{\sqrt2}\right],\qquad
S_*=\frac14(I-P-Q).
\tag{M.6.14c.6.7}
$$
Then $W_*\in\mathsf P$, every causally separable $W$ has $\operatorname{Tr}(S_*W)\ge0$, and
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(S_*W_*)=1-\sqrt2<0.
\tag{M.6.14c.6.8}
$$
More generally, the entire family $W_{r,s}=[I+rP+sQ]/4$ is positive exactly when $r^2+s^2\le1$, and is causally separable exactly when $|r|+|s|\le1$. Thus it has an exact nonseparability boundary, not just one witness. For larger ports choose isometric qubit inclusions $V_X$ and the CPTP maps
$$
\mathcal E_X(\rho)=V_X\rho V_X^*,\qquad
\mathcal D_X(\sigma)=V_X^*\sigma V_X+
\operatorname{Tr}[(I-V_XV_X^*)\sigma]|0\rangle\langle0|.
\tag{M.6.14c.6.9}
$$
They obey $\mathcal D_X\mathcal E_X=\mathrm{id}_2$. Replace a large-port local channel $\mathcal N_A$ in the qubit functional by $\mathcal D_{A_O}\mathcal N_A\mathcal E_{A_I}$, and similarly for $B$. The resulting positive normalized large-port process has a deterministic local restriction equal to $W_*$, so it is nonseparable as well. These are normalized functional classifications; full physical realization of a genuinely non-fixed-order resource remains a distinct predicate.

*Proof.* The strictly positive depolarizing Choi matrix for $A$ is $I_{A_IA_O}/\alpha$. The affine span of the CPTP matrices is this matrix plus every Hermitian $\Delta_A$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_{A_O}\Delta_A=0$. Every such direction is allowed with either sign and sufficiently small magnitude. Its Hilbert--Schmidt types are $A_O$ and $A_IA_O$. The corresponding $B$ tangent has types $B_O$ and $B_IB_O$. Expanding the normalization equation about the two depolarizing matrices forces its constant term to be one and both linear coefficients and the bilinear coefficient to vanish. The constant term is $\operatorname{Tr}W/(\alpha\beta)$. The forbidden linear types are $A_O,A_IA_O,B_O,B_IB_O$; the forbidden bilinear types are $A_OB_O,A_IA_OB_O,A_OB_IB_O,A_IA_OB_IB_O$. Orthogonality leaves exactly (1)--(3). Conversely those restrictions make the contraction one for every complete CPTP pair. Positivity makes every product CP outcome nonnegative, so summing every complete local instrument yields one. This proves necessity and sufficiency. Counting the three orthogonal summands gives (4).

No signaling from $B$ to an $A$ outcome means invariance under every $B$ CPTP tangent after contraction with every $A$ CP outcome. Such outcomes span the full Hermitian $A$ operator space, since sufficiently small positive Choi operators can be completed by a positive remainder inside a full-rank CPTP matrix. Hence that invariance is equivalent to absence of every $B_O$-traceless component, or $W=\mathcal R_{B_O}W$. Together with (2) this is the ordinary $A\prec B$ comb normalization. The exchanged argument proves the other order. A convex mixture of normalized fixed-order processes gives (6); conversely the positive traces in (6) normalize its nonzero summands, and a zero-trace positive summand is zero. This proves the causal-separability characterization. When one input or output dimension is one, its traceless space vanishes, and (1) reduces to the precise preparation/terminal-slot forms of Proposition M.6.14c.4.

For (7), $P^2=Q^2=I$ and $PQ=-QP$. Thus $(P+Q)/\sqrt2$ is a Hermitian involution and $W_*\ge0$ with trace four. Both nonconstant types are allowed in (3). If $X$ is an $A\prec B$ positive summand, $\operatorname{Tr}(QX)=0$ by its $B_O$ dependence, and $I-P\ge0$ gives $\operatorname{Tr}[(I-P)X]\ge0$. If $Y$ is a $B\prec A$ summand, the analogous statements hold with $P,Q$ exchanged. This proves nonnegative pairing with (6). Orthogonality of the Pauli products gives (8).

For the two-parameter family, $(rP+sQ)^2=(r^2+s^2)I$, which proves the disk positivity condition. Pairing with $[I-\operatorname{sgn}(r)P-\operatorname{sgn}(s)Q]/4$ gives $1-|r|-|s|$ and is nonnegative on the separable cone by the same argument. Conversely, when $|r|+|s|\le1$, write $W_{r,s}$ as the mixture of $(I+\operatorname{sgn}(r)P)/4$ with weight $|r|$, $(I+\operatorname{sgn}(s)Q)/4$ with weight $|s|$, and $I/4$ with the remaining weight. Zero-weight terms may be omitted. These belong to the corresponding fixed-order cones, proving sufficiency. Finally the local pre/postcomposition in (9) is completely positive on Choi operators and maps every large-port CPTP operator to a qubit CPTP operator. Its Hilbert--Schmidt adjoint therefore takes $W_*$ to a positive operator, and the same normalized contraction is one on every large-port CPTP pair. It belongs to (2). Given a qubit local map $\mathcal M_A$, the large map $\mathcal E_{A_O}\mathcal M_A\mathcal D_{A_I}$ recovers it under the preceding restriction, because $\mathcal D\mathcal E=\mathrm{id}_2$. Local deterministic pre/postprocessing preserves each causal order and their mixtures. A causally separable large-port process would therefore make $W_*$ causally separable, contradicting (8). This proves nonemptiness in every all-nontrivial dimension. ∎

<a id="proposition-m614c7-finite-register-realizations-and-complete-postselection-flags"></a>**Proposition M.6.14c.7 (Finite Register Realizations and Complete Postselection Flags).** The optimized comb channels of Theorem M.6.14c.5 have a finite physical realization in the following explicit oscillator-register source. Every process matrix of Theorem M.6.14c.6 also has an exact conditional-response realization in that source, with its complete future success/failure instrument and resource record. The latter leaves the full-response realization of a genuinely non-fixed-order resource open.

1. **Actual tensor registers and elementary controls.** Register $\hbar,\Omega>0$ and $T=2\pi/\Omega$. The $q$-level factors on separate one-excitation rail sets, their free Hamiltonians, the local pulses and the cross-Kerr pulses are those of Lemma R.4.2.8d.1, item 1, with the action, peak-coupling, positivity and occupation-preservation properties stated there.

2. **A finite compiler with its workspace counted.** By Lemma R.4.2.8d.1, item 2, any unitary on $r\ge1$ actual registers of total code dimension $D$ is exactly synthesized using at most $B(D,r)$ elementary full-period slots (R.4.2.8d.C.2)--(R.4.2.8d.C.3), with $B(D,r)$ given by (R.4.2.8d.C.4), and with at most $2r-1$ reusable scratch dual-rail registers initially and finally in $0$. Identity padding gives a common deadline when comparing compiled branches.

3. **Channel realization and the memory cut.** A feasible local Choi matrix $C_k$ has a Kraus decomposition with at most
$e_k\le(a_km_{k-1})(b_km_k)$ Kraus operators. Put $p_k=a_km_{k-1}$ and $q_k=b_km_k$, and let $V_k:\mathbb C^{p_k}\to\mathbb C^{q_k}\otimes\mathbb C^{e_k}$ be the corresponding Stinespring isometry. On separate input, output and environment registers, extend

|\psi\rangle_{X_kM_{k-1}}|0\rangle_{Y_kM_kE_k}
\longmapsto
|0\rangle_{X_kM_{k-1}}V_k|\psi\rangle_{Y_kM_kE_k}
\tag{M.6.14c.7.6}
$$
to a unitary. The input and output images are orthonormal subspaces of equal dimension, so a finite unitary extension exists and is compiled by item 2. It uses at most five nontrivial original register factors and code dimension $p_kq_ke_k$ before scratch. Returning an input register to a ready value in (6) transfers its information into the displayed output and environment; it is not an erasure of the complete state.

After the tooth, $Y_k$ is released to its registered output owner. Only $M_k$ crosses the source-memory cut. The environment $E_k$ is physically isolated from every later admitted source coupling and readout. If any part of it is later read, reused or correlated as an accessible control, that part belongs to the crossing memory and the capacities in Theorem M.6.14c.5 must count it. The same rule applies to classical archives and controller states. Fixed prescribed service settings are independent of retained inputs; they do not hide a shared random seed or past-dependent clock. The compiler's temporary workspace, fresh preparations, isolated environments and hardware are charged separately from the defined inter-tooth peak-memory objective. They are not asserted to be absent or to minimize instantaneous apparatus size.

Consequently the product occupancy map intertwines every complete channel leaf, input/effect pairing, spectator, normalized tester and causal history of the synthesized comb. The active crossing register has exactly the optimized capacity. This realizes the accepted finite response carrier; it introduces no new claim that rail dimension alone proves MPU selection or minimality.

4. **All process matrices with a retained future flag.** For $W\in\mathsf P$, put
$$
d=a\alpha b\beta,\qquad
F_W=\frac{W}{\alpha\beta},\qquad 0\le F_W\le I.
\tag{M.6.14c.7.7}

Prepare normalized maximally entangled states on $R_A\otimes A_I$ and $R_B\otimes B_I$, retain the reference halves, and apply the independent local instruments. For local outcomes $a',b'$, their subnormalized joint state on $R_A,A_O,R_B,B_O$ is exactly
